body: ## Summary Adds **New pad** as a third play-time control scheme on the v0.32 gameplay-tags / hall tip. Legacy touch and Legacy pad stay in place and keep their existing backends. ## Settings Menu → **Settings** → **Controls**. After this change the radio group has exactly three options: 1. **Legacy touch** — existing surface `nativeTouch` path. Behavior unchanged. Not repointed at Flat router. 2. **Legacy pad** — today’s nested virtual-stick View hierarchy (`PlayHud` / `StickView` / `SplitStickRow`). Previously labeled “Dual joysticks (default)”. Logic unchanged; pref value stays `dual`. 3. **New pad** — Flat router only (`FlatPadRouter` + full-screen `FlatPadOverlay`). Single touch consumer, math hit-test rects, `pointerId → Move | Look | Jump | None`. HUD sticks/jump are drawn on the overlay; they are not nested View touch consumers. Runtime switch calls `releaseAll`, then enables only the selected path. ## Why New pad is a new path Legacy pad still fails from nested View multitouch (shared events, ownership diverge, unbound MOVE reclaim). New pad changes delivery instead of patching Legacy pad in place. New pad publishes each frame to the same JNI move/look/jump hooks Legacy pad uses (`HudAxes` → `nativeSetMoveAxes` / `nativeSetLookAxes` / `nativeJumpButton`). No gamepad work. No other engine stages. ## Version / release - `versionName` `0.33.0` / `versionCode` `33` - GitHub Release: https://github.com/EliteSavior/vasthall/releases/tag/v0.33-hall - Asset: `VastHall-v0-foss.apk` (473146 bytes, md5 `30486e1c00fb17f16d27f80a4f496130`) — matches the live download - Built with `./gradlew :app:assembleFoss` (fossDebug) - Source commit: https://github.com/EliteSavior/vasthall/commit/99fa0ba58ae26b3dd4717f26b581bb11defa7370 ```bash adb uninstall com.elitesavior.vasthall && adb install VastHall-v0-foss.apk ``` README Download / Direct links on this branch point only at `v0.33-hall`. ## Tests `FlatPadRouterTest` covers bind/move/up, no MOVE revive after lift, jump does not steal look, CANCEL/`releaseAll` clears, scheme switch releases then enables only the selected path, and a smoke that Legacy touch / Legacy pad / New pad remain the three selectable labels. `:app:testFossDebugUnitTest` is green, including existing `PlayInputMachineTest` / `StickViewTest`. author: skydiver
body:
## Summary

Adds a conversational AI assistant that generates and edits Mermaid diagrams in place, making it the app's headline feature for 4.0.0. A collapsible right-hand panel (⌘⇧A) streams replies from a provider of your choice and applies the resulting diagram straight to the editor, with Apply/Cancel so nothing is lost. All provider traffic and credential storage live in the Rust backend, so the webview keeps its `default-src 'self'` CSP and API keys never reach the frontend.

## Changes

**AI provider layer (Rust)**
- New `src-tauri/src/ai/` module with Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama and OpenAI-compatible backends over SSE and NDJSON streaming
- Credentials stored in the OS keychain (`keyring.rs`), namespaced per provider with a separate `-dev` service prefix in debug builds
- API keys redacted from every provider error path before the message reaches the frontend
- System prompt centralized in `ai/prompt.rs` and covered by tests; the frontend never sends a system message
- `list_ai_providers`, `save_ai_api_key`, `delete_ai_api_key`, `test_ai_provider` and `send_ai_message` commands
- `lib.rs` split into `menu`, `file_open` and `fonts` modules

**AI panel (frontend)**
- `AIPanel` with chat log, composer and provider dropdown; `useAIChat` handles streaming, stop, apply and cancel
- Replies are applied optimistically; Cancel restores the previous source exactly, and hand-editing accepts implicitly
- Works from the empty state — asking for a diagram with no document open creates one
- Conversations are in-memory only and cleared only when a document is actually replaced, not when New/Open is cancelled
- Mermaid block extraction helper with its own test suite

**Settings**
- Settings dialog split into General, Editor, AI and About sections
- AI section rebuilt as a provider card grid with per-provider model, base URL and API key fields, plus Test connection
- Experimental warning banner above the provider grid
- New General option for the default diagram view (fit or 100%)
- AI settings schema validated in `validate-settings.ts`

**Workspace**
- AI panel width is draggable up to half the workspace and persisted; widening takes space from the preview, never the editor
- Pane dividers are draggable, double-click to reset
- Keyboard shortcuts resolve by physical `code` when the layout reports an unusable `key` (⌘⇧A was dead on some layouts)
- Preview zoom icons replaced with ones that describe what they do

**Docs**
- README leads with the AI assistant, documents providers, keychain storage and what is sent to the provider
- Version bumped to 4.0.0 across `package.json`, `Cargo.toml` and `tauri.conf.json`

## Notes

- The AI feature ships marked **Experimental** in both the README and the settings UI — results vary by provider and model.
- No new secrets or personal data enter the repo; keys exist only in the OS keychain and never in `settings.json`, event payloads or error messages.
- README screenshots are still from 3.0.0 and do not show the AI panel or the rebuilt settings. They will be replaced after this merges.
- Verification: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build` clean; 151 frontend tests and 49 Rust tests passing; `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

body:
**[architect]** — lead-coder の提案（broker、2026-09-08）を受けた doc 化。**起票はしない／置き場所は architect が決める**という申し送りどおり、私が書きました。`part of #5919`（この夜の 3 例の 1 つがそこ）。

## なぜ書くか

**同じ形が 3 つの独立な設計で選ばれ、しかも 3 つとも同じ代償を払いました。**

| where | 何を列挙していたか | 導出元 |
|---|---|---|
| #5959 | 「メモリの大口」 | `gc.get_objects()`（発見）＋ `walk_config_schema()` の `Axis.BOUNDING` 全数（完全性） |
| #5967 | 「private を借りてはいけない gate script」 | `glob("check_*.py")` ＋ その file 自身の `ast.parse()` |
| #5891 | 「tool-call id を持つ呼び手の種類」 | **持たない** — 引数を必須にして不在を*宣言*させ、「持つはずなのに null」は実 event の census |

置き換えられた数え落としは全部同じ形でした: **在るものを数え、在るべきなのに無いものを数えない。** `git grep <flag>` は渡した site を数えて忘れた site を数えず、`src/` に絞った census は `tests/` を落とし、`| head -12` は表示の切り詰めを母集団にします。（3 つとも今夜、私と lead-coder が実際に踏んだものです。）

## 何を書いたか

`verification-hazards.md` に **§28**。**発火する act を先頭に置きました** — 「**これから、覆う／検査する／免除する物の一覧を書こうとしている**」。

そして**代償を同じ節に書きました**（これが無いと片手落ちになります）: 導出は「腐る表」を「静かに壊れる走査」に交換するので、**fail-closed guard が 2 つ**要ります。

1. **走査する対象が 0 件**（`assert scanned_files`）
2. **走査は動いたが候補が 0 件** — 一段深く、見落としやすい。1 が緑、run も緑、検査は何も噛んでいない

**どちらの zero も、きれいな世界と同じ exit code・同じ出力**です（§3「二つの zero」の corpus 版）。∴ **`0 of 0` と `0 of 217` を出力で区別できる形にする**、を要件として書きました。

**導出できない場合**は正当な答えですが、**理由を一覧の隣に書く**こと — 理由のある一覧は決定、理由の無い一覧は作者より長生きする事故です。

## CLAUDE.md

**新しい行は足していません。** 既存の pointer 行に**発火する act を足しただけ**です:

> - **Before reading a green as evidence, or listing what to cover/exempt** — `verification-hazards.md`

理由: この規則が要るのは「一覧を書こうとした瞬間」で、既存の pointer の trigger（「green を証拠として読む前」）ではその瞬間に読まれません。**trigger の無い規則は規則ではない**（この file 自身の編集規則）。

**word count は baseline 以下**（2644 → 2646 → **2644 相当以下**）: 足した 2 語は、**同じ list 上の冗長な pointer 2 本から回収**しました（`Before writing a review's blocking point` → `Before writing a blocking point`、`When you claim a feature does or does not exist` → `When you claim a feature exists or not`）。∴ `--write-baseline` は不要です。

body:
> I should not be giving instruction to merge, it should be autonomous.

Records the standing directive in `CLAUDE.md` so it holds across sessions rather than living in one
conversation.

**What changes:** a PR on the working branch that is green on its current head, conflict-free, and has
no unaddressed review thread gets taken out of draft and merged without asking — then reported. Both
hosts auto-deploy from `main`, so merging is shipping (§23d).

**What does not change,** stated explicitly so the authority can't be read as a shortcut:

- CI green on the head being merged — never by skipping, disabling or quarantining a check
- the duplicate check done and stated in the PR
- a DB-free proof harness, plus the regression that reproduces the reported defect
- **money-touching changes and migrations still surfaced for owner approval** — autonomy covers
  merging code, not moving money or mutating the schema unasked
- a defect found in live data is reported, never papered over in code

If the bar is not met, the PR waits and the reason is stated — the one case where a *non*-merge is
worth the owner's attention.

Documentation only; no code, no migrations.

body:
Found by the paper session's reviewers, who pinned a citation to `v2.3.1` and followed it into the repository. Pinning a citation to a tag freezes that tag's documentation with it — so they were fixed at the tag as **`v2.3.2`** (documentation only), and this carries the same six forward onto `main`, where all six also live.

| where | claimed | actually |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md:388` | every divergence from the paper is traced to a specific cause | Section 2's FGA `F` row is 5 against 0 with no cause recorded, and is not alone |
| `README.md:78` | rules with no source of uncertainty (R, P) always emit A | rule R has graded C throughout since `v2.2.0` — 1922 findings, none of them A |
| `README.md:291` | the **six** rules run independently | seven; type M carries two. Corrected in `verification.md` before `v2.3.1`, missed here |
| `docs/verification.md:13` | divergences recorded "with an established cause for each" | same overclaim as the README |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md:192` | grade C carries one of **two** `Reason` values | three — `TRANSFORM_REQUIRES_CONTEXT` was missing |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md:204` | `S.pshufb_guard` is the only rule emitting C | S, R and F all do |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md:28` | checkouts found "via the environment variable **or the default path**" | there is deliberately no default path, and `test_verification.py` says why |

Every one was verified against the `v2.3.1` tree and the current source before editing — the `Reason` enum, which rules construct `Evidence.C`, the rule count.

## The v2.3.2 tag

`git diff v2.3.1 v2.3.2 -- src tests` shows **exactly one line**, the `__version__` constant — as the `v2.3.0`→`v2.3.1` diff did before it. The paper session asked for an empty diff there; a package whose metadata disagrees with its tag is what `test_the_declared_version_matches_the_package_metadata` exists to catch, so the constant has to move with the tag. No rule, table or test changed.

Re-run against both pinned checkouts rather than assumed:

```
397 passed
SVT-AV1  3272  A 845, B 60, C 2367
VVenC     449  A 101, B 87, C 261
```

Identical to `v2.3.1`. `main`'s newer figures (3365 / 593, from #42) are deliberately **not** in that tag.

One thing the tag has that this does not: `v2.3.2` also relabels its own figures, which `verification.md` there called "on `main`" while calling `v2.2.0`'s "the tagged release's output" — backwards for a reader standing on the tag. On `main` those are a superseded baseline and already labelled by release, so there is nothing to fix here.

author: ishiland
body:
## Why

`scripts/init-db.sh` only worked as the bundled database's initdb hook, because it called `psql` with no host or port. Managed deployments therefore had to paste equivalent SQL out of the docs, and that copy had already drifted: the published `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA data ...` omits the `FOR ROLE` the reconciler emits, which silently leaves newly ingested `data.*` tables unreadable by `geolens_reader` once an operator adopts the opt-in runtime role.

The role and grant half was already portable and shared by three callers. Only the extensions and schemas block was container-bound, so this closes that gap rather than adding a second script.

## What changed

Host and port arguments are appended only when `POSTGRES_HOST`/`PGHOST` or `POSTGRES_PORT`/`PGPORT` are set, the same pattern `configure-runtime-db-role.sh` already uses. Neither is set inside the db container, so the socket path is unchanged. The reconciler is resolved from the checkout first, falling back to the container mount.

`pg_stat_statements` moves behind a `pg_available_extensions` probe. `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS` only suppresses "already exists", so an unavailable extension still ERRORs, and under `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` that aborted the entire bootstrap on a provider that does not ship it. The four required extensions stay unguarded, so a missing one remains a hard stop matching migration `0001_baseline`.

## Verification

Both paths exercised end to end against real servers.

**Managed simulation** (bare Postgres, no initdb hook, script run from the host over TCP): created all four extensions, both schemas and `geolens_reader`; a second run exited 0, confirming idempotency.

**Bundled path** (fresh container, script mounted at `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/10-init.sh` and the reconciler at `/usr/local/bin/...`, exactly as compose does): no errors in the hook, all five extensions present including `pg_stat_statements`, both schemas, `geolens_reader` created.

Positive control on the guard, same server:

| statement | result |
| --- | --- |
| `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS <unavailable>` | exit 1, `extension … is not available` |
| the same call behind the probe | `NOTICE … skipping`, exit 0 |


body:
From `OPS-BACKLOG-2026-09` §6 P1 — "verify pill colours match the legend".

### Cause
The app had **two** activity-colour palettes that disagreed:

| type | `config/activity_types.php` + `_planning.scss` (instructor planner) | `Event::typeColor()` (events calendar + badges) |
|---|---|---|
| training | `#5c6bc0` indigo | `#28a745` green |
| theory | `#78909c` grey | `#6f42c1` purple |
| pool | `#4a86c8` | `#0077be` |
| apnea | `#00c853` | `#00bcd4` |
| social | `#e91e63` | `#ffc107` |

So the same event rendered one colour on `/events` and another on `/availability`. `events/form.blade.php` carried a *third* hard-coded copy of the 5-value map. The config file's own header comment already declares it "Single source of truth".

### Fix
`Event::typeColor()` now resolves from `config('activity_types.<type>.color')`. `color_hex` still wins; a two-line `match` only covers the legacy `dive` value (which predates the config and maps to `#00695c`, same as `.activity-dive` in the SCSS). The form's colour-picker JS map is now derived from the same config.

Not touched: the form's hard-coded `event_type` option list (`pool/dive/training/theory/social`) doesn't offer the config's `quarry`/`apnea`/`long_trip`/… — a separate gap, left for its own change.

### Tests
`EventModelTest` — the per-type assertions previously pinned the *old* divergent literals; they now compare against `config('activity_types.*.color')` via a data provider, plus the legacy-`dive` and unknown→grey cases. `color_hex`-wins test unchanged. 33 Event-* tests green on staging/PostgreSQL; Pint + PHPStan clean; Blade compiles.

author: hellofrequencylab
body:
## What

Closes LIVE-139. The crawlable event share card, the one a search engine and a first-time visitor see, now leads with the event's cover instead of the brand text layout. To afford it, that one route stops prerendering and serves on demand behind the caching headers it already sets. Export cost of the change: zero.

## Why

The row said to do this behind a real build reading rather than reasoning about it, and the reading is what chose the branch. Measured on this repo's own pipeline at the card's real size:

| Card | Time per slug | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flat text (today) | ~88 ms | 26 KB |
| Cover-led | ~360 ms | 139 KB |

That is roughly 310 ms of extra rasterisation per slug before the remote image fetch, across the ~200 slugs this route inherits, on a 4-core builder with 3 workers. LIVE-123 is open on builds stalling in exactly that phase, so adding that to the export is the kind of change that decides a marginal build. The row named the alternative itself, and this takes it.

Privacy is unchanged and tier 1 only: the cover comes from the public bucket through the anonymous client, so row-level security is the gate, and the private poster bucket stays out because a scanned flyer can carry the street address this surface redacts to city level.

## How to review (owner)

1. Wait for CI to go green (that IS the code review).
2. In the Vercel preview, open a public event's share card URL: an event with a cover gets the photo, one without gets the text card unchanged.
3. If it looks right, merge.

## How / files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/og/event-card.tsx` | The one layout both event cards render. Reads no database and resolves no storage path. |
| Both event OG routes | Compose it; the public one exports on-demand rendering. |
| `app/discover/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.test.tsx` | Real render: poster branch, text fallback, an identity-free branch, exactly one fetch and it is the public URL, and the on-demand export. |
| `scripts/build-fanout.test.ts`, `docs/*` | Fan-out arm, ADR-1257, a stale line in the events audit. |

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `pnpm lint` on touched files
- [x] `pnpm test` (149 tests across the touched suites; the agent's full run was 1231 across 83 files); `check:backlog`, `check:adr`, `check:one-list`, `check:client-boundary`, `check:seo`
- [ ] Checked the Vercel preview

⚠️ **One thing this PR's own preview build must show, and it is the only way this change can fail:** the route table must list that OG route as dynamic rather than prerendered. `check:og-trace` reads a real artifact, which only Vercel produces, so it printed "no .next/server" here both before and after. It should not move, since the route already carried the rasteriser.

## Notes / follow-ups

- Left alone: the member card's gate and redaction precedence, the discover page's own prerender, and the cover aspect field, which a fixed canvas does not use.

author: westkitty
body:
**BUG-001 was still a live defect. The other three held.** Both facts are now established against the real application instead of against variables declared inside a test.

## What was wrong with the previous coverage

`tests/adversarial/async-hammer.test.ts` claimed BUG-001 through BUG-004. Each of its five checks declared its own `let isSubmitting` / `let currentRequestId` / `let cancelled` and asserted on that reproduction. No test in the repository imported `src/App.tsx`, so **deleting every shipped guard left the file green**. It proved the algorithm could be written twice, and nothing about the application.

## The new coverage

`tests/browser/concurrency.test.ts` drives the production bundle in installed Chrome — real DOM handlers, real React state, real IndexedDB, the real import control, the real voice controls. Only same-origin `/api/*` is stubbed, and its responses are **held open on demand**, so the in-flight window is genuine rather than simulated. No credentials, no inference, no neurons.

## Per bug

| Bug | Previously claimed | Real path now exercised | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BUG-001** | double-submit lock | two `.click()` calls dispatched in one browser task on the real submit button | **REAL DEFECT FOUND AND REPAIRED** |
| **BUG-002** | stale closure overwrite | request A held → real campaign import → request B → resolve B then A | VERIFIED REPAIR |
| **BUG-002b** | in-flight STOP/PRIVATE | real `agency-private` / `agency-stop` controls used mid-flight | VERIFIED REPAIR (both) |
| **BUG-003** | import race | real `.file input` import of a synthetic Campaign B while A is in flight | VERIFIED REPAIR |
| **BUG-004** | voice desync | real Talk mode, real mic controls, held `/api/transcribe`, real mode switch | VERIFIED REPAIR |

### BUG-001 — the defect

`submitText` read `isSubmitting` from the **render closure**. `setIsSubmitting(true)` happens inside the async path, so two clicks in the same browser task both observed `false`, both passed the guard, and **both started an `/api/turn` request**. `currentRequestId` then discarded one response — which hid the problem, but Atlas had already performed duplicate provider work and could spend duplicate neuron budget. The first run of the new test reported `expected 2 to be 1`.

**Repair:** a `submitInFlight` ref claimed synchronously before the first `await`, because React state cannot provide mutual exclusion. `isSubmitting` is kept for presentation. The lock is released in the `finally` of every completion path — success, typed failure, throw, import invalidation — and cleared on import, with a test proving a later legitimate submission is not stranded.

## Mutation evidence

One production guard removed at a time, rebuilt and rerun each time:

| Guard removed | Result |
|---|---|
| `submitInFlight` lock | BUG-001 fails |
| `reqId !== currentRequestId.current` rejection | BUG-002 **and** BUG-003 fail |
| commit-time paused/private re-check in `setState` | PRIVATE **and** STOP fail |
| import-time `currentRequestId.current++` | BUG-003 fails |
| `pendingCaptureCancelled` check | BUG-004 fails |

All restored; no mutation is committed.

## Old test disposition

`tests/adversarial/async-hammer.test.ts` is **deleted**. Every obligation it claimed is now covered by real-application coverage, and keeping a toy beside the real proof would only inflate the count. Reported honestly: unit tests **235 → 230**, browser tests **69 → 76**.

## Local validation

- concurrency suite alone — 7/7
- full browser suite — **76/76, three consecutive runs**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm test` — 230 passed, 1 skipped
- `npm run build` — passed
- `git diff --check` — clean

`src/App.tsx` changed, so the client bundle hash changes (`index-CLZDcF-s.js` → `index-fUzHTQZI.js`). That is expected: this pass contains a real product repair.

## Also observed, deliberately not changed

`submitEncounter` carries the same closure-read guard (`isSubmitting` from render state), so a double-tap inside a Boss Fight or Mystery Door could dispatch a stage answer twice. Reaching that state needs level 5 plus three covered dimensions, which this pass could not set up, so it is reported rather than silently patched — no untested production change.

Implementação da camada de acesso a dados (`repository`) para as 4 entidades do domínio.

author: kewton
body:
## 概要

Issue #2406 — PC のチャット面 / ターミナル面で、エージェントが**待機中（ready）でも送信するたびに**「Queued (session busy) — your message will run after the current task finishes.」のトーストが出ていました。#2381 の README hero 収録（claude が idle の状態で 1 行送信）で毎回再現し、シーンでは ✕ で閉じて撮っていたものです。

## 原因

`TerminalSplitPaneContent.tsx` が `MessageInput` の `isProcessing` に `terminal.isRunning` を渡していました。`isRunning` は **#2238 以降「tmux セッションが存在し健全」の意味**で、「前のタスクを処理中」ではありません。セッションが在れば常に true なので、#806 の「送信がノーオペに見えないようにする」ヒントが待機中の送信にも毎回出ていました。

## 変更

- **PC**: `isProcessing` を新設の `isGenerating`（`terminal.sessionStatus === 'running'`）へ差し替え。`sessionStatus` の値域は `SessionStatus`（`'idle' | 'ready' | 'running' | 'waiting'`）で、**`ChatSurface` が生成中バブルに使う `live.sessionStatus === 'running'` と同一の verdict** です。footer の `useMemo` 依存配列にも追加しています（入れ忘れると古い値を掴みます）。
- **すぐ上の `isSessionRunning={terminal.isRunning}`（送信ボタンの活性）は別 prop・別の問いなので変更していません。**
- **スマホ**: `WorktreeDetailRefactored.tsx` の `MobileComposer` に `isProcessing` / `showToast` を新設し、`activeSessionProcessing` を渡すようにしました。スマホはこれまで `isProcessing` を**一度も渡しておらず** `MessageInput` 側の既定 `false` に落ちていたため、PC とは**逆向き**に「生成中に出るべきトーストが一度も出ない」状態でした。

### Issue 本文との差分

Issue は「`MobileTerminalTab.tsx` の同じ prop も確認」と書いていますが、実際には **`MobileTerminalTab.tsx` は `MessageInput` を描画せず `isProcessing` prop も持ちません**（grep 0 件）。スマホの実際の送信経路は `WorktreeDetailRefactored.tsx` 内のローカル `MobileComposer` です。

payload の `isProcessing` が `sessionStatusToActivityFlags(status).isProcessing`（`lib/session/status-mapping.ts`）＝ `status === 'running'` と厳密に一致することを確認したうえで採用しており、PC 側が poller から読む verdict と同じ源になっています。

## 検証

`wait --verify` で **13 ゲート全て PASS（RESULT passed / exit 0）**。

- PC: `TerminalSplitPaneContent.test.tsx` の `queued-send toast gate (Issue #2406)` で **ready / running / waiting の 3 ケース**を固定
- スマホ: `WorktreeDetailRefactored-queued-toast-2406.test.tsx` で**実 `ToastProvider` ＋実 `MobileComposer` / `MessageInput`** を使い、実際に出るトーストを assert（モックの戻り値ではなく描画結果を見ています）

## 断片の一本化

CHANGELOG は `[Unreleased]` に `### Fixed` を新設して 1 エントリ（456 → 457、欠落 0）。**直近の `### Fixed` は `[0.32.1]` のものなのでそこへは足していません。** `docs/module-reference.md` は 491 行目・321 行目への追記のみで、行数 825 のまま・重複キー 0・欠落 0・生パイプ数の変化 0 を機械照合済み。

Closes #2406

author: yo1t
body:
P3-26 decided the wording on 2026-08-14. Its implementation record lists three things that **are not in this repository**:

- the Hub's settings tab renamed to Data Enrichment
- a `lint:terminology` over the user-facing files
- regression tests for it

**Nothing noticed for three weeks.** The thing that would have noticed was the check itself, and the check was the part that did not exist — so the settings tab still said "Data Sources" the whole time, in both languages.

This does the three.

## Choices worth stating

**The i18n keys keep their old names.** They are storage, not wording; renaming them would migrate every deployment's saved state to change a label.

**The check bans a short list of retired product-facing strings and nothing else.** `server` stays legitimate for a Node process, an HTTP server, an authorization server and the MCP server, exactly as the glossary says — banning the word would produce a check people route around.

**CHANGELOG, backlog and past release notes are excluded.** They record what was true when written. Rewriting history to satisfy a lint would make the record less honest rather than the product more consistent.

## The test that matters

It asserts the check **fires**: builds a scratch repository containing the retired wording and requires a non-zero exit.

A test that only read the rule would have passed against the version of this check that never existed — which is the failure being fixed.

## Verification

Node **2,503 pass**, eslint clean, secret scan clean, terminology gate clean (93 user-facing files). Wired into CI next to the lint it belongs with.

body:
## Summary
Expose the renderer's existing display-mapping/export state through `tiny_renderer_render` without adding a CLI-only rendering path or changing framebuffer storage semantics.

## Behavior
- add `--display-exposure VALUE` for the existing non-negative `DisplayMappingState::exposure`
- add `--output-transfer linear|srgb` for the existing `OutputTransferFunction`
- preserve historical PPM defaults exactly: exposure 1 with sRGB output transfer
- keep PFM data-preserving: any display-only output flag on `.pfm` rejects before asset loading or output-file creation
- duplicate, malformed, non-finite, negative, and unknown display controls reject deterministically

## Regression evidence
- implicit default PPM and explicit `--display-exposure 1 --output-transfer srgb` are byte-identical
- custom CLI exposure/linear-transfer output is byte-identical to direct library `Framebuffer::write_ppm` using the same display state
- custom controls observably change PPM bytes relative to the historical default
- legacy CLI PFM is byte-identical to direct library `write_pfm`
- PFM display-control misuse, duplicate exposure, negative exposure, and unknown transfer all reject before output creation

## Scope
This is deliberately independent of the active Milestone 69 `map_Ks` material/parser work: it changes only `src/render_main.cpp` and the existing display-mapping integration test. It does not alter material state, texture ownership, rasterization, tone-map formulas, HDR storage, or performance behavior.

author: hugolytics
body:
## The problem

The suite was 359 files and 3,192 tests, green in 33 seconds. Speed was never
the issue — sprawl was. `tests/unit/` was 269 files in one flat directory, and
some of them were guarding code that nothing calls any more.

Three things were wrong, and only the first is obvious:

1. **Tests outliving their subject.** Six modules test code with no caller
   anywhere in `src/` or `scripts/` — superseded when haunting moved to
   `fateforger/haunt/` and the flow moved to the stage-gated agent. One of them
   asserts the *line numbers* of methods in a code-navigation helper.
2. **A refactor scaffold that outlived its refactor.** `_parse_event_dt` exists
   at three call sites, and each grew its own branch-by-branch table written,
   per its own docstring, "before and after the refactoring to Pydantic
   dispatch". The refactor landed. All three now delegate to one
   `EventDateTime.to_datetime`, whose table is tested directly elsewhere.
3. **Doubles copied instead of shared.** Nine modules had each grown their own
   `DummyClient` for the Slack web client, differing only in the timestamps
   they invent. Where a double *was* shared, it was shared by importing another
   test module — which works only while both happen to be collected.

## What changed

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| test files | 359 | 341 |
| `tests/unit/` flat files | 269 | 0 |
| tests | 3,192 | 3,137 (+89 slow, unchanged) |
| lines | 76,892 | 75,820 |

- **Pruned** six dead-subject modules (44 tests, 6 of them already skipped).
- **Collapsed** the three duplicated date-parsing tables. What each call site
  still *owns* — the ISO-string branch — stays, because those genuinely differ:
  `reconcile` keeps the parsed offset, the planner converts into `tz`. That
  divergence now has a test naming it, which it did not before.
- **Restructured** `tests/unit/` into subpackages beside the `tmbx/` one that
  already worked this way: `timeboxing/` (96), `slack/` (49), `constraints/`
  (34), `core/` (33), `tmbx/` (22), `haunt/` (14), `tasks/` (9), `schedular/` (7).
- **Extracted** `tests/doubles/` — one Slack client recorder replacing nine, plus
  the reconciler, planning, required-block and kernel doubles that modules were
  importing out of each other.
- **Added** `tests/repo.py`. Twenty files found the repo root by counting
  `parents[N]`, so moving a test one level down broke it with a
  `FileNotFoundError` that reads like a missing fixture. It walks up to
  `pyproject.toml` instead.
- **Folded** 20 one- and two-test fragment files into nine subject modules.

## Proof

**Every lost line is accounted for.** Coverage measured per line, before and
after, on the same command:

```
before  22,221 / 28,593  77.71%
after   21,947 / 28,593  76.76%
```

All 274 lost lines are in the six modules with no caller, plus the
`llm/factory` and `tools_config` branches only their tests reached. **No other
file lost a covered line.**

The one exception, `timeboxing_session_store.py:157`, is the `raise
StaleSessionRevision` inside a concurrent-save race. Per-test coverage contexts
run against `origin/main` show that line is **not covered reliably there
either** — the concurrent-save test wins the race nondeterministically. Not a
regression from this branch.

**Merges cannot silently shadow.** The merge tool refuses any merge where two
sources define the same top-level name.

**Three near-duplicates were investigated and kept.** `planning_day_for` against
the starter that calls it, two `ConstraintStore` prune scenarios, two MCP
clients' empty-loader guard — same test name, different seam. Only genuine
duplicates were removed.

```
3,137 passed, 4 skipped, 89 deselected, 1 xfailed
3,231 collected including the slow evals (not run — they hit OpenRouter)
```

## What I did not do, and why

**The dead source modules are still here.** This PR is test-only. Deleting them
is a source change and wants its own PR. The evidence, if you want it:

`admonisher/{base,calendar,commitment}`, `schedular/diffing_agent`,
`timeboxing/{flow,prompts,state,notebook_entrypoints}`,
`slack_bot/{relay_agent,topics}`, `tools_config/` — no caller in `src/` or
`scripts/`, last touched January–February 2026, and now visibly at 0% coverage.

**The docs are in this PR, not a follow-up.** `tests/README.md` was a
hand-maintained per-file index — which is why it rotted, and why it still
listed `test_timeboxing_flow.py` as live logic. It now describes the shape
(subpackages, `tests/doubles/`, `tests/repo.py`) instead of the inventory.
`CALENDAR_QUERY_LOCATIONS.md` and `MIGRATION_ARCHIVE_TO_CALENDAR_HAUNTER.md`
carry superseded banners pointing at `fateforger/haunt/`, with their original
text intact as a record.

Two claims in that rewrite were wrong and are fixed in a follow-up commit: it
said the fast suite is "what CI and pre-merge checks run" (nothing in
`.github/workflows/` runs pytest at all), and it told you to run
`.venv/bin/python` while explaining why worktrees break the venv — a worktree
has no `.venv`, so that path resolves to nothing exactly where the warning
applies.

**`timeboxing/` is still 96 files.** It is the largest genuine subject in the
repo and folding it further needs judgement per file, not another pass of the
merge tool.

**One gap this surfaced but did not fix:** `fateforger/haunt/orchestrator.py`
has its own capped exponential backoff and no test reaches it. The capped-backoff
test I deleted belonged to the dead `BaseHaunter`, so nothing regressed — but
the live one has never been covered. Worth a ticket.

## Checklist for review

- [ ] The six pruned modules really are dead — spot-check one with
      `grep -rn CalendarHaunter src/ scripts/`
- [ ] The kept `_parse_event_dt` string-branch tests are the right call: the two
      implementations disagree about timezone conversion, and neither is
      obviously wrong
- [ ] The subpackage boundaries match how you think about the system —
      `constraints/` split out of `timeboxing/` is the one most open to argument
- [ ] `tests/doubles/` is the right home, and one Slack recorder for nine call
      sites does not over-generalise
- [ ] Whether the dead source modules should go in a follow-up or be left

body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Sonnet 5 (claude-sonnet-5) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

OVOS-MSG-1 §5.3 defines the `.response` shorthand only where the arithmetic is unambiguous: `T` must not already end in `.response`, and must not contain a `:`. "A dispatch topic (§2.1.1) has no `.response` counterpart, and suffixing an answer topic again produces `<x>.response.response`, which no specification defines. Where either condition fails, the answering component names the answering topic explicitly and derives via `reply` instead." (OVOS-MSG-1, ovos-spec-tools architecture repo, quoted from ovos-spec-tools#143, which adds a `ValueError` guard enforcing this.)

The competitor stand-in in `test/end2end/test_common_query_competition.py` answers `question:query` — a dispatch topic — via `message.response(...)`. That call would raise once #143 ships, since `question:query` contains `:`. This replaces it with `message.reply("question:query.response", ...)`, naming the answering topic explicitly as §5.3 requires, while keeping the same §5.2 source/destination reversal that `reply()` and `response()` already share.

Verified against `ovos-bus-client` 2.11.14a2's `Message.reply`/`response`: for this call site, both currently produce identical `msg_type`, `data` and `context`, so the change is a no-op today and becomes load-bearing once #143 merges. Fail-before: I reproduced #143's guard by monkeypatching `Message.response` with its exact §5.3 checks — calling it on a `question:query` `Message` raised `ValueError` before this fix; the new `message.reply(...)` call in this test succeeded, unaffected by the same guard, after it.

Full suite: 32 passed (including the 3 `test_common_query_competition.py` tests) with the fix applied. Test-only change, single file.

author: raghav-arneja
body:
## Summary

Apache Airflow running locally in Docker, per the locked orchestration decision, with two DAGs: the full daily chain and a backfill for quarantined documents. Backfill semantics changed in the jobs themselves: quarantine rows are released, not deleted. Third of the Stage 3 pull requests.

## Motivation

Cloud Scheduler fires ingest and parse each morning, but nothing orchestrated the chain end to end, nothing ran extraction (which is never scheduled because it spends money), and there was no way to reprocess only the documents that had failed after a fix. The brief asks for a backfill DAG that reprocesses only quarantined keys. Doing that by deleting quarantine rows would erase the record of what failed and why, and for the parse stage would have been a silent no-op.

## What changed

**Jobs and storage**
- Quarantine rows gain `released_at`. A released row stays as history but stops counting as processed. Both jobs put released documents first in their selection; the parse job also treats any source with released rows as pending regardless of cap.

**Airflow** (`airflow/`)
- `docker-compose.yml`: Airflow 3.0.6 standalone with Postgres, bound to localhost, authenticating to GCP through the developer's Application Default Credentials file only.
- `filing_facts_daily`: ingest, parse and extract as Cloud Run job executions, with model, prompt and cap as run parameters. No schedule of its own.
- `filing_facts_backfill`: releases the quarantine rows for one stage and reason, then branches: parse reruns once per affected source with `--source-key`, extract reruns for the chosen model and prompt. Low-confidence extractions are excluded on purpose: they kept their answer, and a better one is a new prompt version.
- An integrity test that runs inside the Airflow image and asserts the graphs; CI runs it on every pull request.

## Verification

- 129 tests, three consecutive runs; new tests cover release semantics for both jobs.
- Airflow integrity tests pass in the image.
- Live, locally: `filing_facts_daily` triggered with a 20-document extract cap ran all three Cloud Run jobs in sequence and succeeded (ingest 23 s, parse 23 s, extract 74 s). `filing_facts_backfill` triggered on both branches: the parse branch with nothing to release skipped its mapped rerun cleanly; the extract branch released nothing and ran the extract job with a one-document cap.
- Terraform applied for the new column; image rebuilt and applied to all three jobs.

## Review before opening

Seven findings fixed and logged, the largest being the backfill design itself. Two more defects were found only by triggering the DAGs for real: the provider's BigQuery operator cannot run without a logical date in Airflow 3, and the hook defaults to legacy SQL. Both are logged.

## Deployment and cost

Airflow runs on the developer's machine; nothing new runs in GCP. The live checks cost under a cent.

## Known limitations and follow-ups

- The DAG files are the one Python directory not under Pyright strict, because Airflow is not a project dependency. The in-image integrity test is their gate.
- The CI job pulls the Airflow image on every run with no cache; acceptable for now.

author: senna-lang
body:
Closes #32

## Root cause
`resolve_u1`/`resolve_u2` (loci context) only ever queried `code_edges` (symbol → file → directory tiers). When a file/symbol has no `code_edges` rows yet — fresh install, large distill backlog, or symbol resolution failing for any other reason — the lookup returned nothing, even though `code_touches` (the raw per-edit log written at index time, before any tree-sitter/distill work) already knows which conversations touched that file. The existing `loci context --branch` path already tolerated undistilled data (LEFT JOIN on `palace_objects`); the symbol/file lookup path did not have an equivalent fallback.

## Fix
- `context_lookup.py`: added two more tiers below `directory`, tried only when the distilled tiers are all empty (no top-up across tiers, consistent with the existing "first hit wins" design):
  - **U1**: `symbol(1.00) → file(0.45) → directory(0.25) → touch_symbol(0.20) → touch_file(0.15)`
  - **U2**: `file(1.00) → directory(0.30) → touch_file(0.20)`
  - `touch_symbol` restricts `code_touches` hits to exchanges whose text mentions the queried symbol name (or its dotted leaf) at a word boundary — the same best-effort criterion `eval/gen/gen_symbol_recall.py` already uses to build gold labels, so the fallback's notion of a "symbol match" isn't a new, unverified heuristic.
  - `touch_file` is the unrestricted "this exchange touched the file" fallback.
- `ContextHit` gained a `distilled: bool` field (`True` for symbol/file/directory/semantic tiers, `False` for the new touch tiers) so callers can tell distilled results apart from best-effort touch-based ones.
- `cli/search_cmd.py`: threads `distilled` into the JSON output and appends an `[undistilled: code-touch based]` marker in text output.
- Did not touch `db.py` init-time backfill logic or `search.py` connection handling (owned by #25) — the new query lives entirely in `context_lookup.py` and reads `code_touches` directly.

## Verification
- **RED**: added regression tests to `tests/test_context_lookup.py` (8 new/updated assertions across `resolve_u1`/`resolve_u2`) and confirmed they fail without the fix — `git stash` on `context_lookup.py` alone reproduces `AttributeError: 'ContextHit' object has no attribute 'distilled'` and `assert 0 == 1` for the fallback cases.
- **GREEN**: restored the fix, all 42 tests in `tests/test_context_lookup.py` pass (34 pre-existing + 8 new/changed).
- **End-to-end**: seeded a throwaway repo/DB with only a `code_touches` row (zero `code_edges`, i.e. a fully undistilled DB) and ran the real CLI:
  - `loci context src/foo.py:greet --json` → returns the touching exchange with `"match_kind": "touch_symbol"`, `"distilled": false`.
  - `loci context src/foo.py` (text) → `[1] touch_file (confidence=0.20) src/foo.py [undistilled: code-touch based]`.
- `make check` (ruff + pyright + full pytest, 801 tests) passes.

body:
Data-layer step S5, the last rung of the ladder: the money tables in CrateStack shape, with `worker_kill9` as the gate.

## What changed

- Migration 0037: `intent_status`, `charge_state`, `refund_status` and the shared `failure_code` (three columns) become TEXT + CHECKs named the generator's way; the partial index `charges_live_idx` is dropped and rebuilt (Postgres refuses the ALTER otherwise); the four types are dropped without CASCADE. Applied to a populated database with every label (21 rows, 26 labels): a byte-identical before/after. 0037 alone moves drift by zero, because introspection already synthesised those CHECK names.
- Models for `payment_intents`, `charges`, `refunds`, `checkout_sessions`. Drift 129 → 140 / 19 with every line accounted; ten of the lines are foreign keys that exist, because `cratestack-migrate` 0.12.0 does not introspect FKs at all (the relations are kept: they are true, and the accounting says why).
- **Four reads moved, all on `checkout_sessions`.** Nothing moves on the three money tables: every row struct carries a merchant-authored JSONB column and CrateStack's JSON conversion demotes non-integer numbers, so those three models carry no policy arm and answer zero rows to every action, pinned by two tests. The settlement statement, `jobs`, `idempotency` and `provider_requests` stay raw forever unless a reason appears, as `docs/reference/vpay-db.md` now states.
- Backward compatibility, measured: a previous-release binary keeps answering every read against a 0037 database (`::TEXT` casts survive) and fails only on writes; a restarting one fails in `run_migrations`. The header carries the drain-first rule.

## Review (Opus, `docs/plans/exp34-money-tables-notes/opus-review.md`)

Not safe as delivered, safe now. The draft's last commit message described extracting `latest_by_intent_query` and adding a test on `ORDER BY seq DESC`; neither existed, and the container test's comment had been rewritten to point at the missing test. Written now, red without a container under the mutation. Also: three 0037 claims done by hand and never landed as tests (populated survival, the six CHECKs refusing, the index still reached); deny-by-default on the money models unasserted (a standing read policy was green through twelve gates); five sentences still calling the dropped types enums; two operator-facing claims in the migration header contradicted by measurement and corrected.

## Proof

`just ci` twice: 1575 passed, 0 skipped, 44 binaries, twelve gates. `worker_kill9` both scenarios unchanged and green; `no_over_refund` deletion red twice with the drift count unmoved. The four Cypress specs 11 passing on the reviewer's own stack (the `just test-e2e` recipe itself is blocked by #78 while the demo holds port 3000). `just demo-up` + `demo-walk`: six payments on two rails through the TEXT columns, zero enum types left.

## Maintainer decisions surfaced

Expand/contract instead of in-place enum conversion; whether `CheckoutSessions::create` should move (a `DROP DEFAULT` on a money table); the ledger's two remaining native enums; 0032's header names the wrong boot step for a restart (pre-existing); the reviewer edited 0037's header and its manifest line before it shipped anywhere.

## Summary

- recognize transparent TypeScript wrappers and expression-free templates in CommonJS specifiers, computed member/destructure keys, and static option keys
- restore non-reassigned `let`/`var` CommonJS provenance
- retain reassignment/reinitialization protection and reject numeric computed keys
- add fixture-backed regressions and synchronize rule documentation

## Root cause

The imported-call analyzer used narrower static-string and binding-stability checks at different syntax boundaries. That made equivalent static forms behave differently and treated declaration kind as a proxy for mutation, while a later correction could accidentally coerce non-string computed keys.

## Validation

- focused imported-call tests: 77 passed
- full ESLint-plugin suite: 574 passed
- JavaScript line coverage: 99.81%
- exact repository pre-push under Rust 1.96: no-mistakes, ast-grep tests/scan, Cargo fmt/Clippy, Oxfmt, and Oxlint

- closes #876

## 🦩 Flamingo Code Review Setup

This PR adds the GitHub Actions workflow required for automated code review.

### What this workflow does

The 🦩 Flamingo Code Review pipeline reviews this repository against the org rule corpus:

1. **PR review** - Reviews pull requests against the org rule corpus
2. **Scheduled sweep** - Scans the whole repository when the hub dispatches one
3. **Run reporting** - Reports every run back to the hub dashboard

Per-repo settings (blocking vs observe, models, locale) live in the hub admin and are read at run time — this file does not change when they do. The workflow holds no push credential: fix PRs are opened by the hub.

### Setup steps

After merging this PR, the workflow needs repository secrets to run. The dashboard provisions them for you, you don't paste them by hand.

1. Merge this PR.
2. Use **Sync Secrets** in the hub admin to provision the repository secrets.
3. Runs appear on the code-review dashboard automatically.

author: jdvlazio
body:
Primero de dos. Este es el lado de **código**; el dato de SiembraFest va detrás, para que nunca llegue a producción antes del guardián que lo entiende.

## Qué pasaba

`[activity-duration]` existe porque la duración *"alimenta el cálculo del plan"*. Pero un evento con `info: true` **no entra al plan ni a conflictos** — lo dice `SCHEMA.md` y lo hacen `screensConflict` y `computeScenarios`. A esos el guardián les exigía igual una duración, y la única forma de dársela es transcribir la **ventana de apertura** como si fuera un compromiso del asistente.

Lo destapó la maratón fotográfica de SiembraFest, abierta de 8:00 a 18:00: la tarjeta decía "600 min", que se lee como diez horas de compromiso. La casa ya lo escribía al revés — de los 14 eventos `info` publicados, 12 no llevan duración, solo hora de inicio.

## Dónde va la exención, y por qué ahí

En el **cuerpo del check**, no en `_PENDING`. `_PENDING` es "dato que el festival debe y no entregó"; esto es "campo que no aplica". Mezclarlas ya había pasado: sale de la lista el *Encuentro Colombia Experimental Contemporánea* de CineAutopsia, que es `info: true` y estaba anotado como si el festival no hubiera anunciado el runtime. La lista baja de 7 a 6 y las 6 que quedan sí son deuda de verdad.

## Mutaciones

| Mutación | Resultado |
|---|---|
| a la maratón le quito `info`, sigue sin duración | **suena**, con su nombre |
| a una obra normal le quito la duración | **suena** |
| a esa misma obra le pongo `info` | **calla** — la exención es la que digo |

Unit tests: 539 pasan. Encontré además una línea muerta que **no** toco acá: `('qaff-2026', 'Muestra Artística')` sigue en `_PENDING` y esa actividad ya no existe en el JSON publicado.

author: rafaelcg
body:
Twitch-style live reactions over a shared screen. A viewer taps one of six emoji docked on the video, it floats up over the share for everyone in the room and fades. Off by default behind `VITE_LIVE_REACTIONS`.

`restarts-api` (new WS frame type on the server).

## The two frames

Client to server, one tap:

```json
{ "type": "live-reaction", "channelId": "<voice channel uuid>", "emoji": "🔥" }
```

Server to the room, coalesced over 250 ms:

```json
{
  "type": "live-reactions",
  "channelId": "<voice channel uuid>",
  "items": [{ "emoji": "🔥", "count": 12 }, { "emoji": "😂", "count": 3 }],
  "seq": 41
}
```

Both in `packages/shared/src/live-reactions.ts`, with the closed emoji set (`LIVE_REACTION_EMOJIS`, six, overlapping `QUICK_REACTIONS`) and the burst threshold.

## Why coalescing is the whole design

Two hundred people tapping is two hundred frames per burst if each tap is relayed, which is the traffic shape that fell over during the Twitch spike in September. The server folds a channel's taps into one frame of counts per window and the client spawns `count` particles from one frame, so outbound cost is the number of rooms rather than the number of taps.

It is deliberately not a message reaction (nothing stored, nothing un-tappable, a reload correctly loses everything) and deliberately not per person (counts per emoji, never who tapped).

## Server

- Accepted only from a socket that holds a peer in the room it names. That reuses the room membership the join already granted, where channel access, permissions, blocks and timeouts were checked and where every eviction path removes a peer. No second audience lookup, because a second one eventually disagrees with the first.
- Five taps per second per socket, surplus dropped in silence. No error frame: the only client that can reach the limit is one tapping faster than a person, and answering it hands it a reason to retry.
- Windows publish on the cluster bus (`voice.reactions`), so a room split across instances still sees the whole crowd under `CLUSTER_BUS`. Unlike the other voice topics this one does not gate on `VOICE_REGISTRY`, because a window of counts refers to nothing stored and cannot leave a room in a wrong state.

## Client

- Particles are CSS keyframes. Per-particle duration, delay, sideways drift and size ride in as inline properties, so a hundred of them still compile to one animation the compositor runs off the main thread. Nothing measures layout, nothing runs per frame. The only timer is a lazy sweep that stops itself when the stage is empty.
- Cap of 60 concurrent particles, oldest dropped first, since the oldest is most of the way through its fade already and dropping the newest would make a burst look like it stopped.
- Burst mode past ten reactions in a window: denser spawn, wider spread, bigger particles, and a brief swell of the container.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` builds no particle at all. Not hidden, not slowed: a static counter chip ("😂 12") renders instead.
- The bar echoes the tap locally before the frame leaves. A round trip plus the coalescing window is long enough to read as a dead button.
- PT and EN copy for the bar label, the per-emoji labels and the chip.

## Tests

Server, in `server/src/ws/live-reactions.test.ts`: the limiter drops the surplus **and** passes traffic under it, the window folds taps into counts per emoji with a per-channel `seq`, and both audience gates refuse (a socket that never joined, and a peer naming a room it is not in). Each guard was verified by removing it and confirming the matching tests go red, then restoring it:

- limiter removed: 2 failed
- coalescing removed (flush per tap): 4 failed
- audience gate removed (trust the frame's `channelId`): 2 failed

Client: the coalesced counts render one element per particle, the cap holds at 60 and drops the oldest, and the reduced-motion path renders the chip with no animated container. Plus the pure arithmetic (proportional spawn, every emoji keeps at least one particle, burst threshold).

Green locally: server vitest 665 passed, client vitest 2175 passed, shared 333 passed, both typechecks, `pnpm lint` 0 errors, `i18n:check` ok.

## Native

`docs/PARITY.md` gains the row and a short section with both frame shapes and what iOS and Android need. The mistake worth naming up front: the frame carries counts, not taps, so treating it as one tap makes a room of two hundred look like a room of four. No native code here.

## What I could not verify

- **No real browser check.** This client's tests render on the server with `renderToStaticMarkup`, so the animation was never seen moving, and neither was the reduced-motion path in a browser that actually has the media query.
- **Cross-instance delivery is untested.** The bus publish and subscriber follow `voice.watch`, but nothing here runs two instances; `CLUSTER_BUS` is off in production anyway.
- **`ScreenStage` is not currently rendered by anything on `main`** (`call-stage.tsx` imports only `collectScreenTiles` and `ScreenShareTile` from it). The overlay and bar are mounted there as asked, and the overlay was written to be a drop-in sibling of the video in `ScreenTileFrame` and in the HLS player on `fix/hls-watch-mode-loading`, but adopting it on the live share surface is a follow-up. With the flag unset none of this renders either way.
- Nothing was checked on a phone or on Electron.

body:
## Summary

Owners can deliberately replace a note's share link, including while sharing is paused. The new owner-only POST rotates the token with one conditional database update: concurrent requests have one 200 winner and a 409 loser. The old URL stops resolving while direct grants remain intact. Ordinary first-link creation and metadata/content writes preserve the winning token instead of restoring an obsolete value.

The action uses the real sharing dialog's fresh authority and shared mutation lock. Its confirmation explains the old link's invalidation and retained direct access, initially focuses Cancel, and prevents duplicate submits. If the response is lost after commit, the client refreshes authoritative state and asks the user to check the result; it never retries rotation automatically.

This layer targets `feat/sharing-people-ui` (S3), which already contains S2's active-session enforcement. Merge the stack bottom-up.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation update

<!-- sharing-coderabbit-final-evidence:start -->
## Validation

Latest head `a087f588433eeb79de92e2074745a2416b831da2` includes the reviewed correction from S2. The actual [CodeRabbit review](https://github.com/jovandyaz/knowtis-app/pull/541#pullrequestreview-5136153771) prompted direct reproductions: the real Hocuspocus 4.1 transport could create 107 sockets in 30 seconds beyond the hook's recovery budget, and registration at lease expiry could close the same connection twice. The correction gives the existing hook sole ownership of bounded transport recovery and closes the expired connection once. It preserves the document, awareness, draft, token-refresh policy and wire reasons. Six actual-provider regressions cover socket creation limits, continued halt, ordinary network recovery, terminal denial, unmount and healthy-socket reauthentication. Close reasons now share a derived union; negative delivery/lifecycle/cleanup assertions were strengthened.

Eight bot recommendations were accepted. The other seven were checked against actual behavior and repository policy: publishing already has a settled-promise failure boundary; metrics intentionally count all settled SQL; administrator override is already tested; identity/raw-error logging would weaken the privacy contract; the required Date event contract is retained; forcing a new TLS deployment policy or claiming an audited image digest lacks the required infrastructure evidence. These dispositions do not assert that optional hardening was implemented. Four fresh independent review lenses passed the full 13-file correction.

A fresh independent verifier tested the exact combined candidate tree `3d5c9e3a4ebcd52ff0d63a84b55161b033b3fdeb`: **7/7 actual browser scenarios in 59.685 seconds, zero retries/skips/flaky results**, plus 64 API tests (including 18 native PostgreSQL/Redis cases), 23 Notes tests (six real-provider cases) and four typecheck targets. Two separate API processes, real HTTP authentication, verified users, PostgreSQL/Redis and native WebSockets were used. Controlled closure times: Redis 838 ms, stalled PostgreSQL 1797 ms, rotation 52 ms. These are local fault measurements within the tested five-second bound, not a production SLA. The actual successful HTML, two screenshots and three timing attachments were preserved and inspected; 2160 source blobs remained identical and owned services were removed.

The correction was integrated through ordinary commits with all normal hooks enabled. Each child-layer delta was independently reconstructed over its new parent and checked against the resulting tree; the final S5 tree `d738d84f3b0679eafff085406bd8ff54cff461ec` differs from the independently tested browser candidate only in one page-test mock. The broader pre-push suite exposed its missing explicit-transport export; the test-only correction preserved all six assertions, passed four fresh review lenses, and independently passed 29 Notes cases, typecheck and strict lint. All product and harness blobs remain identical to the seven-case native run. This preserves every separately reviewed product/harness layer. [CI passed on this exact head](https://github.com/jovandyaz/knowtis-app/actions/runs/34175364568/job/101903573071). The final combined head `c2bbbebf9f918decf517d78288a04ed9615f32f3` also passed [actual browser acceptance in CI](https://github.com/jovandyaz/knowtis-app/actions/runs/34175537242): **7/7 in 107.353 seconds, zero retries, skips or flaky results**. Its [downloadable artifact](https://github.com/jovandyaz/knowtis-app/actions/runs/34175537242/artifacts/10037366103) contains the actual successful HTML report, two screenshots and three embedded timing attachments; these were downloaded and independently decoded. Actual CodeRabbit re-review of the corrected heads remains capacity-limited. No PR has been merged and no production rollout is performed.
<!-- sharing-coderabbit-final-evidence:end -->

## Compatibility, rollout and rollback

Adds `POST /notes/:id/share-link/rotate` with an empty body, 200 success and 409 conflict. Existing routes remain; no database migration or MCP tool is introduced. A new frontend against an old API cannot rotate, so deploy the matching backend before exposing the action. Every API process must include S2 before claiming withdrawal from open sessions. The release maintainer must record immutable API/Notes SHAs, use the shared maintenance window, and verify a canary rotation: A returns 404, B works, retained direct access works, and old-link traffic stops within the demonstrated bound. Stop on stale-token resurrection, multiple successful rotations from one confirmation, direct-access loss or an over-bound cutoff.

The preferred rollback is Notes to the matching S3 revision while retaining this API and each current winning token; rotation disappears from the interface without reviving retired links. Do not restore token A from a backup. If backend rollback is necessary, first stop sharing mutations and drain in-flight metadata/content writers and collaboration sockets, preserve the current tokens/permissions/content, then verify the retained token and retired-token rejection before reopening. Rolling below S2 additionally withdraws its active-session guarantee. These deployment/rollback actions require separate authorization; this PR only prepares the change for review.

## Screenshots / Recordings

Independent browser assertions cover confirmation, initial Cancel focus, one mutation, retained direct access and uncertain results. Retained English desktop/Spanish mobile screenshots show the shared People surface; they do not depict every rotation state. The final test-layer CI report carries the available evidence.

## Related Issues

Part of #245, with #246 as a stack dependency. No automatic closure.

The permission contract is in `docs/PERMISSIONS.md`. Decisions follow [PostgreSQL conditional-update concurrency](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/transaction-iso.html), [Drizzle UPDATE/RETURNING](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/update), [Node crypto.randomBytes](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/crypto.html#cryptorandombytessize-callback), and [TanStack mutation behavior](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/reference/functions/useMutation), checked against installed versions. Existing artifact access is tested only at the read-only empty-list boundary. Rotation cannot recall downloaded content or undo previously accepted edits.

## Checklist

- [x] Repository contribution and coding guidance reviewed.
- [x] Concurrent database/HTTP and integrated dialog/query regressions added.
- [x] Independent code-quality, Superpowers, Standards and Spec review complete.
- [x] Independent final verification, normal hooks and production builds recorded above.
- [x] Real browser/session acceptance and available screenshot scope recorded above.
- [x] Latest-head CI confirmed.
- [ ] Actual CodeRabbit review of the latest correction confirmed

author: jmackenzie11
body:
Phase B of the feature-flag investigation. Ships alone; the data repair and the two follow-ups are separate.

## The bug

`computeCompanyScorecard` resolved feature flags through the request-scoped `getCompanyFeatures()`, which reads with the cookie-scoped Supabase client. The weekly cron has no session, so that client reaches PostgREST as `anon`. Every policy on `company_features` is `to authenticated` (migration 0016), so `anon` matches none of them and the read returns **empty rather than an error**.

Both flags resolved `false` on every run since 2026-08-13. All four feature-gated disciplines were written as `{ score: null, breakdown: { notEnabled: true } }` on every snapshot the cron has ever taken.

`/scorecard` looked correct throughout, because the page computes live through a client that does carry a session. The page was right while the history behind it was wrong, and the two are only compared by the trend line and the Guide HQ attention trigger.

## Confirmed blast radius (read-only probe, production)

| | rows |
|---|---|
| Ungated disciplines (foundation, chart, planning, execution) | 104, all scored, correct |
| Gated disciplines | 104, **all null, zero ever scored** |
| ...provably wrong (`snapshot_date >= enabled_at`) | 67 |
| ...ambiguous (flag granted later in the window) | 5 |
| ...consistent with a genuine disable | 32 |

Five companies hold `performance_tracking` today and seven hold `meeting_facilitation_review`, out of eight active. A correct run should have produced roughly 20 and 78 scored rows. It produced zero.

The stored `overall` is derived from the snapshot rows at read time by `overallFrom`, which drops nulls and redistributes weight, so every historical overall point was computed on total weight 6 instead of up to 10. Those points are **distorted, not missing**.

## The fix

Read entitlements through the client the caller was handed. This is the pattern the codebase already had twice, for the same reason: `companyHasFacilitationReview` in `transcripts/analyze.ts` and the `company_features` read in the performance cron.

`computeCompanyScorecard` has two callers with different contexts. The page hands it an RLS-scoped session client; the cron hands it the instance's service-role client from `forEachActiveInstance`. Only the client knows which is which, so the flag read has to travel with it. `getCompanyFeatures()` keeps its request-scoped memo for page callers and delegates to the same helper.

`compute.ts:49` was the only feature-flag call site in the codebase reachable from a session-less context, so this is surgical.

## Also in scope

- **The entitlement read logs its error** instead of discarding it. "No entitlements" and "the read failed" were the same value and must not be the same signal. Same reasoning as `findSimilarOpenItem`.
- **The cron summary line carries the enabled count**, fleet-wide and per company. The old line said `8/8 companies snapshotted, 0 failed` for three weeks straight. It now reads `.../... feature-gated disciplines enabled`, so a `0/N` is the tell. Derived from `DISCIPLINES` rather than hardcoded, so a new gated discipline updates the line for free.
- **One line in the spec** on why a weekly run produces two `snapshot_date` values. `snapshot_date` is stamped in the company's timezone, so a 07:00 UTC Sunday run lands on Saturday for western tenants and a week appears as a Sat/Sun pair. Correct, and previously undocumented enough to read as a bug.

## Tests

`src/lib/maturity/feature-gating.test.ts`. There is no Postgres in this environment, so the session-less context is simulated by mocking `@/lib/supabase/server` to **throw on use**: any path that reaches for a session fails loudly instead of quietly returning `[]` the way production did.

**Verified they fail against the pre-fix resolution** (6 of 12, including all four behavioural cases) rather than only passing against the new one. Unit tests that confirmed the author's mental model are what let this through in the first place, per failure mode E1.

Covers: both flags on, neither on, one on (independent resolution), ungated disciplines never gated, `getCompanyFeaturesWith` reading through the supplied client, and `gatingFrom` counting. Plus a source guard pinning the request-scoped helpers out of `compute.ts`, comment-stripped so it doesn't fire on the prose that explains it.

## Not in this PR

- Deleting the 104 affected snapshot rows. Separate scripted, logged repair for you to run.
- Making then-vs-now comparisons denominator-consistent, plus the false-`scorecard_dropped` bias measurement.
- Giving flag changes a history so "was this on as of date X" stays answerable.

## Manual verification

None needed before merge; the affected path is a cron. The first real signal is next Sunday's run, where the summary line should read a non-zero `N/M feature-gated disciplines enabled`. If it reads `0/M`, the fix did not land.

author: tokuhirom
body:
`make bundle` has been failing since the browser build went in:

```
failed to rename app binary target/release/ekanban-app: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The binary is `ekanban`, not `ekanban-app`. Tauri's CLI reads the `[[bin]]` tables to learn that name, and it skips any target carrying `required-features` — so with `required-features = ["shell"]` on ours there was nothing left to read and it fell back to the package name.

The `required-features` was there so that `--no-default-features` would not try to build a `main.rs` calling a `run` that the shell-less build does not have. Say that with `cfg` in `main.rs` instead: the binary target stays visible to the CLI, and without `shell` it compiles to an empty `main`.

Checked by hand:

- `make build && make bundle` produces `Ekanban.app` and `Ekanban_0.2.2_aarch64.dmg`
- `cargo build -p ekanban-app --no-default-features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` still builds

author: blandisc
body:
Sub-lote **A3c** del cuarto limpio: los últimos residuos de autoría heredada que quedaban en los paquetes propios, y las cadenas del catálogo de cuando el dato venía de una banda física. El compile de la app lo hace CI (etiqueta `ci-app`); aquí se verificó por paquete.

## Alcance A · residuos de paquetes

**Manifiestos reescritos con estructura propia:** `BiometricStreams`, `CenitStore`, `StrandAnalytics`, `StrandImport`, `StrandModels`.

Para probar que la reescritura no cambió el contrato, se comparó el manifiesto **resuelto** (`swift package dump-package`, no el texto) contra el de `origin/iOS`:

| paquete | manifiesto resuelto |
|---|---|
| BiometricStreams | idéntico |
| CenitStore | idéntico |
| StrandImport | idéntico |
| StrandModels | idéntico |
| StrandAnalytics | idéntico salvo el recurso nuevo (el oráculo de abajo) |

**Fuentes reescritas:** `DailyStressModel.swift` completo, y los remanentes de banda en `AppleLoadEstimator`, `Insight`, `InsightEngine`, `SessionRecoveryCost`, `SourceFusion`, `TrainingHabit` y `StrengthCSVImport`.

### El oráculo de `DailyStressModel`

`DailyStressModel` produce un número **persistido** (la serie `stress`): se relee semanas después como historia, dibuja la curva del detalle y alimenta el «tiempo en calma». Reescribirlo entero sin una reja de equivalencia sería reescribir en silencio lo que la persona ya vio.

Así que la reescritura viaja con su propio oráculo:

- `Resources/daily-stress-oracle.json` (60 casos) graba lo que respondía la implementación **anterior** para catorce historias sintéticas fijas y para la aritmética suelta. Se generó ejecutando el código de `origin/iOS` en una copia aislada del árbol — una corrida mecánica de equivalencia, sin leer la fuente heredada.
- `DailyStressOracleTests` sostiene la implementación nueva contra esas respuestas **bit a bit**: cada valor viaja como el texto decimal más corto que vuelve a leerse idéntico, así que no hay tolerancia que aflojar.
- `DailyStressOracleInputs` arma las entradas con aritmética entera y claves de día por calendario civil — sin `Date()`, sin `DateFormatter`, sin azar — y las comparte con el generador, para que las entradas no puedan separarse de lo grabado.

Los catorce escenarios cubren: una fuente, dos fuentes mezcladas (con las bases partidas de FER-623), huecos, valores guardados fuera de rango y con clave repetida, ancla de ayer, ancla vieja, base plana, arranque en frío, filas fantasma con fecha futura, sin señal, sólo guardado, sólo HRV, sólo pulso, e historia de 400 noches. Más una prueba que exige que **ningún caso grabado se quede sin comparar**.

**Comprobación de que el oráculo muerde:** cambiar la ventana de la línea base de 30 a 29 días lo hace fallar en 24 puntos. No pasa en vacío.

### Censo de autoría, antes → después

En los archivos de este lote, `git blame -w -M -C -C -C`:

| archivo | antes | después |
|---|---|---|
| `DailyStressModel.swift` | 74 | 1 |
| `Insight.swift` | 6 | 0 |
| `InsightEngine.swift` | 1 | 0 |
| `StrengthCSVImport.swift` | 4 | 0 |
| `AppleLoadEstimator` · `SessionRecoveryCost` · `TrainingHabit` | — | 0 |
| `SourceFusion.swift` | — | 2 |
| `Package.swift` (los cinco) | — | 3–7 |

Lo que queda no es expresión, es lo que no se puede escribir de otra forma: los preámbulos de manifiesto (`// swift-tools-version: 5.9`, `import PackageDescription`), las URL de dependencia (`GRDB.swift`, `ZIPFoundation`) con la sintaxis que SwiftPM exige, líneas en blanco y llaves de cierre.

Un commit aparte bajó `DailyStressModel` de 8 a 1: el promedio pasa a la expresión única que ya era, y la firma de `rawScore` —que es **contrato público** y no puede cambiar de etiquetas ni de tipos— se acomoda en dos renglones alineados. Sin cambio de comportamiento: el oráculo pasa igual.

## Alcance B · cero banda-dispositivo en el catálogo

Censo por clave sobre `Cenit/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` (los catálogos de widgets y reloj no tenían ninguna). De 53 apariciones de «band»/«banda», **29 eran del dispositivo y las 24 restantes son estadísticas** y se conservan.

**Regla aplicada:** «banda» de valores se queda (la banda de una gráfica, «dentro de tu banda», la banda 10–20 de series por semana, la banda de recuperación, las bandas de VO₂max). «Banda» como aparato se retira.

**Las 29 podadas, todas sin un solo consumidor en Swift** (verificado con `grep -rF` de la clave sobre `Cenit`, `CenitApp`, `CenitWatch`, `CenitWidgets`, `CenitShared`, y después sobre el árbol entero):

- **Estado del aparato:** `BAND`, `Band at %lld%%`, `Band disconnected during the day`, `Band with no signal`, `Band · last night`, `Band only`, `On the band:`, `The band has nothing new.`, `Aged baseline · 6+ days without band`, `No band data yet. Connect it in Live or import your history…`
- **El paso de onboarding que preguntaba si tenías una:** `Yes, I have one` (es: «Sí, tengo una banda»).
- **Lo que sólo la banda podía dar:** `The beat-to-beat tacogram only comes from the band…`
- **La calibración con el gemelo vivo:** `Restarts your calibration… (band change, an anomalous stretch).` — existe la misma clave sin la cláusula de banda, y ésa es la que usa `AjustesView`.
- **El emparejamiento BLE de la misma era:** `Bonded · idle`, `Bonded · streaming`, `Paired · idle`, `Live HR (not fully paired)`, `Connected. Finishing the secure pairing handshake…`, `Live heart rate only: finish secure pairing to save the rest`, `Previously paired but not currently connected…`, `Continue without pairing`, `Keep your iPhone's Bluetooth on.`, `Pair in Live`, `Pairing help: %@`, y las sondas del protocolo: `5/MG probes`, `5/MG probes, frames`, `5/MG protocol probes`, `Record 5/MG frames to a file`, `On a 5/MG connection Cénit sends a probe…`

No hubo bloque de UI muerto que retirar junto con ellas: las pantallas que las usaban ya no existen, por eso las claves estaban huérfanas.

**Cómo se editó:** poda **textual** del JSON, preservando formato y orden — nunca `json.dump`. El script valida que el JSON siga parseando, que las claves quitadas sean exactamente las pedidas y que **ninguna otra clave cambie de valor**. Diff: 471 líneas, todas borradas.

## Los tres pendientes del gate CSO sobre FER-400

1. **Las tres tarjetas de señal, tratadas igual.** Temperatura de piel dice «algo que podrías estar incubando» y SpO₂ dice «un resfriado»; respiración se había quedado sin la causa hedgeada y leía como si una subida sólo pudiera ser esfuerzo o cena. Ahora la nombra **al final**, como la última posibilidad.
2. **es-MX:** «vale la pena mencionarla con un médico» → «vale la pena **comentarla con tu médico**».
3. **`PreparacionDetailScreen.swift`:** la cita de método era el único `String` crudo del plegable, así que con el teléfono en español el método explicaba todo en español y cerraba en inglés. Pasa a `String(localized: "prep.metodo.cita", defaultValue:)` con su valor `es` (bajo la llave «es», nunca «es-MX»).

## Verificación

```
StrandAnalytics   Build complete!   Executed 1228 tests, 0 failures
StrandImport      Build complete!   Executed  219 tests, 0 failures
CenitStore        Build complete!   Executed  239 tests, 0 failures
BiometricStreams  Build complete!   Executed   18 tests, 0 failures
CenitDesign       Build complete!   Executed  623 tests, 0 failures

check-hardcoded-strings.py   ✅ no hardcoded non-English UI strings in 239 file(s)
check-xcstrings-emdash.py    ✅ sin em-dash en valores es
check-xcstrings-cycles.py    ✅ sin ciclos (5 catálogos)
check-xcstrings-es.py        ✅ self-test 14/14 · sin claves nuevas sin es · toda clave usada existe
check-band-copy.py           ✅ sobre CHANGELOG.md
Tools/verify.sh quick        verify: linters OK
```

Ambos archivos Swift de la capa app pasan `swiftc -frontend -parse`. **El compile completo de la app y `CenitUnitTests` los corre CI** con la etiqueta `ci-app`.

Ya mergeado `origin/iOS` (trae la deduplicación de claves de FER-473, #1565): sin conflicto, catálogo válido, gates y pruebas verdes después del merge.

author: moysesemanuel
body:
Reescreve a página pública `/planos` para quem vai comprar, e não para quem construiu o
produto.

## O texto estava escrito de dentro para fora

Não era um trecho isolado. Estavam na página pública, visíveis para o cliente:

- "Escolha o plano certo antes de liberar o acesso ao projeto"
- "A pessoa que vem da landing precisa cair aqui, escolher a faixa certa"
- "Quando a URL do plano estiver configurada, o CTA abre a assinatura do Mercado Pago (...)
  sem quebrar a navegação pública"
- "A página já substitui o checkout?", como pergunta do FAQ
- "A landing educa. A página pública de planos converte."

Isso descreve o funil e a arquitetura para a equipe. A frase sobre a URL do plano é pior que
jargão: descreve um fluxo interno de configuração para alguém que só quer saber quanto custa.

## O que muda

- Todo o texto passa a falar com o cliente: o que cada plano resolve, o que está incluído e
  quanto custa.
- As cores fixas em hex saíram; a página usa os tokens da landing, como o resto do funil.
- Um teste novo trava as duas coisas: falha se voltar qualquer hex fixo na página e se
  reaparecer alguma das frases internas.

## O Max continua na página

O título do commit diz "tira o Max da venda", e isso se refere **apenas ao botão de
assinatura**. O plano segue listado no card e na tabela comparativa, marcado como
`Em breve`. O mapa `purchasablePlans` controla isso, com a regra escrita no arquivo: não
comercializar antes de as automações e o ERP existirem — vender agora seria cobrar por
promessa.

Decisão de produto confirmada em 08/09/2026: o Max fica no catálogo e passa a ser vendido
quando o ERP e o site estiverem completos.

## Validação

Lint, typecheck, suíte e build passam. 400 testes, 0 falhas — cinco a mais, do arquivo novo.
`git diff --check` limpo. A branch foi rebaseada sobre a `main` atual, já com as PRs #67, #68
e #69.
