body:
## What

A watch party becomes its own kind of channel. Created with a name like `cinemoon` and an optional short description, joined by everyone as audience, with a stage only admins and mods (or whoever a cargo or channel overwrite grants it to) can take.

- **Shared**: channel type `watch_party`; `Permission.START_WATCH_PARTY` (bit 23; `PERMISSION_ALL` is now `16777215`). Admin, Manager and the seeded Moderator hold it by default, `@everyone` never does. One gate, `canStartWatchPartyStream`, decides the stage: START_WATCH_PARTY in a watch party, STREAM in a plain voice channel. `ChannelLiveState` is the seam for the HLS branch (below).
- **Server**: create/list/update tolerate the type; `createChannelSchema` gained an optional `topic`. The voice join and `resolveVoicePublish` (SFU token, live re-check) both compute `canStream` through the gate, so `set-sharing-screen` and `set-camera` refuse the audience. `schema.sql` widens `channels_type_check` and a one-shot backfill grants the bit to roles holding MANAGE_CHANNELS plus `system_key = 'moderator'`.
- **Client**: everything behind `VITE_WATCH_PARTY_CHANNELS` (default off, so production shows nothing until flipped; `?watchParty=1|0` latches it with the dev bypass). Create flow, a Watch party section, idle row with its own icon and the description, live row with a pulsing `AO VIVO` pill and viewer count (`motion-safe:` only). Audience sees only `Entrar`; the share and Watch party buttons follow the welcome's `canStream`. Roles UI and channel overwrites list the new bit. PT first, EN second.
- **Native**: iOS and Android decode `type` as a string, so nothing fails to parse; `isVoice` now includes `watch_party` on both so it lists and joins as a voice room. Android's `WireProtocolTest` mirrors the enum and was updated.
- **Docs**: `docs/WATCH_PARTY.md` (type, bit, gate, seam, flag, what the native apps still need).

## Seam for `fix/hls-watch-mode-loading`

`ChannelLiveState { live, presenterPeerId, viewerCount, startedAt, hlsUrl }` uses the same names as that branch's `LiveHlsStream`. On main it is derived from the roster (`liveStateFromRoster`). When the branch lands: the HLS egress start must read `peer.canStream` (not a second `type` check), and `voice-stream` should feed `ChannelLiveState` instead of the roster derivation (`TODO(hls)` marks the spot). Scheduling attaches to the channel; `TODO(schedule)` marks where the next session time renders.

## Tests

- `packages/shared/src/watch-party-channel.test.ts`: admin allowed, member denied (even with the everyday STREAM), overwrite flips it both ways.
- `server/src/ws/voice-watch-party.test.ts`: the same three through the WS join and `set-sharing-screen`, plus a plain voice room still sharing.
- `server/src/voice/speak.test.ts`: the gate in `resolveVoicePublish`.
- Client: flag resolver, sidebar row live/idle/flag-off, call controls hide the Watch party button for the audience, tristate/recipe/icon cases.

Each permission test was checked to fail with the gate removed (helper branch deleted: 6 failures; WS refusal deleted: 2 failures; client conditions inverted: each test failed).

Full server suite ran against a local DB (schema applied, 1701 passing; the 3 remaining need `server/dist`, which CI builds). Client: 2171 tests green, i18n check ok, typecheck clean.

## Not verified

Nothing was clicked in a browser: the pill, the create dialog's second field and the real welcome `canStream` flow are unproven visually. No Playwright run. Native apps were edited but not built.

## Merge notes

`restarts-api` (server + shared). Not `drops-voice`: the gate only changes what a joiner may claim in a `watch_party` room, which does not exist yet. Do not merge; Rafael reviews.

author: lucas-kohorst
body:
## What this adds

Turns the external plugin monorepo into a first-class install path and hardens the whole external-plugin surface for desktop and web.

### Plugin extraction surfaced for normal users
- The `gloomberb-plugins` monorepo is now a registered seed entry (`src/plugins/seed.ts`), so upgrades restore extracted plugins automatically; QA isolated homes seed from `EXTRACTED_PLUGINS` instead of a hardcoded partial list so they never try to clone the pack.

### Discovery (loader + marketplace)
- `listExternalPluginEntries` discovers plugins at the root, inside `<repo>/<plugin>`, and inside the conventional `<repo>/plugins/<plugin>` workspace, including symlinked monorepo roots. Nested packages carry `managementDirName`.
- The legacy plugin-market scan now reuses the loader walk instead of re-implementing it, so discovery cannot drift; dropped the dead `pluginId` field and the duplicated async `resolvePluginEntry`.
- The desktop bundle collector consumes the same discovery list, so TUI and desktop agree on which plugins exist.

### Marketplace management
- Installed external plugins are removable: `[x] uninstall` in the TUI footer with a confirmation dialog, and an Uninstall button on the desktop gallery.
- New renderer-neutral `PluginRemover` seam and `plugins.remove` RPC that deletes exactly the selected package directory (keeping the parent monorepo and sibling packages intact); built-ins are never removable.
- Removed the misleading "featured" dot from the desktop gallery.

### Desktop runtime fixes
- Bundler requests production JSX (`development: false`) and the host publishes the real `react/jsx-dev-runtime` with a production `jsx` fallback, fixing the `jsxDEV is not a function` crashes from workspace TSX on desktop.
- Robinhood keeps node-only HTTP out of browser bundles.

### QA
- New `bun run qa:plugins` runs every external plugin pane through Pilotty in an isolated home: 19 plugins load, 15 panes pass (Prediction Markets included after its watchlist fallback stability fix), registration-only plugins reported separately, quote/article/market probes green.

### Tests
- Nested + symlinked discovery (both layouts), market metadata mapping, exact-package uninstall, production JSX emission, jsxDEV fallback.

## Validation
- Focused suites green; scoped typechecks (electrobun-bun, opentui, electrobun-view, browser) green; external plugin repo: 196 tests + typecheck green; `qa:plugins` 15/15 panes; pre-push `qa --hook` green.

body:
Balance tables used separate full-width basis-date and observation-time columns, crowding amounts and balance kinds. Use one date column with both values explicitly labeled, while preserving their exact text and missingness. Current balances use five columns and history keeps a sixth lineage column.

Add deliberate column widths, captions, and named keyboard-scrollable regions. No financial values, date selection, filtering or backend behavior changes.

Validation: independent subagent review with no remaining findings; 8 layout cases / 161 assertions across local/central modes and 390/1280px, 5 production browser tests, typecheck and hk passed.

## Summary by Sourcery

Improve balance-table readability by consolidating labeled date context and refining responsive table accessibility without changing financial or backend behavior.

New Features:
- Combine balance basis dates and source observation times into one explicitly labeled date column while preserving stored values and missing values.
- Add named, keyboard-focusable scroll regions and captions to latest-balance and balance-history tables.

Enhancements:
- Set deliberate balance-table column sizing and improve date, source-account, amount, lineage, and detail presentation for narrow and wide screens.

Documentation:

author: kurcide
body:
Pasted reports could accidentally constrain memory recall to a timestamp contained in their evidence. A report quoting a verification time could therefore exclude its own canonical source when that source was recorded a few seconds earlier.

Temporal interpretation now separates clearly delimited evidence from the surrounding request. The complete original text remains available for lexical and semantic retrieval. Explicit date and time requests retain their existing meaning and precision; the repair does not widen observation windows or rewrite the query.

Validation covers neutral canonical report recall through the context API, evidence formats and genuine temporal requests. Final CI runs on this combined release head. Installed validation will repeat the unchanged failed operator invocation after backend cutover; its earlier failure remains retained. The native adapter and source-reference protocol are unchanged.

The existing outbox concurrency fixture now controls its callback and lease clocks so database scheduling cannot consume the intended blocked-delivery phase before it starts. It checks enqueue progress, unknown outcome, no premature retry and exactly one retry after lease expiry. Production outbox code and budgets are unchanged; separate real-clock deadline checks remain.

author: sirged
body:
## Summary

Wires up three server halves issue #293 found with no reader.

- **Upload receipt and refuse-or-replace.** `POST /api/upload` now refuses a same-named file with `409` naming the relative path, unless the request sends `replace=true`; the stored bytes are untouched until then. The receipt (`UploadOut`) now names the saved path and whether the call `replaced` an existing file. `Library.svelte` shows the path per upload and, on a 409, an inline conflict with a **Replace** control that resends with `replace=true`.
- **Practice page's Last 7 days.** `GET /api/practice/summary` (`week_seconds`, `week_sessions`, `top_scores`) had zero callers. The practice page's own "This week" section uses a preference-anchored *calendar* week, a genuinely different window from this route's rolling last-7-days - so rather than merge them, `Practice.svelte` renders a separate **Last 7 days** section from the route directly.
- **Vouched identity in the header.** When `GET /api/me` reports `enabled: true`, the sidebar shows the proxy-vouched `username` (or "no identity on this request" when none was carried); nothing renders when auth is off. The display logic is a pure `identityLabel()` function, unit-tested with both shapes.

### Premise re-derivation (measured against main 0d27896)

- Upload's missing existence check - **valid**. `dest.open("wb")` had no prior existence check; a same-named upload silently overwrote the file.
- Discarded `saved` receipt - **valid**. `Library.svelte`'s `onUpload` was `for (const f of files) await api.upload(f);` - the response was never read.
- Zero callers of `practiceSummary` - **valid**. `api.js` had the wrapper; nothing in `web/src` called it.
- No `/api/me` fetch anywhere - **valid**. Confirmed by grep.

### A design correction found by the shared-database verification pass

The first cut held a `replace` against `scanner.hold_library_still()`, reasoning it could overwrite a file a running scan is mid-read on. Running the full shared-browser-DB test set (per this repo's own verification discipline) surfaced that two existing specs (`viewer-practice.spec.js`, `zzzzzz-score-metadata.spec.js`) deliberately re-upload the same fixture path every test - a legitimate pattern the hold made flaky. On reflection, a replace only ever writes at a path *the request itself named*, never one discovered by walking the library, so it cannot invalidate a scan's listing the way a move or delete can - the same exemption a fresh upload already has. Dropped the hold; updated the two specs to pass `replace=true` explicitly (which is what they mean); replaced the now-wrong "refused while scanning" test with one proving the opposite.

### Mutation testing (all reverted afterward)

| Removed / broken | Test that went red |
| --- | --- |
| The `existed and not replace` 409 check | `test_uploading_the_same_name_twice_is_refused_with_409_naming_the_path` |
| The `replaced` field (forced to `False`) | `test_replace_true_overwrites_and_the_receipt_says_so` |
| Reintroducing `hold_library_still` on replace | `test_a_replace_is_also_not_held_against_a_running_scan` |
| `identityLabel`'s `enabled` check | unit test "nothing is shown when reverse-proxy auth is off" |
| `api.practiceSummary()` fetch (stubbed to zeros) | new practice.spec.js browser test |
| `Library.svelte`'s receipt/conflict handling (reverted to discarding the response) | new zzz-library-organise.spec.js browser test |

### Verification

- Server suite: `1429 passed, 92 skipped` (unchanged skip count), `FERMATA_TEST_LIBRARY` unset, `web/node_modules` absent for that run.
- `npm run build` before every browser run; `web/tests/spec-floors/*` gained three new entries (never edited existing ones).
- Shared-database browser rule: ran `navigation.spec.js`, `practice.spec.js`, and every spec sorting after it that asserts emptiness or an exact count (`scope-presets`, `score-compare-disclosures`, `score-compare-warnings`, `score-editor-native-262`, `score-editor-range-251`, `viewer-practice`, `zz-library-missing`, `zzz-library-organise`, `zzzz-library-auto-transcribe`, `zzzz-library-transcribe-batch`, `zzzz-score-progress`, `zzzzz-setlists`, `zzzzzz-score-metadata`) together, in that order, on a private port: **158/159 passed**.
- The one failure (`zzz-library-organise.spec.js`'s pre-existing "practice on a deleted score still counts" test) is **not caused by this change** - confirmed by re-running it against fully unmodified `Practice.svelte`, `api.py` and `api_models.py` in this environment, where it fails identically. It's a timezone-dependent gap: this machine is UTC-6 and past midnight UTC, so a session logged with no explicit `local_date` lands on tomorrow's UTC date, outside `practice/history`'s 90-day window ending at the browser's local "today" - the same class of bug this codebase's `local_date_source` field exists to name, just untested here since this particular spec doesn't pin a timezone. Left alone as out of scope for this bet.

## Test plan

- [x] `server/tests/test_scanner.py` - refuse/replace/not-held-against-a-scan, mutation-verified
- [x] `server/tests/test_api_doc_prose.py`, `test_api_docs.py` - green
- [x] `web/tests/unit/identity.spec.js` - both shapes, mutation-verified
- [x] `web/tests/browser/zzz-library-organise.spec.js` - real file-input upload/conflict/replace flow
- [x] `web/tests/browser/practice.spec.js` - Last 7 days renders the route's own totals
- [x] Full server suite: 1429 passed / 92 skipped (baseline-matching)
- [x] Ordered shared-DB browser set: 158/159 (one pre-existing, unrelated, environment-specific flake)

## After review

Fixed the flake named above rather than leaving it out of scope: `GET /api/practice/summary` now accepts an optional `today` query parameter, parsed and defaulted exactly the way `GET /api/practice/history` already does, and computes its window as `today` and the six local days before it instead of `date('now')` (UTC). `Practice.svelte` and `api.js` pass the browser's local date the same way the history call does. Added a server test (sessions on eight consecutive local days, mutation-verified against a revert to `date('now')`) and updated `docs/practice-data.md`.

The flake itself was `zzz-library-organise.spec.js`'s practice POSTs, several of which never sent `local_date` and so were stamped with the server's UTC date - dropping them from the practice page's local-day window on a machine west of Greenwich after 18:00 local. All four are fixed to pass `local_date` the way `Viewer.svelte` does.

Nits: `Library.svelte`'s `onUpload` now clears the stale `notice` at the start of each upload batch, so a batch that 409s on every file no longer shows a leftover "Saved as ..." beside the conflict sentence (browser test updated to assert the receipt is gone in that case); the upload route now creates the destination folder only after the existing-file check passes, so a refused upload into a brand-new folder leaves nothing behind; dropped a dead `str()` around an already-string path; and the identity tag (which renders on the library page only) no longer carries a deployment-jargon `title` attribute.

author: memocobos
body:
## Por qué el puente va antes que el botón

Medido en las dos bases:

| KameHouse | | Portal | |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| `viajeros_evento` | **2,447** | `clientes` | **1** |
| con correo | **1,318** | walk-ins por reclamar | **0** |
| | | `solicitudes_tour` · `pagos` · `lugares` | **0 · 0 · 0** |

`portal-reclamar-cuenta` solo enlaza a quien se registra si encuentra una fila de `clientes` con **su** correo. Sin puente, la invitación llevaba a ~1,900 personas a un portal que no las reconoce.

## Qué entra

- **`admin-portal-puente`** — POST `{evento_id, accion:'vista_previa'|'ejecutar'}`. Agrupa **por correo**, da de alta el walk-in y escribe `portal_cliente_id` en **todas** las filas de esa persona. Vista previa con **nombres y motivos**.
- **`portal-mi-plan-migrado`** — sirve el plan **leyendo** KameHouse, con la **misma `saldoMigrado`** del Palacio. Candado del correo verificado, igual que `portal-reclamar-cuenta`.
- **`portal.html`** — la sección que lo pinta. Nace oculta, fail-soft estricto. Un puente que nadie ve es la pantalla inalcanzable de COB-MIG-1 otra vez.
- **`_lib/correo-forma`** — la forma del correo y la talla, en **una** fuente; `admin-invitar-walkin` ya la usa.

## 🔒 Cero escrituras de dinero

`admin-saldos` suma los `pagos` en estado `'pagado'` como **entradas de caja**, y el dinero migrado ya lo cuenta `saldoMigrado`. Copiarlo lo contaría **dos veces**. Por eso el plan se **sirve**, no se copia.

## Una corrección al diseño aprobado

**`viajeros_evento.usuario_id` no era el enlace al Portal: es el del STAFF.** El único valor puesto apunta a `usuarios` (Victor, coordinador). El diseño de MIG-1 decía que ahí iría la invitación — reusarla habría metido dos significados en una columna. El enlace es la columna nueva `portal_cliente_id`.

## Las dos trampas, resueltas leyendo la base

- **`numero_cliente`** lo asigna el trigger `clientes_before_insert` con `nextval('numero_cliente_seq')` cuando llega null → el puente lo **omite**. Ese trigger también baja el correo a minúsculas, que es la llave del dedup (`clientes.correo` es **UNIQUE**).
- **`talla_playera`** tiene `CHECK` de XS…XXL en el Portal y es **texto libre** en viajeros: se normaliza o va **null**. Una talla rara haría que la base rechace **esa fila sola** y el puente perdería a esa persona en silencio.

## El careo — `npm run mide:puente-portal`

```
[1] vista previa        escrituras: 0 · se saltan CON NOMBRE Y MOTIVO
                        · Beto Paz — sin correo en su fila
                        · Cris Mora — el correo no tiene forma de correo
[2] ejecutar            solicitudes_tour Δ 0   ·   pagos Δ 0
                        tablas escritas: pt:clientes, kh:viajeros_evento
[3] trampas             Ana: 2 filas → 1 cuenta · 2/2 marcadas · talla «m» → M
                        Dani (ya existía): enlazada, sin cuenta nueva
[4] segundo clic        4 escrituras → 0
[5] CONTROL POSITIVO    handler saboteado que sí escribe un pago → Δ 1
✅ VERDE · 21 aserciones, 0 en rojo
```

Entra por el **handler real** y simula un salto más adentro; la base falsa respeta filtros, guarda estado, usa los nombres reales y **modela el trigger**. El Δ 0 mide **el hecho**, no un grep — y el control positivo prueba que el contador sabe ponerse rojo.

`portal.html` se verificó **en el navegador** (`node --check` no es autoridad en un archivo así): módulo ejecutado, 0 errores de página, sección oculta al nacer — y el probe se validó saboteando el archivo y comprobando por sha1 que mutó.

## Lo que falta

- **MIG-1d-ii**, el botón que invita. Antes del primer envío real, **el render del correo pasa por visto de Jane y Memo**.
- **El primer evento real lo eliges tú, y chico**: el puente inserta en una base que hoy tiene 1 fila; `dalemix` metería ~156 de golpe.

author: holyscotsman
body:
FIXBRIEF_1 · Fix 2. The app reported "this machine has no LibreOffice" on a Windows Server that has LibreOffice installed on it.

It was looking on PATH, and the Windows installer does not put it there. What the app knew was *"I did not find it where I looked"*, and what it said was a claim about the machine.

## More places

`NVCX_SOFFICE_PATH` ahead of everything, then PATH, then the Windows install directories, the registry key the installer writes (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\LibreOffice\UNO\InstallPath`), the Linux package paths, and the macOS bundle.

An override that points at nothing is reported wrong rather than quietly falling through to a different LibreOffice — somebody who typed a path meant it, and silently using another one is how a deck converts against the wrong version for a year.

## The console entry point

`soffice.exe` is the GUI entry point: it hands the work to a background process and exits 0 **before the PDF exists**, so the conversion "succeeds" and the file is not there. `soffice.com` blocks. The search asks for `.com` first; an override naming the `.exe` is corrected to the `.com` beside it, because `.exe` is what Explorer shows and what a person types.

## The refusal is about the search, not the machine

```
LibreOffice was not found, so a .pptx cannot be converted here.

Export the deck as a PDF instead (File → Export as PDF) and upload that —
it renders with nothing to install, and every slide comes through.

If LibreOffice IS installed on this machine, it is somewhere this looked
past. Set NVCX_SOFFICE_PATH to the full path of soffice (soffice.com on
Windows) and try again.

Looked in:
  · the NVCX_SOFFICE_PATH setting
  · soffice.com on PATH
  ...
```

A reader with LibreOffice installed uses that list to find which of those places their install is not in.

## One message, one box

The panel had its own copy of this sentence — shorter, worded differently, ending elsewhere — and a rejected `.pptx` put both up at once, in two colours. The listing endpoint now carries `converter_message` **instead of** the `converter_available` boolean, so there is no second record of the fact to disagree with, and the refusal carries `reason: "no_converter"` so the panel can tell that rejection from every other one.

## Two Windows faults found by reading, since the Linux path proves neither

- **The profile directory was not a URL.** `f"file://{profile}"` writes `file://C:\Users\svc\...` on Windows. LibreOffice does not report that — it ignores the setting and falls back to the shared profile, which under a service account does not exist, so the conversion fails with nothing readable to show for it. Now `as_uri()`, and tested through a `PureWindowsPath` so the Windows answer can be asked for from any machine.
- **A zero-byte PDF counted as a conversion.** The check only asked whether a `.pdf` existed. Rendering it then failed with a pdfium error, instead of the sentence soffice had printed saying what actually went wrong.

## How it was checked

- 32 new backend tests (`test_soffice.py`), plus 4 browser tests (`csp-converter.spec.ts`)
- **19 backend mutations, all caught.** Two survived a first sweep and both were real holes: `_prefer_console` never fired on the search path (the name order already handled it, so it moved to the override where it earns its keep), and the API's `reason` was untested end-to-end.
- **5 frontend mutations, all caught.** One survived twice and was not a flake: `toHaveCount(1)` was being satisfied *before the upload's response arrived*, so the spec was asserting the absence of a box that had not had time to appear. It now waits for the POST.
- The panel was rendered and looked at. `pre-line` collapsed the indent under "Looked in:", putting the bullets further left than the line introducing them; it is `pre-wrap` now.

## Not done, deliberately

LibreOffice is not made a requirement. The PDF route stays, and it is what the message leads with.

[Linear CAK-267](https://linear.app/ctrl-alt-keith/issue/CAK-267/use-an-agent-need-test-to-prevent-prompt-bloat)

## Gateway evidence

Source wording was inspected at base `407277992c64935a31199d9b0b40ce491683f71f`; the continuation starts from reviewed head `92bb19ab807376b4adb9cad1d6de271b137c55b0`.

| Active gateway | Concrete bypass | Result |

| `docs/feature-lifecycle.md#contract-tests` | Advice to add tests/checks/examples and stable-substring assertions can freeze incidental guidance wording despite the baseline's narrower coverage policy. | Retain “Write or update”; select coverage through Test Value and Documentation Validation. |
| `docs/feature-lifecycle.md#capture` | A lesson-recording step leaves placement and promotion content implicit, letting delivery history become runtime guidance. | Record in existing issue/PR/notes/evidence surfaces; route proposed Playbook changes through Doctrine Promotion and Promotion Criteria. |

| `docs/trust-topology.md#promotion-guidance` | “Keep only the reusable part” and “include enough context” admit reusable explanations/cases into runtime guidance without the existing content-selection boundary. | Select content through Promotion Criteria; retain project-detail, tracking, and validation obligations. Optional trust vocabulary stays optional. |
| `docs/playbook-integrity-check.md#review-questions` | This review is explicitly used for new capture docs, but reusable/proven/core-model-explanatory/actionable content can pass its questions while carrying non-operative rationale. | Apply Agent-Read Documentation to agent-read sections before using the existing review questions; human-facing explanation remains eligible. |

Each added gateway actively chooses or reviews incoming guidance, has a current content-selection bypass, and can close it through an existing owner. These are source-supported mechanisms, not a claim that future prose reduction has been measured. No new framework, rubric, checklist, scoring, lint, test, or broader compression pass is introduced.

## Inspected and unchanged

- `docs/prompts.md` already activates the agent-read owner and treats templates as adaptable envelopes, not wholesale checklists; `docs/prompt-contracts.md` forbids hydrating whole doctrine/history.
- Doctrine Promotion, Review Packet, and external-review finding disposition already keep evidence/history outside doctrine and preserve the human decision.
- `docs/alignment-checkpoints.md` asks when capture is needed and explicitly operates alongside the lifecycle; its content path is now governed by the existing Capture owner.
- `docs/ai-workflow-ecosystem.md` gives discovery/scaling direction, not an alternate content-selection procedure. Its reusable-lesson sketch does not justify another local promotion rule.
- Starter bootstrap, AGENTS/review/notes templates, and upstream refresh preserve local authority, adaptation, source inspection, and separate human reports; refresh explicitly reads the engineering baseline. No concrete additional content bypass was established.
- Adapter authoring instructions already limit executor-specific deltas and route shared doctrine to owners. Maintenance reports recurring contract gaps for separately authorized doctrine work rather than adopting findings into its prompt.
- Notes cleanup runs after promotion; onboarding refresh keeps inventory/configuration with their owners. Historical/candidate architecture material and human rationale are outside this pass.

Canonical `make check` passed on `ff6e7d3c80135c50c8c9d6eea61f34b7cfd7ac72`: 18 Recovery tests, byte-identical generated Recovery, Markdown lint, and 249 tests. Both hosted checks passed on this head; the worktree is clean and PR mergeable against current main.

body:
## ทำไม

หน้าจอใน mockup (ข้อ 4, 6, 7) คือ **เว็บแอป LIFF ไม่ใช่การ์ดในแชต** — Flex Message วาดกราฟโดนัทไม่ได้ และไม่มีแถบเมนูล่าง นั่นคือเหตุผลที่ในแชตไม่เคยขึ้นแบบนั้น PR นี้จึงทำหน้า LIFF ให้เป็นแอปตามรูป

## 4 แท็บ

| แท็บ | เนื้อหา |
|---|---|
| 🏠 **งานวันนี้** | ยอดวันนี้ + เทรนด์เทียบเมื่อวาน · การ์ดรายประเภทงาน · **กราฟโดนัท SVG** สัดส่วนงานวันนี้ พร้อม legend · รายการล่าสุด |
| 📊 **สรุปรายการ** | เลือก วันนี้ / 7 วัน / เดือนนี้ · ยอดรวม, รับแล้ว, ค้างรับ, เฉลี่ยต่อบิล · โดนัทตามประเภท · งานยอดสูงสุด |
| 📋 **งานค้างรับ** | งานที่ยังไม่ได้รับเงิน + ยอดค้างรวม |
| ⚙️ **ตั้งค่า** | บัญชีที่ใช้อยู่ + วิธีพิมพ์งานแบบย่อ |

**แก้ไขรายการ** ตาม mockup ข้อ 6 — รายละเอียด, ลูกค้า, ประเภทงาน/หมวด (dropdown), สถานะการเงิน, จำนวนเงิน, รับมาแล้ว, วันที่, หมายเหตุ, ยกเลิกรายการ

## การเปลี่ยนแปลงฝั่งเซิร์ฟเวอร์

- **`GET /api/report?period=daily|weekly|monthly`** — ใช้ `buildReport()` และ `breakdownByCategory()` เดิม ผ่านการตรวจ token เหมือน endpoint อื่น (ไม่มี token → 401)
- สีของหมวดที่ API ส่งมาชนะ palette ในหน้าเว็บ

## การทดสอบ

- `npm test` → **84/84 ผ่าน**
- เรนเดอร์จริงด้วย Chromium (Playwright) โดย stub API: ตรวจครบทั้ง 4 แท็บ + หน้าแก้ไข **ไม่มี console error**
- บูตเซิร์ฟเวอร์: `/app/` → 200, `/api/report` ไม่มี token → 401 ✅

## ต้องตั้งค่าก่อนใช้

หน้านี้จะเปิดได้เมื่อตั้ง env `LIFF_ID` แล้ว (ขั้นตอนอยู่ใน DEPLOYMENT.md) — ถ้ายังไม่ตั้ง บอตทำงานครบเหมือนเดิมทุกอย่าง

author: lshdainty
body:
QA 2026-09-08 **#99 — 앱에서 칸을 비워 저장해도 안 비워진다** (높음·필수).
desk-back **#321**(QA #96, "키 없음=유지 · null=지움 · 값=교체")의 클라이언트 몫이다.

## 증상

앱 → 메모 열기 → 본문 지우고 저장 → 다시 열면 본문 그대로. 메모만이 아니다.
할 일 메모·기한, 저축목표 목표일, 거래 설명·거래처·결제수단·할부·외화 3종,
자산 메모·한도·결제일·결제 계좌가 전부 같았다.

원인은 앱이 본문을 Dart 의 널 인지 맵 엔트리(`'key': ?value`)로 만든 것이다.
값이 null 이면 **키째 빠진다.** 종전엔 서버가 "키 없음" 도 null 로 덮어 **우연히**
지워졌는데, 서버가 세 상태를 가르기 시작하자 옛 값이 그대로 남게 됐다.

## 무엇을 했나

`lib/core/network/patch.dart` — 서버의 같은 이름 타입과 짝인 `Patch<T>` 를 뒀다.

| 호출부 | 본문 | 뜻 |
|---|---|---|
| `Patch.keep()` (기본값) | 키가 없다 | 건드리지 마라 |
| `Patch.set(null)` | `"key": null` | 지워라 |
| `Patch.set(값)` | `"key": 값` | 이 값으로 바꿔라 |

## 제일 큰 위험 — 화면에 없는 칸까지 null 로 실으면 안 된다

**어느 칸을 비울 수 있는지는 화면만 안다.** 그래서 판단을 리포지토리가 아니라 호출부로
올렸다. 자산 수정은 계좌·카드·투자 **세 화면이 한 메서드를 나눠 쓰는데** 셋이 가진 칸이
서로 다르다 — 리포지토리가 일괄로 "비었으면 지운다" 를 정하면, 메모 칸이 없는 카드
화면에서 저장할 때마다 계좌 화면에서 적어 둔 메모가 사라진다.

가른 기준은 **"사용자가 이 화면에서 그 칸을 비울 수 있나"** 하나다.

**싣는다 (화면이 소유 · 비울 수 있다)**

| 도메인 | 칸 |
|---|---|
| 메모 | `content` |
| 할 일 | `content` · `dueDate` |
| 저축목표 | `deadlineDate` |
| 거래 | `assetRowId` · `description` · `merchant` · `paymentMethod` · `installmentMonths` · `originalAmount` · `originalCurrency` · `exchangeRate` |
| 자산 | `memo` · `exchangeRate` · `creditLimit` · `paymentDay` · `paymentAssetRowId` (각 화면이 자기 것만) |

**안 싣는다 (키를 뺀다)**

| 칸 | 왜 |
|---|---|
| 저축목표 `description` · `linkedAssetRowId` | 앱 편집 화면에 **칸이 아예 없다.** 웹에서 적어 둔 값이 지워진다 |
| 거래 `refundOfExpenseRowId` | 환불 연결은 **새 환불을 만들 때만** 정해진다. 편집 시트에 칸이 없어 null 로 실으면 환불 거래를 한 번 고칠 때마다 원거래 연결이 끊겨 통계 상계가 사라진다 |
| 자산 `color` | 앱 어느 화면에도 없다(웹에서만 고른다) |
| 자산 `institution` · `cardCatalogRowId` | 고르는 칸이라 **떼는 조작이 없다.** 값이 없으면 원래 없던 것이다 |
| 자산 `balance` | null 이 "지운다" 가 아니라 "보유로 서버가 평가액을 산정해 달라" 다 |
| 제목 · 종류 · 금액 · 통화 · 우선순위 · 아이콘 · 색 · 합계 포함 | 화면이 늘 값을 들고 있어 비워질 일이 없다(기본값이 있거나 빈 값을 막는다) |
| `splits` · `holdings` · `tagIds` · `sortOrder` | "null=미변경 · 리스트=교체" 로 뜻이 이미 확정됐다(QA #87 · #91). 손대지 않았다 |

**생성(POST) 경로는 건드리지 않았다** — "안 보냄 = 유지" 는 수정에만 있는 뜻이다.
(초안에서 한 번 create 본문까지 바뀌었는데 analyzer 가 잡았고 되돌렸다. 테스트에도
도메인마다 "생성 경로는 그대로다" 를 박아 뒀다.)

## `""` 와 `null` — 어느 쪽으로 맞출까

웹은 빈 칸을 `""` 로 보내고 그것도 동작한다. **앱은 `null` 로 간다.**

서버 코드를 읽어 확인한 것:

- `MemoServiceImpl.updateMemo` 는 `command.content().orKeep(...)` 으로 **받은 값을 그대로**
  넘기고, `Memo.updateMemo` 도 그대로 덮는다. 빈 문자열을 null 로 접는 자리가 update 경로
  어디에도 없다(`NameNormalizer` 는 라벨·보유 이름에만 쓴다). 즉 **DB 에 `''` 와 `NULL` 이
  다르게 남는다.**
- 그런데 `""` 는 "지움" 의 **공통 표현이 될 수 없다.**
  - `color` 는 `@Pattern("^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$")` 라 `""` 가 **400** 이다(`ColorFormat`).
  - `deadlineDate`·`creditLimit`·`paymentDay`·`installmentMonths`·`originalAmount`·
    `exchangeRate`·`paymentAssetRowId`·`assetRowId` 는 날짜·숫자·아이디 칸이라 빈
    문자열이라는 값 자체가 없다.
  - 즉 `""` 로 가면 앱이 칸 타입마다 다른 "지움 토큰" 을 알아야 한다.
- `null` 은 모든 타입에서 통하고, **서버가 "지움" 이라고 이름 붙인 것도 null 이다**
  (`Patch` javadoc, `AbsentAwareOptionalModule`).

두 클라이언트가 만든 값이 `''` / `NULL` 로 갈리는 건 남는다. 그건 **웹을 null 로 옮기거나
서버가 update 경로에서 빈 문자열을 null 로 접어** 맞출 일이다 — 이 PR 범위 밖이라
아래 후속으로 적어 둔다. (앱·웹 둘 다 읽을 때 `content ?? ''` 로 접어 보여 주므로
지금 화면에는 차이가 안 보인다. 갈리는 건 DB 와 `IS NULL`·`COALESCE` 를 쓰는 쪽이다.)

## 검증 — 네거티브 컨트롤 포함

에뮬레이터를 못 쓰므로(QA #23) 저장 페이로드를 테스트로 고정했다. **352 tests passed**
(main 329 + 23).

- `test/features/put_clear_payload_test.dart` (신규) — 다섯 도메인 수정 본문을 실제로 재
  "지우는 쪽"(키가 실리고 값이 null)과 **"안 건드리는 쪽"(키가 아예 없다)** 을 둘 다 고정
- `test/features/memo/memo_edit_dialog_test.dart` (신규) — QA 재현 그대로. 본문을 지우고
  저장 버튼을 눌러 화면이 실제로 무엇을 넘기는지 본다
- `test/features/asset/card_add_dialog_test.dart` — 신용→체크 전환 저장에서 한도·결제일이
  명시적 null 로 실린다 + **이 화면에 없는 메모는 안 실린다**
- `test/features/asset/account_add_dialog_test.dart` — 메모를 지우고 저장 + **이 화면에
  없는 결제일·결제 계좌는 안 실린다**

수정을 되돌렸을 때 실제로 깨지는지 다섯 갈래로 확인했다.

| 되돌린 것 | 깨진 테스트 |
|---|---|
| ① 리포지토리 본문을 `?value`(옛 동작)로 | 다섯 도메인의 "명시적 null 로 실린다" 5건 |
| ② 리포지토리가 `present` 검사 없이 항상 키를 싣게 | "안 넘긴 칸은 키가 없다" (메모·자산) 2건 |
| ③ 화면에 없는 칸(`description`·`linkedAssetRowId`·`refundOfExpenseRowId`·`tagIds`)을 싣게 | "키가 없다" 3건 |
| ④ 화면 호출부를 "널이면 안 보낸다" 로 | 메모·계좌·카드 위젯 테스트 3건 |
| ⑤ 화면이 자기 것 아닌 칸(`memo`·`paymentDay`)을 싣게 | "이 화면에 없는 칸은 안 실린다" 2건 |

게이트: `dart format --set-exit-if-changed lib test` ✅ · `flutter analyze lib/` **0 issues** ✅ ·
`TZ=Asia/Seoul flutter test` **352 passed** ✅. arb 를 안 만져 `gen-l10n` 은 불필요.

## 강제 업데이트 하한 — **안 올린다** (`minBuildNumber: 0` 유지)

기준은 "새 버전이 더 좋다" 가 아니라 **"옛 버전이 위험하다"** 다.

- 옛 앱은 **더 적게 보낼 뿐** 틀린 값을 흘리지 않는다. 지우기가 안 먹을 뿐 잘못된 값이
  DB 에 남지 않는다
- **실패가 눈에 보인다.** 안 지워진 값은 방금 편집한 그 화면에 그대로 다시 뜬다 —
  사용자가 "저장이 안 됐네" 로 알아챈다
- 돈이 잘못 움직이지 않는다. 신용→체크 전환 뒤 남는 `payment_day` 를 확인했는데,
  자동 결제 배치는 `assetRepository.findAllByType(CREDIT_CARD)` 로만 돌아
  체크카드의 낡은 결제일은 아무 일도 하지 않는다
- 서버가 옛 요청을 계속 받는다. API 제거·필수 파라미터 추가·타입 축소가 없다

반반이면 "실패가 보이느냐" 로 가른다는 규칙 그대로, **보이는 쪽**이라 안 올린다.

body:
Part of a triage pass across the creator/income repo family.

**Fix 1 — skill filename casing.** Three skill modules (`worker-integration`, `ai-architecture`, `worker-benchmarks`) were stored as lowercase `skill.md` instead of the canonical `SKILL.md`. `scripts/verify-public-surface.mjs` matches the filename exactly, so all three were silently excluded from the published skill count and from the directory-package convention CLAUDE.md documents. author: fametrano
body:
Closes no issue, deliberately: a small single-purpose correction in the
shape `11b5134` landed in.

`git ls-files` merges the index with the working directory and never
reads a commit — its own manual's first sentence — and `--with-tree`
does not change that, being documented only for use with
`--error-unmatch`. `CLAUDE.md`'s executable-bit rule was checked with
`git ls-files -s | awk '$1 == "100755" { print $4 }'`, and that bullet's
own words are that it states "the rule and not a description of today's
tree". A rule about the committed tree, checked against the index.

Measured in a scratch repository: a file committed at `100644`, then
`chmod 755`'d and staged but never committed, reads as `100755` under
the old command and answers empty under `git ls-tree -r HEAD`. So a mode
change a session staged and never committed reads back as the tree's
own. Three people reproduced this independently — the coder, the
reviewer of the branch this was split from, and the reviewer of this
one.

The two commands answer identically on a clean tree, which is what
leaves the prose beside the command true; a control confirms that
comparison could have shown a difference had there been one.

The four-ways launcher-name comparison higher up in the same file keeps
`git ls-files`, and the other call sites in the tree keep it too. They
ask which files exist in the working set, where an uncommitted sibling
is the state worth seeing rather than a false negative to guard against.

This is the second half of a branch that originally carried it beside
the [ISS 524](https://github.com/btclib-org/portanode/issues/524) fix.
Local review refused that bundle on `REVIEWING.md`'s own first check —
"the whole of them, and nothing beside" — and was right; the bundling
was an orchestration mistake rather than the coder's. The ISS 524 half
landed alone as [PR 527](https://github.com/btclib-org/portanode/pull/527),
and this was rebuilt on top of it rather than rebased, `CHANGELOG.md`
being `merge=union`.

Reviewed at fresh context: `CLEARED ed648ceccfd760b918b3c5bfe961d8b66a9ecdeb`.

author: rriveras
body:
## Qué cambia

Dos líneas de build. No hay cambios en `src/`.

1. **`rollup.config.mjs`** — se añade una segunda configuración que emite **un archivo por módulo** en `dist/esm/`, con `preserveModules: true`. Cada índice publicable (50 componentes, 2 contextos, 14 hooks, 11 utils) se declara como entrada, porque con una sola entrada `preserveModules` poda los re-exports intermedios y emitiría módulos incompletos (`dist/esm/components/DCard/index.js` se quedaría sin `DCardHeader`/`DCardBody`/`DCardFooter`).
2. **`package.json`** — `module` pasa de `./dist/index.esm.js` a `./dist/esm/index.js`. Es el único campo que cambia.

Y aparte, la eliminación de `jspdf`, que estaba declarado como dependencia y no se importa en ninguna parte.

## Qué NO cambia

- **La API pública.** Mismos exports, mismos tipos, mismas props. Cero archivos de `src/` tocados.
- **CommonJS.** `main` sigue apuntando a `dist/index.js`, que se emite igual que antes. `require('@dynamic-framework/ui-react')` devuelve los mismos 105 exports.
- **`dist/index.esm.js`.** El archivo único ESM **se conserva**: `publish-cdn.js` hace `aws s3 sync ./dist/`, así que es un artefacto publicado en el CDN y puede haber consumidores que lo referencien por ruta física o por URL.
- **El CSS.** `dist/css/dynamic-ui.css` y `.min.css` salen byte a byte idénticos.
- **Los tipos.** `dist/types/` sin cambios.
- **`sideEffects`.** Se queda en `["*.css"]`. Ya declaraba que todo el JavaScript de la librería es libre de efectos; es exactamente lo que hace falta, y además protege el CSS de ser podado.
- **Las rutas del paquete.** El tarball pasa de **413 a 765 archivos y no elimina ninguna**. Verificado comparando los listados completos de ambos paquetes:

  ```
  $ comm -23 files-antes.txt files-despues.txt
  (vacío)
  ```

  Las 352 rutas nuevas están todas bajo `dist/esm/`.

**No se añade un mapa `exports`.** Cerraría toda ruta no listada —lo que convertiría esto en un cambio *breaking*— y la medición mostró que aporta 532 bytes brotli sobre `preserveModules` a secas. No compensa.

## Por qué

El ESM publicado era un archivo único, así que todos los `import` de terceros de su cabecera se cargaban sin condición. Un bundler puede descartar *bindings* sin usar, pero conserva el `import` en sí para cualquier paquete que no declare `"sideEffects": false` — que es el caso de `html2canvas`, `@splidejs`, `google-libphonenumber` (CJS puro), `react-international-phone`, `react-responsive-pagination`, `currency.js` y más. Un widget que nunca usaba `DVoucher`, `DCarousel`, `DSelect` ni `DInputPhone` los empaquetaba igual.

### Widget real del template v1.2.0

Mismo código de librería en ambos lados; lo único que cambia es el empaquetado.

| | Antes | Después | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `main.js` raw | 2 170 150 B | **1 005 688 B** | **−53,7 %** |
| `main.js` gzip | 539 234 B | 290 393 B | −46,1 % |
| `main.js` brotli | 441 720 B | **240 328 B** | **−45,6 %** |
| `main.css` | 1 278 396 B | 1 278 396 B | sin cambio |

### Lighthouse móvil — mediana de 5 corridas intercaladas

| Métrica | 1 instancia | 3 instancias |
|---|---|---|
| LCP | 3 767 → **3 165 ms** (−16,0 %) | 8 266 → **4 967 ms** (−39,9 %) |
| TTI | 4 034 → 3 166 ms (−21,5 %) | 8 284 → 4 969 ms (−40,0 %) |
| Bootup de JS | 93 → 57 ms (−38,2 %) | 243 → 58 ms (−76,0 %) |
| Trabajo de main thread | 325 → 224 ms (−31,1 %) | 708 → 429 ms (−39,4 %) |
| Score de performance | 81 → 87 | 58 → 69 |
| JS sin usar | 150 287 → 61 840 B (−58,9 %) | 450 887 → 185 544 B (−58,8 %) |

Los dos bundles se sirvieron en paralelo en puertos distintos y cada ronda midió base e inmediatamente después la rama, para que la deriva de la máquina afectara a ambos por igual. **La rama gana las 10 comparaciones pareadas de LCP, sin excepción.** Las medianas del base reproducen el baseline documentado de v1.2.0 (3 766 y 8 266 ms).

### Dependencias que salen del bundle del widget

`google-libphonenumber` (570 827 B), `html2canvas` (363 899 B), `react-select` (125 700 B) y `@splidejs/react-splide` (83 673 B), más `react-international-phone`, `react-responsive-pagination`, `@floating-ui`, `stylis`, `@emotion/*`, `@react-input/*`, `@babel/runtime`, `currency.js`, `react-hot-toast`, `hoist-non-react-statics` y `prop-types`.

El propio código de la librería también se poda: de 96 651 B (2 módulos) a 33 489 B (25 módulos).

Lo que queda es uso real: `lucide-react` (sigue entero por el `import * as` de `DIconBase`; es otra palanca, fuera de este PR), `framer-motion` (`DPortalContext` lo usa y `DContextProvider` lo monta siempre) y las dependencias propias del template.

## Medición sobre el widget real (template v1.2.0, Lighthouse móvil, 2026-09-08)

Re-medición sobre el template. **Sustituye a las cifras de la sección anterior**, tomadas el 2026-09-07 contra un estado previo del template; la diferencia en el punto de partida (441 562 frente a 441 720 B) es la deriva de ese estado.

| | Solo este PR | Combinado con el plugin `lucideSubset` del template |
|---|---|---|
| `main.js` brotli | 441 562 → **232 681 B** (**−47,3 %**) | → **121 324 B** (**−72,5 %**) |
| LCP móvil, 1 instancia | **−26,2 %** | **−44,1 %** |
| LCP móvil, 3 instancias | **−35,1 %** | **−45,7 %** |
| TBT | — | **0 ms** |

El DOM renderizado es idéntico al del baseline y no hay errores de consola en ninguno de los dos escenarios.

Las dos palancas se acumulan: este PR desbloquea el tree-shaking por módulo, y el plugin `lucideSubset` recorta lo que queda de `lucide-react`, que es el mayor bloque restante. Ninguna de las dos sustituye a la otra.

## Riesgos considerados

- **Efectos de nivel de módulo en un módulo que deja de importarse.** Auditado `src/` completo: no hay imports de CSS en ningún `.ts`/`.tsx`, ni registros, ni llamadas `configure*` al importar, ni sentencias sueltas de nivel de módulo. Los únicos efectos son un `new Set` en `sanitizeHref`, un `PhoneNumberUtil.getInstance()` en `validatePhoneNumber` y nueve `Object.assign` de compound components, todos locales a su propio módulo: si el módulo se descarta, su efecto se descarta con él y nadie lo observaba. **No se encontró ninguno del que dependa otro módulo.**
- **Depender de que el bundler del consumidor respete `sideEffects`.** No es una apuesta nueva: `"sideEffects": ["*.css"]` ya estaba declarado y los bundlers ya lo honraban. Lo que cambia es que ahora hay granularidad por módulo sobre la que actuar. Un consumidor cuyo bundler lo ignore queda **igual que hoy**, no peor: `dist/index.esm.js` sigue existiendo.
- **`dist/esm/` como superficie de facto.** Sin `exports`, nada impide que alguien importe `dist/esm/components/DButton/index.js` por ruta física y ate la estructura interna. Conviene tratar `dist/esm/` como interno.
- **Deriva entre las dos salidas ESM.** Se emiten desde el mismo `dist-transpiled`, pero por configuraciones distintas. Una verificación en CI que compare la superficie de exports de ambas sería sensata; no está en este PR.
- **Consumidores CommonJS.** No obtienen ninguna ganancia: `main` sigue siendo el archivo único. Para ellos el cambio es neutro, no regresivo.
- **Sourcemaps y stack traces.** Los frames del consumidor pasan a apuntar a `dist/esm/components/...` en vez de a un archivo único. Es más legible, pero es un cambio observable para herramientas de monitoreo con reglas por ruta.

## Costo

- **Tarball: 861 647 → 1 014 705 B (+17,8 %).** Sin comprimir, de 5,6 a 6,4 MB. Casi todo son los 176 sourcemaps de `dist/esm/`: sin ellos el crecimiento sería de +6,9 % (921 100 B). Se mantienen activados por coherencia con las salidas existentes; si se prefiere el tarball más pequeño, es un cambio de una línea.
- **CDN:** `aws s3 sync ./dist/` pasará a sincronizar 352 objetos más por versión. No hay que tocar `cdn.yml` ni `publish-cdn.js`: ambos trabajan a nivel de directorio, no por archivo. Verificado que `dist/index.esm.js`, `dist/css/*`, `dist/js/*` y `dist/types/*` siguen ahí tras el build.
- **`jspdf`:** ahorro, no costo. Se van 17 paquetes del

author: mzac
body:
Five issues, four of which close. Each got its own commit; a fifth commit
applies the `/code-review` findings.

| Issue | What lands |
|---|---|
| **#971** | `nfs` backup destination — NFSv4/v3 in userspace via a ctypes binding to `libnfs` |
| **#989** | Write-only + immutable destinations, S3 Object Lock, the `https_put` driver, pull-mode conditional GET (**items 1, 2 and 4** — item 3 deferred) |
| **#985** | Cluster DNS (CoreDNS) health on the cluster-health snapshot, with a card, an alert and an MCP field |
| **#991** | Cross-build the x86-64 appliance ISO on an arm64 host |
| **#1016** | nmtui edits no longer revert silently |

---

## #971 — NFS backup destination

**Both approaches the issue proposed are dead ends, and both were tried
first.** libnfs's own PyPI binding is a 2016 sdist — the only release ever
published — whose SWIG shim calls `import imp`, removed in Python 3.12. It
*compiles* against libnfs 5.0.2 and then cannot be imported, so the failure
looks like a packaging problem right up to the first import. And Debian's
`libnfs-utils` ships exactly `nfs-cat`, `nfs-cp`, `nfs-ls` and `nfs-stat` —
there is no `nfs-rm`, so `delete` could not be implemented and the ABC could
not be satisfied. That is the same defect that rules TFTP out in #989.

What ships instead is a ctypes binding against `libnfs.so.14`: no build
toolchain in the image (runtime `libnfs14` only), no third-party Python
package to age out, and dynamic linking keeps the LGPL-2.1 obligation to its
simple case. `NOTICE` and `THIRD_PARTY.md` record it as the one entry we link
against rather than execute as a subprocess.

The struct layouts are transcribed by hand, and a wrong offset does not raise
— it reads an adjacent field, so an archive reports a plausible-but-wrong
size, or a garbage `mtime` reaches the retention sweep. The tests pin sizes
and offsets against values produced by compiling `offsetof()` against
Debian's `libnfs-dev`, so they assert on the compiler rather than on a
re-derivation of the same guess. The live half — mount, 3 MB multi-chunk
round-trip, atomic rename, squash and read-only error mapping — was validated
end to end against an `nfs-ganesha` export on **both** protocol versions.

Three behaviours worth knowing:

* **Writes are atomic.** Staged to `<name>.part` and renamed, because a PUT
  is atomic and an NFS write is not. The staged name deliberately does not
  match the archive-name pattern, so a run killed halfway leaves nothing the
  retention sweep or `latest/download` can see.
* **Permission errors name both likely causes.** EACCES on NFS is nearly
  always either the export's `secure` option refusing our unprivileged source
  port, or `root_squash` — and they need opposite fixes, so guessing one
  sends the operator in circles.
* **The probe readdirs.** An export that accepts a write but whose directory
  the presented uid cannot read passes a write and fails every listing — and
  listing is what retention, pull mode and the drill all depend on.

`ConfigFieldSpec.type` gains `notice`: prose belonging to the kind rather
than to a field. NFS needs one, because AUTH_SYS has no credential at all and
a passing connection test says nothing about who else can read the export.

---

## #989 items 1, 2 and 4

**Item 3 (appliance USB / removable disk) is deferred**, which is why this PR
does not close the issue. It needs a supervisor mount plane, a host runner, an
appliance-chart hostPath and per-node target affinity.

**Item 1 — write-only and immutable.** The credential that writes an archive
could also delete it, and the retention sweep ran with that credential
nightly. `backup_target.write_only` (migration `b8f4c02e7a19`, defaults false)
skips the prune, answers 409 on archive delete and pull-mode download,
tolerates a refused delete in the probe as `probe_retained`, and makes an
unreadable destination report `cannot_drill` — readiness carries a reason and
is forced to UNVERIFIED. Retention alongside it is a 422 rather than a keep-N
on screen that silently does nothing every night.

S3 gains `object_lock_mode` / `object_lock_days`. Two details that matter: the
probe object is written **without** lock headers (a probe under a 30-day
compliance lock is undeletable litter created every time somebody clicks
Test), and the prune reads `ObjectLockRetainUntilDate` from `head_object` and
skips a locked object **quietly** — a refused delete on a locked bucket is the
feature working, and warning per file per night would make correct
configuration indistinguishable from breakage.

The sharpest bug removed: an empty listing from a destination we are *not
permitted to list* was reported as `failed` with "the destination holds no
archives" — a confident, alerting claim about a target that is very likely
fine.

**Item 2 — `https_put`.** Artifactory, Nexus, a presigned URL, an internal
receiver. Inherently write-only, so the API forces the flag rather than
letting an operator configure a retention policy that could only fail
silently. Redirects are not followed: a followed redirect re-sends the archive
*and* its credential to an address the SSRF guard never saw.

**Item 4 — pull mode.** Both download routes are conditional. Archive
filenames carry a UTC timestamp and the bytes under a name are never
rewritten, so the filename is a legitimate strong validator — a poller that
already has the newest archive gets a 304 instead of re-downloading multiple
GB nightly.

---

## #985 — cluster DNS health

The appliance has *acted* on cluster DNS since #590 / #750 —
`ensure_coredns_ha` matches replica count and spread to the node count — and
showed nothing about it anywhere. So a CoreDNS that was down, single-replica
or co-located read as "everything healthy" until some unrelated pod restart
failed to resolve `spatium-control-spatiumddi-api.spatium.svc`.

Health visibility only: not a CoreDNS driver, not a zone surface, not a
`coredns-custom` editor.

**The probe is the load-bearing half.** Replica counts say the pods exist; the
probe says the path works. `ready 2 / spread ok / probe failed` is a real and
distinct state — kube-proxy or the CNI rather than CoreDNS — so both the card
and the alert report it as itself. Each probe is labelled with the node whose
api replica ran it.

Four decisions worth keeping: match the `k8s-app=kube-dns` **label**, never
the deployment name (GKE calls its deployment `kube-dns`); read the resolver
from the pod's own `/etc/resolv.conf`, not the Service object; `expected_replicas`
is `ensure_coredns_ha`'s target and is documented as re-declared rather than
shared, because the patcher lives in a separately-versioned deployable; and
**null is UNKNOWN, never zero** — a 403 on the pod list returns `(status, [])`
rather than raising, so without an explicit listable flag the card would claim
there are no replicas on a cluster it simply cannot see.

---

## #991 — arm64 cross-build

**Verified rather than asserted.** The builder image builds on both
`--platform linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, and both produce an ISO with the
same El Torito catalogue: a BIOS record at `/boot/grub/i386-pc/eltorito.img`
and a UEFI record at `/efi.img`. Worth stating because a plausible-looking
check goes wrong here — `eltorito.img` is *generated* by grub-mkrescue, not
shipped by `grub-pc-bin`, so testing for the file on the builder reports
MISSING on a perfectly good image.

`dpkg --add-architecture amd64` plus `grub-pc-bin:amd64` /
`grub-efi-amd64-bin:amd64` makes one Dockerfile serve both hosts. On amd64 the
qualifiers name the native arch and `--print-foreign-architectures` stays
empty — checked, not assumed.

**Emulating the builder cannot be made to work**: mkosi dies immediately on
`mount_setattr(2)`, part of the new mount API that neither qemu-user nor
Rosetta implements, and `--privileged` does not help. That is written into the
Dockerfile and APPLIANCE.md, because the error reads like a missing privilege
and the natural next move costs an afternoon.

author: stalniy
body:
## Why

Refs CON-864.

#3844 was supposed to stop the mutation gate scoring observability calls. It did not finish the job: **#3823 still fails, and it now fails on a mutant #3844 itself brought into existence.**

Evidence — run `34171534766`, job `101892665333`, head `cc2c0e4a5`, score **0.00** on a single survivor:

```
[Survived] CallExpression
src/deployment/services/deployment-writer/deployment-writer.service.ts:306:5
-       this.logger.warn({ event: "DEPRECATED_UPDATE_DEPLOYMENT_ENDPOINT_USED", userId, dseq });
+       ;
```

The ignorer answers for the **call** node. Stryker's `CallExpression` mutator (`empty-expression-mutator`) does not always mutate the call: for a statement-level call it emits its mutant on the **`ExpressionStatement` wrapping it**. `IgnorerBookkeeper` sets the active ignore on *enter* and traversal is parent-first, so the statement is entered — and mutated — before the call is ever judged. The ignore begins one node too late.

That also explains why this survivor is new. `empty-expression-mutator` declares `filter: mutantsInScope => mutantsInScope.length === 1`, and `mutantsInScope` counts only *non-ignored* mutants in the subtree. Before #3844 the line carried three mutants, so the deletion mutant was filtered away and only the `StringLiteral` and `ObjectLiteral` survived. #3844 ignored those two, the count fell to one, the filter began to keep the deletion mutant — and the score stayed 0.00 with a different mutant's name on it.

## What

`shouldIgnore` now also answers for an `ExpressionStatement` whose expression is an observability call (through an `await`, if there is one). A statement that does nothing but log has nothing else beneath it, so ignoring the statement ignores exactly the call and its arguments and nothing more.

### The gate still fails a real regression

Verified by running the changed plugin through Stryker's own `transformBabel` + `MutantCollector` — its real traversal, real mutators, real `IgnorerBookkeeper` — and recording which mutants come back ignored. #3844's table still holds:

| case | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `this.logger.warn({ event: "DEPRECATED_…", userId, dseq })` (the #3823 line) | `CallExpression -> ;` **mutated** | **ignored** — gate passes |
| `if (count > 10) { this.logger.warn({ event: "TOO_MANY" }); }` | `>` and `10` mutated | `>` and `10` **still mutated**; only the log ignored |
| `return bid.amount * 1.05 > 100 ? { tier: "high" } : { tier: "low" }` | all 10 mutated | **all 10 still mutated** |
| `Math.log(x * 2 + 1)` | mutated | **still mutated** |
| `catalog.error({ code: "E_NOT_FOUND" }, 3)` | mutated | **still mutated** |
| `takenNames.add(name);` (a non-log statement call) | `CallExpression -> ;` mutated | **still mutated** |

The last row is the one that matters most: this does not blanket-ignore call deletion. A deleted `Set.add` is still scored; only a deleted *log* is not.

### What this does not fix

Three other PRs fail CI on the mutation gate, and I checked each rather than assuming this covers them:

- **#3823** — 3 mutants, all observability. Goes green.
- **#3829** — 16 survivors, of which 3 are this bug. Removing them moves 75.76% to 79.37%, still under 80. It needs one more of its 13 genuine survivors killed; that is a test problem, not a gate problem.
- **#3826** — 2 survivors, `takenNames.add(name)` deletion and `suffix++ -> suffix--`. Neither is observability. Unaffected.
- **#3831** — not a mutation failure at all. Its `validate` job fails on a functional test (`test/functional/deployment-patch.spec.ts:149`, expected 200 got 400). Unaffected.

Their `security-scan` failures are all mirrors of the CI conclusion ("Blocked: Upstream CI conclusion is 'failure'"), not independent findings.

One adjacent case is left mutated on purpose: `BlockStatement -> {}` on a block whose only statement is a log call. It did not arise in any of the four runs, and widening the ignorer to whole blocks trades a real class of signal (an emptied block *is* removed behaviour) for a case with no evidence behind it. Worth revisiting if it ever shows up.

`MUTATION_MIN_SCORE` stays at 80. No label, and no app code, is involved.

author: eminyous
body:
Depends on #1730.

## What changed

- A text box sits above the list of accounts with no request and filters it by name or by phone.
- The matcher is `searchTokens` and `matchesSearch`, the same pair the link panel, the manual register form and the two tournament searches use, so hamza and ta marbuta fold and the words may be typed in any order.
- A query that matches nothing gets its own sentence. `bareAccounts.empty` goes back to meaning what it says, that nobody is without a request.
- A temporary password that has been issued now lives in the section, against the account it belongs to, rather than inside the row.

## Why

Every other tab on that screen opens with a search box. This one held the accounts that signed up and never asked for a membership, and the only way to reach one of them was to scroll a hundred rows.

`useBareAccounts` already loads the whole list in one call, so this filters an array that is in memory. Nothing else is added. An account with no request has no reference code, and no filter sheet was asked for.

The phone is matched whether or not it is on screen. `identify` falls back to the phone for an account added by hand, and `personDetails` hides the phone when there is no name, so a row that shows only a number is still reachable by that number and so is one that shows only a name.

The number on the tab keeps counting accounts with no request. It is handed the whole list, and a search that narrows what is drawn does not narrow that.

A password issued by the reset button used to live in its row, so typing in a search box unmounted the row and lost it. Holding it in the section against the account id means it survives being filtered away and coming back, and it is still there when the supervisor clears the box. Nothing is stored beyond the life of the screen.

The members list is the one place still doing a plain `includes` and it is not touched here.

Closes #1702

## How it was tested

Ran the ui tier. It covers narrowing by name, matching a phone that the row does not display, the sentence under a query that matched nothing against the one for an empty list, no search box when there is nothing to search, and a password issued before a search surviving the row being filtered out and back.

Looked at it at 360 with the list, with a query that narrowed it and with one that emptied it. The box holds its own row and does not wrap.

author: vivek7405
body:
Closes #1466

## Summary

A pass over the landing page, `/why-webjs` and `/what-is-webjs`, mostly reworking what the landing page's six-card grid argues.

**The intro video is gone.** The bytes stay in the R2 bucket `webjs-videos`, so bringing the section back later is an editorial decision rather than a re-upload. The six assertions describing the player are replaced by one counterfactual: the landing page must render no `<video>`, no `<iframe>`, and no reference to the video host, so an embed cannot land there again without failing a test.

**"AI-first" comes out of the one-line definition on three pages.** Each of those sentences is duplicated across the visible lede, a meta description, and an OG-image generator, so all three copies move together and the cards are regenerated. `/why-webjs` also gains "web components" in its category line, which is the one differentiator the shortest spelling of the sentence was dropping. The positioning is not retired: the `/what-is-webjs` FAQ entry that answers "What makes WebJs AI-first?", its capability card, the docs pages, `/ui` and `llms.txt` all keep it. What changes is that the definition of WebJs leads with what it is.

**The six-card grid now opens with the four claims `/why-webjs` argues at length**, in this order: model-agnosticism, architecture, design system, type safety, then the two it already had, auth and the unglamorous half. Model-agnosticism leads because it is the reason to try this framework at all and the rest of the grid is what you find once you have. File routing, typed server actions, streaming and elision gave up their slots; the architecture inset keeps the route tree and adds the `.server` boundary so the routing claim survives in a concrete form.

The comment over the grid records what the page no longer explains anywhere, ranked, so the next slot that frees up has an answer: **elision** first (the chips still assert "Display components ship 0 KB" and nothing explains it, and it is the one claim there no other framework can make), then **streaming**, then the **client router**.

**Two sections are renamed to say what they argue.** "The first paint is the whole page" becomes "Native web components the browser already understands, with better DX", which is what its live `<like-button>` stage actually shows; the lede is rewritten to pay the DX half in nouns a reader can check in that stage rather than as a comparison the page cannot make honestly, and progressive enhancement plus elision move from the lede into the chips, where the P.S. dare still invites the reader to verify the first. "Nothing is compiled away" becomes "What you write is what runs", naming the claim its own first sentence already made, in the same words `/why-webjs` uses for it.

**The two prompt panels on `/why-webjs` are relabelled** from "Where the decisions are still open" and "Where they are already made" to "Other frameworks" and "WebJs". The old labels made the reader hold the section's argument in their head to work out which panel was which.

Smaller: the design-system window shows three tokens with a colour swatch each instead of six names in two columns; the architecture inset's actions line reads `→ mutations`; the "an agent has no reason to reach for any" line is cut from the type-safety claim on both pages that carry it.

## Test plan

- [x] `website` node + browser suites green, 478 node tests and 88 browser tests
- [x] New `website/test/ssr/landing-copy-ssr.test.ts` fails if a video or embed returns, pins the hero wording, pins the DX claim being paid in checkable nouns, and pins the progressive-enhancement and elision chips (a copy pass dropping one would take the page's only statement of either claim with it)
- [x] `why-webjs-ssr.test.ts` category assertion updated, and its panel slice re-anchored: it sliced on the old column heading, where a missing boundary returns -1, silently widening the slice to the rest of the document and leaving every assertion on it passing vacuously. It now slices on the aria-labels and asserts each boundary exists first.
- [x] `( cd website && npx webjs check )` clean
- [x] `npx webjs doctor` clean, 2 pre-existing warnings unchanged by this PR
- [x] `og.png`, `og-what.png`, `og-why.png` regenerated and checked for overflow
- [x] Booted locally throughout, all three pages serve 200

## Surfaces

- Docs site, README, AGENTS.md, the skill, scaffold templates, MCP, editor plugins: N/A, website copy with no framework surface change.
- Bun, e2e, smoke: N/A, no runtime-sensitive source touched.

body:
## 问题（codex 对 #535 的两轮复审）

### 一轮 P1：越池守卫放在 `pool.submit` 之前

```python
if budget[kind] <= 0:
    break          # ← 先 break
budget[kind] -= 1
future = pool.submit(...)   # ← 越池单永远到不了这里
```

Host 在 claim 事务里已把该执行记为 `claimed`，但 worker 不提交执行——**不跑、不心跳、不报结果**，只能等租约过期被 sweeper 收回。爬坡期 Host 持续发活会**逐轮累积**悬挂租约。修法：「照单收下」必须含提交执行，break 移到 submit + active 记账之后（67e9e52a）。

### 二轮 P1：仅 break 当前 pass + 本地预算钳 0 是空转的

- Host 按「`active < 声明容量`」分池发活（`claim_windows.needed_claim_kinds`），而 worker 声明的是**目标容量**（#501，不随爬坡档位走）；
- 本地预算面：`base = 0` 时预算本来就 0（`claim_availability(0, …) = 0`），`base > 0` 时又立即解除——`pool_deferred` 对预算的作用是空转；while 是 `or` 条件，code 池预算让循环照进；
- 结果：Host 每个 pass 都会再发一个越池的活，running 依然爬到声明容量，ramp-up/背压被绕过。

**真修复（ff5910f2）**：越池时把该池记入 `pool_deferred`，抑制期间该池 claim 调用的**声明容量压到 `min(活跃数, 目标)`**——Host 的分池门即关闭，不再发该池的活。预算/声明推导收口到新模块 `worker/claim_budget.py`（`pass_budget` 纯函数，文件预算治理）。

**解除面** = 该池「未被抑制时的预算」转正（`avail > 0`：执行完成/档位推进/背压消退）——比 `base > 0` 更严：背压把 availability 钳 0 时 base 仍可 > 0，此时解除会立刻再越池一个。解除后声明回声目标容量。

### CI 治理违规（61a55e73）

backend-unit 的 `test_test_modules_do_not_import_each_other` 拒绝 test 模块互相 import：`FakeClient`/`_claim`/`_write_main_config`/`_run_main` 抽到 `tests/workers/helpers.py`，两个测试文件都从 helpers import，语义零变化。

## 测试（旧形态复现验证）

- **Host 保真 fake**（`_FaithfulHost`）：镜像 `claim.py` + `needed_claim_kinds` + `sync_declared_capacity` 的语义——按 claim 调用**声明的**容量记账、只发 `active < 声明容量` 的池的活、`release_slot` 归还名额；
- 新用例 `test_main_cross_pool_suppression_caps_declared_capacity`：target=8 + ramp initial=1 场景，**临时还原旧形态复现 running 爬到 8/8**（ramp 档位 1 被完全绕过）；修后断言抑制期间声明恒为 `(1, 32)`、不再被授权、执行完成后恢复发活且声明回 `(8, 32)`；
- 保留一轮断言：每个 claim 必被 submit（旧形态复现 `1 submitted vs 102 claims`）、预算全程非负（复现过 `-1/-2/…` 序列）、每 pass 至多 1 单。

## Quality Impact

568 个 worker 测试全绿；ruff/mypy/architecture 全过（executor.py 224≤224，claim_budget.py 54 行登记基线）；本地 quick gate 全 lane 通过。

Refs #534

author: mvtamn
body:
The intervention lifecycle ran only inside `onDemandSpareReconcile`. So ADR 0026's *"an observed breach creates one internal, deduplicated Suggested Alert immediately"* meant **up to an hour**, and a projected breach — which needs two consecutive evaluations, so one noisy forecast cannot raise a draft — meant **up to two**.

The applicable service standard is **twenty-five minutes**.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observed breach → draft | 0–60 min | 0–5 min |
| Projected breach → draft | 60–120 min | 5–10 min |
| Recovered → intervention closed | 0–60 min | 0–5 min |

Every draft described a trip that had already finished — worse than no draft, because it invites an operator to message customers about a wait that has resolved. Recovery was equally slow in the other direction, so the review queue also held drafts about trips that had recovered on their own.

## What changed

`onDemandInterventionsEvaluate`, a five-minute timer, runs the same lifecycle over the monitor state the hourly reconciliation and the Spare webhook both maintain.

**It makes no claim about currency.** Only the hourly authoritative reconciliation establishes that, and this timer stands down whenever the monitor is not `current`. A degraded source may still be taking webhook updates, and acting on them would create rider-facing drafts from data the console is simultaneously telling operators not to trust — the same rule the workspace already applies to its own actions. The hourly reconciliation still evaluates directly after it stores, on the freshest possible state, and both callers share one implementation and one debounce.

The in-memory set of authoritative request ids becomes a freshness bound in SQL (`last_polled_at >= @covered_since`). Same population — the reconciliation stamps `last_polled_at` on every request it reads, changed or not — but expressed where a five-minute run can use it too.

## Making five minutes affordable

The previous loop issued two round trips for **every** active request, however healthy, then wrote an `UPDATE` that matched no rows for those with no intervention on file. At an hourly cadence that was merely wasteful; at five minutes it would be a load problem on a single B1 worker this app has already lost twice.

Candidate selection is now narrowed to requests that are breaching, forecast to breach, or already have an intervention on file. A healthy request with nothing on file needs no decision. One that has **recovered** still appears — that is what lets its open intervention be closed, and it is the case a naive "only breaching rows" filter would silently break.

## Verification

`onDemandInterventions.db.contract.test.ts` runs the real selection against SQL Server in the existing contract job, importing the statement rather than restating it:

| Row | Selected? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `healthy-untracked` | no | healthy with nothing on file needs no decision |
| `healthy-with-intervention` | **yes** | recovered — its open intervention must be resolvable |
| `observed-breach` | **yes** | past the standard now |
| `projected-breach` | **yes** | forecast past the standard |
| `overdue-but-inside` | no | overdue is a watch condition, not an intervention |
| `strict-zone-breach` | **yes** | past a ten-minute zone override, inside the default |
| `stale-breach` | no | nothing has confirmed it since the last reconciliation |
| `completed-breach` | no | no longer active |
| `no-forecast-healthy` | no | a missing forecast is not a breach |

It also asserts the applicable standard travels with the row (10, not the default 25).

- `functions-restapi`: 683 tests, 679 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped (db-contract files needing a database — mine runs in the contract job).
- `onboard-console`: 352 tests across 45 files pass; typecheck clean across all three workspaces.
- Timer registration confirmed: `onDemandInterventionsEvaluate  0 */5 * * * *`.

**I could not run the contract test locally** — no Docker daemon on this machine. Its first real execution is this PR's `decision-matrix-contract` check.

## What I deliberately did not change

The debounce stays **count**-based (two consecutive evaluations) rather than duration-based. A duration would be more robust to cadence changes but needs a `projected_breach_since` column and a migration; at five minutes, two consecutive evaluations is five to ten minutes of a sustained forecast, which is the behaviour the rule was written to get. Worth revisiting if the cadence changes again.

Nothing here turns the monitor on. It is still `ON_DEMAND_MONITORING_ENABLED=false`, and this timer returns immediately while that holds — so on dev it is inert until the monitor is activated.

## Root-cause finding: no entry-time vs. mid-flight distinction exists in Python

`_revalidate_capability_and_membership_or_403` (the function every post-yield-point revalidation call composes) calls `revalidate_capability_or_403` then `_deny_cross_tenant_project_read` — the exact same function used for the entry-time check. `_deny_cross_tenant_project_read` returns the uniform 404 `unknown_project` envelope whenever the caller's resolved role is `None`, with no structural distinction between "never a member" and "membership revoked mid-flight after already legitimately holding it."

- `perm_gates.rs`: `RevalidateOutcome::DeniedMembership` now maps to the uniform `not_found` (404) response instead of `forbidden` (403), matching Python's real behavior.

author: arqcary
body:
## Qué entra

La **mitad de pantalla** de la ficha 379: T9 (`UsuarioForm`), T11 (`UsuariosModule`) y T13. Con esto la ficha queda completa — su mitad de servidor entró en el PR #736.

**Sin migración.** El único cambio en `lib/actions/usuarios.ts` es **borrar** la anotación `@sin-superficie`, que caducó en el momento en que `UsuariosModule` empezó a llamar a la acción. La guardia de superficie de uso lo exige, y es lo que ya le pasó a `restablecerContrasenaUsuario`.

## Qué ve el usuario

Las tres puertas —inactivar, cambiar rol y cambiar zona— abren el mismo diálogo con el número delante. **Visto en la app**, no razonado: con dinero sembrado dijo textualmente *«Ahora mismo hay 2 cierres aprobados sin consolidar, por ₡1.236.567,99»*, que es la suma exacta de las dos filas; confirmar aplicó el cambio; y con dos Admin satélite en la zona **no apareció nada**, tampoco al activar.

**Sigue siendo un aviso, nunca un bloqueo.** El humano firmó «no, no quiero daños»: ninguna rama de la pantalla impide nada, y el caso «confirmar tras el fallo aplica el cambio» está medido por el camino más peligroso.

## Tres decisiones del implementador, no del humano

1. **Los tres roles del aviso salen de `ROL_LABELS`.** El diseño escribía «un **admin**», que es el valor crudo del enum y R23 lo prohíbe; medido en el árbol, las dos frases de cara al usuario dicen «un administrador». Queda «ni el Maestro ni un Administrador…».
2. **La rama de error lleva título propio** — «No se pudo comprobar el impacto de este cambio» —, porque el título del diseño afirmaba justo el dato que falta.
3. **Cuando falla la comprobación, la zona se nombra con lo que pinta la fila**, porque el servidor no llegó a decirlo; si la fila no tiene zona, «la zona de este usuario».

Las tres con su vuelta atrás escrita en la bitácora y anotadas junto al checkbox de T11.

## Gate

`./init.sh --rapido` sobre el árbol **ya fusionado con `dev`**, que es el gate que este repo pide para abrir un PR: `INIT_EXIT=0` leído de dentro del log, 149 tests relacionados y **las 195 guardias enteras, 2895 tests, todas verdes**.

Antes de eso, el implementador corrió el **gate completo** sobre su árbol: `INIT_EXIT=0`, 1781 archivos, 25.494 tests, 0 rojos, con los archivos contra Postgres ejecutados. Esa corrida es anterior al merge y él mismo lo avisó; el completo sobre `dev` va detrás de este merge.

**16 mutaciones aplicadas, 16 rojas.** Y la autocomprobación del arnés hizo su trabajo: la primera vuelta salió con `vitest` sin ejecutar por un flag mal pasado, y **el arnés se negó a reportar 13 supervivientes** en vez de cantarlos como buenos.

## Un hallazgo ajeno que NO se toca

El select de Rol del formulario pinta los valores crudos del enum (`adminSatelite`, `adminTienda`…). Es de una feature anterior y R23 habla del aviso, no del select. Queda dicho, no arreglado.

author: djibian
body:
## Scope

Bounded #87 C20 research after the settled C19 result.

C19 proved that adding the exact frozen C10 `file_broker.cpp` translation unit to the successful C17-style standalone `QApplication` + exact `libController.so` control is sufficient to reproduce the historical Qt/XCB SIGSEGV/139 even though no broker/provider code runs.

C20 isolates whether the **retained broker code/data sections and their load-time relocations** are necessary for that effect. It preserves the pinned Webots R2025a/Xvfb/Qt/Controller boundary and the exact frozen broker source blobs, then runs three same-path arms in one Xvfb session:

- baseline: C17-style standalone control;
- full: exact C19-style broker translation unit retained;
- gc: the same full build with only linker dead-section collection (`--gc-sections`) added.

The oracle requires the full arm to reproduce the exact C19 SIGSEGV/139 Qt/XCB witness before interpreting the gc arm, and requires the gc image to contain neither `webeeblocks::createQtFileDialogProvider()` nor the broker runtime marker.

Pre-registered discriminator:
1. baseline succeeds, full reproduces exact SIGSEGV/139, gc reaches `QAPPLICATION_OK`/0 -> retained broker sections/relocations are necessary; next isolate the smallest retained section/symbol group without invoking broker behavior;
2. baseline succeeds, full reproduces exact SIGSEGV/139, gc still reproduces the same Qt/XCB SIGSEGV despite broker symbol/marker elimination -> dead-section elision is insufficient; inspect residual ELF/layout/load metadata before source-level behavior;
3. C19 witness not reproduced, gc residue remains, or any other outcome -> UNPROVEN.

Research-only. Do not change QPA/DISPLAY or invoke `QFileDialog`. Preserve the exact settled result on #87 and close without merge.

Refs #87.
