author: hameddavoodi-cmyk
body:
## What

Implements production adapters wiring `cmd/aisma-agent` to the real control plane (Stream 5B):

- `internal/agent/grpcclient`: gRPC client over the generated stubs (`internal/api/gen`).
  - Enrollment listener (server-cert-only TLS 1.3, pinned server CA) driving `internal/enroll.Client`'s TPM-backed EK/AK/DevID/WK creation, MakeCredential/ActivateCredential proof, and CSR through Start/Activate/Finish; the returned publisher key is checked against `Config.PublisherKeyIDs` before being trusted.
  - mTLS Agent listener (client cert = issued DevID cert, key = TPM-resident via a `crypto.Signer` built from the reloaded DevID handle) implementing Pull/Ack/Attest.
  - `.awr` envelopes are opened with `internal/delivery.Receiver` using the TPM-resident WK (P-384 ECDH); plaintext goes straight into the `agent.SealRequest` and is never written to disk or logged.
  - DevID cert + enrollment state persisted under `StateDirectory/enroll` (never a private key — only `tpm.KeyBlob` wrapped material).
  - `agent.Enroller`/`agent.EnvelopeSource` implemented on top of the client.
- `internal/agent/config.go`: `EnrollServerAddr`/`AgentServerAddr`/`ServerCAFile`/`PublisherKeyIDs`; `DisallowUnknownFields` preserved.
- `cmd/aisma-agent/main.go`: wired to `tpm.OpenReal` — startup hard-fails without `/dev/tpmrm0`, no degraded mode.
- `docs/agent.md` updated (transport split, state layout, Known gaps).

## Why

Closes the last gap between `internal/agent`'s daemon loop (`Enroller`/`EnvelopeSource` interfaces + test fakes) and the real control plane implemented in prior streams (`internal/api`, `internal/enroll`, `internal/delivery`, `internal/tpm`) — this is what lets `aisma-agent` actually enroll and pull/decrypt/seal secrets end to end on the profile device, rather than only against fakes.

## Threat-model impact

- No new trust boundary: the Enrollment listener's trust still comes from EK-possession (MakeCredential/ActivateCredential), not the transport; the Agent listener still authenticates the device by its DevID client certificate.
- Plaintext secret material exists only in-process, from `Receiver.Unwrap` to the seal-helper request; never written to disk, never logged (structured logs only carry name/seq/kind, not payload).
- No private key ever leaves the TPM or touches disk — only wrapped `tpm.KeyBlob` material and the DevID certificate are persisted.
- Startup hard-fails without `/dev/tpmrm0` (no software-TPM or degraded fallback in the production binary).
- Bug fixed during this stream (see Test evidence): a TPM storage-primary handle leak in `ensureSession` — not a security issue by itself (no secret exposure), but a resource-exhaustion risk on repeated reconnects against a real TPM's small transient-object pool.
- Known, pre-existing gaps unchanged by this stream (`docs/agent.md` "Known gaps"): policy-bundle envelopes are skipped, not installed (falls back to hard PCR-7-only seal policy); the DevID CSR the device builds is never sent over the wire protocol (proto has no field for it); `enroll.State.CACert` is always empty (client cert chain is the DevID leaf alone).

## Test evidence

- Unit (bufconn, real `api.Server` in-process): `go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/agent/grpcclient/...` — happy path, failed-seal-still-advances-cursor, unparseable-envelope-does-not-advance-cursor. rc=0.
- swtpm-backed dev test (`-tags=integration,dev`, `swtpm_integration_test.go`): real TPM key-reload/`crypto.Signer`/`ECDH_ZGen` path, mTLS handshake against a real TCP-listener `api.Server`. Surfaced and fixed a real primary-handle leak in `ensureSession` (see below). 3 consecutive clean runs post-fix.
- Coverage: `make cover` → `internal/*` 81.9% (floor 80%), rc=0.
- Edge (real hardware, `test/edge/agent_grpcclient_edge_test.go`, `TestEdge_GrpcclientPollAckRealTPM`): `make test-edge` against `aisma@100.105.213.83` (Nuvoton NPCT75x TPM) — real enrollment-shaped key creation, real `ensureSession` reload/Signer/ECDH_ZGen, real Poll/Ack over TCP mTLS on the device itself.
  - `TestEdge_GrpcclientPollAckRealTPM` PASS (5.91s). Full edge suite PASS. `== edge result: rc=0 host=edgexpert-9ecd at 2026-09-08T06:10:23Z`.

## Not done / out of scope

- Policy-bundle installation (pre-existing gap, not introduced by this stream).
- DevID CSR wire-protocol plumbing (proto change needed, out of this package's scope).
- `enroll.State.CACert` population (upstream `EnrollFinishResult` carries no CA cert field).

author: petwashglobal
body:
Residual of the proof→account binding (#2319), which its own code comment records as deliberately out of scope there.

Four routes turn a verified contact proof into account state. Three write the attested contact where the platform reads it; `POST /api/onboarding-verification/validate-tokens` wrote it to Postgres only.

## Confirmed reachable — with one correction to the reported diagnosis

`users.phone` is **not** left NULL. #2319 already added a raw `UPDATE users SET phone` on the attach path (`onboarding-verification.ts:889` pre-fix), so the "claims a verified phone it does not record" half is closed. The half that is still real is the one that carries the harm:

> Firebase owns the phone identifier. `POST /api/auth/phone-session` resolves the account through `fbAdminAuth.getUserByPhoneNumber()`. `validate-tokens` never touched the Firebase record.

The path, traced end to end:

1. Email-first signup (Google / Apple / email). `routes.ts:1630` provisions the row with `phone: phone || decoded.phone_number || undefined` → `AuthService.createUser` writes `phone: data.phone || null`. **NULL.**
2. `client/src/pages/AccountActivation.tsx` is exactly that population — it prompts for a number *because* `user.phoneNumber` is null (`:238`), then posts `smsToken` to `validate-tokens` (`:311`).
3. The route persists `users.phone`, flips `phone_verified` / `mobile_verified_at`, and the activation gate says active. The Firebase record still has no phone.
4. Later, sign in by that number: `getUserByPhoneNumber` throws `auth/user-not-found` → `phone-session` takes its **new-user branch** and `adminAuth.createUser({ phoneNumber })` mints a **second account**. Wallet, loyalty and history stay on the first; the `storage.upsertUser` for the second collides on the UNIQUE `users.phone` and is warn-swallowed as "non-blocking".

## The fix

Route the attach through the same `updateUser` call the siblings use.

1. **Attach.** `fbAdmin.updateUser(uid, { phoneNumber })` before the Postgres write, mapping `auth/phone-number-already-exists` to the same `409 PHONE_IN_USE` `verify-signup-mobile` returns. Firebase's check is atomic and authoritative; the pre-existing `users` SELECT is a courtesy that races.
2. **No inherited constraint 500.** `users.phone` is UNIQUE. With Firebase having already accepted the number, a `23505` here means a stale row holds it with no Firebase record — drift, not a second legitimate owner — so it answers 409, not a raw 500.
3. **A failed attach is not success.** No verified flag is flipped for a number we could not attach; the route returns before `markMobileVerified`.

## Where the write lives — deliberately the route, not the service

`markMobileVerified` takes a `userId` and no contact. Its other callers — `verify-signup-mobile`, `phone-session`, `authBootstrap`, `verify-sms-code` — have each already written the contact, or derived the account *from* it, before calling. Only the caller holds the proof saying which number may be attached; a service-side write would be guessing at one, and would fight callers that already wrote it.

**Email needs no equivalent.** The binding requires the proved address to already equal `users.email`, so this route never has an address to attach.

## The binding is not weakened

All 15 existing pins in `server/tests/validateTokensSubjectBinding.behavior.test.ts` pass unchanged — including *"a valid SMS token for a DIFFERENT phone than the account holds is refused"*. (The brief named this file `validateTokensProofBinding.regression.test.ts`; that path does not exist — this is the suite #2319 shipped.)

The file gains a `updateUser` entry on its existing `firebase-admin` mock and 5 new pins. Reverting the route makes **exactly the 3** that assert the new behaviour fail, and the other 17 still pass:

```
× an email-first row persists the attested number to BOTH stores
  expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 'uid_nophone', …(1) ]
× Firebase is the authoritative uniqueness check — its rejection is 409, not 500
  expected 200 to be 409
× a failed attach is NOT reported as success and flips no flag
  expected 200 to be greater than or equal to 500
Tests  3 failed | 17 passed (20)
```

With the fix in place: **20 passed (20)**. `tsc --noEmit` reports nothing on either touched file.

## Noted, not fixed here

`POST /api/onboarding-verification/verify-sms-code` (`:647`) calls `markMobileVerified` on a row it finds *by* the phone, so it is not this gap — but it is unauthenticated and matches on the last 9 digits. Separate concern, separate change.

author: moperc
body:
## What

Replaces the decorative jet at every plot's cleansing station — one 0.16-stud cyan glass stick from the shower head to the tub — with a particle-driven falling-water effect.

Follow-up to the wash-spray v8 pass (#120): same "realistic over stylised" note, the other piece of "hose water" on a plot.

## Why

The stick is a laser dimmed — the exact shape [`WashController.luau`](src/client/Controllers/WashController.luau)'s header spent seven passes escaping, still standing here as furniture.

The shower head's underside sits ~0.3 studs above the wash stand (it rinses the item *on* the stand), so there's no column to fall. What a real rinse here looks like is a wide curtain off the head, most of it clearing the pedestal into the tub, and a splash where it lands.

## Changes ([`Plots.luau`](src/server/build/Plots.luau), `buildCleansingStation`)

- **Stub** — one short faint cylinder of coherent water at the head, to anchor the source.
- **`Fall`** — a dense curtain of camera-facing droplets, `Squash`ed along their fall so they read as streaks not beads, speeding up under extra gravity and fading before the water.
- **`Splash`** — a low ring of spray off the water surface.

Particles carry the motion, so it animates itself — no per-frame script. Matte (`LightEmission` a fraction, no light): the fallout is the only thing on a plot that glows.

A discarded first cut kept four translucent panes down the pedestal faces — which read as a display case, worse than the stick. Geometry can't be this without reading as solid, hence all-particles.

## Verification

- Drove it in the live Studio session (`Plots.rebuild()` + camera on Plot 1), iterated the emitters against screenshots until the curtain read as water rather than crossed sparks (the fix was dropping `Orientation = VelocityPerpendicular`).
- `selene src/` clean. In-game spec **315/1** (the 1 is the known detector-walk baseline). `World.verify()` passes.

## Deploy note

World geometry — the place file isn't in git. Needs a Studio `World.rebuild()` + Save + Publish to ship, same as any `build/` change.

## Scope

Migrate seven pure, map-confirmed `CAviDecompressor` getters from raw unaligned offset arithmetic to the already-validated `CAviDecompressorView` while preserving the existing free-function ABI:

- `CAviDecompressor_Frames`
- `CAviDecompressor_Fps`
- `CAviDecompressor_IsPlaying`
- `CAviDecompressor_Palette`
- `CAviDecompressor_Header`
- `CAviDecompressor_DecodedFrame`
- `CAviDecompressor_SumSleepTime`

The migration is generated from `data/readability_migrations/avi_getters_v1.json`. Every replacement is pinned to the exact prior `body_sha256`; the branch workflow refreshed only these seven canonical hashes and passed `audit_split_sources.py` plus TU include-block validation before committing.

## Readability improvement

The functions now express semantic fields (`frames`, `fps`, playing state, palette/header handles, decoded frame, sleep time) instead of repeated nested `*(_DWORD *)(... + offset)` expressions. Original unaligned storage remains handled inside the non-owning view via `memcpy`.

- no ctor/dtor or ownership migration
- no `Initialized`, `TimeMs`, bitmap-header field dereferences, setters, event waits, or render/update paths

author: abhiramrajilan
body:
Brings `feature-courtside-dashboard` onto `main`. It had run 11 commits while main
moved 93 past it; ten files collided, and nine of them were not asking a question.

Your colleague's branch is untouched — this merges it, it does not rewrite it.

## The wrapper, which explains most of the conflicts

The court screens need overlays above the court chrome, so the branch introduced
`ChromeDialogContent` and swapped it into 45 files, citizen side included. Three had
been rewritten on main in the meantime:

| File | changed on main | changed on courtside |
|---|---:|---:|
| `add-witness-form` | 1797 | **16** |
| `sign-section` | 999 | **31** |
| `share-dialog` | 110 | **7** |

Their entire contribution to each is the import line and the tag name. So main's file
is kept and the swap re-applied — nothing lost on either side, no screen changes.

**The swap is extended to twelve overlays main grew after the fork**, which their branch
never saw. Those merge silently and would have kept sitting *under* the chrome — no
error, no failing test, just wrong on court screens. `<DialogContent>` now appears
nowhere outside the DS primitives and the command palette, which stays viewport-centred
on purpose.

## The court area

Main's `/employee` said "blank canvas on purpose" in its own comment. Theirs is 120 files
of built product — hearings, register cases, delay condonation, the signing queues, the
order screen. Taken wholesale, along with `/citizen`, which is a redirect on both sides.

## The role chooser is neither version

- **main** asked *"Choose how you are here today"* over two cards each carrying a teal
  button — two primary actions on one screen, against the one-rationed-teal Law.
- **courtside** asked *"How do you come to the court?"*, led with the bench (the smaller
  audience by a wide margin), but named people the way they name themselves and made the
  whole card the target.

Resolved to main's greeting, their card, advocates and litigants first, and the teal
moved onto the icon where it marks the choices without competing. Owner's call, Sept 8.

## Their lint errors are fixed here

Five in `use-sign-step-handoff`, all two patterns: state set inside an effect, and refs
read and written during render. Rewritten as React's "adjusting state when a prop
changes", with the handoff ref cleared after commit rather than mid-render. Behaviour
unchanged, and checked on the screen rather than asserted — on Sign orders, opening an
order hands off to Add signature and Back hands back.

Without this, main would have gone red again on a gate we cleaned up this morning.

## Checks

- `npm run build` — compiles
- `npm run lint` — exits 0
- `npm test` — 480 pass
- `check:ds-fresh` · tokens · typography · ui-sync — pass
- Walked on the render: the new `/welcome`, court home and its rail, the sign-orders
  queue and both directions of its dialog handoff, and a citizen-side dialog to confirm
  the wrapper degrades where there is no court chrome

## The scrutiny screens, in the same PR

`integration/scrutiny-courtside` is merged on top — four commits, one collision, and it
was the test glob for the third time (each line names its own folders and none of them
names anybody else's). Unioned.

One thing the sweep caught here too: the scrutiny work predates the wrapper, so its
review dialog was still a plain `DialogContent` and would have sat under the court chrome
on exactly the screens the wrapper exists for.

Verified on the render: the scrutiny queue in the court rail, a filing opening into the
workbench with the court's own breadcrumb, and the Register case dialog over it.

…ables

El propietario pidio que la version de ayer (hitos hardcodeados en codigo, premio como texto fijo aplicado como linea generica) se reconstruyera como un modulo real de produccion: el administrador debe poder elegir que servicio y/o producto se otorga en cada hito, con conteo automatico de citas agendadas/completadas/pagadas, historial y avance por cliente consultables sin sobrecargar la pagina.

Se reemplaza el diseno de ayer por completo (la tabla client_loyalty_rewards seguia vacia en produccion, count()=0, asi que fue un rediseno limpio, no una migracion de datos):

- LoyaltyMilestoneRule + LoyaltyMilestoneRewardItem: la regla configurable (cada cuantos servicios, que premio) y sus items (servicio y/o producto real del catalogo, no texto). ClientLoyaltyReward ahora referencia ruleId en vez de un milestoneKey de texto; ClientLoyaltyRewardItem snapshotea nombre/tipo/cantidad al momento del hito, igual que PaymentLine snapshotea su description/unitPrice.
- Decision del propietario sobre comision e inventario: un producto regalado descuenta stock real (linea de producto de verdad, pasa por el mismo bucle de stock existente) pero nunca genera comision; un servicio regalado se queda como linea manual en $0 (sin appointmentId, por lo que el calculo de comision ya lo excluye por diseno existente).
- Decision del propietario sobre notificacion: dentro del panel, no por correo. Tarjeta nueva en el Dashboard con los ultimos 5 hitos otorgados, sin necesidad de ningun sistema de notificaciones ni estado de leido/no leido.
- Pantalla nueva "Fidelizacion" (solo admin, permisos loyalty.view/manage nuevos): pestaña Hitos para configurar reglas y premios, pestaña Historial paginada con filtro por cliente y estado. Ficha del cliente ahora muestra el detalle real de los premios pendientes y el avance hacia el proximo hito.

Migracion aplicada contra la base real de este entorno con autorizacion explicita (dropea y recrea la tabla vacia de ayer con el nuevo esquema relacional) y seed corrido para registrar los permisos nuevos (41 permisos totales). body:
Addresses https://github.com/khuepm/LumiBase/issues/461.

Staging omits LUMIBASE_RUNTIME, so request middleware chooses Docker and reaches the Worker-only throwing stub. Selecting Cloudflare then exposes a second failure: CloudflareDatabaseProvider eagerly reads an absent HYPERDRIVE binding during runtime construction, before health can report dependency failures. These are confirmed source-level failure paths; live staging tail logs have not been obtained.

Changes:
- Select Cloudflare explicitly in local, staging, dev and demo Wrangler profiles.
- Initialize the database client at the first query/probe, preserving health and other dependency-independent routes when Hyperdrive is missing.
- Route /health/* to the Worker on shared Pages domains.
- Check deployment secrets before upload and verify /health/ready after deployment, retaining failure response bodies in logs.
- Reject HTTP 500 or invalid health payloads in the workerd startup gate.
- Add regression tests, changelog, setup-impact review, DoD guard and backlog B41.

Validation:
- 18 Node script tests passed, including all Worker profile/readiness routing guards.
- 8 CMS health tests passed using the real runtime middleware/factory for missing bindings.
- 30 Cloudflare adapter/database tests passed.
- CMS and runtime TypeScript checks passed.
- Regression proof: restoring the original database constructor makes both new health tests fail with HTTP 500; restoring this patch makes them pass.
- Registry uniqueness, pnpm settings parity, override drift and git diff --check passed.
- workerd startup verification could not complete because network approval was cancelled by the execution environment. Full workspace tests/build and live deployment are not verified.

Remaining acceptance work (draft; do not close upstream issue yet):
- Staging/dev/demo have no active Hyperdrive, KV, R2 or queue producer bindings in the checked-in configuration. An operator must provision/verify environment-specific resources and deployed secrets. No production resource IDs were reused.
- Obtain redacted staging tail-log evidence and verify real dependency readiness. Cloudflare access was unavailable in this session; the GitHub connector cannot read Worker secrets/tail logs.
- Existing release checker validates vars/secrets, not binding availability. This limitation and infrastructure follow-up are tracked in B41.

Compatibility and review:
- /health remains public and returns 200/degraded; /health/ready returns 503 for unavailable dependencies. Existing observability-token detail restrictions are preserved.
- No API schema, tenant queries, auth bypasses, migration, backfill, wizard steps, SDK or shell contracts change (C7 preserved). No bilingual API documentation change is required because the response contract is unchanged.
- Runtime clients remain per-request on Cloudflare. Docker implementation is unchanged.
- Rollback: revert this commit; no data migration is involved.

author: parsofish
body:
Three changes, all of them things the costed re-run of 2026-09-08 **measured**. T1 rulings **514** and **521**, plus the mechanical class **483/504** already ruled. **15 beats, unchanged.** Record: `_1.0/gate-manifests/M1-C-S6.amend-4.md`.

## 1 · Beat 11a's route was wrong, and it was my error

Amend-3 asserted `route: '/projects/mdtoc'`. The operator does not stand there — beat 10 presses "Architect →" and **lands on `/architect/new`**, which is exactly where `NewIdeaBox.tsx` publishes `data-architect-session-id` after Start. The runner refused it in its own words:

```
no real-nav path to "/projects/mdtoc" from "/architect/new": no [data-nav] pillar
and no link whose PATHNAME is that route. The runner does not fall back to
page.goto — an unreachable route must not pass as a beat.
```

**The cause is worth recording because it repeated.** I copied the route out of the sitting draft instead of re-deriving it from the component that renders the id. The same session had already cost two other corrections of that exact shape — a phase inferred from a missing handle, and a `session-phase` transcribed rather than read off the write that produces it. **A route in a draft is a claim about the product; the component is the product.**

## 2 · Beat 7 now names its query, because the page offers two doors

```
ambiguous real-nav path to "/knowledge" from "/sessions/project-brain/<sid>":
2 links share that pathname and differ only in their query —
/knowledge , /knowledge?id=story-s6
```

The runner will not pick one, and it is right not to: choosing by DOM order is how a beat silently starts asserting a different page. This beat means **the knowledge base it just seeded**, so it now says so.

**It was invisible until now** — the ambiguity only exists on the seeding-session page, and nothing reached that page until amend-3's beats 5 and 6 started carrying the operator there. Fixing one beat is what made the next one measurable, the same pattern as S7 beat 3's unreachable phase one beat along. Route comparison goes through one predicate since #578, so a declared query is compared rather than stripped.

## 3 · `SEED_BRIEF` — the agent never reached the writing stage

Run 2's seeding agent made **thirty tool calls in 95 seconds and every one was read-family**: one `TodoWrite`, then `Glob`/`Grep`/`Read` throughout, ending mid-exploration. **Not a single `Write` in the session.** The runner then threw `the agent turn produced no theme files`, which the product reported honestly as a crash — red banner, message verbatim, `derived from phase failed` (bead `forge-8vfn.7.6.4`, closed premise-corrected under 518).

So this is **not a write-path defect** — the agent was still surveying when its turn ended. The old brief asked for a QUALITY with no stopping point, which on a corpus of archived cycles is an invitation to read all of it. The rewrite asks for a **count**, names **where to start**, and says **when to stop reading** — the one lever the operator actually holds over an agent about to run out of turn, and S6's whole subject is the operator steering what the agent keeps.

**Recorded as a PREDICTION, to be measured by run 3 (521), not a fix asserted in advance.** If beat 6 still reds with no theme files, the brief was not the binding constraint and the turn budget is. Writing that down *before* the run is the point.

## Proof nothing was weakened

| change | before | after | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11a route | a page the operator is not on | the page that publishes the id | **stronger** — the beat can be reached at all |
| beat 7 route | `/knowledge`, ambiguous between two links | `/knowledge?id=story-s6` | **stronger** — names the destination it always meant |
| `SEED_BRIEF` | a quality with no stopping point | a count, a start, a stop | not an assertion; a story constant |

**No `expect.data` key was added, removed or relaxed.** Two routes became MORE specific and one constant changed.

## Gate

`gate.sh`: **exit 0, 20 steps, no FAIL, `npm test` 7741 pass / 0 fail**, on merged main `5ea4b38c`.

author: mishan
body:
`on: push` with no branch filter and `on: pull_request` both fire for every push to a branch that has an open PR, so each commit was built twice. With the sixteen-branch identity/messages stack that is sixteen redundant runs every time the stack is force-pushed.

Scoping `push` to `main` leaves `pull_request` covering every topic branch, and keeps the push build of `main` as the signal that a merge landed green.

The trade: a branch with no PR open no longer builds. That matches the convention in AGENTS.md — work happens on branches and the gates are what a PR must pass.

Independent of the identity/messages stack, and based on current `main`. The stack picks it up when it rebases onto `main`, since a `push` build uses the workflow file from the branch being pushed.

|---|---|---|---|
| `express` | 4.21.2 | **5.2.1** | `qs` ×4, `body-parser`, `path-to-regexp` ReDoS |
| `mailparser` | 3.7.4 | **3.9.23** | `linkify-it` ×2, `nodemailer` ×8 |
| `smtp-server` | 3.13.6 | **3.19.9** | `nodemailer` SMTP command injection, CRLF header injection, TLS cert validation |
| `lodash` | 4.17.21 | **4.18.1** | `_.template` code injection, `_.unset`/`_.omit` prototype pollution |
| `brace-expansion` | 1.1.11 | **1.1.18** (lockfile) | ReDoS ×5, transitive via `cli` → `glob@7` → `minimatch@3` |

### Why Express 5, given it's a major

Staying on 4.x doesn't work. `express@4.22.2` — the newest 4.x — still resolves `qs@6.15.3` and `body-parser@1.20.6`, both vulnerable, and no 4.x release fixes them.

The upgrade is a non-event here. Express 5's breaking changes are route syntax (path-to-regexp 8), removed method aliases, and removed `res.send(status)` overloads. `index.js` uses none of it: routes are string literals (`/api/emails`), no parameters, no regex paths, `app.delete()` not `app.del()`, `res.json()` and bare `res.send()`. `req.query` reads flat scalars only, so the v5 query-parser change is a no-op. `express-basic-auth` is a plain middleware and is unaffected.

### Node engine

`mailparser` and `smtp-server` both require Node ≥20, so `engines` moves `>=18` → `>=20`. Both Dockerfiles here are already `node:22-alpine`, and the consumer image in `ciam-app` is `node:20-alpine` — nothing downstream moves.

---

# Part 2 — dev advisories (24 → 0), via deleting CRA

Every dev-side advisory reported the same verdict:

```
high      svgo                  fix=react-scripts@0.0.0 BREAKING
high      nth-check             fix=react-scripts@0.0.0 BREAKING
high      postcss               fix=react-scripts@0.0.0 BREAKING
high      serialize-javascript  fix=react-scripts@0.0.0 BREAKING
moderate  webpack-dev-server    fix=react-scripts@0.0.0 BREAKING
... 19 more
```

`fix=react-scripts@0.0.0` is npm for *no version of this package fixes it*. `react-scripts@5.0.1` is the **final Create React App release** — CRA is EOL — and it pins `@svgr/plugin-svgo@5.5.0`, holding `svgo` at 1.3.2 forever while the patched version is 2.8.3.

That is what the red Dependabot runs are. [`actions/runs/30888039376`](https://github.com/ReachFive/fake-smtp-server/actions/runs/30888039376) is not a broken build — it is Dependabot correctly concluding `security_update_not_possible` and exiting 1. It fails on every rerun, permanently.

### The migration

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Bundler | `react-scripts@5.0.1` | `vite@8.2.2` + `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.1` |
| Entry HTML | `public/index.html` | `index.html` (repo root) |
| Entry point | implicit | explicit `<script type="module" src="/src/index.jsx">` |
| Sources | `src/App.js`, `src/index.js` | `src/App.jsx`, `src/index.jsx` |
| Dev-mode check | `process.env.NODE_ENV` | `import.meta.env.DEV` |
| Relative assets | `PUBLIC_URL=./` | `base: './'` |
| Output dir | `build/` | `build/` (unchanged) |
| **Packages** | **1377** | **174** |
| Build time | minutes | **129ms** |
| Bundle (gzip) | 71.4 kB js / 31.9 kB css | 72.7 kB js / 30.7 kB css |

`outDir` deliberately stays `build/`: `index.js` serves `path.join(__dirname, 'build')`, `"files": ["build"]` gates the npm tarball, and both Dockerfiles copy it. `vite.config.mjs` is `.mjs` because `index.js` is CommonJS, so `package.json` can't declare `"type": "module"`.

Dropped the `test` script — it ran `react-scripts test` against **zero test files**. `CLAUDE.md` now says so plainly rather than claiming coverage that never existed. Also dropped `eject` and the CRA-only `browserslist` field.

**Neither Dockerfile changes.** Both `COPY` the whole tree and run `npm run build`; the output path is unchanged.

---

## Verification

Backend, against a running server — 20 checks:

```
ok  SMTP send completes (150ms, no DATA hang)
ok  GET /api/emails 200            ok  filter ?to= / ?from= / since / until
ok  html + attachment parsed       ok  bcc-only mail (no To header) does not 500
ok  DELETE /api/emails             ok  CORS header present
ok  --auth 401 then 200            ok  --headers includes parsed headers
ok  AUTH LOGIN over plaintext accepted (was 538)
ok  STARTTLS advertised by default; --hide-tls suppresses it
```

Frontend, driven in a browser against a live backend with two real mails delivered over SMTP: Bootstrap styling applied, display names resolved, collapse expands on click, HTML `From:`/`To:` render as links, moment shows `a minute ago`, the attachment button renders, the HTML body renders with markup, **no console errors**.

Clean-room check on the merged branch: `npm ci` from the lockfile, `npm audit` → **0 vulnerabilities**, `npm run build` → compiles in 358ms.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Release.** `version` is untouched at `0.8.1` — bumped in 2019, never published. The npm release is blocked separately: the sole npm maintainer is a personal account belonging to someone who left the org 8 years ago. Suggest `0.9.0`, given `engines` now requires Node ≥20.
- Once released, ReachFive/ciam-app#6913 can drop its `rm -rf .../node_modules/mailparser && npm i -g mailparser@3` workaround — the 150ms send above confirms the hang is fixed at source.
- `ciam-app/docker/fake-smtp-server-ci/Dockerfile` is still `node:8.5` with an unpinned install. Inert today, but it breaks the moment anyone rebuilds it after a release.
- Superseded Dependabot PRs to close: #89, #92, #94, #95, #97, #98.
- `src/App.jsx` maps attachments to `<Button>` without a `key` prop — one-line follow-up.
- `vite@8` wants Node `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`, stricter than this package's `engines.node: >=20`. Left as-is deliberately: `engines` describes what *consumers* need at runtime, and Vite is dev-only. A contributor on Node 20.0–20.18 can run the server but not build the UI.

body:
## What
New sun/moon button in the sidebar header, next to the Settings gear, toggling a new `theme` setting ("dark" — unchanged existing default, or "light").

## How
- `popup.css`: a `:root[data-theme="light"]` override block for the neutral tokens (bg/panel/text/muted/border) plus darkened back-color/lay-color/amber (too pale for text on a light background otherwise). Every existing rule already reads these same variables, so nothing needed its own light-mode copy.

Same logic duplicated into `options.js`'s own `applyThemeToPage()` so `options.html` looks right standalone too.
- Added an explicit `color-scheme` per theme (missing before).

## Verified
Local popup preview harness: toggling flips every CSS variable and the button's icon correctly — confirmed via computed styles, computed `color-scheme`, and the full painted-background chain at a sample point (all consistently "light" after toggling, with nothing overlaying it). The harness's own screenshot capture rendered the page dark regardless of all that — traced to a Chromium force-dark rendering quirk specific to this sandboxed preview (a trivial one-line test page rendered fine, this one didn't; invisible to every DOM-level check), not the page's own styling. Worth a final look in a real browser once merged, just to be certain.

author: viktoryyyyy
body:
Rosstat HTTPS failed because the leaf requires the 2024 intermediate while the common download supplies the 2022 issuer. Add the verified root and 2024 intermediate as pinned public certificates and use a private TLS client context only for explicit Rosstat document routes. Certificate, hostname and TLS version checks stay enabled; redirects and changed certificate files fail closed. No system-wide trust store or global SSL defaults are changed.

The client freezes raw HTML and receipt manifests, without granting numerical macro or historical PIT admission. Source semantics and latest-release selection remain separate work.

Validation: 18 server tests passed. OpenSSL verified the intermediate signature and Rosstat hostname. A real Python capture returned the official CPI document with SHA-256 1e308b8c32e6df0f5163e3119adb5b3ae501b9760d172f5ff89537774c6adb75, matching the independent curl capture. Root CRLF normalization preserved its DER fingerprint. Training and trading remain disabled.

author: miyashita337
body:
## 概要

画像生成のバックエンドを Nano Banana（Gemini）から OpenAI Images API（`gpt-image-1`）へ移行しました。MCP サーバから Gemini 依存を撤去し、`.mcp.json` のサーバ名も実体に合わせて改名しています。

Closes #159

## 変更内容

### 引数を OpenAI ネイティブへ置換（破壊的変更）

`gpt-image-1` には旧 `aspect_ratio`（5種）/ `resolution`（4段階）に相当する値が**存在しません**。近似変換で黙って別の比率を返すとユーザーが気づけないため、引数自体を置き換えてスキーマで弾く方針にしました。

| 旧 | 新 | 選択肢 |
|---|---|---|
| `aspect_ratio` | `size` | `auto` / `1024x1024` / `1536x1024`（横長 3:2） / `1024x1536`（縦長 2:3） |
| `resolution` | `quality` | `auto` / `low` / `medium` / `high` |
| （なし） | `output_format` | `png` / `jpeg` / `webp` |

許容値の出典はインストール済み SDK（openai 4.104.0）の型定義です。

- `node_modules/openai/resources/images.d.ts:62` — `ImageModel = 'dall-e-2' | 'dall-e-3' | 'gpt-image-1'`
- `node_modules/openai/resources/images.d.ts:242-287` — `ImageGenerateParams`

`response_format` は送っていません。`gpt-image-1` は常に base64 を返し（`images.d.ts:47` "Default value for `gpt-image-1`"）、dall-e 系は既定で URL を返す（同 `:57` "Unsupported for `gpt-image-1`"）ため、モデルごとの分岐を持たずに両方の応答形を受けています。

### ファイル

- `src/tools/image-generation.ts` 新設 / `src/tools/nanobanana.ts` 削除
- `src/config.ts`: `NANOBANANA_MODEL` を廃止し `OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL` / `_SIZE` / `_QUALITY` / `_FORMAT` を追加
- `src/server.ts`: ツールスキーマとハンドラを更新
- `.mcp.json`: サーバ名 `nanobanana` → `chatgpt`
- `package.json`: 画像生成専用だった `@google/genai` を除去（lockfile 同期済み）
- `README.md` / `.env.example`: 移行内容を反映

## 対象外（意図的に残すもの）

`@google/generative-ai` と `GEMINI_API_KEY` は残しています。`/research` が `--model gemini --grounding` を引き続きサポートしており、`src/tools/web-research.ts` → `src/tools/gemini-completion.ts` が依存しているためです。当初は未使用と判断しかけましたが、`src/tools/` 内の import を追って現役だと確認しました。

## 検証

| 検証内容 | コマンド | 結果 |
|---|---|---|
| 型チェック・ビルド | `npm run build` | exit 0 PASS |
| ユニットテスト | `npm test` | 17 passed / 0 failed PASS |
| 旧値を弾くこと | テストケース「rejects the retired Gemini-era aspect ratio values」 | PASS |
| Gemini 参照の残存 | `grep -rn "nanobanana" src/` | 0 件 PASS |
| コミット前チェック | `make pre-git-check` | PASS |

実際の API 呼び出しによる生成確認は、`OPENAI_API_KEY` を使う従量課金のためマージ後に手動で行います（統合ジャーニーAC-1 は未実施）。

## マージ後の手順

`.mcp.json` のサーバ名が変わるため、次回セッションで `chatgpt` サーバの承認プロンプトが出ます。あわせてローカルスコープに残っている壊れた `nanobanana` エントリ（存在しない worktree パスを指し `CONNECTION_CLOSED` になる）を `claude mcp remove nanobanana -s local` で削除してください。

author: junseo2323
body:
`#438` 이 잡은 막다른 길 셋과 **같은 종류가 하나 더** 있었습니다. 인터뷰를 다 끝낸 화면에서 **판정으로 가는 길이 한 개도 없습니다.**

```
S-03(완료)   유일한 출구가 「손실 시뮬레이터로 확인하기」
S-04         출구가 다시 /interview/:sid   ← 248행 · 380행 둘 다 (실측)
             ⇒ 두 화면이 서로를 가리키고, S-05 는 브라우저 주소창으로만 닿는다
```

## 왜 여기는 열어도 되나 — 이 상태에서만 화면의 주인이 이미 바뀝니다

이 화면은 고객 화면(`role: CUST`)이고 S-05 는 등급·근거가 있는 판매자 화면이라 아무 자리에서나 열지 않습니다(`handoff-lost` 분기의 그 주석). 예외의 근거는 **바로 위 문면이 이미 «화면을 담당자에게 돌려주세요» 라고 말한다**는 것입니다 — 그 뒤 이 버튼을 누르는 사람은 판매자입니다.

바로 아래 분기가 이미 같은 논리로 서 있습니다(`#530` · 재검증 직후 「판정 결과로」). 다른 것은 **여기서는 시뮬레이터가 먼저라 2차로 내린다**는 것뿐입니다.

```
                      1차                        2차
재검증 직후 (#530)     판정 결과로                 —
인터뷰 완료 (이 PR)    손실 시뮬레이터로 확인하기    담당자용: 판정 결과로
```

**1차로 올리지 않습니다.** 명세 8절의 순서가 S-04 → S-05 이고 시뮬레이터는 아직 고객이 볼 화면입니다. 여기서 판정을 1차로 세우면 화면이 «이제 판정하러 가라» 고 말하게 되고 그 앞의 손실 확인이 건너뛰어집니다.

**재검증과 겹치지 않습니다** — `interviewDone` 이 `!reverifying` 을 이미 안고 있어서(156행) 재검증 직후에는 위 1차 하나만 남습니다.

## ❗거짓이 된 주석 하나를 같이 고칩니다

`handoff-lost` 분기가 링크를 안 여는 근거로 이걸 들고 있었습니다.

> *"그리고 S-03 에서 `/judgment/:sid` 로 가는 링크는 원래 **한 개도 없었다** — 이 화면이 그 첫 경로를 열 이유가 없다."*

`#530` 이 재검증 자리에 하나를 연 시점에 **이미 거짓**이었고, 이 PR 이 둘째를 엽니다. 근거를 바꿔 적었습니다 — 그 분기가 링크를 안 여는 진짜 이유는 전례가 아니라 **인계가 없어서 지금 화면 앞에 앉은 사람이 누구인지 화면이 모른다**는 것입니다. 결론(안 연다)은 그대로입니다.

## 데모 뒤 재검토

역할 가드(`Role`·`rbac_policy.yaml`)가 서면 이 버튼은 그 뒤로 옮깁니다 — 아래 대시보드 링크와 같은 처리입니다. 지금은 `SecurityConfig` 가 `permitAll()` 이라 막아 주는 층이 없다는 것을 알고 넣습니다.

## 잰 것

`tsc --noEmit` · `vite build` 통과. 화면은 조건부 버튼 하나라 **실행으로는 안 재봤습니다** — 리뷰에서 alpha 로 확인하시는 편이 정확합니다.

author: cycle-five
body:
Implements `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-partial-listings-and-in-page-pagination-design.md`. Bumps to **0.4.0**.

## The bug this starts from

Measured against the deployed `0.3.1` on 2026-09-07:

| request | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/playlist/37i9dQZF1DXcBWIGoYBM5M` (Today's Top Hits) | `extraction_incomplete`, **25 of 50**, 8–15s | **200, `complete: true`, 50 of 50, ~3.2s** |
| `/v1/album/5s5svl5DzlSmEvkjuL8Upw` | 60/60 | 60/60 |
| a 200-track playlist | never completed | full recovery, 7 pages, 4.5s |

Large editorial playlists were effectively unplayable, and the cause was not the parsing. `normalize.ts` already reads Spotify's internal pathfinder GraphQL responses — **the browser was never the data source.** It established a session and provoked those queries by *scrolling a virtualised list* up to 200 times at 350ms a step plus a 3s settle, choosing its scroll container by walking `querySelectorAll('*')` for the largest scrollable element. That heuristic was both symptoms: the 8–15s cold resolve, and the shortfall when it stopped early.

## Three changes, one subsystem

**1. Partial listings are opt-in.** A shortfall is reported on the listing as `complete: false` alongside `declaredItems`, rather than thrown. `?partial=allow` serves it as a 200; **without the flag a short listing still 502s exactly as before.** `withCache` gained an `acceptsCached` predicate, so a strict caller treats a cached partial as a miss and re-produces instead of being handed something it did not ask for.

Opt-in rather than always-200 because `design-notes.md` is right that a truncated playlist looks exactly like a complete one — serving partials by default would re-create the failure the completeness check exists to catch, for every consumer that does not know to look. Policy belongs to the caller; the service reports facts.

**2. Pagination replaces scrolling.** The page's own pathfinder request is harvested as a template and repeated with increasing offsets from inside the page, so the responses arrive through the existing `page.on('response')` listener into the same `Recorded[]`. `normalize.ts`, the counting rules and the whole recorded-fixture corpus are untouched. **The scroll loop is retained as the fallback** when no template can be harvested — it is not dead code.

**3. Fan-out caching.** A listing's tracks are written to `v1:track:<id>`. Album tracks are enriched with their parent album first — they list with `album: null` by design, so caching them verbatim would put album-less records where a later track lookup reads them. Podcast episodes are skipped: their url is `/episode/<id>` and they are not valid track responses.

## Why the phases shipped in this order

Pagination makes partials rare, not impossible — a navigation failure or a token expiring mid-loop still truncates. So partials are the degraded mode pagination still needs, which is why they landed first.

That ordering also creates the hazard this branch had to contain: **once a short listing is a legitimate response, any failure of pagination looks like the feature working.** It caught the plan itself — the original snippet fired `sawEntityData()` before `await response.json()`, so `recorded` was still empty when the race resolved, which would have meant a null declared total, zero fetches, and the same 25-track listing served as a perfectly valid partial. Caught in implementation, fixed by reading bodies through a promise array awaited both before the total is computed and after the loop.

Containment now: strict callers still get a 502, `partialListings{served}` moves either way, and three `console.warn` lines distinguish "a window failed" from "no template was harvested" from "the declared total was never found".

## Verification

- **147 passed / 9 skipped** (114 at the branch point), `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Live-verified against real Spotify by two independent agents; three cold-cache runs with `FLUSHALL` between, all 50/50.
- The pagination branch was confirmed to actually run by probing `recordResponses` directly, rather than inferring it from a green result.
- The failed-window warn was verified by routing every `offset > 0` pathfinder request to `abort('failed')`, so the page loads and exactly the pagination windows die.

Every task was reviewed independently, then the whole branch was reviewed as one change. That final pass found the two seams no single task owned — a strict waiter could stall for the full 150s produce budget, and fan-out fired on cache hits rather than on produce — plus a crash path where a wrong-shaped Redis value would throw synchronously inside a `void`-invoked async function with no `unhandledRejection` handler. All fixed and re-reviewed.

## Known follow-ups, not in this PR

- **Harvest has no entity affinity.** `isWindowedQuery` accepts any pathfinder POST carrying `variables.offset`; if a carousel query won that race we would page the wrong operation. Live runs passed, but the ordering is not guaranteed.
- **`v1:` cache keys predate the required fields.** A TypeScript required field is not a wire guarantee — values from Redis reach the route through a cast, so entries written before this branch serve without `declaredItems`/`complete` until they expire. The Rust client will model them as required.
- `ExtractionIncompleteError` is now unthrowable but keeps its routing arms, so `scrape_failures{reason="extraction_incomplete"}` reports zero forever.
- `?partial=true` and `?partial=1` silently mean strict.
- Spec §4 describes the strict-waiter case more narrowly than the code behaves.

## Downstream

`crack-sleevenote` needs to model `declaredItems`/`complete` and add the request flag; cracktunes then opts in and can say "queued 25 of 50" instead of refusing the link. Neither is in scope here.

author: fabiocicerchia
body:
Layer 3 of the refactoring sweep: the dependency hygiene that nothing else was going to do. Up to three independent commits, each reviewable on its own.

### `ci: run the editorconfig action on node24`

v2 of `editorconfig-checker/action-editorconfig-checker` declares `using: node20`. The runner forces it onto node24 and prints a deprecation warning on **every run in this estate**. v3.0.0 declares node24 outright.

The tool pin stays at `v3.11.3`. That pin exists because editorconfig-checker v4 renamed its release assets from `ec-*` to `editorconfig-checker-*`, and the v2 action only knew the old name. v3 asks for the current name **and falls back to the legacy prefix**, so v3.11.3 resolves exactly as before — and moving to the v4 tool becomes possible later, which it was not with v2.

### `ci: group the codeql-action updates`

`codeql-action/init` writes the analysis configuration and `codeql-action/analyze` reads it back. CodeQL refuses a mismatch outright:

> Loaded a configuration file for version 4.37.9, but running version 4.37.6

Dependabot proposed each step as its own pull request, so they merged at different times and drifted apart — which is exactly how the scan stopped running in several repos here. No dependabot config in the estate used `groups:`. One group means `init`, `analyze` and `upload-sarif` move together and cannot drift again.

### `ci: pin every codeql-action step to one release`

Where the steps had **already** drifted, they are realigned onto the newest release the repo already referenced. 12 repos needed this.

### `ci: let dependabot watch this repo's dependencies`

15 repos had no dependabot configuration at all, so their pinned actions had never been offered an update and never would be. They now match the estate's convention — weekly, 7-day cooldown — with the ecosystems each repo actually has, and the codeql group from the start.

---

Only `.github/` is touched; no source, no behaviour. Every generated file was checked to parse as YAML.

body:
24억 조합원입주권을 채무 6억으로 부담부증여하면 `applyOneRightExemption`이
`input.transferPrice`(= 소령 §159가 안분한 **채무액 B**)로 12억을 재어
6억 ≤ 12억 → **전액 비과세**로 판정했다.

| | 종전 (분모 = 채무액 B) | 정정 (분모 = 증여가액 C) |
|---|---|---|
| 12억 판정 | 6억 ≤ 12억 → **전액 비과세** | 24억 > 12억 → 안분 과세 |
| `isExempt` | true | false |
| 양도차익 | 0 | 235,625,000 |
| 산출세액 | **0** | 67,023,000 |
| 세액합계 | **0** | **73,725,300** |

## 착수를 막던 「해석 A와의 충돌」은 존재하지 않았다

PR #1544에서 이 지점을 🟠 U-8로 남긴 이유는 그 함수 주석의
「국세청 해석례 근거 — 분모 = transferPrice 단일(해석 A)」였다.
**본문을 읽으니 두 해석은 다른 질문에 답하고 있었다**
(taxlaw.nts.go.kr · Playwright 실독).

| | 사안 | 답한 질문 |
|---|---|---|
| 해석 A (3건) | **전부 유상 양도** | 고가입주권 **양도차익 산정 방법**(§95③·영 §160) · 분담금은 대가관계일 때만 산입 · 청산금 분모 미산입 |
| 해석 B (5건) | **부담부증여** | **고가 판정·안분 분모** = 전체 증여가액 |

해석 A는 법 §96①(「양도자와 양수자간에 실제로 거래한 가액」)을 전제하는데
부담부증여에는 그 「실지거래가액」이 **없다**. 해석 A 3건에 부담부증여 언급 **0건**.

- **서면4팀-1692**(2007.05.16 · 「주택의 부담부 증여시 고가주택 판단」)
  「고가주택의 판정은 … **부담부 증여이전 등 이전방식에 관계없이 1주택의 전체가액을
  기준으로 판정**하는 것이므로 … 고가주택 판정은 **당해 주택의 증여가액에 의하는 것**」
  ⭐ 질의 사실관계가 「양도가액을 **채무액 3억으로 보아야 하는지**」였고 답은 **아니다**였다.
- **서면4팀-1526**(2004.09.24) — 영 §160①1호의 「양도가액은 〔채무액 × (전체증여가액 ÷
  채무액)〕을 적용」 = **전체 증여가액**.

## 입주권에도 같은 이유

해석 A 자신이 「입주권이 요건을 충족하면 이를 **법 §89①3호에서 규정하는 고가주택으로 보아**
§95③ · 영 §160으로 계산한다」고 밝힌다. 현행 §89①**4호 단서**(「해당 조합원입주권의
**양도 당시 실지거래가액**이 12억원을 초과하는 경우」)도 3호 괄호(「**양도 당시 실지거래가액의
합계액**이 12억원을 초과하는 고가주택은 제외」)와 같은 문언 구조다.

## 구조

비교와 안분을 **한 상수(`highValueBase`)로 묶었다** — 분모가 갈리면
「12억을 넘는다」고 판정해 놓고 다른 분모로 나누게 된다(완공 APT 경로에서 그 어긋남이
`taxableRatio = −1`을 만든 실측이 #1543에 있다). `??`가 아니라 `> 0` 판정이다.

🔴 **일반 양도 경로는 무변경**이다 — `burdenedGiftDenominator`가 없으면 `transferPrice`
그대로이며 해석 A가 지지하는 동작이다. 대조군 anchor 2건으로 고정했다.

body:
## Implementation qualified

Stacks on PR #26 (`feat/localization-presentation`) and implements accepted v3.2.1 Task 15: CLI-only permanent logical Hero deletion with tombstoned mutation receipts and anti-resurrection semantics.

### Permanent logical delete
- Adds `DeleteHeroPermanentlyAsync` to the Application/admin persistence boundary.
- Uses one non-deferred Serializable SQLite writer transaction.
- Rejects the active default Hero with `HP145`.
- Rejects any Hero with an open Quest with `HP143`.
- Marks all surviving Hero-bound mutation receipts `result_status=target_deleted` before deleting the Hero.
- Deletes Hero-owned Quest history/projections via the already-qualified FK cascade graph.
- Does not alter Projects/catalog rows or erase surviving minimal mutation receipts.

### Anti-resurrection / idempotency
- Common receipt verification now reads `result_status`.
- Canonical encoding/hash comparison still runs first, preserving `HP135` for a reused request ID with changed intent.
- An exact retry whose original target was subsequently deleted returns safe `HP140 hero_not_found` semantics.
- Late Create/Start/Finish retries therefore never recreate the Hero/Quest or expose deleted history.

### CLI-only destructive surface
- Adds `hero delete --hero-id <uuidv7> --confirm-logical-delete [--json]`.
- Explicit confirmation is required even though the option is also parser-required.
- Help/human output states that deletion is logical application-state deletion and is **not forensic erasure**.
- JSON output is bounded to `heroId`, `deleted`, `deletionScope`, and `forensicErasure=false`.
- No delete tool was added to HP-MCP/2; exact MCP Contract tests remain unchanged and green.

### Integrity qualification
The Application delete test proves:
- active/open-Quest guards;
- Hero removal;
- Quest/history/projection cascade cleanup;
- three associated Create/Start/Finish receipts survive as `target_deleted`;
- no associated active receipts survive;
- exact late Create/Start/Finish retries return HP140;
- `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` returns no violations.

### TDD evidence
- RED CI #536: build failed only because `DeleteHeroPermanentlyAsync` did not yet exist.
- Core GREEN CI #540: full pipeline passed after transactional tombstone/delete and common receipt handling were implemented.
- CLI RED CI #541: Build/Core/Infrastructure/Contract remained green; exactly the two new App tests failed because `hero delete` did not exist.
- Intermediate CI #542: command/help/behavior worked; exactly one App assertion failed because the actionable HP300 message did not name `--confirm-logical-delete`.
- Final GREEN CI #543 on head `e9862bae58768fc0b47b7fff718db7acb967e4b2` passed end-to-end:
  - Build: success, 0 warnings / 0 errors
  - Architecture: pass
  - Domain: 135/135
  - Application: 53/53
  - Infrastructure: 21/21
  - Contract: 9/9
  - App: pass, including CLI logical delete subprocess coverage
  - Agent Skill evals: pass
  - Publish packaged app: pass
  - Packaged vertical E2E: pass

### Final review
- Diff against PR #26 base is 7 expected files only: Application/admin boundary, receipt tombstone handling, transactional Hero delete, CLI command, and focused tests.
- No migration/schema change is required because v3.2.1 schema already includes `target_deleted` and receipt IDs intentionally have no FK.
- No MCP tool/schema/game-rule changes.
- No review comments or unresolved review threads.

### Official documentation check
Implementation follows current official SQLite foreign-key cascade semantics, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite transaction guidance, and current System.CommandLine command/option/action APIs.

PR remains draft because it is stacked on draft PR #26.

author: yoshiki0705
body:
## Summary

FSx-for-ONTAP-Adoption-Playbook cites thirty-two claims here and registers an exact substring per citation, failing its own gate when the substring is gone. That is the intended design — a retraction here surfaces there rather than leaving a stale sentence behind — but it put the discovery in the wrong place. **The person who reworded the sentence learned about it from another repository's CI**, and until it was fixed the guidance over there was published without the evidence under it.

This moves the discovery to the commit that causes it.

## Changes

- `tools/check_incoming_probes.py`, new. Reads the contract the sibling publishes; `retraction` fails, `reread` warns.
- `make incoming-probes`, in `all` and in `ci.yml`. `--fetch` in `link-rot.yml`.
- `tests/test_incoming_probes.py`, 16 cases pinning the format decisions.

The mirror of `check_external_anchors.py`, which already does this in the other direction. It reads the published contract rather than parsing the sibling's index — a second reader of a markdown table is a second thing to be wrong.

## Each probe is an opaque byte substring, and nothing is normalised

The sibling's escaping is not uniform, and all three shapes were verified against the real contract:

| Registered | In our files |
|---|---|
| `倍率 2.97 は **1,500 ÷ 500 = 3.0** に一致しており` | identical — **emphasis is part of the claim** |
| ``EFS は `nconnect` にも非対応`` | without the outer double backticks — that wrapper is the table's escaping |
| `3,551〜5,149 MB/s` | without the `**` that surrounds it here |

Stripping emphasis to be helpful would make the first match text that no longer holds the claim. Failing to strip the table's wrapper would make the second never match and report a false break. So: plain substring test, no transformation.

## Two roles, because they are not the same question

- **`retraction`** must survive. Its absence means the claim moved or was withdrawn and the citation lost its evidence. **Fails.**
- **`reread`** pins the minimum and maximum of a measurement set, so adding a measurement rewrites it by construction. **Warns.** Both measurements #88 asked for will fire one.

Seven `retraction` probes carry an *absence* ("not confirmed", "not listed as supported"). Those go missing when the absence stops being true — progress, not a withdrawal — and that is exactly the case this repository has to report rather than let a gate discover. Which is why they fail rather than warn.

## Three paths where a check could report a skip as a pass are closed

1. **An unknown role fails** rather than skipping the row, so the vocabulary cannot grow and quietly drop a probe from coverage.
2. **A contract that parses but holds no row for this repository fails.** Thirty-two were registered; zero means a changed repository name or field order, not an empty registration.
3. **`CONTRACT_PUBLISHED` decides what a 404 from `--fetch` means** — absent before publication, removed after. The response cannot tell those apart, and deriving it from a local checkout cannot either, since CI has none and `--fetch` is the only thing that runs there. So it is an explicit switch, and a test watches that it gets flipped.

## Known limits, stated rather than discovered later

- **Moving the contract's path is the one change that silently returns this to skipping.** Every other format change fails loudly. The path is an interface, and the sibling has been asked to announce a move.
- **Retiring a citation is not detected.** A row leaving the sibling's table passes here silently. That registry is their asset, so this is intended.
- **Green today reads an unmerged branch of a local checkout.** The contract is not on the sibling's `main` yet, so `--fetch` skips and `CONTRACT_PUBLISHED` is `False`. Flipping it is one line once they merge.

## Testing

- [x] `make all` green on this branch, after the last edit — `incoming-probes: 32 probe(s) resolve (30 retraction, 2 reread)`
- [x] Verified green independently of #122, which shares no file with this branch
- [x] 16 new tests exercise the parser without needing the sibling checked out
- [x] `gitleaks` clean

## Claim changes

**None.** No document changed. This adds a gate over claims that already exist, and all thirty-two currently resolve.

## Blocked features

Flipping `CONTRACT_PUBLISHED` to `True`, which waits on the sibling merging its contract to `main`.

author: sidbai
body:
The team's name often says neither — `Top Ballers`, `Lightning`, `SPFC` — and the flight it was entered in says both: `Boys U15 Gold`, `Girls-U11 - Silver`, `Boys-U10 - Silver 1`.

## What it recovers

| | |
|---|---|
| teams with no gender whose division names one | **227 of 227** |
| teams with no birth years whose division states an age group | **75 of 93** |

Dry run against production confirms it: `75 more from a U-number and the event's season`, `227 get a gender`.

That is the entire gender gap, and most of the cohort gap, from data already in the database.

## The team's own name still wins

A name is about the team; a division is about the flight it entered. They almost always agree, and where they do not the team is the better authority on itself — `XF GU12 White` in a `Boys U15 Gold` flight stays girls, U12.

Both the importer and the backfill read it, so a team arriving tomorrow and one imported in August get the same facts from the same rule.

## One thing the tests taught me

My first fixture was `XF GU12 B09/10`, which claims girls *and* boys — `B09` is a boys marker, which is exactly how `90+ B17-18 Valdez` is read. `parseGender` correctly returns null for a name claiming both, and the division then supplied the answer. The test was wrong, not the code, but it is a real property worth knowing.

746 unit, 173 db, typecheck, lint, build. No migration.

## To apply

```bash
pnpm db:backfill:teams --apply --names
```

author: fabiocicerchia
body:
Layer 3 of the refactoring sweep: the dependency hygiene that nothing else was going to do. Up to three independent commits, each reviewable on its own.

### `ci: run the editorconfig action on node24`

v2 of `editorconfig-checker/action-editorconfig-checker` declares `using: node20`. The runner forces it onto node24 and prints a deprecation warning on **every run in this estate**. v3.0.0 declares node24 outright.

The tool pin stays at `v3.11.3`. That pin exists because editorconfig-checker v4 renamed its release assets from `ec-*` to `editorconfig-checker-*`, and the v2 action only knew the old name. v3 asks for the current name **and falls back to the legacy prefix**, so v3.11.3 resolves exactly as before — and moving to the v4 tool becomes possible later, which it was not with v2.

### `ci: group the codeql-action updates`

`codeql-action/init` writes the analysis configuration and `codeql-action/analyze` reads it back. CodeQL refuses a mismatch outright:

> Loaded a configuration file for version 4.37.9, but running version 4.37.6

Dependabot proposed each step as its own pull request, so they merged at different times and drifted apart — which is exactly how the scan stopped running in several repos here. No dependabot config in the estate used `groups:`. One group means `init`, `analyze` and `upload-sarif` move together and cannot drift again.

### `ci: pin every codeql-action step to one release`

Where the steps had **already** drifted, they are realigned onto the newest release the repo already referenced. 12 repos needed this.

### `ci: let dependabot watch this repo's dependencies`

15 repos had no dependabot configuration at all, so their pinned actions had never been offered an update and never would be. They now match the estate's convention — weekly, 7-day cooldown — with the ecosystems each repo actually has, and the codeql group from the start.

---

Only `.github/` is touched; no source, no behaviour. Every generated file was checked to parse as YAML.

I hereby agree to the terms of the [RisingWave Labs, Inc. Contributor License Agreement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/risingwavelabs/risingwave/17af8a747593ebdbfa826691daf75bdab7d14fa0/.github/contributor-license-agreement.txt). ## What's changed and what's your intention? Draft for reviewing an experimental, single-compute-node SST-level pin cache. - Persist an exact physical table selection through the existing streaming-job developer configuration, including an internal table owned by that job. - Cache complete SST objects in a worker-local OpenDAL filesystem sidecar. Remote object storage remains authoritative. - Keep desired-object membership in a separate pin-refill controller. Version deltas schedule whole-SST downloads within the existing refiller/version barrier; ordinary reads never fill the pin cache. - Route reads only to complete, published local objects. Local failures invalidate that publication and use the existing fallback path. - Withdraw stale routes before bounded asynchronous exact-path deletion. Recover complete local files against the initial policy and version snapshot at startup. - Add focused regression coverage for policy propagation, publication/cancellation, recovery, cleanup accounting, and read fallback. Propagate OpenDAL listing/stat failures instead of silently treating a partial listing as EOF. The feature is disabled by default. SET does not warm existing SSTs. Warm, read-through repair, rescale/vnode placement, L0 lifetime admission, and durable GC retries are outside this prototype. Known limitations to review: - Pending or failed cleanup continues to consume accounted capacity; a delta refill can be skipped before capacity becomes available. - Failed/cancelled uploads conservatively retain their reservation until startup recovery. - Independently pinned split-SST branches sharing one physical object can lose local residency early; remote fallback preserves reads. ## Checklist - [x] I have written necessary rustdoc comments. - [x] I have added necessary unit tests and integration tests. - [ ] I have added test labels as necessary. - [ ] I have added fuzzing tests or opened an issue to track them. - [ ] My PR contains breaking changes. - [ ] My PR changes performance-critical code, so I will run (micro) benchmarks and present the results. - [ ] I have checked the Release Timeline and Currently Supported Versions to determine which release branches I need to cherry-pick this PR into. ## Documentation - [ ] My PR needs documentation updates.

body:
> ARTEL-849 (#16) 위에 쌓은 PR 이다. base 가 그 branch 이므로 이 PR 의 diff 는 이 이슈의 변경만 담는다. #16 이 merge 되면 base 를 `main` 으로 바꾼다.

## Why

`StoredCredential.apiBaseUrl` 은 이미 파일에 적히고 있었는데, 읽는 곳이 `auth status` 의 보고뿐이었다. 아무 명령도 그 값을 쓰지 않아서, 로그인한 뒤에도 명령마다 `--api-url` 이나 `ARTEL_API_BASE_URL` 을 다시 요구했다. 주소를 매번 손으로 적는 일은 staging 자격증명으로 운영을 부르는 사고를 연다.

## What Changed

주소의 우선순위가 `--api-url`, `ARTEL_API_BASE_URL`, 자격증명 파일의 `apiBaseUrl` 이 되었다. `auth status` 는 실제로 쓰일 값과 그 출처를 보고한다.

## Example

빌드 산출물에서 실제로 돈 것이다. 자격증명 파일에는 `https://stored.example.test` 가 적혀 있다.

```
$ ARTEL_CONFIG_DIR=$CFG artel auth status
Signed in.
  cli version       0.0.1-alpha.0
  fingerprint       9b7a08a52f16
  credentials file  .../credentials.json (mode 0600)
  ARTEL_TOKEN       not set
  token name        artel-cli@laptop
  token id          01JXDEMO
  expires at        never
  api base url      https://stored.example.test (from credentials file)

$ ARTEL_CONFIG_DIR=$CFG ARTEL_API_BASE_URL=https://env.example.test artel auth status
  api base url      https://env.example.test (from ARTEL_API_BASE_URL)

$ ARTEL_CONFIG_DIR=$CFG ARTEL_TOKEN=artel_from_env artel auth status
  api base url      not set (pass --api-url, set ARTEL_API_BASE_URL, or sign in)
```

세 번째가 이 변경의 경계다. `ARTEL_TOKEN` 으로 들어온 자격증명에는 짝지어진 주소가 없으므로 파일에 적힌 주소를 빌려주지 않는다.

## Code Walkthrough

- `src/config.ts:79` — `effectiveApiBaseUrl` 이 환경 변수와 파일 사이의 순서를 아는 유일한 자리다. 검증하지 않는다. `auth status` 가 이것을 그대로 부르고, 보고하는 명령이 값이 이상하다는 이유로 죽으면 안 되기 때문이다. 그 값이 실제로 쓰이는 자리에서 `invalid_base_url` 로 걸린다.
- `src/config.ts:110` — `resolveApiBaseUrl` 이 그 위에 flag 층과 검증과 실패를 얹는다. 실패 메시지가 `artel auth login --api-url <url>` 을 안내한다. 파일을 직접 읽지 않고 인자로 받는 이유는 의존 방향이다 — `commands` 가 `credentials` 와 `config` 를 둘 다 부르고 반대 간선은 없다.
- `src/qa/context.ts`, `src/case/context.ts`, `src/scenario/context.ts`, `src/testRuns/context.ts`, `src/doc/context.ts` — 자격증명을 먼저 읽고 그 값을 넘긴다. 다섯을 하나로 합치지 않았다: `testRuns/context.ts` 의 주석이 별도로 두는 이유를 이미 적어 두었고 (도메인이 다르고, `resolveQaContext` 를 test run 명령이 부르면 두 도메인이 얽혀 있다고 읽힌다) 이 변경이 그 판단을 뒤집을 이유가 없다.
- `src/commands/game/start.ts:42`, `src/commands/game/logout.ts`, `src/commands/qa/matrix.ts` — 같은 순서로 바꾼다.
- `src/commands/auth/status.ts:26` — `effectiveApiBaseUrl` 로 실제 값과 출처를 채운다. `ARTEL_TOKEN` 경로에서는 `reportOf` 가 이미 `apiBaseUrl` 을 `null` 로 주므로 파일 값이 새어 들어가지 않는다.
- `src/output/contract.ts:31` — `apiBaseUrl` 의 뜻이 "파일에 적힌 값" 에서 "명령이 실제로 부를 주소" 로 바뀌고, 출처는 새 키 `apiBaseUrlSource` 가 말한다. 키를 더하는 것은 계약을 깨지 않는다. 뜻이 달라지는 것은 환경 변수가 설정된 경우뿐이고, 그 경우 기존 값은 status 와 실제 동작이 어긋난 값이었다.
- `src/output/human.ts:88` — `describeApiBaseUrl` 이 값과 출처를 함께 적는다. 값만 적으면 환경 변수를 지웠을 때 왜 주소가 달라졌는지 이 출력으로 설명되지 않는다.
- `tests/game-start.test.ts:265` — console pairing 테스트에 자격증명을 심었다. 이 명령이 자격증명을 먼저 읽게 되면서, 서명하지 않은 상태로는 `no_credential` 이 먼저 걸려 그 테스트가 보려는 규칙까지 가지 못했다.
- `tests/api-base-url.test.ts` — 우선순위 세 단계, `ARTEL_TOKEN` 경계, `auth status` 의 출처 보고를 본다.
- `tests/config.test.ts` — `effectiveApiBaseUrl` 과 새 fallback 층의 단위 테스트.

## Risks

- 순서가 바뀌면서 "로그인도 안 했고 주소도 없는" 경우의 오류 코드가 `missing_api_base_url` 에서 `no_credential` 로 바뀐다. 두 코드 모두 계약에 남아 있고 다른 경로에서 여전히 나온다. 그 조합을 코드로 분기하던 script 가 있으면 영향을 받는다.
- `auth status --json` 의 `apiBaseUrl` 값이 `ARTEL_API_BASE_URL` 이 설정된 환경에서 달라진다. 그 전 값은 status 와 실제 동작이 어긋난 값이었으므로 고친 것으로 본다.

## Validation

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm test` — 25 files, 252 tests 통과 (`api-base-url.test.ts` 8 개, `config.test.ts` 10 개 추가)
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] 빌드 산출물로 위 Example 세 경우를 실제로 확인

## Rollback

`effectiveApiBaseUrl` 과 세 번째 인자를 되돌리고 context 다섯 개의 순서를 원래대로 두면 이전 상태다. `apiBaseUrlSource` 를 지우는 것은 계약에서 키를 지우는 것이므로 `json-contract.test.ts` 도 함께 되돌려야 한다.

body:
The local-time resolver matched only year/month/day/hour/minute. A four-second historical gap in Manaus was incorrectly marked ordinary, while nearby ordinary times received false fold flags. Match complete seconds and milliseconds before classifying candidates, preserving actual historical offsets and the existing earlier-fold/forward-gap policies.

Engine candidate `0.1.1-rc.6`, stacked on #10 (`codex/platform-input-flags`, base `224863eb`). Source `fb57af7a2cd7c30983cc8fb655183d5a11f9cf30`; immutable 23-file archive at carrier `51129a197cd3f2a2a8c966fb797ea4da1e147b3d`, SHA-256 `09c3e63432f8ba2e9df05af137c42f65ab039740a207a89418d9e6470ea3db3e`. Runtime changes are confined to timezone matching and the version. The receipt schema, numerical formulas, site/starter pins and optional read-only ownership SDK remain unchanged.

Validation:
- 579 tests / 32 files on Node 22.23.2 and Node 24.19.0; required workspace build, lint, typecheck, format, package/export/checksum/neutrality and TypeDoc checks pass.
- Two fresh consumers validate the exact packed archive, public runtime imports and TypeScript.
- Independent copied-source review: 278 Node cases and 37 actual Chrome cases; 140 and 15 expected flag corrections respectively, with zero tested instant/offset/numerical changes. Seven actual receipt/replay controls per runtime and separate malformed/settings controls pass.
- The initial 14 regression tests fail 10/14 on the original source. Preserve those failures, raw harness mistakes, exact identities and limitations in `docs/platform/evidence/time-seconds/`.

The original three-sample offset policy is retained; this does not certify complete transition discovery, historical timezone facts or a broad astronomical range. Separate site date-endpoint findings are documented for their own correction. No saved receipt or old artifact is rewritten. Existing SDK #5 do-not-merge/do-not-publish hold and required human/expert/legal review remain. This draft does not publish to npm or deploy the site. Existing SDK CI only targets main PRs; stacked CI acceptance is not claimed.

Rollback: restore the prior candidate source/pin together; retain old artifacts and receipts. Downstream site adoption requires its own reviewed source/artifact pairing and verification.

author: fabiocicerchia
body:
Layer 3 of the refactoring sweep: the dependency hygiene that nothing else was going to do. Up to three independent commits, each reviewable on its own.

### `ci: run the editorconfig action on node24`

v2 of `editorconfig-checker/action-editorconfig-checker` declares `using: node20`. The runner forces it onto node24 and prints a deprecation warning on **every run in this estate**. v3.0.0 declares node24 outright.

The tool pin stays at `v3.11.3`. That pin exists because editorconfig-checker v4 renamed its release assets from `ec-*` to `editorconfig-checker-*`, and the v2 action only knew the old name. v3 asks for the current name **and falls back to the legacy prefix**, so v3.11.3 resolves exactly as before — and moving to the v4 tool becomes possible later, which it was not with v2.

### `ci: group the codeql-action updates`

`codeql-action/init` writes the analysis configuration and `codeql-action/analyze` reads it back. CodeQL refuses a mismatch outright:

> Loaded a configuration file for version 4.37.9, but running version 4.37.6

Dependabot proposed each step as its own pull request, so they merged at different times and drifted apart — which is exactly how the scan stopped running in several repos here. No dependabot config in the estate used `groups:`. One group means `init`, `analyze` and `upload-sarif` move together and cannot drift again.

### `ci: pin every codeql-action step to one release`

Where the steps had **already** drifted, they are realigned onto the newest release the repo already referenced. 12 repos needed this.

### `ci: let dependabot watch this repo's dependencies`

15 repos had no dependabot configuration at all, so their pinned actions had never been offered an update and never would be. They now match the estate's convention — weekly, 7-day cooldown — with the ecosystems each repo actually has, and the codeql group from the start.

---

Only `.github/` is touched; no source, no behaviour. Every generated file was checked to parse as YAML.

## Co wchodzi w ten PR (5 commitów)

### 1. Naprawa krytyczna: formularz kontaktowy (500)
`POST /kontakt/` wywalał się na autoresponderze (silnik wymagał pól rezerwacji, których wiadomość kontaktowa nie ma). Teraz: wpis zapisuje się w panelu (Wiadomości), Studio dostaje powiadomienie, klient potwierdzenie; walidacja pokazuje błędy zamiast białego ekranu.

### 2. Intuicyjna ścieżka zamówienia
- Wybór personalizacji **nie ginie** przy nawigacji (parametr `pers` + pasek `_pers_bar.html` ze „zmień"/„usuń wybór").
- Pasek kroków na każdej podstronie zamówienia.
- Jeden jasny CTA przy kalendarzu zamiast dwóch konkurujących przycisków.
- Po błędzie walidacji formularz wraca wypełniony.

### 3. Hub ZAMÓWIENIA + kreator wg flowcharta (sekcje A/B/C)
- `/zamowienia/` — 3 kafle (Wynajem dekoracji / Personalizacja / Sklep), krem/brąz/shadow, nagłówki butelkowa zieleń + złote litery.
- **A wynajem**: 1 Kalendarz → 2 Pakiet (tylko dostępne w terminie + lista niedostępnych) → 3 Personalizacja (pomiń) → 4 Dane → 5 Podsumowanie → 6 Dziękujemy.
- **B personalizacja samodzielna**: 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 (katalog + pole „opisz pomysł").
- **C sklep**: 7 Katalog (ilości) → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6.
- Bloki 4/5/6 **wspólne** dla wszystkich sekcji (jedna trasa, warianty per typ).
- Progress bar wypełniający się na złoto, dopasowany do sekcji; krok pominięty oznaczony.
- Stan kreatora w tabeli `szkice` (klucz `?w=` — działa bez ciasteczek); edycja wstecz aktualizuje szkic.
- Finalizacja: rezerwacja + sygnatura + autoresponder (dokumenty, dane do przelewu) + arkusz Google.

### 4. Sklep i kody rabatowe
- Tabela `sklep_produkty` (4 produkty startowe — **ceny robocze**), CRUD w panelu: `/admin/sklep`.
- Kody rabatowe: Ustawienia → `KOD:procent` (np. `WESELE5:5`), rabat od najmu+personalizacji/produktów (nie od kaucji).

### 5. Menu i drobne
- Menu główne: Start / Realizacje / **Zamówienia** / Kontakt (serwis + v4 + docs).
- Nowe kolumny rezerwacji: dostawa/adres/kod/dodatkowe + widok w panelu.
- Mail do Studia: „NOWE ZAMÓWIENIE — TYP" z pełnym składem i kwotami.

## Testy
Wszystkie 3 ścieżki end-to-end (curl na żywym serwerze), regresja starego przepływu (`/api/rezerwuj`), panel admina (7 zakładek + CRUD sklepu), formularz kontaktowy z/bez zgody PKE, 17 podstron = 200.

## Uwagi dla wdrażającego
Po mergu: `git pull` + Reload na PythonAnywhere; w panelu ustawić realne ceny sklepu i opcjonalnie kody rabatowe.

author: mazen-alhassan
body: This adds a `--sarif` flag to `sparrow scan` that writes findings in SARIF 2.1.0 alongside the usual JSON, so a run can upload straight to GitHub code scanning. Each advisory becomes a rule, bucket maps to level (reachable/undetermined/unreachable -> error/warning/note), and a location is attached whenever a call path pins one down; a small path-shortening helper already used by the terminal renderer is reused for the location URI. This is an automated Claude Code maintenance pass, and `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` passes (93 tests, including new coverage for the SARIF conversion).

body:
## 改动内容

清理 `content/sutras-raw/` 下「現代語譯」段落中 LLM 翻译时漏出的外语词，共 1071 个文件、约 1580 处，全部逐处对照同节「原文」替换为正确中文，替换词繁简跟随各文件正文用字。

### 修复范围

- **第一轮**（968 文件，约 1350 处）：天城文（निश्चित→決定/一定/確定，按论疏语境）、希伯来文（כולם→全都、לכן→所以）、乌尔都文（ہمیشہ→恆常）、阿拉伯文（كلها→全都）、格鲁吉亚文（აღარ→不再）、韩文（내려→降下）、泰文、希腊/西里尔文等
- **第二轮**（161 文件，约 180 处，原检测正则未覆盖）：孟加拉文（দ্রুত→迅速、ফিরে→返回、জন্ম→出生）、亚美尼亚文（ցույց→顯示、միշտ→總是）、卡纳达/泰卢固/缅甸文
- 7 处日语漏出（また→另外、だから→所以、これは→這是、の→的、ここ→這）
- 6 处「伊字三点」被 LLM 错加的（ॐ）/（इ）/（イ）括注已删除（伊字指悉昙字母「伊」，非 ॐ）
- 4 处注音符号「ㄧ」误代汉字「一」

### 经 CBETA 底本核对后保留的内容

- 日本传承文献原有训点假名与奥书：T1723 各卷、T1840/T1841/T1842、X0925，以及 X0678-002「必ス」、X0686-002「此ス」、X0969/X0979「縱ミ」（均从 cbeta-org/xml-p5 底本逐一核对为原文）
- CBETA 组字式中的注音形（`[半*ㄆ]`、`[(ㄙ*ㄙ)/蚨]`）、IAST 梵文转写（ā/ś/ṇ）、拼音声调注音、制表符表格

### 审阅提示

- 全部改动为逐行同长度替换（1484 行内容改动 + 受改文件 `updated_at` 更新为 2026-09-07），无结构性变更，front matter 除 `updated_at` 外未动
- 复验：两轮检测正则对 `content/sutras-raw/` 全库均已清零

body:
앞선 리뷰 라운드들에서 「지적 범위 밖」으로 미뤄 두었던 것들이다. 새 지적이 아니라 밀린 빚을 갚는 PR.

## 1. `PageHeader` 의 고정 예약폭

제목 좌우로 `7rem` 만 비워서, `rightSlot` 이 56px 을 넘는 순간 가운데 제목과 겹쳤다. 지난 라운드에 프레임 편집기가 자기 슬롯을 줄여 피했을 뿐 함정은 그대로였다.

칸이 실제 내용 폭을 갖는 그리드로 바꿨다. 하한을 `auto` 가 아니라 **`max-content`** 로 잡은 것이 핵심이다 — `1fr` 로 두면 320px 에서 오른쪽 버튼이 먼저 찌그러져 「수정 저장」이 알약 안에서 두 줄이 된다. 양보하는 쪽은 「자르지 않고 줄바꿈한다」고 이미 규정된 제목이어야 한다.

절대 배치를 정당화하던 주석(「제목이 양쪽 내용 길이와 무관하게 정확히 가운데 온다」)은 이제 참이 아니므로 다시 썼다.

실측(시스템 Chrome, 320/390/1280):
- 150px 슬롯 주입 시 **320px 에서 +37.69 겹침 → −12.00 여유**, 390px 에서 +2.69 → −12.00
- 소비처 7곳(`/shoot`·`capture`·`select`·`upload`·`result`·`/theme`·프레임 편집기) 가로 기하 **변화 0**
- 헤더 높이 280~1920px 전 구간 44px 유지

**눈에 보이는 변화 하나** — `/theme` 의 「보관 n/m」 칩이 세로로 13px 내려간다. 옛 `top-0` 은 절대 배치라 어딘가 고정해야 해서 붙은 값이고, 이제 제목과 같은 세로 중앙에 선다.

## 2. 약관 동의 자리의 고정 팔레트

결함이 두 겹이었다.

- **면**: 다크에서 `bg-zinc-900/40` 이 카드(`#18181a`) 위에 `#171718` 로 합성돼 대비 **1.01** — 행 경계가 보이지 않았다
- **글자**: `zinc-500` 이 다크에서 `--hc-muted-soft`(`#6f6f73`)로 풀려 11~13px 이 **3.58:1 로 AA 미달**이었다(지금 9.06:1)

같은 두 겹이 `TermsReconsentDialog` · `TermsConsentFieldset` 에도 있어 함께 고쳤다. 세 곳 모두 사용자 테마를 따르는 앱 화면이다(`signup` 은 `AuthPageShell` 의 `hc-page-app`, 재동의 다이얼로그는 `TermsConsentBridge` 로 앱 전역).

`text-zinc-300` 한 곳은 `--hc-text`/`--hc-muted` 어느 쪽과도 값이 달라 1:1 치환이 안 되고 대비도 안전해서 남겼다.

## 3. 마이페이지 배너

기록 화면이 받은 것과 같은 고정 띠. 새 토스트나 추상은 만들지 않고 `history/page.tsx` 의 것을 그대로 가져왔다.

실측 — 「회원 탈퇴」를 누르면 배너 `top` 이 390px 에서 **−109px**, 요금제를 펼치면 **−347px**, 1280px 에서 **−1035px** 로 전부 화면 밖이었다. 수정 후 +8 / +76 으로 들어온다. axe 는 두 뷰포트 × 라이트·다크 8회 스캔 전부 위반 0.

## 4. storybook 10.6.0 정렬

`@storybook/react` 만 10.6.0 이고 `@storybook/nextjs-vite` 는 10.3.6 이라, nextjs-vite 가 자기 밑에 `@storybook/react` 10.3.6 사본을 따로 들고 있었다. 스토리는 10.6.0 타입으로 검사받고 렌더링은 10.3.6 으로 되는 상태였다.

정렬 후 `@storybook/react` · `@storybook/nextjs-vite` · `storybook` 모두 10.6.0 단일 사본이고 unmet peer 경고도 사라졌다.

## 검증

로컬에서 9단계 통과 — `install --frozen-lockfile` · `lint:web` · `test:web`(71 suites / 645 tests) · `build:web` · `lint:mobile` · `typecheck:mobile` · `check:classes:web` · 계약 테스트 9개 · `build-storybook`.

레이아웃 수치는 전부 시스템 Chrome 을 직접 구동해 실측했다. 이 머신은 Playwright 번들 브라우저를 받지 못해(`SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`) `test:e2e` 를 못 돌린다 — **e2e 검증은 이 PR 의 CI 다.**

## 하지 않은 것

`pnpm test:visual:update:web` — 기준 스냅샷이 낡았지만(이 PR 의 `PageHeader` 변경으로 더 낡아진다) 우분투 CI 와 폰트 렌더링이 다른 윈도우에서 baseline 을 만들면 틀린 기준을 박는다. 리눅스 환경에서 갱신하는 것이 맞다. `test:visual` 은 CI 에 없어 아무것도 막지 않는다.

author: me-solarau
body:
One Meta gateway for Billy's new channels — Facebook Messenger and WhatsApp — feeding the same lead-agent brain, threads, caps and pricing rules as SMS.

**meta-inbound (new edge function, deployed v1)**
- GET: Meta's verification handshake against `MESSENGER_VERIFY_TOKEN`.
- POST: requires a valid `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 with `META_APP_SECRET`, constant-time compare) — unsigned/forged events are rejected, so nobody can puppet Billy.
- Parses both `page` (Messenger) and `whatsapp_business_account` events; text, images (as `[photo: …]` lines), buttons and quick replies forward to lead-agent as `channel_inbound`; echoes and delivery/read receipts are skipped; always answers 200 fast so Meta never disables the webhook.

**lead-agent (deployed v8)**
- `agent_threads.channel` (`sms|messenger|whatsapp`) with per-channel reply routing: Kudosity for SMS, Graph send API for Messenger, WhatsApp Cloud API for WhatsApp.
- WhatsApp's wa_id IS the phone number, so WhatsApp chats continue the same thread and memory as SMS with that customer. Messenger threads key on `fb:<psid>`; the lead is created without a mobile and Billy asks for one once qualified, writing it back to the customer record.
- All existing guards unchanged: message caps, hourly cap, loop guards, suppressions, location-first qualification, marketplace-calibrated pricing.

**0096_agent_threads_channel.sql** — repo copy of the already-applied migration, documenting the thread-key semantics.

Secrets to set (Supabase): `MESSENGER_VERIFY_TOKEN`, `META_APP_SECRET`, `META_PAGE_TOKEN`, `WA_TOKEN`, `WA_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`.
