author: vibecoderst
body:
Merges `Develop` into `milestone/pruning`.

Raised as a pull request rather than pushed directly because `milestone/pruning` is gated by a required-status-checks ruleset (Issue #586). That gate is what makes this PR auto-mergeable — GitHub arms auto-merge only when something blocks the merge — so this lands unattended once its checks are green.

Lands as a **merge commit**, never a squash: the point of the sync is to put `Develop` in this branch's *ancestry*, so its deletions are history here rather than conflicts later (Issue #1048).

Filed by the milestone branch sync (Issue #589).

author: libraminh
body:
Ba thay đổi cho job Điện, mỗi cái một commit riêng.

## 1. `1fd2067` — Thoát kẹt: quay ngang thật trong chu kỳ WATCH 30s NẶNG

Log thật cho thấy bot kẹt từ chu kỳ #3 tới #12 trong ~9 phút, cùng một dòng `lùi S 2.0s → reset camera → W`.

Nguyên nhân: "reset camera" trong nhánh này **chỉ chỉnh trục dọc**. `CameraResetStep` chỉ dùng `SetMouseYRate`; chuỗi `DOWN_TO_GROUND → GROUND_HOLD → UP_TO_NORMAL` là cúi xuống đất rồi ngẩng lên. Hướng nhân vật không đổi một độ nào, nên chu kỳ NẶNG thực chất là *lùi 2s rồi tiến 2s về đúng chỗ cũ*.

Thêm chuỗi `BACKOUT_S → REACQUIRE_INPUT → YAW_TURN → CLEAR_FORWARD` với thang góc ±45, ±90, ±135, ±180 rồi lặp. Góc chốt bằng **đếm count** (`XSentCounts` mới) chứ không bằng thời gian, vì luồng chuột 240Hz có ramp `XTauS = 0.050` hai đầu và có thể tụt lease 120ms.

Hai lỗi thật mà ca kiểm mới phát hiện:
- `Ket1UturnTargetDeg = 168` với cap 950ms ở 420 cps chỉ quay nổi ≈94° — cap literal cắt cụt góc. Cap của chuỗi mới **suy ra** từ hiệu chuẩn, và có ca kiểm chặn đúng lớp lỗi đó ở cả bốn hệ số chuột.
- Không dùng `Lost360RateCps` 1850: quay 45° chỉ mất 103ms, ngắn hơn cả ramp.

## 2. `c71b915` — UI ô bánh/nước dự phòng + bỏ chốt bắt buộc test phím

Ô dự phòng đã có sẵn trong model và runtime (`NavBot` biết "thử ô dự phòng") nhưng **UI chỉ phơi ra ô chính**, nên không đặt được ngoài cách sửa tay `electric.json`. Thêm hàng dropdown thứ ba, tuỳ chọn, chọn `—` là để trống.

Bỏ chốt "phải test phím mới bật được": `CanRun` chỉ còn đòi hiệu chuẩn HUD. HUD vẫn bắt buộc vì không có nó thì bộ đọc tụt về tâm/màu hardcode 1080p và đọc ra số rác.

**Bắt buộc phải bỏ cùng lúc:** `KeysFor` ghi đè hoàn toàn cấu hình bằng danh sách "đã test" của profile. Giữ lại thì ô dự phòng chọn từ UI thành vô hiệu, và sau khi bỏ chốt thì bot bấm phím còn sót từ lần test trước trong khi UI hiện phím khác.

Hai lỗi thật do ca kiểm mới phát hiện:
- `KeepBackup` lấy ký tự hợp lệ **đầu tiên** khác ô chính, nên `"5,6"` đổi ô chính sang 3 ra `"3,5"` — giữ ô chính cũ và **mất ô dự phòng người dùng đã chọn**. Nó cũng tự sinh ô dự phòng mà không ai yêu cầu.
- `DropOverlap` cho bánh thắng và âm thầm dời ô nước sang ô khác, không phải bỏ ô của bánh.

## 3. `9539a14` — Nhận ra bảng nghề mở ngoài ý muốn

Bot đi ngang NPC, bấm E, bảng nghề mở rồi **đứng im vô hạn đợi minigame**.

Nguyên nhân: quyền đọc bảng chết sau 4,22s. `snap.Board` chỉ có giá trị khi `WantBoard` bật, mà cờ đó chỉ sống trong cửa sổ sau E. Hết cửa sổ, **cả hai chốt cùng chết**.

Xử lý: bảng nghề mở mà chưa ở trong luồng reset nghề thì **chạy luôn luồng đó**. `OnJobFinished` ở cuối luồng tự dựng KHIÊN E NPC nên bot không bấm E lại vào đúng NPC đó.

Thêm `NavCapture.ReadBoardNow` (đọc theo yêu cầu, cùng khuôn `AnalyzeObstacleSide`) và probe có nhịp tại bốn mốc nghi ngờ. Mốc `PanelVisible()` phải bỏ qua nhịp vì cổng ngắt chốt trong 0,25s.

Xoá cặp `AfterEEscAccidentalNpc`/`AfterEEnterOpenBoard` và `TapEscWorld`: ảnh chụp panel thật cho thấy panel **che kín minimap**, nên `yellowVisible` luôn false và nhánh ESC là **code chết**.

## Kiểm chứng

`--verify-nav`, `--verify-survival`, `--verify-wire` đều **TẤT CẢ ĐẠT**, 0 ca hỏng. Thêm ~60 ca mới.

Đã soi UI thật trên bản build: hàng ô dự phòng không bị cắt, dòng trạng thái xanh "Sẵn sàng" dù chưa test phím.

## Còn phải thử trong game

Ba việc chưa kiểm được bằng ca tự động:
1. Chu kỳ NẶNG: nhân vật **thật sự đổi hướng**, góc trong log khớp góc quan sát (lệch hệ thống thì hiệu chuẩn `MouseCountsPerDegree`, đừng chỉnh rate), thang góc reset về +45 sau mỗi minigame giải xong.
2. Ô dự phòng: đặt ô chính = ô rỗng, ô dự phòng = ô có bánh → phải thấy `→ thử ô dự phòng` rồi `ĐƯỢC phím …`.
3. Bảng nghề: để bot tự đi ngang NPC → kỳ vọng `[RESET NGHỀ] … bảng đã mở`, chạy trọn luồng, rồi `[KHIÊN E NPC]` chặn bấm E lại.

## Câu hỏi còn treo

`BoardOpen()` có false-positive trên bảng nghề NPC không? Dải hue của chữ tiêu đề bảng điện (70–95) **trùng** với nút cyan bảng nghề (84–96); cái cứu là ROI cách xa nhau (dải tiêu đề ở đỉnh màn, nút bảng nghề ở 54–82% chiều cao). Cần đo pixel trên một khung bảng nghề thật mới kết luận được. Nếu dương thì đó là triệu chứng thứ hai, sửa riêng.

author: glamr-agent
body:
## Overview:

Two guard rails in the vLLM worker's argument parsing never ran. `--realtime --enable-lora` and `--classify-worker --enable-lora` were both accepted on the command line and carried on into worker startup, even though `DynamoVllmConfig.validate()` holds a rule rejecting each. This makes both rules fire.

## Details:

`parse_args` in `components/src/dynamo/vllm/args.py` called `dynamo_config.validate()` before it assigned `dynamo_config.engine_args`. Both rules read that attribute through `getattr(getattr(self, "engine_args", None), "enable_lora", False)`, so with the attribute genuinely absent the expression was always `False` and neither `raise ValueError` was reachable.

This moves the vLLM engine parse and the `dynamo_config.engine_args = engine_config` assignment above `validate()`, which is all the rules need to see a real `AsyncEngineArgs`. `cross_validate_config`, `update_dynamo_config_with_engine`, and `update_engine_config_with_dynamo` stay after `validate()` because they consume state it resolves, notably the `DisaggregationMode` enum.

Both rules keep their guarded lookup. `engine_args` is not a declared field of `DynamoVllmConfig` — only `parse_args` attaches it — so a config assembled in code has no such attribute, and the guard keeps that case meaning "LoRA is disabled" rather than `AttributeError`.

One side effect, on argv that was already going to be rejected: a malformed vLLM flag now reports vLLM's error before Dynamo's. No previously accepted command line becomes rejected apart from the two this change targets.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`components/src/dynamo/vllm/args.py` — the statement order inside `parse_args`, and which calls must stay after `validate()`.

## Validation

```bash
pytest components/src/dynamo/vllm/tests/test_backend_args.py -m 'unit and not gpu'
```

Passes, 87 tests. `TestParseArgsLoraExclusivity` drives the real command line, which is the only place this ordering is observable; its two rejection cases fail against the code before this change with `DID NOT RAISE <class 'ValueError'>`, and its two control cases pass either way. Each validator also has a `test_absent_engine_args_reads_as_lora_disabled` case covering a config built without `engine_args`. `pre-commit` is clean on the changed files.

Starting a worker end to end (`python -m dynamo.vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`) was not run: the machine used had an NVIDIA driver older than the CUDA build of its installed `torch`, which fails identically outside this repository.

- [x] Confirmed — no related issue

author: fabiocicerchia
body:
Layer 3 of the refactoring sweep: the dependency hygiene that nothing else was going to do. Up to three independent commits, each reviewable on its own.

### `ci: run the editorconfig action on node24`

v2 of `editorconfig-checker/action-editorconfig-checker` declares `using: node20`. The runner forces it onto node24 and prints a deprecation warning on **every run in this estate**. v3.0.0 declares node24 outright.

The tool pin stays at `v3.11.3`. That pin exists because editorconfig-checker v4 renamed its release assets from `ec-*` to `editorconfig-checker-*`, and the v2 action only knew the old name. v3 asks for the current name **and falls back to the legacy prefix**, so v3.11.3 resolves exactly as before — and moving to the v4 tool becomes possible later, which it was not with v2.

### `ci: group the codeql-action updates`

`codeql-action/init` writes the analysis configuration and `codeql-action/analyze` reads it back. CodeQL refuses a mismatch outright:

> Loaded a configuration file for version 4.37.9, but running version 4.37.6

Dependabot proposed each step as its own pull request, so they merged at different times and drifted apart — which is exactly how the scan stopped running in several repos here. No dependabot config in the estate used `groups:`. One group means `init`, `analyze` and `upload-sarif` move together and cannot drift again.

### `ci: pin every codeql-action step to one release`

Where the steps had **already** drifted, they are realigned onto the newest release the repo already referenced. 12 repos needed this.

### `ci: let dependabot watch this repo's dependencies`

15 repos had no dependabot configuration at all, so their pinned actions had never been offered an update and never would be. They now match the estate's convention — weekly, 7-day cooldown — with the ecosystems each repo actually has, and the codeql group from the start.

---

Only `.github/` is touched; no source, no behaviour. Every generated file was checked to parse as YAML.

author: peterrichards-lr
body:
## The defect

`scripts/sync_compatibility.py` decided the compatibility matrix's **Docker
Provider** column by looking for the literal word `linux` in the report's
`Platform:` line, falling back to `Unknown`. Every containerised `verify-linux`
arm satisfied that only by luck, because each image's `/etc/os-release`
`PRETTY_NAME` happens to contain the word:

| arm | real `Platform:` |
|---|---|
| fedora | `Fedora Linux 44 (Container Image)` |
| rockylinux | `Rocky Linux 9.3 (Blue Onyx)` |
| alpine | `Alpine Linux v3.24` |
| debian | `Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)` |

Alpine is one upstream rewording from `Alpine 3.25`, at which point the
published, user-facing matrix grows a row reading provider `Unknown` and the
canonical report is renamed
`verify-linux-workstation-alpine-3.25-unknown-pass.txt`. Nothing fails; the
documentation just looks broken.

## How the provider is derived now

LDM-#1614 already plumbs the distro identity through explicitly as an
`Env Label:` header, so a declared label is now sufficient on its own. The
macOS, WSL2 and native-Windows branches are evaluated *first*, so a label
reaching the Linux branch is a Linux arm whatever its vendor put in
`PRETTY_NAME` — no vendor marketing string involved.

```python
elif (
    is_fedora or is_ubuntu or declares_own_env or "linux" in p_low
) and provider in {"Unknown", "desktop-linux"}:
    provider = "Native Docker"
```

**The label is an additional signal, never a replacement.** A contributor
running `scripts/verify_e2e_refactor.sh` by hand sets no `LDM_ENV_LABEL`, so
the string match stays. A label-less report is neither refused nor guessed at:
it resolves exactly as it always has, `Unknown` included where there is
genuinely nothing to derive from.

## No existing row or filename moves

Proven, not assumed. A sandboxed sync — `--results-dir`/`--table` into a temp
tree, `sync_docs` stubbed so it cannot reach the real `docs/TESTING.md` /
`README.md` — was run over the seven committed reports before and after the
change:

```
diff -r sync-out-1631-before sync-out-1631-after
IDENTICAL
```

Byte-identical canonical filenames and a byte-identical table (macOS Colima and
OrbStack, Fedora, Ubuntu, WSL2, and both PowerShell editions). The run asserts
`references/verification-results/` and `docs/reference/compatibility.md` are
untouched, and `git diff --name-only origin/master...HEAD -- references/`
returns nothing.

## Tests

Eleven tests in `TestProviderDerivedFromTheDeclaredLabel`. Every one was
**observed failing** against a deliberately broken script with all symbols and
messages left intact:

| break | tests that fail |
|---|---|
| the unfixed script (`git stash`) | the `Alpine 3.25` regression case (`Unknown` != `Native Docker`) and the end-to-end published row + canonical filename (`…-unknown-pass.txt`) |
| Linux provider branch disabled entirely | those two plus the four real-arm preservation cases and the fallback guard — 7 in total |
| platform-string fallback removed (label-only) | the hand-run fallback guard |
| a label allowed to win *ahead* of the macOS/WSL/Windows branches | all three non-Linux guards (Colima, Docker Desktop, Native WSL2) |
| a label-less report made to refuse | the hand-run "never refused" test |

The non-Linux guards use the **real** platform lines of run 34063433007's macOS
and Windows artifacts (`darwin25`, `Microsoft Windows 10.0.26100`,
`Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS` for the WSL2 row). All five Linux platform strings were
read off that run's artifacts too, not invented. No test asserts source text,
and every one is sandboxed via `--results-dir`/`--table` and `_no_docs_sync()`.

## Verification

- `SKIP=bump-docs-timestamps pre-commit run --all-files` — 17 hooks, all Passed
- `mypy ldm_core --config-file=mypy.ini` — Success: no issues found in 194 source files
- `pytest ldm_core/tests/test_sync_compatibility.py` (whole file) — 59 passed
- `pytest ldm_core/tests/test_ci_verification_reporting.py` (whole file, the LDM-#1625 guard) — 7 passed

Closes #1631

author: yiliang114
body:
## What this PR does

Keeps Live Host packaging inside its standalone npm workspace instead of inheriting the parent repository's pnpm package-manager selection. This is a one-line workspace boundary declaration; no dependency or workflow changes.

## Why it's needed

#10449 introduced the root pnpm declaration while explicitly excluding Live Host from that workspace. electron-builder 26.15.3 nevertheless walks up to the parent's workspace declaration and selects pnpm. The Live Host CI installs with npm and has no pnpm executable, so packaging fails with `spawn pnpm ENOENT`.

An empty child workspace declaration stops that upward lookup and preserves the existing npm lockfile and dependency layout. Declaring only a child npm package-manager version does not stop the later parent lookup.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the Live Host packaging lane against the pnpm-enabled main branch. Dependency collection should select npm with Live Host as the workspace root, retain its production dependency, and complete unsigned macOS packaging without invoking pnpm.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: [Live Host CI on #11314](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/34189887395/job/101945605629) selected the parent pnpm configuration and failed with `spawn pnpm ENOENT`.

After: the real electron-builder detection and production collector were exercised with a parent pnpm workspace and a child npm lockfile. They selected the child npm workspace and collected `ws`. Detection was also verified against this PR's latest-main worktree. Live Host code is unchanged from the locally tested revision: installation, build, typecheck, and all 68 tests passed. Full local packaging selected npm but stopped on an Electron download connection timeout; CI must validate the complete package.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ targeted checks; full packaging blocked by download |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: relies on electron-builder recognizing the explicit child workspace boundary; verified with the locked 26.15.3 version.
- Not validated / out of scope: complete signed/release packaging, API profile behavior, and Web Shell E2E failures.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; Live Host remains an independent npm project.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #10449. Observed in #11314; kept separate from that feature PR.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让 Live Host 打包保持在自身独立的 npm 工作区内，不再继承父仓库的 pnpm 选择。仅增加一行工作区边界声明，不改依赖或工作流。

## 为什么需要

#10449 在根目录引入 pnpm 声明，同时明确将 Live Host 排除在该工作区之外。但 electron-builder 26.15.3 仍向上找到父工作区并选择 pnpm。Live Host CI 使用 npm 安装，环境中没有 pnpm，导致打包报错 `spawn pnpm ENOENT`。

空的子工作区声明阻止继续向上查找，保留现有 npm 锁文件及依赖布局。仅声明子项目的 npm 版本不能阻止后续的父目录查找。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

在已启用 pnpm 的 main 基线上运行 Live Host 打包任务。依赖收集应选择 npm，以 Live Host 为工作区根目录，保留生产依赖，并在不调用 pnpm 的情况下完成 macOS 未签名打包。

### Before & After 证据

修复前：[#11314 的 Live Host CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/34189887395/job/101945605629) 选择父目录 pnpm 配置，报错 `spawn pnpm ENOENT`。

修复后：使用父 pnpm 工作区和子 npm 锁文件，执行真实 electron-builder 检测及生产依赖收集，正确选择子 npm 工作区并收集到 `ws`。也在本 PR 基于最新 main 的 worktree 中验证了检测结果。Live Host 代码与本地已测试版本一致：依赖安装、构建、类型检查及 68 个测试通过。完整本地打包正确选择 npm，但因 Electron 下载连接超时中断；完整产物仍需 CI 验证。

### 测试环境

| OS | 状态 |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 定向验证；完整打包被下载阻断 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ |

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：依赖 electron-builder 识别显式子工作区边界，已使用锁定的 26.15.3 版本验证。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：完整签名及发布打包、API profile 行为、Web Shell E2E 失败。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无；Live Host 保持独立 npm 项目。

## 关联 Issue

#10449 的后续修复。在 #11314 中观察到，独立于该功能 PR 提交。

author: wenhua-huang
body:
## 背景 / 问题

生产工单此前有**两条平行的开单入口**：
- 生产管理 → 生产工单 → 「新增」（手工建单）
- 销售订单 → 「生成工单」

同一批活可能被开两次，工单主线与销售订单从源头就对不上。现收口：**除超级管理员外，所有角色隐藏并禁用生产工单页的「新增」；工单只能从销售订单「生成工单」创建。**

## 改动（4 个文件）

| 文件 | 改动 |
|---|---|
| `V149__revoke_workorder_add_perm.sql`（新增） | 回收非超管角色的 `mes:pro:workorder:add` 按钮权限。按 perms+F 类型动态定位、不限 factory_id（覆盖 0/1 历史授权），DELETE 天然幂等；超管(user_id=1)凭 `*:*:*` 天然保留 |
| `ProWorkorderController.java` | `checkDeviation` 权限 `hasPermi(add)` → `hasAnyPermi(add,edit)`：偏离检测纯计算不写库、新增/编辑向导共用，仅有 edit 权限的角色编辑工单不能被 403 |
| `ProWorkorderChangeController.java` | 工单变更「发起」接口权限 `workorder:add` → `workorder:edit`：发起变更是对**在制工单**的修改（审批本就用 edit），避免回收 add 误伤变更流程 |
| `workorderchange/index.vue` | 变更页「新增(发起变更)」按钮 `v-hasPermi` 同步改为 `edit` |

一处数据回收同时管住前端（v-hasPermi 移除按钮 DOM）和后端（@PreAuthorize 返回 403），遵循若依 RBAC 惯例，未硬编码角色。

## 不受影响

- **销售订单「生成工单」**：走独立权限点 `mes:sal:order:workorder`、独立接口 `POST /mes/sal/order/toWorkorder`，service 内部调用不经工单 Controller 权限切面。
- 工单**查询 / 修改 / 删除 / 导出 / 发起变更 / 偏离检测**等对已有工单的日常操作权限保留。
- app 端无建工单入口。
- F 按钮菜单定义保留，管理员日后可在「系统管理→角色」按需重新授权。

## 验证

- DB：迁移执行后，非超管的 `workorder:add` 授权行（生产/外发角色，含 factory_id=0/1）全部清除，超管保留。
- 接口（生产角色 wubing，有 edit 无 add）：`createWithBom`/基础新增 → **403**；工单列表/查询 → 200；`checkDeviation` → 200；发起工单变更 → 过鉴权；销售转工单 → 正常。admin 新增 → 放行。
- 浏览器：生产角色工单页**无「新增」**、列表正常、变更页可发起；admin 工单页「新增」可见；销售订单页「生成工单」入口完好。
- 后端 `clean package` 通过；前端工单相关单测 **24/24** 通过。

## 部署注意

权限缓存在登录 token（Redis）中，**已在线的非超管用户需重新登录**才会隐藏按钮。

author: emyann
body:
**Supersedes #425** — this branch carries #425's two commits unchanged (a merge, not a rebase) plus the fixes below. Please close #425 and #422 in favour of this one; nothing from either is dropped.

The design is still ADR-016 §3: `check` is part of the **completion condition** beside the declared outputs, and the controller reads 0 / not-0 and knows nothing else. Everything here is a defect in the implementation of that, found by a second high-effort review of #425 — twenty-two of thirty findings reproduced. Most of it is the process-lifecycle corner of the async spawn, which is the hard part, plus two regressions the lease fix introduced.

## The process lifecycle of `runCheck` — one design, six findings

It settled only on `close`, which is the wrong event for a verdict and the wrong bound for a hang.

- **The verdict settles on `exit`.** The shell's exit code is the check's answer the moment it exits. `--check 'node server.js & mocha'` exits 0 in seconds and the server keeps the inherited pipe open behind it — so waiting for `close` waited for the *server*: the full ten minutes, recorded as a timeout.
- **The pipes get their own bound**, `CHECK_DRAIN_MS` (two seconds after the exit — a drained kernel buffer is a `read()`, not a round trip). Without it a descendant that left the process group (`setsid sleep 30 & exit 0`) could not be reached by the timeout *or* by `deps.signal`, so the promise never settled at all and the reconcile pass hung with the lease renewed for ever.
- **The hard kill is unconditional.** It was cancelled on `close`, which is the moment the *shell* died — so a runner that traps `SIGTERM` and has its stdio redirected let the shell close, cancelled the `SIGKILL`, and went on running in the worktree the resumed attempt continues in, while the record said it "was killed". Reproduced via /proc. `SIGKILL` now fires when the grace elapses whether or not `close` did, and settles on it.
- **It never rejects.** `spawn` throws *synchronously* — measured, all three — for an `ENOTDIR` cwd, a command past `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (`E2BIG`) and a command containing a NUL byte. Each resolves the `unstartable` record the module's own contract already promises; an unhandled rejection out of the post-run section is a Job stuck `running`. The command is capped at file time too (`CHECK_COMMAND_MAX_BYTES`, 8 KB).
- **`hkb run` passes a signal.** It wired none, so `Ctrl-C` killed the CLI and left the pass's detached suite running with nothing left to bound it — `deps.signal` is the only route a stop has into a check. Same `AbortController` shape as `hkb up --foreground`, and the handler only *asks*.
- **`stop('abort')` works after `killedFor` is set.** An abort after a timeout that could not settle is the operator's last resort and it returned early.

Tests for each, with real processes: a pipe-holding descendant settles at the drain and not at the timeout; `exit 0` with a background child is a pass; a TERM-ignoring child is gone after the hard kill (`kill -0`); every synchronous spawn failure resolves `unstartable`; an abort after a timeout settles.

## The lease is always released

The renewer's `clearInterval` and the token-fenced `deleteMany` sat ~280 lines after the runtime call with no `try/finally`, so **any** throw in the post-run section — `SQLITE_BUSY` on the fence read, an fs error in `collectResults`, a `runCheck` that rejected — left the renewer ticking for the daemon's lifetime and a Job `running` that no verb could cancel (`whileUnleased` refuses *because* a Lease row exists, and `reclaimExpired` never finds an expired one). Reproduced with a three-second lease still advancing minutes after the pass had thrown.

A lease is a claim with a deadline, and a claim whose holder has stopped must lapse — a property of the release, not of the happy path reaching it. The whole post-run section is now one `try`: the renewer is cleared and the lease released in `finally`, unconditionally and on every path including the `!heldToTheEnd` return (where the token no longer matches, so it deletes nothing). The `catch` closes the attempt `crashed` with the error text and puts the Job back to `pending`/`failed` before re-raising.

## The rest

- **A stop mid-check no longer relabels a completed run.** `ran` was reassigned to `stopped` *after* the results had been collected AND `clearResults` had deleted them — so the resumed attempt could not re-produce them, ended `no_output`, and went terminal. Pressing `Ctrl-C` during a test suite destroyed the Job. What is true is narrower and is all that is recorded: the run completed, the check was interrupted, phase back to `pending`, no retry burnt, results kept.
- **A proposing Job runs no check.** It changes nothing in the tree, and a red check outranks the gate in `nextPhase` — so the Job never suspended for approval. Reproduced: three attempts, the same proposal stored three times, zero Jobs filed. `hkb new --propose --check` is refused by name; the controller's gate covers a check the *board* supplied.
- **Exports are gated on the check alone.** The copy had picked up the whole `!shortfall` condition on its way down past the check, so a declared export that IS present stopped being delivered when a result was missing or the rebase conflicted — and a conflicted attempt is not resumable, so nothing ever delivered it. `main`'s rule is restored; only a check that *refused* withholds the copy. That also fixes `exported: []` being recorded for a stopped-mid-check attempt whose exports were right there.
- **The walk-back does not walk past a nulled session.** `CHECKLESS_OUTCOMES` skipped `crashed` on the premise that it clears no session, but a runtime-error `crashed` nulls `lastSessionId` and sweeps the worktree — so the next attempt started cold and was briefed "the same session, normally the same checkout", with the plain `withCheck` line suppressed. The refusal now counts only while the attempt that earned it is the one whose session the next will resume. `timed_out`/`max_turns` join the walk, because they keep theirs.
- **`hkb job set --check none` means inherit**, matching `str()` one line down and README's own sentence. `''` still means "no check, do not inherit"; `hkb new --check none` is still refused, and its message no longer tells an operator to "leave `--check` out" on a verb where that is a no-op.
- **`--check --json` no longer stores the next token.** `parseArgs` hands a string option the next argv token even when it is a flag; `given` refuses a value beginning with `-`, on every flag that shares it. Third argv trap, filed as such — and the test comment claiming the lost-quotes guard covered it is fixed.
- **Two tail windows, both kept.** Joining stdout and stderr and re-cutting to 4 KB dropped a stdout verdict the moment stderr alone reached 4 KB (`cargo test`, mocha, vitest, `node --test`). Two fields on the record, printed labelled by `hkb show`, both briefed.
- **`fenceSafe` at five.** CommonMark §4.5 closes a fence only with a run at least as long as the one that opened it, so rewriting runs of four put a U+200B into the standard ````-around-``` idiom — in content the worker is told to treat as data and may copy into the repository. `/`{5,}/g` only.
- **The `shellTest` exemption is narrowed to the one shape it was for.** `kind !== 'list'` was thirteen scalar keys, so `model: [ opus, sonnet ]` was filed as that literal string and `check: [ a, b ]` as a command exiting 2 on every attempt. A shell `[ … ]` test has no comma in it; the refusal now says that the quoted form works, which it always did.
- **The bare-flag idiom is closed for every flag**, not just `--check`: `--export`/`--result`/`--artifact`/`--input`/`--label`/`--allow-tool` filed `['true']` (a repeatable flag with no value is `[true]`, not `true`), and `--model`, `--plugin-dir`, `--board`, `--repo`, `--from` threw raw client and `TypeError` messages. One refusing test per flag.
- `hkb new --json` and `hkb show --json` now print the same

author: arnpal961
body:
Makes Archivist deployable and deploys it. **Live at https://archivist.stackedtensor.com**

Supersedes #1 — this branch contains everything in that PR plus the EC2 work,
and removes the Hugging Face Spaces path it added. #1 can be closed in favour
of this one.

## Why EC2 rather than Hugging Face Spaces

#1 targeted a Spaces Docker SDK Space on the free tier. That is no longer
possible: since mid-2026 Docker Spaces require a PRO subscription, and only
Static Spaces remain free. Rather than pay $9/mo for a path that also sleeps
after 48h idle, this deploys to a single EC2 instance.

Three properties of the app drive the shape of the deployment:

- **Memory.** `bge-reranker-base` and `bge-small-en-v1.5` load in-process at
  startup, so the container needs ~2.5-4 GB. A `t3.medium` fits with swap as
  headroom.
- **State.** Uploads and the Chroma index live on disk. Chroma persists through
  SQLite, whose locking is unreliable over NFS, so this must be block storage —
  which rules out Fargate + EFS.
- **A single process.** Per-user BM25 indexes are held in `app.state` and built
  once at startup, so the app runs exactly one Uvicorn worker and must not be
  scaled horizontally.

## Cloudflare Tunnel instead of a public listener

`cloudflared` dials out, so the instance needs **no inbound 80/443**, no
certificate management and no domain wrangling. The security group is SSH-only
and the app is never bound to a public interface.

Two profiles: `quick` gets a throwaway `trycloudflare.com` hostname with zero
setup; `named` gives a stable hostname via a connector token. Production uses
`named`.

## Bugs fixed

Each of these breaks only outside a local dev machine, which is why none had
surfaced:

- **`requirements.txt` was UTF-16 encoded.** Modern pip cannot reliably parse it.
- **`data/` and `chroma_db/` were never created at runtime.** Both are
  gitignored, so the first upload in a fresh container failed. Now created at
  startup.
- **`templates/signup.html` requested `/static/js/signup.js`** while the
  directory is `static/Js`. Resolves on case-insensitive filesystems, 404s on
  Linux — the signup page's JavaScript silently failed to load. Fixed the
  reference rather than renaming the directory, since a case-only rename breaks
  collaborators on macOS/Windows.
- **`bootstrap_db.py` module resolution.** Python puts a script's own directory
  on `sys.path`, not the working directory, so `import database.database` failed
  and the container exited before serving.
- **`psycopg2` -> `psycopg2-binary`**, removing the need for a compiler and
  libpq headers in the image.
- **README documented `uvicorn app:app` and `DATABASE_URL`**; the real entry
  point is `api.main:app` and the variable read is `DB_URL`.

The Alembic history starts *after* the initial tables were created by
`init_db.py`, so `alembic upgrade head` alone fails on an empty database — the
first revision alters `users`, which does not exist yet. `docker/bootstrap_db.py`
detects this and creates-then-stamps instead.

Storage paths and the session cookie's `secure` flag are now environment driven,
defaulting to the previous local behaviour.

## Image

Torch is installed from the CPU index: 191 MB versus ~2.5 GB for the PyPI wheel
with its bundled CUDA runtime. Model weights are baked in at build time so cold
starts do not re-download them. Runs as UID 1000.

## Linting

`.flake8` enforces pyflakes, line length, comparison correctness and whitespace
hygiene, while excluding the spacing style used consistently across the codebase
(`Depends , get_db`, `key = "value"`) rather than reformatting ~2,000 lines.

Fixed 6 unused imports (2 kept with `# noqa` since they register SQLAlchemy
tables by side effect), `conversation_id == None` -> `is None`, and normalized
trailing whitespace and EOF newlines across 30 files. The whitespace pass used
Python's tokenizer to skip lines inside multi-line strings, so LLM prompt text
is byte-identical. `flake8` exits clean.

## Verification

Built and booted against PostgreSQL, then verified in production:

- Both bootstrap branches — empty database creates and stamps; existing database
  upgrades
- Models load from the baked cache with no network access

author: todwadd
body:
A feed fetch or database promise that never settles currently keeps that feed's polling slot occupied indefinitely, even while sibling feeds and the scheduler heartbeat look healthy. This releases the slot after 60 seconds and reports the exact step that stalled, allowing the next scheduled poll to try again.

Expected 4xx rejections from opening/closing a perp are also logged at WARN. User responses and retry rules are unchanged; 5xx failures and errors from scheduled operations remain ERROR.

### Recovery and limits

- Reserve capacity before dispatch: at most **20 outstanding polls across the process**, including active and abandoned work, and **3 abandoned polls per feed**.
- Keep abandoned work counted until its underlying promise actually settles. A late completion cannot clear or relabel the replacement's polling slot.
- Checkpoints stop retired polls before their next read, fetch, price insertion, or contract update.
- A transaction already started finishes atomically; a committed update still publishes its quote and delivers notifications.
- Source adapters retain their existing timeouts and shared Solana request. The deadline does **not** cancel in-flight database queries. If enough operations remain stuck indefinitely, polling is refused and logged until work settles or the scheduler is restarted.

Supersedes #4017 on current main. This carries forward recovery/diagnostics and expected-rejection logging; existing solvency handling, conversion-score improvements, lock budgets, and alert thresholds are preserved.

### Validation

- Common: **48 suites / 1,014 tests passed**.
- Shared: **14 suites / 106 tests passed**, including **17 new regression cases** covering never-settling and late-settling work, exact resource limits, retained notifications, and log severity.
- `tsc -b backend/api backend/scheduler --force` passed.
- ESLint on changed shared TypeScript files, Prettier on all changed files, and `git diff --check` passed.

### Automated checks

[GitHub CI passed](https://github.com/manifoldmarkets/manifold/actions/runs/34193606404): build, all typechecks, lint, formatting, and tests.

The [Vercel dev-project preview](https://vercel.com/mantic/dev/F553P5M7TVba2b1dh76vbnDkyUGY) compiled successfully, then failed prerendering the unchanged `/admin/reports` page: `.reports[0].reporter.entitlements[0].expiresTime` is `undefined` and cannot be serialized by `getStaticProps`. This PR changes no web files; that preview failure is outside this perp change.

### Deploy

No migration. Deploy API first, fully rolled out, then `scheduler-perps` from the same SHA. No production deployment performed by this PR.

author: fabiocicerchia
body:
Layer 3 of the refactoring sweep: the dependency hygiene that nothing else was going to do. Up to three independent commits, each reviewable on its own.

### `ci: run the editorconfig action on node24`

v2 of `editorconfig-checker/action-editorconfig-checker` declares `using: node20`. The runner forces it onto node24 and prints a deprecation warning on **every run in this estate**. v3.0.0 declares node24 outright.

The tool pin stays at `v3.11.3`. That pin exists because editorconfig-checker v4 renamed its release assets from `ec-*` to `editorconfig-checker-*`, and the v2 action only knew the old name. v3 asks for the current name **and falls back to the legacy prefix**, so v3.11.3 resolves exactly as before — and moving to the v4 tool becomes possible later, which it was not with v2.

### `ci: group the codeql-action updates`

`codeql-action/init` writes the analysis configuration and `codeql-action/analyze` reads it back. CodeQL refuses a mismatch outright:

> Loaded a configuration file for version 4.37.9, but running version 4.37.6

Dependabot proposed each step as its own pull request, so they merged at different times and drifted apart — which is exactly how the scan stopped running in several repos here. No dependabot config in the estate used `groups:`. One group means `init`, `analyze` and `upload-sarif` move together and cannot drift again.

### `ci: pin every codeql-action step to one release`

Where the steps had **already** drifted, they are realigned onto the newest release the repo already referenced. 12 repos needed this.

### `ci: let dependabot watch this repo's dependencies`

15 repos had no dependabot configuration at all, so their pinned actions had never been offered an update and never would be. They now match the estate's convention — weekly, 7-day cooldown — with the ecosystems each repo actually has, and the codeql group from the start.

---

Only `.github/` is touched; no source, no behaviour. Every generated file was checked to parse as YAML.

author: eaitbrahim
body:
Found by an install that **worked**. Four console daemons bootstrapped, three wrote their records, and `keel open --port 8765` answered *"no recorded keel server"* — so a success read as a failure.

The command had been run from a source checkout, which is **itself a deployment root** (`is_deployment_root` is deliberately generous, and the tree has a `keel.db` and a `config.yaml`). So it searched the checkout's `run/` while the servers wrote to `~/keel/run/`.

**The message listed three explanations and the true one was not among them.** It could not be — it never said where it had looked.

## After

```
Error: no recorded keel server on port 8765.

  Looked in /Users/…/CodeGate/keel/.claude/worktrees/open-says-where/run, which is the
  deployment this directory belongs to. If your server is a different deployment, run this
  from ITS directory -- `keel open` takes the same bare-invocation path as everything else,
  so a source checkout resolves to the checkout.

  If one is running here, it was started from a terminal …
```

`keel open` takes no `--db` and no `--config`, so nothing in its signature hints that the answer depends on the working directory. The path is the hint, and `--help` now says so in one line.

The **stale-record branch gets it too** — a crashed server and a wrong directory are different problems, and an operator staring at either needs the same fact to tell them apart.

## Checks

**6,413 passed / 3 skipped**, ruff and mypy clean. Three mutants killed: the path dropped from each refusal branch, and the help line removed. Verified by running the command from the wrong tree and reading what it prints.

## One thing worth recording for #756

**launchd does give `keel serve` a stdout that is not a tty.** Three daemons, three records written. That was the single assumption the whole `keel open` design rests on and that nothing in CI could test.

author: viirya
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

Closes #5768.

## Rationale for this change

Three places implemented the same Spark rule — a field of a null struct is null, so the
parent's nulls have to reach the children before the children are read — and each did it
slightly differently:

| | union when |
|---|---|
| `GetStructField::project_field` | a null buffer is present, via the checked `ArrayData` builder |
| the hash kernels' struct branch | `null_count() > 0`, via `StructArray::flatten` |
| `get_array_struct_fields` | the parent and child null **counts** differ |

The issue was filed as a refactor, on the grounds that all three were correct and the risk
was drift. That turned out to be half right: **the third guard is wrong**. Equal null counts
do not imply the nulls sit at the same rows, so whenever the child had a null of its own at a
different row the counts could match and the parent's null was dropped. There is a test for
exactly that shape, which a count-based check fails.

## What changes are included in this PR?

`datafusion_comet_common::struct_nulls`, with `child_with_parent_nulls` for one field and
`children_with_parent_nulls` for all of them, and the three call sites switched over. Net -41
lines at the call sites.

The three decisions the issue asked about:

- **Shape.** Both, with the plural built on the singular, since `project_field` wants one
  field and the hash path wants all of them.
- **Checked or unchecked.** Unchecked, as `flatten` already did. The union only adds nulls, so
  every data buffer is carried over unchanged and revalidating them is wasted work. This
  matters asymmetrically: `project_field` runs once per batch in `evaluate` and did not care
  either way, while the hash path reaches this **once per element** of an `array<struct<..>>`,
  where re-checking a string child means rescanning its whole UTF-8 values buffer. Unifying on
  checked would have pushed the batch-level caller's cost onto the element-level one.
- **The `null_count() > 0` guard.** Applied to all three. It skips the union when the parent
  has no null to contribute, which covers both no buffer at all and a present-but-all-valid
  buffer — the latter is what slicing leaves behind. `NullBuffer` stores its null count, so the
  test is O(1).

It lives in its own module rather than in `schema.rs`, which is about reconciling declared and
runtime *types* rather than null masks.

## How are these changes tested?

Six unit tests on the helper: a hidden child value under a null parent, no parent null buffer
(asserting the same array comes back rather than a rebuilt one), a present-but-all-valid
buffer, a child's own null surviving the union, an empty struct, and the equal-counts-different-rows
case that pins the guard fix.

Existing coverage for the three call sites passes unchanged: `cargo test` gives 720 + 5 in
`spark-expr` and 40 in `common`, and on the Spark side `CometHashExpressionSuite` (40),
`CometArrayExpressionSuite` (59) and `CometExpressionSuite` (141). `cargo fmt --check` and
`clippy -D warnings` are clean.

## Additional context

Raised by @andygrove reviewing #5754. The two earlier fixes in this area were #4432
(`GetStructField`) and #5754 (the hash kernels); this unifies them with the third site, which
the issue had not accounted for.

Implements the frontend half of **HU-22b — Variables inspector and call stack; code in every
family**. Pairs with https://github.com/vista-pdg/backend/pull/7, which should be merged first.

## Acceptance criteria covered (HU-22 CA-2, CA-3, CA-5)

| Scenario | Implementation | E2E (Chromium + Firefox) |
|---|---|---|
| CA-2 · At step 4 the state panel shows the live variables and the pointed node | `CodePanel` → **Variables** section (`var-{name}`, `var-{name}-value`, pointed node in the header) read from `steps[stepIndex].variables` / `highlightedNodeIds` | `hu-22b-ca2` (2): every variable value equals the engine's step, the pointed node is the highlighted one, `salida` grows to `[3, 5, 7, 10, 15]` |
| CA-3 · Nested call pushes a frame with its parameters; return pops it | **Pila de llamadas** section (`call-stack[data-depth]`, `frame-{n}` top first) read from `steps[stepIndex].callStack` | `hu-22b-ca3` (2): depth 1 → 2 (`inorden(nodo=5)`) → 3 (`inorden(nodo=nulo)`) → back to 2 after `retornar`; same in 3D; empty at the end |
| CA-5 · At least one step-by-step algorithm per family, each with visible code | catalog families graph / tree / stack / queue; BFS, pop, dequeue and inorden now ship code + variables | `hu-22b-ca5` (2): each demo opens the panel with the right line count, active line and variables; AVL keeps running without a panel |

## Design notes

**The panel is still a mirror.** Variables arrive serialized from the backend; the panel renders
strings and never interprets types. Sections appear only when the step carries data, so the HU-19
algorithms without instrumentation and the AVL look exactly as before.

**Canvas structure must fit the family.** `core/layout2d.structureFitsFamily` (unit-tested) decides
whether what is on the canvas can feed an algorithm: a tree serves trees and graphs, stacks and
queues only their own family. Without it the inorder demo tried to traverse the queue left by the

body:
## Summary

Implements V1.48 from issue #126.

Architecture:

V1.44 explicit human execution authorization
→ V1.45 CURRENT applicability preflight
→ V1.46 explicit executable TASK request
→ V1.47 CURRENT execution admission
→ **V1.48 provider-agnostic side-effectful execution boundary**
→ later durable execution receipt / persistence / lifecycle consequences

V1.48 is the first side-effectful boundary in this chain. It executes exactly one already-admitted TASK identity through a provider-agnostic protocol and does not select, rank, substitute, persist, mutate lifecycle state, or bind to a concrete provider.

## What changed

- added `TaskExecutionCommand`
- added `TaskExecutionResult`
- added `TaskExecutionPort`
- added `TaskExecutionBoundaryError`
- added `execute_current_admitted_task`
- exported the V1.48 public API from `trajectory_os.application`
- added focused hostile/adversarial tests and AST architecture guards

## Core semantics

- requires one genuine V1.47 `PortfolioProjectFocusNextReadyTaskExecutionAdmission`
- performs fresh COMPLETE strict revalidation before semantic reads
- after revalidation, semantic reads use only the retained fresh copy
- only `admission_state == ADMITTED` may invoke the executor
- exact request/intent/decision/portfolio/project/task identities are projected into an immutable command
- `TaskExecutionPort.execute(command)` is invoked exactly once
- executor exceptions propagate unchanged
- executor return values are treated as untrusted and freshly strict-revalidated
- all result identities must exactly match the command; redirect is rejected
- explicit `succeeded: StrictBool` does not imply any lifecycle transition
- repeated explicit boundary calls are separate explicit executions; V1.48 makes no idempotency claim

## Explicit non-goals

V1.48 does not:

- read CURRENT Portfolio/WBS/relation state again
- recompute V1.45/V1.47 semantics
- select or fall back to another TASK
- call `transition_entity_status` or `transition_entity_status_durably`
- mark TASK completed/failed/running/etc.
- persist execution receipts or history
- access repositories/SQLite
- invoke Ollama directly
- invoke Pi/Aider/agent-specific APIs directly
- invoke shell/subprocess directly
- retry or schedule work
- read wall clock
- generate UUIDs or timestamps

## Validation evidence

Exact reviewed head:

`3137bd902588c343518069d33898551d86c8f89f`

Branch relation to `main`:

- ahead by 4 commits
- behind by 0
- merge base: `8753d2d9c14307865c60bff890ed2593108410ec`

Focused V1.48 tests:

- 39 passed
- 2 intentional Pydantic hostile-construction warnings

Full quality gate:

- 2573 passed
- 47 warnings
- Ruff: clean
- mypy: success on 85 source files
- `git diff --check`: clean

Independent local `qwen3.6:35b` review of the committed V1.48 diff:

- VERDICT: ACCEPT
- BLOCKERS: 0
- MAJORS: 0
- MINORS: 0

The independent reviewer explicitly confirmed fresh-copy TOCTOU protection, immutable identity preservation, exactly-one execution seam, hostile result revalidation, anti-redirection checks, no lifecycle inference from `succeeded`, and no scope overreach.

Closes #126

No merge until GitHub CI is green, review threads are resolved, and explicit human GO is given.

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce a provider-agnostic boundary that executes exactly one freshly validated V1.47-admitted task while keeping execution outcomes separate from lifecycle transitions and persistence.

New Features:
- Add a provider-agnostic execution boundary for running one exactly identified, CURRENT-admitted task.
- Expose immutable execution commands and results plus a pluggable task execution port through the application API.

Bug Fixes:
- Reject invalid, non-admitted, redirected, or hostile execution inputs and outputs before accepting the execution result.

Enhancements:
- Enforce fresh strict validation, exact identity preservation, and exactly-once executor invocation without lifecycle inference or retry behavior.

body:
## 问题

在**未提供外部 `config/application.properties`** 的部署上，预览**任何 xlsx** 都失败（5.0.2 与当前 master 都有）。

页面从 `<html>` 开始正常输出、断在半截 JavaScript 里、**永远没有 `</html>`**，浏览器上表现为白页或一直转圈。
HTTP 状态码是 **200**，服务端日志里只有一句「响应已提交、错误页渲染不了」——**它长得像转换超时，不像模板错**，
所以很容易一路去查 LibreOffice 和转换链路。

真正的报错是：

```
FreeMarker template error:
The following has evaluated to null or missing:
==> watermarkTxt  [in template "officeweb.ftl" at line 25, column 31]
```

## 原因

两处叠在一起，缺一个都不会出事：

**1. 十个 `watermark*` 请求属性可能整族不存在。**

`WatermarkConfigConstants` 没有任何类级注解（对比 `ConfigConstants` 上的 `@Component`），
所以它**不是 Spring bean**，那十个 `@Value("${watermark.xxx:默认值}")` 的 setter 从来不会被调用。
唯一会填充那十个静态字段的是 `ConfigRefreshComponent#loadConfig()`，而它在配置文件不存在时直接 `return`：

```java
if (!Files.exists(configPath)) {
    LOGGER.warn("配置文件不存在: {}", configFilePath);
    return;
}
```

此时十个 getter 全部返回 `null`，而 `AttributeSetFilter` 的 `request.setAttribute(name, null)`
按 Servlet 规范**等同于删除属性**——不是「值是 null」，是「这个属性不存在」。

**2. `officeweb.ftl` 是唯一没有 `classic_compatible` 兜底的预览模板。**

`commonHeader.ftl` 第 1 行是 `<#setting classic_compatible=true>`，而这个设置作用于整个渲染环境、
覆盖到 include 它的那份模板后续的引用（已单独用 FreeMarker 验过）。于是 csv / markdown / pdf / picture 等
所有 include 它的模板在属性缺失时把变量渲染成空串、照常出页面；
`officeweb.ftl` 既不 include 它、自己也没有这个设置，**所以只有 xlsx 预览会硬失败**。

## 修复

给 `officeweb.ftl` 里那十个变量补上 FreeMarker 缺省值，取的就是 `WatermarkConfigConstants.DEFAULT_*`
那一组（`10 / 10 / 微软雅黑 / 18px / black / 0.2 / 240 / 80 / 10`），不另编一套。

`watermarkTxt` 取空串——空串会让模板下一行的 `if (watermarkTxt !== '')` 跳过 `watermark.init()`，
**不会给所有预览凭空加上水印**。其余九个只在水印真的开着时才用得上，但那个 `if` 是 **JavaScript** 的、
不是模板的，FreeMarker 两条分支都会渲染，所以十个都要给（只补 `watermarkTxt` 的话，页面会改为断在
下一个变量 `watermarkXSpace` 上，症状一模一样）。

## 验证

新增 `server/src/test/java/cn/keking/web/OfficeWebWatermarkDefaultsTests.java`，直接用 FreeMarker
渲染这个模板——**不需要把服务跑起来，也不需要 LibreOffice**：

- `shouldRenderXlsxPreviewPageWhenWatermarkAttributesAreMissing`：数据模型里**一个 `watermark*` 都不给**
  （那正是缺陷发生时的情形），断言渲染得出 `</html>`、`watermarkTxt` 落到空串、其余落到声明的缺省值。
  ⚠ 判据取「有没有 `</html>`」而不是 HTTP 200——坏的时候响应头早就发出去了，也是 200。
- `shouldKeepConfiguredWatermarkSettingsWhenAttributesArePresent`：十个值全给上，断言逐个原样渲染，
  保证缺省值不会盖掉真实配置。

改模板**之前**先跑过一遍：第一条报 `InvalidReferenceException`（第 25 行 `watermarkTxt`），第二条通过
——说明红的确实是被测的那个条件，不是模型缺了别的东西。改完之后：

```
mvn -B -pl server -Dtest=OfficeWebWatermarkDefaultsTests test
Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

## 没有一并改的

- `commonHeader.ftl` 与 `pdf.ftl` 里也是裸 `${watermark*}`，今天靠 `classic_compatible=true` 兜着，
  没跟着改——改动越小越好审。
- **更彻底的修法是让那十个值不可能为 `null`**：给 `WatermarkConfigConstants` 加 `@Component`
  （让它的 `@Value` 缺省值真正生效），或让 getter 回落到 `DEFAULT_*`。那会动到配置装载的语义，
  超出这个 PR 的范围；如果维护者更倾向那条路，我可以照着改成那一版。
- 顺带一个不影响本 PR 的不一致，供参考：`server/src/main/config/application.properties` 里
  `watermark.width` 默认是 **180**，而 `WatermarkConfigConstants.DEFAULT_WATERMARK_WIDTH` 是 **240**。
  本 PR 取的是后者（Java 侧声明的默认值）。

author: lemone112
body:
## Дефект
Семь шагов `python3 scripts/extract_X.py extract | python3 scripts/extract_X.py verify` в required `CI / test` доказывали только согласие extractor с самим собой: pinned manifest, названный в docstrings, в дереве не существовал; sabotage-suites `scripts/test_extract_*.py` CI не исполнял; EXT-05/EXT-07 в CI отсутствовали. Ни один инструмент не различал *отключённый* тест от удалённого. Это r11 Unknown ARTIFACT-01: «перечисленный inventory не доказывает исполнение артефактов».

## Закон
Две закреплённые записи в `proof/artifact/`; обе коммитятся, а required CI только пересчитывает и сравнивает канонические байты:

- **`tree.json`** — `path → git blob id` для объявленных корней (`.github/workflows`, `Cargo.*`, `crates`, `conformance`, `bindings/swift`, `packages/colors`, `proof`, `scripts`), tracked и untracked. Blob считает `git hash-object --stdin-paths` с атрибутами: eol чекаута и порядок сортировки ОС не влияют. Закрывает **omission / decoy / parser** на уровне байтов — без regex-парсеров.
- **`tests.json`** — инвентарь тестов. Сила по экосистемам различна и названа честно:
  - **Rust** — compiler-resolved: `cargo test -- --list` и `-- --ignored --list`; новый `#[ignore]` или `cfg`-скрытый модуль меняет запись и **называет тест в diff**.
  - **Python** — loader-resolved: имена тестов + skip, истинные на момент импорта в среде refresh (`__unittest_skip__` на классе/методе, включая `skipIf/skipUnless` с истинным условием); `self.skipTest`/`SkipTest` в `setUp*` — рантайм, невидимы; ошибка импорта модуля — отдельное поле. Diff называет тест (`-python.<suite>.names` / `+python.<suite>.skipped`).
  - **Node** — только текстовые сайты отключения (`x.skip(`, `x.todo(`, `{ skip: }`, `{ todo: }`) в `packages/colors/test/*.test.mjs`; инвентаря тестов Node нет; многострочные option-объекты не детектируются.

  Закрывает **disabled-test** для Rust полностью, для Python — на момент импорта, для Node — по форме записи.

Drift → exit 1 с типизированным diff и подсказкой (`refresh` в Linux с CI toolchain; `ARTIFACT_MATRIX_ONLY=tree` для Windows); порча записи → 64; отказ инструмента → 65; запись вне registry → red. `refresh` отказывается закреплять `tests.json` с import failures. `ARTIFACT_MATRIX_ONLY` в `GITHUB_ACTIONS` отвергается. Изменение любого файла под корнями требует `refresh` в том же PR; diff записей — часть review.

Инвентарь — не семантическое доказательство (INV-03).

## История ревью
1. Первая версия (9 extractor-manifests, 6f556543): изолированный review — FAIL как exit evidence: disabled-test класс отсутствовал; EXT-05/07 админились против STRAT disposition; 796 KB `claims.json` нечитаем; сообщение не actionable; ложный LF-pin. Reviewer показал: omission/decoy/parser достигаются tree-hash в 1/10 кода, disabled-test требует compiler-resolved инвентаря. Переработано.
2. Вторая версия (7f342192): FAIL narrow — Python/Node over-claim; `extract_tests` не исполнялся тестами; `EXIT_TOOL` без теста; 4 survived mutants. Закрыто в 7c89071c.
3. Delta review (7c89071c): PASS conditional — F1 (Python diff не называл тест, order-dependent test), F2 (PR body), C1 (семантика skip). Закрыто в a811cf03 и этом описании. CI red на 7c89071c (copytree `.git` наперегонки с `git gc --auto`) — исправлено в cf18e48c (clone, `gc.auto=0`).

Extractors `extract_*.py` остаются инструментами, их 59 sabotage-тестов исполняются CI (INV-10), но гейтом не являются; их STRAT disposition не меняется этим PR.

## Доказательства
- `scripts/test_artifact_matrix.py` — 26 тестов: omission записи; untracked decoy `.rs` (назван); удалённый workflow (назван); однобайтная правка (файл назван); CRLF-чекаут LF-файла — **не** drift; stale запись с верным self-hash; порча parser ×5 → 64; запись вне registry; новый `#[ignore]` → `-rust.enabled/+rust.ignored` с именем; статический Python skip из середины списка → назван; молча удалённый тест; модуль с ошибкой импорта → назван; новый Node skip site; неизменный инвентарь → green; `EXIT_TOOL` при отказе инструмента; `refresh` отказывает при `load_errors`; knob в CI → 64; CI-binding трёх шагов; inventory→execution binding (каждый `scripts/test_*.py` из записи исполняется CI); **реальный слой извлечения без mock**: fixture-крейт с `#[ignore]` через cargo; fixture-модуль static/conditional/class-level skip и import failure; Node regex positive/negative.
- Полы против вакуума: `ignored_count ≥ 1`, `count ≥ 100` на suite, disjoint enabled/skipped.
- Записи закреплены в `rust:1.96.0-bookworm` (CI toolchain): `check` OK; 26/26; 59/59. Windows: `tree` воспроизводится байт-в-байт; 26/26.
- Гейт поймал собственные правки (`ci-worker.yml`, тесты) как drift до refresh, а также squash #732.

## Unknowns для записи в план (не блокеры)
Python skip — decoration-time в среде refresh; Node без инвентаря, single-line формы; `tests.json` привязан к Linux CI toolchain; inventory→execution binding эвристический только для `scripts` suite; Rust `#[ignore]` (кроме axis-membership oracle) инвентаризованы, но не исполняются CI (по замыслу); composition-мутанты (c)/(n) убиваются CI `check` + полами, не unit-suite отдельно.

## Границы
Не CONF-01 корпус, не MEM-01 лимиты, не публикация. `labcolors-audit` не трогается. Rollback — revert.

Plan: agents-config `lab-colors/ARTIFACT-01` (CLAIM lemone112/r11, in progress).

author: hurkyungsoo
body:
목업 등록폼의 **"임시저장"** 버튼 대응. 등록 마법사(5단계)를 중간에 저장했다가 이어서 작성.
`jobposting` 도메인 내부, 타 도메인 의존 없음. PR #23 과 독립 (겹치는 파일 없음).

## 설계 판단

- **별도 엔티티 `JobPostingDraft`** — draft 는 미완성 폼이라 `JobPosting` 의 `nullable=false` + `@NotNull` 불변식을 만족 못 함. `JobPostingStatus.DRAFT` 로 재사용하면 그 불변식이 약해짐.
- **`formJson` 불투명 스냅샷** — 프론트가 폼 스키마의 주인. 서버는 문자열 그대로 보관·반환만 (검색·정렬 대상 아님). `CreateRequest` 모양이 바뀌어도 draft 코드 안 건드림. `title` 만 목록 라벨용으로 별도.
- **경로 `/api/job-posting-drafts`** (`/api/job-postings` 밑 아님) — `GET /api/job-postings/*` 이 `SecurityConfig` 에서 permitAll 이라 `.../drafts` 목록과 충돌. 분리하고 `WebMvcConfig` 인터셉터에 `/api/job-posting-drafts/**` 추가 (승인 시설 게이트).
- **발행(publish) 엔드포인트 없음** — 프론트가 폼 완성 → 기존 `POST /api/job-postings` 등록 → draft `DELETE`. 검증 로직 한 곳 유지, BE 코드 최소.

## 엔드포인트 (전부 승인 시설 본인)

| | |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/job-posting-drafts` | `{title?, formJson?}` → 201 (빈 draft 허용) |
| `GET /api/job-posting-drafts` | 내 목록 `[{id, title, updatedAt}]`, 최신 수정순, formJson 제외 |
| `GET /api/job-posting-drafts/{id}` | 단건 (formJson 포함) |
| `PUT /api/job-posting-drafts/{id}` | 덮어쓰기 |
| `DELETE /api/job-posting-drafts/{id}` | 204 |

- 남의 draft / 없는 id → **404 `JOBPOSTING_005`** (존재 여부 비노출)
- 시설당 최대 20건 → **409 `JOBPOSTING_006`**
- `formJson` ≤ 20,000자, `title` ≤ 100자 → 초과 시 400
- 미승인(PENDING) 시설 → 403 `FACILITY_001` (인터셉터)

## 검증

- `./gradlew build` — `JobPostingDraftRepositoryTest` (`@DataJpaTest`): updatedAt 내림차순 목록 / 다른 시설 격리 / `findWithFacilityById` 소유자 로드
- 런타임 스모크 **16/16**: CRUD 왕복, 빈 draft, 소유권 404(GET/PUT/DELETE), 없는 id 404, formJson/title 길이 400, 미승인 시설 403, 구직자 403, 익명 401

## 변경

| 파일 | |
|---|---|
| `JobPostingDraft` / `JobPostingDraftRepository` / `JobPostingDraftService` / `JobPostingDraftController` / `JobPostingDraftDtos` | 신규 |
| `ErrorCode` | `JOBPOSTING_005` / `JOBPOSTING_006` |
| `WebMvcConfig` | 인터셉터 경로 1줄 |
| `docs/API.md` / `docs/ERD.md` | 갱신 |

author: perolipotic
body:
Closes story 1.3's first acceptance clause: a member with no email address signs in with an admin-issued username. Two commits — 1.3a's review findings, then 1.3b itself.

## What this does

The organization slug rides in the URL as `/prijava/$slug`, so the credential form keeps **exactly** the two fields story 1.1d froze. Bare `/prijava` is a one-field organization prompt, because three places have no slug in scope: `/`'s redirect target, a typed `/prijava`, and the not-found link. `/`'s `beforeLoad` is now session-conditional and resolves three ways — signed in renders a placeholder, signed out redirects carrying search and hash, and a session that *cannot be read* fails closed rather than falling through to the blank page 1.1d removed.

Alternatives considered and rejected (2026-09-07): globally-unique usernames, a third form field, and an anonymous username-resolution RPC. The last is an enumeration oracle, which is also why —

## The security claim

**Wrong password, unknown username and a deactivated account collapse to one message.** Distinguishing them would answer *"does this username exist in this organization?"* for an unauthenticated caller. A test compares the three outcomes **to each other** rather than to a constant, so a later added operand cannot quietly reopen the oracle.

## Review guide

`_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-3b-spa-sign-in-path.md` ends with a **Suggested Review Order** — 20 stops grouped by concern, entry point first.

Start with the collapse itself (`apps/web/src/supabase/sign-in.ts`), then the extraction pattern: AD-15 bans jsdom and `.tsx` is collected by nothing, so every decision that can live outside a component does — the auth client is a parameter to `signIn`, the router context holds a session *reader* rather than a value, and the message mapping and the prompt's normalize-and-guard are their own modules.

## What review caught

Three adversarial layers found four places where a source-text assertion stood in for an executed one. Each survived a mutation that breaks the product:

| Mutation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Session binding → `async () => null` | green, signed-in user loops forever between `/` and the form | red |
| Swap the two error messages | green, outage ↔ wrong password | red |
| Drop the prompt's `ref` | green, button inert | red |
| Hard-code the slug | green | red |

Two defects that would have shipped looking like user error: the username was neither trimmed nor lowercased while the slug half was both (so `Ivan.Maric` was refused as bad credentials with no way to discover why), and `/prijava/DVD-Kastel-Novi` rendered a working form that refused every correct credential forever.

## Note for the reviewer

`@supabase/supabase-js@2.113.0` enters the bundle, which puts the literal `sb_secret_` in it as the library's own key-shape check — so `key-hygiene.test.ts`'s bundle scan is **narrowed** to key *values*, using the threshold the repo-wide committed-file scan already applies, paired with a new assertion that every occurrence carries no key material. Verified empirically: the prefix appears once, followed by nothing, and an injected key still turns both scans red. This is the one place a security assertion was relaxed and it deserves a second opinion.

## Gates

build · lint · typecheck green. **1265 tests** (946 root + 315 web + 4 domain), none skipped — up from 1115 at baseline.

## Not in this branch

Nine findings went to `deferred-work.md` rather than here — most notably that there is still **no sign-out affordance anywhere** (`Odjava` is reserved for the navigation shell), so a signed-in user on a shared device cannot end their session. That wants resolving with the story that earns the word, not a guard bolted on here.

Sprint tracking: `1-3b-spa-sign-in-path: review`. The `1-3` parent stays `in-progress` until this is accepted.

body:
## Census 270 ca hỏng dải trang — 62 % là MỤC LỤC, không phải offset

| họ nguyên nhân | ca | % |
|---|---|---|
| **TOC · không có trang trong mục lục** | **95** | 35,2 % |
| **TOC · mục là PHẦN CON của bài** | **51** | 18,9 % |
| BOUNDARY · lệch đúng 1 trang | 40 | 14,8 % |
| OCR · không thấy tên trong ±5 trang | 36 | 13,3 % |
| OFFSET · lệch nhiều trang | 27 | 10,0 % |
| TOC · attach không gắn được | 12 | 4,4 % |
| TOC · mục lục hai cột đan nhau | 9 | 3,3 % |

## ⚠ Không dùng book-level offset mapping

Đo phân bố trước như anh yêu cầu: offset trải từ **−4 tới +5**, và **không ổn định trong cùng một cuốn** — **20/44 sách** có nhiều giá trị khác nhau (TV5 tập hai: +2, −1, −2 cùng lúc). Điều kiện «offset ổn định theo sách» **không thoả**, nên một bảng offset theo sách sẽ sai.

## Nguyên nhân thật của họ lớn nhất — soi tận trang

Mục lục Tiếng Việt ghi **phần con của bài**. «Luyện từ và câu: Liên kết câu…» là một mục **bên trong** «Bài 9» — bài mở ở p044 («Tuần 23 · Bài 9 · HỘI THỔI CƠM THI»), mục ấy ở p046.

**Độ mịn của mục lục ≠ đơn vị bài của sách.** Toàn corpus: **530/3.679 (14,4 %)** mục mục-lục là phần con.

## Một luật generic phủ cả hai họ lớn nhất

Tìm trang mà tên đơn vị xuất hiện — trước hết **trong dải**, rồi nới **±2**. Nhận **khi và chỉ khi đúng một trang khớp**.

| họ | sửa được |
|---|---|
| phần con | 29/51 |
| lệch 1 trang | 40/112 |

**Duy nhất là điều kiện, không phải sở thích.** Nhiều trang khớp nghĩa là ta không biết trang nào là mở đầu; chọn trang đầu tiên là **đoán**, và đoán sai thì trẻ đọc nhầm chỗ. Không khớp trang nào cũng vậy. Cả hai ⇒ **giữ lại**. Dải sau khi dịch được **kiểm lại** trên dòng đọc đầy đủ.

## Kèm một lỗi nguyên tử lộ ra khi dựng

`build_lesson_figures.py` **xoá kho hình cũ ngay từ đầu**, nên một lần dựng hỏng giữa chừng (đã xảy ra thật: `disk I/O error` ở lớp 7) làm mất luôn kho **đang chạy tốt**. Nay dựng sang `.building` rồi `os.replace` — cùng bài học với `GradePackInstaller`.

Và bất biến pack **bắt được đúng trạng thái dở dang ấy trên dữ liệu thật**, không phải trong test: «lớp 5: pack tự khai `figuresPending`».

author: goldflag
body:
Adds authoritative Rust fleet battles and runs custom battles through the same Rust simulation in a WASM worker. Players select a fleet before queueing or joining an invite: at most 200,000 metric tonnes, eight ships and two carriers. Battles end on fleet destruction or after 30 minutes; remaining original tonnage determines the winner, with draws for equal tonnage or mutual destruction. Online matches draw map, weather and daylight, with night at 10%.

- Axum/Tokio handles admission and WebSockets; capped dedicated threads own full combat, bots, carrier operations and outcomes. SQLite persists immutable results and infrastructure aborts. Commands are ownership/epoch checked, both clients must load before countdown, and reconnects restore an authoritative baseline.
- Integrates current master’s Shōkaku, aircraft-specific ordnance, torpedo protection and carrier selection behavior. Keeps the shared versioned ship-definition format and renderer-free simulation.
- Claude Fable 5.1 reviewed the implementation and then the fixes. Addressed trusted-proxy admission, ghost tickets, compressed reconnect metadata, panic cleanup, input liveness, sunk-ship command spam, local failure visibility, cancellation and exit behavior. Its follow-up admission-budget and persistent-notice findings are fixed with regressions. [Review disposition](https://github.com/goldflag/ship-game/blob/goldflag/rust-fleet-multiplayer/docs/reviews/rust-multiplayer-review-disposition.md) links both verbatim reviews.

Linux CI exposed floating-point ties in centered hull contacts. Added matching Rust/TypeScript rules for centerline side selection and equal-depth collision axes, with regressions that perturb contacts/heading by rounding-sized amounts while preserving real off-center hits. Collision fixtures were refreshed deliberately for these corrections.

Validation: native workspace tests and Clippy with warnings denied; native/WASM comparisons across 28,800 full-battle ticks, 36 motion checks and 48 projectile cases; 133 TypeScript test files after final master integration (plus five overlay tests); production build and ship/aircraft checks; live HTTP/WebSocket cancellation, load barrier, ownership, movement, reconnect/replacement, forfeit and frozen-result smoke. Orca’s GPU browser also exercised two-client play, reconnect to a new epoch, Take helm switching and frozen-result retrieval after reload. Added all major checks plus the release-server socket smoke to GitHub Actions, with LFS assets downloaded for the real model checks. Six stale comparison packs were rebuilt through the pipeline with local Blender before master retired that archive. Integrated master `8495e905`, preserving those removals; no model geometry was authored.

Public launch remains separate: prior carrier-heavy measurements reached about 3.6–3.7 MB/s per player and missed the proposed 8 ms p99 complete-tick target. The default cap is two matches, exercised locally but not qualified on a deployment host. The build retains its large shared JavaScript chunk warning. No infrastructure is deployed by this PR. See [implementation and measured limits](https://github.com/goldflag/ship-game/blob/goldflag/rust-fleet-multiplayer/docs/rust-multiplayer-implementation.md) and [retained validation](https://github.com/goldflag/ship-game/blob/goldflag/rust-fleet-multiplayer/assets/reviews/rust-multiplayer-fable/README.md).

Full Linux validation passed on commit `6402f452`: [native/WASM, TypeScript, production build and release-server smoke](https://github.com/goldflag/ship-game/actions/runs/34202887964).

The duplicate PR run hit a shared-runner timeout in the existing 90-second simulated bot test (24.6 seconds against its 20-second wall-clock limit; the passing run took 17.5 seconds). Raised that test’s allowance to 60 seconds without changing its assertions or simulated duration. All 14 battle tests pass locally afterward; final CI is rerunning this timing-only adjustment.

author: francisdb
body:
Inserting a directory entry appended it to the storage's sibling tree without rebalancing. Streams created in ascending name order, which is the common case (`Item0`, `Item1`, ...), therefore formed one long right-leaning branch, and each insert walked all of its predecessors: creating `n` streams cost O(n²) name comparisons.

This applies the standard red-black insertion fixup, as MS-CFB 2.6.4 expects, so the tree stays balanced for this writer and for any reader that walks it.

**Compatibility.** The shape of the tree is visible to every other implementation. A file with 5600 streams in one storage written by the current code has a sibling tree 5600 levels deep; Python's `olefile`, which walks the tree recursively, fails to open such a file with a `RecursionError`. With this change the same file has a depth of 22 (the red-black bound for that count is 26), on par with what other writers produce, and `olefile` lists every entry and reads every stream back identically.

**Changes**

- `insert_dir_entry`: new entries join the tree red and get the insertion fixup (recolor while the uncle is red, otherwise one or two rotations). Every entry the fixup touched is written back.
- `remove_dir_entry`: the predecessor that moves up takes over the removed node's color, and a red child spliced under a red parent is made black, so a written file never has a red-red pair. Black height is not restored on removal; no reader checks it, and rebalancing on delete can be a follow-up.
- Entry writes no longer walk the directory chain from its start on every write; the chain's sector ids are cached (the chain only grows).
- Unallocated entries come from a free list instead of a scan of all entries.

**Measurements** (single-threaded, in-memory writer)

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| create 5611 streams of a few KB in one storage | 173 ms | 52 ms |
| criterion `write_streams_memory/n=10000,size=0B` | 267 ms | 8.5 ms |
| criterion `write_streams_disk/n=10000,size=0B` | 425 ms | 25 ms |

author: cbirkbeck
body:
`exp_norm_smul_of_ae_norm_le` and `exp_abs_smul_of_ae_abs_le` are the two declarations `lint-dot-notation` flags in `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Function/BoundedSupportExponential.lean`, and together they are the whole of `TauCeti.Integrable`.

## Why `MeasureTheory.Integrable` and not root `Integrable`

The obvious reading of the linter — move to the root namespace of the same name — would be wrong here. Mathlib's namespaces hold:

| namespace | declarations |
|---|---:|
| `MeasureTheory.Integrable` | **174** |
| root `Integrable` | **1** (`norm_condExp_rpow_le`) |

The lone root declaration is the anomaly, not the home. The predicate in both statements is `MeasureTheory.Integrable` — this file already says `open MeasureTheory` — so that is where dot notation on an `Integrable g μ` hypothesis resolves, and where these two belong.

Both stay `protected`, as they were.

The one external reference, a docstring in `Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Trigonometric/Chebyshev/Envelope.lean`, named the `TauCeti.Integrable.…` path this move destroys; it now names the rooted one, and the surrounding paragraph is rewrapped for the longer name.

`lint-dot-notation`: 978 → 976, 0 new.

body:
Players can now choose screen-reader output during character creation and change it later with `screenreader on|off|status`. The saved mode suppresses automatic ASCII maps and gameplay prompts while retaining room descriptions, input instructions, protocol delimiters, and underlying display preferences.

Adds independently saved `sound on|off|status|test` controls, requiring both player consent and negotiated MSP. Includes original bundled test and successful-door-open cues, checked preference saves with rollback, PREFEDIT updates, structured onboarding support, help content, and an additive help SQL migration.

Also includes the requested documentation and script updates standardizing the development game port on 4100.

## Validation

Rebased onto master `487c10f3d`. Review fixes are in `2d0128363`: Restore Defaults now revokes sound consent, the autorun path and 4100 guidance are corrected, and the help migration is included in the CI schema manifest. Added persistence regression coverage, missing function documentation, and the fixture's required `mkdir()` declaration.

Local CI-equivalent validation:

- `LUMINARI_IO_DRIVER=libevent make test-all` and `LUMINARI_IO_DRIVER=select make test-all`: pass, including 1,269 production-linked tests with isolated MariaDB, 31 protocol tests, world tools, schema tests, and auxiliary checks.
- ASan/UBSan production suite and 15-second protocol fuzzing: pass. Valgrind: zero errors and zero definite, indirect, or possible leaks.
- Coverage: 25.4% lines and 15.5% branches, above the 10.50%/7.16% CI floors.
- All 57 applicable component SQL files applied to fresh master schemas; the new help migration applied twice with exact flat-file text parity.
- Isolated autorun startup on game port 4100, healthy database/readiness, zero startup SYSERRs, and normal graceful termination: pass.
- Clean builds with `-Wall -Wextra`, formatting, secret scanning, DG/world documentation, shell syntax, shared port inventory, and byte-identical sound asset regeneration: pass.
- C/C++ security-extended and Python code-quality CodeQL analyses completed. The 22 C/C++ and 65 Python findings have no locations in changed lines. Dependency comparison reports no additions.
- Build/install and commit/push hooks pass; no root-level server binary remains.

The earlier live development checks covered creation, saved settings, map/prompt behavior, reconnect/copyover, MSP wire output, and mute behavior. The initial corrected persistence run also verified that the development player-index SHA-256 remained unchanged.

Final follow-up in `8e0217cdd`: deployment now stops with clear 4100 remediation for stale/custom game ports while preserving existing configuration. The extended `scripts/autorun/test_autorun_supervision.sh` passes. All 44 changed C function definitions have preceding documentation comments, and the new declarations are documented. Formatting, shell syntax, and commit/push build hooks pass. All four actionable review threads are addressed.

## Player-index regression and recovery

The initial persistence test incorrectly saved its synthetic player table into the real development `lib/plrfiles/index`. This hid existing characters from account menus. The final change fixes all five affected persistence fixtures to use self-cleaning filesystem directories; no additional database or server environment is introduced.

The local index was reconstructed with 6,303 entries from existing player files linked in the development database, and dedicated-account login was verified. Database account links were intact. For the reported account, 15 of 48 linked characters have local files and are indexed again; the cause of the other 33 absent files has not been established. This recovery limitation is documented, not treated as resolved by passing tests.

Real screen-reader usability and audible MSP playback remain unperformed follow-up validation. The requested code work is complete; production deployment is separate.

Implementation plan: `docs/ongoing-projects/SCREEN_READER_AND_MSP_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
Evidence and incident details: `docs/testing/SCREEN_READER_AND_MSP_ACCEPTANCE.md`.

Refs #137. Account-wide/automatic detection (#127) and score presentation (#126) remain separate.

author: blas1n
body:
**PR #892 를 버리게 만든 CI 실패가 이것이었습니다.** 그리고 **제품 코드는 한 줄도 잘못되지 않았습니다** — 창(window)이 잘못됐습니다.

## 왜 깨졌나

`claim_due` 는 claim 한 행에 **아무것도 쓰지 않습니다.** 락이 기제의 전부입니다:

```python
# backend/workflow/infrastructure/github/repository.py:97
stmt = build_merge_watch_claim_stmt(...)   # SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
result = await self._session.execute(stmt) # UPDATE 없음
```

그래서 이 테스트는 **첫 claim 의 트랜잭션이 열려 있는 동안에만** 의미가 있는데, 그 창을 `asyncio.sleep(0.05)` 로 샀습니다. 진짜 PG 에서 시각을 재보니 실제 여유는 **5ms** 였습니다:

```
A enter        0.0ms
A select ->6   2.4ms   ← 풀의 따뜻한 커넥션
B enter       22.8ms
B select ->0  49.3ms   ← 찬 asyncpg 커넥션 핸드셰이크에 26.5ms
A commit      54.2ms   ← 여유 4.9ms
```

부하 걸린 러너에서는 핸드셰이크가 이 경주를 이깁니다. 그러면 B 의 SELECT 가 COMMIT 뒤에 도착하고, 락이 없고, 표시도 없으니 **여섯 행을 그대로 다시 잡습니다** — 완전 중첩. CI 가 PR #892 에서 보여준 서명(`double claim: [6개] & [같은 6개]`)과 정확히 같습니다.

⭐ **완전 중첩이 단서였습니다** — 진짜 경합이면 부분 중첩이 나옵니다.

## 대조군

같은 제품 코드, 같은 진짜 PG, **창을 만드는 방식만** 다르게:

```
sibling +   0ms | sleep: overlap=0 ok           | handshake: overlap=0 ok
sibling +  50ms | sleep: overlap=6 DOUBLE CLAIM | handshake: overlap=0 ok
sibling + 200ms | sleep: overlap=6 DOUBLE CLAIM | handshake: overlap=0 ok
sibling + 500ms | sleep: overlap=6 DOUBLE CLAIM | handshake: overlap=0 ok
```

슬립 버전은 형제가 **50ms만 늦어도** 깨집니다. 핸드셰이크는 어떤 지연에서도 안 깨집니다.

## 수정

벽시계를 없애고 이벤트로 순서를 못박습니다 — 리포에 이미 있는 관용구(`tests/glue/test_session_release.py` 의 `parked`/`release`)를 따랐습니다:

```
A: SELECT (락 획득) → holding.set()
B: await holding.wait() → SELECT → sibling_done.set()
A: await sibling_done.wait() → commit
```

B 의 SELECT 가 A 의 SELECT 와 COMMIT **사이**에 있음이 보장되고, 커넥션이 얼마나 걸리든 상관없습니다. `wait_for(timeout=30)` 이라 배선이 깨지면 매달리지 않고 실패합니다.

`assert first` 를 더했습니다 — 원래 테스트는 **아무도 락을 안 잡아 `first` 가 비어도** 교집합이 공집합이라 통과했습니다. 공허하게 초록일 수 있었습니다.

## 인수인계 §Ⅳ.d 정정

인수인계는 이 실패를 *"`_is_pg` 를 버려서 조용히 SQLite 로 떨어졌다"* 로 진단했습니다. **틀렸습니다**:

- 이 테스트는 `skipif(not use_real_pg())` 뒤에 있고, 그 가드는 테스트가 생긴 날(#644, 2026-07-29)부터 있었습니다 — CI 에서는 **진짜 PG 로 돌았고 거기서 빨개졌습니다**
- `_is_pg` 를 버리는 곳은 7이 아니라 **164** (쓰는 곳 4). 이름이 `_pg` 인데 버리는 테스트는 **3개**이고 그 셋 다 `skipif` 로 보호됩니다

§Ⅳ.d 를 그대로 실행했으면 없는 문제를 고치고 진짜 원인은 남겨뒀을 겁니다.

## 나머지 두 레이스 테스트

`test_multi_server_safety.py` 의 delivery/relay 레이스도 20ms 슬립을 씁니다. 하지만 **같은 방식으로 깨지지 않습니다** — 그 drain 은 처리한 행을 DELETE 하므로, 형제가 늦게 와도 잡을 게 없어 이중 dispatch 가 안 납니다. 다른 약점(겹침이 실제로 일어났는지 확인 안 함 = 공허할 수 있음)은 있고, 별도로 다룰 일입니다.

## 검증

```
ruff ✅  format ✅  lint-imports ✅  mypy --strict ✅
진짜 PG(일회용 프로브 컨테이너)로 전체 스위트: 6728 passed
  └ 유일한 실패 test_rls_is_active_layer3_for_the_runtime_role 는 프로브 DB 가
    단일 superuser 역할이라 그 테스트의 첫 전제가 성립하지 않아서입니다.
    CI 는 최소권한 bsvibe_app 역할을 만들어 주므로 거기선 통과합니다.
```
