author: onlinerj
body:
## What is in this PR?

Fixes #443.

Events containing only word-cloud responses previously showed no Polls & Suggestions data to download. This adds word clouds to the combined event response export: each response gets its own `Wordcloud` row, with its prompt, participant, submission time, room, and upvotes. The file is named `prompt-responses-<eventId>.csv`.

## Changes in the codebase

- Save `WordCloudData` metadata alongside the existing response strings in participant agenda details. Transactions keep metadata and responses consistent, including concurrent duplicate submissions and explicit removal. New entries retain the prompt at submission time.
- Add `GetMeetingWordCloudData` request/response models and callable registration. Match existing export permissions: community admins or the event creator. Read main and breakout meeting responses and filter by the exact event/room path to prevent cross-event results when IDs are reused.
- Include word clouds in the export dialog count, empty-state handling, and combined CSV. Retry failed loading instead of silently exporting partial results. Pass the event agenda snapshot explicitly for suggestion prompts.
- Preserve existing CSV columns and poll/suggestion rows; use `Response` for the submitted message. Keep formula sanitization and add a UTF-8 BOM for Unicode-friendly spreadsheet imports.
- Update the existing labels in all four locales; regenerate shared models and add the Cloud Function deployment mapping.
- Add explicit browser-test plugin dependencies already present transitively; dependency versions are unchanged.

## Changes outside the codebase

Deploy `GetMeetingWordCloudData` before serving the updated client. No data migration or new Firestore index is needed: the existing collection-group `participant-details.meetingId` index covers the query. Evidence uses synthetic data in local Firebase emulators; no production data was changed. Evidence files live on a separate fork branch and are not part of the application diff.

## Testing this PR

**Passed: 9 targeted tests and the Functions build.**

- Six backend emulator tests cover admin/event-creator access, member/outsider/unauthenticated rejection, malformed paths, main/breakout entries, saved and legacy metadata, multiple entries/prompts, retained responses after meeting completion, and cross-event isolation.
- Two browser CSV tests cover word-cloud-only and mixed exports, headers/filename, UTF-8 BOM, Unicode, quotes/newlines, formula sanitization, and main/waiting/numbered rooms.
- One browser Firestore-emulator test verifies persisted submission metadata, concurrent duplicate suppression, multiple responses, and removal.
- Focused backend analysis: no issues. Focused client analysis: only two pre-existing `avoid_print` warnings in `firestore_meeting_guide_service.dart`.
- Manual browser verification: a legacy fixture with three responses across two prompts changes from an unavailable export to **3 Items**. Downloaded through the actual UI and verified all three CSV rows, prompts, Unicode, room names, zero upvotes, blank legacy times, and BOM bytes.

Commands (using the repository's local Flutter/Dart environment and a running Firestore emulator):

```bash
cd firebase/functions
GCLOUD_PROJECT=demo-frankly-443 FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:8080 CLOUD_RUNTIME_CONFIG=./test/test_config.json dart test test/events/live_meetings/get_meeting_word_cloud_data_test.dart --reporter expanded
dart run build_runner build --output=build --delete-conflicting-outputs
```

```bash
cd client
flutter test --platform chrome --web-renderer html --dart-define=WORD_CLOUD_EMULATOR_TEST=true test/lib/features/events/features/event_page/data/providers/prompt_responses_csv_export_test.dart test/lib/features/events/features/live_meeting/features/meeting_guide/data/services/word_cloud_storage_test.dart
```

### Before

Three stored word-cloud responses, but the original export reports None:

![Before: word-cloud responses unavailable for export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/onlinerj/frankly/0b5150a5881b43761da1ce54fffa53b02589f0ec/before-admin.png)

### After

The same responses are counted and the download is enabled:

![After: three word-cloud responses available for export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/onlinerj/frankly/0b5150a5881b43761da1ce54fffa53b02589f0ec/after-admin.png)

[Actual downloaded CSV](https://github.com/onlinerj/frankly/blob/0b5150a5881b43761da1ce54fffa53b02589f0ec/prompt-responses-wordcloud-443.csv) · [Callable response](https://github.com/onlinerj/frankly/blob/0b5150a5881b43761da1ce54fffa53b02589f0ec/api-after.json) · [Reproduction and evidence notes](https://github.com/onlinerj/frankly/blob/0b5150a5881b43761da1ce54fffa53b02589f0ec/README.md)

## PR Checklist

- [x] Where applicable, I have added localization (l10n) entries to my feature for user-facing text.
- [x] For new Cloud Functions, I have added the function to `function-mapping.json`.

## Additional information

The existing response strings were already persisted; this adds the missing metadata and export path. Legacy responses remain exportable with a blank Time and the current agenda prompt as a fallback, since historical timestamps/prompts cannot be reconstructed. New metadata retains the submitted prompt even if the agenda item is later edited or removed.

Word clouds have no voting mechanism, so Upvotes defaults to `0`. Existing one-copy-per-identical-word behavior, explicit removal, and agenda reset behavior are preserved. Ending an event does not delete its stored responses.

**AI tools used:** OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, automated checks, browser evidence capture, and this PR description. Human maintainer review is requested; this disclosure does not represent a completed independent human code review.

body:
## MCP Server Package Vulnerability or Malicious Package Risk

Autonomously authored by the Netzilo AIDR Lab. **status: experimental, action: report** — this rule observes, it does not enforce.

### Threat
This appears to be a package published on PyPI that presents itself as an MCP server but describes itself as a 'registry of software failures that report success.' This suggests a potential supply chain attack vector where a malicious or compromised MCP server could report false verification results, causing downstream AI agents or systems to trust untrusted or compromised software.

### Behavioural sequence
An attacker publishes a package verifyfirst-mcp on PyPI that presents as a legitimate MCP server. When integrated into an AI agent system, this server would provide false verification results, claiming success for failed or malicious operations. An AI agent relying on this MCP server would then trust and execute decisions based on fraudulent verification data, potentially leading to acceptance of compromised dependencies or execution of harmful operations.

### Provenance
- https://pypi.org/project/verifyfirst-mcp/1.2.1/
- source trust at ingest: 0.5
- content hashes: 76cf95e9b553e820

### Triage
- DAS **44.65** (lane P1)
- O=1.0 P=0.2 N=0.3769 I=0.7 E=0.6 H=0.5 (unmeasured)
- panel agreement: 0/3
- dissent:
  - triage_analyst: Malicious/deceptive MCP server packages that falsify verification results represent a genuine supply-chain trust attack against agentic pipelines, and the low similarity (0.34) to the nearest rule (MCP command-injection via shell metacharacters) confirms no existing rule captures this trust-falsification pattern. However, the deterministic findings show the engine rejects every semantic signal this attack actually needs — event_type 'mcp_server_call', 'load_model', and edge kinds MCP_CALL, REPORT_SUCCESS, TRUST_DECISION, VERIFY_FAILURE are all unknown to the schema — leaving only generic 'execute_process' telemetry live, which cannot distinguish a fraudulent verification report from any other MCP tool invocation. Until the schema models MCP call/response semantics and verification outcomes as first-class events/edges, this threat cannot be meaningfully detected beyond generic process-spawn monitoring already covered by process-based rules.
  - triage_coverage_skeptic: The nearest match (ae6e3887, MCP Server Command Injection via Shell Metacharacters) covers a completely different mechanism—injection of shell metacharacters into MCP command execution—not a package that fraudulently reports verification success to manipulate agent trust decisions. Similarity is only 0.34, and the schema explicitly rejects the edge kinds this threat would need (MCP_CALL, REPORT_SUCCESS, TRUST_DECISION, VERIFY_FAILURE) and the event type mcp_server_call, confirming no rule models this semantic content. I cannot honestly cite prior coverage; this is a genuinely novel supply-chain/trust-deception vector, and the engine currently has no telemetry surface (only execute_process events, no relevant edge kinds) to observe fraudulent verification reporting from an MCP package.
  - triage_reality_skeptic: The attack narrative depends entirely on edge kinds MCP_CALL, REPORT_SUCCESS, TRUST_DECISION, and VERIFY_FAILURE, all of which are explicitly rejected as unknown by the schema, and on event types mcp_server_call/load_model that the engine does not recognize. The only live event type is generic execute_process, which can show that a package was installed or run but carries no semantic information about an MCP server's verification claims or an agent's trust decisions — the actual mechanism of harm described here. Without a way to observe the content of MCP protocol exchanges or downstream trust decisions, this remains a speculative supply-chain narrative built on a single suspiciously-named PyPI package, not a demonstrated or telemetry-visible exploit chain.

### Gauntlet
- **G0** `pass` — lint clean
- **G1** `pass` — engine loaded 1 rule(s)
- **G2** `skipped` — no attack fixture for this threat
- **G3** `skipped` — no false-positive evidence (corpus tier 0, 0 benign fixtures)
- **G4** `pass` — p99 0.0ms over 0 sessions
- **G5** `skipped` — no fixtures to replay twice
- **G6** `skipped` — no attack fixture to mutate
- **G7** `skipped` — no existing corpus or no attack fixture to compare
- stamps: `no-determinism-evidence`, `no-fp-evidence`, `no-mutation-evidence`, `no-overlap-evidence`, `no-tp-evidence`

- corpus tier at authoring: **0**
- verified against 0 fixture(s)

### Invariants

author: danbeckdev
body:
Closes A1c (#487)

## What it is

A1b (#477, merged 06:15Z) selected tests by the import graph under `packages/*/src/` only. A change
outside that tree — `scripts/*.mjs`, a git hook, the workflows they are tested by — printed `BROAD` and
fell back to the full package-level scope. The chairman opened PR #479 (a git-hook change) expecting the
narrow path and saw the full suite: every conflict-fix row in flight that night was exactly this shape,
so none of them demonstrated the narrow path.

## The fix

Two more reference kinds, so `BROAD` narrows to what genuinely has no better answer:

- **`scripts/*.mjs`: BY IMPORT**, via the SAME reverse index `packages/*/src/` already uses —
  `sourceClosure`'s relative-import walk was never package-restricted, so a test reaching
  `scripts/foo.mjs` via `../../../../scripts/foo.mjs` was already in the index; this row is the first
  place anything LOOKS it up for a script's own changes.
- **A hook, or a non-`ci.yml` workflow file: BY PATH STRING**, since neither is ever `import`ed. Comments
  are stripped first (`@a11ign/evidence/source-text`'s `stripComments`, the same tool A2's
  `command-line-census.mjs` already uses) so a doc comment merely MENTIONING a path in this repo's own
  `` `scripts/foo.mjs` `` markdown convention cannot be mistaken for a test that actually exercises it —
  the #446 heading-collision shape applied to this search.

`BROAD` now applies to exactly two things: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` itself (a job definition can affect
anything the job runs) and `ci-changed.mjs`'s own `ROOT_TS_FILES` (exported rather than re-typed — this
file's own most-repeated lesson applied to itself).

The zero-tests fallback is unchanged in spirit: a `scripts/*.mjs` or hook/workflow file with no reference
anywhere falls back to **every implicated package's** full suite (there is no "its own package" for a
file outside `packages/`), named, never silent.

`selectTests` refactored to an options-object signature (was six positional params, tripping
`max-params`/`complexity`/`max-depth`) with the per-file dispatch extracted into `classifyOneFile`.

## Measured, on #479's own real shape

`scripts/git-hooks/pre-push` + its new test (`pre-push-resolve-toward-main.test.ts`):

| | files | wall clock |
|---|---|---|
| today's package-level scope | 260 | 212.9s |
| A1c (by-reference selection) | 7 | 42.0s |

**~5x, smaller than A1b's 29x, and the reason is specific rather than a shortfall of this row**: two of
the seven selected pre-push tests spawn real `git` subprocesses against repo history (one single test
took 14.4s in isolation) and are inherently slow regardless of how few files run. The narrowing itself —
260 candidates down to the 7 that actually reference the hook — is exactly as precise as A1b's; the wall
clock is dominated by what those 7 tests individually cost, not by how many ran.

Zero broad fallback on this diff — every selected test was found by real reference, none by the
package-level safety net.

## Mutation-checked, three separate breaks, because this is a *narrowing* change

A selector that silently picks too few tests is indistinguishable from a green suite, so each of these
was verified to actually turn a passing test red, not just to run:

1. **Remove the reference search call** (`const referencedBy = ctx.referencesPath(...)` →
   `const referencedBy = [];`) — makes every hook/workflow test go unselected. **THE GUARD BITES**: the
   three-hop and cross-package fixture tests, plus the real `#479` smoke test, all go red.
2. **Skip the comment-strip** (`stripComments(readFileSync(...))` → `readFileSync(...)` bare) — makes a
   doc-comment MENTION of a path read as a real reference. **THE GUARD BITES**: the dedicated
   "path mentioned only inside a comment is NOT a reference" test goes red.
3. **Break the zero-tests fallback aggregation** (`if (verdict.selectedBy.length === 0) { ... }` →
   `if (false) { ... }`) — the load-bearing half per dispatcher's explicit ask: this makes EVERY
   uncovered file (in any of the three shapes) silently report nothing, no fallback package named.
   **THE GUARD BITES**: every fallback-shaped test in the suite goes red at once.

## Verification

- New/updated tests in `select-changed-tests.test.ts`: 23 tests total covering both new reference kinds
  (synthetic fixtures + real-repo smoke tests), the comment-stripping guard, and the narrowed `broadReasons`.
- All 73 tests across `select-changed-tests.test.ts`, `ci-changed.test.ts` and `generated-paths.test.ts`
  pass (the last confirms `docs/commands.md`, regenerated after merging `main`, matches the tree).
- Also re-ran `cli-flags.test.ts`, `commands-documented.test.ts`, `command-dispatcher.test.ts`,
  `git-population-vacuity.test.ts`, `git-spawn-classification.test.ts` — 86 pass, 0 fail. No exemption
  needed on either git-population guard (both git-spawning call sites already import `sandboxGitEnv`).
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors. `npm run typecheck` — clean.

## A coupling worth naming, not fixed here

`ci.yml:163-167`'s `fetch-depth: 0` on the `ts` job's checkout is load-bearing for this selector
(`git diff <base>...HEAD` fails on a shallow clone). Worker-audit's A1 moves that job into
`reusable-build-test.yml`; the two diffs never touch the same line, so nothing here would show it in a
review, but the checkout declaration is the first place to look if the selector starts behaving oddly
after A1 lands.

## Acceptance

```
npx tsx --test packages/lab/src/packaging/select-changed-tests.test.ts
```

## Region

`scripts/select-changed-tests.mjs` and its test; `docs/pipeline.md` (new section documenting the
mechanism, regenerated `docs/commands.md`).

## Standing diff-check

```
$ git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD
M	docs/commands.md
M	docs/pipeline.md
M	packages/lab/src/packaging/select-changed-tests.test.ts
M	scripts/ci-changed.mjs
M	scripts/select-changed-tests.mjs

$ git diff --name-status origin/main..HEAD | grep '^D'
(none)
```

author: haribo
body:
## Summary

`file.download` refuses to fetch anything without a mandatory `sha256`. `docker.install` pipes `https://get.docker.com` into `sh`, as root. Two opposite answers to the same trust question, in one stdlib, with the contradiction never stated — so a reader cannot tell a considered exception from an oversight.

The position taken, and written into the def:

- **`file.download` fetches an artefact**: immutable, at a version the plan names, usually executed later by something else long after anyone looked. A hash is checkable and refusing an unverified one costs nothing.
- **`get.docker.com` is a script that changes with every Docker release.** Pinning a hash would break the def on each one, and a hash bumped without reading the diff is a ritual — the appearance of the guarantee `file.download` actually provides. What is trusted is TLS and the domain, which is what the apt route would need anyway: adding Docker's repository and signing key, on the authority of the same domain.
- So the def is **a convenience, not a guarantee**. A plan that does not want that trust does not call it — it installs docker through apt with a repository and key it chose, which shellf can already express.

## What is not being claimed

This does not make `docker.install` safe. It says why the risk is accepted and what a plan can do instead. `test/e2e/def-coverage.sh` now names the cost its exemption was hiding: this is the only def no e2e run ever executes, so **the least verified instruction in the stdlib is the one running remote code as root**. That sentence was the honest thing missing.

## Test plan

- [x] `grep -rn "get.docker.com" internal/` leads to the stated position, as the issue asked.
- [x] The def still parses and resolves — a plan calling `docker.install()` loads and reaches the transport.
- [x] `go test ./...`, `lint.sh`, `dead-code.sh`, `coverage-ratchet.sh`, `changelog-rule.sh`, `def-coverage.sh` (49 defs) — green.

## Scope

Documentation only. No behaviour changes, `file.download` is untouched, and no ADR: the position belongs next to the code it governs, and the issue offered either.

No changelog entry — a comment explaining a def is not something a shellf user observes in the tool.

Closes #601

author: tonyvelichko
body:
## Why

`sdk-rust` declares `reqwest = { version = "0.11", features = ["json", "rustls-tls"] }` without `default-features = false`, so reqwest's default `native-tls` stays enabled alongside rustls and every consumer links OpenSSL (`libssl.so.3`). In psonet/pso-chain-next that failed the production image's runtime-library gate on every release since v0.23.0; downstream `default-features = false` on the SDK cannot switch off a transitive default.

## What

One manifest line: `reqwest = { version = "0.11", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls-tls"] }`, and the SDK lockfile regenerated without any version change (the native-tls/openssl subtree drops out). No source change; the SDK's behaviour over `https` is unchanged since rustls was already enabled.

Consumed by pso-chain-next at commit 8de4c58 (pso-chain-next#158, released in v0.25.1). Please merge with a merge commit and keep the branch, since that revision is pinned downstream.

author: aoleon
body:
Automatic provider, model and reasoning selection could override the choice made in a session, including during retries, subtasks, reviews and compaction. This change removes those selectors and their policy endpoints, settings, templates and operational jobs from the public source tree.

Sessions and delegated work now inherit explicit selections. Choosing a different connection uses that connection's configured default unless a model is also explicitly selected. An unavailable selection produces an actionable error. Startup preserves existing choices, including legacy model IDs. The desktop and compact interfaces expose the connection, model and reasoning controls.

Existing transcript metadata remains readable. Context limits, cost budgets, permission controls and retries on the selected connection remain enforced. Fixed metadata helpers and credential diagnostics remain separate from task execution.

Validation:

- All workspace TypeScript checks and the complete Electron development build pass.
- The expanded focused CI suite passes 375 tests, including mission inheritance, task overrides, compaction and query selection.
- Source-boundary validation and its 8 Python regression tests pass; CI now blocks known removed routing implementations.
- Focused backend, Pi, configuration and renderer regressions pass. Browser checks cover desktop and compact manual selection, including persistence across connection changes and disabled controls during processing.
- Release, installer and packaging contract tests pass; no release or installed application is produced by this PR.

The journal stress test now has an explicit 30-second timeout for its 100 durable rewrites, avoiding cleanup races on slower or busy disks.

author: flpanbin
body:
## Overview:

Fixes the opaque HTTP 500 returned when a chat/completion request contains more than 4 `stop` (or `stop_token_ids`) entries. The request now fails fast at the HTTP boundary with a clear 400 validation error, and the two previously inconsistent stop-sequence limits in the codebase are aligned to a single constant.


## Details:

The bug had two layers:

- **Inconsistent limits**: pre-validation allowed up to 32 stop sequences (`MAX_STOP_SEQUENCES = 32` in `validate.rs`), while request extraction bailed at more than 4 (hard-coded in `openai.rs::extract_stop_conditions`). 
- **500 instead of 400**: the extraction failure was a plain `anyhow::bail!`, which the HTTP error mapper could not classify, so it fell through to the generic "Failed to generate completions" 500.

Changes:

- `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/validate.rs`
  - `MAX_STOP_SEQUENCES` tightened from 32 to 4, matching the OpenAI API contract.
  - Validation error messages corrected to the accurate "Maximum of N stop sequences allowed, got M" (the old "less than 4" wording was wrong — exactly 4 are accepted).
- `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai.rs`
  - `extract_stop_conditions` now uses the shared `MAX_STOP_SEQUENCES` constant instead of a hard-coded 4, with corrected messages.

The 500→400 fix is structural, validation now rejects over-limit requests at the entry point, so they never reach the engine path that produced the opaque 500.

## Where should the reviewer start?

1. `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/validate.rs` — the constant, the two `validate_stop` messages, and the new `stop_token_ids` count check in `validate_no_unsupported_fields`.
2. `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai.rs` — `extract_stop_conditions` backstop now shares the same constant.
3. Tests: `validate.rs` and `chat_completions.rs`

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib protocols::openai`
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-llm --lib`
- `cargo fmt -p dynamo-llm`
- E2E(Frontend + vLLM worker):

```bash
curl -s http://<frontend>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi"}],"max_tokens":5,"stop":["a","b","c","d","e"]}'

# response
{"message":"Validation: Maximum of 4 stop sequences allowed, got 5","type":"Bad Request","code":400}
```

```bash
curl -s http://<frontend>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"model":"Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi"}],"max_tokens":5,"stop_token_ids":[1,2,3,4,5]}'

#response
{"message":"Validation: Maximum of 4 stop token IDs allowed, got 5","type":"Bad Request","code":400}
```

author: jar-ben
body: A transient failure while downloading a *completed* (SUCCEEDED) cloud job's results used to bubble up and re-run the entire (often hours-long) proof. Retry the fetch itself with capped exponential backoff against the already-finished job instead — never re-prove. Complements the ProverCLI request-level retry/timeout: POU retries individual requests; this covers a whole-fetch failure that outlives those.

author: dbn1972
body:
## Summary

Closes **DOM-001** (P0): `project-service`'s delay-forecast endpoint
(`GET /v1/projects/:projectId/delay-forecast`) ran its Monte Carlo simulation
over a hardcoded array of 7 synthetic tasks (`task-1`..`task-7`) for **every**
project and tenant, so every project received an identical, fabricated
P50/P80/P95 forecast dressed up as real output.

- **`delay-forecast/repo.ts`** (new): loads the project's real tasks and
  dependencies from this service's own tables (`project.project_tasks`,
  `project.task_dependencies`), honestly mapping only the columns this schema
  actually persists onto the simulation inputs. Signals with no real source
  in this schema (per-task assignee, resource utilization, an SPI
  time-series) are left at 0/undefined rather than invented; a real
  dependency graph plus a real critical-path computation drive
  `isCriticalPath`.
- **`scheduling/repo.ts`**: adds `getProjectDepsWithLag()`, a tenant-scoped
  read of a project's dependency edges (type + lag) for the critical-path
  computation above.
- **`delay-forecast/routes.ts`**: the hardcoded `getProjectTasks()` stub is
  gone — replaced by the real repo call. A project with zero tasks (or none
  with usable planned start/end dates) now gets `422 INSUFFICIENT_DATA`
  instead of a silently fabricated `now()`-based estimate. The synthetic
  `task-1..7` constants are deleted, not left as a fallback.
- **`tests/delay-forecast.test.ts`**: seeds real rows for four distinct
  projects (two with ≥5 completed tasks and very different real durations,
  one with <5 completed tasks for the baseline-fallback path, one with zero
  tasks) and asserts on those real inputs, including a cross-project
  sabotage check that fails if two projects with different real task data
  ever produce the same forecast again.
- **`tests/all-routes.test.ts`**: this service-wide route smoke-test file
  mocks `project/repo.js` and `scheduling/repo.js` at the module level and
  had never needed to stub `listTasksByProject`/`getProjectDepsWithLag`
  (the old route never touched the DB) — both were missing, so every call
  threw and the generic error handler turned it into an opaque 500. Added
  both mock exports, seeded a real task row for the "returns forecast data"
  case (now pinned to that row's own baseline end date), and added a
  companion test asserting `422 INSUFFICIENT_DATA` for a project with no
  seeded tasks.

## Verification

- **Fresh, isolated Postgres bootstrap** (container `dom001-pg`,
  `localhost:5440`): `0 observed, 6 allow-listed` migration failures (the 6
  are the known PostGIS-conditional entries, correctly excluded from the
  ratchet), `RATCHET HOLDING — no new migration failures`, bootstrap
  completed cleanly.
- **Full `project-service` test suite** against that bootstrapped DB:
  **400/400 tests passing (18 files)**.
- **`tsc --noEmit`**: clean.
- **Sabotage check** (required for this class of fix): committed the fix,
  then temporarily replaced the current `delay-forecast/routes.ts` with the
  pre-fix version containing the hardcoded `task-1..task-7` stub, and
  re-ran `tests/delay-forecast.test.ts` + `tests/all-routes.test.ts`:
  **8 tests failed** with exactly the expected symptoms — synthetic
  `task-N` ids reappearing in `taskRisks`, the hardcoded
  `completedTaskCount=5`/`totalTaskCount=7` sent to ml-service regardless of
  which project was queried, two different real projects producing the same
  forecast, and a zero-task project getting a fabricated `200` instead of
  `422 INSUFFICIENT_DATA`. Restored the real fix afterward; the tree is
  clean and `git diff` against the restored file is empty; full suite
  re-confirmed **400/400 passing**.

## Test plan

- [x] Fresh Postgres bootstrap (migration ratchet holding)
- [x] Full `project-service` suite green (400/400, 18 files)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Sabotage check: reintroducing the deleted synthetic stub fails 8 tests
      with the expected symptoms; restoring the fix returns the suite to
      400/400 passing
- [ ] Review — not self-merging

| [17993915](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/single/17993915?groupId=628) | Unapproved registry usage | `spark.Dockerfile` | 60 medium | SLA 2025-01-18 |

~20 months past SLA.

## Why this is safe

The change is a **no-op for image content**. `3.5.5.0-slim` is byte-for-byte identical in
both namespaces — `sha256:e2c4762e38e3f57bfa99afdd68621c0be46eb373475c5578113c0e683b193126`
— verified anonymously against the Docker Hub registry API on 2026-09-08. Because an OCI
image-index digest hashes the whole index, including every child manifest digest, an
identical index digest proves the entire image graph is identical. The image remains
multi-arch (`linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`) and **public and anonymously pullable**, so no
registry credentials are introduced and fork PRs keep building.

## Why the icanbwell namespace and not the private ECR

CIE-8032's ratified target is the private services ECR. That was implemented on this branch
and then **deliberately reverted**: this repo is public and runs on `ubuntu-latest`, so a
private ECR needs a credential (static IAM key or OIDC) that does not exist today, and
**fork PRs would receive no credential at all**. The icanbwell namespace clears the same
finding with zero infrastructure dependency.

This is the **interim** option from CIE-8032, not the ratified target — it closes the finding
but does not complete the ticket, and does not block moving to the ECR later.

**How we know the rule keys on the namespace, not on Docker Hub:** this repo's own
`pre-commit.Dockerfile` pulls `python:3.12-slim` *from Docker Hub* and has **no** "Unapproved
registry usage" finding, while `spark.Dockerfile` pulls `imranq2/...` and does. Both files
carry the root.io and Alpine rules, proving both `FROM` lines are parsed. Across the org the
correlation is 10/10: every `imranq2` reference has the finding, every non-`imranq2`
reference does not.

Aikido's remediation text ("please publish them to public ECR") does not describe what
actually closes the finding — helix.pipelines cleared it by moving to the **private** ECR.

## Still open after this PR

Not fixable by a code change, and not dependent on any credential:

| Issue | Rule | Why not fixed here |
|---|---|---|
| [506324628](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/single/506324628?groupId=628), [506324629](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/single/506324629?groupId=628) | Not sourced from root.io ECR mirror | Accepts only `.../root-mirror/*`. `helix.spark` is b.well's own image, so Root.io will not mirror it. Needs the Aikido allowlist update tracked as CIE-8032 ask #3. (The ticket names `CUSTOM-RULE-558`; the rules actually firing are 559 and 2300.) |
| [648393632](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/single/648393632?groupId=628), [648393636](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/single/648393636?groupId=628) | Use Alpine base images | Keys on the repository **name**, not the tag — fires on images that genuinely are Alpine. Needs a false-positive exception. |

## Testing

CI on this PR is the first real build-and-test on this branch (earlier runs failed at an
AWS-credentials step that has since been removed). No Docker daemon was available locally,
so the build was not exercised on this machine — the digest identity above is the basis for
expecting no behaviour change.

## Why I'm doing:

When snapshot-protected and post-snapshot physical partitions share a shard group, StarMgr metadata sync can rediscover the group's full shard list while visiting an unprotected partition and delete shards owned by the snapshot-protected partition. This makes snapshot restoration unsafe and can surface as missing tablet errors.

## What I'm doing:

- Keep shard-group snapshot protection sticky for the entire table metadata-sync pass when either the exact materialized index or the exact shard group is present in cluster snapshot metadata.
- Remove all protected shard groups from redundant-shard candidates before any data or StarMgr metadata deletion.
- Add an order-independent regression test covering both snapshot predicates and a stale redundant shard.
- Preserve the existing deletion counter and deletion/error logging for unprotected shard groups. No new observability signal is needed because protected candidates now leave the destructive path before deletion.

body:
## Summary

- add per-root `follow | reject | ignore` symlink policy, with `follow` as the default
- preserve symlink objects while synchronizing their physical targets, including targets outside the selected local root
- make ignored/cyclic symlink namespaces non-authoritative so they cannot be misread as deletions
- pin physical local mutation targets in the durable operation journal for retarget-race and crash recovery safety
- expose paused-root configuration through `root config ID --symlinks MODE`
- document watcher behavior: root-external targets are repaired by authoritative periodic scans rather than recursive fsnotify expansion

## Safety / correctness

- self-links, mutual cycles, and physical-parent links are excluded safely
- dangling followed links remain authoritative virtual absence and can be recreated without replacing the symlink object
- downloads and local deletes revalidate the pinned physical target before mutation
- a surviving local recovery artifact blocks automatic replay instead of risking data loss
- schema v3 migrates existing roots to `follow` and adds the pinned local target field

author: creativedesignlead
body:
Groundwork for `Sidebar`. Adding these first so the rail's fixtures never
carry stand-in glyphs — a wrong icon on `main` is harder to dislodge than one
that never landed, and it would go straight into Chromatic's baselines.

## I was wrong about how many

I said three were missing. That count came from the **export's Heroicons
names**, not from the glyphs the design draws. Reading
`_VCP_SideBar_Item_Preset` — twelve rows, each with its icon — the real list
is eight.

| Row | Glyph |
|---|---|
| Dashboard | `layout` |
| My Values | `lightbulb` |
| Assigned | `user-check` |
| Task Log Trail, Contact List | `list-dashes` |
| Manage | `package` |
| Archive | `archive` |
| Planning | `rows` |
| Accounts | `users-three` |

Drafts and Domains were already covered by `file` and `globe`.

**Not one shares a name with what the export asked for.** It wanted
`squares-2x2`, `queue-list`, `pencil-square`, `clipboard-document-list`,
`archive-box`, `building-office`, `envelope`. Picking by name would have
produced eight wrong drawings — including `database` for Archive, which is
what the stand-in was. Each glyph was rendered beside the Figma frame and
chosen by looking at it.

## `@phosphor-icons/core` is now a devDependency

So the glyph source is in the repo and the next addition is a copy rather than
a transcription. It ships nothing — the markup is inlined into `icons.ts`,
which is what `Icon` reads, and the package is dev-only.

`docs/icon.md` now says to pick by looking, not by name, and records why.

## Three worth a second opinion

Close calls, each a one-line swap:

- **`layout` for Dashboard** — the design's is an asymmetric grid;
  `squares-four` is the symmetric alternative.
- **`user-check` for Assigned** — the design's check looks circled, which
  would be `user-circle-check`.
- **`package` for Manage** — `tray` is the flatter alternative.

## Product terms

The navigation rail can draw its own icons instead of borrowing ones that
mean something else.

## Tier / Tokens

No tier changes — `Icon`'s glyph set only. No tokens added or changed.

## Breaking changes

None. Eight names added to the `IconName` union; nothing removed or renamed.

## Checks

`npm test` — token lint, composition lint (52 pieces), plugin version,
typecheck. All green.

Verified by rendering all eleven nav rows with their new glyphs in Storybook
and comparing against the Figma preset frame.

author: nsta1
body:
## What

Four more `[GenerateSerializer]` / record value types whose only or principal payload is a `byte[]` (or a nested collection of `byte[]`) relied on the compiler-generated record equality, which compares a byte array with `EqualityComparer<T>.Default` - i.e. by **reference**. Two instances built from independently allocated but byte-identical payloads therefore never compared equal, and in particular an instance never equalled its own post-serialization self, silently breaking any value-equality assertion, cache, or de-duplication framed as record equality over these results.

This continues the established byte-array value-equality sweep (`SnapshotEntry`, `WalShardShippingEntry`, `CrdtElementsToolResult`, `DataGetToolResult`, `GSetDelta`, ...).

## Types fixed

| Type | Package | Byte payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CrdtMapToolResult` | `Orleans.Lattice.Api.Mcp` | `Fields` - `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IReadOnlyList<byte[]>>` |
| `AtomicActionEntry` | `Orleans.Lattice` | `Value` - `byte[]` |
| `LatticeSchemaRemediationReport` | `Orleans.Lattice.Schema` | `OffendingValuePreview` - `byte[]?` |
| `LatticeSchemaRemediationOutcome` | `Orleans.Lattice.Schema` | `OffendingValuePreview` - `byte[]?` |

Each now hand-writes `Equals` / `GetHashCode` comparing its byte payloads by content. `CrdtMapToolResult.Fields` is compared as an order-independent map whose per-field value lists are compared element-by-element (matching the sibling `CrdtElementsToolResult`), and its hash XORs per-field contributions so field order does not affect the hash.

## Safety

- **No public API change.** These records already expose `Equals` / `GetHashCode` / `==` / `!=`; hand-writing `Equals(T)` + `GetHashCode()` replaces the synthesized bodies and adds no new public member.
- **Wire format unchanged.** Orleans and System.Text.Json serialize the `[Id]`-tagged / JSON members, not `Equals`, so the change is serialization- and API-compatible. Verified by per-type post-serialization round-trip equality tests.

## Tests

Adds four regression fixtures (27 tests) mirroring the existing `SnapshotEntry` / `CrdtElementsToolResult` templates: value equality across independently allocated arrays, inequality on differing bytes / scalars / collection shape, empty-and-null handling, and a serialization round-trip that asserts a decoded instance equals its pre-serialization self. Existing `ImmutableGrainBoundaryContractTests`, sibling equality suites, and the schema remediation suites remain green.

No open issue tracks these types, so this PR closes none.

author: 0krt
body:
Four requests, in the order they were asked.

## Cube and icosahedron

Both are the sphere's own parameterisation pushed out to where each direction leaves the solid: for a body cut by planes at one distance from the centre that is `d / max dot(dir, n)` over the face normals, and with the normals in ± pairs the max is just the largest `|dot|`. The icosahedron's twenty face normals point at the twenty vertices of a dodecahedron, ten of them up to sign.

Keeping the sphere's `(u, v)` is the point — the surface bake, the pole folding, the metric the solver weights its laplacian by and the wireframe all carry over untouched, and only where the surface sits changes. The creases fall where they fall across the uv grid, so these two want more mesh than a smooth object before their edges read straight; the mesh density default went up to 256 for that among other reasons.

## Cell size

A new reaction slider, 0.6–4.0. Spot size is not normally a free parameter of Gray–Scott — it falls out of the diffusion lengths measured in grid cells, so the only ways to change it were the resolution setting or, on an object, the tiling. This scales the reference cell the solver already keeps.

The stencil can only step over whole texels, so the nearest whole number is what it steps and the field is read back between the cell centres. What is left over after that rounding is taken two ways:

- **short of a whole cell** — every tap is damped, which is exactly a shorter diffusion length, and costs nothing;
- **past a whole cell** — there is nowhere for the stencil to widen to, so the diffusion itself is raised and the timestep comes down by the same factor. `dt · D` is what the explicit scheme is stable in and it does not move, so the stability cap stays where it was and only the reaction integrates in smaller steps. A cell size a little above a whole number runs up to about twice as slow, which steps / frame buys back.

Without the second case half the slider would be dead: rounding alone can only give whole multiples. Verified continuous and monotonic across 0.7 → 1.0 → 1.25 → 1.5 → 2.0 → 3.0.

Two things fall out of solving on a lattice coarser than the field is stored on, and both are fixed here:

- A texel between cell centres now carries the reconstruction instead of running the reaction on its own. The kinetics are nonlinear, so the update of an interpolated value is not the interpolation of the updates, and the drift showed up as grain over a coarse field. Those texels are left exactly one step behind the centres, which nothing can see.
- Every derivative the shading takes — the emboss, the displacement normal, the liquid bead — is measured across a whole cell. The reconstruction is smooth in value but not in slope: its gradient dips to nothing at each cell and swells between, and a one-texel central difference was drawing that ripple as a lattice.

The v axis also gets the cell-centre reconstruction u already had, so a cell wider than a texel in v no longer leaves the even and odd rows solving independently of each other.

## Round seeds

Soft-edged discs of varying size, jittered inside their cells and swept 3×3 so a disc can cross a cell boundary whole rather than being clipped back into a square. A square hands the reaction four corners and two axes to grow along and the first frames of the pattern remember them. The seed pitch follows the cell size.

## Displacement at higher tiling

Displacement is a vertex move, so a feature of the field that falls between two vertices cannot lift the surface at all — it can only pull the two of them apart. Tiling makes the pattern finer on the object without touching the mesh, which is exactly why it only held together at low tiling.

Mesh density now sets the tessellation for *one repeat* of the field and the tiling multiplies it, under a vertex budget. The slider's ceiling went 256 → 512 and its default 144 → 256, and the displacement slider's step 0.005 → 0.002. The mesh build goes straight into typed arrays (at a few hundred thousand vertices the array growth cost more than evaluating the surface did) and is debounced, since the sliders that ask for a rebuild fire on every pixel of a drag.

## Checks

Driven headless in Chromium over SwiftShader: no shader compile or link errors, no page errors, and screenshots inspected for every object on and off the surface, every generative model, the wireframe, presets, band lock/unlock, and the cell size range. Displacement at tiling 6 now resolves individual pattern features as relief; before, the mesh could not have carried them.

author: dadofsambonzuki
body:
Follow-on from PR https://github.com/lnbits/lnbits/pull/4066

## Problem

When an NWC relay connection drops, the `NWCConnection` subscription-timeout sweeper (`_handle_timeouts`) skipped entirely because it started with `if not self.connected: continue`. As a result, in-flight request futures held by the old subscriptions were never resolved — not given a result and not given the timeout exception. Callers `await` those futures forever, so every NWC wallet on that connection stalls — and only a process restart (which wipes the state) recovers it.

## Change

- Run the sweeper's timeout scan even while the relay is disconnected, so timed-out subscriptions have their `future` raised with `Exception("timed out")` and callers unblock instead of hanging indefinitely.
- When the connection is down, close the stale subscriptions with `send_event=False` — dropping them from local state rather than attempting `CLOSE` against a dead socket (which would block on `_wait_for_connection` for up to 2 minutes per entry).

The change reuses the existing `send_event` parameter on `_close_subscription_by_subid` to avoid adding a new method.

## Test plan

- Drop the relay connection while requests are in flight and confirm callers resolve (timeout) rather than hang.\n- Confirm normal relay disconnect/reconnect still behaves as before.

author: shibinraj-cr
body:
Birthdays and work anniversaries surface in DesGro: a band on every page for everyone, and a one-time greeting for the person whose day it is.

DesGro has stored `Employee.dob` and `Employee.joinDate` since `0_init`, and has had a thin band under the header since News & Updates. It had never used the first to fill the second, and `joinDate` had never been read by anything at all.

## Two surfaces

**The band, for everyone.** `NewsTicker` generalises into `AnnouncementBand`: today's celebrations lead, unread headlines follow. Mounted once in the app layout that wraps every route, so it rides above every module rather than being wired per page. It sits *in flow*, so it pushes content down instead of covering it, and renders nothing at all when there is nothing to say — the band appearing *is* the notification.

**The greeting, for one person.** Canvas confetti and their name, on their first page load of the day. Silent, unlike the enrolment fanfare — a birthday greeting arrives unannounced, possibly in a meeting, on a machine whose volume nobody checked.

## Derive, don't store

Who is celebrating today is a pure function of the date and the employee table. No daily job to babysit, no backfill, and a corrected date of birth is right immediately. The one persisted fact is `HrCelebration` — one row per `(employee, kind, year)` written when a greeting is shown, so it fires exactly once a year across devices.

The band query is chained inside the layout's existing `Promise.all`, so it overlaps the badge counts rather than adding a round trip to every page render. `pendingGreeting` only spends a query when the viewer is actually one of today's celebrants.

## Decisions worth a second opinion

- **Anniversaries run every completed year**, not only round-numbered ones.
- **Dates are IST-anchored** (new `istToday` in `dates.ts`). Every other date helper here is UTC, which flips at 05:30 IST — a UTC "today" shows yesterday's birthdays to anyone looking at the screen before dawn.
- **29 February is celebrated on the 28th** in non-leap years, not 1 March, so it stays inside the month the person thinks of as theirs. One-directional: a real 28 February birthday never fires twice.
- **`joinDate` landing on today in the year of joining is a start date**, not an anniversary. Anniversaries begin at year one.
- **Age is off by default.** A date of birth is on file for payroll, not for publication; HR can turn it on deliberately.
- **Opting out is the employee's own switch** on `/me/account`, not an HR field, and it suppresses both surfaces.
- **The band caps** celebrations at 4 and headlines at 4 alongside them. The marquee scrolls a fixed distance in a fixed time, so a longer reel does not take longer to read — it moves faster.

## Also in here

Corrects the birthday template's sign-off from `Team DESGRO` to `Team DESMA`, in the column default and in any saved row still carrying the shipped default verbatim (an edited row is left alone). DESMA is the company; DesGro is the ERP it runs on. This has been wrong since `0_init`.

`/me/birthdays` grows a Today section covering both kinds, because that is where the band lands — a page answering with birthdays alone would not contain what the reader just clicked.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, `vitest run` all clean. 16 new tests in `tests/celebrations.test.ts` cover the IST rollover, the leap-day rule in both directions, and template rendering.
- **Not smoke-tested against a live database or in a browser** — there is no branch DB configured (`.env.branch` absent), and the only connection string available is production. Needs a Neon branch, `npm run db:migrate:branch`, and a look at the band and the greeting before merge.

## Migration

`20260908130000_celebration_band` — adds `Employee.celebrationOptOut`, five columns on `HrBirthdaySettings`, and the `HrCelebration` table. Additive; no destructive statements.

author: bwsalmon
body:
Give branch boxes the search-and-pick the repo boxes have

Every branch on these forms was a bare text box: whoever filled one in
had to remember how the branch they wanted was spelled, and a typo only
surfaced later as a run that could not find its base. The repo beside it
has offered a list to pick from for a long time, and a branch is the
same kind of answer.

BranchField.jsx is that box -- type to search, arrow keys and Enter or a
click to pick, free text still the ordinary thing to type, since grain's
branch list is what it has been asked to create or adopt and never the
whole of GitHub's. The suggestions come from two places: the branches
grain knows about on the repo the box is about, fetched from
/api/repos/{owner}/{name}/branches the first time the box is opened and
cached per repo, and (state.js's branchesInUse) the branches this
deployment's own tasks are already working off in that repo.

Wired into the task forms first: New task's own base branch, the base
box beside each extra repo a task may write to, and the base branch on a
task's detail pane. The detail pane's save now takes the settled value
from the field rather than reading its own state, because a pick reports
the branch and updates that state in the same tick.

Also on this branch:
- Offer branch suggestions on the rest of the branch boxes
- Test the branch suggestions, and keep a settled list off the button below

author: eggsleggs
body:
Both Worker `Env` types had drifted from the configs that generate them.

- The API's was missing six secrets its `wrangler.jsonc` declares and its code reads: both Supabase auth overrides, the Metafy webhook secret, both Upstash keys and the TCGplayer affiliate id. Its `LEGAL_TERMS_VERSION` literal was also a version behind after #172.
- The ingest worker's was missing the two secrets added in #175.

A binding missing from the generated type is not a compile error, because nothing reads the type for a key it does not contain. The drift is invisible until someone trusts the type and finds the value absent, which is the same shape as the bug #175 fixed one layer down.

## The change

Both files regenerated with `wrangler types`. Then `scripts/check-wrangler-consistency.mjs` grew a fourth check: every name in a Worker's `vars` and `secrets.required` must appear in that Worker's generated `Env`.

It compares **names only**, never the generated file's shape or its hash. A full regenerate-and-diff check would have been sensitive to the wrangler version, so a Renovate bump would turn an unrelated PR red; this cannot.

## Verification

- Proven to fire: restoring the stale API types produced six failures naming each missing secret and the command to fix it. Restored, and the check passes.
- Three unit tests beside the existing ones, covering a missing binding, an optional one counting as present, and a name that appears only inside a longer identifier.
- `bun run check` passes, including `check:wrangler`.

author: shuette42
body:
A gap in the gate that closed itself the same day it was opened.

The Lint job ran the linter and never the formatter. So the reflow that made the tree consistent was held in place by nothing at all, and it decayed within hours: the pull request that landed between that pass and this one brought three files in unformatted, the check stayed green, and the only reason anyone noticed is that the formatter was run by hand afterwards.

```
custom_components/ecoflow_energy/ecoflow/frame_capture.py
tests/test_fixture_identifiers.py
tests/test_frame_capture.py
```

The job now runs `ruff format --check` as its own step, and those three are reformatted. The formatter touched only whitespace; nothing else in this change.

Worth stating for the record, because it is the same shape as the finding that started this whole line of work: a check that runs but gates nothing is not a gate. That was true of the linter and the type checker before they were added to the branch ruleset, and it was true of the formatter until this.

## Numbers

- `ruff check` clean over both trees
- `ruff format --check`: 146 files already formatted, from 143
- The type checker reports no issues in 62 source files and none in 84 test files
- 3331 tests pass, 1 skipped

Aucun `.cursor/environment.json` n'existait auparavant. Cette PR ajoute une configuration **gérée par le dépôt** qui provisionne toute la stack automatiquement. ## Fichiers ajoutés - `.cursor/environment.json` — image par défaut, utilisateur `ubuntu`, scripts `install`/`start`, terminaux `backend`/`frontend`, ports `3333` et `5173`. - `.cursor/install.sh` — bootstrap idempotent : installe PostgreSQL, crée le rôle/la base `bnb`, génère les `.env`, `npm ci` (back-end + frontend), `prisma generate`, `prisma migrate deploy`, et seed (uniquement si la base est vide). - `.cursor/start.sh` — démarrage par boot : lance le cluster PostgreSQL (gère un pid obsolète du snapshot) et attend qu'il soit prêt. ## Lifecycle - **install** : dépendances système/npm, client Prisma, migrations et données de démo (baked dans le snapshot). - **start** : réconciliation par boot du serveur PostgreSQL. - **terminals** : serveurs de dev backend (`npm run dev`) et frontend (`npm run dev`). ## Validation | Vérification | Résultat | | --- | --- | | `install.sh` exécuté deux fois | Idempotent (seed ignoré si des utilisateurs existent) | | Backend `npm run build` (tsc) | OK | | API `/health`, `GET /logements`, `POST /auth/login` | OK (60 logements seedés, JWT) | | Frontend `http://localhost:5173` | Charge les 60 logements + flux de connexion complet | | **Build d'environnement draft** `bld-20260908-bc5022b1…` | **SUCCEEDED** — PostgreSQL, migrations et seed sur machine propre | | **Agent frais** (boot depuis le build) | node 22.14 / npm 10.9.7 / psql 16.15 ; 11 users, 60 logements ; `.env` + `node_modules` présents ; API + login JWT + frontend 200 | ## Notes - Les fichiers `.env` sont générés par `install.sh` et restent gitignorés (valeurs de dev par défaut ; `GEMINI_API_KEY` optionnelle pour les fonctionnalités IA). - L'échec préexistant de `npm run type-check` côté frontend (types `jsdom` manquants dans `tsconfig.test.json`) est hors périmètre de cette PR.

Both are follow-ups this session measured while landing #4569/#4571/#4574/#4577. A third finding I had offered is **retracted below** rather than filed.

---

## W1-T3141 — the inherited-violation notice cannot fire in the one place it runs

W1-T3037 shipped a real repair: when `source-size-ratchet` blocks, it re-measures each violating file at `origin/main` and tells the author which reds they **inherited** rather than grew. Ten tests cover the helper. None of it reaches CI.

**The job cannot see the ref it measures against.** `source-size` checks out with a **bare** `actions/checkout` — no `with:` block at all, so the default `fetch-depth: 1`, and on a `pull_request` that fetches only the merge ref. It is the only ratchet job in the file that reads `origin/main` at check time without asking for it. Nine siblings set `fetch-depth: 0`, and the two either side of it say why:

| job | its own comment |
|---|---|
| `task-id-existence` | "so that ref must exist. An unreadable base read as an empty one is the **false zero** that produced the 2026-08-26 id collisions" |
| `comment-load-ratchet` | "Without it the base read fails and the gate **REFUSES by design** (an unreadable base read as an empty diff is a false zero)" |
| **`source-size`** | *no `with:` block* |

**And a missing ref is indistinguishable from a missing path.** `contentAtRef` decides between `absent` and `unreadable` on the exit **status** of `git show <ref>:<path>`, and git exits 128 for both — measured in a throwaway repository, with a positive control:

```
git show main:nosuch.txt   -> fatal: path 'nosuch.txt' does not exist in 'main'   exit 128
git show origin/main:f.txt -> fatal: invalid object name 'origin/main'.           exit 128
git show main:f.txt        -> (content)                                           exit 0
git rev-parse --verify --quiet 'main^{commit}'         -> exit 0   <- separates them
git rev-parse --verify --quiet 'origin/main^{commit}'  -> exit 1
```

So every violation is pushed to `introduced`, `inherited` is empty, `inheritedNotice` returns `undefined`, and **nothing prints**. The gate reports the author grew every one of those files.

This is the third outcome the helper exists to preserve, lost at the boundary. Its own comment says an unreadable ref "is not treated as clean either; it yields `undetermined`, because 'we could not ask' and 'the base is fine' must not arrive as the same answer." That is exactly what happens.

It survived because the split runs only when the ratchet **blocks**, all ten tests inject a `run` so none exercises a real checkout, and the failure is a **missing sentence**, not a red.

## W1-T3142 — a PR cannot restate its own shard's acceptance criteria

Driving the shipped `bodyContradictsDiff` over a diff of `[.github/workflows/ci.yml, test/x.test.ts]`:

```
1 contradiction   "a plan-only diff still classifies as PLAN_ONLY when commits land on the base"
                    ^ W1-T3060 acceptance criterion 2, VERBATIM from the merged shard
1 contradiction   "This PR is plan-only."            <- CONTROL: a deliberately false claim
0                 "`a plan-only diff still classifies ...`"   <- the same text, backtick-quoted
0                 "Fixes the diff base. Touches the workflow and one test."  <- no claim
```

**The criterion and the lie are indistinguishable.** #4577 hit this and had to **omit its Acceptance block** to be reviewed — on a task whose criteria the gate then resolved from the shard anyway.

The sharpest evidence is in this repository's own history: **that exact criterion sits in #4484's merged body**, harmless, because #4484's diff was plan-only and the violator set came back empty. The same words became fatal on the PR that implemented it. The wording never changed; only the diff did.

**Why the W1-T3061 guards do not cover it.** The attributive arm reads the noun the shorthand modifies (`diff`, a changeset word) then asks whether a copular frame names a foreign subject. In "a plan-only diff still classifies …" there is **no copular frame at all** — the noun phrase opens the sentence, `ATTRIBUTIVE_SUBJECT_RE` returns null, and the arm's documented fail-closed rule ("an absent frame leaves the refusal standing") refuses. Correct for the arm; wrong for this text, because the text is not the author speaking.

**It has bitten before, in the same place, and was recorded rather than fixed.** The comment above the shorthand loop already reads: *"TRAP: W1-T413's own criteria name `test/trailer-credit-plan-only.test.ts` … so quoting the required proof forced failure."* That is this defect with a proof path instead of a claim.

The fix is the third application of a principle already in the file — **a quotation is not an assertion** (W1-T308 blocks and fences, W1-T2534 inline spans) — extended to the acceptance region, for claim scanning only, through **one shared region walk** rather than a second copy of the boundary.

---

## Retracted, not filed

I had also offered *"`source-size` is PR-only, so main's own push run skips it and a merge can land over an unrecorded ceiling."* **That is wrong.** `ci.yml` line 206 runs `run_main_ceiling_gate source-size-ratchet source-size-ratchet` on main's push lane — W1-T3068's merged design already covers a merge crossing a ceiling no PR crossed. No id was spent on it.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `lint-plan --base origin/main` | **2 task(s) checked — 0 failing, 1 warning** |
| that warning | W1-T3141 `[sizing]` spans 4 concerns at `band_meaning: span` — "reported, not refused (W1-T2503)", and the `risk:` line carries the Rule 19 note |
| all 12 proofs | `parse: OK` — 10 `kind=test`, 2 `kind=grep` |
| every proof at this head | **`verdict: fail`, 0 hits** — the forward-referencing shape a filing needs |
| both `grep:` proofs at base | `refResolvable` and `acceptanceBlockRegion` are **new symbols**, absent on `origin/main`, so each discriminates |
| `files:` form | both **inline** `files: [...]` — a block-form list silently empties `forwardReferenceFiles` |
| ids held | `git ls-remote origin 'refs/rmd-id/W1-T314*'` returns both, alongside `W1-T3140` |

No trailer: a filing cites a task, it does not implement it.

## Acceptance

- claim: a ref that is not present in the checkout is reported as unresolvable rather than as a file absent at the base, so no violation is attributed to a diff on a base nobody could read
  proof: unit test: test/an-unfetched-base-is-not-an-absent-file.test.ts
- claim: git exits 128 for a missing ref and for a missing path alike, so exit status alone cannot separate them while the rev-parse probe can
  proof: unit test: test/an-unfetched-base-is-not-an-absent-file.test.ts
- claim: the shipped ratchet run against a checkout with no origin/main says it could not determine whose red this is, instead of printing nothing
  proof: unit test: test/an-unfetched-base-is-not-an-absent-file.test.ts
- claim: a criterion restated inside the Acceptance block is not read as the body's own scope claim, so a PR can state what it must achieve in the words its shard already uses
  proof: unit test: test/a-criterion-restated-is-not-a-claim.test.ts
- claim: the same sentence in ordinary body prose is still refused, so the exemption is the region and never the wording
  proof: unit test: test/a-criterion-restated-is-not-a-claim.test.ts
- claim: a body carrying no acceptance header scans exactly as it does today, character for character
  proof: unit test: test/a-criterion-restated-is-not-a-claim.test.ts

author: jackthepunished
body:
The spec re-pull in #46 brought in 30 paths the brief was written before. This calls fourteen of them and settles the brief's two judgement calls; managed PostgreSQL follows separately.

**On the app page**
- **Request analytics** (`/analytics`, `/analytics/timeseries`) on the Metrics tab: aggregate tiles, the API's own grouping dimensions (route, country, referrer host, client, status) as a bounded table that says when it was truncated, and the hourly series drawn as a line — the timeseries endpoint zero-fills its buckets, so a line is honest there where scalars stay tiles. A clamped window says it was clamped.
- **Restart** in the header (`/restart`): parks every instance and queues one replacement wake, and the toast names the `wake_id` so it can be found in the wake timeline. `409` is one already running; `402 admission_refused` is the spend cap, not a fault.
- **Cache purge** in Configuration (`DELETE /cache`): optional path glob, and the wording says a purge was *requested*, which is what a 204 there means.
- **Deploy an archive** on the Deployments tab (`/deployments/source-tarball`): the console's half of `gregale deploy --tarball`, with the ADR-116 annotations (reason, tag) that make a deploy auditable later.
- **Rollout recovery** in the deployment drawer (`/rollouts/recover`, judgement call 1 — implemented): advance, promote, abort with a reason. Advance is only legal once the platform calls the rollout stuck, and its `409 rollout_not_stuck` is repeated verbatim, suggestion included, rather than softened.

**Elsewhere**
- **Request evidence** (`/debug/requests/{req_id}`, `/evidence`): a row in the debugger opens the spans behind it and the platform's own explanation, with the blamed span marked and the matched regression stated against its baseline.
- **Upstream probe history** (`/upstreams/history`) under the upstreams table: a sparkline per upstream because the shape is the point, buckets with no samples left out rather than drawn as zero, and the last measured pair in words.
- **Bucket access** (`/access-grants` ×2, `/s3-credentials` ×2) under the object browser: API-key grants show the key's own status, because a grant on a revoked key grants nothing; S3 secrets are shown once, with the warning that they are not kept.
- **Object storage usage** (`/v1/account/object-storage-usage`) on the Usage page, against the policy caps, with a stale report saying so.
- **Trigger configuration** (`GET /v1/triggers/{id}`, judgement call 2 — implemented): read-only detail under the counts. Editing stays in `gregale.yaml` and the CLI; reading what is deployed answers "why is nothing arriving".

Non-goals recorded for the rest of the pull: the resumable upload protocols (`/v1/uploads` ×3, multipart ×5) are driven by the CLI and SDK — the console deploys an archive in one request and uploads objects through signed URLs; `dev-source` and `/v1/dev/sessions` belong to the local `gregale dev` loop; `verify-email` is a non-UI auth flow; `POST /v1/apps/{slug}/deployments` keeps registry credentials out of the browser; and the admin usage report belongs to the operations console.

Exercised over HTTP against the mock (33 checks): analytics with each dimension, bad `group_by` (400), a clamped window, 24 timeseries points; debug request and evidence, unknown id (404); cache purge with and without a glob (204) and a bad glob (422); restart (202) then again (409); restore on a live app (409); upstream history and a bad bucket (400); recover advance (409 `rollout_not_stuck`), bad action (400), promote (200), again (409 `rollout_state_invalid`); storage usage; grants list, PUT, bad permission (422), unknown key (404), DELETE then again (404); S3 credential create (201 with the one-time secret), no label (422), revoke (204); trigger detail; archive deploy (202) and a JSON body (400). Under `MOCK_PLAN=free`: analytics and timeseries 402 `plan_per_app_metrics_not_allowed`.

Coverage: 176/255 → 193/255 paths called. `npm run check` green (32 new tests, 403 total).

---

**Review fixes:** two Criticals. (1) `BucketAccess` was handed the bucket **name**, but every bucket sub-route takes the bucket **id** (`format: uuid`), and every pre-existing call site passes the id — all six requests would have failed against the real API. The mock accepted any string as the identifier, which is exactly why the HTTP check passed; it now enforces the id shape so this cannot be masked again. (2) `TriggerConfiguration` read five field names that do not exist on the schema (`filter`, `batch_size`, `max_retries`, `target`, `app_slug`), because a cast to `Record<string, unknown>` opted out of the typing that would have caught it; the panel rendered only Created and Updated. It now reads `filter_criteria`, `batch_size_max`, `max_attempts` and the `config` blob, untyped-cast removed, and the test fixture is the real schema. Also: object-storage costs fall back to EUR (the documented currency) rather than USD, and the 409/422/413 branches match on codes rather than status.

author: dejeune
body:
> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The AI layer ran chat, embedding, rerank and image requests through one undifferentiated pipeline (`AiBaseRequest` → `buildAgentParamsFor` → `buildAgentParams` → `resolveProviderAiSdkConfig`), with no type that says "this is a chat request". A chat-only need therefore had no legal home: OpenCode Go/Zen's mandatory `x-opencode-session` header was set from an optional `sessionId` on the provider config that only the chat path supplied, so model health checks, context compaction, image jobs and gateway calls reached OpenCode without it. `chatId` doubled as stream key, topic id and provider affinity key, and `streamPrompt` rewrote it for gateway streams.

After this PR:

The modality axis exists end to end:

- **Types** — `AiRequest` is the transport base (model, credential, request options). `AiChatRequest` adds `conversation: ConversationRef { id, topicId? }` and the turn-shaping fields only chat uses (`mcpToolIds`, `reasoningEffort`, `serviceTier`, `fastMode`, `knowledgeBaseIds`, `contextOwner`, `callOverrides`). `AiStreamRequest` and `AiGenerateRequest` extend it; embedding, rerank and image requests extend `AiRequest` and have no conversation. The IPC schemas split the same way (`aiRequestShape` / `aiChatRequestShape`).
- **Pipeline** — `src/main/ai/provider/sdkConfig.ts` is the modality-agnostic transport core (`resolveSdkConfig`: provider config + wire model id + `providerOptions` namespace). `buildAgentParams` is chat-only and layers tools, prompt, context and fallbacks on top. `AiService.embedMany` / `rerank` / `generateImage` call the core directly instead of the chat pipeline.
- **Provider** — builders never read request context. `buildOpenCodeGoConfig` only declares `ProviderConfig.conversationHeader = 'x-opencode-session'` (unless the user configured the header explicitly); `buildAgentOptions` fills it from `request.conversation.id`, and caller-supplied headers win.
- **Callers** state the conversation where the request is born: the three chat context providers and agent-session runtime turns pass the topic (raw agent session id as the conversation), `streamPrompt` passes the stream id or the trusted agent session, `TopicNamingService` its topic, `checkModel`'s text probe one id per probe, and the `ai.text.generate` handler one id per renderer call. `chatId` is no longer rewritten for gateway streams.

Fixes #

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The root cause is structural, not a missing parameter: different kinds of requests shared one pipeline that could not tell them apart, so any chat-specific requirement pushed into it had to become either optional (silently absent on every path but the one that added it) or fabricated for callers that have no conversation at all. Giving the pipeline a modality axis lets the requirement live where it is meaningful and nowhere else.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- `conversation` is required on `AiChatRequest` and absent from the other request types. There is no optional context parameter and no fallback anywhere below the caller; `ProviderConfig.conversationHeader?` is provider capability metadata ("absent" is a real value), not request context.
- Callers without a topic (health probes, renderer one-shot `ai.text.generate`) mint one id per call at the call site. That is the caller stating its unit of work, not a default inside shared code.
- `resolveSdkConfig` moved to `provider/` so the transport core no longer lives inside the chat params module; `SdkConfig` is re-exported from `params/scope.ts` for existing importers.
- `chatId` stays on `AiStreamRequest` as the stream manager's topic key; `ConversationRef.topicId` carries the same value below the pipeline boundary. Collapsing the two is left for a follow-up.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Keeping `sessionId` optional on the provider config and passing it from more call sites — rejected; every future path would still have to remember.
- Making a required identity on the shared base and stamping it inside `AiService` — rejected; the verbs do not own that fact, and non-chat callers would have to invent one.
- A `randomUUID()` fallback inside the OpenCode builder — rejected; a builder must not invent a conversation.
- A provider-keyed header table in `buildAgentParams` — rejected; a second per-provider dispatch next to the existing builder table.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #18184 introduced the optional `sessionId`.

### Breaking changes

None for users. Main-internal API: `AiBaseRequest` is replaced by `AiRequest` / `AiChatRequest`; `AsInProcess` no longer carries chat-only sinks (`AsInProcessChat` does); `AiStreamRequest` and `AiGenerateRequest` require `conversation`; `AiGenerateRequest.chatId` is removed; `ProviderToAiSdkConfigOptions.sessionId` is removed.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- Deleted the two behavior-pinning tests that asserted `sessionId` forwarding, and replaced them with contracts: the OpenCode builder declares (and does not declare when the user configured the header), `buildAgentParams` fills the declared header from the conversation with caller headers winning, and the stream manager's conversation decisions (`AiStreamManager.test`).
- `AiService.test` now spies `resolveTransportFor` for embedding / rerank / image tests instead of the chat pipeline.
- `docs/references/ai/provider-resolution.md` and `params-pipeline.md` describe the transport core, the chat-only pipeline and the "builders declare, the chat pipeline fulfils" rule.
- Verified locally: `tsgo` main project clean; vitest over `src/main/ai`, `features/apiGateway`, `features/knowledge`, `shared/ipc`, the IPC `ai` handler and `TopicNamingService` (428 files / 6388 tests green); eslint, biome and `oxlint --deny-warnings` on changed files; `pnpm docs:check`.
- Follow-up (separate PR): split `checkModel`'s probe dispatch into a per-modality table and move the image job branch out of `AiService`.

### Checklist

This checklist is not enforcing, but it's a reminder of items that could be relevant to every PR.
Approvers are expected to review this list.

- [x] Branch: This PR targets `main`
- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future contributors
- [x] Code: [Write code that humans can understand](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Martin_Fowler#code-for-humans) and [Keep it simple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KISS_principle)
- [x] Refactor: You have [left the code cleaner than you found it (Boy Scout Rule)](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/97-things-every/9780596809515/ch08.html)
- [x] Upgrade: Impact of this change on upgrade flows was considered and addressed if required
- [ ] Documentation: A [user-guide update](https://docs.cherry-ai.com) was considered and is present (link) or not required. Check this only when the PR introduces or changes a user-facing feature or behavior.
- [x] Self-review: I have reviewed my own code (e.g., via [`/gh-pr-review`](/.claude/skills/gh-pr-review/SKILL.md), `gh pr diff`, or GitHub UI) before requesting review from others

### Release note

```release-note
[Provider] OpenCode Go/Zen requests from model health checks, topic naming and context compaction now carry the required `x-opencode-session` header.
```

author: basharsroor-droid
body:
Follow-up to #217. Adds a comparison band to `/pricing` so visitors see the fixed-per-business price is a good deal — **without naming any competitor**.

## What

A three-item band below the plan cards:

| | |
|---|---|
| כלים גלובליים | per-user billing ($3–9/user) → a rendered ILS range for a team the size of the `business` plan, computed from `lib/plans.ts` so it tracks re-pricing |
| מערכות נוכחות ותיקות בישראל | custom quote + one-off setup fees |
| **ShiftPilot** *(highlighted)* | the anchor plan's flat monthly price — no per-head billing, no mandatory setup fee |

Category ranges, not live quotes, with a dated "for illustration only" footnote.

## Why not a named comparison table

Discussed with the user. Naming competitors publicly is an accuracy + maintenance liability (their prices move), gives them free attention on our own pricing page, and positions us as the budget option. The structural point — *fixed price, not per-user* — is 100% true, doesn't go stale, and is the real differentiator. The named, sourced comparison stays internal in `docs/PRICING_BENCHMARK.md` for sales use.

## Checks

- `typecheck` — no new errors (the 6 `@capacitor/local-notifications` errors are pre-existing on `main`).
- No data-model or migration changes — pure marketing-page addition.
- Visual check of the 3-up band (and its 1-col mobile stack) is for CI + a reviewer eyeball on the Vercel preview.
