author: enunezvn
body:
Completes **#1958 step 2**. Step 1 landed in #1959.

## Precondition re-verified before renaming

The issue is explicit that the order matters: namespacing `agentKeys.status()` while other components still hardcoded `'agent-status'` would split **one** shared cache entry into **two**, making those components refetch independently and drift out of sync — a behaviour change disguised as a consistency fix. So the rename is only safe once nothing else names the key.

Checked on this tree, not assumed:

```
$ grep -rn "'agent-status'\|\"agent-status\"\|\`agent-status\`" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" .
frontend/src/hooks/api/use-agents.ts:35: * `status()` still returns the bare `['agent-status']` value it replaced, and
frontend/src/hooks/api/use-agents.ts:51:  status: () => ['agent-status'] as const,
```

Only the comment and the definition itself. The wider substring grep also hits `data-testid="agent-status-panel"` in four `AgentOrchestration` test files — that is a DOM test id for the panel component, not the query key, so no test pins the old key string.

Stronger than "the literal is gone", all five consumers were confirmed to reach the key *only* through the hook — none builds its own:

| consumer | line |
| --- | --- |
| `pages/Home.tsx` | `useAgentStatus()` @ 522 |
| `components/dashboard/ExecutiveSummary.tsx` | `useAgentStatus()` @ 86 |
| `components/chat/E2IChatSidebar.tsx` | `useAgentStatus({ enabled: copilotEnabled })` @ 416 |
| `components/chat/E2IChatPopup.tsx` | `useAgentStatus({ enabled: copilotEnabled })` @ 63 |
| `pages/AgentOrchestration.tsx` | `useAgentStatus()` @ 267 |

One risk the issue does not mention, checked because namespacing can *create* a match that did not exist: a key under `['agents', …]` becomes reachable by a **prefix** invalidation. There is no `['agents', …]` matcher anywhere in `frontend/src`, and no `invalidateQueries` / `removeQueries` / `cancelQueries` / `resetQueries` call touching the agent queries at all. `agentKeys` is also read only inside its own module. So the rename is self-contained.

## The change

`status: () => ['agent-status']` → `status: () => ['agents', 'status']`.

## Stale comments

The note at `:35` and the block at `:39-42` existed to explain **why the key was bare**. Once it isn't, they describe a state that no longer exists — the defect class this repo has been closing all night. Rewritten to carry the invariant that is still worth stating (one definition, one cache entry, do not reintroduce an inline literal), with the step-1-before-step-2 ordering kept as history rather than as pending work.

The module header was also left implying `AgentOrchestration` is the only consumer, which stopped being true at step 1; it now names the other four.

## Tests

New `frontend/src/hooks/api/use-agents.cache-key.test.ts`. Two assertions pin the namespacing and were **red before the change**:

```
AssertionError: expected [ 'agent-status' ] to deeply equal [ 'agents', 'status' ]
AssertionError: expected [ [ 'agent-status' ] ] to deeply equal [ [ 'agents', 'status' ] ]
 Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

The other two are deliberate guards rather than change-detectors — they pass on both sides and fail only if a second inline key for `/agents/status` is ever reintroduced: independent consumers under one `QueryClient` must produce exactly **one** cache entry and **one** fetch. That is the property the issue is actually protecting.

After:

```
✓ src/hooks/api/use-agents.cache-key.test.ts (4 tests)
✓ src/hooks/api/cache-keys.test.ts (16 tests)
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

All five consumer suites, including the shared-roster assertion `renders REAL agent tier counts (never the hardcoded 15/21)`:

```
 Test Files  8 passed (8)
      Tests  117 passed (117)
```

`npm run typecheck` (`tsc -b --noEmit`) rc=0; `eslint` on both changed files rc=0. No prettier gate exists in `frontend/package.json`, and `prettier --write` was not run.

## Notes

- `use-agents` is still **not** exported from `hooks/api/index.ts`, per the issue — consumers import from the module path.
- `frontend/**` is a deploy-trigger path, so this merges into a production deploy. Not merging; leaving that to the serialized queue.
- Nothing in the issue body was contradicted.

Closes #1958.

author: stipsitzm
body:
## What

The `theme-tokens/no-hardcoded-style-values` rule was added as warnings-only so the legacy backlog would stay visible. This works through the part of that backlog where the fix is provable rather than a judgement call.

Nine warnings, all of them the theme's **own palette values written out by hand**:

| Literal | Is exactly | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.08)` ×2 | `alpha(primary.main, 0.08)` | crop chevron button hover (`cropHierarchyRowSx.ts`) |
| `rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.12 / 0.32 / 0.16)` | `alpha(primary.main, …)` | selected crop hierarchy row (`CropHierarchyRow.tsx`) |
| `rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.28)` | `alpha(primary.main, 0.28)` | crop title selector focus outline |
| `rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.86)` | `alpha(primary.main, 0.86)` | page-help edit icon |
| `#d32f2f` | `error.main` | shared delete icon button |
| `rgba(211, 47, 47, 0.08)` | `alpha(error.main, 0.08)` | its hover background |

`primary.main` is `#256f2a` = rgb(37, 111, 42); `error.main` is `#d32f2f` = rgb(211, 47, 47). Each becomes `alpha(theme.palette.<role>.main, x)` — the pattern already in use a few lines away in the same styles module as `getPrimaryOverlay`.

Warnings: **94 → 85**.

## Proof that nothing changes visually

For a value substitution, "the pixels are the same" is provable rather than something a screenshot has to be trusted for. Running MUI's own `alpha()` against the palette values:

```
IDENTICAL  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.08)  vs  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.08)
IDENTICAL  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.12)  vs  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.12)
IDENTICAL  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.16)  vs  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.16)
IDENTICAL  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.28)  vs  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.28)
IDENTICAL  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.32)  vs  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.32)
IDENTICAL  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.86)  vs  rgba(37, 111, 42, 0.86)
IDENTICAL  rgba(211, 47, 47, 0.08)  vs  rgba(211, 47, 47, 0.08)
```

Every substitution emits byte-identical CSS. The change is what the value is *named*, not what it is.

## Deliberately left alone

This is the part worth reviewing, because the tempting fixes here are the wrong ones:

- **`rgba(46, 125, 50, x)` in `authPageStyles.ts`** (7 warnings). That is `#2E7D32` — **MUI's default green, not this project's primary `#256f2a`.** Replacing it with `primary.main` would visibly change the auth pages' focus rings and borders from one green to another. That is a design decision, not a refactor, so it needs your call rather than a silent swap.
- **The hierarchy highlight keyframes** (`fieldsBedsHierarchyStyles.ts`). Keyframe values cannot take a theme callback, so the literal would only move into a module-level constant — the same hardcoded colour with an extra hop. I started this one and backed it out.
- **`#fff` (14 warnings), bespoke shadows, one-off greys.** No exact theme equivalent, or the "right" token is a semantic judgement (`common.white` vs `primary.contrastText` mean different things even where they render the same today).

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/__tests__` — 231 files, 2388 tests passed.
- `npx tsc -b` — clean.
- `npx eslint src` — `theme-tokens/no-hardcoded-style-values` 94 → 85; every other rule's count unchanged (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` 50, `no-case-declarations` 39, `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` 17, `purity` 4, `refs` 3). No errors.

## Breakpoints checked

No layout, spacing, JSX or component changed — only colour values, and those are byte-identical as shown above. Nothing can differ at any breakpoint, on any of the affected surfaces (crop hierarchy rows and their chevrons, the crop title selector, the page-help panel, the shared delete button). Desktop, tablet and mobile are unaffected.

The `no-case-declarations` backlog (39 warnings) is untouched on purpose: every one of them is inside `src/gantt-chart/`, the vendored implementation the project deliberately keeps outside these sweeps.

author: plombeer31
body:
> **Stacked on #333 → #332 → … → #327.**

## What was on screen

```
Telegram  · channel failed to start
Discord   · gateway failed — see the Discord tab
```

Three faults in two lines:

1. **"see the Discord tab" points at a tab that does not exist** — removed in #332 when Discord moved into the hub. I fixed this same string in the `configured` branch and missed the `down` branch.
2. **Both lines throw away the reason.** Each channel knows exactly why it failed and exposes it via `lastError()`; the hub simply wasn't reading it. *"channel failed to start"* tells the operator nothing the red badge didn't already say.
3. **The most common cause read like a crash.** A second atomic-agent holding the lock surfaced as `telegram lockfile held by live pid 123` rather than "you already have one running".

## Fix

`IntegrationStatusContext` gains `channelErrors`, populated from `lastError()`, and both descriptors render it:

```
Telegram  · another atomic-agent (pid 42) is already running the Telegram channel — stop it first
```

Lock messages now name the cause **and** the fix.

## Also: inbound Discord logging

An `info` log on every inbound message, emitted **before** any drop decision. When a bot "doesn't answer", the first question is whether the message reached the gateway at all or was deliberately ignored (not addressed, not the owner) — previously indistinguishable from outside.

That log earned its place immediately: it's what proved the Discord gateway was healthy and the real fault was a **stale lock left by a dead process**, not the channel.

```
discord: message received {channelId:"…", authorId:"…", isDm:false, mentionsBot:false}
```

## Testing

`npm run lint` and `npm test` green (7320 tests). New cases pin that the real reason is surfaced, that a plain fallback is used when the channel has none, and — across every channel state — that **no status line ever mentions a Discord tab again**.

author: yishentu
body:
Remove Claudian's external context feature. Most provider CLIs now support working with files outside their current working directory through their native tools and permission controls, so a separate Claudian-managed directory selector and access configuration are no longer needed. Users can reference an outside file or directory by path and let the provider handle access under its own policy.

The tradeoff is losing quick selection of external files through `@mention` in chat and inline edit. Vault file/folder mentions and agent mentions remain available.

This removes the folder toolbar icon, `/add-dir` built-in command, external-file scanning and mention expansion, provider directory injection, and associated state, styles, and tests. Existing `persistentExternalContextPaths` settings and `externalContextPaths` conversation metadata are stripped during loading and migration. Provider-native configuration and session data remain unchanged. The shared system prompt already contained no external-context section.

The remaining mention code is simpler: remove unused attachment tracking, rename/delete listeners, and controller dependencies; narrow the inline-edit resolver to Vault paths; and remove the obsolete parallel mention-item model. File selection inserts text directly, while agent selection retains its callback and Vault caches remain shared with Linked content.

Validation: typecheck, lint, production build, 8,879 tests (2 skipped), and 53 repository checks passed.

author: rengokitakawachi
body:
## 調査結果

コードを読み、**トップへ戻る経路を洗い出した。アプリ内には2つしかない。**

1. 全問終了（`next()` で `idx` が `pool` 長に達したとき）
2. 「✕ 中断」ボタン（`quit()`）

他に画面遷移を起こす箇所は **Obsidian リンク（`obsidian://` スキーム）の1つだけ**。同期処理が呼ぶ `renderHome()` は表示の切り替えを行わないため、**出題中に勝手にトップへ戻る経路はコード上に存在しない**。

したがって原因は次のいずれか。

- **ページの再読込** — iOS Safari のタブ破棄、アプリ内ブラウザからの復帰、Obsidian リンクからの戻り
- **中断ボタンの誤タップ** — カード上部にあり親指が触れやすい位置

**どちらかは、この時点では確定できていない。**

## 本質的な問題

原因がどちらであれ、**出題中の状態（`pool`・`idx`）がメモリ上にしかなく、失われると必ずトップに戻る**。これが症状の実体で、ここを直せば原因によらず解決する。

## 対処

- 出題中の状態を `localStorage` に保存（問題IDの並びと現在位置）
- ホームに **「▶ 続きから（n問目から・全m問）」** を出す
- 全問終了時は消去。12時間で失効
- **中断してもセッションを残す** — 誤タップでも続きに戻れる
- 問題が削除・変更されても壊れないよう、存在するIDだけで復帰する

## 原因の切り分け

読み込みのたびに **navigation type** と「出題の途中だったか」を記録し、直近10件をフッターの **「読み込み履歴」** から見られるようにした。

```
09-08 13:42:11  reload  ← 出題の途中で読み込まれた
09-08 13:05:03  navigate
```

- `nav=reload` → **ページが再読込された**
- `nav=navigate` → 通常の読み込み（＝中断ボタンや初回起動）

**次に事象が起きたら、この履歴を見せてください。** どちらが原因か確定できます。確定したら、再読込なら原因側（Obsidian リンクの扱い等）を、誤タップなら中断ボタンの位置や確認ダイアログを手当てします。

## changed files

- `shaichi-ch1-2.html`

版: `868c41c1` → **`72aa0054`**

## test command と結果

疑似 `localStorage` で挙動を実測した。

| 検証 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 20問中7問目で保存 → 復帰 | idx=7・20問で復帰 ✓ |
| 全問終了後 | セッション消去 ✓ |
| 13時間前のセッション | 失効 ✓ |
| 存在しないIDが混ざる場合 | 生存分だけで復帰 ✓ |

```
$ node --check（抽出した全 script ブロック）
JS OK

$ npm test
PASS build-check: index.html 再現一致 (bytes=1920373, questions=1803)
PASS version-stamp: shaichi-ch1-2.html 版 72aa0054
```

total 2 / pass 2 / fail 0。総合版 `index.html` は無変更。

## known limitation

- **原因そのものは直していない。** 症状（途中の状態が失われる）を消し、原因を特定する材料を用意しただけ。再読込が起きること自体は止まらない。
- **回答途中の1問分は復元されない。** 復帰するのは「何問目か」まで。その問題は最初から解き直しになる。定着度は回答時に記録済みなので、記録は失われない。
- 12時間で失効するため、前日の途中セッションは残らない。
- 読み込み履歴は端末ごと。同期しない。

## runtime impact

`localStorage` への書き込みが1問ごとに1件増える。出題・採点・遷移・同期に変更なし。

## rollback 手段

`git revert`（1コミット）。戻すと途中の状態が失われる挙動に戻る。

author: paologaleotti
body:
## Issue
- [PIN-10828](https://pagopa.atlassian.net/browse/PIN-10828)

Related: [PIN-9908](https://pagopa.atlassian.net/browse/PIN-9908), [PIN-8886](https://pagopa.atlassian.net/browse/PIN-8886), [PIN-10781](https://pagopa.atlassian.net/browse/PIN-10781)

## Stack
This PR is stacked on #3707. It needs the `shouldRetry` predicate that #3707 adds to the shared `retry` utility in `commons`, and it reuses the retry constants that #3707 adds to the BFF. Merge #3707 first.

## Context / Why
In QA, `POST /backend-for-frontend/clients/{clientId}/purposes` returned HTTP 500. The log of `authorization-process` showed:

```
duplicate key value violates unique constraint "events_stream_id_version_key"
```

This is not a broken event. It is the optimistic lock of the event store. `addClientPurpose` reads the client version from the read model and writes the next event at `version + 1`. Two situations produce the same version twice:

1. **Parallel requests.** The BFF endpoint accepts one `purposeId` per call. When the frontend adds several purposes at the same time, every call reads the same client version. Only one insert can win.
2. **Stale read model.** When the user creates a client and adds a purpose right after, the read model can still lag behind the event store. The process then computes a version that already exists.

PR #3432 (PIN-9908, PIN-8886) already changed the event repository to throw `eventConflictError` on this duplicate key. The error maps to HTTP 409 with code `006-10034` for `authorization-process`, and the BFF forwards it as is. That change is on `develop` but not in release 2.22.x, so QA still saw the 500.

After that release, the user gets a 409 with "Please retry" instead of a 500. The frontend then shows an error and the user has to repeat the action. #3707 (PIN-10781) already decided that a transient conflict must be retried by the BFF for document upload. This PR applies the same rule to the client-purpose association.

## Scope
- Retry the `addClientPurpose` call to the Authorization Process when it returns the event stream conflict.
- Keep every other error unchanged.
- No change to `authorization-process`, to the API spec, or to the code of #3707.

## Key Changes
- `src/config/constants.ts`: add `AUTHORIZATION_EVENT_CONFLICT_CODE`, built from `serviceErrorCode[AUTHORIZATION_PROCESS]` and `commonErrorCodes.eventConflictError` (`006-10034`).
- `src/utilities/eventConflict.ts`:
  - `isEventConflict(error, code)` returns `true` only for an Axios error with status 409 whose `errors` array contains the given code. Business conflicts such as `purposeAlreadyLinkedToClient` (`006-0013`) keep a 409 but a different code, so they are not retried. The check guards the response body, so a 409 without a JSON body is forwarded as is and does not become a 500.
  - `retryOnEventConflict(code, fn)` bundles the retry policy: `EVENT_CONFLICT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5) and `EVENT_CONFLICT_RETRY_DELAY_MS` (1000) from #3707, plus the predicate above. A future call site is one line.
- `src/services/clientService.ts`: wrap the `addClientPurpose` call in `retryOnEventConflict`. Every attempt re-runs the full process handler, so the process reads a fresh client version from the read model. The original Axios error is rethrown after the last attempt, so the router still forwards the downstream Problem.

## Why the retry is in the BFF and not in the process
- The BFF retry repeats the whole downstream call. The process re-reads the client on every attempt, so a stale read model heals during the delay.
- No process service retries its own event writes today. A retry inside `authorization-process` would be a new pattern for all services.
- The M2M gateways poll the read model after every client write, so sequential M2M writes do not hit the stale version. A concurrent M2M writer gets a documented 409 and can retry on its side.

## Behavior notes
- When the concurrent writer added the same purpose (double click), the retry returns the real final state: 409 `purposeAlreadyLinkedToClient`. This is more precise than the generic conflict.
- The fixed 1 second delay comes from the shared `retry` utility of #3707. Backoff or jitter is a change to that utility and is out of scope here.

## Follow-up
- The same conflict can happen on every write of the client stream: `removeClientPurpose`, `addClientUsers`, `removeClientUser`, `createKey`, `deleteClientKeyById`, `setAdminToClient`, `removeClientAdmin`, `deleteClient`, and on the producer keychain writes. This PR covers only the case in the ticket. Each of them becomes a one-line `retryOnEventConflict` call.
- After #3707 merges, replace the inline `isCatalogEventConflict` in `catalogService.ts` with `isEventConflict(error, CATALOG_EVENT_CONFLICT_CODE)`, so that one predicate exists.

## Testing / Validation
- [x] Lint
- [x] Typecheck
- [x] Unit tests: `test/addClientPurpose.test.ts`, with fake timers
  - a 409 with code `006-10034` on the first call and a 204 on the second call completes the association with 2 calls, and the second call carries the same headers
  - a persistent conflict stops after 5 attempts and rethrows the last Axios error
  - a 409 with code `006-0013` (purpose already linked) is not retried
  - a 409 without a JSON body is not retried and is rethrown as is
  - a non-HTTP error is not retried

## Traceability Checklist
- [x] Branch contains Jira key
- [x] PR title respects standard: type: description (KEY)
- [ ] Fix Version set in Jira (if required)
- [x] Service labels applied
- [ ] API and integration tests updated
- [ ] OpenAPI spec updated
- [ ] Bruno endpoint definition updated

author: eamon-b
body:
Found while verifying the world contour pipeline on the rented build box for #34, before committing to the full run.

## The bug

`gdalwarp` reads each 2° cell with a **0.01° buffer** so contours are continuous across the cell edge before `ogr2ogr -clipsrc` trims them back. The DEM fetcher didn't know that: `neededTiles()` called `dem1DegTiles(cell)`, which loops `lon < cell.east` / `lat < cell.north` and so returns the cell's *own* 1° tiles only — never the ring around them.

The build therefore warps a window it has no DEM for. GDAL fills the missing strip with nodata and `gdal_contour` stops short of the cell edge, so every 2° boundary gets a hairline break.

Interior cells hid this completely: their buffer ring is their neighbours' own tiles, already on disk from the same fetch. It only bites at the outside edge of whatever region you fetched — which is exactly what a sharded world build is made of.

## Measured

At lon 134.0 (a cell boundary), z15, an 81-tile band, counting west-cell contours whose easternmost vertex reaches the boundary:

| build | reach edge | stop ~12 m short |
|---|---:|---:|
| production Australia archive | 201 / 795 | 0 |
| world, fetcher unfixed | **0 / 554** | **225**, all on one meridian at 133.99989 |
| world, fetcher fixed | 193 / 517 | 0 |

## The fix

`CELL_BUFFER_DEG` and `bufferedDem1DegTiles()` move into `scripts/lib/world-grid.ts`, next to the grid, because **both** the fetcher and the build have to agree on the number. `build-contours-world.ts` drops its private copies and re-exports the shared one; `fetch-dem-copernicus.ts` now plans against it. A regression test asserts the fetcher's tile set is exactly the set the build reads, so the two can't drift apart again.

Cost: +580 lattice tiles across the ten-shard union, **+1.1%** — free globally, though +52% for an isolated shard like `iceland`.

## Also in here

Three things that cost time on the box and would cost it again:

- **`--cell X --fetch-dem` died with "DEM directory not found".** Step 0 of the shard path sits outside the single-cell branch, so child mode skipped the fetch and then failed in `buildDemMosaic`. Fetch moved into the branch.
- **`scripts/remote/bootstrap.sh` aborted at the Node install when run as root.** `$SUDO -E bash ...` with an empty `$SUDO` expands to `-E bash ...` → `-E: command not found`, and `set -e` kills the whole bootstrap. Which is what `ssh root@<box>` does every time. Now `${SUDO:+$SUDO -E}`.
- **Runbook section for Ubuntu 20.04 hosts.** vast.ai and other GPU-container images are focal (EOL), where `apt-get install gdal-bin` silently gives you GDAL 3.0.4 and the ubuntugis PPA *appears* to add itself but never actually offers a newer build — `apt-cache madison gdal-bin` is the giveaway. Documents the conda-forge/micromamba route, the `/etc/profile.d` caveat for detached builds, and "check the disk before anything else" (container disk is a hard quota).

## Verification

Beyond the unit tests, the `oceania` shard was built end-to-end with the fix (447 cells, 32.8 GB, 9.35M tiles, z9–z15, integrity ok) and gated against the production Australia archive:

- Mt Sonder z15/28450/18593 — 43 distinct elevations, 840–1260 m, step 10, `is_index` still a string. Matches. 44 features vs prod's 43: the 900 m contour splits in two, an ordinary SRTM-vs-GLO-30 difference.
- Seam at lon 134.0 — 194 features reach the edge exactly (archive reference 201). The 18 that stop short scatter across 16 distinct meridians from 1.9 m to 47.8 m, i.e. real contour turn-backs, not the single-meridian nodata signature.

author: matze4u
body:
`road-to-a-graph-that-is-shipped` reaches **25/25**. Every step and every acceptance criterion is closed against a fresh `verify:` run whose output is quoted in the roadmap. The roadmap is **not archived** — one pre-existing blocker is open and this run may not resolve it; see § Terminal state.

Base: `origin/main` @ `3969c8b96` (merged in, 14.22.0).

## What the roadmap was for

A consumer who `npm install`s this package gets a working code graph on the next command; the graph answers `impact` / `tests-for` / `dead` from an indexed store; the answers reach the agent over MCP; and the repository's own regression selector reads this graph instead of its documented substitute. Phases 0–2 were already closed. This run closed **1.3, 2.3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3** and discharged **AC-4, AC-5, AC-6**.

## Per-step evidence

### 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3 — the three verbs a gate can read

The three share one `verify:` block: *golden outputs on a fixture; each prints `resolved_via` counts and the staleness state; `describeImpact` is listed by `dead` and by nothing else.*

- Four verbs in `src/scripts/code_graph/verbs.ts`, dispatched as `code-graph` subcommands from `src/scripts/code_graph/cli.ts` (no new top-level verb, per K4). `src/cli/registry.ts:86` synopsis updated.
- `tests/scripts/code_graph_gate_verbs.test.ts` → **23 passed**. Every list assertion is `toStrictEqual` over the full sorted array, never `toContain`, so an extra element fails. The fixture is a real PHP+TS tree built through `buildFromRepo` — never a graph literal, which would let the verbs pass over a shape the extractor cannot produce.
- Two histograms per verb, not one: `accepted resolved_via` and `rejected resolved_via`, so a caller can tell "no callers" from "no callers I would trust".
- `describeImpact` — declared, called by nothing, imported by nothing — is absent from `impact`'s dependents, absent from `tests-for`, present in `dead`. One assertion catches both over- and under-reporting. It **is** listed by `untested`, which is correct rather than a leak and is recorded as such: `untested` is 3.2's second verb, not one of the three the verify names.
- End-to-end through the CLI on a git fixture: `impact --diff HEAD~1` → exit 0, 4 dependents, 1 test file, 6 producing edges; `tests-for handle` → exit 0, `tests (1)`; `untested --diff HEAD~1` → exit 0, `tested (1) · untested (2)`; `dead` → **exit 1** with a refusal and no list, `dead --accept-missing-exports` → exit 0 with 6 symbols, `dead --entry-points <file>` → exit 0 with 5 and 1 excluded.

**Two sensitivity pairs, each proven by neutralising the mechanism and watching the suite go red.** A test never seen red has unknown sensitivity:

| mechanism neutralised | result |
|---|---|
| `isAcceptedEdge` forced to `true` | 2 failed / 15 passed |
| `member` added to `REFERENCE_RELATIONS` | 5 failed / 12 passed |

The accepted-edge case is a real `INFERRED / name-lookup` edge — a bare PHP `helper()` with no `use` — which the filter must drop and which shows up as `rejected_via: name-lookup 1`.

**The containment filter is a finding, not a design flourish.** The build pass emits `file --member--> symbol` for every declaration, so on the first fixture every one of the ten nodes had an accepted in-edge and `dead` returned the empty set — a verb that can never report anything, which is worse than a wrong one because it looks calm. A declaration is not a use.

### 3.2's prerequisite — the `tests` relation, derived rather than extracted

`buildGraph` emits `test file --tests--> subject` for every `imports` edge whose source is a test file and whose target is an in-repo node in a non-test file. `resolved_via: test-import` — a value 2.2 declared and left unemitted for exactly this — and `confidence: INFERRED`. The two axes are split deliberately: the import is a syntactic fact, so the evidence is extracted, while "this test tests that subject" is an inference from a path convention.

Derived in the build pass, not the extractor, because the predicate is a property of two **paths**, which no grammar can see, and `buildGraph` stays pure over its extract set. Three exclusions, each of which would otherwise manufacture a false edge: an `external:` / `symbol:` target, a target in another test file, and — via the sensitivity twin — the same import from a non-test path, which derives nothing.

`SCHEMA_VERSION` 3 → 4 and `GRAPH_STORE_VERSION` 3 → 4. The store bump is the one worth explaining: **no column changed**, which is precisely why it is needed. A v3 twin would read back cleanly, answer `tests-for` with the empty set, and the caller could not tell "nothing tests this" from "this twin predates the relation".

### 3.3 — `dead` refuses by default

`grep -n 'isExported\|exported\|export_statement' src/scripts/code_graph/extract.ts` returns **zero**. `FileExtract` (`extract.ts:82-90`) carries `nodes / rawEdges / inherits / parseError`; `CodeNode` carries no export flag. So one of the four entry-point sources step 3.3 names cannot be evaluated from this graph at all, and without it every exported-but-not-yet-imported public symbol reports as dead — Risk-Register rank 4 arriving through the verb rather than around it.

`dead` therefore prints each source with a status (`read` / `empty` / `unavailable` + reason) and then **refuses**: exit 1, empty list, unless the caller supplies the missing source (`--entry-points <file>`) or states the gap (`--accept-missing-exports`). Fail-closed in the shape `selectionVerdict` (`src/scripts/_lib/regression_neighbourhood.ts`) already uses here — no option object relaxes it, only a visible command line. `routes` reads `empty`, not `unavailable`: this repository has no route table, and an absent route table is a fact about the tree rather than a gap in the graph.

Over MCP the refusal is a **status** a caller can branch on rather than an exit code nobody sees; both branches are fixtured.

### 3.4 — the regression selector reads the native graph

- `grep -c 'no index to select against' src/scripts/_lib/regression_neighbourhood.ts` → **0**.
- `tests/scripts/regression_neighbourhood.test.ts` → **20 passed** (13 pre-existing on the artefact path, all still green, + 7 new).
- The fixture that proves a neighbour regression is caught now runs on the native graph: `caught: ['reg-neighbour'] · missed: []` at depth 2, and the falsifiable arm at depth 0 — the diff-scoped selector this step replaces — gives `caught: [] · missed: ['reg-neighbour']`.
- `NeighbourhoodReport` gains `producing_edges` (sorted, so two runs over one graph produce byte-identical records), `rejected_via`, and `graph: 'artefact' | 'code'`. The third is what keeps the retirement honest: a verdict record can no longer be read as a claim about the other surface.
- The mechanism axis is what distinguishes the two graphs' notion of a neighbour, and it has its own case: a bare PHP `helper()` yields `selected: [] · skipped: ['reg-php-caller'] · rejected_via: 'name-lookup 1'`. The artefact graph has no axis on which that distinction can be expressed.

**Both surfaces are kept, and that is a reading of "retires the substitute-graph section" rather than a hedge.** What was retired is the *substitution* — reading the artefact graph *because the code graph would not resolve*, which was the whole content of the deleted docstring section. The artefact path stays for artefact candidates, because for a rule or skill rewrite `supersedes` / `routes_to` / pack membership is the coupling a change breaks and the code graph does not model it. Deleting it would have removed a capability this roadmap never proposed to remove. `selectionVerdict` now names the graph it refused against, so a code-path refusal no longer points a reader at the wrong surface.

### 4.1 — five MCP tools, catalogue 36

- `npm run build:mcp-catalog` → `wrote src/scripts/mcp_server/consumer_tool_catalog.json (36 tool(s))`. All five carry `implemented_on: ['stdio']` — the field that separates a real tool from a d

author: ideotion
body:
## What & why

`docs/plans/2026-09-06-repo-analysis/00_INDEX.md`'s top-level "what is actually open" rollup
still listed, as open item 4, "Fifty-six `async def` handlers still taking `Depends(get_db)`".
That was accurate when the index was written (2026-09-06), but `INVENTORY.md`'s `PERF-01` row —
the detail row this line summarizes — was correctly updated to **BUILT 2026-09-07** in commit
`984258be` ("S3.6's other half: 56 DB handlers off the event loop, and PRH-23"). The index rollup
was never edited to match, so a reader skimming only the index (which is exactly what an index is
for) would be misled into re-investigating a closed item.

This PR removes the shipped item from the numbered "open work" list, renumbers the remaining nine
items, and adds a short parenthetical explaining the gap and pointing at the `PERF-01` row and the
shipping commit, so nothing just silently disappears from the document's history.

I re-read `INVENTORY.md`'s `PERF-01` row in full before writing the replacement text, and confirmed
commit `984258be` exists and matches the subject line cited in the underlying finding. I also
checked the rest of `00_INDEX.md` for an established "done-in-place" marker convention to match —
there wasn't one yet, and no other line in the same list showed an equally clear-cut drift against
its own detail row, so I kept the change to the one confirmed target rather than doing a broader
staleness sweep (that's flagged in the source finding as a separate, larger prompt).

One adjacent line — the prompts table's note that "09 … Holds the 56-handler slice" — was left
untouched: it describes what PROMPT_09 covers (still historically true), not the item's open/closed
status, so it isn't the kind of "still open" claim this fix targets.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor / internal
- [ ] Build / CI / tooling

## Checklist

- [ ] `make check` is green (ruff + pytest) on Python 3.13 — not run; this is a docs-only prose
      change with no code touched, so no ruff/pytest surface is implicated, but I did not execute
      the full suite in this sandbox. Relying on CI.
- [ ] Added or updated tests for the changed behaviour — N/A, no test coverage applies to a
      docs-only prose fix in a `docs/plans/` analysis artifact.
- [ ] Any number shown to a user comes from a real method with stated uncertainty — N/A, no
      user-facing surface changed.
- [ ] New outbound traffic — N/A, none added.
- [ ] Schema changes go through Alembic — N/A, no schema touched.
- [ ] New user-facing chrome strings are keyed in all 12 locales — N/A, no chrome strings added.
- [x] Docs updated where behaviour changed — this PR *is* the doc update; no other doc references
      the stale claim (checked with a repo-wide grep for the relevant strings).

## Notes for reviewers

This is a `docs/plans/` analysis artifact, not `CLAUDE.md`/`docs/ledger/`, so none of the
ledger-ratchet or `shipped.csv` mechanics apply — plain prose edit, no code changed, so mypy/ruff/
`node --check` don't apply either. Verification here was a careful cross-read of `00_INDEX.md`
against `INVENTORY.md`'s `PERF-01` row, plus confirming the cited commit exists in this branch's
history.

body:
## 改動前

AI 用量只有固定的供應商開關與單份快照，無法在設定頁管理各帳號；回報資料沒有保留 Codex 帳號身分。

## 改動後

- 設定頁可新增、改名、暫停、隱藏、排序、移除與還原用量來源，選擇指標與過期隱藏時間。
- Codex 回報綁定該次抓取使用的帳號；不同帳號分開保存，自訂名稱不被回報覆蓋。舊快取與較舊回報不刷新用量時間。
- 自訂來源使用各自的回報金鑰；僅保存雜湊，普通查詢不回傳金鑰。設定了共用管理金鑰時，管理操作必須驗證。
- 手機單欄、平板雙欄、桌機三欄；操作按鈕至少44px。Pi 右側依帳號顯示，超過可見空間時輪播，不合併百分比。
- 排序失敗不留下部分排序；相同設定不重新啟用暫停來源；設定存檔失敗時還原原值。

## 驗證

- 全套：`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` → **993 passed**。
- Python 語法：23個新增／修改檔案通過；`git diff --check`通過。
- 本機 Chromium＋全新暫存資料：新增／管理金鑰重試、編輯／取消、暫停／隱藏、移除／還原、排序正常／故障／重試、長名稱與文字安全、來源金鑰隔離、HTTP帳號A/B分流及快取重送均通過。
- 390／820／1440px：無整頁橫向溢出，按鈕至少44px，乾淨載入沒有頁面程式錯誤或失敗請求。
- Pi 1920×480深／淺色渲染與六個以上來源輪播測試通過；這不是Pi實機觸控驗收。
- 既有測試未修改；這輪新增的測試也涵蓋無效更新與其他帳號不變的對照。SQL review：not applicable。

## 邊界與待驗證

- 只收集各收集器目前登入的帳號；不會自動登入或切換其他帳號。自訂系統仍需實作回報，不會抓取任意URL。
- 本輪使用合成資料；尚未部署，尚未驗證真實帳號與Pi/Mac線上同步。正式更新需先確認部署授權，且Pi程式與Mac用量收集器都要更新。
- 未改Wi-Fi、Tailscale、小喜喜、sessions、鬧鐘或行事曆功能；原有未追蹤`.claude/`未提交。
- 設定與來源兩個檔案有執行期失敗回復，不宣稱跨檔案斷電交易。
- 這個分支承接尚未合併的 #1（`fix/stable-usage-endpoint`），正常目標分支為`build/v1`。不自動合併或部署。

author: irfan-yulianto
body:
💡 What: Extracted static constants (`R`, `TO_RAD`) and removed inline closures from `haversineDistance`.
🎯 Why: `haversineDistance` runs in tight loops (e.g., sorting map results). Defining constants inside the function re-allocates memory and re-calculates `Math.PI / 180` on every single iteration.
📊 Impact: Expected to reduce CPU overhead and garbage collection in hot paths. Benchmark tests show an improvement from ~7.28M ops/sec to ~7.63M ops/sec.
🔬 Measurement: Run `pnpm vitest bench --run src/vitest_profile.bench.ts` with a mock test comparing the two versions.

author: jnnngs
body:
**#128 merged carrying only its first commit**, so this one stayed behind on the branch. It is the half that matters most, because without it `main` currently states something untrue on the home page.

## The defect

`docs/index.md` says, on `main` right now:

> The catalogue is generated from one table in the code, so these docs cannot drift from what is published.

`gen_catalogue.go` rewrites four files — the Makefile, both workflows and `docs/naming.md`. **`docs/index.md` is not one of them.** The sentence is false about the very line it sits on.

I wrote that sentence in #125, and the positioning audit's last verifier caught it. It matters beyond the wrong wording, because the same commit put the versioned five-item list into `README.md` *and* `docs/index.md` — two files nothing regenerates and no test read.

Fedora 42 and Rocky Linux 9 will be superseded. When that happens `make generate` updates the four generated files, `TestDocsListTheCatalogue` and `TestConfigurationPageNamesEveryVariant` fail for the two guarded pages, and **the two pages a reader meets first go quietly stale** — the worst place in the repository to be wrong about what is published.

## The fix

The claim is made true rather than deleted. `TestTheLandingSurfacesNameEveryVariant` holds `README.md` and `docs/index.md` to the catalogue by name, in the same shape as the configuration page's existing guard, and the sentence now says what is actually so:

> The catalogue is generated from one table in the code, **and a test holds this page to it**, so neither can drift from what is published.

A test rather than a fifth generator target because these are sentences written for a person, not a table: what must not drift is the set of names, not the words around them.

**Confirmed to fail both ways it can:**

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drop "Rocky Linux 9" from `docs/index.md` | `index.md never names "Rocky Linux 9", so the page a reader meets first no longer says what is published` |
| Move the catalogue to Rocky Linux 10, leave the pages alone | fails naming **both** files |

## Also here

A merge of `main`, which has moved on with #127 (the per-repository runner label work) as well as #128. Resolved cleanly with no conflicts; the guard passes against the merged tree.

## Checks

`go test ./...`, `make lint`, `mkdocs build --strict` all clean on the merged branch.

author: microbit-matt-hillsdon
body:
Replace the hand-run Crowdin zip export with the shared tool, configured
in i18n.config.mjs and installed in simx/, the repo's Node project. The
config lists the languages and three things Crowdin holds for us on the
`new` branch under makecode-extensions/pxt-microbit-ml: the simulator's
react-intl catalog, the extension's block and JSDoc strings, and the docs
directory. `npm run i18n:download` in simx replaces update-translations.sh.

The simulator's compiled catalogs in simx/src/messages/ become generated
output: gitignored and compiled on install and before dev and build. Its
lang files take Crowdin's canonical casing (ui.pt-BR.json) and hold only
what is translated, with English backfilled at compile time; the language
query parameter is matched case-insensitively, as MakeCode sends it in
mixed case. This replaces simx/bin/tidy-lang.cjs and @formatjs/cli.

Two workflows: translations-download runs weekly through
translations-sync-action, which pushes with the microbit-i18n App token so
the pull request gets CI, requests review from the web team, and opens the
pull request on a partial download with the summary in its body.
translations-upload is run by hand and replaces all the English in
Crowdin: ui.en.json, the two _locales strings files, and the help pages.
pxt's own Crowdin upload never covers a GitHub extension (it handles
bundled packages only), so `pxt gendocs --locs` then this workflow is the
documented route for new block text.

Each help page's package block pins this extension by tag, and Crowdin
treats that line as a string, so a release would change the source of
every page and unsettle its translation. The docs entry's upload hook
sends `#{version_placeholder_do_not_translate}` in the tag's place and its
download hook restores the tag from the English page, which is what the
old script did with perl. The first upload must not keep translations, so
the stale tags in each language's copy are cleared rather than carried on
indefinitely; the placeholder is then entered as their translation in
Crowdin.

build-simx moves to Node 24, which the tool requires, and the translation
workflows install npm 11 as the build workflows do, which simx/package.json
now requires. simx/.npmrc exempts our own scopes from the seven-day
release age, as the ui repo does, so a fresh i18n-tools release installs.

author: the-running-dev
body:
## Summary

Closes #310. `S3.3` ("replay_gap is emitted exactly once when the spill genuinely cannot serve the range...") deleted `events.ndjson` immediately after observing `turn.ended` in the live subscription, without waiting for that envelope's durable append to land — the append is chained onto the session's write queue and only starts *after* live delivery (`emit`, `src/session-manager/index.ts`, synchronous fan-out ahead of the queued spill write; D18/I27).

On Windows this races the in-flight `open('a', ...)` for that append against the test's own delete of the same path — the shape of the `EPERM: operation not permitted, open '...\events.ndjson'` observed on PR #308's `windows-latest` job. `S3.4`, three tests below, already hits the identical race and already guards it by polling `store.readLastSeq` until the spill has caught up to what the live `control` array holds, before touching the file. This applies the same guard to `S3.3`.

## Reproduce / diagnosis

- Not reproduced locally under normal conditions — matches the issue's own note (two full Windows `npm test` runs at the failing commit, both 499/499 passing). This is consistent with #167 and #99, the same *class* of Windows-CI-timing flake in this suite, both previously investigated with no local repro across multiple environments.
- Verified the mechanism by code reading rather than forcing the failure: `emit()` (`src/session-manager/index.ts`) delivers to subscribers synchronously and only *then* chains the durable append onto `entry.writeQueue`, so the durable write for the very envelope `S3.3` waits on can still be in flight, unguarded, at the moment the test deletes the file. `S3.4`'s own comment states this race in the same terms and already fixes it with the exact guard applied here.
- Attempted to force a local repro by injecting an artificial delay into the wrapped store's `appendEvent` and by holding a real file handle open across a `rm()`/reopen in a standalone script; neither reproduced Windows's pending-delete `EPERM` on this machine's Node/NTFS combination, which is consistent with this being a CI-runner-specific condition (timing and/or AV-scan-related) rather than one this Windows install exhibits under simple synthetic pressure.

## Verified

Ran and passed:
- Run tests — `npm test` (build + `node --test dist/**/*.test.js client/**/*.test.js`): tests 499, suites 66, pass 494, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 5, todo 0, duration_ms 214662.6186
- Parse-check PowerShell scripts — parsed every `*.ps1` with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` recursively from repo root: 0 parse failures
- Run Pester tests — `Invoke-Pester -Path tools -Output Detailed -PassThru`: Tests completed in 101.54s. Tests Passed: 403, Failed: 0, Skipped: 35, NotRun: 0
- Check design/10-design.md references resolve — `./tools/Test-DesignReferences.ps1`: Design references OK - 2 citation(s) checked, all resolve to a real heading. State: Valid, Findings: [], CitationCount: 2. Exit code: 0

Ran and failed:
- none

Did not run:
- none — all four discovered gates (`.github/workflows/verify.yml`) ran

## Out of scope

#167 and #99 are a different test/file each; this fix does not touch either and no claim is made that it affects them.

author: wisdomcg-ai
body:
Third of the budget-store PRs (spec: `.planning/BUDGET-STORE-PLAN.md`). Builds on the tables from #486 and the resolver seam from #487.

## The one line that matters

`getXeroBudget` is called for the **whole fiscal year**, elapsed months included. The forecast seed deliberately drops closed months — correct for a forecast, which projects what's left — but *every monthly report is about a closed month*, so a budget sourced that way can never fill the column it exists for.

Distinct Directions is the live case: its seeded forecast holds Sep–Jun, and its August budget column reads $0 against a $471,250 actual.

## Shared classification, not a second opinion

The Xero-facing half is reused unchanged — `getXeroBudget`, the catalog/actuals loaders, the tenant-ownership guard. The part that had to move is the classifier: `resolveBudgetLineIdentities` is now exported from the seed service and used by both, so the import and the seed cannot decide the same account differently. **The seed's 22 characterisation tests pass untouched.**

What gets stored:

- `category` — the report's Title-Case vocabulary (`Revenue` / `Cost of Sales` / `Operating Expenses` / …)
- `account_type` — the 5-bucket `PLBucket`

An account that can't be classified stores **NULL, not a guess**. Guessing would file a revenue account under Operating Expenses and invert its variance, invisibly, because the consumer's fallback is a `push` rather than a throw. The consumer already defaults NULL to Operating Expenses, so NULL is the honest value.

## Never overwrites

A revision is a new `version_number`. `effective_from` defaults to the first month with **no finalised report**, so a month already issued keeps the budget it was issued against — a revision applies prospectively rather than restating a period.

Insert order is version (unlocked) → lines → lock, because supabase-js can't span two inserts in one transaction. The resolver reads only locked rows, so a half-written import is invisible rather than a zero-line budget that blanks a client's whole budget column. If the lines fail, the version is deliberately left unlocked and the route says so rather than reporting a success with nothing behind it.

## Tests

`import-xero-budget.test.ts` — 15 cases, pinned to **DD's own workbook and Calxa pack**, not to our own output: August 2026 must come back as Bathurst income $222,876.58, Bathurst wages $116,410.32, Bathurst COGS $200. Plus: elapsed months present (the whole point), classification into all three buckets, expenses carried through positive, an unclassifiable account left NULL rather than guessed, the stored-type fallback that rescues a super-admin import whose catalog reads empty, an omitted month staying absent rather than filled from actuals, partial coverage reported rather than completed, months outside the FY ignored, a zero-budgeted account named, and an archived-but-budgeted account surfaced.

`defaultEffectiveFrom` — 4 cases including the gap case (July finalised, August not → August).

Full suite: 302 files pass, only the known local timezone failure in `plan-period-banner.test.tsx`. tsc and eslint clean.

## Not yet wired

Nothing reads a budget version until one is pinned — the resolver skips the version tier without a pin, so importing is not itself a switch-over. The settings `budget_version_id` column, the picker, and the `templates` ownership check are the next PR.

author: blackfoxmedia2026
body:
P2-6. Ogni piatto portava **quattro** pulsanti a icona — su, giù, modifica, elimina. Quattro bersagli per riga su un elenco di centoventi piatti sono un muro di frecce, e il nome del piatto — che è la cosa importante — diventa il testo fra le icone.

Da telefono ora c'è un solo «⋯» con le azioni **scritte a parole**:

```
Modifica
Segna come finito
Sposta in su
Sposta in giù
─────────────────
Elimina il piatto
```

Dentro un menù non c'è l'ambiguità di un simbolo, e «Elimina il piatto» dice più di un cestino. Sta in fondo, dopo una riga di separazione, perché è l'unica azione che non si disfa.

## «Segna come finito»

È il gesto più frequente durante un servizio — lo si fa in cucina alle nove di sera, con una mano — e prima si raggiungeva **solo aprendo la scheda del piatto**. Ora è una voce del menù, e la carta pubblica si aggiorna subito (verificato dal vivo).

## Da tablet in su la fila resta

Col mouse quattro bersagli in fila si raggiungono più in fretta di un menù da aprire. **Non è la stessa interfaccia rimpicciolita**, ed è il punto di tutto il lavoro sul telefono.

Le frecce restano nascoste mentre un filtro è acceso, come già faceva la fila: riordinare un elenco parziale manderebbe al server un ordine che non è quello vero.

---

**762 test verdi · 7 percorsi e2e verdi · `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, `next build` puliti.**

Provato dal vivo su telefono: quindici piatti, quindici pulsanti «⋯», il menù si apre con le cinque voci, e il piatto segnato finito compare barrato con la sua etichetta.

author: g-garciac2022
body:
## La tarjeta del análisis rotulaba el modelo declarado, no el que se ejecutó

Sin issue: es la corrección de un fallo introducido por #160 (#119/#87) y
detectado al ejecutar lo que aquélla entregó. Va suelta porque abrir una issue
para cerrarla en el mismo movimiento no añade trazabilidad — el rastro está en
#119, cuya sección del README recoge esto.

### Qué pasaba

#119 hizo configurable el modelo de cada señal y se ocupó de que la ficha
publicada fuera la del modelo **efectivo**, en las dos fachadas: el catálogo REST
y `describe_models`. Había una tercera puerta.

Levantando el sistema con otro modelo configurado —`elozano/bert-base-cased-clickbait-news`,
el que #115 midió y descartó—:

```
GET /tools                      → elozano/bert-base-cased-clickbait-news   ✔
POST /tools/describe_models     → elozano/bert-base-cased-clickbait-news   ✔
POST /analyze  →  signal.label  → «RoBERTa dedicado (entrenado en Webis-17)» ✘
```

El orquestador guardaba `_CARDS`, un índice de las fichas **declaradas** resuelto
al importar, y rotulaba con él cada `SignalResult`.

Es la misma divergencia que cerró #116 por tercera vez, y **la peor de las
tres**: el catálogo lo mira quien va a inspeccionar el sistema; la tarjeta la
mira quien lee el resultado.

### Qué cambia

- **`orchestrator.py`** — `_build` construye el `SignalResult` desde
  `ficha_efectiva`, y **desaparece `_CARDS`**. Dejar ahí un índice declarado es
  dejar puesta la trampa para el siguiente que lo lea.
- **`tests/api/test_analyze.py`** — un test que configura otro modelo y exige
  que el `label` lo refleje. Ninguno lo comprobaba, y por eso la suite estaba en
  verde con el fallo dentro.

### Por qué no lo cazó nada

Los tests de #119 comprobaban el `model_id` de la ficha por las dos fachadas que
sí se habían arreglado, y el `label` de la tarjeta no lo miraba ninguno. No había
forma de que saltara **sin ejecutar el sistema con un modelo configurado**, que
es justo lo que se hizo después de mergear.

### De regalo: el hueco del mapeo, medido

La misma ejecución dio el argumento empírico de **#159**, que hasta ahora era una
deducción:

```
titular clickbait → ok      elozano dice «Clickbait», que sí está en el mapeo
titular factual   → error   «devolvió la etiqueta "Normal", que no está en el
                             mapeo ['Clickbait', 'Not Clickbait']»
```

`elozano` usa `Normal`/`Clickbait` y el sistema espera `Clickbait`/`Not
Clickbait`: **media convención coincide**, así que el modelo sustituido funciona
con unos titulares y falla con otros — el peor reparto posible, porque una prueba
rápida con un titular clickbait lo daría por bueno. Queda registrado en el README
y en #159.

author: prisis
body:
Fixes #863.

Two adoption papercuts in the release subsystem — plus a dispatch bug found while verifying them.

## 1. A bare `vis release` ran the CI publish flow

Every release subcommand is registered as `commandPath: ["release"]`, so nothing owned the flat `release` name. `vis release ci release` has the **leaf name `release`**, and cerebro's name-keyed map handed it that slot — so `vis release`, `vis release --help` and `vis help release` all resolved to the CI version-PR/publish command.

Declaring a flat `release` umbrella command fixes it: `Cli.addCommand` re-keys the nested namesake under its full path. `vis release` now prints usage + subcommands.

> Note on the issue's first point: `group: "Release"` already existed, so `vis --help` *did* render a Release group — but as the 12th and last of twelve, which is why it read as missing. The umbrella entry gives it a one-line description and moves the group 7th.

## 2. `release doctor` blamed workspace discovery when nothing was opted in

`ctx.packages` is the *release-managed* set, so an empty list had three causes collapsed into one "check your `pnpm-workspace.yaml`" error — pointing at the one file that was not the problem.

Split into two checks:

| managed | workspace | `workspace-discovered` | `release-managed-packages` |
|---|---|---|---|
| N>0 | — | pass | pass |
| 0 | N>0 | pass | **warn** — names `defaultManaged` / `vis-release.managed` |
| 0 | 0 | **error** — original message | skip |

`warn`, not `error`, because incremental adoption is a supported state and the doctor should still exit 0 mid-migration. A third cause gets its own hint: an all-private workspace yields zero managed packages even with `defaultManaged: true`, because private packages additionally need `release.privatePackages.version`.

Two neighbouring vacuous passes fixed the same way: `plan-readable` no longer reports a clean "No pending releases." when nothing *can* release, and `catalog-consistency` reports `skip` instead of claiming all references resolve after inspecting zero packages.

## Fixes from review

- **`workspace-discovered` re-created the very conflation it set out to split** — it reported `ctx.packages.length` (the managed subset) in its pass branch, so 50 packages with 3 opted in printed "Discovered 3 workspace package(s)". It now probes the package manager unconditionally and reports `"3 of 50 package(s) are release-managed."`
- **`cerebro`: `findChildren` required equal path depth**, so `vis release` listed 16 children and silently hid all six `release ci *` commands — the whole `ci` group was undiscoverable from the only place a user would look. Changed to prefix matching. Also completes `vis advisories` and `vis ai`, the other two depth-2 groups.
- Corrected two comments that claimed registration order is what stops the nested namesake winning the flat slot. It isn't — `cli.ts:865-878` re-keys either way; order only sets help-group placement.

## Testing

vis: 2982 passing. cerebro: 679/680. The new cerebro test was verified to fail without the `findChildren` fix. Remaining failures are pre-existing on `main` (10 `cache-scope-cli` git-commit failures; one `cross-env` binary missing from a fresh worktree).

# fix(workflows): compare Bicep formatter output files

Corrected the formatting comparison that stopped
[foundation run 34207636893](https://github.com/sekharrcs/optima/actions/runs/34207636893)
before Azure authentication or what-if execution.

## Root Cause

The failed Ubuntu 24.04 runner image listed Azure CLI 2.89.1 and used Bicep 0.46.1.
The Azure CLI wrapper's `format_bicep_file` used `print(output)` for `--stdout`,
adding a newline to already LF-terminated formatter output.

Sources: [Azure CLI 2.89.1 wrapper implementation](https://github.com/Azure/azure-cli/blob/azure-cli-2.89.1/src/azure-cli/azure/cli/command_modules/resource/custom.py)
and [the failing runner's software manifest](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/ubuntu24/20260831.293/images/ubuntu/Ubuntu2404-Readme.md).

Local byte captures with those versions confirmed that committed
`infra/main.bicep`, direct Bicep stdout, and Azure CLI formatter `--outfile` were
identical: 13665 bytes, SHA-256
`ca24df04358bd3265a189f9619dc457e9e12844b4ed4411190183da6c5326f47`.
The Windows Azure CLI stdout capture additionally translated LF to CRLF and
ended in two CRLF sequences.

Hosted Linux reproduced the failure on Ubuntu 24.04.4 image 20260831.293.1,
the same image as the failed foundation run. With Azure CLI 2.89.1 and Bicep
0.46.1, stdout contained 13666 bytes: the exact formatter bytes plus one LF.
Its SHA-256 was
`b22e611ce887ace7aecdb1e3750f653856fcd7fa5b643af82fef501aa451e8f9`.
All 12 files showed the same extra-LF behavior; every original comparison
returned 1 and every formatter-written comparison passed.

## Changes

- Replaced all four stdout-based comparisons in the foundation and production
  workflows with formatter-written temporary files and strict `diff --unified`.
- Added temporary-directory cleanup on success and failure. Kept formatter and
  comparison failures fatal without trimming whitespace or ignoring blank lines.
- Added unprivileged PR validation using isolated Azure CLI 2.89.1 and Bicep
  0.46.1 installations, with no Azure login or OIDC permission.
- Added regression checks for all 9 templates and 3 parameter files, exact byte
  provenance, reproduction of the old comparison failure, execution of both
  complete Bicep validation blocks, cleanup/source preservation, and rejection of
  spacing, extra EOF blank lines, and missing final LF.
- Updated the existing PR shell-block inventory for the new validation step.

## Validation

- [x] All 12 Bicep files built and exactly matched formatter-written files locally
- [x] Frozen dependency sync and lock check; no dependency or lockfile changes
- [x] Ruff format and lint; mypy across 116 source files
- [x] Actionlint for all three workflows; scoped ShellCheck and Bash syntax
- [x] Full local pytest: 1929 passed, 13 skipped, one existing warning
- [x] Final version-pinning regressions: 122 passed, 13 skipped
- [x] Exact Linux byte reproduction and corrected workflow blocks in PR CI
- [x] Final-head Linux suite: 1933 passed, 9 opt-in skips; all 9 toolchain cases separately passed
- [x] Hosted exact-head application and final-container checks

The local skips were nine opt-in Linux toolchain cases and four existing
Windows-specific limitations. The PR toolchain step runs the nine cases explicitly.
Final-head application job
[102037513053](https://github.com/sekharrcs/optima/actions/runs/34219027659/job/102037513053)
passed at commit `c2ab59f45ac2cd93bf7b7f26479f6b2a2c1efdb4`.
Final-container job
[102039242087](https://github.com/sekharrcs/optima/actions/runs/34219027659/job/102039242087)
also passed, including image builds, runtime smoke tests, SBOMs and Trivy policy.
The complete [PR run 34219027659](https://github.com/sekharrcs/optima/actions/runs/34219027659)
succeeded on attempt 1. Application validation took 6m9s; container validation
took 4m11s.
Both complete corrected workflow blocks passed with source preservation and
cleanup. All six spacing/EOF-drift cases were rejected. An earlier Linux run
exposed an overbroad test cleanup assertion, corrected to permit only Bicep's
own `.bicep` scratch entry while rejecting leaked comparison directories.
A supplied-code reviewer identified the need to pin Azure CLI and require actual
legacy failure; both were corrected before this draft. That reviewer had no
filesystem or test execution access.

## Safety and Scope

No Bicep templates, parameter files, deployment inputs, model settings, permissions,
environment protections, promotion checks, or dependency locks were changed.
No foundation/production workflows were dispatched, and no Azure resources,
permissions, or GitHub configuration were changed. No merge was performed.
The unrelated local modification to `tests/test_production_composition.py` remained
byte-for-byte untouched in the original checkout; all work used an isolated worktree.

Authenticated foundation/production execution was not exercised. Independent
review is the next step; any later foundation dispatch requires new authorization
after eventual merge and refreshed readiness checks.

## Related Issues

None.

author: damir-vistablox
body:
## Summary
- Adds `restart: "no"` to the `migrate` service in `docker-compose.staging.yml`.
- Coolify defaults every compose service to `restart: unless-stopped` when the file doesn't specify one, and `unless-stopped` restarts a container regardless of exit code -- so `migrate` (which correctly exits 0 once it's confirmed there's nothing new to apply) kept getting relaunched by Docker forever.
- Confirmed via `docker inspect` on a live deployment: `RestartCount` for `migrate` climbed past 10 within a minute of a fresh deploy, cycling every ~1-2s.
- `migrate` is a one-shot task by design, so it now explicitly opts out of Coolify's default restart policy.

body:
This stacks on #324 and cleans up the pruning/recovery implementation before it lands. Workspace persistence and managed-worktree maintenance now return typed `better-result` values through the prune and lazy-restore paths; the CLI and workspace boundary are where failures are converted back into user-facing errors.

The cleanup also tightens the workspace lifecycle type, removes redundant timing/foreign-key tests, and compensates destructive partial failures so a failed persistence transition cannot leave an active session pointing at a deleted checkout.

author: the-running-dev
body:
**What changed, and why.** The watcher's pre-claim clean-tree check read `Clone.state === 'ready'` — a lifecycle flag saying the clone directory is materialised and unmarked, which says nothing about the working tree. A tick could therefore run its whole file-delivery protocol against a tree someone else was holding work in. `CloneStore` now exposes `isClean(declarationId)`, observing `git status`/`git stash list` directly at the moment of the call — the signature `design/20-contract.md` already declared (D16/D17) in the 2026-09-07 contract-amendment backlog decision, just not yet implemented. The watcher's gate calls it directly rather than through a dispatched `repo_status` tool call, so a dirty or unobservable clone now makes no dispatch, Git, or host call at all, and the file stays in the inbox untouched. Pending-pull-request reconciliation deliberately stays independent of this gate — that is the already-settled S24.3 design (a merged PR should still be reconciled even while its declaration's clone needs attention), reaffirmed by invariant D17. `design/90-decisions.md`'s existing entry covers the design choice; this PR is the implementation against it. Closes #78 ### Verified Ran and passed: - Run the full test suite — `npm test`, 581 tests, 581 pass, 0 fail. - Run typecheck and every check:* gate — `npm run build` (typecheck, typecheck:console, typecheck:e2e, build:registry, build:console, check:layering, check:migration, check:layer-direction, check:parity all passed). - Run S18.13's end-to-end browser suite — `npm run test:e2e`, 1 passed (32.5s). - Build S28's container image — `docker build ... -t subzerodev-git:ci .`, image exported and tagged (one pre-existing, unrelated Docker linter warning: SecretsUsedInArgOrEnv on `CREDENTIAL_MOUNT_ROOT`). - Build and boot S35's example-consumer image — image built, container reported "server: listening on :8080" within the poll window. Ran and failed: none. Did not run: none — every discovered gate ran. ---
Agent detail - **Issue:** #78 — `Require a live clean-tree check before watcher claims or reconciliation` - **Criteria met:** - W03.1 — `CloneStore.isClean` (`src/clone/clone-store.ts`) observes `git status --porcelain=v1` and `git stash list` live; fails closed on any command it cannot run. - W03.2 — the watcher checks `needs-attention` then `isClean` before claiming a file or dispatching any host/Git call for it (`src/watcher/watcher.ts`, `tickOneDeclaration`). Reconciliation is intentionally excluded from this gate, per the settled S24.3 design and invariant D17 (see decision-log note above) — not a new fork opened by this fix. - W03.3 — a dirty or unobservable clone makes zero dispatch calls; proven in `watcher.test.ts` (`dirtyLog.length === 0`, `dispatchLog.length === 0` for the `isClean`-error case). - W03.4 — `clone-store.test.ts` adds four `isClean` tests against a real materialised clone and real `git` subprocesses (staged/modified/untracked/stash-present blockers, fail-closed on a forced `git status` failure, `needs-attention` on an absent clone), not a mocked lifecycle state. - **Regression-tested:** the new tests were confirmed to fail (type errors — `isClean` does not exist) when the implementation was reverted via a temporary stash-and-restore, then restored; full suite (581 tests) and `typecheck`/`check:layer-direction` pass with the fix in place.

author: rodrigoteamx
body:
## What

`milpa/mcp-server` now declares the two events it dispatches — `mcp.request` and `mcp.responded` — to the dispatcher it receives, from the same constants its dispatch sites use.

- New `Milpa\McpServer\Events\McpServerEvents`: `REQUEST` / `RESPONDED` constants and `declarations()`, one `EventDeclaration` per name (dispatched by `JsonRpcService`, subject under `event` as `McpRequestEvent` / `McpRespondedEvent`, readonly; `mcp.request` is interceptable because its payload carries an `InterceptionSlot`).
- `JsonRpcService::__construct()` declares them when the dispatcher implements `Milpa\Interfaces\Event\DeclaredEvents` (instanceof guard — a plain dispatcher is asked nothing). Dispatching never depends on the declaration.
- `JsonRpcService::handle()` dispatches through the constants, never a retyped literal.
- `milpa/core` floor raised to `>=0.11 <1.0` (the contract ships there).

## Why

Greenhouse decisions/0228 («los eventos se declaran al despachador y la casa los cuenta»): the authority on which events exist is the emitter, and the one place every dispatch passes through is the dispatcher — so each package declares its own events next to its dispatch sites, and a catalogue reads them from the dispatcher instead of scanning source.

## Falsifier

`tests/TheEmitterDeclaresEveryEventItDispatchesTest.php` drives the real code path (a `tools/list` request through a spy implementing both `MilpaEventDispatcherInterface` and `DeclaredEvents`) and asserts: no undeclared dispatch, the declared set equals the pinned list `['mcp.request', 'mcp.responded']`, each declaration's subject key/type/`dispatchedBy`/interceptability matches the dispatched payload, and — control — a dispatcher that cannot hold declarations runs the same path unharmed. Proven able to fail: deleting the `mcp.responded` declaration made it red (2 failures); restoring it went green.

Gates locally: phpunit 33/33, phpstan OK, docblocks OK, php-cs-fixer 0 fixes, coverage 100.00% (floor 100), attribution OK.

author: izagood
body:
에이전트 설정 화면(1992줄)을 영어 원본으로 옮긴다. **146개 키, 13개 덩어리.**

## 영역을 `agents` 로 잡았다 — `settings.agents` 가 아니라

세 칸 규칙(`<area>.<chunk>.<name>`)에서 `settings` 를 영역으로 쓰면 **화면 이름이 셋째 칸을 먹고 덩어리가 사라진다**(`settings.agents.runnerStopHint`). 설정 화면끼리는 문자열을 공유하지 않으므로 **한 화면 = 한 영역**이다.

덩어리 13개는 화면의 실제 구획에서 왔다 — 화면을 열고 짚으면 키가 나온다: `create` · `detail` · `disable` · `grid` · `memory` · `pat` · `permissions` · `profile` · `run` · `runner` · `stale` · `stop` · `teams`. 덩어리 안은 키 이름 알파벳순(`sidebar` 머리말이 정한 리베이스 이유 그대로).

## 세던 것보다 두 배였다

집계 도구가 센 67개는 **따옴표 안**만이었다. 같은 수의 긴 안내문이 **JSX 텍스트 노드**로 맨몸으로 적혀 있었고(중지/시작 안내, 비활성화 경고, "누가 러너를 띄우나"), **화면에서 사실을 가장 많이 지는 것이 그것들이다.**

## `<strong>` 을 사전에 넣지 않는다

후보가 셋이었고 셋째를 골랐다:

| 길 | 왜 안 되나 |
|---|---|
| 값에 태그 + `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | 이 저장소가 이미 거절한 길(`lib/markdown.ts` 머리말). 번역문은 사람이 고치는 파일이라 태그가 언젠가 깨진다 |
| 문장을 조각으로 쪼개기 | `waitChain.link` 가 금지한 그것 — 어순이 언어마다 달라 조각이 갈 자리가 없다 |
| **문장은 통째, 굵을 마디를 `{strongX}` 로** | ← 이것. 사전은 평문이고, 굵기가 어디 걸리는지는 그 자리가 정한다 |

**함정 하나를 실측으로 잡았다:** 가르는 것은 **자리표시자를 채우기 전의 원문**이어야 한다. 채운 뒤 값으로 찾으면 같은 글자가 문장 다른 곳에 있을 때 엉뚱한 자리가 굵어진다 — `{strongStart}` 의 값 `실행` 은 같은 문장의 `러너 실행` 에도 있다.

## 한국어가 지고 있던 사실을 영어가 지킨다

- 이름 규칙은 **무엇이 되는지**를 적는다 — `Invalid name` 이 아니라 `…2 to 32 characters (this is what you call in a channel with @name)`
- 끊김은 한 단어로 안 끝난다 — `Disconnected — its presence is unknown` (아니면 "오프라인"으로 읽힌다)
- `활동 없음` → `No activity yet`. `yet` 이 *"한 번도 안 돈 것과 죽은 것을 murmur 가 못 가른다"* 를 진다
- 비활성화/활성화 실패를 **결과 상태**로 다시 썼다(`The agent is still enabled` / `still disabled`) — 쓸모 있는 사실은 "동작이 실패했다"가 아니라 **지금 어느 쪽인가**다
- `Resume` 이 아니라 `Start` — 이 버튼은 자동 시작 집합에 되돌릴 뿐이고, `Resume` 은 `#129` 가 금지한 거짓 신호를 되살린다

## 사전에 **안** 넣은 것

- `runnerStatusLabel` · `daemonFactRows` · `lastTurnAgo` — 이 파일 밖이다. 사이드바 작업이 그은 경계 그대로, 이 화면은 **껍데기만** 옮겼다(`agents.detail.lastTurn` 이 `{ago}` 를 받는다)
- 시각 — `toLocaleString()` 이 이미 locale 을 따른다
- 제품 고유어 — `admin` · `PAT` · `harness` · `daemon` · `attach` · `murmur`
- `auto`/`readonly` — 저장·전송용 값(`sidebar.notify` 의 `all`/`mentions`/`none` 과 같은 규칙)

## `Cancel` 을 `common` 에 올리지 않았다

판단 순서 1번(*"두 번째 화면이 실제로 부를 때"*)만 보면 지금이 승격할 때다(`Cancel` 넷, `Save` 하나). **그런데 안 올렸다.**

`Cancel` 이 여러 자리에 있는 것은 *같은 말을 여러 화면이 쓰는 것*이 아니라 **각 폼의 취소가 저마다 다른 것을 되돌리는 것**이고, 이 PR 에서 실제로 그 갈림이 났다 — **기억 지우기의 반대짝은 `Cancel` 이 아니라 `Keep it`** 이다(무엇이 남는지를 말해야 한다). 한 키로 묶는 순간 하나를 고치는 일이 나머지 셋을 함께 바꾼다.

**`common` 에 올릴 자격은 "글자가 같다"가 아니라 "뜻이 하나다"** 이고, 그 근거와 다음 후보(`Loading…`, 현재 2)를 `en.ts` 에 적었다.

## `lastTurnLabel` 이 번역기를 **필수** 인자로 받는다

기본값을 주면 `Profile` 이 안 넘겨도 컴파일되고 **그 화면만 영어로 굳는다** — `i18n.test.tsx` 가 화면을 렌더해서 잡으려는 바로 그 실패다. `memberErrorText` 주입 선례를 따랐다.

## RED/GREEN — 코드 줄에 프로브를 넣어 실측

| 프로브 | 빨개진 수 |
|---|---|
| `useT` 가 locale 을 무시하고 항상 `translator('en')` | 6 (기존 포함 16) |
| `emphasize` 가 `<strong>` 대신 `Fragment` | 2 |
| `lastTurnLabel` 이 `t` 를 무시하고 영어를 직접 적음 | 8 |
| `ko.ts` 에서 `agents.stop.heading` 삭제 | **컴파일 차단**(`satisfies Catalog`) |

코디네이터가 독립으로 하나 더 쟀다 — `emphasize` 를 *"채운 뒤 값으로 가르기"* 로 되돌리자 **3개가 빨개졌고**, 되돌리자 초록. 위에 적은 그 함정이 회귀선에 실제로 걸린다.

## 검증

- 5개 패키지 `typecheck` 통과
- **Node 22**(CI 엔진) 실측: **176 파일 / 2258 테스트 통과**
- 남은 한국어 문자열 **0** — 도구가 세는 따옴표 문자열과, 도구가 못 세는 맨몸 JSX 텍스트를 따로 훑어 둘 다 0
- CJK 오염 없음

## 회귀선 한 곳의 단언을 바꿨다

`agentActivity` 의 끊김 축이 **낱말 `알 수 없음` 을 그대로** 재고 있었다. 문구가 더 정확해지면서(`연결 끊김 — 살아 있는지 알 수 없다`) 그 단언이 깨지는데, 낱말이 아니라 **사실**을 재도록 바꿨다 — *"모른다고 말하고, 오프라인이라고는 말하지 않는다"*. 나머지 회귀선 11개는 기존 관례대로 한국어에 고정했다(그것들이 재는 것은 언어가 아니라 그 언어로 표현된 규율이다).


---

## 갱신 — #622 와 합류하면서 반쪽 둘이 한 줄이 됐다

#622(시간 표기 통합)가 먼저 머지되어 리베이스했다. 14곳이 충돌했는데 **뜻이 하나였다**: 두 PR 이 `lastTurnLabel` 의 **각자 반쪽**을 옮기고 있었다.

| | 옮긴 것 | 남긴 것 | 필요한 인자 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#622** | 경과 `11분 전` → `Intl` | 접두는 한국어 | `locale` |
| **#641** | 접두 → 사전(`Last activity:`) | 경과는 한국어 | `t` |

**합치면 완성된다.** `lastTurnLabel(iso, now, locale, t)` 이 넷을 받고, 한 줄이 통째로 그 언어로 뜬다:

```
Last activity: 11 minutes ago      ← 접두는 사전이, 경과는 Intl 이
마지막 활동: 11분 전
```

### 반쪽 상태가 며칠 살아 있었다

머지 사이에 `Last activity: 11분 전` 이 실제로 존재했다. **컴파일도 회귀선도 조용했다** — 두 쪽 모두 자기 반쪽만 재고 있었기 때문이다(#641 은 *"경과는 아직 한국어다"* 를, #622 는 *"접두는 아직 한국어다"* 를 각각 **의도된 상태로 잠그고** 있었다).

그래서 회귀선 4개가 리베이스 후 빨개졌고, **그것이 옳은 실패다.** 각각의 전제가 상대의 반쪽이었다:

- `"접두는 언어를 따라오고 **경과는 아직 한국어**다"`
- `"경과가 영어로 나온다 — **사전에 그 문구가 없는데도**"`

넷을 새 사실로 다시 썼다. 이제 그 축들이 재는 것은 *"어디까지 옮겼나"* 가 아니라 **두 출처가 한 줄에서 어긋나지 않는 것**이고, 옛 반쪽 상태가 되살아나면 잡힌다:

```ts
expect(row.textContent).toBe('Last activity: 11 minutes ago');
expect(row.textContent).not.toContain('분 전');   // 반쪽 상태 금지
```

### 중복 import 둘

두 PR 이 각자 `useT` 를 들여 `Profile.tsx` · `AgentsSettings.tsx` 에서 중복 선언이 났다. 한 벌로 합치고 **양쪽 주석이 지고 있던 사실은 살렸다** — *"이 화면은 아직 안 옮겼다"* 와 *"화면은 `useT`, 화면 밖 순수 함수는 `Translate` 를 인자로"* 둘 다 남는다.

### 재검증

- 5개 패키지 `typecheck` 통과
- **Node 22: 176 파일 / 2273 테스트 통과** (2258 → 2273; 합류로 축이 늘었다)
- 남은 한국어 **0**, CJK 없음

author: jon890
body:
## 어떤 이유로 PR을 하셨나요?

- 대화방에 진행 상황을 여러 번 보고하면 본문에 메시지가 쌓여 읽기 어려워지는 문제가 있었습니다.
- 스레드로 묶으면 대화방에는 한 줄만 남고 나머지는 그 안에 쌓임
- 그래서 스레드를 여는 `messenger thread-send` 를 추가하고 `--log` 유무로 공식 endpoint 둘을 가르게 했습니다.

## 작업 내용

- `thread-send` 명령

  | `--log` | 호출하는 endpoint | 요청 body |
  |---------|-------------------|-----------|
  | 없음 | `channels/{id}/threads/create-and-send` | `{ text, threadText? }` |
  | 있음 | `channels/{id}/logs/{log-id}/threads/create-and-send` | `{ text }` |

  - `--quiet` 은 log-id 가 아니라 스레드 채널의 `channelId` 를 냄
  - `--thread-body` 는 생략 가능, 생략하면 스레드만 열림
  - `--log` 와 `--thread-body` 를 함께 주면 경고 후 무시

- 순수 함수 분리
  - `buildThreadRequest` 가 경로와 요청 body 를 생성
    - `threadText` 는 값이 있을 때만 키를 넣음
  - `checkThreadOptions` 가 옵션 조합을 판정
    - 던지지 않고 결과를 반환해 호출부가 경고와 에러를 나눠 처리
  - 테스트 12건

- 문서
  - README 에 메신저 절 신설
  - 스레드에 메시지를 잇는 방법을 명시
    - 새 명령이 아니라 `channel-send` 에 스레드 채널 id 를 주는 경로

- phase 검증 절 수정
  - 실제 발송으로 확인하는 단계 제거
    - 대상 자리를 placeholder 로 두면 실행 주체가 그것을 채움
    - `--channel` 은 이름 부분일치도 받아 엉뚱한 대화방으로 나감

## 리뷰어가 집중해 주길 바라는 부분이 있다면 입력해 주세요.

- 공식 문서는 `threads/create-and-send` 응답에서 `$.result.threadChannelId` 를 쓰라고 적지만 그 필드는 오지 않습니다. `channelId` 가 스레드 채널 id 이고, 그 값으로 `logs` 를 보내 스레드에 붙는 것을 실측했습니다. 근거는 ADR-052 에 남겼습니다.
- `--quiet` 이 `channelId` 를 내는 것은 다른 messenger 명령과 다릅니다. 스레드를 연 다음에 하는 일이 그 스레드에 메시지를 잇는 것이라 그 값이 필요합니다.
- 리뷰 반영 커밋 셋이 들어 있습니다. `--log` 일 때 스레드 본문을 읽지 않도록 고쳤고, `channelId` 검증을 세 출력 경로로 모았고, stdin 충돌 문구에 실제로 준 옵션 이름을 넣었습니다.
- 원래 #167 로 올렸으나 base 브랜치가 머지와 함께 삭제되면서 자동으로 닫혔습니다. 같은 브랜치로 다시 엽니다. 리뷰 이력은 #167 에 있습니다.

---
> 이 PR은 AI에 의해 작성되었습니다.

author: beyondworks
body:
## 제보
"쪽지함에서 1시간 넘게 배달이 안 된다"(2026-09-08). 제보자 환경(버전·화면 상태)은 미확보라 원인은 후보 순위로 두고, 코드로 확정된 구조적 결함 두 가지를 닫습니다.

## 원인 사슬(코드 근거)
1. **직렬 대기**: 스케줄러 틱은 회사당 배달 패스 1개(`mailDelivering`)이고 안에서 `await runTurn`으로 순차 배달 — 한 회사의 쪽지 처리량은 "동시에 턴 하나". 앞 턴(v0.1.65부터 최대 30분 × 재시도 3회)이 뒤 쪽지를 전부 막습니다.
2. **잔재 회수 3시간**: `.claimed` 회수 창이 #458에서 45분 → 3시간. 앱 재시작·크래시 뒤 쪽지가 그동안 "배달 중"에 갇히고 화면엔 진행 표시가 없음.

## 처방(커밋 8개, 분리 검수 7라운드)
- **회수를 자기 심박(mtime) 기준으로**(0df9d92→79f70c9): 배달 프로세스가 `.claimed`의 mtime을 30초마다 `utimes`로 찍고, 회수는 "mtime이 3분보다 오래됨" 단독 판정. 크루 상태 파일 의존 없음. 회수는 한 번의 시도로 계수(attempts+1).
- **회사별 동시 배달**(d3eae39→41f6622→47d1acd, 유건 지시 "회의실처럼 동시에"): 선점(순차·파일 원자 연산)과 실행(`deliverOne`)을 분리하고 `runLimited`(`src/run-limited.mjs`로 공용화, room은 재수출)로 동시 실행. **같은 크루는 순차, 크루 간에만 동시**(한 크루의 동시 턴은 상태 파일을 서로 지움). 착수는 크루별 **라운드로빈**(한 크루 백로그가 다른 크루를 막지 않음). `MAIL_CONCURRENCY` = clamp(`ARGO_MAIL_CONCURRENCY`, 1..16, 기본 8) = 사실상 "동시에 도는 크루 수". 착수 전 **예산 게이트**(월 한도 도달 시 그 패스는 순차).
- **선점 신원(claimBy)**(f7869d6→5a2b4ea→6294dbd): 선점 시점에 토큰 각인, 회수 시 제거, 실패 정착·착수는 신원 일치일 때만(회수→재선점 뒤 남의 claim을 되돌리던 창 봉합). 생략 분기의 심박·inFlight 정리.
- 쪽지함 화면 "배달 중 · N분 경과"(ko/en, NaN 가드), 안내 문구·`docs/selfhost.md`.

## 검증(근거)

author: ayushchangedia
body:
Pushed on request mid-run — this is 2 commits, not the 9 that were asked for.
Both are complete and green; the rest of the plan is listed at the bottom.

## Tests for the playback state machine

`timeline.js` is the only stateful thing in the project and it drives
everything the viewer sees. It also has no renderer in it, so it can be driven
at any speed a test likes — there was no reason for the gap beyond it being the
file that never broke loudly.

Its failure modes are all silent. Playback that stops halfway looks like a
short repo. A commit applied twice double-counts its line changes, and that
building stays the wrong height for the rest of the replay.

30 tests. The ones pinning real behaviour rather than restating the code:

- the whole history plays in ~45 seconds at 100, 300 and 562 commits — the promise the README makes
- every commit is applied exactly once across a full run
- a part-accumulated step survives across frames, so playback doesn't run slow by a fraction of a step every frame
- a seek *discards* that partial step, so a jump doesn't apply the next commit early
- seeking to the index it's already on does no work — the seek handler tears the city down and rebuilds it, and a dragged scrubber fires on every mouse move
- a tab backgrounded for ten minutes applies at most 8 commits rather than replaying 600 in one frame, and the discarded backlog doesn't leak into the next frame

## Fix: `setSpeed(0)` froze playback silently

`setSpeed` took whatever it was handed. Zero leaves `playing` true while the
accumulator never reaches a step — the button says pause, the scrubber doesn't
move, the city sits still. A deadlock with no error, indistinguishable from a
very slow step.

**NaN is the one that matters.** It poisons the accumulator, and since
`NaN >= step` is false for every future frame, playback stays dead *even after
the speed is set back to 1*. I verified that before fixing it: NaN then 1
applies zero commits, forever.

Zero and below are now refused, keeping the previous speed — "stop advancing"
is what pause means, and that's a button already. Numeric strings are accepted,
since that's what a range input hands you. `tick` got the same guard on its
delta: the first frame after a resume can arrive with no previous timestamp,
and one NaN there kills playback permanently rather than dropping a frame.

Reverting `timeline.js` fails 4 of the 5 new tests.

## Not done

I'd found a third real bug and was mid-fix when this went out:
`scripts/fetch-history.js`'s `parseArgs` **silently drops the 300-commit cap**
when `--limit` is passed with no value — the key is set to `undefined`, the
`!== undefined` guard skips the `Number()` conversion, and `Math.min(undefined,
HARD_CAP)` downstream is `NaN`. `--limit abc` gives a NaN limit the same way,
and `--repo --synthetic` takes the flag as the value.

Say the word and I'll finish that plus the remaining commits — `world.js` sun
vector and fog derivation, the `fetch-history` CLI helpers, and a CI/docs pass.

Жалоба владельца со звонка 8 сентября 2026: рубль → бат на 25 000 ₽ выходит дешевле, чем на 50 000 ₽. Причина не в коде, а в первой ступени сеток бата на проде: фикс 5 $ (кошелёк 10 $) до 500 $ при 4,5 % (5,5 %) дальше — на 300 $ клиент платит 1,7 %, на 600 $ уже 4,5 %. Сетка совпадает с ТЗ от 10 августа, и в августе скачок был записан в спеку ценой решения; владелец назвал его ошибкой.

**Что меняется.** `feeScheduleSchema` в `@nemo/types` получает правило: на каждой границе комиссия ступени до неё за сумму порога не меньше комиссии ступени после (фикс в валюте выдачи сравнивается отдельно, равенство проходит — юань годится). Отказ словами с границей и обеими комиссиями, одними и теми же в ядре (`InvalidInputError`) и в форме панели до нажатия. Заготовка новой сетки начинается с «4,5 % + 5 $».

**Что не меняется.** Действующие сетки при чтении не проверяются: после выкатки бат считается как считал, а пересохранить его с прежней первой ступенью панель не даст.
