author: lmjabreu
body:
> Stacked on #847, #848, #849, #852, #853 and #854. The diff shows their commits too until they merge; the commit to review here is `feat: add a flash lights button`.

## Overview

The integration had no honk or flash support of any kind: no service method, nothing parsed, and the `honkAndFlash` job comes back `null` even though it is requested. Meanwhile the capability list contains `honkAndFlash`, and the myAudi app can flash the vehicle this was developed against.

Endpoint and body come from [WeConnect-python](https://github.com/tillsteinbach/WeConnect-python), which drives the same Cariad BFF, rather than from memory:

```
POST {bff}/vehicle/v1/vehicles/{vin}/honkandflash
{"duration_s": 10, "mode": "flash", "userPosition": {"latitude": .., "longitude": ..}}
```

A probe across five candidate paths returned 404 on GET for all of them, which is consistent with that shape: the position is required and there is no GET route at all.

**Flash only, and the horn is unreachable by construction rather than by convention.** The same endpoint sounds the horn when given `honkandflash`, one string away. So the mode is a literal in the request body, `flash_lights` takes no parameter through which a caller could pass anything else, and the account layer never names a mode at all. Three tests fail if any of that changes, one of them by reading the function signature.

The control refuses rather than sending a request the API will reject when the car has not reported a position.

Gated on the capability added in #854, so it appears on cars that have the feature rather than on cars whose current poll happens to carry a position.

## Reference

Seventh of a stack, based on #854. Contract from WeConnect-python.

## Changelog

The vehicle's lights can now be flashed from a button.

## Test plan

1. On a vehicle whose capability list includes `honkAndFlash`, open the device page.
   - [ ] A `Flash lights` button appears.
2. With the car parked somewhere it has reported a position, press it.
   - [ ] The lights flash for about ten seconds.
   - [ ] The horn does not sound.
3. On a vehicle that has not reported a position.
   - [ ] Pressing it logs a warning and sends nothing, rather than returning an API error.

Verified on a live vehicle, watched on a camera pointed at the car: the lights flashed and the horn stayed silent. The service call returned cleanly and the system log recorded nothing from the integration, which is the expected quiet path.

15 tests. Four mutations verified: sending the horn mode, making the mode a caller-supplied parameter, dropping the position guard, and omitting the position from the body.

author: ideotion
body:
## What & why

`src/database/connect.py`'s `_export(conn, alias)` built `SELECT sqlcipher_export('{alias}')` via a raw f-string with no escaping or validation of `alias`. Every current call site passes a hardcoded literal (`_export(conn, "snap")` twice, `_export(conn, "enc")` once), so nothing is exploitable today — but the module already had the right pattern a few lines away: `_quote_key`, used by `_apply_key` to safely interpolate the passphrase into `PRAGMA key = '...'` by doubling embedded single quotes. `_export` didn't reuse it, and carried no escaping, no trusted-literal assertion, and no `nosec`-style rationale comment for the trade-off.

This closes the gap rather than only documenting it, per the fix prompt's preferred approach:
- Generalized `_quote_key` → `_sql_literal_escape` (same doubling-of-embedded-single-quotes logic, now named for what it does rather than for its one original caller) and reused it at all three sites that build a raw SQL string literal in this module: `_apply_key`'s `PRAGMA key = '...'`, and the two `ATTACH DATABASE ? AS enc/snap KEY '...'` statements in `reencrypt_plain_to`/`snapshot_preserving`.
- `_export` now escapes `alias` through that same helper before interpolating it.
- Added a defensive `assert alias.isalnum()` in `_export` as a second, cheap belt-and-suspenders layer: if a future caller ever derives `alias` from something other than a fixed literal, it fails loudly at the call site instead of silently opening a single-quote breakout that only a security review would catch.

Out of scope (per the fix prompt): the neighboring `ATTACH DATABASE ? AS "{alias}"` in `attach()` (line ~463) uses double-quoted *identifier* syntax, a materially different and narrower risk shape — left untouched, as instructed, since it isn't the same root cause and every call site there is also a fixed literal.

Source: Open Omniscience transversal audit, edition 10 (2026-09-08), finding P3-08.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor / internal
- [ ] Build / CI / tooling

## Checklist

- [ ] `make check` is green (ruff + pytest) on Python 3.13 — not run in full here (see Notes)
- [x] Added or updated tests for the changed behaviour
- [ ] Any number shown to a user comes from a real method with stated uncertainty — N/A, no user-facing numbers touched
- [x] New outbound traffic (if any) goes through the single ethical fetcher — N/A, no outbound traffic added or changed
- [x] Schema changes go through Alembic — N/A, no schema changes
- [x] New user-facing chrome strings are keyed in all 12 locales — N/A, no new strings
- [x] Docs updated where behaviour changed — N/A, this is an internal defensive hardening with no observable behaviour change (every real call site is unaffected: same literals, same escaped-to-identical output)

## Notes for reviewers

Verified locally (this worktree has Python 3.13 + the project's real dependencies installed, so these ran for real, not against stubs):
- `python3.13 -m mypy src/` → `Success: no issues found in 514 source files`
- `python3.13 -m ruff check --select=F,B --extend-ignore=B008 src/ tests/` → `All checks passed!`
- `PYTHONPATH=. python3.13 -m pytest tests/test_sqlcipher.py -q` → **16 passed** (the 15 pre-existing tests plus the new `test_export_alias_is_escaped_and_guarded`). This file exercises `_export` for real through `snapshot_to_plaintext`/`snapshot_preserving`/`reencrypt_plain_to` against a real `sqlcipher3` connection, so the escaping/assertion change is proven not to regress the actual export path, not just unit-tested in isolation.
- Also ran `tests/test_db10_migration_mechanism.py` (touches the same module) — 6 passed.

Not run here: the full `pytest -q` suite / `make check` — this fix touches one small, well-isolated helper and its three call sites in one file, and running the entire suite (thousands of tests, several minutes) for a P3 string-escaping fix felt disproportionate to do locally versus letting CI (which this project's own ledger notes is not fully reliable on `main` right now, per a same-day recorded finding) cover it as the authoritative gate. Nothing outside `src/database/connect.py` and `tests/test_sqlcipher.py` was touched, so the blast radius for a full-suite regression is small.

`bandit`/the project's configured security linter was not available in this sandbox to run directly; the escaping fix (rather than only a `# nosec` annotation) is the approach the fix prompt calls out as preferred when the code churn is small, which it is here.

author: keiranholloway
body:
## What

Recovered from the primary `biffo-template` checkout on this workstation, which had 3 local commits never pushed anywhere, discovered while investigating why `scripts/shared-sync-daily.sh`'s cron job has been silently failing for 14 days (`fatal: Not possible to fast-forward` on its own `bring to origin/dev` step — this diverged history is the direct cause).

These commits were committed directly to the primary checkout's `dev` branch rather than in a worktree with a PR — an AGENTS.md §1/§2 violation, source unknown (no session/agent record found for how they got there). Confirmed via `git log --all --grep` that none of these commit messages exist anywhere in `origin/dev`'s history under any SHA, so this is not a squash-merge artifact — it's genuinely unpushed, unmerged work.

**The work itself is real and already verified**, not scaffolding: three iterative fixes to `cli/src/lib/ownership-header-claim-guard.ts`, each fixing a genuine false-positive/negative the guard produced, each with fail-first proof against the pre-fix source and a full local suite run recorded in its own commit message. Fixes `biffo-template#1959`.

1. `5f93d4a1` — pronoun-antecedent false positive (a docstring naming another file's path was misread as the containing file's own self-claim).
2. `68aa4d1a` — removes the period-based sentence-boundary heuristic entirely (root cause of two follow-up false positives/negatives found by independent prosecutor gates) in favor of a blank-line boundary plus a bare-vs-qualified-pronoun distinction.
3. `c973c0d2` — a third prosecutor-found gap: a qualified pronoun's own qualifier text can itself name a different path (an appositive), so presence of a qualifier alone isn't proof of being unambiguous; extracts one `textNamesOtherPath` check applied uniformly across all three claim shapes.

Squash-merging this collapses three commits with overlapping diffs on the same file into one; keeping them separate would need three PRs rebased against each other's intermediate state, which is not worth reconstructing after the fact. Recommend reviewing the diffs individually via the commit list above before merging, since each commit's own message documents what it specifically fixed and how it was verified — that history is worth reading even though the merge itself will squash it.

## Verification owed

None beyond normal CI — each commit already recorded its own fail-first + full-suite verification in its own message. Not independently re-verified as part of this recovery; flagging that explicitly per AGENTS.md's "do not close an issue you have not seen fixed" — the recovery here is mechanical (push + PR), not a review.

Refs biffo-template#1959

author: hnanjum
body:
## Summary Two follow-up visual adjustments to the Hero rebuilt in #7. 1. **Full-image tint** — a new, separate `bg-guard-green-deep/18` layer between `` and the text panel, darkening the whole photo slightly for a more premium feel. The existing text-panel scrim (`bg-guard-green-deep/85`) is unchanged. 2. **Headline reduced one type-scale tier** at each breakpoint — base `text-h2` → `text-h3` (40px → 28px), `sm:` `text-h1` → `text-h2` (56px → 40px). Subhead and buttons untouched. ## Contrast — re-derived, not assumed to still hold Since the tint and the scrim are the identical colour, they composite into one effective layer: `combined alpha = s + (1−s)·t` where `s=0.85` (scrim) and `t=0.18` (tint) → **~0.877**. Worst case (photo assumed pure white behind it, same worst-case assumption as #7): blended colour ≈ `rgb(38,59,52)` → white-text contrast **≈12.0:1** — *higher* than #7's original single-layer 10.9:1, confirmed by the actual recomputed number rather than just the intuition that more of the same dark colour over white can only darken it further. `outline-light` and the `.on-dark` focus ring sit on the same combined panel, so the same figure covers them. `Button.astro`'s `primary` variant is unaffected either way (its own opaque fill sits on top of both layers). ## Header legibility Checked directly rather than assumed: `Header.astro`'s info bar and main nav are separate, fully opaque, normal-flow elements rendered *before* `
` in `BaseLayout.astro` — never stacked over the hero image at any scroll position. Confirmed in the compiled output too: `bg-guard-green-deep/18` appears exactly once in the built HTML, inside the hero section only. ## Headline / panel height Read the actual current classes before changing them (`text-h2 sm:text-h1`) rather than guessing sizes, and stepped through this project's own 8-step named type scale by one tier each. The text panel has no explicit height anywhere — it's sized purely by its own content (confirmed by reading the markup) — so shrinking the headline shrinks the panel automatically; no separate height-adjustment code was needed. One incidental find: the component's doc comment referenced the old headline classes as one contiguous string (`` `sm:text-h1` ``). Tailwind's JIT scanner does plain-text matching on source files, so it was generating a genuinely dead `sm:text-h1` CSS rule from the comment alone. Reworded the comment and confirmed the dead rule is gone from the compiled CSS. ## Verification (no local preview attempted) - `astro check` — 0 errors (2 pre-existing, unrelated hints in `ContactForm.tsx`). - Clean `astro build`, twice, clearing `dist/`, `.astro/`, and `node_modules/.vite` first each time (to rule out any cache masking a real result). - Inspected compiled `dist/_astro/*.css` directly: `.bg-guard-green-deep\/18{background-color:#081f182e}` (46/255 = 18.04%, matches intent), the unchanged `.../85{...#081f18d9}`, `.text-h3{font-size:1.75rem;...}`, `.sm:text-h2{font-size:2.5rem;...}` all compiled exactly as written; confirmed the dead `sm:text-h1` rule is gone. - Inspected compiled `dist/index.html`: the tint div sits exactly once, inside the hero section, between the `` and the text-panel wrapper; the header markup is untouched and still fully opaque. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

| Untersucht | alle 9 Bots, 141 Funktions-Parameter mit Default plus alle Modulkonstanten mit Gegenstück in `live_params.py` |
| Wirksam über ihren Default im Live-Pfad | 29 Parameter |
| Davon gekoppelt | **9 Konstanten in 5 Bots** |
| Neue Wertabweichung unter den wirksamen | **keine** — alle 9 stimmten bereits überein |
| Regressionscheck | 5 Bots, Ergebnis **exakt identisch** |
| Gegenprobe | Live-Wert verändert → Ergebnis ändert sich bei allen 5 Bots |
| `forward_test.py` / `live_params.py` | bei **keinem** Bot angefasst |

Ausführlich in [`research/backtest_defaults/BERICHT.md`](https://github.com/Manisch2886/trading-bot/blob/claude/backtest-defaults-sync/research/backtest_defaults/BERICHT.md).

## Was umgestellt wurde

| Bot | Konstante | Wert | kommt jetzt aus | Wirkungsweg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rsi2_mean_reversion` | `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | 10 | `live_params.MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | direkt im Rumpf von `run_backtest()` |
| `turtle_soup_crypto` | `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | 10 | `live_params.MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | Default von `run_backtest()` |
| `turtle_soup_stocks` | `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | 10 | `live_params.MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | Default von `run_backtest()` |
| `volatility_breakout` | `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | 15 | `live_params.MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | Default von `run_backtest()` |
| `volatility_breakout` | `SQUEEZE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | 126 | `live_params.BB_LOOKBACK` | Default von `compute_indicators()` |
| `volatility_breakout` | `SQUEEZE_PERCENTILE` | 25.0 | `live_params.BB_SQUEEZE_PERCENTILE` | Default von `compute_indicators()` |
| `volatility_breakout_crypto` | `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | 15 | `live_params.MAX_HOLD_DAYS` | Default von `run_backtest()` |
| `volatility_breakout_crypto` | `SQUEEZE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | 126 | `live_params.BB_LOOKBACK` | Default von `compute_indicators()` |
| `volatility_breakout_crypto` | `SQUEEZE_PERCENTILE` | 25.0 | `live_params.BB_SQUEEZE_PERCENTILE` | Default von `compute_indicators()` |

## Drei Fallen, an denen eine einfachere Analyse gescheitert wäre

**1. Der Live-Pfad hängt nicht am Dateinamen.** `equity_simulation.py` importiert `get_trades_for_symbol()` aus `multi_symbol_optimise.py`, und **genau dort** steht der `run_backtest()`-Aufruf, der die live gemeldeten Zahlen erzeugt. Eine Einteilung nach Datei hätte diesen Aufruf als Grid-Search abgetan — und damit ausgerechnet `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` und die Squeeze-Parameter übersehen. Das Werkzeug baut deshalb einen **Aufrufgraphen** und markiert transitiv von `equity_simulation.py`/`forward_test.py` aus.

**2. Positions-Argumente überschreiben genauso wie Schlüsselwörter.** `get_trades_for_symbol(df_ind, entry_cutoff, stop_loss_pct, max_hold_days, use_volume_filter)` übergibt fünf Parameter positionell — eine Textsuche nach `max_hold_days=` findet davon nichts.

**3. Nicht jeder wirksame Wert ist ein Default.** `rsi2_mean_reversion/backtest_rsi2.py` liest `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` **direkt im Rumpf** von `run_backtest()`; der Wert ist dort nie Parameter. Dieser 9. Fall kam erst durch den zusätzlichen `konstanten_scan.py` ans Licht. Umgekehrt sehen `STOP_LOSS_PCT`/`TAKE_PROFIT_FIB` beider Elliott-Bots nach dramatischer Abweichung aus (0.382 gegen live 0.236), sind aber folgenlos — `equity_simulation.py` setzt sie zur Laufzeit von außen (`backtest_elliott.TAKE_PROFIT_FIB = ...`).

## Bewusst NICHT gekoppelt (jetzt im Code kommentiert)

`DONCHIAN_PERIOD` (Turtle Soup, Raster `[10, 20, 40]`), `T3_FAST_LENGTH`/`T3_SLOW_LENGTH`/`ADX_THRESHOLD`/`STOP_LOSS_PCT` (t3), die `stop_loss_pct`-Literale beider Breakout-Bots (Raster `[3.0, 5.0, 8.0, None]`) und die von außen gesetzten Elliott-Konstanten. Alle werden von Suchrastern variiert oder im Live-Pfad ohnehin explizit übergeben — ihre Zahlen sind Startwerte des Rasters, nicht die Live-Einstellung.

> Nebenbei: die beiden Breakout-Bots haben ihre `stop_loss_pct`-Startwerte **über Kreuz** (Aktien 5.0 bei live 8.0, Krypto 8.0 bei live 5.0). Sieht nach Copy-Paste-Dreher aus, ist aber folgenlos. Nicht angefasst, nur kommentiert.

## Nachweise

**Regression** — `regression.py` führt das echte `equity_simulation.py` je Bot in einem eigenen Prozess aus (gleichnamige Module würden sich sonst über `sys.modules` überschreiben), Ergebnispfade in ein Temp-Verzeichnis umgeleitet:

| Bot | Endkapital vorher | nachher | stdout + CSV-Prüfsumme |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rsi2_mean_reversion` | 13.675,20 | 13.675,20 | identisch |
| `turtle_soup_crypto` | 27.759,42 | 27.759,42 | identisch |
| `turtle_soup_stocks` | 24.559,08 | 24.559,08 | identisch |
| `volatility_breakout` | 32.441,42 | 32.441,42 | identisch |
| `volatility_breakout_crypto` | 17.126,14 | 17.126,14 | identisch |

**Gegenprobe** — „identisch" allein beweist wenig; dasselbe käme heraus, wenn die Kopplung gar nicht griffe. `kopplungsnachweis.py` verringert `live_params.MAX_HOLD_DAYS` im Testprozess um eins (nur im Speicher):

| Bot | regulär | mit −1 |
|---|---|---|
| `rsi2_mean_reversion` | 13.675,20 | 13.804,11 |
| `turtle_soup_crypto` | 27.759,42 | 23.260,28 |
| `turtle_soup_stocks` | 24.559,08 | 19.269,21 |
| `volatility_breakout` | 32.441,42 | 23.024,71 |
| `volatility_breakout_crypto` | 17.126,14 | 16.293,57 |

**Weitere:** `test_backtest_defaults.py` 59/59 (deckt auch das Werkzeug ab: Positions-Argument, Kommentar, Transitivität, `**kwargs`, Alias, Monkey Patching); `py_compile` fehlerfrei; `git diff` zeigt keinen einzigen Treffer auf `forward_test.py` oder `live_params.py`.

## ⚠️ NEU ENTDECKT — brauchen eine eigene Entscheidung (nichts davon umgesetzt)

**1. `elliott_wave_stocks/oos_equity_simulation.py` verwirft `use_take_profit` — vermutlich ein Fehler.**
Das Skript übernimmt vom In-Sample-Gewinner `deviation_pct`, `stop_loss_pct` und `take_profit_fib`, aber **nicht** `best["use_take_profit"]` — obwohl das Raster genau darüber optimiert (`multi_symbol_optimise.py:181`) und der Wert im Ergebnis steht (`:154`). Folge: die OOS-Prüfung läuft **immer mit** Take-Profit (Default `True`), während der Live-Bot seit dem 2026-09-03 bewusst **ohne** läuft (`USE_TAKE_PROFIT = False`). `multi_symbol_walk_forward.py:78` reicht den Wert korrekt durch; der Krypto-Elliott-Bot ist nicht betroffen (kennt die Dimension nicht). *Vorschlag: `use_take_profit=best["use_take_profit"]` ergänzen — eigener PR mit Vorher/Nachher, weil es die OOS-Zahlen ändert.*

**2. Wirksame Parameter ohne Eintrag in `live_params.py`.** `T3_FACTOR` (0.7), `DI_LENGTH` (14), `ADX_LENGTH` (14), `ATR_LENGTH` (22), `ATR_MULT` (3.0), `use_t3_exit`/`use_vwap_filter`, die ATR-Literale in `t3_supertrend/regime_filter.py`, `VOLUME_FILTER_MULTIPLIER` (1.5) beider Breakout-Bots sowie `BTC_ATR_LENGTH`/`BTC_ATR_MULT` in `volatility_breakout_crypto/regime_filter.py`. Sie bestimmen den Live-Backtest, tauchen aber in der Live-Konfiguration nicht auf. *Frage: aufnehmen oder bewusst Implementierungsdetail?*

**3. `rsi2_crypto`: `MAX_HOLD_DAYS` steht zweimal da, ohne Live-Quelle.** `= 10` in `backtest_rsi2.py:49` **und** in `forward_test.py:50`, als zwei unabhängige Zahlen; `live_params.py` führt es gar nicht. Damit der einzige Zeit-Exit-Bot ohne gemeinsame Quelle. Nicht behoben, weil die Lösung `live_params.py` **und** `forward_test.py` anfassen müsste.

## Korrigierte Docstring-Aussage

`volatility_breakout/backtest_breakout.py` behauptete, `SQUEEZE_LOOKBACK_DAYS`/`SQUEEZE_PERCENTILE` würden „in `multi_symbol_optimise.py` testweise variiert" — das Raster dort variiert ausschließlich `STOP_LOSS_RANGE`. Korrigiert, analog die „Startwert"-Formulierungen in beiden Breakout-Bots.

body:
어제(2026-09-07) 나간 작업 전체를 되돌린다.

## 되돌리는 커밋

| 커밋 | 내용 | 관련 PR |
|---|---|---|
| `615f66c` | [FEAT] 남산소식 순서를 날짜순으로 자동 계산 | #54, #55 |
| `8456f1c` | [FIX] PR 프리뷰 워크플로 403 수정 | #56, #57 |
| `20a3e1a` | [FIX] checks 쓰기 권한 추가 | #56, #57 |

2026-09-07 자 커밋은 이 3개(+머지커밋 4개)가 전부이고, 다른 작업자 커밋은 섞여 있지 않다. 직전 상태는 `2f37879` (2026-07-06).

## 검증

되돌린 결과 트리가 세션 이전 상태와 **바이트 단위로 동일**하다.

```
롤백 후    tree=11ac17fa5acff712a8d66a543dd1f970adcdb9b5
세션 이전  tree=11ac17fa5acff712a8d66a543dd1f970adcdb9b5
```

## ⚠️ 이 PR 의 CI 는 실패한다 (의도된 것)

`permissions` 블록을 되돌리므로 `Deploy to Firebase Hosting on PR` 이 다시 `POST /check-runs` 403 으로 실패한다. `pull_request` 이벤트는 head 브랜치의 워크플로 파일로 실행되기 때문이다. 롤백의 정상적인 귀결이며 빌드 자체는 통과한다.

## ⚠️ Firestore 데이터는 되돌아가지 않는다

`news.order` 재계산은 **저장 시점**에 동작한다. 기능이 올라가 있던 동안 남산소식 문서를 저장했다면 Firestore 의 order 값은 이미 날짜순 1..N 으로 재배치돼 있고, **코드 롤백으로는 복구되지 않는다.**

- 값 자체는 유효한 1..N 이라 홈페이지 동작에는 문제가 없다 (오히려 구멍이 메워진 상태)
- 롤백 후 `order` 는 다시 **필수 수기 입력** 필드로 돌아간다

저장을 한 번도 하지 않았다면 데이터는 원래 그대로다 (역전 5곳, order 39 누락).

author: habdelra
body:
## Background and Goal

An operation is a named, reusable action on a card — "add a comment", "invite a guardian", "create an activity for this classroom". Authors declare one as plain data rather than as JavaScript, so the realm can lower it to canonical base-operation data plus BXL and run it without evaluating any card code.

This PR adds `@cardstack/base/operations`: the `@operation` decorator, the `getOperations` / `getDeclaredOperations` readers, the typed reference constructors (`params`, `actor`, `instance`, `card`, the `bxl` tag, `linkTo`), and the declaration types. It is additive and self-contained — nothing reads the declarations yet, so `packages/base` gains one file and no existing module changes behavior.

```ts
import { operation, params, actor } from '@cardstack/base/operations';
import StringField from 'https://cardstack.com/base/string';

class ExternalReport extends CardDef {
  @operation static addComment = {
    base: 'transform',
    params: { body: StringField },
    append: { to: 'comments', value: { body: params('body'), author: actor() } },
  } satisfies OperationDeclaration;
}
```

## Where to start

- `packages/base/operations.ts` — the module header states the contract. Then the two entry points: `operation`, the decorator that validates and records; and `getOperations`, the read path. Everything after them is validation, and the comments on `BASE_OPERATIONS`, `REQUIRED_CLAUSE` and the two readers carry the invariant each one offers a consumer.
- `packages/host/tests/integration/operations-test.ts` — merge and override semantics, the implied base operations, marker shapes under `JSON.stringify`, every guard, and the type-level assertions for the `params` typing.

## Key decisions and non-obvious mechanics

- **`getOperations` returns every operation pertinent to the def**: the base operations its def type implies — all six for a card def, `read` for a file def (whose metadata is content-derived and read-only), none for a field def (whose instances have no URL) — merged with the author's declarations, where a declaration takes the place of the base operation it names. A synthesized entry is the bare `{ base }`, because the base operations are the executors and what a plain `create` or `query` needs travels with the invocation rather than the declaration. `getDeclaredOperations` is the authored-only view, and the one to lower from: its entries all went through the decorator, so a clause the base requires is present.
- **A base operation's name is the verb; its `base` is what carries the verb out.** A declaration named after a base operation specializes that behavior when it names the same `base` — a card's own `read` projection or `update` validation — and rebinds the verb when it names another: a `delete` declared on `transform` is a soft delete, so every caller asking that card to delete itself archives it instead. A dispatcher therefore reads name and `base` separately rather than inferring one from the other.
- **Declarations live on the class under a symbol, per class**, merged base-most-first up the constructor chain so a subclass overrides inherited names wholesale — the same shape as `getScreenshots`. Both readers return a record with **no prototype**: an operation is dispatched by a name that arrived over the wire, and a record backed by `Object.prototype` answers `toString`, `constructor` and `__proto__` with something that is not an operation.
- **The plain-data invariant is enforced, not assumed.** A declaration reaches the realm as JSON in a definition-cache entry, so the walk refuses anything that would not survive the trip: a function, `undefined`, a symbol, a bigint, a non-finite number, a class instance, a cycle. A def class is legal only where the position names a type — the `of` a create targets, a filter's `on` or `type` at any nesting depth, and the `on` a sort entry roots its path in — and only a card or file class, since a field has no type row of its own to name. That precision is what stops a thunk being read as a *value* under `eq`, where it would lower to nothing and leave a saved search matching every card instead of one.
- **A declared query is also checked against the query grammar's own definition.** The placement rule above encodes where the realm's filter grammar puts a type, which means it has to stay in step with a grammar defined elsewhere. So the query is handed to `assertQuery` — that grammar's single definition — with every def class swapped for a sentinel that reads as a code ref where a type belongs and as a function everywhere else, and the realm re-checks both the placement and the rest of the shape. A query the realm would refuse is refused at class-definition time rather than at invocation. The second opinion is skipped for a query carrying a typed reference, since a reference stands in for a value the realm types concretely — a `matches` string, an `in` array — and only lowering resolves it.
- **`QueryDeclaration` is the realm's query narrowed to what a saved search states**: `filter`, `sort`, a `queryString` a payload may supply, `realms` as the fan-out list, and offset paging — `size` with a 0-based `number`. There is no cursor to declare, since the index generation a request is pinned to is the server's to mint. `realm` in the singular is left out because the fan-out list is the scope; `asData` and `fields` are left out because a query operation answers with entry rows, a different response shape than a data query.
- **Validation happens at class-definition time**: the target (a `BaseDef` subclass, never a `FieldDef`), the name (a string that does not already resolve on the class, unless it names an inherited operation), and the declaration — a base the def type actually carries, read from the same list `getOperations` synthesizes so the two cannot drift; only the keys that base can express; a well-formed `params` schema; and declarative clauses or a raw program. `of` names the type rather than the work, so it stands alongside a program rather than competing with it.
- **A static-property decorator has to return a descriptor carrying `value`.** With an `initializer` left in place, the decorator transform defers the field to instance construction — where a static never runs — and the property never appears on the class.
- **The `bxl` tag takes no substitutions.** `params()`, `actor()` and `instance()` are BXL builtins that read the operation context, so a program reads the payload and the actor directly; splicing values into program text would be a second, unchecked path into it.
- **Typing follows the `satisfies OperationDeclaration` idiom**, which type-checks the declaration in place and keeps the literal types `OperationsOf` and `ParamsOf` read. Overriding an inherited operation needs the inherited one annotated `: OperationDeclaration`, since TypeScript requires a subclass's static to stay assignable to what it shadows — and that annotation costs the annotated name its payload type, so it is worth writing only where a subclass really will reshape the operation.
- **The module is plain TypeScript with no template**, so it lands as `operations.ts` alongside its non-component siblings (`searchable.ts`, `field-support.ts`); the `@cardstack/base/operations` import specifier is unaffected by the extension.

author: fruppel
body:
### 1. Why is this change necessary?

`sync.yml` force-pushes trunk to `shopware/shopware-private`, so this workflow is mirrored there and triggers on issues closed in the private repo. Those runs always fail, because the octo-sts identity `ShopwareLinkClosingPR` only trusts `repo:shopware/shopware:ref:refs/heads/trunk` ([example run](https://github.com/shopware/shopware-private/actions/runs/34209436454)).

### 2. What does this change do, exactly?

Guards the `link_pr` job with `if: github.repository == 'shopware/shopware'`, like the other trunk-only workflows. `linkClosingPR()` looks the issue number up in `shopware/shopware` regardless of the triggering repository, so private-repo runs would be wrong even with a working token.

The mirror is invisible from this repo, so a second commit documents it in `.github/AGENTS.md` (identity allows `(-private)?` vs. `github.repository` guard) and adds the incident and a review question to `coding-guidelines/core/ci-workflows.md`. A lint rule cannot cover it: the subject patterns live in `shopware/.github`.

### 3. Describe each step to reproduce the issue or behaviour.

Close an issue in `shopware/shopware-private`: the job fails at `shopware/octo-sts-action` with `Failed to get a token`. With this change it is skipped there and unchanged in `shopware/shopware`.

### 4. Please link to the relevant issues (if any).

None.

### 5. Checklist

- [ ] I have written tests and verified that they fail without my change
- [ ] I have updated developer-facing release notes if this change is **relevant** for external developers
- [x] I have written or adjusted the documentation and agent skills according to my changes
- [x] This change has comments for package types, values, functions, and non-obvious lines of code
- [x] I have read the contribution requirements and fulfilled them

Agent results could be delayed by earlier workers, and a worker failure could prevent sibling results from being saved. This change persists each completed agent turn independently, drains remaining completions before reporting errors, and unregisters executions after result collection.

## Summary

Implements nested column projection pushdown in `ProjectionPushdownUtil` for the `yosegi-2.0_spark-3.2` branch (backporting the fix merged in #66).

When a Spark query only accesses a subset of leaf fields inside a `StructType`, the connector now pushes down the full path (e.g. `[["parent_a","leaf_1"],["parent_b","leaf_2"]]`) instead of just the top-level struct names (`[["parent_a"],["parent_b"]]`).

## Background & Problem

The Yosegi core reader (`PushdownSupportedBlockReader` / `ColumnBinaryTree`) already supports child-column filtering and IO skipping via nested paths. However, `ProjectionPushdownUtil.createProjectionPushdownJson` previously emitted top-level field names only.

As a result, selecting a few leaf fields out of a wide struct still forced the reader to decompress and read every unrequested child column inside that struct, causing unnecessary disk IO whenever a query pruned a nested schema down to a handful of leaves.

## End-to-End Spark SQL Impact

Spark SQL's Catalyst optimizer already performs nested schema pruning (via `spark.sql.optimizer.nestedSchemaPruning.enabled=true`, default in Spark 3.x) and passes the pruned `requiredSchema` to the file format reader.

Because the limitation was purely the translation gap in `ProjectionPushdownUtil`, fixing `yosegi-spark` enables all standard Spark SQL queries (`SELECT parent_a.leaf_1 FROM table`, DataFrame `df.select("parent_a.leaf_1")`, etc.) to automatically and transparently benefit from leaf-level IO skipping without requiring any modifications to Spark engine binaries or user query code.

## Solution

1. **Recursive struct traversal** — `ProjectionPushdownUtil` now recursively walks nested `StructType` fields and generates full leaf paths.
2. **Special-type handling** — path recursion terminates at `ArrayType`, `MapType`, primitive types, and empty `StructType`s.
3. **JSON serialization** — uses Jackson `ObjectMapper` for correct quoting/escaping of path segments.
4. **Null safety** — added null guards in `SparkParserFactory`, `SparkStructParser`, and `SparkMapParser`.

## Tests & Verification

- **Unit tests** (`ProjectionPushdownUtilTest`): flat, 2-level, 3-level deeply-nested structs, empty structs, struct containing Array/Map, and special-character escaping.
- **Integration test** (`NestedProjectionPushdownTest`): end-to-end correctness and value parity between unpruned and pruned reads.
- **IO regression test** (`PrunedReadBytesBenchTest`): synthetic benchmark with 60k rows containing one "heavy" struct (6 string fields) and one "light" struct (2 fields):
  - Full read: `46.4 MB` (100.9% of file)
  - Pruned to light struct only: `378 KB` (0.8% of file — **~99% IO reduction**)
  - Pruned to 1 heavy + 1 light field: `7.9 MB` (17.2% of file)
- Full test suite passes (`mvn clean test`, JDK 8, 854 tests passed).

author: sauersml
body:
### Motivation
- The shipped manifold-SAE example fails at the first ladder rung because the terminal polish phase accepts only residual-norm decreases, not penalized-objective decreases, producing a refine/polish limit cycle that never converges.
- At indefinite exact-stationarity Hessians a residual-minimising step can block an actual objective descent, so the acceptance currency must be the penalized objective while keeping the KKT residual as the convergence certificate.
- The change targets the algorithmic mechanism (acceptance currency) rather than tuning or time/budget workarounds so the solver can take scientifically correct descent steps and avoid the measured crawl.

### Description
- Add `shifted_objective_descent_step` to `ExactHessianSpectralBlock` (in `crates/gam-sae/src/manifold/construction_exact_hessian.rs`) which forms an objective-directed step by shifting negative eigenvalues so that retained spectral components produce an objective-descent direction. 
- In the terminal polish (`construction_quasi_laplace.rs`) attempt the shifted exact-Hessian objective step first and globalize it with the existing Armijo/backtracking machinery (`initial_step=1.0`), accepting a genuine objective decrease while leaving the residual-based gate as the convergence certificate. 
- Pin the behavior with a unit/regression test `indefinite_exact_hessian_step_is_objective_descent_2267` in `crates/gam-sae/src/manifold/construction_tests.rs` which asserts the shifted step descends the penalized objective on an indefinite spectrum and add the minimal `opt` imports needed for the line-search call. 

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` and code-style diffs locally which reported no lint diffs from the edits. (`git diff --check` returned clean.)
- Ran `cargo check -p gam-sae` which reached the `gam-sae` crate but failed on pre-existing `-D warnings` diagnostics (unused methods flagged as dead code: `apply_exact_hessian_minus_b` / `apply_exact_hessian_matrix_free`, and `decoder_prior_beta_hvp_pair`), so the new test could not be executed in this environment. (Outcome: compilation reached crate, then failed due to those diagnostics.)
- Attempted the focused test run `cargo test -p gam-sae indefinite_exact_hessian_step_is_objective_descent_2267 -- --exact` but it could not run because `cargo check`/build failed on the unrelated deny-warnings baseline; an uncapped workspace build (`cargo build --workspace --all-targets`) was also started but could not be completed inside the interactive sandbox window. (Outcome: test not executed; follow-up needed once baseline diagnostics are cleared.)

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Owned plugin inspections currently combine execution revocation and physical registration cleanup. That cannot represent a borrower that still needs a registration's native resources after inspection authority ends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate registration resource claims from the inspection view. The existing inspection owns an initial claim; an internal borrower can retain native backing without extending the inspection's authority. This three-file kernel is another slice of #140674 and serves the existing inspection path immediately.

Inspection release still revokes scoped signals synchronously and returns the same Promise to reentrant callers. Claims drop in release-call order, so a final borrower released in the same turn or from an abort listener correctly owns physical cleanup and its failures. Construction reports failed-registration rollback; the last claim disposes successful registrations. Mixed errors retain registration order and independent disposal runs in parallel.

## User Impact

Existing inspection behavior is preserved. Subsequent owner migrations can keep resources alive for their actual users while revoked callbacks remain fenced. Cached and prepared registry disposal are not activated by this kernel.

## Evidence

Fourteen unchanged baseline cases pass. Independent review found a same-turn release-order bug in the first candidate; two native reproductions failed there and pass with the correction. All 22 current lifecycle/native cases, the full canonical changed gate, a fresh full build, and the corrected Codex review pass.

Four isolated built plugins doctor cases cover healthy human/JSON output, registration rollback, and disposal failure with one JSON result. They verify native SQLite closure and preserved data. Retained-claim behavior is exercised with native SQLite in the source suite; this PR does not claim compiled borrowing or Gateway lifecycle coverage. Source, index, and built artifacts stayed unchanged through validation, and all owned processes joined.

author: malinfossum
body:
A fresh install lands on the Focus surface with `activeTab` set to `today`, so the first thing anyone sees is **"Nothing due today."** It is accurate and it teaches nothing. This replaces it, when the database is genuinely empty, with a line that says what the app is for.

> Sometimes all it takes is a spark. Capture the first thing on your mind — it lands in Focus until you decide where it goes.

## Why it names Focus

Capture defaults to the Focus notepad with no date, so the first task captured from Today does not land on Today. I verified this in the browser: after one capture the Focus count read 1 and Today still read 0, "Nothing due today." Without that second clause a new user's first action looks like it did nothing.

The copy carries no directional word for the capture bar. Decision D9 pins the bar to the bottom on phones and the top from 768px up, so "below" and "above" are each wrong on one of them.

## How the trigger works

Derived from state — `state.tasks.length === 0` — not persisted. No `seen` flag, no settings field, no migration on existing databases. An app with nothing in it reads the same whether that is a first run or one emptied back out, and a user with a full app and a clear day still gets the terse line.

`renderWelcome` returns `isEmpty: true` so `renderPanel` still applies `tabindex="0"`. The welcome is the only thing on screen on a first run; without that the whole first paint is unreachable from the keyboard.

## Verified

Run on port 4173, a separate origin from the dev server, so this was a genuinely empty database rather than my working one.

- Welcome renders on Today when the app is empty
- Tomorrow, Starred and Focus keep their own copy — no leak
- Once one task exists the welcome stops and Today falls back to "Nothing due today."
- Panel carries `tabindex="0"` and takes focus
- Light theme at 375px: three lines, no horizontal scroll

258 tests passing, 63 files Biome-clean, build green. Bundle 70.46 → 70.68 kB (gzip 20.02 → 20.09).

No new CSS and no new element — the welcome reuses the existing `.empty` paragraph. Views have no unit coverage in this project by design, so this was verified in the browser.

## Also in here

The README hero opened on adjectives; it now opens on the idea the name is built on and says what the app does. "zero bloat" gives way to "no account, no paywall" — concrete, and already true elsewhere in the file. The test count under Tech still read 247 and is now 258.

One stale comment fixed: the note above `EMPTY_STATE` claimed Focus was the first tab a new user sees. It is Today.

## Still owed, unchanged by this PR

A real-device pass. Every check here was desktop Chromium at a resized viewport. A real Return on the capture bar still creates nothing through CDP — I reproduced that again and used `form.requestSubmit()` to exercise the real handler — so the empty-database Enter path remains unproven on hardware.

author: mec07
body:
Replaces the `WOP` skill with `WIP`: same core idea — cross-reference your pull requests against your tickets and flag anything stale or inconsistent — but it works for anyone and covers three sources instead of two.

`WOP` was inherited from someone else's setup and only ever worked for them. It hardcoded a Google Drive Obsidian vault path, a single GitHub repo, their `OPEN_LOOPS.md`, a `DEV-` Jira prefix, and referred to them by name throughout.

## Portable by construction

No identity, organisation, repository, project or ticket prefix appears anywhere in the skill.

| Value | Resolved from |
|---|---|
| GitHub user | `@me` |
| GitHub repos | none — `gh search prs` spans every repo you can see |
| Azure user | `az account show` |
| Azure org/project | `az devops configure` defaults |
| Jira user | `currentUser()` |
| Jira projects | `getVisibleJiraProjects` |

## What changed

- GitHub is no longer restricted to one repository; Azure DevOps added as a peer source
- Jira matched on status *category* rather than project-specific status names
- Each source probed independently — a missing tool skips its own section instead of aborting
- No stored state: the services track the work, the skill queries live and renders. The summary file is overwritten each run and lists open items only, so it cannot grow.
- `SKILL.md` is 40 lines: what the skill is, a routing table, and pointers. Detail lives in the files that execute it.

## Triage

The first live run surfaced 21 open PRs with no activity for between 57 and 2414 days, which a summary alone does nothing about. `Workflows/Triage.md` asks about each one older than 28 days with a multi-choice question and acts on the answer: action today, ignore for a week, waiting for a response, close it, or free text.

Stale PRs are grouped first — eleven README PRs opened the same day in the same repo are one decision, and asking eleven times is how triage stops being run.

Two answers mean "do not ask me again yet", which no service records, so they need a file. `Reference/Deferrals.md` specifies it. Every entry refers to a currently-open PR; entries leave when their PR is merged or closed. Repeat snoozes back off — 7, 14, 30, 90, then 180 days — because a fixed week means being asked weekly about work being deliberately ignored. No PR is ever closed without being named by URL and confirmed.

## Details that only showed up against live data

Every documented command was run against real accounts before being written down.

- `gh search prs --json` does not expose `reviewDecision`, `statusCheckRollup` or `mergeable`, so per-PR detail needs a second `gh pr view` pass
- Ticket keys are validated against the Jira **project list**. Filtering by prefixes seen in the assigned-ticket query would hide any PR citing a project you have no open ticket in
- Keys absent from the open set are resolved rather than discarded, so a done ticket with an open PR, or a PR against someone else's ticket, surfaces as a flag
- `az repos pr list` needs `--detect false`, or it warns whenever the skill runs outside an Azure checkout
- Date arithmetic falls back from GNU to BSD `date`
- The per-PR fetch is a script file driven by `xargs`; inlining it fails at a few dozen URLs with "command line cannot be assembled, too long"

## Verification

- GitHub: 28 open PRs across 4 distinct repositories; all 8 `--json` fields validated
- Azure DevOps: 8 active PRs; all 9 documented fields present on real payloads
- Jira: `statusCategory != Done` succeeded; project list returned 13 projects
- Ticket regex rejects `UTF-8`, `SHA-256`, `RFC-2119`
- `./install.sh --check` exits 0; the old `WOP` install was removed
- `install.test.sh`: 27 run, 0 failed

author: jake-bliss
body:
## The problem

The stale reaper drops any session that goes 30 minutes without a hook event (`server/state.ts`, `reapStale`). Its escape hatch is `sessionAliveCheck`, backed by `SessionRegistryWatcher`, which reads `~/.claude/sessions` **on the machine the server runs on** (`server/session-registry.ts:5`).

That is the agents' machine only when the server is local. On a hosted server the directory does not exist, `poll()` returns early, the cache stays empty, `isSessionAlive()` is always false — and an idle-but-open session is indistinguishable from a finished one. A session parked on a question, or blocked behind a long build that fires no hooks, vanishes while its terminal is still up.

Observed on a Render deployment: 6 live sessions on one machine, 3 avatars on screen.

## The fix

Machines push the same signal instead of the server reading it.

- **`POST /api/registry/heartbeat`** — `{ session_ids, username }`. Requires an installation credential (401 otherwise) and secure transport. Unlike `/api/hooks` an unsigned report is refused: a hook carries work, while a report's only effect is keeping a session on screen, and session ids are public in `/api/state`.
- **`RemoteSessionRegistry`** (`server/remote-registry.ts`) holds a reported id for 90s, filed per installation. Sparing a session does **not** touch `lastEventAt`, so when reports stop the session goes with the next sweep rather than getting a fresh 30-minute window.
- **`agent-factory heartbeat`** reads the local registry and reports every 30s on a fixed-rate ticker. `heartbeat install` runs it under launchd / `systemd --user`; `agent-factory uninstall` takes it back down.

Nothing changes for a server running on the same machine as its agents.

## What bounds it

**Admission is the only bound**: a report is held only for a session already in world state whose `ownerId` equals the reporter's. It fails closed. There is deliberately no capacity limit of its own — a capacity is a scarce resource, credentials are self-minted, and refusing a real machine's report is precisely how a live session gets reaped. Entries are dropped as soon as their session leaves the world, so what is held tracks the world rather than recent throughput.

Consequences worth stating:

- Owned sessions can only be held open by their own installation; ids read from world state cannot pin or drop someone else's agent.
- A restart spares restored sessions for one TTL, since the registry comes back empty and the first sweep lands before any reporter is sure to have checked in.
- The client validates the server address before sending — HTTPS, or HTTP only for loopback — and does not follow redirects, so the credential cannot cross plaintext or be forwarded.
- Batches are split at the server's 500-id read limit rather than truncated by the far end, and servers are reported to concurrently so one unreachable server cannot stretch another's cadence toward expiry.
- Dead pids in the local registry are skipped; sessions are grouped by the server *their own directory* resolves to, so repository overrides keep holding.

## Tests

`tests/remote-registry.test.ts`, `tests/hook-ownership.test.ts`, `cli/cmd/heartbeat_test.go`, `cli/internal/sessions/sessions_test.go` — TTL and expiry, per-installation isolation (including an attempted overwrite of another installation's entry), admission and orphan release, the restart warm-up wired exactly as `index.ts` wires it, unsigned/wrong-owner/unknown-id rejection at the route, batch splitting, concurrent reporting via a two-server barrier, failure aggregation, the plaintext and redirect credential boundaries, interval validation, and dead-pid filtering.

The behavioural tests were checked by reverting each fix and confirming the matching test fails by name.

`pnpm test` (1028), `pnpm build`, `go test ./...`, `go build ./...` all green. Verified end-to-end against a local server: 3 registry files (one with a dead pid) → `reported 2 session(s)`, server logged `[heartbeat] user=Jake sessions=2`.

## Review

Nine adversarial passes with an independent model (Codex), 23 findings, all accepted and fixed, converging to an explicit approve. Three of the findings were defects introduced by fixes to earlier findings — an eviction rule, a capacity cap, and a credential-transport gap — which is why the design ended up smaller than it started.

author: mostafa
body:
## Summary

hamba/avro is archived and unmaintained. This PR swaps it for [confluent-avro-go](https://github.com/confluentinc/confluent-avro-go) (v2.32.0), Confluent's maintained fork that continues the hamba v2 line and powers confluent-kafka-go's own Schema Registry Avro serde — the same Kafka client library xk6-kafka ships, so our wire behavior stays aligned with Confluent's serde by construction.

## Due diligence: fork vs hamba v2.31.0 (our pinned version)

File-by-file diff of the two modules:

| File | Delta |
| --- | --- |
| `codec_union.go`, `resolver.go`, `config.go`, `decoder.go`, `encoder.go` | **byte-identical** — every behavior we depend on is preserved |
| `schema.go` | import-path rename only |
| `reader.go` | endianness-safety fix (unsafe pointer cast → `binary.LittleEndian`) |
| rest | test import renames, CI/metadata |

Our Avro test suite encodes the full behavioral contract (wrapped union maps, `int.date` discriminators, nullable-union bare slices, resolver decode envelopes, logical types, bytes/fixed conversion) and passes unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

[twmb/avro](https://github.com/twmb/avro) (v1.9.0, actively maintained): a modern rewrite with schema evolution (`Resolve`/`CheckCompatibility`), OCF, single-object encoding, schema-aware JSON, and native `float64`→`int32` coercion that could eventually replace our `convertFloat64ToIntForIntegerFields` layer. However, it has a completely different API (`SchemaNode` introspection, different union defaults and branch naming), so adopting it means rewriting and re-verifying the entire conversion layer for features xk6-kafka does not use today. It also started in Jan 2026 with a single maintainer, whereas the fork is battle-tested hamba code under corporate maintenance.

## Changes

- `go.mod`: `github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0` → `github.com/confluentinc/confluent-avro-go/v2 v2.32.0`
- Import path swap in `avro.go`, `schema_registry.go` and the three Avro test files (package name is `avro` in both — no code changes)
- Doc/comment reference updates (README, schema-registry.md, v2.2.0-subcommand.md, complex-schema script)

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, gofmt/goimports clean, `golangci-lint run`: 0 issues
- Full `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./... -race` against a live Kafka + Schema Registry: pass

No behavior changes; not a breaking change.

author: aline-senai
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses two issues: (1) orphaned sprint plannings and reviews that became invisible after the team-based split, and (2) lack of real-time updates when multiple users collaborate on the same board.

## Key Changes

**Backend - Data Migration:**
- Added Alembic migration `b3c6d8e0f1a2` to backfill `grupo_id` for orphaned planning/review records
  - Identifies records with `NULL grupo_id` (created before the team-based split)
  - Distributes each orphaned record across all teams in the class: the first team inherits the original record, subsequent teams receive copies with identical content
  - Deletes orphaned records if their associated class has no teams
  - Makes `grupo_id` non-nullable in both `sprint_plannings` and `sprint_reviews` tables

**Backend - Model Updates:**
- Changed `grupo_id` column from `nullable=True` to `nullable=False` in `SprintPlanning` and `SprintReview` models to enforce data integrity

**Frontend - Board Synchronization:**
- Extracted board data fetching logic into a new `syncBoard()` function for reusability
- Added background polling that syncs board state every 15 seconds
- Polling runs silently (errors don't interrupt the session) to ensure real-time visibility of changes made by other users (moving cards, editing activities, creating plannings/reviews)
- Refactored `refreshAll()` to use the new `syncBoard()` function

## Implementation Details
- The migration preserves all planning/review content by duplicating records rather than aggregating data
- Downgrade path is intentionally one-way: duplicated records are not removed to avoid data loss
- Frontend polling uses a 15-second interval to balance responsiveness with server load
- Silent error handling in polling prevents disrupting the user session on transient failures

author: cortejojicoy
body:
Implements docs/PLAN.md. Turns the package from "pluggable auth + sidebar" into a config-driven admin toolkit, and fixes four defects that were live in the published 0.1.8.

Shipping bugs in 0.1.8 (all typechecked cleanly, all reached the registry):

- exports pointed `import` at dist/*.mjs, which tsup never emitted, so the package could not be imported at all
- "use client" was stripped from the client bundles by tsup's treeshake pass, breaking every App Router build
- middleware's passthrough returned an empty 200, blanking every page
- tsconfig set jsx:"preserve", so esbuild emitted React.createElement with no React import — 53 call sites, every one throwing at runtime

Found by building and running the new example app:

- each client entry bundled its own copy of the React contexts, so the provider and its consumers were different contexts
- verifyJWT failed in the edge runtime, which rejects a cross-realm ArrayBuffer
- DataStore mutated cache entries in place, so useSyncExternalStore never re-rendered and every CRUD hook stayed loading forever

Added:

- /data — DataProvider + createRestDataProvider: every operation is an endpoint you declare, with bidirectional wire mapping and CRUD hooks over a dependency-free query cache
- /access — catalog/entitlement/permission as separate gates, none|view|full levels, wildcards, hierarchy, deny rules, and server gates that refuse
- /ui — launcher panel and sidebar panel, generated resource screens, and a stylesheet that actually ships
- admin-kit CLI — init scaffolding, plus docs generated from your own config with --check for CI
- serializable config (string icon keys), server-only config for secrets, HttpOnly cookie sessions by default
- 194 tests, an eslint config, examples/app-router built in CI, and `pnpm verify` as the publish gate

Release tooling (tool/, adapted from trackbnb-flutter):

- tool/version.py — staged version scheme (alpha < beta < rc < lts, then promote) with git tags as the source of truth and package.json derived from them; pre-releases publish under their own npm dist-tag
- tool/release.sh — guarded sequence: verify, promote CHANGELOG, sync, commit, tag, push
- CI publishes only from a pushed tag. The auto-bump-on-push job is removed: it cannot coexist with tag-driven versioning, and it is how 0.1.8 reached npm with no tag pointing at it

author: jacksonmafra-umain
body:
## Summary

Generates `mach_exc_server` from the SDK's `mach_exc.defs` (the 64-bit variant `MACH_EXCEPTION_CODES` and arm64 need, not `exc.defs`) and wires it into a `machbug_mig` static library target that `MachBug_tests` links.

- `src/cross/MachBug/cmake/MachBugMig.cmake`: runs `mig` with `-server`/`-sheader`, redirecting the client-side `-user`/`-header` outputs to `/dev/null` — a debugger only ever receives exception messages, so those outputs would be generated and never linked. Depends on both the `.defs` file and the `mig` binary so an Xcode update that changes what `mig` emits from the same `.defs` file is still noticed.
- `src/cross/MachBug/cmake/MachBugMigStubs.c`: `mach_exc.defs` declares three routines, so the generated dispatch table always references three `catch_mach_exception_raise*` symbols. `catch_mach_exception_raise` and `catch_mach_exception_raise_state` are permanent no-op stubs (this debugger only uses the state-identity variant). `catch_mach_exception_raise_state_identity` is a *weak* stub so `machbug_mig` links and is testable now; the real implementation (Task 4) overrides it with a strong definition, no duplicate-symbol conflict.
- `src/cross/MachBug/tests/mig_exception_server.cpp` + `tests/cmake.toml`: a compile-level test asserting `mach_exc_server` links and that the exception payload is the 64-bit shape.

## Verified

- Failing state reproduced first: `fatal error: 'mach_exc.h' file not found`.
- After wiring: `MachBug_tests` builds and all 9 test cases (21 assertions) pass.
- Confirmed the generated header is the 64-bit variant: `grep -c 'mach_exception_data_t\|MACH_EXCEPTION_CODES' .../mig/mach_exc.h` → 3, and the request/reply structs carry `int64_t code[2]`, not `exc.defs`' `integer_t code[2]`.
- All six verification scripts green: `check-toolchain.sh`, `verify-vendor.sh`, `check-credits.sh`, `check-bundles.sh`, `smoke-launch.sh`, `check-build-warnings.sh`.

## tests/cmake.toml change

Three lines: added `mig_exception_server.cpp` to `sources`, added `include-before = ["../cmake/MachBugMig.cmake"]`, added `machbug_mig` to `link-libraries`.

## Design notes

- **User stub**: dropped. `mig`'s client-side routines (`mach_exception_raise` etc.) are for a caller sending an exception message; this debugger only ever receives them. Redirecting `-user`/`-header` to `/dev/null` avoids generating and never linking that code, while still satisfying `mig`, which otherwise always writes a default-named user file even if `-user` is omitted entirely.
- **SDK path staleness**: `xcrun --show-sdk-path` resolves once at configure time and is baked into the generated build files. A reconfigured tree picks up a new SDK; one that isn't reconfigured after an in-place Xcode update keeps using the old path — if that path still exists, the `DEPENDS` on `mach_exc.defs`' mtime (and now also on the `mig` binary's mtime) still catches a changed file and regenerates. Only a *removed* SDK path (a major Xcode bump) fails loudly rather than regenerating; there's no silent-stale-and-successful case, but it isn't self-healing either — a `cmake --fresh` is needed after a major Xcode version change. Documented in `MachBugMig.cmake`.

Closes #54

author: alexisjamet
body:
When the user comes back from an MCP provider's consent screen and Auth0 cannot silently restore the session (expired or revoked refresh token, cleared storage), `ProtectedRoute` redirects to Auth0 login without a `returnTo`. Auth0 sends the user back to the origin, `HomeRoute` navigates to onboarding, and the single-use `code` and `state` are lost with no error shown. The pending context also stays in localStorage for a later callback to pick up.

`ProtectedRoute` now passes `appState: { returnTo: pathname + search }` to `loginWithRedirect`, and `Auth0Provider` gets an `onRedirectCallback` that navigates back to it. Since the provider sits above `RouterProvider`, `Router.tsx` exposes the single data router instance and the callback uses `router.navigate(returnTo, { replace: true, flushSync: true })`, so the location commits before the SDK flips `isAuthenticated` and `HomeRoute` cannot race it to onboarding. A small `sanitizeReturnTo` helper accepts only same-origin relative paths (rejects `//host`, `/\host`, absolute URLs, control characters); anything else falls back to the SDK's default `history.replaceState`.

Testing: `npm run biome:check`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npx vitest run` in apps/web all pass (18 files, 152 tests, including 8 new tests for `buildReturnTo` and `sanitizeReturnTo`).

Addresses https://github.com/bayesimpact/bayes-platform/pull/710#discussion_r3915044385

author: jeong-sik
body:
Sangokushi II's “create D disk” operation stopped in its `DISK I/O ERROR` loop. Replaying the saved prompt with disk-call tracing confirms the first request is BDOS `16h` (create file), which returned unsupported. Add FCB file creation and `26h` random block writes backed by real FAT12 disk-image bytes, so game-created data survives disk swaps and emulator checkpoints.

The FAT writer validates geometry, mirrored tables, root allocation ownership, duplicate targets and file-size bounds before publishing replacement bytes. Existing nonzero-extent creates preserve file contents, concurrent FCB writers use current disk bytes, and zero-count writes resize the file. Directory end markers and unrelated allocation remain intact. Replay gains opt-in disk-call tracing to reproduce compatibility failures after restoration.

Synthetic CPU tests exercise create/write/close/reopen/read, checkpoint continuation, truncation, two writers and malformed media. Independent FAT fixtures cover fragmentation, nibble packing, mirror agreement, full/read-only/corrupt media, crosslinks and directory-marker preservation. No local Dune builds; Linux/macOS CI supplies compiled runners for private game verification.

Contract: [MSX-DOS function specification, FMAKE and WRBLK](https://map.grauw.nl/resources/dos2_functioncalls.php). Real game verification and later B/C campaign media are separate from synthetic coverage; a completed campaign or ending is not claimed.

## Summary

- add a provider-agnostic, bounded ReAct-style `READ_ONLY_RESEARCH` agent
- expose five typed read-only tools over canonical instruments, exact events, existing market features, portfolio context, and canonical research health
- validate typed `BUY` / `HOLD` / `SELL` / `AVOID` proposals against universe, weight, confidence, duplicate, freshness, and critical-health gates
- persist an immutable per-run audit trail with prompt/model IDs, inputs and hashes, tool calls and result hashes, raw/parsed output, validation, final proposals, and safety counters
- add deterministic fake-model coverage and a reproducible committed sample artifact

## Safety

```text
AGENT_MODE=READ_ONLY_RESEARCH
AGENT_RESEARCH_CAPABILITY_READY=YES
BROKER_MUTATIONS=0
REAL_ORDERS_SENT=0
PAPER_ORDERS_SENT=0
PORTFOLIO_MUTATIONS=0
LIVE_OUTCOMES_READ=0
```

author: copilot
body:
### What are you trying to accomplish?

Large pnpm workspaces can spend most of Dependabot’s job budget repeatedly running root-level exact-version `pnpm update --lockfile-only` checks during version discovery. This narrows those checks to updates that can affect peer compatibility or pnpm trust policy enforcement.

### Anything you want to highlight for special attention from reviewers?

- **Skip path**
  - Return the latest allowable version without invoking pnpm when candidate metadata has no `peerDependencies` and current manifests/lockfiles do not list the dependency as a peer.

- **Safety guards**
  - Keep existing pnpm checks when peer relationships are present.
  - Keep existing pnpm checks when `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` is configured.
  - Fail closed on parse issues by falling back to the existing pnpm subprocess path.

- **Coverage**
  - Added focused `VersionResolver` specs for both the skip path and the peer-involved pnpm path.

### How will you know you've accomplished your goal?

Version discovery avoids repeated expensive pnpm root checks for dependencies with no peer dependency relationship, while preserving pnpm validation for peer-sensitive and trust-policy-sensitive updates.
