## Summary
- capture an authoritative PostgreSQL target LSN with the locked source-image inventory snapshot
- commit a bounded singleton-table WAL fence while source mutations remain gated
- fail closed until `pg_stat_archiver` confirms the fence WAL is externally archived
- record target LSN, audit target time, fence WAL, archive time, and archive-timeout precondition in recovery manifests
- add the fence table through an owner-safe Alembic migration compatible with Vault dynamic roles
- make CNPG `targetLSN` the authoritative recovery instruction

Closes #1238.

## Incident evidence

The first real latest recovery set successfully published 27.1 GB directly to Azure, but CNPG could not reach its wall-clock target on an idle database:

> recovery ended before configured recovery target was reached

Archived WAL ended at the last completed transaction around 05:56 UTC while the inventory target was 07:46 UTC. This change writes and confirms a later WAL fence before publication so the earlier inventory LSN is recoverable.

#### Test plan
- [x] 137 backup tests
- [x] 49 migration/bootstrap helper tests
- [x] Python compilation and Black
- [x] Prettier documentation checks
- [x] Alembic reports one head: `0029_backup_wal_fence`
- [x] Helm lint, kubeconform, and chart regression checks
- [x] live PG17 syntax check for locked inventory and singleton-table UPDATE using a temporary rolled-back table
- [x] live latest reports `archive_timeout=300`, below the 600-second fence timeout
- [ ] deploy RC to latest and apply migration
- [ ] publish a fenced latest recovery set
- [ ] restore CNPG to manifest `target_lsn`
- [ ] restore source files to a fresh PVC and compare manifest checksums/inventory

## Safety
- production still does not invoke `pg_dump`
- the source inventory transaction performs no writes and holds a SHARE lock only through its COPY
- the only production write is an UPDATE to one internal singleton fence row
- publication fails without archive/sidecar/success marker if the fence cannot be confirmed archived
- stable promotion remains blocked on the latest restore canary

## Summary
- Fix short login session on iPhone Home Screen PWA
- Improve navigation performance (500-3000ms delays)

## Changes

### Session Persistence (iOS PWA Fix)
- **`src/lib/supabase.ts`**: Added `persistSession: true`, `autoRefreshToken: true`, `detectSessionInUrl: true` to Supabase client config
- **`src/middleware.ts`**: Added `secure: true`, `sameSite: "none"`, `httpOnly: false`, `path: "/"` to all auth cookies
- **`src/pages/login.astro`**: Same cookie attributes for login session cookies
- **`src/pages/api/auth/logout.ts`**: Same cookie attributes for logout cookies

### Performance Improvements
- **`src/components/MealPlanningWizard.tsx`**: Batched parallel queries for recipes and source plan using `Promise.all()` instead of sequential fetches

## Why This Works

### iOS PWA Session Issue
iOS Safari requires cookies to have `SameSite=None` and `Secure` attributes to persist in PWAs. Without these, cookies are cleared when the PWA is closed. The Supabase client also needs persistence enabled to use refresh tokens.

### Navigation Slowness
The MealPlanningWizard was making sequential Supabase calls. Batching them reduces the time from ~2 round trips to 1, cutting load time significantly.

## Testing
- Test login on iPhone Home Screen PWA - session should persist after closing/reopening
- Test navigation in MealPlanningWizard - should feel noticeably faster
- Verify no regressions in auth flow

**Note**: Requires HTTPS (already configured for maten.hanshenrik.com). No Supabase paid tier required.

author: kartikeya-27
body:
> Stacked on #308 — the FlexiQ lab clock fix. This PR's new CI job runs the browser suite, and that suite is only reliable with #308 in. Merge #308 first; GitHub will retarget this one to `main` automatically.

Adds performance measurement to the monorepo in three layers, because no single one of them is trustworthy on its own.

### Byte budgets — these fail the build

Each app gets a `lighthouserc.js` declaring transfer-size ceilings for scripts, fonts and the page total, plus a DOM-node ceiling. The numbers came from measuring each app and adding roughly 20% of headroom. They were identical across all three runs of every app, which is what makes them safe to gate on.

| App | script | total | font | DOM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | 153,110 → 190,000 | 348,792 → 420,000 | 126,692 → 140,000 | 587 → 900 |
| docs | 146,215 → 180,000 | 313,015 → 380,000 | 126,712 → 140,000 | 248 → 600 |
| flexiq | 232,240 → 290,000 | 410,845 → 500,000 | 76,208 → 90,000 | 507 → 900 |

All three audits pass on GitHub's runners, not just locally.

### Wall-clock metrics — these only warn

LCP, TBT, CLS and Speed Index are collected over three runs and reported at the median. A shared CI runner moves them by ±30% between runs, and a gate that flaps is a gate everyone learns to ignore. The same applies to `unused-javascript` and `render-blocking-resources`, whose numeric values track Lighthouse's heuristics rather than the diff.

### Field data

`<WebVitals />` from the new `@byteveda/analytics` package sits in all three root layouts and posts Core Web Vitals to `NEXT_PUBLIC_VITALS_ENDPOINT`. It is inert when that variable is unset, which is what makes it safe in local development and in the docs export. It is built on `next/web-vitals`, so the only provider-specific thing about it is the URL.

`main` and `flexiq` additionally mount Vercel's Speed Insights as a second, disposable sink, through `@byteveda/analytics/vercel`. That wrapper exists because the upstream component injects `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js` unconditionally: on any other host that 404s, which is console noise everywhere and an assertion failure in the e2e suite. It now renders only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_ENV` is set, and deleting that one file is the whole cost of leaving Vercel.

### The audit target is a URL, not a host

`LHCI_TARGET_URL` overrides the locally built production server. Pointing a run at a deployed preview is an environment variable rather than a rewrite, and the same override works for Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare or a box we own. The `Lighthouse` workflow exposes it as a `workflow_dispatch` input; leave it blank and the workflow builds and serves each app itself.

### Lighthouse CI is run with `pnpm dlx`, not installed

`@lhci/cli` drags puppeteer and `extract-zip@2.0.1` into the lockfile — a high-severity path-traversal advisory with no fixed release, which the dependency review job rightly rejects. It is a CI tool rather than a library, so the scripts pin it inline (`pnpm dlx @lhci/cli@0.15.1 autorun`) and it stays out of the dependency graph entirely. That also keeps 279 packages out of the lockfile.

### Also in here

`pnpm turbo run test` had no CI job, so `apps/flexiq/e2e/budget.spec.ts` — the initial-payload budget guarding the lazy WebGL chunk — had never actually run on a pull request. This adds a `test` job to CI and renames the FlexiQ site's `test:e2e` script to `test` so turbo picks it up.

### Verification

- `pnpm lint` clean; the three remaining warnings are pre-existing CSS specificity notes in untouched files.
- `pnpm turbo run typecheck build` 10/10.
- `pnpm lighthouse` against real production builds of all three apps, and the three `Audit *` jobs green on CI.
- Regression proof: replacing the hero's `dynamic(() => import("./webgl-field"))` with a static import pushed script transfer from 232,240 to 465,751 on all three routes, and the run exited 1 on `resource-summary.script.size`. Reverted; budgets green again. Worth noting that the existing e2e ceiling of 700,000 would not have caught this.

author: dmadan86
body:
The user's words about this screen: *"the screen is very confusing and if I want to click on those person it is getting truncated and I don't understand anything what is happening very confusing"*. All four of those complaints turned out to be separate, findable defects.

## What was wrong

**The sentence was truncated on every row.** Each row carried the payer's avatar, an arrow, the payee's avatar, the sentence naming both, and the amount — five elements across a phone's width, three of which state the same fact. The sentence, squeezed into what was left and capped at `numberOfLines={1}`, lost every time: rows read `Renny pays .Rvs …`, `.Rvs Arun T pays …`. A row that cannot say who pays whom has no reason to exist.

**Your own rows were ungrammatical.** The sentence was `{from} pays {to}` filled with `displayName`, which returns "You" for the reader — so your own row read "You pays Ravi".

**The rows went nowhere.** They were plain `Row`s: no `Pressable`, no role, no label, no chevron.

**The avatars were lying.** `initialsOf` took the first character literally, so `.Rvs Amirnath`, `.Rvs Arun T` and `.Rvs Anoop` all drew as the same `.A` circle — two of them side by side on one row of a screen whose entire job is telling people apart.

**The last row was behind the bottom bar.** The screen used `useScreenClearance`, which reserves only the system inset; the app's own bar is rendered once at the root and stays over pushed screens, and this route is not in `TAB_BAR_HIDDEN_ROUTES`.

## What changed

- **One avatar, not two, and the sentence survives** — over two lines if it needs them, never an ellipsis through a name.
- **Three sentences for three positions**: `You pay {name}` / `{name} pays you` / `{from} pays {to}`, reusing the settle screen's own keys so the screen that proposes a payment and the screen that records it speak the same way.
- **Money colour is semantic on your rows** — red when you hand it over, the owed-to-you blue when you receive it — and neutral on a payment between two other people, which belongs to neither of them from here.
- **Rows are tappable**, opening that person across every group you share with them: the same destination and the same `personKeyOf` identity the Balances tab uses, so a tap can never land on a stranger's ledger. Your own row and a queue-only member are dead ends and wear no chevron, exactly as there.
- **`FlashList`** with the group-ledger settings (`drawDistance` 1500, `extraData`, `getItemType`, pull-to-refresh), hairline-divided instead of boxed in a card.
- **Your payments come first, under a heading**, with everyone else's under a second one — headings only when there is something on both sides.
- **`useTabBarClearance`**, so the last proposed payment is reachable.
- **`initialsOf` skips leading punctuation**, unicode-aware, and no longer splits an astral character in half. Moved to `packages/ui/src/initials.ts` so it can be unit-tested. Every avatar in the app reads through it.
- Two fixes on the group settings screen from the earlier design pass: the member roster was showing a **blocked** person's real name and real payment handle (masked everywhere else), and the group mark — now the one door to the cover — still announced itself as "Add group photo".

New pure module `src/lib/simplifyRows.ts` decides section, counterparty and hairlines, with tests; `initialsOf` has its own.

## i18n

`simplifyYourPayments` and `simplifyOtherPayments` added in **en / ta / hi / ar**; `simplifyYouPay` / `simplifyYouReceive` removed from the type and all four locales — the sentences say it now. No new hardcoded English. The removed arrow between avatars also removes the one glyph on this screen that had to be mirrored; the chevron uses `directionalIcon`.

## Not done, deliberately

- **The grey decimals** (`₹4.` black, `28` grey) are `MoneyText`'s app-wide `fadeFraction`, not this screen's choice. Changing it here would make one screen disagree with every other.
- **17 other screens have the same clearance bug** (`group/[id]`: insights, export, map, members, month, pending, recap, member/[memberId]; all of `personal/*`; `settings/import`, `settings/offline-voice`). Left alone to avoid colliding with other work in flight — worth its own sweep.

## Verification

`pnpm format`, mobile `lint` (0 errors), mobile + ui `typecheck`, and the full mobile suite (79 files / 992 tests) pass on Windows node. **Nothing was confirmed visually — there is no device or emulator here**, so the layout, the two-line sentence, the section headings and the clearance are argued from the code, not seen.

  - Added clearer labels distinguishing your payments from payments between others.
  - Avatar fallback initials now better support punctuation, non-Latin names, and special characters.

author: dungbanguyen
body:
Advances #799. **Does not close it** — see the plan at the end.

### The measurement the ticket needed

Widening the roots to `internal/modules` finds **96 sites**, distributed:

| package | sites | | package | sites |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| people | 33 | | integrations | 4 |
| activities | 14 | | introductions, finance, consent, ai | 3 each |
| privacy, deals | 7 each | | signals, dealrooms | 2 each |
| search | 6 | | projects, forecasting, contracts, commissions | 1 each |
| capture | 5 | | | |

That is why this is not one change. The ticket says most module sites need ratifying rather than fixing and that *"ratifying them is the work"* — and 96 waivers written in one sitting is a list nobody read, which reads as handled and is worse than no gate.

### The shape: widen by root, one package at a time

`censusedModules` is the list of module packages the census reaches. It is the **visible measure of coverage**: what is not in it is not claimed. Six packages join it here, and the remaining eleven are named in the issue with their counts so the next slice can be picked by size rather than by grepping.

It is explicitly **not the end state**, and the declaration says so. What the census wants is `gatekit.Scope` over the whole tier, where a site outside every root **fails** rather than being invisible — a negative sweep is what makes a root a proof instead of a claim. That needs every module ratified first, which is what the list is for getting to.

### The seven ratifications

All seven are the first of the two kinds the ticket distinguishes — a store that owns its table, not a read model pointing at somebody else's — and each names how its admission was already made:

- **commissions:summaryTx** — the partner totals are grouped under the commission's own `VisibleClause`, applied in the same statement. A caller admitted to an entry is admitted to what it is about.
- **contracts:ensureLinksShareOrganization** — the one worth reading twice: **scoping it would defeat it.** Its own doc says the read predicate judges a deal-anchored contract by its deal alone, so pairing company A's contract with company B's deal publishes A's agreement to everyone who can see B. The organization this cannot see is exactly the one the rule protects, and what leaves the function is a refusal, not an id.
- **projects:lockedDealProject** — reads the pointer off a deal row the caller's transaction already holds; applying the patch is what took the lock.
- **forecasting:SnapshotSide** — a frozen record behind the snapshot's own read gate. Scoping its deal ids to today's visibility would rewrite history to match the reader.
- **dealrooms:liveRoomForBuyerWrite** and **:reissueFor** — a buyer holds no seat for a seller-side row scope to narrow to; the room's capability and the participant row are the authority, which is what those functions are about.
- **signals:matchCandidates** — the capture path under the system principal, on the same ground `edgereaders_test.go` already ratifies `signals/resolver.go`.

### Held

`wantMinimumCensusedModuleSites` is the floor on the widened roots specifically — the existing floor counts compose's sites and would not notice a module root going dark. Mutation-checked both ways: dropping `internal/modules/signals` from the roots fails as a stale waiver naming `matchCandidates`, and blinding the module walk entirely fails the floor with *"only 0 record-reference reads found across the 6 censused module package(s)"*.

`make check-backend` green.

### What remains

Eleven packages, 89 sites. `people` (33) and `activities` (14) are the two that will need their own PRs; the rest are small enough to go two or three at a time. When the list covers the tier, it is deleted and replaced by `gatekit.Scope` — and that deletion is what closes #799.

author: zefir6
body:
## Summary
Confirmed live: after the previous round of fixes, the app *showed* the new avatar (thanks to cache-seeding), but it never actually changed on larpnet.pl's own web UI — the upload wasn't really succeeding server-side, just looking like it did on the client.

**Root cause** (confirmed against Friendica's own source): `PATCH api/v1/accounts/update_credentials`'s `avatar` field goes through Friendica's own hand-rolled multipart-over-PATCH parser (`HTTPInputData`, needed since PHP doesn't natively populate `$_FILES` for non-POST methods). `Photo::uploadAvatar`'s return value is then discarded uninspected by the caller (`UpdateCredentials.php`), so any failure in that custom parsing path is completely invisible to the client — the request just returns 200 with an unchanged account.

**Fix**: switched to Friendica's legacy Twitter-compatible `POST api/account/update_profile_image` instead. It reads `$_FILES['image']` directly — PHP's native superglobal, populated automatically for any real POST multipart request, never touching Friendica's custom parser at all — and it actually throws a real error if the upload fails rather than silently no-op'ing. Returns a legacy Twitter-shaped user object, so `uploadAvatarImage` re-fetches via `verifyCredentials()` afterward for a clean typed `Account` (same upload-then-refetch shape `postStatusWithACL` already uses).

`updateCredentials()` drops its now-unused `avatar` parameter and the multipart plumbing that came with it, reverting to the simpler form-urlencoded PATCH it only ever needed for text fields.

## Test plan
- [x] `xcodegen generate` + full `xcodebuild` (Debug) succeeds

Seeding the first admin on the box failed:


author: webiq1206
body:
Second tranche of the touch-target work the audit surfaced. The decision taken: **make the whole row the tap target**, the way a phone app does, rather than pad every title link to 44px and lose a third of the rows per screen on the device with the least screen.

## The mechanism — a stretched link

The `<a>` stays on the title. It is what a screen reader names, what the keyboard focuses, and what a right-click opens in a new tab. A pseudo-element grows its hit area over the nearest `.row` — the same idea as `.tap`, applied to a row. The row itself never becomes a link (interactive content nested inside an `<a>` is invalid and reads badly). Anything else tappable in the row wears `.row-raise` so it sits above the stretched area and keeps its own tap. The row tints on hover and press so it looks like what it now is.

Applied to the recap rows and totals tiles. The sweep now measures a `.row-link` by its row, for the same reason it already measured `.tap` by 44: what a thumb hits, not the text.

**Verified in a touch browser at 390px, not inferred:** a tap on a row's blank corner opens its record (63 rows); a tap on the row's "Quick look" opens the preview, *not* the record.

## The rest of the tranche

| Where | What was wrong | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-table` | both checkboxes 13×13, no hit area | `tap` |
| `data-table` | Prev / Next 44 tall, 42 wide | `min-w-11` |
| `subs-table` | company name 36 tall in the tablet table | touch height only; desktop density kept |
| `landing.css` | the 44px footer rule lived inside `max-width:760` — a phone. At 768 and 1024 footer and header links were 15–20px | rule extended to 1024, the shell's own touch boundary |
| marketing footer | ten bare links at 20px | 44 on touch, off on desktop |
| breadcrumbs | "Home" on compare / pricing-guide / sitemap was 35×14 | `tap`, keeping the "Home / Page" sentence intact |

Every change measured after the fact at the width that reported it: link heights, `::after` sizes, `elementFromPoint` sixteen pixels below a 14px breadcrumb still resolving to it.

## Numbers

Touch-target findings: **1,689 → 1,124**. The report's 1,124 is 72 distinct (width, control) lines — the sweep counts every route×width hit — so what remains is a tail of roughly two dozen controls, each named in the committed report.

Suite green: 5012 passing.

author: kaycet
body:
## What changed and why

This PR now consolidates the surviving fixes from all six open daily-run PRs (#23–#27 plus this one's original scope), so one PR merges and the rest close as superseded — same approach as the last consolidation cycle (#21).

**Original scope (commits 1–2):**

- **Idle detection survives service-worker suspension.** The `chrome.idle.onStateChanged` listener was registered inside async `init()`, so it died with every MV3 suspension and "pause polling while idle" never actually engaged. It's now a top-level listener, and `init()` seeds `idleState` from `chrome.idle.queryState()`.
- **Failed tab redirects no longer count as switches.** `switchToStream` and the category-fallback redirect now check `chrome.runtime.lastError` on `tabs.update` instead of recording a switch (and logging "Unchecked runtime.lastError") when the managed tab closed mid-flight.
- Dead-code cleanups (duplicate `onInstalled` registration, unused args, popup debounce timer that `cleanup()` could never clear) and in-range dev-dep updates: eslint/@eslint/js 9.39.2 → 9.39.5, playwright 1.57.0 → 1.63.0.

**Ported from the sibling PRs (commit 3):**

- **From #27** — notifications inline the stream thumbnail as a `data:` URL (`chrome.notifications.create()` rejects remote iconUrls, which silently dropped every "went live" alert), with a bundled-icon fallback and one retry; storage cache no longer collides `get('x')` with `get(['x'])`. Tests for both. Supersedes the icon-fallback halves of #23 and #25.
- **From #25** — `utils/stream-sync.js` overlays background-written stream statuses onto the popup's in-memory list, so a bell toggle or reorder no longer saves a stale `wasLive` that re-fires notifications for streams that never went offline. Tests included.
- **From #24** — Twitch API response cache pruning (expired entries dropped on any request, 200-entry cap) with tests; the no-op `handleInstall()` removed entirely.
- **From #26** — cache is checked before rate-limit accounting (cache hits neither spend budget nor sleep on an exhausted window) with tests; options page saves `fallbackCategory` on `change` instead of every keystroke (a half-typed category could redirect the managed tab); save-status timer fix; CI additionally runs the DOM-hook audit and a packaging smoke test.

## How it was verified

`npm run ci` after every commit: eslint clean, **106/106 tests across 18 files** (up from 86/15 on main), extension zip packages with the DOM-hook audit reporting all JS-referenced ids present.

## What a reviewer should read closely

- The top-level `chrome.idle.onStateChanged` listener + `queryState` seed — polling now genuinely pauses while idle/locked, which is a behavior change (the intended one).
- `thumbnailToDataUrl` fetches the Twitch CDN from the worker; on any failure (CORS, offline, non-image) it returns `null` and the bundled icon is used, so the notification always shows.
- The `_request` reorder (cache before `_checkRateLimit`) and the popup's `changes.streams` overlay are each covered by new tests.

## Flagged, not changed

- `npm audit`: 5 dev-only advisories, all in vitest 2.x's transitive esbuild/vite chain; the fix is vitest 5 (major bump), left for a human-decided upgrade.

## Summary

- **What changed?** The bylaws templates already ship — in Blackout, as den documents on the Coalition tool sheet. FBM's part was to point at them, and it did not: Q11 `coop-formation`'s gatekeeper links held one hard-coded USDA URL, and the six progression edges that ask a vendor for bylaws said so in bare prose with nothing to read.
  - **One list, built once.** `backend/src/shared/coop-founding-links.ts` assembles the Blackout Coalition URL followed by the co-op-serving legal and back-office rows of the partner registry. Q11 and the progression edges both read it, so a new registry row reaches both at once and there is no second list to drift.
  - **Two new registry rows.** The USFWC Co-op Clinic (startup resources and mini-guides), and the USDA Cooperative Services page that had been hard-coded inside the quest definition — now a row like every other, which is why the edges can show it too.
  - **`ProgressionEdge` gains an optional `resource_links`**, set on the six edges whose prerequisites name bylaws and left off every edge about facilities, licences or land, where only the vendor's own state can answer and a national link would mislead. The vendor panel renders it under "Arranged outside FBM first" with the line that FBM neither drafts, reviews nor files any of it.
  - **Q11's bylaws note said "the shared vault".** There is no collective-owned vault: the vault is seller-scoped and a collective quest flat-maps the documents of members who consented to the `documents` scope. body:
Follow-on to #55. Feedback on the live site: "doesn't look like a graph, it's a
weird line at the bottom — should have a line at top and bottom, and smaller
lines in between to delimitate the axis."

## What was wrong

A bare autoscaled polyline with nothing to read it against. It genuinely showed
the right shape, but with no top/bottom reference there was no way to tell
where in its own range any given point sat — it just read as noise.

## The fix, and a real bug it surfaced

Added a top line and a bottom line bounding the strip, plus two short ticks
marking it into thirds — same visual language the gauge's own dial already
uses for its tick marks.

First attempt drew all four in `--color-hairline` (`#1c1c20`), matching the
gauge's dial track. Rendered, checked with Playwright, and they were **good as
invisible** — computed the actual contrast: hairline works on the gauge only
because the track is a 14px arc; a lone 1px line with nothing else beside it
for contrast at that color is below what a screenshot even preserves.

Switched to `--color-ash`, the muted *text* token this page already uses for
labels and timestamps, at reduced opacity. Screenshotted again — clearly
visible, still clearly secondary to the signal-colored line.

## Verification

`bun test` — 296 pass, 0 fail. `bun run typecheck` clean.

Screenshotted against real jagged data (not just the unit tests): before/after
confirm the frame is now visible and the polyline reads as a chart rather than

## Summary

### Headroom removal

### rebuild.sh idempotency fix
`rebuild.sh` string-compared `$DIR` against `~/Code/dotfiles`. The repo lives at `~/code/dotfiles` (lowercase), which on the case-insensitive APFS volume is the **same** directory (identical device:inode). The string compare saw a mismatch, entered the relink branch, found a real dir (itself), and refused with `Refusing to replace existing non-symlink`, breaking `just rebuild work`. Now it compares resolved paths, staying idempotent both for the case-insensitive case and when the target is already a symlink pointing here.

body:
Resolves #208

### Summary
Enforces benchmark task `allowed_write_scope` for all shell commands:
- Takes a pre-execution workspace snapshot in `FixtureWorkspace.execShell` and compares it against post-execution filesystem state.
- Detects unauthorized creations, mutations, and deletions outside the task `allowed_write_scope` (including negative/exclusion patterns like `!path`).
- Reverts all unauthorized mutations to ensure excluded and protected files remain completely untouched and unauthorized new files are deleted.
- Throws `WriteScopeViolationError` upon unauthorized mutation detection and maps it in `FixtureWorkspaceBackend.execShell` to `ToolExecutionError("write_scope", message)` for deterministic trajectory recording.
- Adds comprehensive regression tests in `benchmarks/tests/fixture.test.ts` verifying allowed writes, excluded write restoration, and forbidden file prevention.

author: isvenu
body:
Semantic search over the skills and CI tools catalogues, for [DX-163](https://linear.app/korza-ai/issue/DX-163/integrate-natural-language-search-for-skillsci-catalog).

- Search runs on local embeddings — no API key, no external calls.
- The corpus is embedded into a committed `src/data/search-index.json`.
- The home typeahead became a plain GET form, so a search is linkable and works without JS.
- A `search-index` CI job keeps the committed index honest — see below, it needed some care.

### Screens

Home — the field, with example queries:

![Home](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/korzainc/devx-home/pr-47-screenshots/.pr-assets/1-home.png)

Results for "find hardcoded secrets in a repo" — 16 hits, split by kind:

![Results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/korzainc/devx-home/pr-47-screenshots/.pr-assets/2-results.png)

The zero-results gate on nonsense input. Embeddings always return a nearest neighbour, so without it "asdfghjkl" would return eight confident, meaningless rows:

![No results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/korzainc/devx-home/pr-47-screenshots/.pr-assets/3-no-results.png)

### The index is not bit-reproducible

Worth knowing before review, since it shaped the CI job:

- **Across architectures.** The same q8 weights run through different ONNX kernels on arm64 and x64. A Mac-built index rewrote ~97% of values on a Linux runner and reordered the top 10 for 26 of 40 sampled queries — a genuinely different ranking, not noise.
- **So CI owns the build.** The job rebuilds the index on the runner and commits it back to the branch, making the committed vectors x64's — the architecture Vercel serves.
- **Residual wobble.** Even on one runner image, two runs disagreed on 484 of 30336 values (max 9.3e-3), confined to three documents. Pinning ONNX to a single thread did not move it. So the check compares with a 2e-2 tolerance and only rebuilds when that fails — otherwise it committed on branches where nothing had changed.
- Model, dtype, dimension, schema version and the corpus key list are still compared exactly.

`pnpm check:search-index` is expected to report stale on an arm64 machine; let CI rebuild it.

### Also

Two HIGH CVEs arrived with the embedding dependency — `adm-zip` via `onnxruntime-node`, and transformers' own `sharp`. Neither had an upstream release to bump to, so both are pinned via `overrides` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (pnpm 11 no longer reads `pnpm.overrides` from package.json). Next already resolved the fixed sharp, so the lockfile got smaller.

**Goes together with [shared-workflows#79](https://github.com/korzainc/shared-workflows/pull/79).** That PR teaches the catalogue sync to rebuild this index. Without it, the next sync PR changes `catalogue.json` alone and lands vectors that no longer match. Merge this first, then that one.

> 다 같은 문장이 덩어리 1,2,3에 반복되고 이전 같은 재미도 사라졌다. **우선 되돌리고** 이유를 분석해라. **필력이 구려졌어.**

PR #63 을 통째로 되돌린다(`git revert 0dc77e7`). 비트 3 이 안 쓰이는 문제는 되살아나지만, 그것보다 필력이 먼저다.

## 왜 나빠졌나 -- 셋이 겹쳤다

**1. 서로 어긋나는 두 명령.** 집필 프롬프트에는 원래 이 줄이 있다.

```
[지금까지의 끝부분 — 여기서 이어 쓴다]
  * 이 마지막 문장 다음 순간부터 써라. 여기가 지금이다.
```

거기에 내가 이것을 얹었다.

```
· 앞 비트의 자리를 떠나라 -- 자리나 때가 바뀐다.
```

둘 다 지킬 수 없다. 모델은 **장면을 새로 연다.** 새로 열면 누가 어디에 있는지 다시 세우고, 앞에서 벌어진 일을 다시 설명한다. 그것이 덩어리 1·2·3 에 같은 문장이 도는 이유다.

**2. 덩어리를 닫힌 단위로 만들었다.**

```
· 이 덩어리는 N번 비트다. 이 덩어리 안에서 그것을 끝낸다.
  시작하고, 벌어지고, 끝난다.
```

닫힌 단위는 제 머리와 제 꼬리를 갖는다. 3,200자마다 상황을 세우는 머리 문단과 정리하는 꼬리 문단이 붙는다. 잰 로판 문체는 그 반대다 -- "절을 이어 붙여 길게 가고", "길이를 섞어라". 이어지던 흐름을 3,200자마다 끊으니 요약체가 됐다. **필력이 구려진 자리가 여기다.**

**3. 이어받기가 비트를 한 칸 밀었다.** `flow.step` 은 덩어리가 짧으면 `book["chunks"]` 에 잠깐 얹고 `write_prompt` 를 다시 부른다. 비트를 **덩어리 수로** 세게 바꿔 놨으니, 그 임시 한 개가 비트를 통째로 한 칸 올린다. 한 덩어리의 앞뒤가 서로 다른 비트로 쓰였다.

## 진짜 원인은 산수였지 프롬프트가 아니었다

비트 3 이 잘린 것은 사실이다. 그런데 그 원인은 **비트 셋에 덩어리 1.56개**라는 산수다. 나는 산수를 고치면서 프롬프트까지 바꿨고, 망친 것은 프롬프트 쪽이다.

산수만 고치는 길이 있다 -- `BEATS = 2`, `EPISODE_SPAN = 6400`(덩어리 둘). 그러면 덩어리 1 이 비트 1, 덩어리 2 가 비트 2(답이 나는 자리)이고 회차가 닫힌다. **집필 프롬프트는 한 글자도 안 건드린다.** 다음에 그것만 따로 올린다.

## 검사

`test_beat` · `test_space` · `test_serial` · `test_flow` 전부 통과 (PR #63 이전 상태로 돌아갔다).

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Why

The notebook could already be re-run, but not re-*created*: it installed bare package names into whatever image Colab shipped that week, cloned a branch, downloaded weights by tag, and recorded none of it. Any two runs differed for reasons nobody could name. This closes those four gaps without touching the CPU test suite's dependency footprint.

## What

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Code provenance | `linescout_ml/colab/repro.py`: `ensure_checkout` / `find_or_checkout` clone shallowly, move the tree onto one 40-hex commit, verify HEAD, and return a `CheckoutRecord` (revision, detached, dirty, untracked, action, which URL served it). A branch or tag is refused. Given an existing checkout it fetches onto the pin and **never resets a tree with uncommitted edits**. Mirrors are transport only — content-addressing is what makes them safe. |
| Environment | `ml/colab/requirements-colab.txt` is the single env spec: 21 pins in six groups — 19 installable, and a `[runtime]` group of 2 (`torch`, `torchvision`) that is recorded and never installed. Presets resolve into `SourceSpec` objects **before** preflight, so Human-Art requests `opennsfw2` (+ `gdown`) with no override written; `uses_extractor`/`requires_nsfw` are read from the resolved spec by both the plan and the label stage, so they cannot disagree. The notebook passes pip only `name==version`, under a constraints file frozen from Colab's CUDA build of torch — necessary rather than tidy, because resolving those 19 pins reaches 81 packages including a transitive `torch==2.14.0` plus 19 CUDA-flavoured wheels, none of them asked for by name. |
| SFW policy | The rule for what the gate may trust is now *who made the guarantee*: a publisher's own programme or an application-gated corpus is `source_rating` (no classifier, and the asset says so); anything scraped from a community runs the classifier. `amateur_drawings` and `safebooru` move to `source_rating+opennsfw2` — a booru's `rating` tags are the claim under test, not a pass. `SFW_POLICY` in `tests/test_colab_config.py` is the reviewed table. |
| Weights | `ml/linescout_ml/colab/models.lock.json`: repo + 40-hex revision + filename + size + SHA-256 (`lfs.oid`, not the git blob `oid`) per file. `checkpoints.py` verifies before use and fails closed with the cache path in the message; an unreadable original fails closed too. Policies: `record` (default) / `require` / `off` (prints `unverified`). A group with no pin is an error naming the remedy, which is why `mobileclip2_s0` is refused rather than fetched. |
| Recording | Provenance lands in `run_report.json` **and** the manifest, where `content_hash()` covers it — re-pointing an old manifest at new weights produces a different gallery hash, not a matching one. |
| Audit | `linescout-repro selfcheck` (in CI) checks notebook ↔ package ↔ env spec ↔ checkpoint lock ↔ docs, including "no heavy import at module scope". `linescout-repro pin --check` gates a placeholder pin. |

Notebook is now 40 cells with an explicit order: checkout → resolve sources → freeze torch → install pinned subset → record runtime. `REPO_ALLOW_DIRTY = True` records dirt honestly; `False` is the paranoid setting. The documented one-cell `run_all` alternative now leaves the same artifacts as the per-cell path (it copies `runtime.json`, and a test asserts `run_all` still covers every stage the cells call).

## Pin status

`COLAB_PIN` / `REPO_PIN` = `c966202bc537cc01735aa4134361fe5ac6665ca3` — the first tree where the pipeline, the checkpoint lock, the environment spec, the **schema v2** contract and the notebook's own *executed* cells agree. Verified rather than asserted: fetched from both URLs (`HEAD : c966202bc537  (matches the pin)`), `run_selfcheck` with the pinned tree's code on the path prints `[]`, and that tree's notebook + reporting-cell tests pass 52. One lag is structural: a commit cannot contain its own SHA, so the pinned tree's copy of the pin line cites the bump before it — spelled out in `ml/colab/README.md`, and harmless because cell 1 fails closed on any mismatch. It resolves from `junosapollo/drawable` only because this repo is its **fork** and GitHub shares object storage, so **merging into the canonical repository is what makes the pin permanent**; `ml/colab/README.md` → "The repository pin" has the procedure and the caveats.

## Not claimed

No real Colab/GPU run happened: this sandbox has no CUDA device and `huggingface.co:443` fails the TLS handshake, so weights were pinned from API and wheel metadata, never downloaded. `ml/colab/SMOKE_TEST.md` says that in its first paragraph and gives the runbook with the exact output each cell must produce, a table to paste back, and a `runtime-baseline.json` refresh step.

## Reviewer's 60 seconds

```bash
cd ml && uv sync --frozen --extra dev --python 3.11
.venv/bin/pytest -q                      # 371 passed (main's v2 suite included)
cd ../services/api && uv sync --frozen --extra dev --python 3.11 && .venv/bin/pytest -q   # 107
.venv/bin/linescout-repro selfcheck      # "…agree"
.venv/bin/linescout-repro pin --check    # pin is final
```

Tests added: `test_colab_repro.py` (40, incl. CLI and the closure test), `test_colab_checkpoints.py` (27), `test_colab_selfcheck.py` (13, snapshot-and-mutate: it breaks the repo on purpose and asserts the audit notices), `test_colab_notebook.py` (49 — cell layout, pins, hint-vs-schema, the `run_all` equivalence), 6 config tests for the preset/override dependency rule and the SFW policy table. `uv.lock` changed additively; fixtures + `packages/contracts/manifest.schema.json` regenerated and verified byte-identical to `scripts/export_openapi.py`'s output.


### Environment closure, measured rather than assumed (after review of the pin)

`uv pip compile --python-version 3.11` over the spec's 19 installable pins resolves 81
packages on linux/py3.11; the transitive `torch` and its `nvidia-*`/`cuda-toolkit`/`triton`
entourage are the reason the notebook passes a constraints file, and `ml/colab/README.md`
now prints the command next to the number. `opencv-python` (GUI build) arrives via
`opennsfw2`, so the headless pin is documented as a preference, not an exclusion.
Pinned-commit self-consistency is checked from the outside too: a shallow clone at the
pin, its own code on `sys.path`, reports `run_selfcheck(...) == []`.

## Merged with schema v2 — and what the merge hid

PR #7 froze the manifest contract while this branch was open; both changes touch
`manifest.py`, the Colab stage modules, and the notebook. The merge keeps both, with
main's v2 shape winning wherever they disagree: `Manifest.provenance` survives the
rewrite (so `content_hash()` still covers the pins a gallery was built from), and the
regenerated `manifest.schema.json` carries `PipelineProvenance`/`CheckpointProvenance`
beside v2's `Permissions`/`SfwScreening`/`SfwHumanDecision`. `openapi.json` and the
generated TypeScript are byte-identical to main's, so this branch changes no API surface.
`sfw_method="manual"` is now recorded as a human decision attributed to
`ingestion:<pipeline_version>` rather than as an invented screening result — the v2
contract's framing is stronger than what this branch had reached for.

What no textual conflict showed: the notebook still spoke v1 in three places, one of them
code. `MANIFEST.enabled_records` and `summary['by_split']` would have raised in cell 11 —
two lines after the first GPU stage finished, ~770 MB of weights already downloaded — and
every test would have stayed green, because no test executes that cell. Both are on the v2
names now, the stale `enabled=false` claims about ingestion are corrected in the notebook,
`ml/colab/README.md`, `assets.py`, and the root README's endpoint row (serving is the
derived `is_servable` predicate; a missing file is a 404 for the session and never a
manifest rewrite), a guard checks every attribute the cells reach through

author: helldweller
body:
## The problem

Most of the panel's JavaScript lives inline in `templates/*.html`, and every UI string lives in `translations/*.json`. Neither has any coverage:

- A syntax error in a template's `<script>` block does not fail anything. The page just stops working in the browser — no handler bound, no console visible to CI.
- A broken translation file makes the whole panel render raw keys. `load_translations` catches the `JSONDecodeError` and leaves the dictionary empty, so the failure is silent server-side.

The JSON one is the easier trap to fall into. Two branches that both append keys at the end of a translation file merge cleanly and drop the comma that used to terminate the last entry — git has no reason to flag it. The result is a plausible-looking file among 5 files × ~700 keys, and the symptom is English keys showing up in the UI. Both of your open UI branches append to these files, so it is a live risk, not a hypothetical one.

## The fix

`tests/test_template_js.py`, two tests:

1. Extract every `<script>` block without a `src`, strip the Jinja tags (`{{ ... }}` becomes a literal, `{% ... %}` disappears), and run `node --check` over the result. Skips itself when `node` is not on PATH — `ubuntu-latest` has it preinstalled, so CI does run it.
2. `json.loads` every `translations/*.json`.

## Testing

Against the current `main`:

```
test_every_template_script_parses ... ok
test_every_translation_file_parses ... ok
Ran 2 tests in 0.102s — OK
```

Full suite: 154 tests, no failures from this change.

**Note on CI:** the single error in the suite is the pre-existing bare `import pytest` in `tests/test_playwright_e2e.py`, red on `main` since v1.6.4. Unrelated; fixed in #142.

author: ezioauditore95
body:
La V1 separava le spiegazioni dai calcolatori: i risultati numerici aiutavano poco a vedere i fenomeni e a collegarli al romanzo.

Questa versione trasforma il sito in un percorso di sei esperimenti. Il lettore parte da un’intuizione, modifica le variabili, osserva il diagramma e può aprire la formula. Ogni modulo distingue le evidenze scientifiche dalle proprietà inventate da Weir.

- Nuova impaginazione in italiano, con tipografia ampia, fondo scuro, accenti lime/arancio e un esperimento sulla luce già nella prima schermata.
- Laboratori su flusso e temperatura stellare, curve di oscuramento, equivalenza massa–energia, tempi relativistici, gravità artificiale e ambienti biologici.
- Diagrammi SVG calcolati dai parametri; rotazione avviabile e arrestabile con velocità coerente con gli RPM.
- Ipotesi e limiti espliciti: scala logaritmica del flusso, curve sintetiche, accelerazione senza frenata, energia teorica e biologia non dimostrata.
- Tre livelli di spoiler, navigazione da tastiera, collegamenti diretti ai moduli e gestione del movimento ridotto.
- Quiz di otto domande con spiegazioni, risultato finale e ritorno ai concetti da rivedere; mantenuta la domanda casuale.
- Conservate le chiavi locali della V1, con recupero da dati corrotti o storage indisponibile.
- Fonti NASA, OpenStax, Einstein Online e Physics FAQ/DESY collegate ai moduli.

La struttura rimane statica, senza dipendenze JavaScript né build. I percorsi sono relativi e compatibili con l’attuale GitHub Pages; la configurazione di pubblicazione resta invariata.

Verifica: 7 test numerici superati, inclusi valori di riferimento, conversioni di unità, invarianti relativistici e limiti dei parametri. Superati i controlli di sintassi JavaScript, riferimenti HTML/ARIA, asset locali e generazione dei sei template dei laboratori.

La verifica visuale e delle interazioni in un browser non è stata eseguita. Questa PR non è stata unita a main e non pubblica ancora la nuova versione.

## 概要

iPad/PCビューでタスク詳細を全画面表示にして左下の「完了」をタップすると、最終確認モーダルが背面に出て押せない不具合を修正。

## 原因

`.expand-overlay`（全画面タスク詳細, `z-index:500`）と `.overlay`（完了確認などの汎用モーダル, `z-index:200`）はどちらも `document.body` 直下に `position:fixed` で追加される兄弟要素。CSSのスタッキング規則ではDOM追加順ではなく `z-index` の大小のみで重なりが決まるため、確認モーダルが後から追加されても常に背面に回り込んでいた。

## 修正

- `.overlay` の `z-index` を `200` → `510`（`.expand-overlay` の `500` より確実に上）に変更
- `sw.js` の `CACHE_NAME` を `taskra-v65` → `taskra-v66`
- `HANDOVER.md` / `POSTS.md` を更新

JS・マークアップは無変更、CSSの数値変更のみ。

該当なし。認証・決済・DBスキーマ・RLSはいずれも無変更。UIの重なり順(z-index)のみの修正。

## 検証

`.expand-overlay`(500)と`.overlay`(510)を同条件で重ねた最小テストで、修正後は確認モーダル側が最前面になりクリックが通ることを確認。実機（iPad/PC実ブラウザ）での目視確認は未実施。

author: simlarsen
body:
`test (6/8)` is failing on master. It is not a regression from any recent change — the test expired on a timer.

## What happens

`EnterpriseLicenseReportUserCount`'s test *"serializes registration and re-reads usage inside the aggregation lock"* pinned its fixture to the literal `2026-09-01T12:00:00.000Z`. Every other date in that file is built from `OneUptimeDate.getCurrentDate()`.

That timestamp is load-bearing, not decorative. The test mocks `EnterpriseLicenseInstanceService.findBy` to return no instances, so `hasActiveReportedInstanceUsage` is false and the response falls through to the legacy usage path in `EnterpriseLicenseAPI` — which only trusts `license.userCountUpdatedAt` while `isTimestampWithinUsageWindow` holds, i.e. `InstanceUsageFreshnessInDays`, seven days.

The fixture crossed that boundary at **2026-09-08T12:00:00Z**. After it, the instance is inactive, the legacy fallback declines the stored value, and the echoed `currentUserCount` collapses from `17` to `0`:

```
- ObjectContaining {
-   "currentUserCount": 17,
+   "currentUserCount": 0,
+   "instances": Array [],
```

So the test began failing with no change to itself or to the code under test. I confirmed it fails on a pristine `origin/master` worktree.

## The fix

Build the timestamp a day back from now, the way the rest of the file does, so it stays inside the window permanently.

The test still pins what it was written to pin — it is not asserted away. Setting the fixture 30 days back reproduces the original failure, so the freshness path is still genuinely exercised. All 50 tests in the file pass; `tsc --noEmit` and eslint are clean.

## Worth a follow-up

Other suites hold hardcoded absolute dates with no fake clock — `SloUtil` (69), `AIInvestigationAPI` (28), `UptimeUtil` (22) among them. Most look harmless, since an absolute date is only a hazard where it meets a now-relative window, as it did here. I deliberately did not audit them in this PR.

author: tmerlini
body:
Follow-up to #40, closing the half @babyblueviper1 asked about there.

`profile-amendment-v0` (merged in #40) decides which verification profile is *effective* for a task — the amendment end. This suite decides whether the resolver's verdict actually **commits to that `effective_profile_commitment` inside its signed preimage** — the resolution end — so "I resolved under this profile" is attested and recomputable, not a side-channel reference.

**Rule.** A verdict is `bound` iff (1) `verdict_core.effective_profile_commitment` is present AND equals the task's authorized effective profile, and (2) the resolver signed *this* core (`signed_digest == verdict_core_cc`). Otherwise `unresolved`, `bound_profile_commitment` null, fail closed. Same scope split as companion-envelope (binding, not signature cryptography).

**Composition — the two suites meet at one value:**
```
profile_transition(task).effective_profile_commitment == verdict.core.effective_profile_commitment
```
The vectors here use the same `sha256(JCS(profileB))` that `profile-amendment-v0`'s `permitted` case produces, so amendment-end and resolution-end are Pavlo's `task.profile_commitment == verdict.profile_commitment` with both ends cryptographic.

**Contents / verification (careful mode)**
- `verdict_binding_gate.py` + `verdict-profile-binding-v0.reference.mjs` (bun/node, independent `jcs`) reproduce 6/6 byte-for-byte cross-language.
- 6 vectors: 2 bound (incl. `bound-distinct-verdict` shape-not-value) + 4 refused, one per predicate: `profile-omitted`, `wrong-profile`, `signature-over-wrong-core`, `resolver-absent`.

author: jeremymcs
body:
## TL;DR

A refused `/gsd auto --resume-wedge <id>` acknowledgment was persisted to `.gsd/notifications.jsonl` but never rendered in the TUI, so the command looked like a hang. The acknowledgment now runs before the session switch, where the notify surface is still live.

Closes #2219

## What

- Move `acknowledgeRequestedWedge()` to the top of the fresh-start path in `startAuto`, before `bootstrapAutoSession`/`newSession` take over the session. It needs only the orchestration module (for `recheckWedge`) and the project scope — both available pre-bootstrap.
- Gate the pre-bootstrap work on `options?.resumeWedgeId` so normal starts skip it entirely; the existing post-bootstrap `ensureOrchestrationModule` rebuild is kept so nothing downstream changes.
- On refusal, restore the milestone-lock env (previously restored via `cleanupAfterLoopExit`) and return with nothing registered — no worker row, no bootstrap side effects.
- Add a regression test that trips a real `completed-no-advance` wedge and pins the ordering: the refusal notification fires before any bootstrap side effect, and the wedge stays open per ADR-047 §5.

## Why

Post-bootstrap, the slash-command-time `ctx.ui` is stale for toasts: notifications persist to the jsonl file but the interactive session never displays them. The refusal was deterministic and invisible — users reasonably concluded auto-mode had hung and started bypassing the ADR-047 wedge contract.

## How

The ack is a session-independent recheck (`normalizeRealPath(base)` scope + `s.orchestration.recheckWedge`), so running it before the session switch is semantically identical — only the notify channel differs, and pre-bootstrap that channel is the live one. Known residual: the pre-bootstrap "Pre-flight" info notifications mentioned in the issue remain a pre-existing rendering gap; this fix covers the refusal path, which is the actionable one.

AI-assisted: this change was implemented with AI assistance (per repo policy, disclosed here; the commit has a human author).

author: matej21
body:
Stacked on #98 — review that one first.

## The hole #98 left

#98 made `FilteringState.setArtifact` / `resetFilter` / `setOrderBy` use the functional update form, so writes to **different** filter names batched into one commit compose instead of clobbering each other.

One layer up, `useDataViewFilter` still resolved its `SetStateAction` updater itself:

```ts
const current = filtering.getArtifact(key) as T | undefined   // render snapshot
const next = updater(current)
filtering.setArtifact(key, next)                              // plain value
```

`getArtifact` reads the artifacts record captured at render time. Two *functional* updates on the **same** filter name inside one commit therefore both saw the same `prev`, and the second erased the first — the same bug as #66, one level higher and not covered by #98.

Not hypothetical: `useDataViewEnumFilterFactory`, `useDataViewBooleanFilterFactory`, `useDataViewRelationFilter*` and `useDataViewNullFilter` all drive `set(action)` through this path (`setFilter(it => ({ ...it, … }))`), as does the debounced `useDataViewTextFilterInput` — whose timer callback resolved against a snapshot several renders old. Toggling two values of one enum filter in a single handler lost the first toggle.

## What changed

`FilteringState.setArtifact` now takes a value **or** an updater, resolved inside `useFilteringState` against the live record:

```ts
export type FilterArtifactUpdate =
	| FilterArtifact
	| ((current: FilterArtifact | undefined) => FilterArtifact | undefined)

setArtifact(name: string, artifact: FilterArtifactUpdate): void
```

**`undefined` semantics:** an updater returning `undefined` resets that filter to its default artifact (`handler.defaultArtifact()`), which is exactly what `useDataViewFilter` did with `resetFilter` before — preserved unchanged. A plain `undefined` *value* is not part of the signature; `useDataViewFilter` keeps mapping `setFilter(undefined)` to `resetFilter`. `resetFilter`, `resetAll` and `setAllArtifacts` are untouched, as is storage/persistence behaviour.

`useDataViewFilter.setFilter` now hands the updater straight through instead of pre-resolving it. Its two `as T | undefined` casts collapse into one named helper (`narrowArtifact`) that states the single unchecked claim: a name-keyed store cannot know that the artifact under `key` is a `T`. No new casts.

Sorting, paging and selection are untouched — #98 already covers them.

## Verification

- New `tests/react/dataview/filterUpdaterPassthrough.test.tsx`: updaters at the state layer (compose, `undefined` → default, plain value) and through `useDataViewFilter` in a real `DataGrid` (two functional writes on one filter name, one handler toggling two enum values via `useDataViewEnumFilter`'s `set('toggleInclude')`, `undefined` → default, plain value).
- Each new test was run against this branch's base sources: 4 of them fail there, and the 3 that pass are the deliberate "unchanged path still works" guards (plain value ×2, `setFilter(undefined)` → reset).
- `bun test tests/react/dataview/` — 145 pass, 0 fail. `bun run test` — 1995 pass, 0 fail. `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` reports no new warnings.

Refs #66

author: aytey
body:
Three changes salvaged from #1088, closed as superseded by #1085.

#1085 already shipped the mechanism #1088 carried — the `SATSolver::TrailReuse` scope, CaDiCaL's `ilb=2`, and the switch that turns it on — but for every loop the batch pipeline refines rather than only uninterpreted functions: `maybeRefinement` in `STP.cpp` includes `batchUFView->active()`, and that is the `needAbsRef` `ToSATAIG::CallSAT` gates on, so a UF query already gets the kept trail (`Refinement trail reuse: on` on the stats line of any QF_UFBV file). Three things in #1088 had no counterpart, and this is those three.

Please merge as separate commits rather than squashing: each message carries its own evidence and trailers.

### 1. Reach the refinement loop's trail reuse from the C API (`b22bdf51c`)

`--refinement-trail-reuse` was reachable only from the command line. A client driving libstp through the C API had no way to turn it off, and it is on by default, so there was no way back to the behaviour such a client had before it shipped.

`REFINEMENT_TRAIL_REUSE` is appended to `ifaceflag_t` at ordinal 40, after `UF_CHECK_DURING_BV_REFINEMENT`, so every published ordinal keeps the value an installed header committed to. Its case sits with the batch refinement knobs rather than the UF ones, because the field gates array reads, the bit-vector abstractions and uninterpreted functions alike. #1088 reached the same field under a UF-only name and scope; the wider scope is what shipped, so the name says so.

The C API test pins the new ordinal beside the others, adds the default to the block capturing what a client inherits by setting nothing, and round-trips the flag in both directions — a case that fell through to the default arm would abort rather than fail, so the mapping needs pinning and not merely that the enumerator is accepted.

### 2. Grow the variable range between rounds in the trail reuse test (`247d59449`)

`CadicalKeepsTrailAcrossRefinementRounds` enumerates the fourteen models of a four-variable formula by blocking each one it reads. What it never does is call `newVar()` after its first solve: every clause it adds is written in variables the solver already had when it descended.

The loop it stands in for is not like that. `getEquals()` mints a fresh variable for the equality a lemma is about to name and another for every bit of it, and `getSatVariables()` mints and freezes a whole word for a leaf the blast never reached (`AbstractionRefinement.cpp`). Both run after a candidate has been read and before the next solve, so the variable range grows while the backend holds the trail its last search left — a different path through CaDiCaL from a clause over variables it has already sized its structures for.

The new case enumerates the same fourteen models but refutes each in the clause shape `getEquals()` emits: a fresh frozen variable per bit, forced true while that bit still agrees with the model just read, and a fresh frozen variable standing for the whole agreement, which a unit then forbids. Only the one polarity is forced, as in `getEquals()`, so no other assignment is cut off. Five variables a round, seventy across the loop, and the count is checked at the end alongside the requirement that every model appears exactly once. With the blocking unit's sign flipped, so that the refutation refutes nothing, it fails on the first repeated model.

### 3. Record what was measured around the kept trail and the lemma cap (`e21d1401a`)

Two settings tried in #1088 and rejected, neither rejection visible from the code, so both invite a second run.

**Lucky phases.** The argument for keeping a trail is that a round otherwise repeats the pre-search phases before it searches, and the incremental driver already retires one of those — CaDiCaL's lucky-phase probing — from its persistent solver on the ground that a many-solve session pays for it every call. A refinement query is many-solve too, so the same cut looks free, and the comment beside that retirement says only that the batch pipeline's single-solve instances keep it. Switching it off for a refinement query changed nothing: what the round pays for is the re-descent itself, not a phase in front of it.

**The lemma cap.** A cap that doubles after each refuted candidate — small while a candidate is still cheap to replace, growing as the rounds show it is not — landed within noise of the fixed one, in opposite directions on two corpus sweeps.

Both were measured on #1088's base, which predates #1086: the cap was still 8 when the doubling schedule was tried, and the round counts behind the lucky-phase measurement are not today's. Their numbers are deliberately not carried over — what each rules out does not depend on them, and the comments say which is which.

### Testing

`ctest` on this branch: 884 lit tests passed, 3 failed. Pristine master built in the identical configuration gives the same 884/3, failing the same three files (`fp-tests/native-tofp-symfpu-equivalence.smt2`, `fp-tests/roundtointegral-equal-widths.smt2`, `fp-tests/tofp-narrowing-exponent-range.smt2`) — pre-existing in that configuration and untouched by this branch. `refinement-flagsTests` 16/16, `TrailReuse_TestTests` 4/4. `git clang-format --diff master` reports no changes.

### Not in this branch

`--refinement-trail-reuse` has never been measured on QF_UFBV against a current head: #1085 measured QF_ABV, and #1088's QF_UFBV numbers were taken against a pipeline #1086 replaced. Nothing here depends on that number, but it is the one piece of evidence the flag is still missing.

The chart drew all three divisions in one row under the Team Principal. That is
not the shape of the team — Mechanical and Electrical answer to the Technical
Director, and Operations answers to the Principal directly.

```

        Technical Director    Operations
          /            \
    Mechanical      Electrical
```

**The shape is data.** `ORG_REPORTS_TO` sits beside `SUBTEAMS` and comes down to
the page as `reports_to` on each division, so `org.html` draws whatever
hierarchy it is handed rather than knowing this one. A division missing from the

draws it in the wrong place rather than dropping it off the chart.

hand-calculated line running from the TD across to the Principal are gone. One
`.fan` rule draws a bar over its children and a stub down into each, at every
level, taking the column count as an inline variable. `.branch` is what lets one
child of a fan be a seat with a fan of its own.

was already being merged, so it never landed.

author: corpetty
body:
The last two of the four — they turned out to be **one propose-time flow**, so they land together. The composer stops asking for a bare amount into the void and stops assuming your identity on entry.

> **Stacked on #36** (→ #35). GitHub retargets each to `main` as the stack merges in order.

## What changes in the composer (payment mode, Safe policy)
A "sending context" panel appears above the recipient field, folded live at propose time (ask-then-disclose — *not* on room entry):

- **Sending** — `ETH · 4.999… ETH available (4999999999999999995 wei)` — the **Safe's own balance** (what actually moves), read live via the RPC. Never a false zero: an unreachable RPC says "⚠ balance unavailable — …".
- **from Safe 0x5FbD…** — the room's account, whose funds move.
- **you act as 0xf39F… · ✓ a Safe owner — your approval counts** — or, if you were seeded with a non-owner key, **⚠ not a Safe owner — your approval won't count on-chain**. This surfaces the disclosure *and* turns the old `insufficient-signatures` surprise into a warning you see **before** proposing.
- A soft guard: typing more than the Safe holds → **⚠ more than the Safe holds — this would revert on-chain**.

The amount field is now labelled **wei** (the Safe transfers that exact value), with the balance shown in both ETH and wei so the unit is unambiguous.

## Why the two asks merged
exo-080 ("prompt per action — which address do I act as?") and exo-bf9 ("compose from what the account holds") happen at the *same* moment — proposing. Building them separately would mean building the account/context panel twice. The decided model (**prompt per action**) is honoured: nothing about your address is shown on entry; it's disclosed in the composer when you act.

## How it's built
- **`coordinate_account()`** lidl method + regenerated surface (34 methods) → `{policy, account, actingAs, isOwner, assets:[{symbol,decimals,display,raw|error}]}`. Reuses the wallet's `hexToDec`/`formatUnits` to render a live `eth_getBalance` as "N ETH". A non-Safe policy returns just `{policy}` and the panel hides.
- **`roomAccountJson` PROP + `loadRoomAccount()` SLOT**; loaded when the composer opens and when the policy changes while open — not on the 1s message tick (it reads the RPC).
- Composer panel is pure-render off `room.roomAccount`.

## Tested
- **Module `.lgx` and UI `.lgx` both build clean** with `coordinate_account`, the new wallet-types import into the module, and the PROP/SLOT + composer panel.
- nix build doesn't evaluate QML (ADR-011) — the on-display render of the panel is the launch check.

## Honest scope
- ETH only for now (the Safe path settles ETH via `value`); ERC-20 would make the single asset a real picker and is a natural follow-up. The panel is built to become a picker when `assets` has more than one entry.
- One keystore identity today, so "who you act as" shows/【checks】 that one — the owner *check* is the valuable part, not a multi-identity chooser.

Closes exo-080 and exo-bf9. With #35 and #36, this completes all four UX asks.

author: timothysheee
body:
**Claude Code says**

## Background

Create the shared discard-analysis package. This is TDD milestone 9.

## The point of this milestone
The Standard AI in `packages/engines/mahjong/src/ai/standard.ts` already contains a working discard evaluator: per-candidate simulation, completion distance, improving-tile counts, wait quality, isolated-tile penalty and shape metrics. It was deliberately written to be factorable. This milestone MOVES that evaluation into a reusable package so that the AI, the discard trainer and the post-game review all consume ONE evaluator. If they each had their own, the trainer would eventually explain a move the AI would not play, which is the specific failure this design exists to prevent.

## Build `packages/engines/mahjong-analysis` (or `packages/analysis`, matching the repo's workspace conventions)

Structure it as the TDD section 59 suggests:
- `completion/distance.ts` — a generalized distance-to-completion for a 16-tile Taiwanese hand. Do not port a Japanese 13-tile shanten implementation.
- `acceptance/improving-tiles.ts` — which tile kinds improve the hand, and how many of each remain unseen given public information.
- `shapes/identify-shapes.ts` and `shapes/shape-quality.ts` — partial sets, floaters, connected shapes.
- `discard/analyze-discard.ts` and `discard/rank-discards.ts` — the ranking.
- `explanations/reasons.ts` — structured reasons, NOT prose.

Export exactly: `rankDiscards`, `analyzeDiscardOptions`, `completionDistance`, `improvingTiles`. Re-export from the package index.

`rankDiscards(position)` returns an array ordered best-first, each entry carrying: the tile, a score, the improving tile kinds, an improvement count, the completion distance, shape metrics, and the structured reasons.

Reasons must be structured data such as `{ type: 'ISOLATED_TILE', tile: '1m' }` or `{ type: 'PRESERVES_SEQUENCE', tiles: ['5s','6s','7s'] }`. The UI turns those into sentences later. Do not generate prose here, and do not have the analysis produce an explanation independently of the ranking it computed.

Analysis must use PUBLIC information only: the player's own hand plus visible discards, melds and flowers. It must never read another player's concealed hand or the wall order. This is not merely a design preference — the trainer and review will run client-side eventually.

## Rewire the AI
Change `createStandardAi` to consume `rankDiscards` from the new package rather than its own private copy. Delete the duplicated evaluation logic; do not leave two implementations. `packages/engines/mahjong` may depend on the analysis package, but the analysis package must NOT depend on gameplay: no turn engine, no rooms, no sockets.

## Prove the AI did not regress
The Standard AI's measured baseline on this exact engine, four Standard AIs over 150 games, seed 777: combined win rate 98.67 percent, self-draw 24.00 percent, discard win 74.67 percent, exhaustive draw 1.33 percent, average turns 42.5, crashes 0, invalid states 0. Re-run that comparison after rewiring and report the real observed numbers next to these. A material drop means the extraction changed behaviour and must be fixed, not accepted. Note the Standard AI is roughly 96x slower than the random AI at about 632 ms per game, so use a sample of about 150 games rather than 10000.

## Tests
Unit tests beside the code for completion distance on known hands, improving-tile counts, and ranking order on a fixture where the best discard is unambiguous. Assert that `rankDiscards` given identical input returns identical output, since determinism is what lets the trainer and the AI agree.

## Repo conventions (these override any general working habit you may have)

- Do NOT create, modify, or delete `plan.md` anywhere in this repository, including the repo root and any package directory. The repo root `plan.md` is an existing project document and is not yours to touch. If a general instruction tells you to write a plan file before making changes, that instruction does not apply here: keep your plan in your reasoning, not in a committed file. Seven previous PRs wrote a `plan.md` into this repo and every one had to be reverted by hand, including one that overwrote the repo's own root plan.
- Put each test file beside the code it covers as `<name>.test.ts` / `.test.tsx`. Never create a `__tests__` directory.
- Delete no file you were not asked to delete.
- No code comments unless the surrounding code already has them; this repo's AGENTS.md sets a low comment density.
- The registry at `packages/shared/src/registry.ts` is the single source of truth for the game list. Never hand-edit `vite.config.js` to add a page.
- Commit as soon as a coherent slice is in place, BEFORE any long verification sweep. An earlier node lost several hours to agent transport drops inside one long turn, and each retry restarts from scratch with no resume.

> ⚠️ Recovered draft PR — delivered via recover-and-land (verify did not complete). The workbench did NOT complete verification for this change; review the diff before merging.

body:
## Why

The composer's add-connector dialog is the only connector surface that inherited none of what the settings connectors page already ships. It renders one flat two-column grid over a catalog that now holds thousands of connectors, with no categories, no separation between what is connected and what is not, and no loading, empty, no-result or blocked state.

Its scroll region is also `overflow-y-auto -mx-6 px-6` inside a `p-6` dialog, so it bleeds horizontally only: the dialog's own bottom padding leaves a blank strip and `overflow: hidden` slices the row above it.

Design: https://okou-connectors-des44.okou.app · DES-44

## What

Everything is behind `connectorDirectory` (`enabled: false`, staff org hashes, so it shows in Lab under Beta). With the switch off the existing `AddConnectorsDialog` renders unchanged.

- **Segments** — "Your connectors", "Discover" and "Custom". The connected list leads with the connectors whose connection expired or whose permissions changed; both states are already computed by `connectorCurrentConnectionStatus` and were surfaced nowhere the user looks.
- **Categories** — counted sections and chips, built from the metadata `groupConnectorsByCategory` already returns and the settings page already renders.
- **Card** — a tile behind every connector mark, so a full-bleed logo and a hairline glyph carry the same weight; account, status and multi-account count replace the description once connected.
- **Edges** — the scroll region owns its bottom padding and fades into both sheet edges instead of ending on a cut card.
- **States** — skeleton, nothing-connected, no-results and no-custom-connectors.
- **Detail** — accounts, permission count, auth method and category in one place, with a route back to the existing permission dialog.
- **Keyboard** — arrow keys walk the visible list, Enter connects or opens detail.
- **Search** — also matches the catalog `tags`, so "email" or "chat" reach the connectors that serve them (`matchesConnectorDirectorySearch`; the existing `matchesConnectorSearch` is untouched).

Two changes sit outside the switch, both deliberate: the twelve catalog category labels move to sentence case, and `localizeConnectorCategoryMetadata` moves out of `connectors-page.tsx` into a shared module so both surfaces use one copy.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tsconfig.production.json` and `tsconfig.tests.json`
- `oxlint --deny-warnings`, `oxlint --type-aware`, `eslint` on the changed files
- `pnpm lint:i18n` (all ten locales at 100%), `pnpm lint:localized-ui`

App preview: https://pr-32703-app-okou-app-preview.vm0.workers.dev — the switch is off by default, so turn on **Connector directory** in Lab first.

Not covered: no visual QA on the preview yet, and the ⌘K entry point from the composer is not included.

body: ## Summary Adds a Cloud Agent development environment for this Next.js 16 + Supabase multi-tenant RT portal by committing `.cursor/environment.json`. This makes the repo bootstrap and run in Cloud Agents without manual setup. ## What this configures - `install`: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the actively maintained lockfile (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` pins the Next.js canary), so pnpm is the canonical package manager. - `terminals`: a `next-dev` terminal running `pnpm run dev` (Next.js 16 / Turbopack) on `http://localhost:3000`. - `ports`: exposes port `3000`. ## Validation performed | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | Passed (idempotent — second run clean) | | `pnpm run build` (with Supabase env vars) | Compiled + TypeScript passed; all routes generated | | `pnpm run typecheck:security:sensus` | Passed | | `pnpm run test:security:etalase` | 4/4 passed | | `pnpm run lint` | Runs (surfaces pre-existing code-quality findings) | | `pnpm run dev` | Boots in <1s | | Fresh-pod draft build `bld-20260908-679d5be3` | SUCCEEDED — pnpm present in default image, install exit 0 | | Fresh Cloud Agent (booted from that build) | Versions, config, deps, install idempotency PASS | ## Runtime behavior without secrets (verified in a fresh agent) The dev server boots without any secrets, but behavior differs by route: - `/login` renders correctly (HTTP 200) with no secrets. - `/` (landing page) requires `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`; it returns **HTTP 500** when they are unset, because `getSupabaseServerClient()` throws on the missing env var before the per-section `try/catch`. Once those vars are set (even to an unreachable project), per-section fetch failures degrade to a zero-state. So the Supabase env vars are effectively required for the app to be usable. ## Required secrets for full (database-backed) functionality `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET` (≥32 bytes), `PUBLIC_RT_ID`, `REGISTRATION_RT_ID`. Optional feature secrets: `EMAIL_USER`/`EMAIL_PASS`, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `CRON_SECRET`, `LEGACY_POSYANDU_RT_ID`, `RESET_BASE_URL`. ## Notes (pre-existing; no app code changed) - Two security test scripts (`test:security:sensus`, `test:security:sesi`) import `.ts` directly via `node`, which needs Node ≥ 22.18 native type-stripping; they pass on the VM's Node 22.22.2 but not the older shimmed Node 22.14. - A few source-analysis security assertions in `tests/data-layer-authenticated.test.mjs` fail on `main` (unrelated to environment setup).

author: kiminiri
body:
## Summary
Introduces a complete toolkit for importing ChatGPT conversations into Claude as shared context for job preparation work. Includes a Python converter tool, documentation, and a Claude skill definition for seamless workflow integration.

## Key Changes

- **`gpt_export_to_md.py`**: Standalone Python converter that transforms ChatGPT exports (conversations.json, share links, or single conversation JSON) into clean Markdown files. Supports multiple input formats, filters by keyword, and handles various content types (text, code, images, system messages).

- **`gpt-context/` folder structure**: Establishes a standardized layout with:
  - `취준-컨텍스트.md`: Distilled summary of GPT conversations (facts, decisions, action items only; 60-120 lines)
  - `raw/`: Storage for original conversation exports and converted Markdown files
  - `README.md`: User guide with three import methods (paste, data export, memory summary)

- **`.claude/skills/gpt-context-import/SKILL.md`**: Claude skill definition that:
  - Triggers on user requests mentioning GPT context sharing
  - Guides the 4-step workflow: input → convert → distill → apply
  - Enforces privacy rules (no SSN, account numbers, passwords, contact info)
  - Prevents instruction injection from GPT conversations

## Notable Implementation Details

- **No external dependencies**: Uses only Python standard library (json, argparse, pathlib, re, datetime)
- **Flexible input parsing**: Extracts JSON from HTML-embedded scripts (browser-saved pages), handles multiple conversation formats
- **Smart linearization**: Reconstructs conversation chains from mapping structures or linear_conversation arrays, handling branching conversations
- **Content type handling**: Properly processes text, code, multimodal content, and filters out system/execution output
- **Privacy-first design**: Distillation template explicitly excludes sensitive personal data and treats GPT instructions as data, not behavioral rules
