body:
## What A `settings` block in `autumn.config.ts` that manages a subset of the org config through the CLI. Unlike every other lane it is PATCH-shaped: a stated flag is written, an omitted flag keeps its value, and an omitted block manages nothing. ```ts export default atmn({ features: [...], plans: [...], settings: { multiCurrency: true, paydownOverages: true }, }); ``` ## Server - `POST /v1/organization.preview_update` and `POST /v1/organization.update`, internal-router-only (same posture as `catalogV2.*`). Body is `{ config: { ...8 boolean flags } }`. - `computeOrgSettingChanges` returns one row per flag that differs: `update` when the request states a different value, `unmanaged` when the request omits a flag that sits off its **spec** default (not the row's — a row written with every default spelled out still reads as default). - `updateOrganization` merges only the stated keys into the jsonb column, mirrors `include_past_due` like the dashboard PATCH does, and clears the org cache. - The shared param schema strips `OrgConfigSchema`'s `.default()`s so parsing never fills an omitted flag, and re-attaches the default through oRPC's `JSON_SCHEMA_REGISTRY` so it still lands in the spec. ## Generator - `SINGLETONS` registration beside `COLLECTIONS`: one object on the config, no id, no history; its type is read off the operation's request body. - Overlay gains a `settings` entry: `persist_free_overage → paydownOverages` (the one rename). Renames now reach the runtime as `renamedPaths` hints, applied on the way out and inverted on the way in. - `wire.ts` gets `settings?: Settings` and `splitWire()`, which cuts the document into the catalog body and each singleton's request body. - `emit.ts` ships `SINGLETONS` with a `{ key, wireKey, default }` field table pull drives from. - Labels are scraped from a new `shared/utils/orgUtils/orgSettingsLabels.ts`; the dashboard's `BillingSettingsSection` reads the same map, so CLI and UI can't disagree on names. - Spec defaults now surface in fixture JSDoc wherever the description didn't already say them. ## CLI - `push`: previews catalog and settings in parallel, renders a `Settings (n)` section, applies settings first then the catalog. Only stated flags that move count as work; unmanaged flags print as `~ Pay down overages: true -> unmanaged (set false explicitly to disable; atmn won't override)` and apply nothing. - `pull`: always asks the settings preview (with `{ config: {} }` when the config states none), then patches the block key by key — seeded when absent, pair appended when new, literal replaced when wrong, pair removed when the server's value is the spec default. - `atmn login` now requests `organisation:write`; a scope refusal on the settings lane says to re-login or drop the block. ## Also in this diff - `openapi-internal.yml` regen picked up pre-existing drift (`markups` on plan items) that landed in shared after the last regen; the generated plan/variant/license types follow. - Dev flow pieces the base-state doc describes but this checkout lacked: root `atmn-nightly: workspace:*`, `dev` script, `scripts/watchBuild.ts`. ## Tests - Generator: `singletons.test.ts` (type, no builder, rename, defaults, field table, hint rooting). - CLI unit: `settingsWire`, `settingsActions` (push routing, absent block, unmanaged-only, pull seed/append/replace/remove), `renderSettings`, `surgery/patchSingletonProperty`. - Server unit: `computeOrgSettingChanges` including the spelled-out-defaults case. - E2E: `atmn/crud/settings/settings-push-pull-unmanaged.test.ts` through the real server: push → round-trip → drop a flag → unmanaged in preview → pull writes it back → state false → applied → pull removes the default pair → no block, no organization calls. Gates run: `server bun ts`, `server tests/unit/{catalogV2,orgs}` (473 pass), generator `test` (80) + `generate` idempotent, CLI `ts` + `test` (260), the new e2e plus two existing atmn e2es as regression. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a PATCH-shaped `settings` block to `autumn.config.ts` for managing eight organization flags as code. Stated flags are written, omitted flags keep their server values, and `atmn push` and `atmn pull` synchronize the block through internal organization endpoints. **Server and generator** - Adds internal organization preview and update RPCs that merge stated JSONB keys and clear the organization cache. - Uses the stored `block_overdue_entitlements` value for previews, matching entitlement checks, while updates continue mirroring the deprecated `include_past_due` field. - Generates singleton settings types, wire splitting, defaults, runtime rename handling for `persist_free_overage` ↔ `paydownOverages`, and shared CLI/dashboard labels. - Regenerates internal OpenAPI artifacts, including existing plan-item `markups` drift. **CLI** - Push previews settings separately, reports unmanaged non-default flags, applies settings before catalog changes, and may leave settings applied if a later catalog update fails. - Pull edits inline, local-const, or imported settings blocks to match non-default server values; spread-built blocks are refused. - Existing login tokens need `atmn login` again for the new `organisation:write` scope, which is now allowed on the reserved atmn client. Written for commit 9cfbc410bfbad4fc7dc0945d63c39c22cf21beab. Summary will update on new commits.

author: deancron
body:
## Summary

Makes the Recon Report more decision-ready by adding **explainability evidence** to every factor, without changing the A–F grade math. Evidence is purely additive.

For each factor the report now surfaces:
- **State** — `Verified`, `Caution: limited data`, or `Data unavailable` (conveyed with text + `aria-label`, not colour alone)
- **Source & rule** — which provider answered and how the point was evaluated
- **Freshness** — data vintage where the provider exposes one
- **Why it matters** — short real-world-impact note

A compact **Data quality** summary sits next to the grade. Saving is gated until every analysis check completes, so each saved snapshot's grade, breakdown, and evidence are internally consistent. Evidence persists in saved analyses; legacy records degrade gracefully with a "re-analyze to refresh" note.

## What changed
- `src/map/evidence.ts` — evidence/quality model + `summarizeReportQuality`, `qualitySummaryText`/`qualitySummaryTone` helpers
- `src/map/scoring.ts` — `computeLocationGrade` returns `evidence` + `quality`; **scores, tier weights, and thresholds unchanged**
- `src/map/savedAnalyses.ts` — persist evidence/quality (backward-compatible optional fields); `canSaveAnalysis` gated on full completion
- `src/pages/MapPage.tsx` — wire save-gating at both call sites
- `src/components/FactorEvidence.tsx` (+ test), `src/components/AnalysisDetailPanel.tsx`, `src/map/CompareScorecard.tsx` (+ CSS) — render evidence in report + compare views
- Test infra: `@testing-library/react` + `jest-dom` (dev deps), `src/setupTests.ts`, vitest config

author: allensanborn
body:
## Summary

Two documentation lines claimed AWS parity for behaviour that is Floci's own choice. Both were raised in earlier reviews and left as follow-ups; this is that follow-up.

- `docs/services/lambda.md`: the `ApplicationLogLevel` / `SystemLogLevel` sentence said the no-op-under-`Text` behaviour matched "the fact that the response never surfaces them for Text". That points at Floci's own response shape, not at anything observed on AWS, so the request behaviour was being justified by the response behaviour and both are our call. Now marked as such.
- `docs/services/s3.md`: `log-delivery-write` was described as accepted on `PutBucketAcl`/`PutObjectAcl` "matching AWS". AWS documents that canned ACL as bucket-only and the SDK's `ObjectCannedACL` enum omits it. The bucket path matches AWS; the object path is a Floci leniency, and it now reads that way.

Docs only, no behaviour change.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [ ] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [x] Docs / chore

## AWS Compatibility

No API behaviour is changed. The point is to stop the docs asserting parity that was never probed, so nobody later cites those lines as a measured result.

The S3 leniency is real and shared: `putBucketAcl` and `putObjectAcl` both resolve through the same `cannedObjectAclXml` helper, so the object path also accepts `log-delivery-write`, and the bucket path accepts `aws-exec-read` which the SDK models as object-only. That mirror-image case is named in the docs rather than silently left. Enum membership confirmed against the botocore `s3` model shipped with awscli 2.36.30.

## Checklist

- [x] `./mvnw test` passes locally
- [ ] New or updated integration test added
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

No test: the change is prose in two docs files, with no production change to exercise. Flagging that explicitly rather than leaving the unticked box unexplained.

author: avijit-kumar-git
body:
Docs-only follow-up after #43 (per-folder memory) merged. Records a design
principle, maps a comparable tool's release to Fella, and starts a
performance/feel track.

## What changed

- **`DECISIONS.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md` non-goals — "vertical, not horizontal".**
  The zero-config base build stays small in *feature count* and spends its
  weight on intelligence and quality-of-life: better answers, fewer
  interactions, faster and lighter — not more commands. A capability earns its
  place by making the existing job better or shorter, not by adding a parallel
  thing to do; breadth lives in extensions.

- **`QUESTIONS.md` — `fx` v0.0.8 (`vercel-labs/fx`) mapped to Fella.** It was an
  almost entirely *subtractive* release.
  - *Validates:* fx removed its memory **tool** (kept the saved memories) —
    direct support for the choice in #43 to make memory a deterministic
    prompt-injected block, not a tool the model decides to call; keep the store
    decoupled from any future `recall()`. 12→3 shell actions reinforces
    "smallest useful tool set".
  - *Actionable → issues #44–#47* (below).
  - *Deferred:* fx's keep-recent + fresh-window compaction, as the reference if
    long multi-step runs ever flail (`folder-scale` says not yet).

- **`PERFORMANCE.md` — new "Interaction cost & perceived performance" section.**
  A code trace of every user flow with min / typical / max interaction counts;
  onboarding chains (Ollama-ready **3**, hosted-known **5**,
  hosted-discovering **~11–14**); findings (the model picker already caps its
  menu at 8 items so there is no "dozens of clicks"; `recent_workspaces` is
  written but never read, so every launch re-opens the folder; the command
  palette only pre-fills a command); and the metrics still to capture
  (keypress→render p95, `appReady` ms distribution, installed binary size per
  release). A dated log is started. Ongoing "truthfully faster **and** feels
  faster/smaller" track.

Issues opened from this: **#44** reopen the last folder on start, **#45**
mid-run steer (a message sent while busy cancels + re-asks with it appended),
**#46** merge `describe_schema` + `sample_rows` → `inspect_table` (measure in
`agent_eval`), **#47** publish TUI latency percentiles + binary size as tracked
metrics.

## Lane

- [x] App code (docs only — no code, engine, or UI change)

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm run check` is 0 errors / 0 warnings
- [x] `cargo test` passes from `src-tauri/` (unchanged; docs-only)
- [x] Dated entry added to `docs/DECISIONS.md` (the vertical-not-horizontal principle)
- [x] `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` updated in this PR (non-goals)
- [x] Conventional Commits (`docs:`)

## How I verified it

`pnpm run check` (0/0) and `cargo test --locked` (unchanged, green). No runtime
behaviour changes — this PR adds documentation only.

author: bochenmint
body:
Cztery rzeczy zgłoszone po obejrzeniu strony na żywo.

## Kółko oddalone od kursora

Pierścień kursora był doganiany w pętli `requestAnimationFrame` z wygładzaniem, czyli poruszał się tak szybko, jak pozwalały klatki. Ta strona liczy jednocześnie shader nagłówka, cztery renderery sześcianów i torus w hero — klatek brakuje dokładnie wtedy, gdy kursor jedzie po hero. Przy ukrytym kursorze systemowym to nie jest ozdoba, tylko zepsuty wskaźnik.

Obie kropki są teraz zapisywane wprost ze zdarzenia `mousemove`; pętla i wygładzanie usunięte. Pierścień nie może zostać w tyle, bo nie ma już czego doganiać.

Sprawdziłem najpierw hipotezę pozycjonowania (transformowany przodek zmieniający układ odniesienia `position: fixed`) — w drzewie nie ma takiego elementu i pierścień jest jeden, więc to było opóźnienie, nie przesunięcie.

## Kontrast nagłówka w jasnym motywie

Shader malował wszystko poniżej horyzontu wartością `0.95` — prawie biel na tle `#eef0f3`. Dolna trzecia część każdej litery znikała.

Jasny motyw jest teraz **odwrócony, a nie przestrojony**: ciemny metal (`0.13`–`0.31`) i jedno jasne pasmo odbicia (`0.97`), dokładnie tak, jak ten sam nagłówek renderuje statyczny gradient `.chrome-text` przy braku WebGL. Prążki i refleks kursora dodają teraz światła zamiast je odejmować — przy białym korpusie liter odejmowanie miało sens, przy ciemnym nie ma.

## Typografia

**Hanken Grotesk** zastępuje Geista i Bricolage w nagłówkach i w tekście. Czysty, neutralny grotesk z pełną osią wag 100–900 — potrzebną, bo akcent w nagłówku robi kontrast wagi (Light przy Semibold), a nie drugi krój. Pokrycie polskich znaków potwierdzone w manifeście subsetów Google Fonts, nie w materiałach foundry. Jedna rodzina zamiast dwóch to też **69 kB mniej** do pobrania.

## Hasło i ton

> Tworzę strony, aplikacje i systemy, które wspierają rozwój Twojego biznesu.

Reszta copy dociągnięta do tego tonu w trzech językach — prościej, w drugiej osobie, bez żargonu: „Direct revenue, nie tylko wizytówka" → „Klienci rezerwują u Ciebie, nie u pośrednika"; „Excel o północy → pipeline" → „Koniec z arkuszami po godzinach"; „Cztery ekosystemy. Jeden standard." → „Cztery systemy, które działają na produkcji.".

## Płynny metal

Horyzont nie jest już płaski. Szersze i wolniejsze fale (1,3 cyklu na nagłówek zamiast 2,0), amplituda 0,26 zamiast 0,10, długa fala przetaczająca się wzdłuż wiersza oraz jasny menisk na krawędziach liter — poziom metalu zbiera się przy krawędzi tak, jak robi to napięcie powierzchniowe. Wszystko próbkowane w układzie współrzędnych całego nagłówka, więc powierzchnia czyta się jak jeden rozlew, a nie jak efekt wstemplowany osobno w każdą literę.

## Checki

`tsc` czysto, `npm run lint` 0 błędów, `npm run build` przechodzi.

## Czego nie zweryfikowałem

Panel podglądu ma 280 px szerokości, więc kontrast sprawdziłem przy tej szerokości 1:1 (kontrast nie zależy od skali), ale **kompozycji hero na desktopie i samego ruchu płynnego metalu nie obejrzałem** — statyczny zrzut nie pokazuje animacji. To jest do oceny okiem.

author: eliasiofir
body:
# Description

Closes: N/A (reported by Stake Village during their audit of the Cardano spec, tracked on the Lava product board as "Cardano Specs Update"; needed for the Sep 17 CARDANO / CARDANOT incentivization)

## The bug

The six Blockfrost `/blocks/{hash_or_number}` routes in the `CARDANO` spec (and therefore in `CARDANOT`, which imports it) declared:

```json
"block_parsing": { "parser_arg": ["latest"], "parser_func": "DEFAULT" }
```

so `GET /blocks/1` was classified as a request for the latest block. The URL sent to the provider was untouched, but on the Lava side:

1. the archive rule (`"block": 8192`) never fired, so archive providers were not guaranteed for historical blocks and a non-archive provider could return an error even when archive providers were available;
2. when an archive provider did answer, the archive extension and its `cu_multiplier: 5` were not applied;
3. requested-block tracking, QoS and data-reliability logic saw `latest` instead of the real height.

## The fix

`specs/mainnet-1/specs/cardano.json` and `specs/testnet-2/specs/cardano.json` (kept identical, as before):

**Block parsing on the six `{hash_or_number}` routes** — `/blocks/{hash_or_number}`, `/next`, `/previous`, `/txs`, `/txs/cbor`, `/addresses`:

```json
"block_parsing": {
    "parser_arg": ["hash_or_number", "=", "0"],
    "parser_func": "PARSE_DICTIONARY_OR_ORDERED",
    "default_value": "latest"
},
"parsers": [
    { "parse_path": ".params.hash_or_number", "parse_type": "BLOCK_HASH" }
]
```

- `PARSE_DICTIONARY_OR_ORDERED` on the path parameter is the existing Aptos (`/blocks/by_height/{block_height}`) and Cosmos SDK (`/cosmos/base/tendermint/v1beta1/blocks/{height}`) pattern. `RestMessage.GetParams()` exposes path parameters as a map keyed by the placeholder name, so a numeric value resolves to that block height.
- A Cardano block hash is 64 hex chars without a `0x` prefix, which `ParseDefaultBlockParameter` rejects. `default_value: "latest"` makes hash requests keep exactly today's behaviour (latest, `UsedDefaultValue = true`) instead of degrading to `NOT_APPLICABLE`.
- The `BLOCK_HASH` generic parser surfaces the hash as a requested block hash. The consumer already ships it in `BlocksHashesToHeights` and resolves it through the relay cache (`resolveRequestedBlock` picks the cached height when the block was parsed from the default value), so hash requests can be routed to archive once the height is known. For a numeric value the hash parser fails the minimum-length check and falls through to the legacy parser, as in `TestParseBlockFromParamsHash`.

**Routes deliberately left on `DEFAULT latest`:** `/epochs/{number}/...` (epoch numbers, ~500 on mainnet) and `/blocks/slot/{slot_number}` / `/blocks/epoch/{epoch_number}/slot/{slot_number}` (slot numbers, far above the block height). Both would be mis-classified against the archive boundary if parsed as block heights. A hash-to-height decision for those is a separate routing policy question.

**Spec gaps** — diffed the API list against the current Blockfrost OpenAPI (`blockfrost/openapi`, `master`). Added the chain-data endpoints that were missing, with the same CU convention as their siblings (10 for a single object, 20 for a list):

| Endpoint | CU |
| --- | --- |
| `/assets/{asset}/utxos` | 20 |
| `/scripts/{script_hash}/utxos` | 20 |
| `/governance/committee` | 10 |
| `/governance/committee/votes` | 20 |
| `/governance/committee/{cc_id}/votes` | 20 |

Not added, on purpose: `/addresses/{address}/txs` and `/assets/{asset}/txs` (marked `deprecated` in the OpenAPI, superseded by `/transactions`), `/`, `/health`, `/health/clock`, `/metrics`, `/metrics/endpoints` (Blockfrost account/service status, not chain data), and `/ipfs/*` (separate Blockfrost add-on product). Every endpoint currently in the spec exists in the OpenAPI and none is deprecated.

Everything else in the spec (verifications, `pruning` at `latest_distance: 8193` vs the 8192 archive rule, finalization and block-time values, min stake, `CARDANOT` chain-id override) was reviewed and left unchanged.

## Verification

New tests in `protocol/chainlib/rest_test.go` load the real spec through `CreateChainLibMocks("CARDANO", rest, ...)`:

- `TestCardanoSpec_HistoricalBlockRequestsAreNotLatest` — `/blocks/1`, `/blocks/11500000` and the five sub-routes resolve to the numeric height; a 64-hex hash resolves to latest with the hash captured in `GetRequestedBlocksHashes()`; `/blocks/latest`, `/epochs/1` and `/blocks/slot/1` stay latest.
- `TestCardanoSpec_HistoricalBlockActivatesArchive` — with the archive extension enabled by policy and `LatestBlock = 12,000,000`: latest and `latest-1` get no extension and 10 CU; `latest-8193` and `/blocks/1` get the `archive` extension and 50 CU.

Against the original spec the first test fails on every numeric route with `expected: 1, actual: -2` (`LATEST_BLOCK`), which reproduces the report.

```
go test ./x/spec/keeper -run 'TestSpecs$' -count=1        ok   (both spec copies load, expand and validate)
go test ./protocol/chainlib -run TestCardanoSpec -count=1  ok
go test ./protocol/chainlib -count=1                      ok   (9.9s)
go test ./protocol/parser -count=1                        ok
go vet ./protocol/chainlib                                ok
```

CI on `8e92aae`: all 30 checks green (lint, CodeQL, test-protocol, test-consensus, protocol e2e, payment e2e, codecov patch, binaries, docker images).

author: claude[bot]
body:
Three follow-ups from this session's findings, in three commits.

## 1. Page the order list before decorating it — closes #10

The item summary and line count are correlated subqueries against `OrderLines`. In the SELECT list of the paging query, the optimiser evaluated them for **every candidate row** and applied `OFFSET/FETCH` afterwards — so drawing 25 rows performed ~1,900 seeks into `OrderLines`.

Measured at 40,000 orders and 100,000 lines, total logical reads per call:

| Statement | Before | After | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| by status | 13,320 | **1,399** | 9.5× |
| unfiltered, page 3 | 15,946 | **1,399** | 11.4× |
| by search text | 16,775 | **2,243** | 7.5× |
| by date range | 2,549 | **1,155** | 2.2× |

`OrderLines` alone: **8,962–11,396 reads → 152**, and ~1,900 seeks → **50** — two per row on screen, which is what it should always have been.

### One asymmetry worth reading

The page query uses `EXISTS` for the customer search; the count query keeps its `JOIN`. That is measured, not stylistic — and I got it wrong first.

Writing both the same way made the count **ten times worse**: 80,040 logical reads against 844. The page has a row goal and stops once `OFFSET/FETCH` is satisfied, so a seek per candidate ends early. A count has no row goal — it must look at every matching order, and `EXISTS` then becomes 40,000 seeks into `Customers`. Same predicate, opposite right answer. The reasoning is in the procedure so nobody tidies it back.

**No behaviour change.** The 143 integration tests covering paging, totals, the search predicates and the date rules pass untouched — which is what made this safe to attempt.

## 2. CI fails on known-vulnerable dependencies

Two dependencies with published advisories reached this project by ordinary means *this session*: SSH.NET through Testcontainers 4.1.0, and ImageSharp 1.0.4 while hunting for an Apache-2.0 version. Both were caught by a person happening to read restore output. That is not a control.

- Backend: `dotnet restore -warnaserror:NU1901,NU1902,NU1903,NU1904`
- Frontend: `npm audit --audit-level=high`

Verified both directions — the current tree passes, and a restore carrying ImageSharp 1.0.4 exits non-zero. A gate that has never been seen to fail is not known to work.

## 3. Where the tokens live, and why

`docs/security.md` gains a section, because the question keeps coming up.

Nothing is in `localStorage` — the only thing kept there is the shopping cart. The access token is a module variable, memory only, 15 minutes. The refresh token is `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/auth`, rotating, with reuse detection that revokes the family. Both facts are asserted by tests that now run in CI.

It also records **why the access token is not moved into a cookie**: `HttpOnly` stops exfiltration but not in-page abuse — script on the page can call the API as the user regardless — the gain is bounded further by the 15-minute lifetime, and the cost is CSRF surface on every mutating endpoint, which is new code in the most expensive place to get it wrong. The credential actually worth protecting is the refresh token, and that one already is `HttpOnly`.

If the trade-off ever changes, the doc says what the work would be.

author: praneeth132006
body:
Two fixes to the Question Bank, both from working with 303 questions on a 200-row page.

## The stat tiles described the pagination, not the question bank

The tiles counted the rows the current page had been handed. With 303 matches and a page size of 200, **"Posted (page)" read 200** — and it changed when you pressed Next. That is a fact about the pagination, not about the bank, which is not what anyone reads those tiles for.

`Posted`, `Approved` and `Needs Detail` now count every row the filter matched, and the `(page)` qualifier is gone from the labels.

The counts are computed in the Apps Script rather than the dashboard, because `listQuestions` already materialises every matched row before slicing out the page. So this is one extra pass over an array that is already in memory — **no additional sheet reads**, no extra round trip, no measurable cost.

## A sheet running an older script degrades honestly

Existing staleness detection only fires on an *unknown action*. This adds a field to an action that already exists, so an older script returns successfully and simply omits `counts` — nothing errors.

Rather than let that silently render a page-scoped number as if it described the whole bank, the dashboard falls back to counting the page and says so: the label keeps `(page)` and the subtitle reads "this page only — sheet script is out of date".

## The pager only existed below the table

With 200 rows on a page, reaching Next meant scrolling past every row first. There is now an identical pager above the table, driven by the same state so the two cannot disagree.

## Testing

Two regression tests in `test/apps-script.test.js`, against the existing sandboxed Apps Script harness. The important one walks four rows one page at a time and asserts the counts are byte-identical on every page — which is the actual property that was broken:

```
✔ listQuestions counts the whole filter, not the page it returns
✔ listQuestions counts posted rows across the whole filter
```

The second also covers the legacy `YES | timestamp` Posted cell, which counts as posted the same way it does elsewhere in the script.

Full suite: 248/248.

## For the reviewer

- **This needs `apps-script/*.gs.js` re-pasted into all five sheets.** All five are regenerated from `google_apps_script.js` via `npm run build-scripts` — they are generated files, not hand-edited. Until they are pasted, the tiles show the labelled page-scoped fallback.
- **The rendered page is unverified.** The dashboard is behind Firebase sign-in, so I confirmed both pagers are served in the HTML (top at line 92, footer at 108) and that the suite passes, but I could not load the page to look at it. The top pager's spacing against the bulk-action bar above it is worth a glance.
- `dashboard/shared.css` gains only `.pagination-top`; the existing `.pagination` rule is untouched.

body:
## Resumo

- Corrige a exportação em PDF das respostas de formulário (`GET /api/v1/sgp/upfs/{id}/formularios/exportar/?formato=pdf`), que hoje imprime `respostas_json` como um bloco de JSON indentado bruto, substituindo por uma renderização estruturada e legível.
- A renderização espelha as mesmas regras já usadas na visualização completa da resposta (FE-17/BE-17): chaves humanizadas como rótulo (`renda_familiar` → "Renda familiar"), booleanos como "Sim"/"Não", campos vazios/nulos como "—", listas de valores simples em linha, e listas de objetos/grupos repetíveis como blocos numerados ("Item 1", "Item 2", ...) renderizados recursivamente.
- A exportação em CSV, os filtros existentes e o restante do endpoint não foram alterados.

## O que mudou

- **Novo** `backend/apps/sgp/services/form_response_render.py`: módulo de renderização canônica de `respostas_json` — uma função pura que monta a árvore de campos (`build_response_tree`) e um construtor de flowables do reportlab (`build_respostas_flowables`) usado para montar o PDF.
- **`backend/apps/sgp/views/form_responses.py`**: `_pdf_response` passa a usar o novo renderizador no lugar do `json.dumps(...)` despejado num `Paragraph` monoespaçado.
- **`backend/requirements/base.txt`**: adiciona `pypdf` (dependência de teste, para extrair e validar o texto do PDF gerado).
- **Novo** `backend/apps/sgp/tests/test_form_response_render.py`: testes unitários da árvore de renderização (humanização de chave, ordenação, tipos de valor, casos vazios).
- **Novo** `backend/apps/sgp/tests/test_form_response_pdf_rendering.py`: testes de integração que geram o PDF via API e extraem o texto para validar rótulos, formatação de tipos, grupos repetíveis, Unicode/acentuação, isolamento entre múltiplas respostas e ausência de JSON bruto.
- **`backend/docs/export.md`**: atualizado para descrever a nova regra de apresentação do PDF.

## Limitação conhecida (documentada)

O sistema ainda não persiste um schema/definição versionada dos formulários do SGF (`apps/sgf` não tem modelos hoje). Por isso, os rótulos exibidos são as chaves de `respostas_json` humanizadas — não os rótulos reais de pergunta/opção definidos no formulário original, e campos de seleção mostram o valor armazenado, não um rótulo de opção resolvido. Essa limitação é a mesma já existente na visualização completa (FE-17/BE-17) e está documentada em `backend/docs/export.md`.

## Testes

- Testes unitários e de integração novos passando (`test_form_response_render.py`, `test_form_response_pdf_rendering.py`).
- Testes existentes de exportação (`test_form_response_exports.py`, incluindo os de CSV) inalterados e passando.
- Validado manualmente via Insomnia (login, criação de resposta de teste, exportação em PDF cobrindo texto, número, booleano, lista simples, campo vazio, grupo aninhado, lista de grupos repetíveis e acentuação).

author: peaky8linders
body:
Finishes the refactor PR #389 half-shipped — **this time with the modules actually committed** — and validates every behavioural delta it was carrying.

## What was really in the working tree

Measured **by value**, not by diff. Of the 21 public constants in `graph_rag_prompts`, **19 are byte-identical** across the move, so extracting `ANSWER_GENERATE_SYSTEM`, `CYPHER_TEMPLATES`, `MINIMAL_COMPOSER_SYSTEM`, `QUERY_PARSE_SYSTEM` and `SUGGESTED_QUESTIONS` into `app/data/graph_rag_prompt_templates.py` is a **pure move**. Exactly two changed — that is the entire reviewable surface.

## 1. `USER_CRITICAL_RULES_CLAUSE` — live on every Stage-2 call

`_graph_rag_impl.py:9462`, `REGENOLD_USER_CRITICAL_RULES` default ON, V3 OFF. It corrects **four material legal errors**, each checked here against the verbatim adopted text via `get_provision_text`:

| | was | the Act |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **(k)** Annex VIII | "Section B for Annex III **high-risk** systems" | Section B is the Art 49(2) register for systems the provider concluded are **not** high-risk under Art 6(3) — the exact opposite. Annex IX was likewise conflated with 6(3) registration; it covers Art 60 real-world testing |
| **(j)** Art 50(4) | "law enforcement is a **full exemption**" | the duty is disapplied only "where the use is **authorised by law** to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offence" — a law-enforcement purpose alone is not enough |
| **(g)** Art 44(1) | "an **official Union language** easily understood by the **notifying authority**" | "a language which can be easily understood by the relevant authorities in the Member State in which the **notified body** is established". Annex VII 4.6 sets certificate **contents**, not validity |
| **(d)** Art 6(3) | the four tasks remove a system from high-risk outright | they qualify it for the derogation **only where** it "does not pose a significant risk of harm… including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision making" |

**(j) is already leaking into shipped answers.** Production today, asked whether a police deepfake is exempt, replies: *"This is a full exemption rather than the lighter regime"* — the flawed clause's own words coming back out.

`VOICE`, `DIRECT VERDICT FIRST`, `LENGTH (at most four sentences)` and `REFERENCE SELECTION` are **untouched**, so every conciseness and over-citation instruction is byte-identical.

## 2. `COMPACT_ANSWER_CONTRACT` — inert in production

Removes the hard "strictly under 950 characters" cap. Reached only via `build_compact_answer_user` under `REGENOLD_PROMPT_COMPACT`, whose code default is `"0"`. Already cache-keyed (`regenold.py:1552`). Affects an opt-in experiment arm only.

## 3. `prompt_budget` is not a pure move — and one delta is a real bug

The original **adds its truncation banner on top of the budget**, so the "shrunk" message comes back up to 60 chars *longer* than the limit the function exists to enforce. Each branch now subtracts the banner first. Also: a tail marker at offset 0 was ignored (`pos > 0` → `pos >= 0`); `"Latest question:"` must now precede the protected tail (a later marker made `user[idx:tail_start]` an empty slice); `budget <= 0` returns `""`; and `" CHALLENGE TURN:"` joins the protected markers — without it the R379 V2 challenge clause was the one tail rule the shrinker could cut.

Reachable only on the Groq tertiary Stage-2 leg, which R360 strict transport refuses by default.

## 4. Cache-key completeness (AGENTS.md invariant #4)

author: ricardojjulia
body:
## Summary
Found and fixed during a full end-to-end test (import -> critic -> rewrite -> accept -> post-critic -> export) run against a real imported manuscript, not just spot-checked.

- **Critic and the Rewrite Architect Plan silently ran on blank context for any imported book.** `chapters.summary` is only ever populated by AI drafting (`generate-draft`); manuscript import never touches it, so both fell back to the literal `\"No summary yet.\"` for every chapter of an imported book. Fixed with a shared helper (`buildChapterFallbackExcerpts`) that falls back to the chapter's own paragraph text when no summary exists.
- **Bare Roman-numeral outline headings** (\"I. Growing Up Years\", \"II. Current Life\" -- common in nonfiction/memoirs) weren't recognized as chapter breaks, collapsing a real book's 5 top-level sections into one mega-chapter. Fixed with a value-bounded check that avoids misreading A/B/C/D outline-letter bullets as chapter numerals (C and D are technically also valid Roman numerals).
- **Short outline-header fragments** (e.g. \"F. Strengths and Weaknesses\") fell under rewrite's word-count skip threshold and survived verbatim into the final export, contradicting the rewrite plan's own stated goal of removing them. Forcing them through rewrite instead produced invented, duplicate filler on real front-matter lines (a book's title-page lines each independently rewritten into near-identical filler paragraphs). Now excluded from rewrite eligibility entirely and omitted from export when never rewritten, plus a guard against two adjacent paragraphs converging on identical rewritten text.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Full `vitest` suite passes (3 pre-existing unrelated failures confirmed via `git stash`, not caused by this change)
- [x] 24 new tests across 3 new test files (`structural-heading.test.ts`, `chapter-fallback-excerpt.test.ts`, `markdown.test.ts`) plus 3 new regression tests in `parser.test.ts`
- [x] Live-verified end-to-end against a real imported manuscript on local dev: baseline critic scores went from nonsense (0/50/100s, \"no content provided\") to real, content-aware feedback; re-ran the exact `forceTinyParagraphs` sweep that previously produced duplicate title-page filler and confirmed it now correctly skips all heading-shaped fragments while still rewriting genuine short content; re-exported and confirmed zero leftover outline debris with no manual DB intervention

author: tgoodhew
body:
The claim was fixed in the captures README and `manual-qa.md` §15 when the GLONASS capture landed — and left standing in two places that repeat it. **Both are documents a person reads to decide what hardware to buy**, which is the worst place for it.

- **`docs/nmea-against-lady-heather.md`** called the sitting *"one GPS-only puck on one afternoon"* while arguing the asymmetry with Heather's many receivers is real. The asymmetry *is* real; it was being **overstated by an assumption rather than measured**.
- **`docs/tutorial-nmea-driver.md`** listed three things the receiver refused to show and gave *"the puck is GPS-only"* as the reason for one. Two of those three turn out to be **configuration rather than limitation** — GLONASS via `CFG-GNSS`, `GNS` via `CFG-MSG`.

That second correction **strengthens the paragraph's conclusion rather than weakening it**: what the receiver genuinely refused was the **outage**, the one case no configuration reaches and the one the simulator supplies on demand. That is the argument for keeping both, and it now rests on the right example.

Both amendments are **marked and dated rather than rewritten away**, because the mistake is the useful part: *the receiver was never asked.*

**No gate could have caught this.** `Test-DocumentReferences` checks links, section numbers and issue references — a wrong claim needs a reader, which is exactly what the #316 audit concluded.

author: psvampa
body:
Backlog items: 1.10, 1.12, 2.8. **No verdict moves.** CHANGELOG entry twenty-fifth.

## What the tool used to get wrong

- **A reversed pair produced a plausible clean audit.** `./audit.sh glibc-2.34 glibc-2.28` ran to the end at exit 0. Nothing compared the order: the wrapper tested `[ "$OLD" = "$NEW" ]` and `check_refs` only that both refs resolve. Measured on that pair, the output is the shape of the published `2.28..2.34` run — step 2 reporting two files that touch `LC_COLLATE`, step 5 a hunk count, no `!!` anywhere. What it hides: step 4 scans the tag it is handed, so reversed it scans the older one and `ckb_IQ` and `mnw_MM` (absent at `glibc-2.28`, `copy "iso14651_t1"` at `glibc-2.34`, read from the pinned clone) leave the exposed set; step 2 swaps "Added … not analysed" for "Deleted … any index using one of these will fail", so a locale deleted in the real upgrade reads as a harmless addition; step 3 closes over the wrong tag's `copy` graph.
- **The same-tag notice compared text, not commits.** `./audit.sh glibc-2.39 ef321e23c20eebc6d6fb4044425c00e6df27b05f` — the tag and the sha the run's own provenance line prints for it — never fired it: rc 0, no "nothing was compared", summary "none — no locale's `LC_COLLATE` changed". The sixteenth entry's false negative, reopened by spelling.
- **An option without a value exited 1 with no message.** `--new-locales-dir` as the last word on the line died in `shift 2` under `set -e`, printing nothing — and those options enable the only checks that can see `C.UTF-8`.
- **A hand-run step said nothing about a pair that is one commit twice.** `diff_collation_code.py <tag> <tag>` ended in "No substantive collation code change", rc 0, no `!!`: a clean verdict over a comparison that never happened.

## What changed

- `glibc_locale_data.pair_order()` — a STATUS, not a bool: `same` / `forward` / `reversed` / `undetermined`. Ancestry first (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), then the glibc RELEASE each divergent commit descends from (`git describe`, read as major.minor). Commit dates are not read.
- `glibc_locale_data.nearest_glibc_tag()` — three states: a tag with its release, a tag whose name is not read as a release, no name at all. Only the release counts, never a point release's `.2` or a snapshot's `.9000`.
- `glibc_locale_data.require_pair_order()` — refuses `reversed` (exit 2) unless `--allow-reverse`; prints the same-commit and undetermined notices; silent on `forward`.
- `glibc_locale_data.py order [--allow-reverse] [--quiet]` — the status word for the shell, warnings on stderr.
- `glibc_locale_data.warn()` — the `!!` formatter, moved out of `diff_distro_locales` (alias kept) so all callers share one copy.
- Four entry points ask: `audit-locale-diff.sh` (step 1, before it prints a finding, and it takes `--allow-reverse` now), `filter_lc_collate_changes.py`, `diff_collation_code.py`, `diff_node_locales.py`.
- `audit.sh` — `SAME_TAG` from commit identity; a `-- Direction of the pair: NOT ESTABLISHED` summary block; an unrecognised status stops the run; `needs_value` on every `--*` option; the summary heading now says "One commit, compared with itself".

## Verified

- Suite: 363 tests, 0 skipped, run in the main checkout.
- CI: green on the second commit. The first push went red, and it was worth the red: three fabricated-repository tests took the commit author from the machine's global git config, which the runner does not have, so they failed there after a green local run. The identity now lives in each fixture's own config.
- Acceptance: `audit.sh` byte-identical before and after on 2.28..2.34, 2.34..2.39, 2.12..2.17 (output path aside), 544/1291/1788 lines — re-run after each of the four designs this PR went through.
- Sixteen pairs measured on the pinned clone, each answering as the CHANGELOG entry states, including `glibc-2.34 -> origin/release/2.28/master` refused and the master-versus-branch shapes at 2.28, 2.17 and 2.12 undetermined.
- Mutants: twenty-five, each failing the test named for it — the ancestry return each way; a probe exiting 128; the release comparison dropped, made on the tag name, and read as the whole dotted version; the unreadable-name state collapsed and its sentence reworded; the fall-through to `undetermined` turned into `forward`; the refusal; the same-commit notice; the `undetermined` warning; `SAME_TAG` by text; the `NOT ESTABLISHED` block; the unrecognised-status branch; four `needs_value` branches; step 1's call and its flag; step 5's call and its flag; step 8's call; and a reworded control. Control: a docstring-only edit leaves the suite green. One guard is deliberately redundant and un-mutatable, recorded in `tests/README.md`.
- `false-negative-reviewer`: five passes, each on the previous one's corrections. It found the date-first ordering (a release branch is dated after the next release, so the reversed pair read as forward), snapshot tags read as releases, point releases doing the same from the other side, and a detail line that called an unparsed tag unreachable. The fourth and fifth passes found nothing in the defect class.
- `doc-sweep`: four sweeps; every stale passage fixed, including a header comment claiming the sha case is refused when it is run, and an `import time` left behind by the abandoned ordering.
- Sources checked for claims about other projects: the pinned clone `scripts/glibc` with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` (`ckb_IQ`, `mnw_MM`, the 125 tags matching the `describe` glob, `glibc-2.28.9000` one commit after `glibc-2.28`, `release/2.12/master` describing as `glibc-2.12.2`); `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and `git describe` exit codes and messages on git 2.50.1.

## Backlog

- 1.10, 1.12 and 2.8 closed by this PR. Item 1.10's own proposed fix — order by `git log -1 --format=%ct` — was implemented as written and measured **false**; the backlog records that, because the fix a backlog item proposes is a hypothesis, not a design.
- Opened: 2.22 (`--quiet` is not asserted to be quiet; its failure mode is repetition) and 2.23 (the redundant exit-status guard no mutation can show). Both recorded in `tests/README.md`.

author: damson
body:
## 👥 High-level summary

The number this project publishes for how much of itself its tests exercise has
been wrong, in a way that pointed work at the wrong place. Several files here
embed a small program written in another language, or a long list of patterns,
inside a single instruction. The measuring tool counts each line of those as an
instruction that was never run, so they are recorded as untested forever and no
test can ever change that. One file read 57.9% and looked like the most
neglected thing in the project, when almost all of its shortfall was those
lines. This marks them as what they are, so the figure measures the code that
tests can actually reach.

## 📋 What changed

- The nine embedded `awk` programs in the shared library, the two in the skill
  validator, and the three pattern lists in the secret linter are wrapped in the
  ignore markers this repository already uses in two other scripts and already
  passes to the coverage tool.
- The markers are placed *inside* each construct, so the surrounding statement
  stays measured. A `#` line is a comment in `awk` and inside a bash array
  literal alike, so nothing about the runtime behaviour changes.
- The coverage workflow's comment now says why the flag exists and where the
  line is: wrap data and foreign source, never a bash statement, because a bash
  statement inside a region stops being measured at all.

## ✅ Test plan

- [x] Automated checks pass: `bats tests/` (312 tests, 0 failures) and
      `shellcheck -x -S warning -e SC1091` over every script, both clean. The
      suite is the evidence that the marker comments are inert: the secret
      linter, the skill validator and every registry reader are exercised by it
- [x] `just lint` and `just check` both exit 0
- [x] `.github/workflows/coverage.yml` still parses as YAML
- [ ] New or updated tests: none, and deliberately. This changes what is
      counted, not what runs. Behaviour is held by the 312 tests already here
- [ ] CI is green: to be confirmed on this PR
- [ ] **The number itself is confirmed by this PR's own Coverage run, not
      locally.** kcov traces no bash on macOS. Before: `lib/common.sh` 57.9%
      (178 lines, 75 missed, every one of them awk source),
      `bin/lint-secrets.sh` 68.8%, `bin/validate-skills.sh` 71.9%, project
      84.3%. I will post the after figures from this PR's report

## 🤖 Review

- [ ] Automated/AI review has run and its comments have been read
- [ ] **Findings addressed or explicitly skip-justified after every push**
- [x] Statusline doc in sync: `user-dev/statusline.sh` is untouched

author: anothernocoder
body:
## Why

The props tables for `Field`, `Select` and `PinInput` said nothing: one row, `size`, typed `SelectSize` — a name a reader can't act on. `Dialog`'s table said something false: "This component forwards the native element's attributes only", about a root that wraps a machine with a portal, a focus trap and a scroll lock.

## What changed

The table documents the surface this design system owns — the props Moderno adds — and now says out loud what it leaves out.

**The rows say something**

- An aliased literal union is unfolded: `size` reads `"sm" | "md" | "lg"`, not `SelectSize`.
- The **Default** column works. It was an em dash on every row of every table because a recipe's default lives in a value (`cva({ defaultVariants: { size: "md" } })`), not in the prop's type. `cva` now exposes `defaultVariants` for the same reason it already exposed `variants` — "for docs/introspection" — and the props-doc manifest hands it to the extractor, so the documented default can't disagree with what the component does.
- Types print the way a consumer writes them. The printer parenthesises a function type to sit in a union with `undefined`, and names types through whatever alias the file imported them under, so a chart's formatter arrived as `((value: number) => string)`. It is now `(value: number) => string`.
- A prop's JSDoc summary is shown, collapsed to one line, under the prop name rather than in a fifth column — a Description column pushed the table into a horizontal scroll with every row as tall as its hidden prose.

**The table says what it omits**

A root wrapped around a headless machine reaches the docs with only its own props, because `props-doc` drops Ark/Zag's declarations along with the DOM noise. That is deliberate — re-publishing `Select.Root`'s thirty-odd inherited props would document Ark rather than the wrapper — but a one-row table with nothing else reads as "this is the whole API". The generated `propsComplete` flag, which already recorded the difference and until now only `valid-props` consulted, now drives a line under the table pointing at the Ark machine. `Dialog`, which adds nothing of its own, says exactly that instead of the native-attributes message.

**Table layout**

Fixed column widths, so a long type can't dictate the table's width; the Spanish header labels ("Obligatoria", "Por defecto") no longer wrap into each other.

## Notes for review

- `propsComplete` semantics are unchanged, so `moderno/valid-props` behaves exactly as before: it does not judge unknown props on the Ark-backed roots, and still validates enum values against the recipe.
- `agentPropsHash` is bumped on every affected page — the props changed, and the `agent:` guidance blocks were re-read against them (no prose needed changing).
- Prop names, types and JSDoc summaries stay in English on both locales, per the existing rule that the API is not translated. Only the new footnote is translated.

## Verification

`vitest` (776), `eslint`, `tsc`, `prettier`, `pnpm -r build`, docs build, Playwright e2e (7), slug parity, registry lint, and the `agent:` drift gate — all green. Tables checked in the browser in both locales and both themes.

author: sbuerk
body:
Every select of the frontend profile editor opened on a placeholder option
showing the literal text `—`. Reported from a review of the new editor,
and reproducible in the frontend.

## The defect

`Partials/Profile/Field/Control.html` passed the label as
`prependOptionLabel="—"`. Fluid does not decode a character reference
inside a ViewHelper argument: it arrives as that string,
`SelectViewHelper::renderOptionTag()` runs it through `htmlspecialchars()`, and
the page carries `&#8212;`. In element content the same spelling works,
because there it is the browser that decodes it — which is why the contact
summary cell of the same editor was right and the select was not.

The reference is a typographic rewrite of the `---` the pre-3.0 editor used,
which rendered fine.

## What changed

The placeholder is **unlabelled rather than un-escaped**, which is a decision
and not only the smaller edit. Writing the character itself would have rendered
as well; the editing placeholder means "nothing chosen yet" rather than "this
value is empty", and it sits under a control that carries its own `<label for>`.

Fluid still renders the option: `hasArgument()` asks whether the argument was
given, not whether it is empty, so `prependOptionLabel=""` prepends an
`<option value="">`. That empty value is what makes constraint validation refuse
a required select — `gender` is the only one — and it is unchanged. Probed
against Fluid 4.6.1 on v13 and 5.3.1 on v14, uncompiled and compiled. The
neighbouring `required=""` behaves the opposite way and disappears, because
`AbstractTagBasedViewHelper::initialize()` drops a registered tag attribute
whose value is the empty string.

The editor's second character reference, the empty-value dash of the contact
summary prototype, is written as the character it stands for. It was never
wrong — it is element content — but none of the idiom is left now. An audit of
all Fluid templates and XLIFF files of the repository found no third occurrence.

## Tests

Two cases. The first asserts that every select of the rendered page opens on an
option with an empty value and no text, and pins which selects those are: the
live `gender` and the `control-select` prototype, which `DOMDocument` matches
because it has no `<template>` semantics. Against the previous partial it fails
with `Select "gender" labels its empty option` and `'—'`. The second
states the rule over the profile editing Fluid *sources* rather than over one
rendered page, so a reference in any ViewHelper argument fails it wherever it is
written.

The JavaScript fixture transcribed `—` for that prototype — the template
source, not what a visitor received: jsdom decoded it to an em dash while the
page carried the escaped form, so the jsdom suite ran against markup nobody was
served. It is corrected, and the first case asserts the transcription.

## Also corrected

- The comment in `academic_base` pointing at `prependOptionLabel="---"` named a
  label that exists nowhere and a mechanism that is not the one in play: the
  prepend is gated on the label, never on the value.
- `docs/architecture/profile-editing-contract.md` claimed the em dash of
  `documents.ts` is "the same placeholder Fluid spells as `prependOptionLabel`",
  and gains the rule and the asymmetry instead.

No changelog entry: 3.0.0 is unreleased, the partial exists only since ACE-262,
and nothing in the manual describes the placeholder.

## Follow-up found on the way

The trait's only caller, the `academic_jobs` new job form, prepends no empty
option at all, so its `employmentType` and `type` selects submit a value nobody
chose. Reported as ACE-527, on `main` and on `2`; not part of this change.

## Verification

TYPO3 v13.4 and v14.3, each after its own `composerUpdate`: `lintPhp`, `cgl -n`
and `phpstan` green, `unit` 784 tests / 1990 assertions on v13 and 779 / 1973 on
v14, the full `functional` suite on SQLite 1967 tests / 12594 assertions / 8
skipped on v13 and 1981 / 12793 / 6 on v14, and `checkRstRenderingAll` on both.
Run once: `lintTypescript`, `typecheckJs`, `testJs` (431 cases, 0 failed),
`checkJsBuildClean` and `lintMarkdown -n`.

author: joshuad2824-art
body:
Two things before the site gets demonstrated this week.

## The sample records had started aging out

They were written around a Friday in August 2026, and the rules that govern them had begun taking them away: wins and FYIs past their fourteen-day archive, threads approaching their purge, care windows closed. The board was showing one win and one FYI — emptier than it will ever be in real use, and a poor way to meet it for the first time.

So on a **first load** the whole set slides forward as one piece (`src/data/freshen.ts`). Every date moves by the same number of days, which keeps every relationship intact: the gap between a decision and its announcement, the interval between when a commitment was held and when it falls due, the order of a conversation. Nothing is invented.

Three details that matter:

- **The shift is a whole number of weeks**, so weekdays survive it — a Sunday service has to stay on a Sunday, and the Wednesday study has to stay next to the standing Wednesday services on the calendar.
- **It never reaches so far that something written in the past lands in the future.** A win posted tomorrow would be worse than a stale one.
- **It runs only when nothing is stored yet.** Once anybody has used the board, the dates on it are theirs and are left alone.

Coming Up labels are re-derived from the events they point at; the one typed by hand slides with everything else, so the printed issue still agrees with the calendar.

**Result:** the Huddle opens with 3 wins, 3 tensions, 2 FYIs and 5 items due next; threads forget in 9 and 4 days; the bulletin is the current issue with its Coming Up lines all on or after its own service date, and "Duplicate for next week" still works from that state.

## The capped surfaces are centred now

You asked about this last round. On a wide monitor the prose surfaces were left-aligned with all the leftover space piled on the right, which read as a mistake rather than a decision. They are centred now, so the margin sits evenly either side.

Aligning the header to the same block took an actual fix: its padding sat *outside* the centred column while the content's sat *inside* it, which put the title 40px left of everything beneath it. Both are measured the same way now.

## Verified

| | 3840 | 2560 | 1512 | 390 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Title aligns with content | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Horizontal overflow on any surface | none | none | none | none |

Every surface visited at each width; no console errors.

author: jerry73204
body:
Fixes #1221 (`docs/issues/1221-*`). Files #1236 as the follow-up.

Not one crate in `packages/{core,api,platform,boards,rmw,drivers,tooling}` denied or forbade `unsafe_code` — the only three `forbid` sites in the tree were host CLI crates. So `nros-serdes`, the CDR serializer where a pointer bug is a wire bug and the crate the Kani/Verus harnesses assume, was held at zero unsafe by nothing but habit.

## Re-measured first

The issue's counts are from 2026-09-07 and a crate that had since gained an `unsafe` would take a build break rather than a guard. Nothing had. The census also found **thirteen** crates at literal zero, not three — the issue measured `packages/core` and stopped.

| crate | src LOC | `unsafe` | gated |
| --- | ---: | ---: | :-: |
| `core/nros-serdes` | 5 013 | 0 | ✅ |
| `core/nros-serdes-packed` | 434 | 0 | ✅ |
| `core/nros-diagnostics` | 181 | 0 | ✅ |
| `boards/nros-board-common` | 3 998 | 0 | ✅ |
| `boards/nros-board-threadx-port-riscv64` | 165 | 0 | ✅ |
| `tooling/nros-platform-config` | 4 268 | 0 | ✅ |
| `tooling/nros-cargo-profile` | 737 | 0 | ✅ |
| `tooling/nros-build-paths` | 418 | 0 | ✅ |
| `tooling/nros-cbindgen-headers` | 159 | 0 | ✅ |
| `tooling/nros-cc-flags` | 150 | 0 | ✅ |
| `boards/nros-board-s32z270-freertos` | 25 | 0 | — |
| `boards/nros-board-mps3-an536-freertos` | 29 | 0 | — |
| `rmw/cyclonedds/cyclonedds-sys` | 13 | 0 | — |

No `allow` was added anywhere to make a crate qualify.

## Zero is necessary, not sufficient

The ten that took the lint are crates whose **role** implies the property: three pure data-transformation core crates, five host-side build-script helper libraries that compute paths/flags/profiles, and two board crates carrying no hardware access (`nros-board-common` is a trait plus a manifest parser; `nros-board-threadx-port-riscv64` states it "ships no runtime Rust" and exposes the paths of six vendored `.S` files).

The three left alone are at zero because the crate is **unfinished or is the FFI seam itself**:

* the two FreeRTOS board crates say so in their own module docs — *"This Rust side is deliberately minimal … A Rust entry lane (console writer, panic behaviour) lands with phase-372 W5."* A bare-metal console writer is MMIO; forbidding now schedules its own removal.
* `cyclonedds-sys` is thirteen lines of doc comment and `#![no_std]`. A lint against unsafe in the crate that exists to expose a C library is a category error.

## `forbid` IS the gate here — a census script was considered and rejected

1. **It cannot be locally overridden** — `forbid` outranks a later `allow`, so an `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` inside the crate is itself an error. A census baseline is a text file anyone can edit in the same commit.
2. **It fails in the author's own `cargo check`**, not in a lane someone else rebases into.
3. **It has no reach to keep in step with the rule it enforces** — the 0196 shape this repo keeps re-finding in its own gates. No crate list to forget to extend, no baseline to go stale.
4. **It cannot be satisfied vacuously.** A grep census is satisfied by a spelling change; the compiler's answer is about the code.

What a census *would* buy is the other population — the 62 crates carrying all 5 047 occurrences, which cannot forbid. That is a different argument (69 % of it sits in five crates, and `nros-node`'s share is the type-erased bump arena that exists to avoid `alloc`), so it is filed as **#1236** rather than left in an archived file where nothing looks.

## Proven to fire, not read

`forbid` is only a guard if it is in the crate root of the crate you think it is. A `let _v = unsafe { *_p };` probe appended to each root, `cargo check -p <crate>`, file restored:

```
enforced      nros-serdes — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-serdes-packed — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-diagnostics — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-board-common — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-board-threadx-port-riscv64 — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-cc-flags — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-cbindgen-headers — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-build-paths — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-platform-config — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
enforced      nros-cargo-profile — error: usage of an `unsafe` block
```

Ten of ten.

## Builds, including bare metal

* `just check no-std` — green; it already covers `nros-serdes` and `nros-diagnostics` on **both** `thumbv7m-none-eabi` and `riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf`.
* `nros-serdes-packed` is not in that lane's crate list, so it was checked explicitly on both targets, with `nros-board-common --no-default-features` (its `no_std` arm) on `thumbv7m-none-eabi`.
* Host `cargo check --all-targets` over all ten, plus `--all-features` on the two with non-trivial feature sets.

## Tier

`just ci gate`: `cli-fresh`, `check::fast`, `api-parity`, `test-unit`, `test-lane-contracts` green. `check::build`'s four reds (`rmw-uorb`, `rmw-xrce`, `borrowed-e2e`, `staticlib-symbols`) are the known agent-worktree class — `nros_build_root` resolves to the main checkout from a linked worktree.

author: thebabeldragon
body:
Duck Gate owns truth. The e-ink unit only renders an admitted snapshot of that truth.

```
admit → commit FieldTick → emit GateEvent → EInkSink → framebuffer
```

- New `duck_gate/` observer surface. Zero admission logic.
- Canonical `gate_tick` event (`duck-gate/v0.1`).
- `GateDisplaySnapshot` is a tiny projection, not the gate object.
- `EInkSink` ignores invalid/duplicate sequences and keeps the last committed frame on HALTED.
- `EInkWorker` coalesces ticks so the gate never blocks on refresh.
- ACK is `display_ack`: physical witness, not approval.
- Software framebuffer at `/tmp/metafield/eink_frame.txt`. SPI/I²C implements the same render/refresh port.
- `python -m observer.startup --full` does not drive the panel and does not bind a second UDP socket.

```bash
python -m unittest tests.test_eink_sink
python -m duck_gate.eink --sequence 1842 --deltas 3
python -m duck_gate.eink --status HALTED --reason "INVALID DELTA"
```

author: jsongo
body:
## 概述

修复 PAT 通道假流式卡住（315s 无语义内容）、离线期账号凭据无法自愈两 个核心问题，并接通 GPT-6、补齐管理界面的负载/凭据观测能力。

## 主要改动

### 1. PAT 真流式转发（修复核心 bug）
- 根因：`_post_chat` 用 `response.read()` 整段缓冲上游 SSE，生成期间客户端只收到本地合成心跳
- `_SSEDecoder` 增量解码：任意 TCP chunk 边界、CRLF、跨块 event/data、UTF-8 增量
- `stream_pat_native`：httpx 逐块读取，事件到达即下发
- 严格 failover 边界：首语义事件前白名单错误码才切号；提交后绝不重放/拼流
- 空流保护：无语义内容 done → 502；缺 done → 502；不再伪装空 200

### 2. 卡住保护（provider 层）
- 语义超时 `WB_TRAE_SEMANTIC_TIMEOUT`（默认 180s）：保活/注释不算进展，超时报 504
- 客户端断连即终止上游读取（stop_signal）
- 心跳改为 SSE 注释，不再伪造 reasoning_content

### 3. 凭证自愈（不再靠请求踩坑）
- 后台 token keeper 循环（默认 600s）：先探测换 token 端点可达性，可达即补签缺失/临期账号
- 离线期新增账号在恢复后自动补齐；凭据失败账号跳过，不拖垮通道

### 4. GPT-6 接通
- `gpt-6-astra` 仅在 `solo_agent` function 目录开放（chat_v3 报 4001）
- `models_config.json` 支持 per-model `function` 字段，通用化而非硬编码

### 5. 管理界面
- 「查询模型负载」按钮（10 分钟缓存）+「补签 Token」按钮 + 账号状态面板
- 额度日包按模型系列区分（GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-6）

### 6. 其它
- 账号级稳定设备指纹（PAT 多账号）；native 分流收敛到 provider 层
- `.env` 支持多行 JSON 数组
- doubao CDP：新开聊天标签页替代劫持 App 内部页（修复工具失灵）
- launchd 常驻模板（可选安装）
- 53 个 PAT 测试用例（完整隔离，不触真实服务）

## 验证
- `test_trae_pat_failover.py` 53/53；全量 94 通过（1 个失败为既有 zcode 标签用例，与本次无关）
- 真实联调：gpt-5.6-sol / gpt-5.6-terra-max / kimi-k3 / gpt-6-astra-max 流式与非流式全通，首字到达 < 3s（GPT-6 排队除外，为上游拥挤）
- 离线演练：端点不可达时自愈循环正确等待、恢复后自动补签 3 个缺 token 账号

body:
This update advances the hybrid collection model (authorized local capture + autonomous repo pipeline) by making ingestion contract-driven and more fault-tolerant. New capture evidence is now normalized into a reusable intermediate dataset before canonical export updates, with stronger provenance and trust controls.

- **Ingestion contract + canonical normalization**
  - Added support for evidence envelopes with `capture_metadata`, `observed_facts`, and `provenance`.
  - Preserves artifact hash lineage and source reliability in normalized donation/aggregate outputs.
  - Writes intermediate normalized observations to `data/research/capture_observations.normalized.json` before updating `data/raw/gofundme_manual_export.json`.

- **Quality/trust controls**
  - Added automated guards for duplicate observations, negative/future values, and parser drift (accepted pack but no extractable facts).
  - Added impossible aggregate regression detection (near-zero collapse vs prior totals), routed to review queue as high risk.
  - Improved conflict signaling/event emission for downstream triage.

- **Schema and contract surface**
  - Extended capture manifest schema with `source_reliability`.
  - Extended donation schema for richer provenance/capture metadata and `UNRESOLVED` confidence handling.
  - Added a new schema for normalized capture observations (`data/schema/capture_observation.schema.json`).

- **Docs + contributor workflow**
  - Updated collection and automation docs to reflect the authorized local collector model, contract fields, intermediate normalization artifact, and quality-gate behavior.

- **Targeted test coverage**
  - Added ingestion tests for contract-envelope payloads, normalized output generation, and impossible regression quarantine behavior.

author: lisachenko
body:
## What

Metadata (key 3) and Produce (key 0), version 0, expressed as `getScheme()` declarations on the `BinarySchema` engine of T1. Every class starts from its counterpart on `main` (`git show origin/main:<path>`) with the fields that v0 does not have removed, so the cascade merge upwards stays a field diff.

| Class | v0 shape | Stripped from `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `MetadataRequest` | `parent::getScheme() + ['topics' => [TYPE_STRING]]` | nullable topic array (v1) |
| `MetadataResponse` | `brokers`, `topics` | `clusterId`, `controllerId` |
| `Common\Node` | nodeId, host, port + `getConnection()` | `rack` |
| `Common\TopicMetadata` | topicErrorCode, topic, partitions | `isInternal` |
| `Common\PartitionMetadata` | identical to `main` | – |
| `ProduceRequest` | requiredAcks, timeout, topicMessages | `transactionalId` |
| `Data\ProduceRequestTopic` / `ProduceRequestPartition` | topic, partitions / partition, `messageSet` BYTEARRAY | `recordBatch` + CRC32C of the v2 batch |
| `ProduceResponse` | topics | `throttleTime` |
| `Data\ProduceResponseTopic` / `ProduceResponsePartition` | topic, partitions / partition, errorCode, `baseOffset` | `logAppendTime` |

The `packPayload()`/`unpackPayload()` overrides of all of these classes are deleted, and none of them uses `$header = null;` — the header always comes from `parent::getScheme()`.

* `ProduceRequestPartition::__construct(int $partition, string|\Stringable $messageSet)` stores the bytes in the `messageSet` BYTEARRAY, whose int32 length prefix is exactly the `MessageSetSize` of the spec. `MessageSet` of T3 (#4) is a `Stringable` and plugs in unchanged; until it is merged `Client::produce()` still assembles the buffer from the message classes on the branch (marked with a `TODO` that names #4).
* `RequiredAcks = 0` is the only request in the protocol that the broker never answers. `ProduceRequest::expectsResponse()` states that, and `Client::produce()` writes such a batch to each partition leader without reading anything back (returning an empty result) instead of blocking in `stream_select()`.
* `Cluster`, `Client::produce()` (the only method of `Client.php` touched) and `KafkaProducer` keep working, and the metadata cache file still round-trips through `var_export()` / `RestorableTrait::__set_state()`.

## Spec references

* `docs/protocol/0.8.2.md`, sections "Metadata API (key 3, v0)", "Produce API (key 0, v0)", "MessageSet and Message"
* Kafka 0.8.2.2 sources: `kafka/api/TopicMetadataRequest.scala`, `TopicMetadataResponse.scala`, `ProducerRequest.scala`, `ProducerResponse.scala`, `kafka/server/KafkaApis.scala`

## How it was tested

`composer check` (php-cs-fixer, PHPStan, PHPUnit) is green, `find src tests -name '*.php' -exec php -l` is clean, and `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=127.0.0.1:9092 vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite integration` passes against a real Kafka 0.8.2.2 broker (256 unit tests, 14 integration tests).

Spec tests (`tests/Unit/Protocol/Request/MetadataApiTest.php`, `ProduceApiTest.php`) pin hex vectors for:
* the Metadata request with an empty topic list (v0 asks for all topics with an *empty*, not a null, array) and one with two topics;
* a response with 2 brokers, 1 topic and 3 partitions including replicas and in-sync replicas;
* a topic announced with error 5 (LeaderNotAvailable) and no partitions;
* produce requests with acks `-1`, `1` and `0`, single- and multi-partition, and with the message set handed in as a `Stringable`;
* a produce response with error 6 on one partition and base offset `-1`;
* a metadata response surviving `var_export()` → `__set_state()` (the cache file of `Cluster`).

The message sets of those vectors are built directly from the specification by `tests/Fixture/SpecMessageSet`, so the request classes are never verified against bytes they produced themselves.

Integration tests against the broker:
* metadata of an auto-created topic — the first call answers `TopicErrorCode = 5` with no partitions, a later call has 3 partitions with elected leaders that are contained in their replica and ISR sets;
* an empty topic list returns the whole cluster, `Cluster::bootstrap()` resolves the leader of every partition, and a second `Cluster` restores everything from the metadata cache file without talking to the broker;
* produce with acks `1` and `-1`: `errorCode = 0` and base offsets that increase by the number of appended messages (0 → 2 → 5);
* produce with acks `0`: the broker sends nothing back (the next request on the same connection gets its own correlation id) and the messages are appended anyway, including through `Client::produce()`.

The broker validates the CRC of every message it appends — a deliberately corrupted CRC comes back as error code 2 — so the green produce runs also prove the message layout is right.

## Deviations worth reviewing

The ticket writes `brokers => [Node::class]` and `partitions => [PartitionMetadata::class]` (plain lists, as on `main`). Here both are keyed — `['nodeId' => Node::class]`, `['partitionId' => PartitionMetadata::class]` — because `Cluster::nodeById()`, `leaderFor()` and `partition()` look entries up by broker id and partition number, and a 0.8 broker does not promise any ordering for them. This matches the `['topic' => …]` / `['partition' => …]` convention used everywhere else and the `ClusterMetadataResponse` fixture from T1.

Closes #5

body:
## 这个 PR 是什么

用户两问:「给胶囊加进度条」「deepseek-v4-flash 是 1M,这里怎么是 2M」。

### 2M 的出处(事实)

`settings.json` 里 `/global/contextWindow = 2000000`,来自当前活跃预设 `[主预设] V19.5 狐神抚 · 毓忻` 的 `openai_max_context: 2000000` + `max_context_unlocked: true`;2,000,000 正是 ST 的 `unlocked_max`(`openai.js:137`)。`presetScalarPatch` 映射了数字、丢了标志。1,998,976 = 2,000,000 − 1,024 预留。**ST 也不会夹**:你的 ST 走 Custom 源,ST 对 Custom 无条件用 `unlocked_max`(`openai.js:5704-5710`),不查模型表。所以这里的夹住是 Iris 的**改进**而非补兼容,`contextUnlocked` 把上游的答案还回去。第一稿把 2M 写成「上一个预设的残留」是错的(把非活跃的咩咩预设当成了活跃的),已在账本 §44 保留更正过程。

**deepseek-v4-flash 的 1M** 来自 DeepSeek Models & Pricing 页(2026-09-08 读取):CONTEXT LENGTH 1M、MAX OUTPUT 384K;页面只写「1M」没有精确整数,表里记 1,000,000(与 ST 的 `max_1mil` 同读法)。DeepSeek 的 `/models` 只回 id/object/owned_by,探不到。

### A. 模型上下文长度识别

`model-context.ts`:`CONTEXT_LENGTH_FIELDS` 五条带出处与读取日期的字段路径(vLLM `max_model_len`、OpenRouter `context_length` / `top_provider.context_length`、LM Studio `max_context_length`、llama.cpp `meta.n_ctx_train`);`MODEL_CONTEXT_TABLE`(DeepSeek 按官方文档,OpenAI / Claude 按上游 `openai.js` 顺序转写);未知返回 undefined,**不用** ST 的 128k 兜底。`modelListOf` 读 `/models` 每行两次(之前只留 id);提供方永远优先于表。`resolveWindow` 是原四处 `windowOf` 的唯一后继,四向来源(`model` / `settings` / `unlocked` / `host`),每次读都夹、不写回。协议:`ChatBudget`、`ContextWindowSource`、`ModelContextLength`、两种连接行的 `modelContexts`、`ChatView.measured`。

### B. 胶囊进度条

胶囊底边 2px 填充,< 60% `--iris-ink-faint`、60–85% `--iris-accent`、> 85% `--iris-warn`;数据源是 `ChatView.measured`——宿主本来就为每回次记的 itemization,现在投影出来,不付装配;卡打开时预览优先,胶囊与卡不会不一致;hover 给精确数字 · 窗口来源 · 实测还是预览。容量卡多一行窗口来源;卡上四行顺序:缓存命中 → 稳定前缀 → 分叉 → 窗口来源。

### 顺手修的

真实回次记录的 `budget.context` 一直是 32768(`#itemizationOf` 漏传 window;B 组也报过)——现在参数**必填**,第三个调用方不可能再漏;探测结果按原样键存而表折叠大小写;2,000,000 上限在三处重复(抽屉滑块也是它)→ 协议里唯一 `MAX_CONTEXT_WINDOW`;fake 声称 `source: 'settings'` 却没存;死的 `windowOf` 删除。

**账本**:host §44、web §68,根账本清扫。

## 验证

rebase 到 359c03d(12 文件冲突由代理语义合并,`resolveWindow` 成为 #32/#33/#34 各处窗口读取的唯一来源)后总指挥复跑:
```
ROOT_TSC_EXIT=0  WEB_TSC_EXIT=0  BUILD_EXIT=0  render check: ok
ℹ tests 3134  ℹ pass 3129  ℹ fail 0  ℹ skipped 5
check-corpus-skips: 33 skipped, 0 failed
```
牙齿 26 处全红,一处洞(改名 gauge 外层仍绿)已补。

8791 挂本分支构建:输入框下胶囊底边有细条;容量卡末行「窗口 …」;设置里有 `contextUnlocked` 开关。

## 未做

- **预留 vs `max_tokens` 不一致**:装配预留 1,024,请求 `max_tokens` 65,535,两者相加可超窗口。既有问题。
- 卡的「第 N 回实测」文案仍不可达(Composer 调 `itemize()` 不带 turn),胶囊可达。
- `iris-llm-openai-compat` 的 `ModelEntry.contextWindow` 由 `cordis.yml` 种成 32768,对 1M 模型是陷阱,刻意不读。
- `CACHE-CENSUS.md` / `CACHE-TARGET.md` 引用旧的 `windowOf` 规则与 2M 前提,是缓存组的文件,只报不改。

Die prefers-reduced-motion-Regel setzt zusaetzlich die Zahl der Durchlaeufe

body:
## Summary
- Model "thinking"/reasoning and every tool call + its result — previously only ever printed to the terminal running the server — now stream into the web UI as small collapsible panels above each reply, matching how most chat UIs (ChatGPT, Claude.ai) surface this.
- A thinking panel streams live (visible while it's happening) and collapses once the real reply text starts. Each tool call shows up immediately as `tool_name(args)` with a "running…" status, then collapses to just its name once the result comes back — click either to expand/collapse and read the full text.
- New `EventCallback` (`on_event`) threaded through `Provider.chat()` and `Agent.run()`/`_call_tool()`, alongside the existing `on_chunk` text callback:
  - `ClaudeProvider` fires `"thinking"` for each `thinking_delta` when `show_thinking` is on (existing `CLAUDE_SHOW_THINKING` setting).
  - `OpenAICompatProvider` does the same on a best-effort basis for any router that relays a reasoning model's chain of thought via a `reasoning_content`/`reasoning` delta field — not standard OpenAI wire format, so not guaranteed across routers.
  - `Agent` fires `"tool_call"` before and `"tool_result"` after running a tool.
- `/api/chat/stream`'s wire format changes from raw streamed text to newline-delimited JSON (`{"type": "chunk"|"thinking"|"tool_call"|"tool_result"|"error", ...}`), so the browser can tell these apart. Updated the frontend's stream reader to parse/buffer NDJSON lines instead of concatenating raw text.
- This is a live view of the current turn only, not persisted anywhere new — reloading the page still only restores final reply text via `/api/history`, same as before.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest -q` — 210 passed
- [x] `py_compile` / `pyflakes` clean on all changed files
- [x] New tests: `Agent` fires `tool_call`→`tool_result` in the right order (success and error-in-handler cases), `on_event` is passed through to the provider; `ClaudeProvider` fires `"thinking"` for each `thinking_delta`; `/api/chat/stream` end-to-end with a real tool (`remember`) carries `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`chunk` events in order

- [x] Visually verified via headless Chromium against a fake provider that emits thinking + two tool calls + a final markdown reply: thinking streams live then auto-collapses once reply text starts, tool-call panels show args and a "running…" status then collapse with a result available on click, zero page errors — checked in both light and dark mode

The changefeed flips only after #373, #374 and the minimum #377 contract") schedule it there; decision 0053 recorded the surface verdict and named this flip as its follow-up. author: tejaskm-dev
body:
Four new tools, and the thinking panel now reflects what actually ran.

WEB SEARCH — Groq's compound models have search built in but refuse custom tool definitions, so using them would have cost artifacts, curriculum lookup and progress. Implemented as our own tool instead, keeping both.

Results are recorded server-side and streamed as `sources` events, so citations are the pages that were genuinely fetched rather than URLs the model recalled — which is where citation UIs usually go wrong. Favicons resolve from the domain.

Requires TAVILY_API_KEY or BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY. I tried shipping DuckDuckGo's HTML endpoint as a keyless fallback and tested it: it answers HTTP 202 with an anti-bot page, so it returns nothing. That was worse than no fallback, because the model would report "I searched and found nothing" — indistinguishable from a real empty result. The tool now distinguishes not-configured from no-results and instructs the model not to claim it searched. When no key is set, search_web is withheld from the tool list entirely rather than offered and always failing.

CALCULATOR — a hand-written recursive-descent parser, deliberately not eval or new Function. The expression originates from the model, which can be steered by injected text in retrieved content, so it is untrusted by construction and handing it to a JS evaluator server-side would be a remote execution path. A fixed grammar can only ever produce a number. Verified: 12/12 arithmetic cases correct, and 8/8 injection attempts rejected (process.exit, require, constructor.constructor, __proto__ and friends).

PROJECT FILES — list_my_projects and read_project_file read the learner's own FreeCode projects, scoped by user_id, so Loopy can review real code rather than hypothetical code.

THINKING PANEL — driven entirely by real tool events with measured durations. It deliberately shows no "understanding your question / preparing an answer" sequence: reasoning_format is "hidden", so the app has no access to the model's reasoning and any such steps would be invented. Steps that don't match what happened teach people to distrust every other status in the UI.

Verified against the live API — the model selects the right tool for calculator, web search, projects, curriculum and progress prompts; produces an artifact for "build me an interactive demo"; and answers a small question inline with no artifact and no tool.

author: wdocustom
body:
Follow-up to #173. This commit was pushed seven minutes after that PR merged, so it missed the merge and is not in `main`.

## The problem

Stripe may not have attached the dispute's balance transaction yet when `charge.dispute.created` fires, which leaves `disputeFeeCents` at 0. The installer's chargeback alert then rendered:

```
Disputed Payment       $288.15
Stripe Dispute Fee       $0.00
Total Held             $288.15
```

Both numbers are wrong — Stripe takes a $15 dispute fee on top, so the alert understates what was actually pulled from the installer's balance, in the one email they act on.

It can't self-correct. The opening alert is gated on `installer_alerted_at` so a re-delivered event can't email the same chargeback twice, which means the later `charge.dispute.updated` delivery — the one that does carry the fee — updates the `disputes` row but sends nothing.

## The fix

Drop the fee and total rows when the fee isn't known yet, and move the highlight to the disputed amount so the email still has a clear headline figure. Stating one accurate number beats stating three where two are wrong. When the fee is present, the email is unchanged.

The subject line already reads `amount + fee`, which stays correct either way.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npx vitest run` — 149 passed. The 11 failures are pre-existing on `main` (incomplete Supabase mock: `maybeSingle is not a function`, plus `customer.test.ts`), unchanged by this commit.

Presentation-only change to an email template; no logic, schema, or Stripe call paths touched.
