body:
## Summary
- `captureUserShellPath` interpolated `$PATH___PATH_END___` — the shell parses that as ONE (unset) variable name, so the END sentinel never printed, the regex never matched, and shell-PATH capture **silently failed on every platform**, always falling through to `buildFallbackPath`.
- The fallback ordered `/usr/bin` before `~/.local/bin`, so spawns resolved a stale root-owned Claude CLI (2.1.120) instead of the service user's self-updating 2.1.263 → newer models 400'd with `claude_code_version_too_old`.
- Fix: brace the expansion (`${PATH}`), reorder the fallback (user-local installs before system paths), regression tests for both.
- Also checks in `scripts/staged-unit-path-dropin.conf` — the systemd PATH drop-in already deployed on the box.

## Why
- Any Companion install running as a systemd/launchd service could silently pin sessions to a stale system CLI while the user's own install was current. Observed live: model switch to a newer model 400'd `claude_code_version_too_old` from a 2.1.120 spawn while 2.1.263 was installed.

## Testing
- 35 path-resolver tests green (2 new regression tests: capture-command shape, fallback ordering).
- Real end-to-end smoke on the box (no mocks): capture returns `/home/auracomp/.local/bin` first; `resolveBinary("claude")` → `/home/auracomp/.local/bin/claude` (2.1.263).
- `bun run typecheck` green; pre-commit hook (typecheck + tests + coverage) passed.

author: keegs2
body:
Implements the operator-approved E.164 design (per the Sinch requirement: E.164 anywhere a valid number appears — RURI/From/To/PAI/Diversion).

## What changes on the wire (gate ON)
RCF/trunk egress From, Contact, Diversion, and (trunk) PAI users go from bare 10-digit to `+1…`. RURI/To/API-path values were already E.164 (passthrough; drift-warn if the $rU/$tU arms ever fire — catches the legacy plus-strip path). Strict never-touch rules: anonymous/Restricted/short codes/911/988/malformed users byte-identical — a bogus `+1` is structurally impossible (NANP `[2-9]` area-code anchor).

## Fixes two LIVE STIR bugs as a side effect (audit findings)
- **Every RCF div PASSporT today signs `div.tn:"+5305480845"`** — plus-without-1, parses as Cuba; junk to strict verifiers.
- **Every trunk attestation-A call signs a malformed `orig.tn`** the same way — downstream verifiers can treat our signed trunk calls as unsigned.

body:
Documentation only. Amends ADR 0006 after #234 and #235:

* **Status line** records the amendment date and the retraction.
* **Clause 3** no longer defers a `UnionIteration` signature audit: certificate completeness is not a consumer of ω-iteration, so the consumer-gating trigger has not fired and `UnionIteration` stays as it is.
* **Spike findings**: the ω-iteration completeness route is marked superseded; the claim that the routes avoiding ω are exactly the ones needing Power Set is retracted as too strong. What remains binding is that Power Set anywhere in tranche 2 is a stop-and-review signal, and the compiled proof charges none.
* **New section "Amendment (2026-09-08)"**: the direct-induction argument, the two modules and their roles, and the ledger of certificate completeness — one Collection instance, one Separation instance, Pairing, General Union; no Infinity, Empty Set, Power Set, or Binary Union — explicitly **scoped to certificate completeness**. Atomic definability retains its existing Infinity-priced costs; recognition is an addition to that ledger.

No code changes; no status artifact moves (#161, ROADMAP, M7 status unchanged until the recognizer and its consumer exist).

author: zaartix
body:
`write_launchd_plists()` is create-if-missing, which is the right call — a hand-tuned plist should not be clobbered. The problem is that it is also *silent*, so an install that would generate a different agent says nothing at all.

## How it bites

macOS ships `/bin/bash` 3.2, which cannot parse `darkflow-run.sh` — the script uses syntax that fails at parse time, not at runtime:

```
$ /bin/bash -n ~/.darkflow/darkflow-run.sh
~/.darkflow/darkflow-run.sh: line 2107: syntax error near unexpected token `;;'
```

`BASH_BIN` is resolved from `command -v bash` at install time, so a first install on a machine without Homebrew bash bakes `/bin/bash` into the plist. The operator then does the obvious remedy:

```bash
brew install bash
bash install.sh --self-update
```

`BASH_BIN` is now `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`, but the plist already exists, so the branch is skipped and nothing is printed. The worker keeps dying at parse time under launchd, and the install output looks completely clean. I only found it by reading `write_launchd_plists()` after deleting the plist by hand made the problem go away.

The same silence hides a stale `PATH` — including the one that gains entries from the `_launchd_path()` fix in its own PR, which existing installs would otherwise never pick up.

## The fix

Keep create-if-missing. Render the agent into a variable, and when an existing plist differs, write the generated one alongside as `.new` and say so, quoting the interpreter and `PATH` this install would use plus the command to adopt it. Nothing is overwritten.

## Verified

Ran `install.sh --self-update` against a throwaway `HOME`, all three paths:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| no plist | writes it, `✓ Wrote launchd agent …` — unchanged behaviour |
| plist identical | silent, no `.new` — unchanged behaviour |
| plist edited to `/bin/bash` | warns, writes `.new`, original left at `/bin/bash` |

author: maxgekk
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

The one shape in milestone 4's debt register where Varka ran slower than the engine it forked. `SELECT d FROM t WHERE d < d2` measured 0.66x of stock Spark with a columnar consumer and 0.57x counted in task 62's 1B-row run, on a predicate whose own kernel answers at 681.2 M rows/s.

The plan is [`sql/varka/plans/PLAN_TASK_78.md`](sql/varka/plans/PLAN_TASK_78.md); its section 2 is the admission check and its section 9 has the measurement with the three registered predictions scored.

**The losing family is not what the task's title says, and finding that out is what made the cheap fix possible.** Spark's own column pruning runs long before any columnar rule sees the plan. For a one-column predicate the pruned child output is that column, the projection above it is redundant, and the optimizer removes it — so those shapes fuse whole and always did. For a two-column predicate the pruned output is both columns, the filter forwards both (a filter narrows nothing), and `Project [d]` survives because it genuinely has two columns to narrow to one. That is the entire losing family: **a predicate that reads more columns than its consumer wants.** It is a plan-time signal, which is why the rule can act on it — and it is why every filter row in task 62's surface carries a narrowing projection in its SQL while only the three two-column predicates were ever classified partial.

**The surviving projection cost two things, and the milestone section named one.** An operator boundary out of the node's row iterator, and — this is the second — a row conversion over `d2` as well as `d`. The node built `UnsafeProjection.create(childOutput, childOutput)` and applied it per selected row, so it serialised a column that the projection above then discarded.

`VarkaFilterColumnarToRowExec` now carries an optional `narrowing`. When set, `output` is the projected schema and the `UnsafeProjection` the node *already built* is created over the projected expressions instead. So the fix removes work rather than moving it, and the unnarrowed path is unchanged expression for expression.

`columnarSibling` wraps the columnar filter in a `VarkaProjectExec` carrying the same list. `VarkaFusedTransition` promises "the columnar-out node computing exactly what this fused transition computes", and the cache serializer swaps one for the other when a cached view's top is this node — a sibling that dropped the narrowing would hand the cache a two-column schema where the plan promised one, which is the class of error task 21 found when a stripped transition dropped a filter. There is a test asserting the round trip rather than trusting it.

The rule's new arm sits *after* the eligibility arm, so a projection with anything to fuse still becomes a Varka projection node and only a forwarded-only one reaches here; `isForwardedNarrowing` takes a column or a rename of one and refuses anything computed. It refuses a node that already has a narrowing, so the pass is idempotent, and it cannot reach across a residual `FilterExec` — that falls out of the match shape, and it must not, since the residual predicate reads columns the narrowing would remove.

### Why are the changes needed?

`SELECT a FROM t WHERE b < c` is the common shape of a two-column predicate under a projection, not a corner. It was the only entry in the debt register where the honest answer to "should Varka have run here" was no, and milestone 4 closes by rewriting the README from task 62's run for outside readers.

### The measurement

`VarkaNarrowingBenchmark` is new, with its own results at both widths. It is a file of its own because `VarkaFilterBenchmark`'s fixture has a single date column and every predicate in it reads one column: this shape cannot be written against it without adding a column, which would move every number that file has committed for a question it was never asked.

| shape | 10% selected | 70% | 100% |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SELECT d ... WHERE d < d2`, narrowed | 2.2x / 2.2x | **1.5x** / 1.5x | 1.3x / 1.3x |
| `SELECT d, d2 ...`, the control | 2.3x / 2.3x | 1.3x / 1.2x | 1.1x / 1.1x |
| `COUNT(*) ...`, nothing crosses the floor | 2.2x / 2.1x | 1.1x / 1.1x | 0.9x / 0.8x |

AVX-512 / 128-bit, against a Janino session on the same data. The losing shape is a win at every rung, all three rows fall with selectivity — the floor's cost is per selected row while the kernel's advantage is per input row — and the two widths agree inside a rung's noise, which is what a change to the row boundary rather than to the lanes should look like.

**These are laptop numbers on this task's own fixture and are not comparable to the 0.66x above**, which is task 62's surface on a pinned 512-bit runner against three distributions. They establish the sign and the size; the ratio the public table quotes still needs that dispatch.

**Two of three predictions missed, and the second is the finding.** Prediction 2 said absorbing the projection alone would not turn this shape into a win at 70% selected. It is 1.5x there. The plan pre-committed to what that would mean — "the floor is cheaper than task 19 measured, and that is a finding about task 19, not about this shape" — so making the node `CodegenSupport` is not needed to make this family win, and scope item 13 keeps its own justification instead of inheriting this task's. Prediction 3 (the two-column row costing more to cross the floor) holds at 70% and 100% by 12% and 14%, and inverts at 10%, where almost nothing crosses the floor and the gap is inside the run-to-run band; that is recorded rather than explained away.

### What broke, which is worth its own paragraph

The benchmark's first fixture was mislabelled, and it is the same bug task 63's third review had just found in `VarkaArithmeticBenchmark`. `d2` was `d` cycle-shifted by `s` days, so `d < d2` holds for `(cycle - s) / cycle` of the rows — the inverse of the shift. The rungs labelled 10, 70 and 100% were really 90, 30 and 0% selected, and the top rung's `s = cycle` made `d2` equal `d` on every row, so it selected nothing while claiming everything.

Nothing failed, because nothing was broken: it measured a real plan over real data and answered a question other than the one on its label. Being the second instance in a day, the fix is not only the arithmetic — selectivity is now the sign of `d2 - d`, one day either way, exact whatever the cycle does, and `requireSelectivity` asserts each rung's real fraction against the engine before anything is timed, so a mislabelled rung fails the run instead of publishing. The docstring records the original error rather than quietly correcting it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, in speed only, and for one plan shape: a query whose predicate reads more columns than its projection wants no longer pays a row-engine `Project` above the Varka filter, nor a row conversion of the columns that projection discards. Same answers, same rows, same schema.

### How was this patch tested?

`dev/varka_gate.sh`, green: catalyst and sql Varka suites at both vector widths, the opt-in sweep, scaladoc, `dev/lint-java`, `dev/scalastyle`, and `dev/varka_quote_check.py`.

New coverage:

* **The rule**: the projection absorbed; a rename absorbed; anything computed refused; a second pass idempotent.
* **The sibling**: the columnar round trip carrying the narrowing, and unchanged without one — the assertion that keeps the cache serializer's swap honest.
* **The node**: only the narrowed columns emitted, with reordering, and the same rows either way since the predicate is untouched.
* **The differential**, end to end: `SELECT d FROM varka_date_pairs WHERE d < d2` matching the row engine with no `ProjectExec` left in the plan — and the one-column predicate asserted to still need no narrowing at all, which is the evidence this moved only the shape that was losing.
* **The benchmark's own gu

author: dhruvgohil07
body:
Establishes the recall ceiling every later stage inherits. On Abt-Buy the union of all blockers reaches pair completeness 0.9928 at reduction ratio 0.9644, cutting 2,359,878 possible pairs to 84,117 candidates. The 8 true pairs no blocker emits are unrecoverable: the classifier never sees them, so system recall cannot exceed that figure however good the model becomes. Committed to reports/blocking.md.

Blockers are scored on pair completeness and reduction ratio, always together and never on accuracy, precision or F1 -- their output is overwhelmingly non-duplicates by construction, and discarding non-duplicates is the job rather than an error. PC divides by all 1,118 ground-truth pairs; union.py:score raises if handed a denominator taken from the survivors, which is the self-fulfilling measurement the blocking-eval skill records as having reached publication.

- blocking/pairs.py: candidate pairs packed as int64 i*n+j with i<j. 8 bytes per pair against 100+ for a tuple in a set, so the same code survives the jump to synth/ scale, and union is np.unique over a concatenation rather than millions of Python hash lookups.
- blocking/standard.py, sorted_neighborhood.py, lsh.py, ann.py: the four blocker families. Oversized blocks are dropped, not expanded -- one 5,000-record block is 12.5M pairs and discriminates nothing -- and a drop now surfaces as a report warning, since a silently lowered ceiling is the same class of defect as a hidden denominator.
- blocking/union.py, evaluate.py: the union and the CLI behind `python -m dedup.blocking.evaluate`, which CLAUDE.md previously listed as an intended contract.
- normalize.py: new public code_key(), and model_number_key alongside model_number. Abt writes KXTS208W where Buy writes KX-TS208W for the same phone; both are correct as printed codes, so the printed form is kept for the review queue and the stripped form does the blocking. Worth pair completeness 0.3354 -> 0.5349. code_key decomposes NFKD internally because its callers disagree about how folded their input already is -- without that a precomposed U-umlaut is dropped whole while a decomposed one keeps its base letter, keying one code two ways.

Two defects found by an er-invariants audit are fixed here. The report claimed its parameters were chosen on a held-out split; they were swept over the same catalog they are scored on, and no blocking module imports split_by_entity at all. That sentence is replaced by what is true, plus the measured held-out ceilings (0.9949 train, 1.0000 test) so the selection bias is visible rather than asserted away. blocking/standard.py also carried a private second copy of the vendor-code rule built on str.lower; it now calls normalize.code_key, so one edit changes both.

faiss builds its HNSW index single-threaded on purpose: parallel graph construction gave 14,608 / 14,603 / 14,602 candidates across three runs of identical input, and a committed report whose numbers drift between runs is not reproducible.

Open questions updated in the same commit, per the convention. Recorded under "Settled by measurement": the model-number key finding above, the leave-one-out marginal table showing three of six blockers add no completeness the others do not already have (the model-number blocker is entirely subsumed by code tokens, and LSH earns nothing for 18,317 candidates), that ann is the load-bearing blocker at PC 0.9562 alone, and that the 8 remaining misses are disjoint identifier systems and truncated titles rather than near-misses -- neither reachable by tuning a window. Nothing is deleted from the blocker set: a negative result someone can re-run is evidence, and every row is configuration- and dataset-specific.

author: horsto
body:
This fixes a subtle issue where, in multi-label projects, a single video frame could end up in two different splits at once. It also brings OCTRON's command-line (CLI) training tools in line with the graphical interface when preparing training data. From the CLI you can now control whether incomplete frames are pruned, whether touching objects are separated (watershed), and how big a gap to leave between training and validation/test frames — with defaults living in the same `config.yaml` the GUI already uses. 

## Technical summary
- `octron split`/`octron train` gain `--prune/--no-prune`, `--watershed/--no-watershed`, and `--buffer`, matching the GUI checkboxes (the CLI previously always pruned).
- New `split_buffer` config key joins `split_train_fraction`/`split_val_fraction`/`split_seed`; precedence is CLI flag > `config.yaml` > built-in default, and the GUI reads the same values.
- `prepare_split` computes the train/val/test assignment once over the union of every label's frames and filters it per label, so a frame shared across classes can't leak into different splits (previously this duplicated images across split folders with incomplete `.txt` labels).
- Shared empty-geometry pruning is extracted into `prune_frames_by_geometry`; new unit tests cover the CLI flags, the config, per-frame split consistency, and buffer forwarding.
- Validation: ruff + all pre-commit hooks pass; 208 tests pass.

Closes #90

author: xav59213
body:
## Pourquoi

Retour utilisateur (Dimitri) après HA **2026.8** :

- Homexa crée un device par client LAN (tracker + RSSI), alors que HA ne fusionne plus les devices entre intégrations.
- DeviceTools / merge ne fonctionne plus.
- Un client hors-ligne ou Ethernet au premier lancement n’a souvent pas de capteur RSSI.
- Demande : pouvoir importer les capteurs **sans** device Homexa pour les appareils déjà connus ailleurs.

## Changements

Nouveau flux d’options : **Paramètres → Freebox Homexa → Configurer**

| Option | Défaut | Effet |
|---|---|---|
| `track_lan_clients` | oui | Crée les `device_tracker` des clients LAN |
| `create_wifi_sensors` | oui | Crée les capteurs RSSI Wi-Fi |
| `create_lan_devices` | oui | Rattache tracker + RSSI à un device Homexa |

- Désactiver `create_lan_devices` laisse tracker / RSSI en entités seules (nom explicite sur le RSSI).
- Server, répéteurs F-RP01A et pack Home (alarme, PIR, DWS, caméras, volets) **gardent** leurs devices.
- Le RSSI est toujours ajouté plus tard si le client passe en Wi-Fi après le 1er scan (`signal_device_update`).
- Changer une option recharge l’intégration.

Comportement par défaut inchangé pour ne pas casser les installs existantes.

## Hors scope

Le décalage PIR ~10 s avec l’intégration officielle + Homexa n’est pas un bug : deux polls indépendants de la même API. La doc le précise.

## Test

- [ ] Options cochées (défaut) : même comportement qu’avant
- [ ] `create_lan_devices` désactivé : plus de nouveau device client, entités toujours là
- [ ] `track_lan_clients` désactivé : plus de tracker client, répéteurs / Home OK
- [ ] Client Wi-Fi qui arrive après le 1er lancement : RSSI créé ensuite
- [ ] Ethernet : pas de RSSI (normal)

author: daiimus
body:
Owner ruling on #3029: `to` should be able to address the things around you — what you're holding, the people present — and the pocketed-radio disagreement should then solve itself rather than being legislated.

It does.

### The rule

`to` had **no reachability rule at all** for ordinary targets — `caller.search` resolves the room plus your entire inventory, so you could address a crate on the floor or something buried in a pocket — and then a bespoke restriction for radios bolted on top. Two answers to one question, and the radio one was the odd shape.

Now: **you can address what is out where you or the room can see it.** Anything in the room, plus anything on your person that is held or worn.

What that excludes is the pocket, and that settles the radio case without a word about radios: a pocketed handset is neither held nor worn, so `to` refuses it exactly as `xmit` always did.

### Room items are kept

You were hesitant about them ("may get in the way of things") — right about the risk, but it lands somewhere else. Nothing that worked was removed: you can still speak at a crate, a corpse, a console.

### Where the hesitancy was right

My first cut made room items fully equivalent and let a base station be transmitted through **while standing**, which broke `test_to_console_refuses_the_standing`. The desk seam is that you take the chair.

So the two acts are separated: **speaking AT** a radio is reachability, **transmitting THROUGH** one is operation. A set on the floor can be addressed and not keyed.

The operating rule is no longer written out twice. `world.radio.can_transmit_through` is the same worn / held / seated-board answer `xmit` gets from `active_transmit_radio`, stated once so the picker and the judge can't drift apart again. **That divergence, not the existence of a check, was the defect.**

### Fixtures that encoded the old rule

- `test_radio.test_to_retarget_transmits` passed with the radio merely in `caller.contents` — a pocket. Corrected, plus new siblings for worn and pocketed.
- All five room helpers in `test_communication` built a room whose occupants were never actually put in it.
- Dropped `patch("world.radio.is_radio", return_value=True)` throughout: `_held_radios` walks every hand slot, so an always-true `is_radio` makes an **empty hand** read as a radio and `active_transmit_radio` returns `None` out of `held[0]`. The stub was under test, not the code.

### Evidence

- 17 new tests. **Two fail behaviourally against the unfixed tree**: `test_a_pocketed_radio_is_refused`, and `test_a_pocketed_set_does_not` in the pre-existing radio suite (no new symbols, so it loads both ways).
- The other 11 *error* against unfixed code because `addressable` doesn't exist yet. That's a loader error, not evidence, and isn't counted as such.
- 455 tests across speech, radio, dispatch and identity pass.

body:
Two things a reader notices and cannot explain — both fixed by **removing special cases**, not by adding anything.

## The butterfly explorer was bolted on beside the Cycles world, not built inside it

Five special cases nothing else here has:

- it sat **outside** `cycGroup`, a sibling of the whole world
- it **hid the entire group** whenever it was on — a second authority over a fact the declaration table already owns
- it **bypassed `updateCyc`**, so the world had one tick path and an exception
- it **returned early** out of the top of the framing function, before the layout guides or any other frame
- it **replaced the control panel** — entering one frame of thirteen threw away the epoch controls, the multiphase solar control, the frame chooser and every cycle row

None of it was needed. `cycGroup` carries no transform, so the explorer is a sibling of every other instrument; `CYC_FRAME_INSTRUMENTS` — which already listed it — is the single authority on visibility; it ticks and frames itself where the others do; and it **contributes a section** to the shared panel exactly as the galactic butterfly and the wheels do.

Measured across five frames: same fourteen chips, same multiphase control, same frame chooser, explorer section present only in its own frame, zero foreign furniture.

## "All cycles" was showing everything, which is not an overview

Measured on screen: **seven instruments and 165 visible labels**. A frame with 165 labels has no reader — the eye finds no entry, and the declutter pass hides whichever labels lose the collision test, so what is seen is arbitrary rather than chosen.

```
before   7 instruments · 165 labels
after    3 instruments ·  31 labels
```

The four instruments taken out are not lost and never were — each already had its own frame, and the grouped chip row from an hour ago puts every one a click away. *"The stage that shows everything" was a reasonable home when several of these had nowhere else to be. They all have somewhere now, and a stage that shows everything shows nothing.*

**And removing `hierarchy` from the declaration moved the count only to 112**, because two assignments below the loop named the frame again on their own. A declaration something else can override is not a declaration.

## Two older checks went red, and both pinned a decision rather than an invariant

One required chronometry to be declared for *"the hierarchy and its isolated frame only"*; the other — written this morning — required the Saros engine in both. What each exists to defend is unchanged and still enforced: **an instrument in no frame is unreachable**, and **a frame whose chip names an instrument must show it**. Which *other* frames it also appears in is a composition choice neither file has an opinion on, and both say so now.

Every one of the thirteen frames still has an instrument of its own; the busiest is the resonance web at 84 labels, which is that subject rather than clutter.

## Verification

Five mutations, each failing by name: the explorer back outside `cycGroup` · its section removed from the shared panel · its tick removed from `updateCyc` · the overview showing everything again · the web naming its own frame over the table.

validate green · multiphase green · linked contract 15/15 · `npm test` green (**eleven** verifiers) · API suite **70/70** · zero page errors across all thirteen frames.

body:
Заменяет #2 — тот закрылся автоматически, когда после мержа #1 удалилась его базовая ветка. Содержимое то же плюс правки после первого реального запуска в Docker.

## Что внутри

**Инфраструктура**
- `db/init/001_schema.sql` — схема по `SPEC.md` §4: `students`, `sessions`, `tasks`, `timetable`. Поля для пароля нет намеренно. Сверх спеки: `moodle_event_id` с частичным уникальным индексом, чтобы повторный импорт дедлайнов не плодил дубли, и `ON DELETE CASCADE` — студент должен уметь удалить все свои данные.
- `docker-compose.yml` — `postgres:16-alpine` с healthcheck, порт наружу только на `127.0.0.1` и через `POSTGRES_HOST_PORT`.
- `.env.example` с командами генерации обоих секретов, `Makefile` (`up/down/logs/psql/reset`).

**Общий пакет `shared/sduhub_common`**
- `BaseConfig`, `Database` (пул asyncpg), `TokenCipher` (Fernet), `require_internal_key`, `setup_logging`.
- Маскирование токенов и паролей встроено в сам логгер, включая логи доступа uvicorn — `SECURITY.md` требует не допускать токены в логи, и полагаться на аккуратность каждого вызова здесь нельзя.

**`auth-service`** — `POST /login`, `POST /logout`, `DELETE /account`, `GET /internal/session/{id}`, `GET /internal/token/{id}`, `GET /health`.

## Решения по безопасности

- Пароль появляется ровно в одной функции (`moodle_login.py`), уходит в Moodle по HTTPS и не сохраняется. У поля `password` стоит `repr=False`, чтобы не всплыть в трейсбеке.
- Ошибки `httpx` не пробрасываются наружу: в их тексте лежит URL с паролем.
- Ошибка входа всегда одна и та же — иначе перебором можно узнать, существует ли учётка.
- Токен отдаётся только по `/internal/*` за проверкой `INTERNAL_API_KEY` через `compare_digest`.
- Не расшифровался токен (сменили ключ) → 401 «требуется повторный вход», не 500.

## Проверено вживую

`make up` на реальном Docker: `postgres` healthy, схема из 4 таблиц накатилась, `auth` отвечает `{"service":"auth-service","db":true}`. `/internal/*` без ключа даёт 403, `/logout` без `X-Session-Id` — 401. `pytest` — 14 тестов зелёные.

Запуск вскрыл два бага, оба починены здесь же: порт 5432 на хосте был занят локально установленным Postgres, и логи uvicorn писались дважды (не хватало `propagate=False`).

Вход в реальный Moodle с настоящим логином не проверялся — это Фаза 0 на своём аккаунте, отдельно.

## Problem

`DflashWeights::load` and the base/windowed `DflashScratch` constructors transfer GPU owners through multi-step construction without RAII. Ordinary late errors could strand completed layers, staged weights, optional scratch, or window-extension allocations.

## Change

- stage global/per-layer DFlash weights until complete publication and roll back completed layers plus unpublished owners on error
- upload raw DFlash weights through the reusable GPU pool, returning the allocation if H2D copy fails
- stage every base-scratch allocation and free the ledger in reverse order on failure
- keep the fully owned base scratch as the window-extension rollback owner, including the replaced position buffer
- add private deterministic boundaries for final-owner and final-layer fault injection; public constructors and outer `GenericDflashStaging` / Qwen35 `or_free!` ownership remain unchanged
- add ignored gfx1151 regressions for late weight, completed-layer, base-scratch, and window-extension failure followed by immediate retry

## Verification

Final head `53bba32a5` on upstream/beta `fdb750d6d`:

- `cargo test -p hipfire-runtime --lib construction_tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture`: 4 passed on gfx1151

author: janzen01
body:
Stacked on #25 → #24 → #23. Merge in order.

Closes F16, including its open question 1 (the F63 reversal), and is **the reason this release is `10.1.0`**.

## The change

`Build()` throws without `WithTieBreaker`. Required outright, not "a `DefaultSortBy` **or** a tie-breaker" —
default-sort fields are filtered through `When(...)` and the tie-breaker is not, so the weaker rule passes for
a config whose only default is disabled for this caller and still leaves nothing to order by.

The rule is not new; its *location* is. It used to be a `400` per request, which reported a configuration
defect as a client error and stayed invisible for as long as every caller happened to send `sortBy` — the same
condition under which the paging was silently non-deterministic anyway. Deleted with it: the runtime
exception, its row on the errors reference, and the `keys.Count == 0` guard.

## Why `SortBy` comes back non-nullable in the same PR

`ApplyPaginateFilters` skipped sort resolution only because `ResolveSorts` could *refuse* a config with nothing
to order by — rejecting a facet count over a request that never wanted an order. No such config can exist now,
so both composers validate identically and `[]` unambiguously means "resolved, nothing requested". Shipping
this later would have published a nullable `SortBy` whose only justification this PR had just removed.

## One thing to know before tagging

**The break is behavioural, not binary.** `dotnet pack` stays silent: `IReadOnlyList<string>?` →
`IReadOnlyList<string>` is a nullable *annotation* and the CLR signature is unchanged, so ApiCompat has nothing
to compare. `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` (RS0017) is the only guard that fires. `10.1.0` therefore still carries
**one** suppression entry (F62's `WithGuards`), not two.

## Review findings, all fixed with a failing-first test

1. **`AllowUnlimited(int.MaxValue)` silently returned nothing.** `maxRows + 1` overflowed to `int.MinValue`,
   and `Take` with a negative count returns no rows — so an unlimited read answered 0 items and a 0 count, with
   no exception anywhere. Clamped through `long`.
2. **The derivation promised ranges the engine cannot build.** `IsOrdered` accepted `IComparable<T>`, but
   `BuildComparison` only uses its `CompareTo` stand-in for enums, `string` and `Guid`. A registered
   `IComparable<T>`-only type got the range row, advertised it through metadata and OpenAPI, and answered `400`
   to every range request. The probe is the relational operator now.
3. **The `-1` carve-out had loosened `limit` parsing.** `AllowLeadingSign` also started accepting `+5` on
   `limit` while `page` kept rejecting it. Matched as a literal instead — and the theory that looked like it
   covered this was fooled by `+` decoding to a space, so it now uses `%2B`.
4. **The packed NuGet readme's RBAC example had no tie-breaker**, so copying it would now throw.
5. **Both removed API entries are recorded as `*REMOVED*` lines** in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` rather than
   deleted from `Shipped`, which is what keeps the removal visible to the guard the release checklist describes.

404 tests, up from 399. Build clean under `-warnaserror`, pack clean, docs green through both verifiers.

author: honanevan
body:
Volcano is missing from the add-on compatibility catalogue. This adds its upstream Kubernetes compatibility matrix, a repeatable scraper, catalogue metadata, Helm-rendered image references, and the aggregate catalogue entry.

The scraper joins explicitly named release-family rows in Volcano's maintained README to stable application/chart versions in its official Helm index. Only check marks count as exact compatibility. It excludes HEAD, prereleases, families absent from the matrix, and historical chart entries with ambiguous appVersion 0.1. Source failures or malformed matrices stop processing before the shared updater is called; previously stored historical rows are preserved by the updater.

On 2026-09-08, 24 stable releases matched the matrix. Plural's existing reduction logic stores seven entries across the 1.10–1.15 families, including latest 1.15.2. This is upstream-declared family compatibility, not independent Kubernetes integration testing. Some release-tag READMEs omit their own family, which is why this uses the maintained matrix instead of guessing from a tagged HEAD row.

## Sources

- [Maintained compatibility matrix](https://github.com/volcano-sh/volcano#kubernetes-compatibility)
- [Exact documentation snapshot used for the fixture and generation](https://github.com/volcano-sh/volcano/blob/606c628d364db8de18c045e947d5255ef058aa26/README.md#kubernetes-compatibility)
- [Official Helm index](https://volcano-sh.github.io/helm-charts/index.yaml)
- [Volcano installation documentation](https://volcano.sh/docs/gettingstarted/installation/)

## Test Plan

- Python 3.12 with the repository's compatibility requirements: `python -m pytest utils/compatibility/tests -q` — 147 passed, 81 subtests passed.
- 20 new offline tests cover source fixtures, non-compatible markers, prereleases, malformed/ambiguous matrices, empty joins, failures before writing, version ordering, and shared-updater persistence.
- A scoped GitHub Actions workflow runs the new offline tests. No GitHub CI run is claimed yet.
- Live `scrapers.volcano.scrape()` completed with Helm 3.19.0, rendering images for all seven stored entries. Paid summarization was disabled.
- Both generated YAML files validate against `static/compatibilities/schema.json`. Existing aggregate entries are semantically unchanged.
- Official icon URL verified; patch whitespace checks pass.

Test environment: local Python 3.12 on Windows; no running Plural deployment required for this catalogue-only change.

## Checklist

- [x] I have added a meaningful title and summary to convey the impact of this PR to a user.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- Documentation updates: not required; source links and fixture provenance are included.
- Agent deployment: not applicable; no agent code changes.

Plural Flow: console

## Contributor programme

Prepared with OpenAI Codex for @honanevan; implementation and validation were agent-led, with no separate human review claimed. Please consider this contribution under the README's published $300 new-compatibility-scraper reward, subject to your review and one-award-per-month rule. Could you confirm eligibility and whether an accepted award can be paid via PayPal? Payment information will be exchanged privately through the appropriate payout channel when ready. No award or payment is assumed.

App Doctor's current agentic pack does not have dedicated checks for lifecycle/replay failures, dependency reachability, or upload-to-active-preview execution paths. These are separate from the prompt refinements in #8495 and deserve their own review surface.

### WHAT is this pull request doing?

- `DEPENDENCY_REACHABILITY`

author: stardustsuperwizard
body:
Closes #87

## Changes

**Resolution**

- `rules/actions/attack_action.gd` — `_init()` now takes `attacker_template`,
  `target_template` and `combat_profile` in place of the weapon and the two
  `DiceProfile`s. `resolve()` parses the attacker over `_attacker_template` and
  the target over `_target_template`, so every stat each reads through is its
  own; `_read_fighter()` takes the template as a parameter and its docstring
  says why the flanking candidate list may pass either. Reach is
  `attacker.range_hexes()`, the attack pool `attacker.attack()`, the damage
  `attacker.damage()`. Two new private helpers resolve spec §7.3's two charts
  separately — `_resolved_attack_target()` (attack baseline, the *target's*
  flanking priced from `attack_*`, plus `_engagement_bonus()`) and
  `_resolved_save_target()` (save baseline, the *attacker's* flanking priced
  from `save_*`, `extra` 0). `_engagement_bonus()` compares the board distance
  to `engagement_range`, never the Range stat. Draw order is unchanged: attack
  pool in full through `DicePool.roll_dice()`, then the save pool, then
  `count_at_or_above()`. Two accessors added, `attack_target()` and
  `save_target()`, so the acceptance chart is directly assertable.
  `FAILURE_MISSING_DATA` now covers the three injected objects.
- `rules/combat/dice_pool.gd` — `roll()`, `success_symbols()`,
  `count_successes()` and `CRITICAL` deleted; docstring rewritten around the
  d6/target-number model.

**Model deletions**

- `rules/fighters/weapon_template.gd` (+ `.uid`) — deleted.
- `rules/combat/dice_profile.gd` (+ `.uid`) — deleted.
- `resources/weapons/sword.tres`, `resources/weapons/bow.tres`,
  `resources/dice/attack_die.tres`, `resources/dice/save_die.tres` — deleted;
  both directories are gone.
- `rules/fighters/fighter_template.gd` — `weapons` removed; docstrings no
  longer reference the deleted weapon resource.
- `rules/fighters/fighter.gd` — `weapons()` removed; class docstring and the
  gdlint waiver's method count updated.
- `resources/fighters/warrior.tres`, `resources/fighters/archer.tres` — the
  `weapons` array and its two `ext_resource` entries removed. No stat retuned.

**Tests**

- `rules/tests/attack_action_test.gd` — re-derived against target numbers.
  Fixtures are now `fighter_template()`, `standard_profile()` (the authored
  dials restated in memory) and `forced_profile()` (targets of `ALWAYS_TARGET`
  / `NEVER_TARGET`, so an outcome is fixed by the die rather than the seed).
  Refusals, the inclusive range boundary, the three null-injection refusals,
  draw order, Hit/Drawn/Miss, damage, defeat, flanking tiers and determinism.
- `rules/tests/attack_action_target_test.gd` — **new.** Spec §7.3's chart: all
  eight acceptance rows, simultaneous flanking at different tiers, the
  attacker's-own-stats test, warrior/archer damage, and reach as the
  attacker's. Folded into `AttackActionTest.run()` exactly as the push suite
  is; not registered in `_suites`. Split out because `attack_action_test.gd`
  would otherwise cross `.gdlintrc`'s 1000-line ceiling.
- `rules/tests/attack_action_push_test.gd` — fixture forwarders and every
  `AttackAction.new()` updated; outcomes forced through `_forced_profile()`.
- `rules/tests/dice_pool_test.gd` — symbol tests removed; the pinned-sequence
  hand-worked test replaced by one worked from the definition of the die.
- `rules/tests/fighter_test.gd`, `rules/tests/fighter_template_test.gd` —
  weapon fixtures and assertions removed. `fighter_serialization_test.gd`
  follows through `FighterTest.make_template()` and needed no edit.
- `tests/resource_data_test.gd` — reduced to the three surviving `.tres`;
  "retuning is a file edit" now retunes a `FighterTemplate`; the stat
  read-through test runs over both rosters.
- `tests/action_runner_test.gd` — the gate test builds a `CombatProfile`
  instead of a weapon and two dice profiles.
- `rules/tests/determinism_test.gd` — no change needed. Its `"weapons"` key is
  an opaque `GameState` payload field, not a weapon resource.
- `rules/README.md` — no change needed; it lists neither deleted class.

## Validation Performed

```
GODOT_BIN=/tmp/Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64 .github/scripts/validate-godot.sh
```

```
Godot Engine v4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f
... 33 PASS lines ...
All 33 test suites passed.
Godot headless validation passed.
```

Also run: `gdformat --check` (52 files unchanged) and `gdlint` (no problems)
over every tracked `.gd` plus the new file.

Godot was not installed in this environment; a 4.7-stable Linux build was
downloaded to run the repository script unmodified. `project.godot` declares
`config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7")`, so that is the matching engine.

Four negative controls were run to prove the new assertions are not vacuous,
each reverted afterwards:

| Injected defect | Reported |
| --- | --- |
| engagement derived from `attacker.range_hexes()` | `FAIL archer -> warrior in contact must attack on 4+, got 5+` |
| attacker parsed over `_target_template` | 11 failures across reach, pool size, damage and the chart |
| save target priced from the `attack_*` dials | `FAIL ... must save on 3+, got 4+` and two more |
| attack target priced from the `save_*` dials | `FAIL ... must attack on 4+, got 3+` and two more |

- [x] `.github/scripts/validate-godot.sh` — passes, all 33 suites
- [x] Existing tests pass — all 33 suites, including both contract scanners
- [x] Tests added for new behavior — the eight chart rows, simultaneous
      flanking, the attacker's-own-stats test, per-attacker damage and
      attacker-owned reach

## Acceptance Criteria

body:
Resolves #3531.

## Summary
Six workflows triggered on `pull_request` events used the unsafe `${{ vars.FLUXION_LINUX_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}` pattern — when the `vars.FLUXION_LINUX_RUNNER` repo variable is set, PR-controlled code silently routes to a persistent self-hosted runner, violating `docs/SECURITY.md §7` (Issue #3445).

Migrated 9 affected `runs-on:` lines across 5 workflow files to the canonical guarded pattern (already used by `onnx-integrity.yml` / `python-tests.yml`): `runs-on: >-<newline>${{<newline>github.event_name == 'push'<newline>&& github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'<newline>&& vars.FLUXION_LINUX_RUNNER<newline>|| 'ubuntu-latest'<newline>}}`.

Added `scripts/check_runner_routing_policy.py` to catch future regressions at PR time. Mirrors `scripts/check_required_checks_sync.py` pattern (#2866 / #3116).

## Changes
- `.github/workflows/surrogate_drift_gate.yml:128` — guarded
- `.github/workflows/ashrae_140_strict_energy_gate.yml:140` — guarded
- `.github/workflows/h_tr_em_regression_gate.yml:84` — guarded
- `.github/workflows/fast_math_check.yml:130, 202, 278, 491` — guarded (4 jobs)
- `.github/workflows/rust-tests.yml:755, 808` — guarded (cuda-smoke + cuda-parity)
- `scripts/check_runner_routing_policy.py` (new) — gate script
- `.github/workflows/scripts-tests.yml` — wire-up of the new gate

## Verification
- `python3 scripts/check_runner_routing_policy.py` exits 0
- `git grep -nE 'runs-on.*vars\.FLUXION_LINUX_RUNNER.*\|\|.*ubuntu-latest' .github/workflows/` returns only 4 matches, all correctly classified as exempt:
  - `loom-stress.yml:48`, `memory-budget.yml:63`, `mutation-nightly.yml:52` — schedule-only workflows (never run on PR-controlled code)
  - `rust-tests.yml:492` — `build-release` job with `if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` (main-only)
- No other files touched; canonical `onnx-integrity.yml` / `python-tests.yml` patterns untouched

Closes #3531.

Scope guard: Do NOT change `vars.FLUXION_LINUX_RUNNER` defaults, secrets, or any other runner-related config. Do NOT touch the canonical pattern in `onnx-integrity.yml` / `python-tests.yml`. Do NOT migrate workflows that don't trigger on PR.

## Summary by Sourcery

Harden PR-triggered GitHub Actions workflows against unsafe self-hosted runner routing and add a regression gate for future policy violations.

New Features:
- Add automated detection for unsafe self-hosted runner routing in PR-triggered workflows.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent PR-controlled jobs from selecting the persistent self-hosted runner through the Linux runner repository variable.

Enhancements:
- Restrict self-hosted runner selection to pushes on the main branch while retaining GitHub-hosted runners for PRs.

CI:
- Enforce the runner-routing security policy in the workflow script tests.

body:
## Problem

The setup commands only rendered inside the one-time panel shown just after
minting a token, and disappeared for good when that panel was dismissed. Anyone
returning to the profile page later — the common case — had no way to find out
how to wire up a client.

The command itself is not a secret. Only the token is.

## Fix

A **How to connect** disclosure that is always present on the card, covering both
Claude Code and Codex. It opens itself immediately after a mint with the real
token already substituted so the command can be copied and run as-is, and stays
available afterwards showing `<your token>` as a placeholder, alongside a
reminder that tokens are shown only once and a lost one means minting a new one.

## Tests

`McpTokensCard.test.tsx` 11 → 15, covering: instructions visible without creating
a token, both clients present, the real token substituted after minting, and —
the regression that matters — the instructions surviving dismissal of the
one-time panel while the secret itself goes.

Frontend suite 957 → **961 passing**, 0 failures. `tsc` clean, build green.

## Note

This is an interim improvement. The better end state is CLI-initiated OAuth,
where `claude mcp add --transport http` opens a browser consent screen and the
token lands in the CLI with nothing to copy at all. That is phase 2 in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-mcp-auth-design.md` and would make this card
a fallback for headless use rather than the primary path.

author: timo-42
body:
## Summary

Two dev-tools follow-ups from `.plan/progress-probe-7.md` (read-only, referenced for context only — not part of this branch):

- **`--reachability-cell-cap N` / `--reachability-round-cap N`**: `--reachability-report`'s per-round cell cap (40,000) and round cap (6) were fixed in source with no CLI override. A map whose round-0 reachable area is itself larger than the default cap — `c4a2` in probe-7's own finding — stops the walk before a single round-advance edge (door/breakable/pushable/pendulum) ever runs, hiding whatever those edges would otherwise reveal. Both caps are now overridable, each bounded by a new hard sanity maximum (`ohl_engine::reachability::MAX_CELL_CAP` = 2,000,000, `MAX_ROUND_CAP` = 64) documented as a safety ceiling, not a per-map tuned value, so an override can't turn a single report into unbounded work.
- **`--reachability-assume-pendulum-wait`**: the walk had no way to model a `func_pendulum` swinging through a corridor — it is neither a door, a breakable, nor a pushable, so it stayed on the frontier forever regardless of every other assumption flag (probe-7's `c1a2` finding, with the button hypothesis fully exhausted). The new flag treats a `func_pendulum` on the frontier as passable between rounds, the same "detach the brush" treatment a broken breakable or a shoved pushable already gets, on the documented assumption that a player can time the swing and walk through during a clear moment — not a claim the corridor is permanently open. The round that follows one being treated this way is tagged `(pendulum wait assumed)` in the printed report (`RoundReport::pendulum_wait`), so a route depending on this assumption is distinguishable from one that isn't.

Depends on #130 (`m9/start-inventory`): this branch was built on top of it since it was still open/unmerged when this work started; this PR targets `main` but will need a rebase once #130 merges.

## Details

- `ohl_engine::reachability::ReachabilityConfig` gained `assume_pendulum_wait: bool` (default `false`, matching every other assumption flag) and the `cell_cap`/`max_rounds` fields are now caller-overridable through the CLI up to the new `MAX_CELL_CAP`/`MAX_ROUND_CAP` constants.
- `RoundReport` gained `pendulums_opened: usize` (parallel to `doors_opened`/`breakables_opened`/`pushables_opened`) and `pendulum_wait: bool` (the round-following-a-pendulum-detach tag).
- `FrontierClass`/`FrontierAgg` gained `pendulum_openable: bool`, detected via the existing `ohl_game::registry::Pendulum` component the same way `Door`/`Breakable`/`Pushable` are already checked.
- New CLI flags in `ohl-app` (`dev-tools` only, `requires = "reachability_report"`): `--reachability-cell-cap`, `--reachability-round-cap`, `--reachability-assume-pendulum-wait`, each validated by a dedicated parser that rejects anything outside `(0, MAX]`.
- `run_reachability_report` was split (`print_reachability_round`) to stay under the project's line-count lint once the new printed fields were added.
- New synthetic fixture `reachability_pendulum_bsp`/`REACH_PENDULUM_MAP` in `ohl-engine`'s `test_support`, reusing the existing breakable/pushable obstacle-corridor shape with a `func_pendulum` obstacle instead. No bytes come from any game installation (`docs/CLEAN_ROOM.md`).
- README's `--reachability-report` section documents all three new flags with usage examples.

## Real-payload verification (aggregates only, per this project's clean-room output policy)

`c4a2` with `--reachability-assume-armed --reachability-cell-cap 500000`: round 0 now completes uncapped at 79,296 reachable cells (matching probe-6's own manual, never-shipped 300k-cap reimplementation) instead of stopping at the old fixed 40,000 cap. The frontier is `func_breakable` x4 and `func_wall` x3, neither use-openable; `trigger_changelevel` is not reached this round (~1640 units from spawn). The breakables here are not reported damage-openable despite `--reachability-assume-armed`, and the walk accordingly stops after round 0 — a map-data finding (not investigated further in this PR), not a flag malfunction; the cap itself is confirmed lifted.

`c1a2` with `--reachability-assume-armed --reachability-assume-longjump --reachability-assume-pendulum-wait --reachability-round-cap 12`: the walk now advances past the `func_pendulum` that previously stalled it forever (probe-7's finding) — round 1's frontier reports `func_pendulum` x1 as pendulum-openable, and round 2 is tagged `(pendulum wait assumed)`. The walk continues through 8 rounds (reachable cells growing from 223 to 1994), clearing all breakables along the way, and settles with `func_button` x4 and `func_wall` x2 as the final frontier; `trigger_changelevel` stays unreached (~230 units from spawn) — consistent with probe-7's own conclusion that the remaining blocker there is the buttons-exhausted `func_wall` frontier, not the pendulum.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p ohl-engine -p ohl-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ohl-engine -p ohl-app --all-targets --features dev-tools -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p ohl-engine -p ohl-app` (all green, including two new regression tests: a small `--reachability-cell-cap` stops the walk early and reports `capped`; a `func_pendulum` fixture is passable only with `--reachability-assume-pendulum-wait`, and the following round is tagged `pendulum_wait`)
- [x] `cargo xtask policy`
- [x] `cargo xtask graph`
- [x] Manual run against the real payload on `c4a2` (cap) and `c1a2` (pendulum), as summarized above

author: onamfc
body:
Two commits: the schema-initialisation fix, and a comment cleanup.

---

## 1. Serialise schema initialisation with an advisory lock

`initializeDatabase()` is safe to call from one process and unsafe to call from several at once against an empty database.

`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is **not atomic**. The existence check and the creation are separate steps, so two connections can both find a table absent and both attempt to create it. The loser does not quietly do nothing — it fails:

```
duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_type_typname_nsp_index"
```

The `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` and `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` statements have the same property.

### Reproduction

Four initialisations run concurrently against one empty database:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Succeeded | 1 of 4 | 4 of 4 |
| Failed | 3 of 4 | 0 |

Against an **already-initialised** database all four succeed even without the fix, because every statement short-circuits. That is why this only surfaces on the first boot of a new environment that starts more than one instance — or a test harness initialising in parallel — and why it stays invisible in ordinary use.

### The fix

A session-level advisory lock around the initialisation, so the second caller waits instead of racing.

- Postgres releases the lock automatically when the connection ends, so a process that dies mid-initialisation cannot wedge the others.
- Blocking is the desired behaviour here: another instance is building the schema this one is about to use.
- No transaction is introduced, so failure semantics are unchanged — partial progress still persists exactly as before.
- `SCHEMA_INIT_LOCK_KEY` is exported so an embedding application taking its own advisory locks on the same database can avoid colliding with it.

### Testing

A database-backed test covers both halves of the contract: that initialisation **blocks** while another session holds the lock, and that the lock is **released** once it completes. A leaked lock would block every subsequent boot, so the second half matters as much as the first.

The behaviour under test is a property of Postgres locking — a mocked client would accept any sequence of queries and prove nothing — so it needs a real server. The test skips itself when `DATABASE_URL` is absent, keeping `npm test` green without one, and a new CI job supplies a Postgres service so it actually runs rather than silently skipping.

Verified by mutation: with the lock removed, both cases fail.

---

## 2. Remove internal tracker ids and downstream references from comments

author: ralyodio
body:
### The directory

`nixamp.com/directory` lists the nixamps that agreed to be listed. The PWA gets a
**Browse the directory** button next to the address field, so picking a stream
takes no typing.

The registry is in memory with a TTL and heartbeats. A directory restart costs
one heartbeat rather than a migration, and a stream that dies falls out of the
list without anyone having to notice it went. It lives on whoever hosts the page,
so only the deployment behind nixamp.com passes `--directory`.

### Publishing the share link would have handed strangers the controls

One key guarded both listening and `/api/command`, so publishing it would have
let anyone in the directory pause your music or point your machine at a
different source.

A server mints **two** keys now. The share link drives the player; the listen key
hears it and gets a 403 from `/api/command` and `/api/source`. Only the listen
key is ever published.

### Asked for, not assumed

```
  List this stream at https://nixamp.com/directory so anyone can find it?
  It publishes http://198.51.100.7:4321/s/Lk1EM_mP977e1VT — listen only,
  not the controls. [Y/n]
```

Yes is the default, and the prompt shows the exact link. A terminal that cannot
ask never publishes, because nobody being there to answer is not consent.
`--publish` and `--no-publish` skip the question; `--name` sets the label.

Loopback and link-local URLs are refused: an entry only its publisher can open is
not an entry. Names and track titles are stripped of control characters, since
that text is drawn in a terminal as well as a browser.

### It also fixes every Windows build

Both Windows jobs failed on v0.2.0. `new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname` is
`/D:/a/nixamp` on Windows, so `resolve()` produced `D:\D:\a\nixamp` and the icon
writer died on a doubled drive letter. Ten files carried the same line; they all
use `fileURLToPath` now.

### Verified

- 103 tests (was 92), typecheck clean
- Live: a real registry accepted an announcement, listed it, and refused a
  loopback URL
- Live: the two keys are different, and on a running server the listen key gets
  200 from `/api/state` and `/api/stream/0` but **403 from `/api/command` and
  `/api/source`**, while the control key gets 200
- Live on a pty: the prompt appears with `[Y/n]`, `y` attempts to publish and `n`
  skips. It currently reports "could not reach nixamp.com", which is correct —
  the deployed 0.2.0 has no directory endpoint until this merges
- Live: no prompt at all without a terminal

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_017Df2FNu5DhinMV2soRz3cy

author: setoelkahfi
body:
Reopening a saved thread in Zed opened an empty one that looked like a new conversation (#77). Also fixes https://sigit.si/sigit/sigit/issues/11

`session/load` is a replay in ACP: the client renders the reopened thread from the `session/update` notifications the agent streams while the request is still in flight, and keeps nothing of its own. Our handler restored the saved history into the backend, which is what makes the model remember the conversation, and sent the client nothing. The model had the thread, the editor showed a blank page. Zed's own log confirms it, `load_session: restored 192 message(s)` with no updates behind it.

`history_replay_updates` now turns the saved snapshot into notifications, and `handle_load_session` sends them before restoring the history:

* user and assistant text replay as message chunks, with `<think>` blocks stripped the same way they are stripped live
* a tool call replays as one completed `tool_call` carrying its arguments and its result, instead of a call plus a loose result message
* `write_todos` replays as a plan, so a reopened thread shows the todo list rather than a raw tool call
* system messages are skipped, since they seeded the model and were never on screen

Fork still starts clean. It never had persistence to begin with, and that is worth a separate look.

## Testing

`tests/acp_session_load.rs` drives the real binary against a scripted endpoint: one prompt that talks and reads a file, then `session/load` on the same session id, asserting the user turn, both rounds of the reply and the completed tool call with its output come back. It fails on `development` and passes here. Four unit tests cover the snapshot to update mapping, including empty messages, block form content and the plan case.

Also checked by hand against a real 192 message session file from `~/.config/sigit/sessions`: 8 user chunks, 41 agent chunks, 83 tool calls and 7 plans replayed.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` are all green.

author: guilhermemarini

0.2.0 shipped with `py61850>=0.3.0.dev2` because 0.3.0 did not exist yet, and
PEP 440 sorts a `.devN` **before** its release — a plain `>=0.3.0` matched no
published version and would have made the wheel uninstallable.

[py61850 0.3.0](https://pypi.org/project/py61850/0.3.0/) is on PyPI now, so the
pin names it.

A specifier that names a pre-release also tells the resolver that pre-releases
are acceptable for that requirement, so leaving it would keep letting a future
`0.4.0.dev1` in on a fresh install.

body:
The Segmentation 13 and 14 tests compared assignments against external solver output, even though those assignments are feasible results rather than certified optima. Independently scoring both assignments shows TensorInference's candidates have higher log objectives by 31.5093806324 and 3.1385028268 respectively.

This restores all three cases and checks that the returned assignment reproduces the reported objective and meets the external feasible lower bound. It also adds an independent exhaustive oracle over small MMAP models. The oracle derives expected output variables directly from the query and evidence, verifies the model exposes that order, and brute-force enumerates assignment scores without using TensorInference contraction results. A better external score alone is not treated as proof of global optimality.

author: gonzalobenegas
body:
Add an opt-in coordinate-only workflow that projects each human anchor's central nucleotide through existing checksum-pinned chain files.
It emits 255-bp target windows using the shared center-1 acceptance contract, rejects ambiguous mappings explicitly, and accounts for every unmapped query.
The legacy HAL/MultiZ workflow and shared implementations are unchanged.

The reader checks chain direction, chromosome dictionaries, and input identities, then benchmarks one batched `liftOver` invocation per species.
It has no path to HAL staging, chain generation, sequence extraction, dataset publication, or training.
Full-chain contig aliases must be supplied explicitly from verified assembly metadata.

Validation:

- 236 locked project tests passed remotely; CI is green.
- Legacy dry-run: 79 jobs; additive chain-only dry-run: six jobs.
- Real synthetic workflow through Kent 482 and S3: two accepted strand-aware projections and one unmapped query.
- Saved-HAL comparison: 10,000/10,000 exact outcomes each for baboon, mouse, and elephant, with zero mapping or multiplicity discrepancies.
- liftOver including whole-chain loading: 23.89 / 38.42 / 35.44 seconds respectively.
- Independent review completed and findings addressed.

The biological gate is stratified sampled agreement, not genome-wide equivalence.
The table adapter still materializes one species at a time, and whole-workflow peak RSS reached 12.50 GiB on the mouse sample; all-grid memory optimization remains a follow-up.
Detailed evidence and artifact identities are recorded in #523.

Part of #523; supports the anchor recommendations in #517.

author: rhgrive3
body:
## Batch PR — owner area: managed formats (batch #4)

Four valid issues fixed across js/managed/shared + wasm probe.

## #5401 — ManagedTargetProfile id drops feature/options/policy
**Validity:** reproduced on main `058177e3b`: `createManagedTargetProfile({frontendId:'wasm', featureSet:['simd'], validationPolicy:'strict', options:{enableReferenceTypes:false}})` and the same with `featureSet:['threads'], validationPolicy:'permissive', options:{enableReferenceTypes:true}` produced the **identical** id `managed-profile:wasm:1:core-3.0` despite different `decodingOptionsHash`es.
**Fix:** js/managed/shared/identity.js — `createManagedTargetProfileId()` accepts the semantic tail (frontendSemanticVersion, normalized featureSet, runtimeVersionHint, validationPolicy, decodingOptionsHash); when any is defined the canonical id becomes `managed-profile:<front>:<fmt>:<spec>:<stableDigest(tail)>`. js/managed/shared/profile.js — `createManagedTargetProfile()` always passes the normalized tail. Deterministic: same configuration → same id; feature order normalized. Frontends' direct 3-arg calls (VM effects descriptive ids) keep the base schema.

## #5296 — validator accepts tampered/under-specified profiles
**Validity:** `validateManagedTargetProfile()` checked field types and id presence but never re-derived the id, so a profile with an id from a different configuration (or a stale descriptive id) validated `true`.
**Fix:** js/managed/shared/profile.js — the validator re-derives the canonical id from the profile's own semantic fields and fails with `managed-profile-identity-mismatch` on any mismatch. The #7311-era #5401-queued queued ... (tampered/stale ids and semantically altered profiles are rejected).

## #5294 — validation report id ignores profileId/status
**Validity:** two reports for `targetId:'method:m'` under different profiles with `valid`/`invalid` statuses both produced `id === 'val-rep:method:m'`.
**Fix:** js/managed/shared/validation.js — report id is now `val-rep:<targetId>:<profileId|->:<status>`; different profile/outcome are different validation facts and cannot alias. No production consumer pins the old single-denominator format (`validationReportId` is currently never populated).

## #5384 — wasm probe claims support for versions the parser rejects
**Validity:** `probeWasm(\0asm\x02...)` returned `supported:true, confidence:0.8` while `openManagedImage` threw `wasm-unsupported-version` — the public probe contradicted the actual open capability.
**Fix:** js/managed/wasm/parser-core.js — non-v1 versions probe `supported:false, reason:'unsupported-version'`; `parseWasm` maps that reason to the same `wasm-unsupported-version` code it already used, so probe and open agree fail-closed.

## Regression tests
- `tests/phase11/shared/issue-5401-5294-5384-identity-batch.test.mjs` (5 tests; all red on main, green here)
- Updated id pins in `tests/phase11/foundation/contracts.test.mjs` and `issue-4485-managed-profile-string-boundary.test.mjs` to the new canonical contract (readable triple + content digest). #4485's malformed-profile rejections remain green.

## Test commands run
- `node --test tests/phase11/shared/issue-5401-5294-5384-identity-batch.test.mjs` — 5/5
- `npm run phase11:test` — 100 pass / 4 fail; identical 4 pre-existing failures on clean main (cil-adversarial export, managed-frontends conformance, dex #3729/#1143 — documented in progress file)
- dex/jvm/cil/wasm pipelines + shared bridge + foundation #4391/#4484/#4485 — green
- `npm run lint` — 3111 files ok

Strictly within owner area: js/managed/shared/{identity,profile,validation}.js, js/managed/wasm/parser-core.js + foundation/shared tests. No generated files touched.

author: pramodathani
body:
The tenth and last adapter. All ten brokers now have one.

## The only broker an ordinary HTTP client cannot reach

The host serves `trade.wisdomcapital.in` under a certificate **issued for a different name**, so a client that checks the hostname refuses to connect before any request is made.

`VERIFY_CERTIFICATE_HOSTNAME` on the base class exists for this and nothing else, and this is the only broker of the ten that sets it false. What it turns off is the hostname check alone — **the certificate chain and its expiry are still verified.** Deliberately narrower than switching verification off, and the same trade `utilities/broker_login.py` and the portfolio adapter already make for this host.

This is its first use anywhere in the execution package, and both books answered over it.

## XTS is a fourth wire vocabulary

After Kite's, Dhan's and Noren's. Three conventions are its own.

**Every field of a modification is prefixed with `modified`** — and the product and order type are mandatory even when unchanged, so a modification restates the whole order. **Fourth broker of the ten** to need the resting-order state:

```
after qty->6      {'modifiedOrderQuantity': 6, 'modifiedLimitPrice': 14.0,  'modifiedProductType': 'CNC', ...}
after price->13.4 {'modifiedOrderQuantity': 6, 'modifiedLimitPrice': 13.4, 'modifiedProductType': 'CNC', ...}
```

**A cancellation carries its arguments in the query string**, not a body — the only one of the ten:

```
DELETE https://trade.wisdomcapital.in/interactive/orders
  params={'appOrderID': 1100000123, 'clientID': 'WD9620', 'orderUniqueIdentifier': 'tradingmachine'}
```

**The instrument is named by a number.** `exchangeInstrumentID` is an integer rather than text, so a non-numeric token is refused by `instrument_identifier` rather than by the broker. Exchange and market are joined into one word:

| segment | exchangeSegment | exchangeInstrumentID |
|---|---|---|
| nse_equities / bse_equities | `NSECM` / `BSECM` | 758898 / 531738 |
| nse_equity_futures, nse_equity_index_options | `NSEFO` | 61732 / 51266 |
| nse_currency_futures | `NSECD` | 1159 |
| mcx_commodity_futures | `MCXFO` | 584330 |

## ⚠️ This broker's instrument mapping is missing

Found while exercising the adapter, and it affects more than execution.

On **2026-09-08 `instruments.broker_mappings` holds rows for nine brokers and none for Wisdom Capital.** The raw table has no `download_date` of 2026-09-08 either — its most recent is 2026-09-07 with 209,598 rows. **So the download did not run for this broker that day**, rather than the mapping failing on it.

| broker | rows mapped on 2026-09-08 |
|---|---|
| stoxkart | 436,224 |
| dhan | 200,493 |
| kotak | 188,411 |
| shoonya | 162,439 |
| fyers | 159,520 |
| flattrade | 148,109 |
| groww | 135,343 |
| zerodha | 108,713 |
| indmoney | 103,167 |
| **wisdom_capital** | **0** |

The consequence here is total rather than partial: with no mapping there is no handle, so `instrument_routing` cannot name a single instrument at this broker and the router will never select it. **The adapter is correct and simply unreachable until a download runs.**

Recorded rather than worked around. The adapter was exercised against the 2026-09-07 mapping instead, which is what the checks above use.

## Verified

Both books answered live on 2026-09-09 over the relaxed transport:

```
{"type": "success", "code": "s-orders-0001", "description": "Success order book", "result": []}
```

Rows under `result`, refusal detected by `type`:

| input | `failure_reason` |
|---|---|
| the real success envelope | `None`, `parse_orders` → `[]` |
| `{"type":"error","code":"e-orders-0002","description":"Invalid instrument"}` | `e-orders-0002: Invalid instrument` |

Session key from the previous morning still worked after midnight — matching Shoonya, Groww, Fyers and IND Money.

## One inherited inconsistency, resolved deliberately

The sibling project sends **title-cased** order types on a modification and **uppercase** ones on a placement, in the same file. Only uppercase is used here: it is the form that project documents as the XTSConnect SDK's own constants, and a broker taking two spellings of one enumeration on two endpoints would need more evidence than one project's inconsistency.

## Not verified

Both books were empty, so no field name inside a row is confirmed. Nothing about placing, modifying or cancelling has been confirmed at this broker — and it cannot be, until its instrument download runs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: explosivebit
body:
## Summary

Smith's Agent index tells the orchestrator which agents to dispatch and what evidence each row must produce. A row could demand an EVIDENCE artifact from an agent labelled **B** while nothing verified the agent could physically create one. **That defect has already shipped once** — three B-labelled reviewers carried allowlists containing zero `forgeplan_*` tools (marketplace#236, EVID-231) — and a person reading files caught it, not CI. Since then the only guard was the author's memory. Closes NOTE-013 **DEFER-033**.

- **`scripts/ci/routing-profile-check.js`** — read-only, no `--write` mode. Per index row: resolves to exactly one agent file; frontmatter parses and carries `name`; the name matches the index; the profile label is understood; and the tool surface honours the letter — required tools reachable, forbidden tools not.
- **The rules were measured, not imagined.** The reachability matrix for all 26 indexed agents was built *first*; the invariants were written from it. Every non-dagger row already satisfies them, so the gate is green today and holds a regression rather than listing a backlog.
- **Dagger rows are excluded from the letter check, deliberately.** The index footnote declares the letter *advisory* for those. Enforcing a label the document itself calls advisory would manufacture findings against a recorded decision. They still get the structural checks.
- **An unrecognised label fails loudly** — a checker that silently skips what it does not understand reports success for work it never did.

## Verification

- ✅ **Self-test, 11 cases**: 6 must-fire (one per problem class), **2 must-refuse** so it cannot pass vacuously (an index with no rows; a renamed section), 2 must-NOT-fire, 1 parser cross-check.
- ✅ **A controlled pair carries the dagger logic**: the *same* broken agent fires under a plain row and does **not** fire under a dagger row. One difference, so the advisory skip is demonstrated rather than assumed.
- ✅ **The gate's own parser is verified, not trusted.** It carries a hand-written frontmatter reader to stay dependency-free — the one place it could go blind (mis-parse an allowlist into `null` and every reachability question answers "inherited, therefore yes" while the gate still prints OK). Diffed against a real YAML parser across all 26 agents: **identical**. During development that comparison once "passed" because *both* sides were empty; the self-test now treats empty-vs-empty as a **failure**, not a match.
- ✅ **Live mutation on the real tree, both declaration styles** — `guardian` loses its `activate` denial (inline denylist) → exit 1 naming the file; `pii-detector` loses `forgeplan_new` from its allowlist (**the DEFER-033 shape itself**) → exit 1. Both revert clean; gate green afterwards.
- ✅ **Two subtleties that would otherwise make the gate wrong**: an allowlist constrains *harder* than a denylist (anything unlisted is unreachable) and both forms are read; matching is on the **bare** tool name, because the `mcp__server__` prefix is runtime-specific (marketplace#212).
- ✅ Registered in **both** runners; `gate-parity-check` sees **16** gates in each.
- ✅ `./scripts/validate-all-plugins.sh` → ALL PASSED.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/ci/routing-profile-check.selftest.sh` — 11/11
- [x] Live mutation, denylist path (`guardian`) and allowlist path (`pii-detector`)
- [x] Parser cross-check vs PyYAML over all 26 indexed agents
- [x] `gate-parity-check` — both runners agree
- [x] `validate-all-plugins.sh` — ALL PASSED

## Scope note

**No plugin changed, so nothing new ships to users.** The catalog bump marks the repository release, not a plugin update. Only `scripts/ci/`, the two runners, `CLAUDE.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` are touched.

Refs: NOTE-013 DEFER-033, marketplace#236, EVID-231

body:
## Summary

Three changes to the **Variétés** tab, built on the repository reorganisation into `src/`, `assets/`, `scripts/` and `docs/`.

### 1. Filters by characteristics
The Variétés tab now combines the text search and the five plant-type pills with facet filters for:
- fruit colour, size and shape
- maturity / earliness
- leaf type (when documented)
- climate tolerances and declared resistances (chaleur/sécheresse, froid/saison courte, maladies)

An active-filter counter and a "Réinitialiser" button appear as soon as a filter is applied.

### 2. Truthful tolerance filters
Tolerances are derived only from explicit, positively-phrased claims, evaluated clause by clause. Negations ("aucune résistance… n'est garantie"), hedges, and unrelated words ("usage frais", "couleur chaleureuse") are excluded, so a variety is never promoted for a trait it does not actually declare. Each sheet now shows a "Caractéristiques retenues" summary — the exact values that drive the filters.

### 3. In-app sheet editing
