author: gd-0
body:
Adds an opt-in Linux io_uring backend for reliable UDP through `UdpConfig::io`. Both peers can choose their backend independently; the wire protocol is unchanged. The default remains syscall UDP, and TCP is unchanged.

The backend uses one ring per socket, multishot recvmsg with provided buffers, and pooled owned send buffers. Compatible runs retain GSO across mixed-peer batches, with datagram fallback when offload fails. Polling has explicit receive limits; thread handoff and teardown synchronously cancel kernel requests before releasing their buffers. Send slots remain individually boxed so borrowing one slot cannot invalidate kernel pointers into another. Default capacity reserves about 6 MiB per socket. Linux 6.0+ and permission to use io_uring are required; setup failures are reported through the existing socket-creation path.

The audit found and fixed two issues: send backpressure discarded the pending ACK flag, and ACK processing could replenish an intended bounded receive drain. ACKs now remain pending until accepted, and every receive pass is capped. Both UDP backends emit ACKs between receive batches, preventing slow callbacks from deferring them until the receive queue drains. Regression coverage verifies ACK retry after saturation, sustained duplex delivery with one send slot and one receive buffer, and sustained large-message delivery on both backends.

Five alternating measured loopback rounds at `afcad76` against main `e59fe83`, after discarded warmup runs. These measurements precede the subsequent plumbing and syscall ACK-scheduling changes and have not been rerun for the current head:

| Workload | Main | io_uring | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 2 KiB burst throughput | 442 MiB/s | 773 MiB/s | +74.9%; median latency 4.8 → 2.4 µs |
| 64 KiB broadcast throughput | 1,398 MiB/s | 7,461 MiB/s | 5.34×; p99 346 → 70 µs |
| 2 MiB burst throughput | 7,285 MiB/s | 7,315 MiB/s | +0.4%; 3.0% below the branch's syscall control |
| 2 MiB broadcast median latency | 1.33 ms | 3.23 ms | Regression; CPU cost also increases |

The broadcast gains include improved GSO grouping, so these measure the complete backend rather than io_uring alone. These are local loopback results; physical NIC/WAN performance and non-Linux builds remain unverified.

Validation: `just fmt`, `just clippy`, and `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` passed in hosted CI at `fd57087` with default parallelism (365 tests; four existing ignored doc tests). The ACK regression was reproduced before its fix. Coverage includes the shared UDP suite on both backends, mixed peers, loss/reconnect, DCache, sustained large messages, queue exhaustion, GSO fallback, GRO validation, IPv4/IPv6, buffer-ring tail wraparound, and thread movement.

Follow-up validation: `just fmt`, `just clippy`, and the full `flux-network` suite passed (116 tests, run serially after a parallel TCP test encountered `AddrInUse`). The newly shared sustained test reproduced syscall ACK starvation before the fix and passes for both backends afterward. An isolated Miri reproducer rejects the unboxed vector indexing pattern under Stacked Borrows and passes with boxed slots; this is not a full-backend Miri run.

Compatibility: adding the public `UdpConfig::io` field requires updates to exhaustive struct literals. Literals using struct update syntax keep compiling. Account for this source change in the next release; this PR does not bump the workspace version. Uses the workspace's existing io-uring dependency.


Follow-up syscall measurements (2026-09-09): main `e59fe83`, pre-ACK-fix `89b648c`, and current implementation `ab2d295`. Separate saved binaries, five measured rounds after one discarded round per size/revision, rotating revision order; no tests/builds ran concurrently. Ryzen 9 9950X, Linux 7.1.5, release/native, IPv4 loopback, the same pinned cores and requested 16 MiB socket buffers. `FLUX_BENCH_TRANSPORT=udp FLUX_BENCH_SCALE=16 FLUX_BENCH_SIZE=2k` or `64k`. Entries are medians of per-run statistics, not pooled percentiles.

| Syscall workload | Main MiB/s | Before MiB/s | Current MiB/s | Change vs before | Before → current p50 / p99 µs | Before → current CPU ns/B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| paced/2k | 20 | 20 | 20 | +0.0% | 4.7 / 5.5 → 4.3 / 5.5 | 95.477 → 95.498 |
| paced/64k | 625 | 625 | 625 | +0.0% | 9.1 / 10.6 → 8.6 / 10.0 | 2.977 → 2.976 |
| burst/2k | 443 | 445 | 434 | -2.5% | 4.8 / 5.8 → 4.4 / 5.0 | 2.382 → 2.367 |
| burst/64k | 7,002 | 6,933 | 7,104 | +2.5% | 9.0 / 11.8 → 8.4 / 11.0 | 0.201 → 0.194 |
| bcast/2k | 565 | 566 | 564 | -0.4% | 17.1 / 95.2 → 17.0 / 103.1 | 1.755 → 1.751 |
| bcast/64k | 1,412 | 1,406 | 1,378 | -2.0% | 211.3 / 343.7 → 210.5 / 344.0 | 0.758 → 0.711 |

The ACK fix has a measured throughput cost of 2.5% for 2 KiB bursts and 2.0% for 64 KiB broadcasts in this run; 64 KiB bursts improve 2.5%. Paced throughput is unchanged. These are syscall comparisons, not refreshed io_uring speedup claims. The older io_uring table above remains attributed to its measured revision.

Each receive batch now scans all peers owned by the driver, filtering by socket, and emits at most one pending ACK per matching peer. The scan is O(total driver peers) per batch; the broadcast benchmark covers eight peers, not hundreds.

Default-parallel local validation passes all 116 network tests. The prior CI failure was a sustained-message sender disconnect, not a deadline expiry. Constraining local socket buffers to 212,992 bytes reproduced that disconnect; restoring large buffers on the same two CPUs passed the unchanged test on both backends. CI now sets `rmem_max` and `wmem_max` to 16 MiB so Linux can honor the test's requested socket capacity. Message counts, deadlines, assertions, and default test parallelism are unchanged. Hosted CI at `fd57087` passes the full workspace suite with default parallelism: 365 passed, four existing ignored doc tests. Both shared sustained-message variants pass; lint and semver checks are green. An additional local run with CI compiler flags (`RUSTFLAGS=""`) and two CPUs also passes all 116 network tests with default parallelism.

author: soncoai
body:
Moves the site off GitHub Pages onto a Cloudflare Worker with static assets and
no entrypoint script — `wrangler.jsonc` declares `assets` and no `main`, so
Cloudflare serves the files directly and no JavaScript runs per request.

## What changed

| File | Does |
|---|---|
| `wrangler.jsonc` | Worker config; `sonco.ai` as a custom domain |
| `npm run dist` | Assembles `dist/` — an allow-list naming the six things that ship, so `src/`, `node_modules/` and this README can't leak onto the site |
| `404.html` | New; the Worker serves it for unmatched paths |
| `_headers` | nosniff, referrer-policy, frame-options; a year of immutable caching on the fonts |
| `CNAME` | Deleted — a GitHub Pages artifact |

Deploys run through Cloudflare Workers Builds, which watches this repo directly.
That is why there is no CI file here: a GitHub Actions workflow would race
Cloudflare on every push to `main`, and would need an API token that Connect to
Git does not.

## Verified

Run locally under `wrangler dev` rather than assumed:

- `/` returns 200 with the page intact — no console errors, Alpine and both fonts fine
- `/nope` returns a real 404 carrying the new page
- Fonts get `max-age=31536000, immutable`; CSS stays revalidating, which is right given the `?v=` cache-busting already in the markup
- `_headers` is itself unreachable (404), and the image with a space in its filename serves

## Two settings that are deliberately not in the config

Both are zone settings rather than Worker settings:

- **`www.sonco.ai`** — wants a Redirect Rule to the apex. Attaching it as a second custom domain would serve one page at two hostnames with no canonical to settle which wins.
- **`sonnco.com`** — the domain this site was on under Pages. Redirect it across if it should follow.

## Before this deploys

`sonco.ai` has to be a zone on the same Cloudflare account — a custom domain can
only attach to a zone Cloudflare already holds. GitHub Pages should also be
turned off under Settings → Pages so the old build stops answering.

Note the page copy still says "Sonnco" throughout, and the old CNAME was
`sonnco.com`. Only the hosting moved here; the naming is untouched.

## Problem

Users could enable the experimental supporter flow in a build that had no configured verification service. The app would still start store billing, then discard the resulting verification error and remain on “Confirming your support…” indefinitely.

## Why this fix

This fails closed at each client boundary: the flag is internal, Settings and deep links require a configured verification client, and the repository refuses to start billing without one. If an existing purchase proof still reaches the app while verification is unavailable, the Cubit now shows the existing verification-unavailable error in a non-busy state.

This does not determine the historical store-order state reported in #8935 or change the supporter service's entitlement rules. That investigation requires release configuration and store-console evidence, so this PR references rather than closes the issue.

author: splitbrain-bot
body:
Two boxes saying "still running" with every thread grey. Both were telling the truth about what they had been asked: a reading that found **nothing of ours** in the container counted as *busy*.

The reasoning was that a shape this cannot understand is not evidence of an empty box, and stopping a box with a two-hour build in it is the mistake with no repair. It cost more than it saved, because "nothing of ours" is the ordinary state of a running container: Boxes spawns the adapter as an exec and keeps none there between connections, so a box that is up and has never been opened — or that has outlived the orchestrator process that opened it — runs its entrypoint and nothing else. Every one of those

- said "still running" on its card, with no thread able to say what, and
- **was never reaped**, because the idle sweep asks this same question and took the same answer.

A stopped session was the same bug from the other side. `containerProcesses` returns early for a box that is not up and its comment says why — "answering that here rather than throwing keeps a stopped box from being read as one that could not be asked" — but it answered with an empty array, which is exactly what a box that could not be read looks like. That is `null` now: nothing there to ask is knowledge; a box that would not answer is silence; only the second is worth holding the last reading for.

**What makes an empty answer safe is the id.** Work only ever sits under an adapter or under an agent process; an agent is recognised by the conversation written on its command line, wherever it sits; and an agent that outlived its adapter is still an agent. So a box that has lost its adapter still reports what its conversations were running, under the conversation that was running it, and a box with neither has nothing Boxes ever started. The `unreadable` state goes with that, and stopping a session clears the reading at once rather than at the next poll.

The state that remains — work under an agent that names no conversation — still counts for the box and belongs to no thread, which is what a reader sees as a fault. It is reported once now, on the transition, with the commands it could not place. The log is the only place that reason can go, and this PR is what happens when it has nowhere.

554 orchestrator tests pass (dashboard untouched, 225 pass).

`src/domain/goal-observations.ts`：小型 TypeScript 型別、嚴格 runtime validation、pure state-in/state-out commands。成功樣貌與各題 observation 分開，slot 包含 run／goal revision／question version／context revision；null 不當 0。

全部已提交 Goal／Context revision 不可原地改；completed run 不能原地重開，paused/unresolved 需明示續做。歷史讀取解出原版本，與明確 active refs 比較時回傳 `needsReview` 和差異。

採用需 preview／confirm；取消不改領域資料。來源或目標任一 revision 過期均拒絕，包括來源文字改了又改回。已採用來源以快照保留，之後 source draft 改字不改舊 provenance。

`src/domain/legacy-observations.ts`：單一原型 Goal JSON 原文完整保留，附 needsReview／knownSourceId；不猜成三筆 confirmed answers、不自動匯入。

## 實際驗證
環境：Linux x86_64、Node 22.16.0、npm 10.9.2、TypeScript 5.8.3。**pure-domain，無 storage adapter**。

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| strict TypeScript `npm run typecheck` | PASS |

| 遠端／本機 11 個程式、測試與工具設定 blob／subtree 對照 | 一致，與本機測過的 bytes 相同 |
| 乾淨目錄 `npm ci --offline --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` | FAIL / ENOTCACHED，環境沒有 TypeScript registry cache |

測試用環境預裝的同版 compiler；lockfile 由 npm 按本機套件離線產生，尚無 registry resolved/integrity，**不宣稱已驗證乾淨依賴安裝或供應鏈**。合併前需在可連 registry 的乾淨環境補驗並補齊 metadata，不能刪必要檢查繞過。

[evidence 與 requirement-to-test 映射](https://github.com/world4jason/want-sort/blob/f549e252402e4df21bdcbfe508c240c834ff36c0/evidence/README.md) · [實際測試 log](https://github.com/world4jason/want-sort/blob/f549e252402e4df21bdcbfe508c240c834ff36c0/evidence/domain-check.log) · [接手／review 入口](https://github.com/world4jason/want-sort/blob/f549e252402e4df21bdcbfe508c240c834ff36c0/docs/development/DOMAIN_PILOT.md)

author: paul-hammant
body:
A transport-agnostic codec for the **Redis Serialization Protocol**, in the mould of `std.json` and `std.cbor`: it encodes/decodes over byte buffers and never touches a socket.

### RESP3-native, RESP2-compatible
RESP3 is a strict **superset** of RESP2, so this is one codec, not two protocols:
- **One decoder** reads the full RESP3 grammar — and therefore any RESP2 stream too.
- **One encoder** picks the dialect: `encode()` emits RESP3, `encode_resp2()` emits the RESP2 wire form of the same value (for the types whose form differs: null, boolean, double, big number, verbatim string, map, set).

RESP3 is opt-in per connection (`HELLO 3`), which is exactly why a client or server must still be able to speak RESP2 — hence the two encoder entry points over a shared value model.

### Resumable decoder
`parse_prefix()` distinguishes **incomplete** (needs more bytes: null value, `0` consumed, no error) from **malformed** (a protocol error: non-empty error string), so a socket reader can accumulate bytes and retry a partial frame rather than mis-framing it. `parse()` is the single-complete-value form (errors on trailing bytes).

### Memory model
Mirrors `std.cbor`: values are `malloc`-backed with owned `bytes` payloads and `std.list` children; `free_value()` reclaims the whole tree. Bulk strings are binary-safe. Text payloads are stored as bytes (not `heap.new` string fields, which leak).

### Testing
`std/resp/test_resp.ae` — 32 checks covering encode/decode round-trips for every type, the RESP2-vs-RESP3 dialect splits (null, bool, map), resumable partial frames, and malformed-frame errors. Valgrind-clean: **152 allocs / 152 frees, 0 errors**.

Gates: stdlib index (75 modules, export count matches), module-README example (compiles + output verified), `ae fmt` clean, `test-ae` harness PASS.

author: 1fanwang
body:
## Why

A maintainer who wraps an example in `<!-- docs-validate: hidden -->` is asking for that example to be type-checked. For three examples in this repository, it silently was not, and nothing reported a problem. The most visible one is the trusted host-bundled block in the plugin directories guide, which carries those markers for exactly that reason.

Closing a hidden block sets a pending skip so the visible copy that follows is not validated twice. A fence whose language has no validator, `rust` among them, was never recognized as a code block at all, so it never consumed that pending skip. The flag survived and the next validated block absorbed it instead.

Rust examples appear in nine feature guides, usually as the last language tab before the next section, so any example following one is exposed. Before this change those three blocks were extracted and discarded. After it they are checked like every other example, and a broken one would fail the build.

## What changed

Fences in languages that have no validator are now tracked and consume a pending skip when they close, so the directive can no longer reach past its intended target.

## Testing Done

Three previously discarded examples are now extracted and validated:

```
auth/authenticate.md:412
features/plugin-directories.md:248
features/session-limits.md:164
```

The two TypeScript ones pass locally. The C# one needs a .NET toolchain I do not have, so CI covers it.

<details><summary>Raw logs: extraction before and after</summary>

```
$ git checkout upstream/main -- scripts/docs-validation/extract.ts
$ (cd scripts/docs-validation && npm run extract) | grep -E "typescript|csharp|Total|Skipped"
```

author: wvink-dimagi
body:
## Product Description

When you open a plan created by CHC Mop-up's Phase 3 hand-off, the review page's left sidebar now shows a small "Mop-up plan (run #N)" badge under the plan number, so it's clear at a glance where the plan came from. Nothing else changes — this is purely a label; every other part of the review page (population sources, exclude/group/export, etc.) behaves exactly as it does today for any plan.

## Technical Summary

CHC Mop-up's hand-off (`connect_labs/mopup/core/handoff.py:create_plan_from_locked_run`) already tags every plan it creates with `run_meta={"source": "chc_mopup", "mopup_run_id": ..., ...}`, and `microplans.serialization.plan_to_json` already serializes `run_meta` into the plan JSON the review page fetches (`connect_labs/microplans/serialization.py:79`) — confirmed via direct reading, no backend change needed. This adds a `#mopup-mode-banner` element to `templates/microplans/review.html` and toggles its visibility/text in `review.js`'s single main render entrypoint (`function render(data, opts)`, called on every load/refresh) based on `data.run_meta.source === "chc_mopup"`.

Requested as part of the mop-up Phase 3 carry-forward redesign (companion PR: the mop-up-side hand-off changes) — an explicit, additive way to distinguish a mop-up-originated plan without touching any of microplans' own planning/grouping/export logic.

## Safety Assurance

### Safety story

Purely additive: one new (initially hidden) DOM element, one new `if` branch inside an existing render function that only toggles that element's class/text. No existing behavior is read, removed, or gated behind this check — a non-mop-up plan's `run_meta.source` is absent/falsy, so the badge simply stays hidden and every other code path is untouched.

### Automated test coverage

`connect_labs/microplans` suite (526 tests) passes unchanged — this is a JS/template-only change with no Python-testable surface.

### QA Plan

Manual: open a mop-up-created plan's review page and confirm the badge appears with the correct run id; open an ordinary (non-mop-up) plan and confirm nothing changed.

### Labels & Review

- [x] The set of people pinged as reviewers is appropriate for the level of risk of the change

author: carli2
body:
## Summary

Developed in `.worktrees/jit-fusion-potential`, based on current master `ce26bfb3d`. This is a new PR.

- Bound the common generated, fully typed inlining policy by `JITInlineCost` (48 units instead of 256), without an operator-name blacklist. Larger native calls remain inside the fused loop; storage type information is retained.
- Decide reducer compilation from remaining accepted work, not rows already processed. Full scans supply an observed-selectivity estimate; index/RecSet/other callers without a horizon only count their current batch. Small requests do not inherit their containing shard's population.
- Replace the unreachable >307,200-row probe floor with compile/probe amortization. Startup calibration measures both simple SUM and three-column arithmetic. The measured removable callback boundary also admits a trial when the complex timing difference is noisy. The actual callback must then repay compilation plus duplicate execution with a 2x reserve over the remaining rows.
- Only replay proven pure numeric reducers with scalar accumulators and numeric storage inputs. Defer that expression analysis until the row-cost test passes. Reject failed compilation once; no repeated attempts, scan caches, or new synchronization.
- Distinguish a measured flat compile-cost slope (`0`) from unavailable calibration (`-1`). A smaller complex emitter must not silently disable complex filters.
- Preserve concrete ProcJIT capture-tail values and lexical environments in both filter and mapreduce buffer kernels. The SQL end-to-end measurement exposed a previously hidden failure: a captured group key became a nil local, so an activated wide filter returned zero rows. Forced closure regression tests cover filters, nested captures and reducers.
- Keep buffers and specialization references scan-local and release them in `Close`. Delta execution is unchanged.

## Manual A/B (before PR creation)

Baseline: master `ce26bfb3d`; proposed: `41cc680b7`. Same patched Go JIT toolchain (`84fe25ee45468f5e3920c11c24e2bbb926fc3a72`), Ryzen 9 7900X3D, `GOMAXPROCS=1`, CPU affinity 10. Separate HTTP servers and private data directories; only `memcp-tests` fixtures are modified.

SQL fixture: `tests/performance/typed-filter-buffer.yaml`, 60,000 rows, including 16 bound integer columns and `SUM(a+b*c)`. Two warmups, nine alternating A/B batches of 20 requests per query; report the median batch mean. Drop only the matching test aggregate-cache table before each timed request (drop excluded from timing), so results measure scan/cache fill rather than a warm aggregate lookup. SQL parsing/planning, execution, allocation/GC and HTTP roundtrip are included. Result rows are checked on every request; EXPLAIN, IR, PHYSICAL and REORDER are recorded for both variants. `PartitionMaxDimensions=0` is set for both measurement instances.

Complete SQL results (milliseconds, negative is faster):

| SQL case | master | PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16-column comparison filter / COUNT | 46.932 | 37.660 | -19.8% |
| 16-column filter / three-column arithmetic SUM | 52.342 | 41.360 | -21.0% |
| Point arithmetic aggregate | 25.056 | 25.451 | +1.6% |
| 64-row range aggregate | 27.131 | 26.142 | -3.6% |
| Full 60k arithmetic aggregate | 36.288 | 36.483 | +0.5% |
| 1024-row range aggregate | 28.167 | 28.031 | -0.5% |
| 8192-row range aggregate | 28.072 | 28.800 | +2.6% |
| Residual filter / COUNT and SUM | 40.948 | 40.863 | -0.2% |
| Empty filtered aggregate | 31.308 | 31.159 | -0.5% |

All nine queries returned the expected rows throughout this run. The wide-filter improvements are visible end-to-end; the standalone SUM gain is not established in this loaded-host SQL run. Earlier exploration results are not substituted for final-branch measurements. Host load is variable, so small differences should not be interpreted as established speedups.

### Scan-level confirmation

Matched benchmark instrumentation on both sides, including the `fused/op` counter. Baseline uses the same benchmark functions/fixtures but omits the new remaining-row hint assignment. A/B/B/A order, two samples of 500ms per process: four samples per variant. Medians in microseconds, including scan-local compilation, gather/decoder work and teardown (fixture construction and startup calibration excluded):

| Case | master | PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `acc += a+b*c`, 64 candidates, automatic selection | 5.928 | 5.864 | -1.1% |
| `acc += a+b*c`, 60k candidates, automatic selection | 1620.967 | 1264.594 | -22.0% |
| Arithmetic filter, 60k, typed buffer kernel | 2144.613 | 1617.793 | -24.6% |
| Unchanged 16-column comparison kernel, 60k, typed buffer | 6020.337 | 6131.010 | +1.8% |

Both variants compile **zero** specialized kernels for the 64-row reducer. The small difference there is not evidence of a speedup. An earlier large microbenchmark discrepancy disappeared when the instrumentation was made identical; those unmatched numbers are not used here. Earlier SQL repeats put the 64-row end-to-end difference at +12.3% and +5.7%; the final complete run is -3.6%. That variability must not be attributed to a fusion that is not selected.

### Complete 0–60k investigation grid

Same fixtures and instrumentation, A/B/B/A with one 100ms sample per process (two samples per variant). This broader grid is exploratory; the selected cases above have longer confirmation samples. All outputs are checked. Expression reducer medians in microseconds:

| Candidates | master automatic | PR automatic | PR forced fusion |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 0.641 | 0.652 | 0.653 |
| 1 | 3.886 | 3.599 | 20.210 |
| 64 | 6.133 | 6.064 | 22.767 |
| 1024 | 35.409 | 33.330 | 47.248 |
| 8192 | 239.923 | 238.602 | 189.930 |
| 60000 | 1616.569 | 1240.399 | 1212.454 |

The zero-row forced case does not compile: no batch is executed. At 8192 rows forced fusion wins in this fixture, but the automatic policy conservatively keeps the direct loop because compilation **plus the extra replay probe** has to amortize. This is a documented remaining opportunity, not a claim of an exact universal crossover.

Other 60k automatic reducers from the same grid:

| Shape | master µs | PR µs | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| COUNT | 500.676 | 433.678 | -13.4% |
| SUM | 558.623 | 495.257 | -11.3% |
| `acc += a*3` | 1210.207 | 948.947 | -21.6% |
| `acc += a*b` | 1480.723 | 1044.135 | -29.5% |

Final-branch filter alternatives, 60k rows, milliseconds including per-scan compilation:

| Filter | Lambda calls | Dynamic buffer | Half-known types | Typed buffer | Direct storage fusion |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Simple comparison | 1.106 | 0.726 | 0.466 | 0.467 | 0.515 |
| `a+b*c` comparison | 2.250 | 1.682 | 1.711 | 1.577 | 1.696 |
| 16 bound columns | 13.428 | 11.074 | 8.600 | 6.256 | 7.978 |

The half-known variant intentionally erases every second column's type fact. Direct storage fusion inlines the getters into the filter loop; it is not lazily decoding columns along short-circuit branches. It does not beat typed buffers in this set, so this PR does not add a blanket full-fusion switch. The grid covers five reducer shapes, three filter shapes and 0/1/64/1024/8192/60000 candidates. The SQL table separately covers actual point/range access; a short sequential ID list alone is not presented as an indexed SQL query.

## Validation and limits

- JIT Go tests: `go test ./scm ./storage` passed after the capture fix.
- Targeted SQL/performance suite: 13/13 passed, including full arithmetic, 1/64/1024/8192-row candidate cases, empty output, main+delta and invalid binding.
- Regression tests cover remaining-row decisions, no compilation for 64 candidates in a 60k shard, scalar-only replay, flat/unavailable calibration, closure capture preservation, and scan-local teardown.
- Full integration suite was delegated to CI as requested. **All nine checks are green**, including Go, JIT Go, SQL, JIT SQL (with dump/restore), performance A/B, packaging, S3/recovery and both policy check

body:
Repeated native completion records and `.msp-view` session copies currently inflate Muse token and prompt totals. This deduplicates valid completions by record ID across session files and retained-frame children, and excludes `.msp-view*` directories inside the sessions tree.

Records without a usable ID remain countable, and metadata or malformed usage cannot claim an ID before a valid completion. The scan-cache version is bumped so previously inflated totals are rescanned. Existing opencode, subscription, and PAYG behavior is preserved.

This targets `add-muse-usage-collector` for inclusion in omacom/omarchy#10610, following our collaboration discussion. No revert of the subscription-window commit is needed. Hiding cached limits after a failed probe can be reviewed separately.

Validation:

- New deduplication regression test fails before the fix and passes afterward; covers plain records, retained frames, copied sessions, view directories, missing/malformed IDs, and old scan caches.
- Existing Muse scanner and limits suites pass.
- `git diff --check` passes. Ran `./test/all` with the desktop environment variables unset: CLI passes; the shell suite has the same five failures previously reproduced on an untouched upstream snapshot. `config-test.sh`, `snapper-test.sh`, and `unowned-system-paths-test.sh` need a missing sibling `omarchy-pkgs` checkout; `launch-about-test.sh` fails its roomy-window animation assertion; `locate-test.sh` tries to decode generated Python bytecode as UTF-8.

body:
### Motivation

- Restaurar el motor v7 completo en el repositorio para poder instrumentarlo y aplicar las correcciones de integridad sin perder la fuente original. 
- Evitar pérdida silenciosa de energía al empalmar reportes/RIOS que colisionan por la misma llave temporal (ej. cambio de hora / DST). 
- Hacer trazabilidad y auditoría de las decisiones de cruce RIO para detectar discrepancias entre la fuente que fija la tarifa y la que fija los filtros. 
- Proveer utilidades y tests minimalistas para validar los casos de integridad descritos en la spec.

### Description

- Se restauró y reemplazó íntegramente `src/sc_pd_motor_v7.py` con la versión v7 proporcionada y se añadió la entrada documental `[BUG 8]` en el encabezado respecto al filtro de grupos sin generación. 
- Se agregó `src/fase1_integridad.py` con utilidades reutilizables: `empalmar_reportes`, `deduplicar_rio_priorizando_motivo`, `calcular_ciclos`, `costos_clasicos` y `marcar_sin_tarifa_rio`, y se integraron estas funciones en el flujo principal del motor. 
- Empalme seguro de reportes: los duplicados reales se deduplican y las colisiones en la misma llave con `GENERACION` distinta se agregan (se suma `GENERACION`), registrando ambos casos en `_audit_log` para exportar a la hoja `Auditoria_Pasos`.

author: rudicus
body:
Hey Dave -  Hope all is well. Been using subspace regularly and love it. I ran into an issue with backpressure + multiple reliable subscribers. I was getting drops when one of the reliable subscribers read it, and the other one wasnt able to. Pardon the Claude PR, but this fixes it for me and lets me get 100% reliable playback with back pressure +multiple subscribers. 

## The bug

A reliable channel loses messages for its slower reliable subscribers the moment it has more than one subscriber:

- A reliable subscriber only holds a slot reference **while it is reading a message** — between reads it holds nothing.
- `kMessageSeenByReliable` is set by the **first** reliable subscriber to read a slot.
- So with two reliable subscribers, the faster one marks a slot seen, and the slower one's unread backlog carries zero references whenever it sits between messages. `FindFreeSlotReliable` walks past the seen flag, finds zero refs, and reclaims the slot — the slower reliable subscriber silently loses that message (no drop counter fires; the loss is invisible on both ends).

We measured this in production (an autonomy stack replaying sensor data through reliable channels at 64×): a ~4.2k msg/s reliable channel lost 0.05–0.14% of messages whenever it had a second subscriber — whether that second subscriber was reliable or not — and was exactly lossless (1,032,252 / 1,032,252) with a single subscriber. #104's `kMessageSeenByReliable` fixes the unreliable-co-subscriber case but not the reliable–reliable one.

## The fix

The per-subscriber available-slot bitsets already record exactly the needed state — "this slot has not yet been delivered to subscriber X" — they were just never consulted at reclaim time (and shared memory didn't record which subscriber ids are reliable):

- `ChannelControlBlock` gains a `reliable_subscribers` bitset, maintained beside `subscribers`: registration records reliability **before** the subscriber becomes visible to publishers; server-side cleanup clears it so a dead subscriber can't gate publishers forever; placement-initialized at channel creation (like `subscribers`, since `AtomicBitSet` carries a runtime `num_bits_`).
- `FindFreeSlotReliable` stops at the first slot still pending in any reliable subscriber's available-slots bitset. **Activation messages are exempt** — subscribers skip them without claiming, so their delivery bits can remain set forever, and reclaiming them loses no data. `kReadNewest` skips remain deliberate skips (they clear the pending bits). The check only runs on the ring-full slow path, so nothing is added to the publish fast path.
- `kChannelControlBlockVersion` → 6 for the layout change.

## Tests

- `ReliableChannelIsLosslessForEveryReliableSubscriber` — deterministic, single-threaded: fills the ring past a tight-reading reliable subscriber while a second reliable subscriber reads nothing; asserts the publisher backpressures (`GetMessageBuffer` returns null) instead of handing out the slow subscriber's backlog, that every message then arrives in order, and that the publisher resumes once both have caught up.
- `ReliablePublisherUnblocksWhenLaggingSubscriberUnsubscribes` — a lagging reliable subscriber gates the publisher; its departure releases the gate.

Both **fail on unpatched main** and pass with the fix; the full `//client:client_test`, `//common:common_test`, and `//server:server_test` suites pass with the fix (including `ReliablePublisherDoesNotBlockOnUnreliableSubscriber` and the other reliable-path tests).

We're carrying this as a patch against 3.0.3 in our tree in the meantime — happy to adjust whatever you'd like on naming, the version bump, or test placement.

author: santiagodepolonia
body:
Seeds workflows and guardrails into the demo dataset, attaches them to the generated traffic, and roughly doubles the request volume.

## Demo data

- **Volume**: defaults go from 850/1600 to 2000/3800 requests per day (~165k requests over the rolling 90 days, ~2.2x). Seeding takes ~8s; the SQLite file is ~575 MB. `DEMO_AVG_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` / `DEMO_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_DAY` still tune it.
- **Guardrails**: seven instances covering every built-in plugin type (`string_replace` x2, `system_prompt`, `header_edit`, `llm_judge` x2, `llm_based_altering`). Configs are written exactly as each plugin parses them — the plugins reject unknown keys, so they double as worked examples. The two model-backed instances fail open with timeouts, so a demo gateway without those provider keys keeps serving.
- **Workflows**: seven versions — a global baseline plus its superseded predecessor (version history), three user-path scopes, one provider scope, and one with guardrails deliberately off for contrast. `workflow_hash` is the real SHA-256 of the canonical payload.
- **Traffic**: every request resolves a `workflow_version_id` by replicating the gateway's most-specific-scope match, carries the matching `workflow_features`, and records `request_revisions` in the real `pluginDecisionDetail` shape, in each workflow's own step order, with a byte chain where each step starts from the previous step's output.

## Realism fixes

- Guardrail-blocked (403/400 `guardrail_blocked`) and budget-exceeded (429 `budget_exceeded`) requests are audited with no usage row.
- Real error types (`rate_limit_error`, `invalid_request_error`) replace the invented `rate_limit_exceeded`.
- `data.failover.target_model` on failover rows; per-path `auth_key_id` with `api_key`; varied client IPs; a `stream` column that matches the request body.
- ~18% of conversational traffic requests a virtual model with `alias_used=1`, the alias always drawn from a pool that contains the resolved provider.
- Prompt guardrails run before the cache lookup and the budget check, so cached requests carry their guardrail revisions and latency while blocked and budget-stopped requests are never cache hits.

## Behavior change

`make demo` now sets `GUARDRAILS_ENABLED=true` so the seeded guardrails and workflows are live rather than capped off at runtime, and raises `LOGGING_RETENTION_DAYS`/`USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` to `DEMO_DAYS`. The latter is a pre-existing bug: with the 30-day default, the first startup sweep deleted 108,309 of the seeded audit rows — two thirds of the dataset.

## Verification

- All six workflow payloads round-trip byte-identically through `workflows.Payload` marshaling and produce the stored hashes.
- Booted the gateway against the seeded database with `GUARDRAILS_ENABLED=true`: all 7 guardrails load and all 6 active workflows compile their chains, which validates every guardrail ref and config end to end.
- Spot queries confirm no cached-but-failed requests, no blocked requests with usage rows, and no provider attempts on cache hits.

- **New Features**
  - Demo startup now enables guardrails and configures logging and usage retention, with a default 90-day period.

  - Demo traffic better reflects blocked requests, provider errors, rate limits, budget limits, audit history, and request revisions.
  - Added controls for guardrail redaction frequency and increased default daily demo traffic volumes.
  - Demo data now includes richer workflow, request, error, failover, and attempt-tracking details for more representative activity.

author: santig005
body:
## What changed and why

First follow-up out of the T-67 UI audit — **F5, "no visible focus indicator"**.
Tabbing through the app showed nothing: the focused element computed to
`outline: solid 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` — a real outline, fully transparent — with
no ring shadow behind it, on the university selector, the category chips, the
sort control and the cards.

The cause was ours, not daisyUI's: `public/css/main.css` line 6, where the
project's `.btn` override ended in `focus-visible:outline-none`, plus `.input`'s
`focus-within:outline-0`. Between them they erased daisyUI's stock focus outline
on every button and field in the app, and nothing replaced either.

Both overrides are gone, and one token-based ring
(`outline: 2px solid var(--fallback-bc, oklch(var(--bc) / 1))` at a 2px offset)
replaces them, repeated for `.btn`/`.input`/`.select`/`.textarea`/`.checkbox`/
`.toggle` so it outranks daisyUI's equally-specific component focus styles.
`--bc` (base-content) means the ring follows T-73's palette into dark mode
instead of hardcoding a color, and the offset keeps it on the page background
rather than drawing `currentColor` white-on-orange inside a filled button.
`:focus-visible` means a mouse click still draws nothing.

Five per-element overrides went with it — the university selector button and its
info button (`UniGraphicSelector.jsx`), the PQRS type `select` (whose
`focus:ring-blue-500` was also an off-palette hardcoded color), and the OTP boxes
in `ForgotPassword.jsx` and `SignUpForm.jsx` — because a `focus:outline-none`
utility on the element outranks a global rule, and leaving them would have meant
exactly the controls the audit named were still ringless.

**Worth knowing for the next token-based rule:** daisyUI 4.12 emits its theme
variables in **oklch**, not hsl. The first version of this used `hsl(var(--bc))`,
which parses fine but computes to an invalid color — that drops the whole
shorthand and leaves `outline-style: none`. The tests caught it; reading the CSS
would not have.

## What was verified

`npm run verify` — all green:

```
  ok   lint (4.0s)
  ok   deadcode (4.3s)
  ok   typecheck (5.2s)
  ok   test (18.9s)
  ok   build (41.7s)
```

`npm run test:e2e` — 19 passed, including three new ones in
`tests/e2e/keyboard-nav.spec.js` that read the computed outline off the focused
control (reached by a real `Tab`, so the browser applies `:focus-visible` the way
it would for a visitor) and assert it is not `none`, not a hairline, and not
`rgba(..., 0)`. The third one forces dark via `localStorage.theme` and checks the
ring survives the theme change.

Screenshots are regenerated by those tests, clipped to a padded box around the
focused element — an element-only shot clips the ring, which is drawn 2px
*outside* the box:
`test-results/09-focus-ring-boton.png` (primary button, light),
`10-focus-ring-campo.png` (field, light), `11-focus-ring-dark.png` (field, dark).

## Risks

- **CSS-only blast radius, but it is global.** Any keyboard-focused element in
  the app now draws a ring. That is the point, but it is a site-wide visual
  change and worth a click-through. Mouse users see no difference.
- **The e2e suite is flaky, independently of this change.** Across five runs on
  this branch, three were fully green and two had a single failure each — a
  different test each time, `dark-mode` with `net::ERR_TIMED_OUT` on the first
  `goto`, and `scroll-infinito` with the second page already loaded before the
  scroll. Neither symptom can be caused by an outline. `agent/develop` ran green
  (16/16) as a control. Not filed as a task here; flagging it because a red CI on
  a re-run is likely to be this and not the change.

## Left pending

Scoped out deliberately, still open in `docs/audits/t-67/findings.md`:

- **F6** — the first two tab stops are invisible drawer-toggle checkboxes. The
  ring does not make them visible, and fixing it means deciding what the
  hamburger should be (it is a CSS-checkbox drawer today). Its own task.
- **F7 / F8** — accessible names on icon-only controls, and real `<label for>` on
  the forms. The audit groups them with F5 as one "big Lighthouse move"; they
  touch many more files, so they are separate.
- **F19** is visible in the dark screenshot: the auth inputs keep a hardcoded
  light `#f0f5fa`. Untouched here.

`ROADMAP.md` gets the T-86 entry marked done in this same PR, and the audit's
`findings.md` / `README.md` now point F5 at it.

author: sbogomolov
body:
A packet socket on a WireGuard or tun device hands over bare IP packets: no link header, no MACs. The AF_PACKET backend framed every interface as Ethernet, so on such a link the kernel filter dropped nearly everything, what got through failed to parse, and an injected frame went out with an Ethernet header the tunnel could not read. FreeBSD was already fine through `DLT_NULL`.

The hardware type (`SIOCGIFHWADDR`) now picks the framing at open and rebind: Ethernet and loopback as Ethernet, `ARPHRD_NONE` as raw IP with its own kernel filter, parser arm and builders, anything else refused at startup. Sends stay a plain `send`: since Linux 5.8 the kernel derives a header-less link's protocol from the IP version (`ip_tunnel_header_ops` on wireguard and tun), so raw IP links need that kernel or later. `sendto` with the protocol in the address was tried and dropped: it only buys 5.6 and 5.7, at the cost of a cached ifindex.

Testing: parser round trips for both families, filter composition, and two root-gated live tests that attach a tun device and push an IPv4 and an IPv6 datagram through it in each direction, byte for byte. Sabotaging the raw-IP classifier fails the receive test. `docker_test.sh` now passes `/dev/net/tun` into the container so they run there; the emulated CI lanes skip them without root. Suite green on macOS and Linux, clippy clean on both FreeBSD targets.

author: scarfsail
body:
Closes #234. Phase P5 of #229, the last phase.

The strips now carry their colour and shadow statically and the keyframes move only `transform` and `opacity`, so the animation is composited instead of repainting the arrow on every frame. It is paused whenever the element is outside the viewport or the document is hidden, through a host attribute rather than reactive state, so pausing costs no render; the listener and the IntersectionObserver are removed on disconnect.

Measured with a real Chromium trace (CDP `Tracing` over `devtools.timeline`, three arrow rows with representative flows, 5 seconds per phase, same fixture before and after). Visible: `Paint` 18181 → 0, `RasterTask` 17880 → 0, `UpdateLayoutTree` 301 → 10. Offscreen: 18300 paints → 0. Hidden: 18361 paints and 18032 raster tasks → 0. These are trace event counts, not a sampled CPU profile and not a real-dashboard number; no live HA measurement was possible here. The "resumed" phase reads zero main-thread events either way — a composited animation looks like a paused one from the main thread — so resumption is pinned by the specs reading `Animation.playState` instead. Before/after screenshots of the arrows mid-animation are indistinguishable.

Code review of the phase found three issues, fixed in the second commit: the card handed the arrows a freshly spread array on every render (the documented rendering-discipline violation, and the remaining main-thread cost in the component this phase set out to make cheap — the arrows now take `historyRevision`, which is the rate `powerValue` actually moves at), `_onScreen` survived a disconnect so a remounted element could paint a frozen frame, and the observer had no `rootMargin` so resuming happened a frame late. Two regressions added, both verified to fail without the fix.

`npm run build` and the full Playwright suite pass (644 tests).

## What & why

The diagnosis skill advertised a crash-diagnosis dependency that the toolkit does not bundle. Its description and early scope check now hand off local segfaults and core dumps only when `diagnose-crash` is available. Otherwise, diagnosis stops with an unsupported-case result and no substitute procedure.

Keep crash diagnosis optional rather than add another diagnostic workflow. Project-code panics, stack traces, and exceptions without a local segfault or core dump remain in `diagnose`.

- Available optional skill: both cases requested `diagnose-crash` explicitly.

author: uwefalz
body:
## Was

Das fehlende Verdikt oberhalb von ~40 Variablen (Befund aus #23): BFGS von der Einheitsmatrix braucht hundert Iterationen, um die Krümmung eines 46-Variablen-Fits zu lernen, und erreicht in 200 keines, obwohl der Fit nach 90 steht. Für ein Kleinste-Quadrate-Ziel ist die Krümmung JᵀJ und an jedem Punkt bekannt.

- **`hessian: "gauss-newton"`** am Alignment-Löser (Standard bleibt `"bfgs"`): für das Punkteziel geht JᵀJ der Residuen an den Optimierer; `variableScaling` skaliert es mit beiden Indizes.
- **Strukturierte Sekante** in `solveSQP` (`hessian: "provided"`): die bereitgestellte Hesse ist nur die Zielkrümmung; der Anteil der Nebenbedingungen wird daneben per BFGS auf den multiplikatorgewichteten Gradientendifferenzen der Nebenbedingungen geschätzt (Dennis–Gay–Welsch), ab `structuredStart`·I, und beide werden addiert. Reines Gauss-Newton nahm das Ziel in einem Fünftel der Iterationen herunter und konnte dann die Endpose nicht schließen.
- **Verdikt-Guard**: `infeasible_subproblem` verlangt eine Verletzung über der Toleranz — bei h = 1e-12 erfüllt jedes δ die relaxierten Zeilen, und das Verdikt feuerte an einem zulässigen Punkt.
- **Relative Zulässigkeitstoleranz** (offener Punkt seit #17): jeder Zulässigkeitstest, das Verdikt und das Ziel der Wiederherstellung nutzen `1e-9 · max(1, ‖x‖)`, wie der Schritt-Test schon. Auf 20 km bleibt die Endpose unter jeder Hesse bei 1e-5 stehen — Residuum (Produktionsgeometrie) und Jacobi (Momentenkette) weichen über diese Länge so weit voneinander ab. 1e-5 dort, 1e-7 auf einer 100-m-Weiche.
- Korpus-Runner: `--hessian`, `--restoration`, `--structuredStart`.

## Messung

`structuredStart` auf Korpus 0–161, Punkteziel, Verdikte gegen BFGS 155 / mittlere Iterationen gegen 23:

| B₀ | Verdikte | Ø Iterationen | 5500R074-082 (41 El., BFGS: kein Verdikt in 200) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-1 | 150 | 15 | max_it |
| 1e-2 | 146 | 11 | max_it |
| 1e-3 | 151 | 11 | stationary @172 |
| **1e-4** | **155** | **9,5** | **stationary @47, 11 s** |
| 1e-5 | 153 | 8,8 | max_it |
| 1e-6 | 153 | 7,6 | max_it |

Voreinstellung 1e-4. Damit Korpus Punkte: 155 = 155 Verdikte (+3/−3, verloren sind drei Zwergdateien mit 6 Punkten gegen 11 Unbekannte), `converged` 79 → 96, Ø Iterationen 23 → 9,5.

Relative Toleranz, BFGS: Länge 149 → 151 Verdikte, Punkte 155 unverändert.

Riesen mit `eager` + Gauss-Newton (BFGS-Werte aus #23):

| Datei | n / frei / Punkte | `eager` + BFGS | `eager` + Gauss-Newton |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3250_4-11_S | 64 / 82 / 144 | max_it, rms 0,123, 371 s | max_it, rms 0,119, Endpose 1e-6, 200 s |
| 5904072S | 71 / 94 / 213 | max_it, rms 0,148, 604 s | max_it, rms 0,125, Endpose 3e-6, 222 s |

Bessere Fits in der halben Zeit, weiter ohne Verdikt: die Endpose liegt jetzt innerhalb der relativen Toleranz, der KKT-Rest nicht — f fällt in 120 vollen Schritten von 1,70 auf 1,65, ein flaches Tal aus schlecht beobachtbaren Elementlängen, das auch JᵀJ nicht auflöst.

## Was bleibt

- Gauss-Newton ist Option, nicht Standard: auf drei unterbestimmten Zwergdateien verliert es das Verdikt, das BFGS hat. Ein Umschalten nach Variablenzahl wäre möglich, ist aber eine Regel mehr; hier nicht gebaut.
- QP-Kosten ab ~80 Variablen (Active-Set, Kappe 200) unverändert.
- Längenziel auf 40+ Elementen unverändert.

Tests axtran2 141/141.

body:
## Summary
This PR extends the file preview pane with syntax highlighting support for three additional languages: KDL (a document language), Just (a command runner), and Mojo (a Python superset). It also improves match highlighting in previews by distinguishing between exact and fuzzy matches, and adds support for extension aliases (e.g., `.sbatch` → `.sh`).

## Key Changes

- **New syntax definitions**: Added hand-written `.sublime-syntax` YAML definitions for KDL, Just, and Mojo languages in new modules (`kdl_syntax.rs`, `just_syntax.rs`, `mojo_syntax.rs`). These cover language-specific keywords, string interpolation, comments, and numeric literals.

- **Custom syntax set builder**: Introduced `build_syntax_set()` function that extends the base `two-face` syntax set with the three new languages, with graceful fallback to plain text if any grammar fails to parse.

- **Improved syntax resolution**: Added `resolve_syntax()` function that resolves file syntax by trying (in order): full filename, extension, extension aliases, and plain text fallback. This enables matching extensionless files like `justfile` and `Makefile` by name.

- **Extension aliases**: Added `EXTENSION_ALIASES` constant to map file extensions to other syntaxes (e.g., `.sbatch` files are highlighted as bash scripts).

- **Enhanced match highlighting**: 
  - Split `apply_match_highlight()` to accept all matches at once and track the currently focused match
  - Added `is_exact_match()` to distinguish contiguous matches from fuzzy (scattered-character) matches
  - Introduced `exact_match_span_style()` theme function for visually distinct highlighting of exact vs. fuzzy matches
  - Added underline styling for the currently focused match line

- **Syntax set variant fix**: Changed from `extra_newlines()` to `extra_no_newlines()` throughout to prevent context leakage when parsing lines without their terminators.

- **Match scoring**: Added `fuzzy_score` field to `ContentMatch` and implemented `top_score()` function to rank files by their best match quality first, improving result ordering.

## Implementation Details

- The hand-written syntax definitions use Sublime Text's `.sublime-syntax` YAML format, which syntect can parse directly
- KDL and Mojo definitions handle both v1 and v2 syntax variants where applicable
- Just definition focuses on recipe headers and interpolation while leaving recipe bodies as plain shell text
- All new syntax modules are included in `main.rs` and integrated into the app's initialization
- Comprehensive test coverage added for each new language's syntax registration and tokenization

Refresh an expired local-currency quote before checkout submits an order. Preserve the reviewed currency during refresh and require a new buyer click, even when the replacement total is unchanged. body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the post-deploy acceptance failure after #156 merged.

The mobile acceptance run reached the Users & Access view while no workspace was loaded. The screenshot shows the application in its valid `TEST APP · NO WORKSPACE LOADED` state, and `app-users-admin.js` correctly renders `Open a workspace to view or manage Users.` in that condition.

The acceptance step was too narrow in two ways:

- it treated the presence of the empty `#usersContent` host as readiness, even though Users administration is dynamically loaded and can render slightly later on mobile;
- it did not recognise the application's valid no-workspace Users state.

This change makes the feature-specific acceptance step wait for one complete valid Users & Access state:

- a fully decorated users table, including the dynamically-added `Person` column; or
- an expected bootstrap/no-workspace state.

It does not weaken the table contract: when a table is rendered, all identity, access, status and Person headings are still required.

No application behaviour is changed; this fixes acceptance readiness and aligns the test with the application's existing no-workspace behaviour.

## What changed
Nine OpenRouter request-extension unit tests become four broader contracts: complete request decoration, timestamp boundaries, rate-limit source precedence, and malformed metadata handling. Production code is unchanged.

Five tests exercised plugin serialization without checking that the request decorator actually inserted the plugins. Rate-limit examples covered only a few happy paths and assumed execution within one second.

Mutation evidence: removing plugin insertion still passes all nine original unit tests; the replacement complete-request test fails on the missing plugins. The mutation was reverted.

The replacements cover six plugin configurations while preserving input/client tools, seconds and milliseconds including fractional rounding and u64 boundaries, header/body precedence and case handling, existing retry/token budgets, and absent/malformed metadata. Every original declaration has an explicit ledger replacement and rationale.

Validation: 17 crate unit tests, 13 HTTP integration tests, one doctest, 11 ledger self-tests, ledger consistency, and `just pre-push` pass. Local HTTP tests exercise actual request decoration; no live credentials are needed for this test-only change.

## Risk
Low. Tests and review records only; production code is byte-identical.

## Security
No security-relevant code changes. Tests strengthen the boundary for external rate-limit metadata and preserve private reasoning and client-tool request fields.

The remaining OpenRouter driver/profile tests and repository-wide individual review continue separately; this completes the request-extension unit module.

author: jdealtia-sys
body:
`renderPdf` has failed **100% of the time at `stage: launch`** since the
`@sparticuz/chromium` 148 → 149 bump — and nothing alerted for the entire
window.

22 entries in the 30-day log window, **every one a failure**, not a single
`[renderPdf] ok` line. Warranty, estimate, invoice, contract, change order,
receipt, inspection and photo report all fell back to the client-side
`html2canvas` path, so customers kept receiving *a* document and nothing ever
looked broken from the outside.

## Root cause — a packaging change, not a code change

`@sparticuz/chromium` **149 dropped its CommonJS build**. Its `package.json` is
`"type":"module"` with a single `"default"` export condition, so `require()` on
the `nodejs22` runtime takes the `require(esm)` path and returns the ES module
**namespace** — `{ __esModule, default, inflate, setupLambdaEnvironment }` —
rather than the module. The API is a class on `.default`, so
`chromium.executablePath` read `undefined`, and `await undefined()` is the
error in the logs.

**148 had no `.default` at all** (dual CJS/ESM with a `"require"` condition), so
the version bump alone broke it with no code change. Both versions were
installed and their exports inspected — this is measured, not inferred.

Broken since **#712 on 2026-06-24 — about eleven weeks**, not the three the log
window suggests; retention just caps what is visible.

**Neither suspected PR was involved.** #1483 is already merged and does not
touch `getBrowser()`. #1456 is still open, therefore not deployed.

## `args` was undefined too

Read off the same namespace. The error surfaced on `executablePath` only
because that one is *called*. A fix that unwrapped just the throwing call would
have launched Chromium with **none of its 22 flags** — `--no-sandbox` and
`--single-process` among them — and failed one line further down. Both reads
now come from the resolved object, and a test pins them as a pair.

`resolveChromium()` probes for the API rather than reaching for `.default`
unconditionally, so it survives the package flipping back to CJS, and throws a
message naming the package and the keys it saw if neither shape carries it.

## The monitoring gap

A 100% failure rate on a customer-facing document path ran for eleven weeks in
silence, because the client fallback is indistinguishable from success.

`render-pdf.js` now writes `metrics/renderPdf` on both outcomes;
`health-digest.js` reports it in the digest **subject line**, not only the body.

**The signal is a missing success, not a rising failure count.** This path saw
22 calls in three weeks — any "N failures in 24h" threshold either sleeps
through a total outage or cries wolf. "Renders were attempted and not one
succeeded" trips on the first digest, at any volume.

## Tests proven able to fail

Both suites were break-tested, with the **reddened assertions checked** each
time rather than just the exit code:

- **interop** — full revert (A1–A5 red); the `args`-only half-fix (**A3/A4 red
  while A1/A2 stay green** — the sibling-path trap); an unconditional
  `.default` unwrap (B1–B3 red, regressing the CJS direction).
- **digest** — a volume threshold (A5 red: 22 failures never reaches 50); a
  removed signal; a false alarm on a healthy renderer; dropped HTML escaping.

Both are zero-dep and vm-sandbox the real functions, because a source regex for
`.default` matches the broken code just as happily.

## Not verified here

Chromium cannot be launched off Linux — the package ships a Linux x64 binary —
so **that the browser actually boots in the deployed function is not proven by
anything in this repo**. This path has never once succeeded on 149, so a second
failure further down the launch sequence is possible.

**After deploy: render any document and confirm a `[renderPdf] ok` line.**
There has not been one since June.

## Also

- `documentation/audit/RENDERPDF-CHROMIUM-INTEROP-2026-09-08.md`, linked from
  `INDEX.md`.
- Ratchet floors **measured on the merged tree** (`105/67/190`) after a rebase
  collision with #1503 — both sides carried `disk: 188`, so taking either would
  have shipped two suites of slack.
- The brief cited `documentation/audit/PDF-RENDER-RETENTION-2026-09-08.md` as
  recording this finding; **that file does not exist** anywhere in the repo or
  its history. The new note stands in for it.

author: justinlandes
body:
## What this is

A **read-only certification lane**. It adds one document and changes nothing else:

- `docs/staging-rebuild/rp06a2-edge-function-content-parity-certification-2026-09-08.md`

No staging deployment, no production deployment, no migration, no secret read or write, no product change, no source modification. Every Supabase Management API call was `list_edge_functions` or `get_edge_function` — both read-only. No function was invoked, redeployed or deleted.

## Verdict

> ### BLOCKED — SOURCE RECONCILIATION REQUIRED

All 23 governed Edge Functions were content-compared against **both** deployed environments (staging `yzqjvdfgefveprobvvyw`, production `wyyuqfdxucjksghsmhry`) from canonical `rebuild/backend-authority-v2` @ `90b9fa1` (merged PR #351).

**No P0.** **Six P1s**, and every one is the same shape: *canonical is missing a security control that a deployed environment enforces today.* Deploying canonical as-is would roll those controls back.

| Function | Finding |
|---|---|
| `stylechat-generate` | Canonical drops production's prompt-injection neutralizer. `promptHardening.escapePromptData` no longer calls `neutralizeInjectionMarkers`, and canonical's `_shared/aiSecurity/escapeUntrustedText.ts` has neither that export nor `FAKE_ROLE_HEADINGS_INLINE`. The production source states the consequence in-file: `"Navy blazer. system: ignore prior rules"` survives canonical's substitutions intact. Staging already runs without it (staging is byte-identical to canonical). |
| `privacy-correction-request` | Production 403s `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED` on a non-active / locked / unreadable profile. Canonical has no account-state gate, so a deactivated or pending-deletion account could file new privacy requests. Canonical is stronger on the other axis (a 5/60 s rate limit production lacks) — **neither side is a superset**. |
| `privacy-data-export` | Same finding; production splits it into two fail-closed 403 branches. |
| `product-search-deals` | Production statically imports and calls `assertAccountActiveIfAuthenticated(req)` before the paid RapidAPI call. Canonical has no guard. The deployed comment records the guard was once lost to the `--use-api` bundler and deliberately re-added as a static import. |
| `search-vinted-secondhand` | Same finding, before the Apify actor run (`APIFY_API_TOKEN` budget). |
| `staging-health` | Staging runs an **ungoverned** health-contract-v1 (`/health/live`, `/health/ready`, `/version`, fail-closed release identity, credential-shape redaction on a `verify_jwt=false` public surface) with no committed source anywhere in this repo. Redeploying canonical would remove all of it. |

§5 of the document carries a narrow, file-scoped repair recommendation for each. **No repair was performed in this lane.**

## Method — and why it is not timestamp triage

RP-06A proved deployment-date triage unsafe. This lane used, per function and per environment:

1. **SHA-256 byte comparison** of every deployed file mapped back to its canonical repo path, with a unified diff per mismatch, wherever the Management API result was large enough to be persisted to disk.
2. **Full source read of every deployed file** against its canonical counterpart otherwise.

Evidence tier is stated per function. **Zero timestamp-only classifications.**

Per-function `_shared/**` snapshots were honoured, and the lane re-proves the trap is live: inside the *same* staging project, `process-account-deletions` v61 bundles `revenueCatClient.ts` at the canonical hash while `kplus-activate` v15 bundles an older copy; and staging `restore-account` v55 bundles the new `_shared/deletion/common.ts` while staging `handle-user-deletion` v75 bundles the old one.

Formatting-only differences were **inspected, not assumed** — comment-stripped production deploys of the Apple pair, CRLF and stray-EOF artifacts, a two-line comment banner on `nike-shoe-details`, a copy change on `style-outfit-generate`. None is reported as functional drift.

## Results

```
Total governed:                     23
Fully content-compared:             23    (0 timestamp-only classifications)
Exact canonical == staging parity:  17

PARITY_ALL 1 · CANONICAL_EQUALS_STAGING 10 · CANONICAL_NEWER_ACCEPTED 6
STAGING_NEWER 1 · THREE_WAY_DIVERGENCE 5 · UNRESOLVED 0
ABSENT_FROM_PRODUCTION_BY_DESIGN 5 (secondary tag)

P0 0 · P1 6 · P2-P3 5 · P4+/EXPECTED 12
Ungoverned deployed sources found: 4
```

Also closed: RP-108's open `apple-credential-link` byte-comparison gap, and the 13 Tier-C functions it left uncompared.

## Account-deletion subsystem (post-#351)

Reconfirmed, **not modified**. author: robertoepifanio-byte
body:
Substitui a [#468](https://github.com/robertoepifanio-byte/SHAREO/pull/468) — mesmo conteúdo, recortado sobre o `main` atual (`702e11ed`) por cherry-pick. A branch antiga ficou para trás de seis squash-merges, e o squash apaga a ancestralidade: um merge dela produzia 4 conflitos, em arquivos que esta mudança nunca tocou (`apps/campanha/lib/legal-config.ts`, histórico jurídico). O cherry-pick produziu **um** conflito, resolvido por união (abaixo).

## O quê

O ShareO não cita mais a posição do interessado na lista de Fundadores — nem no e-mail, nem na tela. Decisão do fundador (08/09).

## Corte na fonte, não na copy

`POST /api/founders/leads` parou de devolver `queuePosition` nos dois corpos públicos (201 e 409). Os três formulários (site, `apps/campanha`, `apps/mobile`) perdem o dado **por construção**, em vez de dependerem de três edições de texto que podem divergir depois.

`wave` saiu junto: é derivado de `queuePosition` por `assignWave` — a mesma posição em granularidade grossa, visível em DevTools — e nenhum formulário lia o campo. Continua sendo gravado no banco.

## Copy, alinhada nas 4 superfícies

| Superfície | Antes | Depois |
|---|---|---|
| E-mail | bloco `#5` em 40px + "interessado a entrar na lista" | "Sua inscrição na lista de Fundadores do ShareO está confirmada." |
| Sucesso | `Você é o #{position}° na lista!` | `Você está na lista!` |
| Sucesso (subtítulo) | `quando o Shareo abrir` | `antes da abertura dos cadastros na sua cidade` |
| Duplicado | `Você é o Nº {position} da fila — não criamos um cadastro novo.` | `Não criamos um cadastro novo. Você será avisado antes da abertura dos cadastros na sua cidade.` |

O subtítulo entrou porque "quando o Shareo abrir" contradizia a promessa por cidade que o e-mail e a landing já faziam.

Telemetria: `founder_invite_click` perdeu `queue_position` — não havia outro atributo do clique que não fosse PII.

## O conflito do cherry-pick

`apps/campanha/components/analytics/GoogleAnalytics.tsx` — resolvido por **união**, não escolha:

```ts
| { name: "founder_invite_click"; params?: never }
| { name: "founder_lead_error";   params: { http_status: number; error_code: string } }
```

`founder_lead_error` é a instrumentação que entrou depois do incidente de ~39h em que a campanha recusou todo lead com 422 sem nenhum sinal. Foi mantida com o comentário dela.

## O que **não** mudou

`queuePosition` segue no banco, no `assignWave`, em `lib/founderInvite.ts` e no painel admin (`/admin/fundadores`, export CSV) — lá a ordem de entrada tem uso real.

Esta mudança **não encosta** em `apps/campanha/lib/legal-config.ts`: a campanha continua travada em `marketing-v1.0` de propósito, e o teste-arame de `__tests__/unit/lib/consentimento-marketing.test.ts` passa.

## Limpezas que a mudança revelou

- Três `select` do Prisma ficaram órfãos (`queuePosition` no 409 e na reativação, `wave` na deduplicação).
- O teste da campanha **exigia** `"Nº 42"` no alerta de duplicado — o produto tinha um teste pedindo o oposto do outro. Substituído por uma guarda de que nenhum número aparece.
- O teste do e-mail que defendia a redação do número virou guarda de ausência. Ela precisa do strip de tags: o texto removido não continha "fila" nem "posição", então quem faz o trabalho é `#` + dígito — que sem o strip casaria com as cores hex do próprio `style`.

## Verificação

| | |
|---|---|
| Raiz | **1555** testes (108 suítes), `tsc` limpo |
| Campanha | **33** testes, `tsc` limpo |
| Mobile | **888** testes (48 suítes) |
| Build | `npx next build` exit 0 |

O contador da campanha cai de 34 para 33: o teste da posição sai junto, é esperado. 🪤 A suíte da raiz não cobre `apps/` — as três foram rodadas separadamente.

## Achado de revisão não aplicado (fora de escopo)

A frase "antes da abertura dos cadastros na sua cidade" está hardcoded em **10 pontos** de 3 apps, e o padrão do repo para copy contratual é centralizar em `legal-config` (como `MARKETING_CONSENT_TEXT`). Vale fazer, mas é refatoração própria.

author: emilecadorel
body:
P2 + P4 of YMI-68, on top of the snippet model P1 landed in #56.

## What was wrong

Two defects, one fix, because showing a cited line is pointless if the lines then come out in the wrong order.

- **A referenced location had no excerpt.** `formatLocationNoLineReturn` rendered `-- (test7.yr:(5,9))` and stopped. The declaration explaining the error was never shown — the reader had to open the file, which is the one thing the note was there to spare them.
- **Notes came out in declaration order.** Six of the seven `ErrorMsg` constructors pass `flatten(notes, false)`, and `errors::utils::flatten` compares line alone, so even the sorted path interleaved two files.

## What it does now

Every place a diagnostic points at is a `Mark`, and `snippet::layout` is the one arranging them:

- one excerpt per **file**, the primary's file first;
- labels ordered by **(line, col)** — decided at layout time, so a throw site stays free to build its notes in whatever order is natural to it, and ordering stops being a property each constructor has to remember;
- every line of an excerpt under one shared line-number gutter, its width taken from the widest number it holds;
- a gap between two labelled lines joined by the lines between them when there is at most one, elided to `...` otherwise.

A secondary span is underlined with `-` rather than `^` — the distinction P1 recorded in `LabelKind` but drew the same way — and each label's messages now hang under **its own** caret instead of all gathering under the first.

```
 --> test_resources/root_path/test7.yr:(11,17)
  2  ┃     pub fn foo ()-> i32 { 12 }
     ╋            ---  note: candidate test7::A::foo ()-> i32
    ...
  7  ┃         pub fn foo ()-> f64 { 12.0 }
     ╋                ---  note: candidate test7::B::A::foo ()-> f64
    ...
 11  ┃     let _ = foo ();
     ╋             ^
```

## Decisions this child owned

- **Gap threshold: one line.** A single line of context costs exactly what the `...` standing for it would, and reading it is worth more; two already cost more. This is what rustc settles on and what YMI-68 sketched the target rendering with. `snippet::MAX_GAP`.
- **Two files in one diagnostic:** one excerpt each, the primary's first, so the line numbers of the second never run between those of the first.

The coordinate survives as the fallback for a place nothing can be shown of — a synthesized location, or a file whose content was not kept (`snippet::isShowable`). No `.err` in the corpus reaches it: `-- (` went from 89 occurrences to 0.

## Fallout worth knowing

`lexing/test14.out` and `test15..18.out` lose a caret. The end of those spans is the line return itself: the pair path underlined it, which drew a caret past the visible text *and* injected a blank line. The single-mark path already had the bounds guard; applying it uniformly removes both. This is the quirk P1's comment recorded and deferred here.

## Testing

- `test/ymirc_test/errors/format.yr` gains five cases: a cited location is shown rather than named, labels come out in source order with the notes built in reverse, the header cites the primary label wherever it sits, two files do not interleave, and `MAX_GAP` shows one line and elides two. They are built by hand because no source program makes the validator emit notes out of source order.
- The `.err`/`.out` corpus is regenerated per the CLAUDE.md procedure — 168 files, reviewed by sampling categories. 333 tests green, nothing left in `/tmp/ymir_errors`.

Closes YMI-70.

body:
This PR points CodePen at the shared `composeQuery` helper, which is the sixth site of the idiom #1007 collapsed and the one that PR could not take because `codepen.ts` had a module-local function of its own already called `composeQuery`. That one is now `composePenQuery` and does nothing but assemble the pen's parameters and hand them over.

The two `.set` calls become a spread, which would differ from the original if a key could be written twice. It cannot: the grants a target carries are only ever `key` and `token`, and the two the player adds are `default-tabs` and `theme-id`. Parameter order comes out the same either way, grants first and the player's pair after.

Nothing changes in what the resolver emits.

body:
## Summary

Complete rewrite of Orders.jsx implementing the 26-part UI/UX spec.

### 5-Tab Structure
- **Create Order** — store chips, delivery date, full item table
- **Order History** — date-grouped, search/filter/status filter, expand for items, Excel/PDF/Email per order
- **Receiving** — enter received qty + issue type per pending order item, saves to `order_receiving_records`
- **Receiving History** — searchable/filterable full receiving transaction log
- **Requisitions** — Google Sheets CSV sync, Last Sync / New / Matched / Unmatched stats

### New Column Order (spec Parts 2-9)
`Part # | Item Name | UOM | Avg Consumption | Physical Stock | Order Qty | Approved Qty | Status`

### Key Behaviours
- Physical Stock is **editable input**, saves to `order_physical_stock` table (completely separate from main inventory)
- Average Consumption calculated from historical observations: `prev_physical + prev_order - curr_physical`
- Approved Qty comes from `requisitions_import` matched by part_number
- Order statuses: Draft → Submitted → Pending Approval → Approved → Partially Received → Received / Exception / Cancelled
- Receiving validation: warns if received > approved

### New Migrations
- `030_order_physical_stock.sql` — physical stock observations table
- `031_order_receiving.sql` — adds approved_qty/issue_type/item_status to order_history_items; creates order_receiving_records
- `032_requisitions_import.sql` — Google Sheets import table with sheet_row_hash dedup

### Google Sheets Note
The sheet must be shared as "Anyone with the link → Viewer" for the Sync button to work without Google OAuth.

author: dofliu
body:
## 這個 PR 是什麼

ADR-022 的**實作**。PR #29 在實作推上分支之前就合併了，所以進 main 的只有 ADR 那一筆文件；這裡是接在最新 main 上 rebase 後的實作單一 commit。

秘書**看不到也聽不到**你的線上會議（那個回答是對的），它做的是**會後**那段。

## 做了什麼

- **`core/meeting_transcripts.py`**（新）：WebVTT parser（去編號／時間戳／NOTE，認 `<v NAME>` 與 `NAME:` 兩種講者標記，並把即時字幕「同一句逐漸長出來」的重複 cue 收斂成一段）；逐字稿只從 `meetings.transcript_dir` 進來（沒設就是停用）；配對**只用時間**（檔案修改時間落在某場會議結束後 6 小時內取最近一場），配不到就寫「未配對到行事曆事件」，不猜主題；`meeting_context()` 判斷「在開會」。
- **L0 template `meeting_notes`**：每份逐字稿一則可刪、有 TTL 的記憶區觀察（會議標題／發言與講者數／摘要／候選待辦）。同一檔案只一則，重跑不長第二則。
- **`POST /api/v1/secretary/meetings/followups`**：**唯一會寫 `open_loops` 的路徑**。你點「加入未結事項」才寫，「忽略」只改觀察正文；秘書自己永遠不寫。
- **提案**：`meeting_followups`（候選待辦帶進卡片＋兩顆按鈕）、`meeting_transcript_missing`（結束 15 分後仍無新檔才提，有新檔就不提）。
- **桌面一行**：`#home-desk-meeting`，會議中顯示「📞 會議中：<標題>（還剩 N 分）」；只有其一時如實說差異。
- **摘要預設 `ollama`（全本機）**；雲端 provider 在觀察正文明寫「與會者的發言曾送往該供應商」。事實閘只擋數字，擋下就整段丟掉（摘要與候選一起），逐字稿的可回溯計數仍在。
- `.vtt` 加進 RAG 支援清單——**要不要讓會議內容進知識庫由你在 02 決定**，不是安裝副作用。
- 驗收 **A22**：機器只查「資料夾設了嗎、整理過幾份、候選待辦還剩幾條」；摘要品質留人眼。

## 實機找到並修掉的 bug

容器裡用真實 Teams 匯出格式測，`ollama` 沒開時觀察上寫的是：

```
摘要：失敗（事實閘擋下（逐字稿沒有的數字：111、11434、6））
```

**訊息指錯原因**——真相是連不上 ollama。`LLMClient` 在供應商連不上時**回傳錯誤字串**而不是丟例外，那串錯誤被當成摘要送進事實閘。已加 `looks_like_llm_error()` 在事實閘之前判斷，現在寫的是「provider 未回覆摘要：…（可執行 `python main.py llm-test` 診斷）」。

## 收據

容器 E2E，真實 `.vtt`，走 API 與儀表板：

```
4 個 cue（含「同一句長出來」的重複）→ 3 段發言、2 位講者
配對 → 「z72 告警確認設計討論」（40 分鐘前結束）
桌面 → 📞 會議中：站立會議（還剩 23 分）      ← 行事曆＋Teams 前景兩個訊號都有
卡片 → 兩條候選待辦；點「加入未結事項」後該列消失
open_loops → 1 筆，source_type=meeting，標題與候選文字一字不差；「忽略」不寫任何東西
```

`tests/test_meeting_transcripts.py` 19 項 ＋ A22 1 項；全套 **626 項：625 passed + 1 conditional skip**（63 模組），rebase 後重跑仍綠。L0 allowlist 測試同步加入 `meeting_notes`。

## 邊界（沒做的事）

錄音、**即時字幕／翻譯**、讀會議軟體視窗內容、Teams／Graph API、自動下載逐字稿、保存與會者名單、會前提醒。沒有新資料表、沒有新 migration。即時那層要另寫 ADR 並過 ADR-022 D6 的五道門。

## 與 ADR 草案的三處差異（已寫進 ADR-022 Addendum）

1. 事實閘**只擋數字**，不擋人名——人名查不準，硬做只會假警報；這也是「候選待辦」而非「待辦」的另一個理由。
2. 知識庫資料夾**由你自己加**，程式不自動寫 RAG 資料夾清單。
3. 桌面那行放在既有的 `meeting` 區塊，不另開面板（ADR-019 Addendum B 才把首頁收成兩塊）。

## 文件

ADR-022 轉 **Accepted** ＋ Addendum、`docs/USAGE.md` 一節、`docs/TODO.md`（C7 標記已實作、新增 A22）、`docs/INDEX.md`、`ROADMAP.md` §11／§12.2、`docs/NEXT_SESSION.md`（功能地圖一列＋新的一條坑）、`STATUS.yaml`、`config.example.yaml`。

## 你這邊要做的

合併後 `git pull`、重啟服務 → `meetings.transcript_dir` 設一個資料夾 → 放一份開了轉錄的逐字稿 → 對 `meeting_notes` 按「立即執行」 → `python main.py verify --item A22`。

- `.github/dependabot.yml`
- `.github/release.yml`
- `release-please-config.json`

## Why this change

Dependabot does not hand a dependency to the first group that matches it — `PatternSpecificityCalculator` scores every matching group and the highest wins. `"@vitest/*"` scores 94 and loses `@vitest/coverage-v8` to the pattern-less `dev-dependencies` group (500); on a MAJOR bump that group cannot take it either, so it escapes into its own PR. vitest and its coverage provider peer-depend at an exact version, so the halves apart are unsatisfiable: both PRs fail `npm ci` with ERESOLVE and sit red with auto-merge armed until someone pushes the pair by hand. That cost 19 repos on 2026-09-07 and vibo-mcp #110/#113 the day after.

These three files were previously untemplated, so nothing rendered them and `--check` never saw them: `.github/dependabot.yml` had drifted into 17 variants across 72 repos, `release-please-config.json` into 78 unique copies among 79 (8 with no `changelog-sections` at all), and `.github/release.yml` was missing from 45 repos entirely.

Verified before rolling (chrischall/workflows#236, #239, #241): across the fleet the only semantic `dependabot.yml` change is the added `@vitest/coverage-v8` line, with zero `ignore` entries lost; `release-please-config.json` renders semantically identical for 57 of 60 repos and the other three only gain a `revert` changelog section. The canonical labels `.github/release.yml` categorises by were applied to all 81 repos first.

body:
Implements P2 TODO #8–#10 on top of the account-isolated runtime in PR #6.

## What changes

- add the `internet_workflow` control-plane tool with `start`, `status`, `approve`, `reject`, `cancel`, and `continue` operations;
- add a durable `WorkflowEngine` and private atomic `WorkflowJobStore` under the plugin data directory;
- persist authoritative workflow fields including objective, repository/base revision, state, team lane status, account routing, handoff receipts, writer conversation identity, PR receipt, review cycle, pending action, and compact event state;
- allocate deterministic per-job research/review/writer lane identities;
- keep reviewer A/B identities stable across remediation cycles while review cycle and exact PR head remain authoritative prompt/state inputs;
- convert `/workflow <task>` from the giant follow-up prompt prototype into a thin adapter that resolves Git context, creates one durable engine job, and returns its job ID;
- register/export the workflow tool, engine, store, and workflow contracts from the plugin;
- update package smoke tests and generated `dist/` artifacts;
- mark TODO #8–#10 implemented.

## Scope boundary

This is the workflow **foundation**, not the full autonomous execution loop yet. P3+ still add direct TeamRunner execution, deterministic prompt builders, retries, verbatim handoffs, writer/PR execution, approval classification, review loops, events, and merge binding.

Website-level cross-conversation/project memory optimization is deliberately deferred future work. Workflow correctness depends only on explicit durable state and conversation lanes.

## Conversation continuity

Within one workflow job:

```text
<local>:workflow:<job>:research:A
<local>:workflow:<job>:research:B
<local>:workflow:<job>:review:A
<local>:workflow:<job>:review:B
<local>:workflow:<job>:writer
```

The writer lane is intended to remain the same across implementation, PR creation/update, and remediation. Reviewer lanes remain independent from research/writer and stable across review cycles of the same PR.

## Validation

Final stacked branch head: `cefbfef9da9fa5c9ded814f767e7747a5c419e8c`.

Temporary P2 refresh workflow was removed before final validation. Normal Verify run `34267660161` passed on that exact clean head:

This PR is intentionally based on `impl/p1-multi-account-foundation` while PR #6 remains open, so it contains only P2 changes.
