## Summary
Stacked on #665 (the A1 spec) so the `docs/superpowers/README.md` index rows and the CHANGELOG entries don't collide; until #665 merges this diff shows both specs. Its own change is one document: the design for roadmap A3's endgame — `nsl-abi` as the single typed source of the runtime C-ABI, and dropping the codegen → runtime dependency edge. Like the A1 spec it is a design, not code: it records what is already done (the wire constants, the text cross-check), measures the three hand-written copies and the edge as they stand today, and lays out the renderings, the moves and six gated steps. Nothing changes a symbol's signature or the emitted CLIF.

## Changes
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-a3-abi-extern-table-design.md` (new, 235 lines):
  - **Where it stands** — 813 runtime externs; ~370 codegen declarations across 15 `RUNTIME_FUNCTIONS*` tables; the `c_wrapper::emit` header surface (~20 prototypes) and the 6 hand-written Python `argtypes`; the measured edge: 371 `nsl_log!` sites, 9 format/record symbols, 8 compile-time device probes, a 248-crate dependency closure of which 113 are the runtime's own.

## [Phase 1] Walking Skeleton

**Goal:** The pinned stack boots as a single process, reads from SQLite through a generated Prisma client, and loads inside the Pivota preview frame — so that no later phase is built on an unproven persistence path, and no UI phase is ever debugged as an application bug when the real fault is a blank iframe or a dropped cookie.

## What was implemented
- One command sequence brings up `next dev` on `0.0.0.0:3000` serving one USWDS-styled page reading a seeded row from SQLite through the generated Prisma client; no Docker/service/2nd process/queue.

- The page renders inside an iframe; an automated scan of **every** response (middleware included) finds zero `X-Frame-Options` and zero restrictive `frame-ancestors`.

- Structural layout gate

body:
## El patrocinador con campo de Tanner

**La lógica ya era correcta desde el principio**, en el navegador y en el servidor: `sync()` oculta el campo Tanner salvo para familia, y `command_create_parking` exige Tanner solo para `familia` y nombre para el resto.

Lo roto era el CSS. El atributo `hidden` lo pisa **cualquier** regla de autor que ponga `display`, y ninguna hoja del proyecto lo definía. `.park-form label{display:grid}` hacía que `hidden` no ocultara nada — por eso al elegir Patrocinador seguía apareciendo el Tanner, y el motivo de cortesía se veía sin estar marcada la casilla.

Se define en `shell.css` y en `styles.css`, que entre las dos cubren todas las pantallas. Es la misma clase de bug que `.hidden`, que vivía solo en la hoja del shell viejo — y afecta también a Scouting, que usa el mismo patrón.

Medido en el navegador con las hojas reales:

| Para | Tanner | Nombre | Teléfono |
|---|---|---|---|
| Familia | **visible** | oculto | oculto |
| Patrocinador | **oculto** | visible | visible |
| Profe | **oculto** | visible | visible |

## El buscador de Tanner

Eran 65 opciones en una lista larga. `smart-select.js` ya existe en el repo, ya observa el DOM para enganchar selects creados después, y ya lo usan Contabilidad, Porteros y Deportivo. Bastaba el atributo `data-smart-search`.

Verificado sobre HTTP (los módulos ES no cargan por `file://`):

| Escribes | Sale |
|---|---|
| `gonza` | Gonzalo García Zarazúa |
| `inaki` | Iñaki Tadeo Carpio Preciado — **ignora acentos** |
| `t10` | Erick García Medina · T10 — **también busca por categoría** |

## Dos falsos positivos míos, para que queden en el registro

En el primer probe quité las interpolaciones de plantilla del formulario en vez de expandirlas, así que el `<select>` quedó sin opciones y **los tres casos salieron "oculto"** — parecía que el arreglo no servía. En el segundo, el buscador reportó ausente porque `file://` bloquea módulos ES por CORS. Ninguno de los dos era un problema del código; los dos eran de mi prueba.

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- `%TypedArray%.prototype.indexOf`, `lastIndexOf` and `includes` match an element that is not there when the search value is outside what the element type can hold. Three paths of the one conversion helper, `toNativeFromValueWithoutCoercion<Adaptor>()` (`runtime/ToNativeFromValue.h`), wrap, round or truncate the needle instead of reporting "not representable":
  - BigInt needle: `new BigInt64Array([1n]).includes(2n ** 64n + 1n)` and `new BigUint64Array([2n ** 64n - 1n]).includes(-1n)` are `true`. The path calls `JSBigInt::toBigInt64` / `toBigUInt64`, the modular ToBigInt64 / ToBigUint64 meant for stores.
  - int32 needle, Float32 / Float16 elements: `new Float32Array([16777216]).indexOf(16777217)` and `new Float16Array([Infinity]).indexOf(65536)` are `0`. `toNativeFromInt32WithoutCoercion` casts with no round-trip check.
  - double needle, Uint8Clamped elements: `u8c.indexOf(-1)` finds a 255 and `256`, `1e10`, `2 ** 31`, `Infinity` find a 0, in bun's release build only. `Uint8ClampedAdaptor::toNativeFromDoubleWithoutCoercion` (`runtime/TypedArrayAdaptors.h:339`) does `static_cast<uint8_t>(double)`, undefined behavior outside (-1, 256). #205 replaced the same cast in `IntegralTypedArrayAdaptor` but not this one.
- V8 (Node 26, Chromium 148) returns -1 / false for all of these, as the spec requires.

### Fix
- Add `JSBigInt::tryExtractInt64` / `tryExtractUInt64` next to `tryExtractDouble` (they share a new `absoluteAsUInt64` helper) and use them for the BigInt path. They return `std::nullopt` unless the BigInt is in [-2^63, 2^63) or [0, 2^64).
- `FloatTypedArrayAdaptor` and `Float16Adaptor`: the int32 path now goes through the checked double path (an int32 converts to double exactly). The double path does its range check before the narrowing cast instead of after, because converting a finite double beyond FLT_MAX (or 65504) to `float` (or `_Float16`) is undefined behavior too.
- `Uint8ClampedAdaptor`: convert through `truncateDoubleToInt64()` and then narrow, the form #205 gave `IntegralTypedArrayAdaptor`. The 64-bit truncation is an intrinsic with a defined overflow result, so the optimizer cannot fold the round-trip check away.
- Verified: `JSTests/stress/typed-array-index-of-unrepresentable-needle.js` (new) covers all 12 element types with int32, double and BigInt needles at and beyond each type's limits, plus -0, NaN and the double-array source from the original report. With a Release JSCOnly build of this branch it passes under default options, `--useJIT=0` and eager tiering. The unpatched engine fails it at `Float32Array int32 2^24 + 1 indexOf: expected -1 but got 0` (any build) and at `Uint8ClampedArray double -1 indexOf: expected -1 but got 2` (bun 1.4.2 release). The 714 test262 cases under `built-ins/TypedArray/prototype/{indexOf,lastIndexOf,includes}` and `built-ins/TypedArrayConstructors/internals` pass (strict and sloppy), as do the 266 typed-array, DataView and BigInt64 stress tests that run without ICU data.

### Background
- The spec compares the search value with each element's Number or BigInt value by IsStrictlyEqual (`indexOf`, `lastIndexOf`) or SameValueZero (`includes`). JSC instead converts the search value to the element type once and scans raw storage with `WTF::find8/16/32/64/Float`. That is only equivalent when the conversion is exact, so the helper returns `std::optional` and the callers answer -1 / false on `nullopt` (with the detached / `undefined` special case for `includes`).
- Why the Uint8Clamped face is build-dependent: LLVM lowers the cast to `fptoui double to i8`, which is poison out of range, and the check `static_cast<double>(integer) != value` to `uitofp` + `fcmp`. LLVM 22's DAG combiner folds `uitofp (fptoui x)` to `ftrunc x` whenever the sign of zero cannot be observed (`canIgnoreSignBitOfZero`), which an `fcmp` use satisfies. LLVM 21 only did this under `-fno-signed-zeros`. The WebKit prebuilt is compiled by clang 21, but bun's release link is ThinLTO through rust-lld (LLD 22.1.8), so the `-lto` prebuilt's bitcode is code-generated by LLVM 22. The check becomes `roundsd $0xb` + `ucomisd` ("is `value` integral?") and the needle is the low byte of a 32-bit `cvttsd2si`, which is `0x80000000` for anything outside int32 range. bun 1.4.2's `typedArrayViewProtoFuncIncludes` has exactly that sequence at `+0xcfb`.
- There is no DFG/FTL intrinsic for these three functions on typed arrays, so the C++ built-in is the only implementation and every tier was affected the same way.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- Standalone reproduction of the codegen: compiling the old `toNativeFromDoubleWithoutCoercion` to bitcode with clang 21 (`-O3 -flto=thin`) and linking with `--ld-path=<rustup nightly-2026-07-20>/gcc-ld/ld.lld` produces `cvttsd2si %xmm0,%eax; roundsd $0xb,%xmm0,%xmm1` and reports `1e10` found; the `truncateDoubleToInt64` form produces `cvttsd2si %xmm0,%rax; cvtsi2sd %ecx,%xmm1` and is correct. Plain clang 21 `-O3` keeps the round trip for both, which is why the non-LTO prebuilt (local `bun run build:release`, the release-asan build) never showed it.
- The wrong bytes quoted above are x86-64 (`cvttsd2si` gives `0x80000000` out of range, so its low byte is 0). Any other release target whose LTO link code-generates with LLVM 22 folds the check the same way but searches for a target-specific byte (arm64 `fcvtzu` saturates, so a double `-1` would match a 0 rather than a 255). Non-LTO builds of every target keep the round trip.
- `tryExtractDouble` keeps its behavior; it now calls `absoluteAsUInt64` for the digit gathering it used to inline.
- `toBigInt64` / `toBigUInt64` are unchanged and still used for stores and `Atomics`, where the modular conversion is the specified behavior.
- Upstream WebKit `main` has the same code in all three places.

</details>

author: tangosdev
body:
# The matched-loss exception, and the evidence it now needs

Three corrections to the generalized exception, one commit each, each with the negative
control that reproduced the defect before it was fixed. Every one of the reproductions
below was driven through the real `build_report` on a committed tree, not through a
hand-built dict.

## A. The overlay word reader took its base from the first function

`_module_image` read an overlay at `_rev_enrolment(rev)[0][module][0]`, which is a list
of FUNCTION addresses. `modules._overlay_base`, the derivation the comment claimed to
follow and the one the byte gate, `match.py --module ovNNN` and `evidence_rom` all use,
takes the lowest address of ANY symbol. A module whose lowest symbol is data therefore
answered every query with an earlier word.

`_module_symbol_base` is the revision-pinned equivalent of that all-symbol base, and
itcm and dtcm are readable now too, from the two places `modules.py` looks. ARM9 keeps
its fixed 0x02004000 load base, which is not its lowest symbol (`overlay_100` at
0x00000064 is).

Negative control, `DataLeadingOverlayImageBase`: an ov001 with four bytes of data in
front of its first function, `bx lr` at 0x020ab150 and `mov r0, #0` at the retired
record 0x020ab154.

| test | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_the_reader_answers_from_the_lowest_symbol_not_the_first_function` | reader returns 0xe12fff1e | 0xe3a00000 |
| `test_a_non_return_tail_in_a_data_leading_overlay_is_refused` | Passed, `reasons: []`, one absorbed | refused, `lost 1 matched function(s)` |
| `test_the_same_overlay_fixture_with_a_real_tail_return_still_lands` | (positive control) | lands |

Measured on this tree: 72 of the 73 modules that declare functions have equal bases
either way, so no live read moves. The exception is ARM9, which does not use this path.

## B. Zero functions did not make an empty relocation file complete

The inventory check exempted an empty `relocs.txt` whenever the module's symbol table
declared no function. A module with no code can still hold a table of callback pointers
in its `.data`, and every one of them is an incoming reference the index would then not
know about.

`_empty_relocs_defect` asks what dsd wrote instead, in this order: a module declaring a
function is refused as before; otherwise the module's own section inventory decides, and
a module whose non-`bss` sections are all zero-length really does reference nothing
(`.bss` is uninitialised and occupies no cartridge bytes); a module WITH initialised
bytes has to be read, and passes only when those words are all zero. No inventory, or no
image to read one, is a defect naming the file it wanted.

Negative control,
`test_a_data_only_module_with_an_empty_relocation_file_fails_closed`: a data-only ov001
added to the real absorption fixture, with a nonempty four-byte `.data` holding the
retired ARM9 address and an empty `relocs.txt` in both snapshots. Before: `Passed`,
`relocationEvidence.valid: true`, one absorbed record. After: refused, naming
`config/arm9/overlays/ov001/relocs.txt is empty`.
`test_a_data_only_module_whose_data_is_zeroed_is_still_legitimate` is the other half:
the same layout with a zeroed word still lands. Four `RelocIndex` controls cover the
bss-only inventory, the missing inventory, the unreadable image and the zeroed data.

Live census unchanged: **92 destination buckets, 96,395 destinations, 0 defects.**
Disclosed, and in the docstring: on a checkout with no `extracted/` it is the same 92
and 96,395 with **one** defect, `config/arm9/dtcm`, whose 0x20 of `.data` can only be
shown harmless by reading it (it is all zeroes). That makes the exception unavailable
there, which is the position it is already in without the ROM image, and it changes no
other number in the report.

## C. A four-byte tail with return-shaped bits is not an owned epilogue

Three independent fixtures returned `Passed`, no reasons and one absorbed record at
92f9ad43b. Reproduced here first, all three, then refused:

1. **A named callback at the covering range's tail.** The existing control put it
   mid-range, so it tested position rather than identity.
2. **A compiler-generated literal pool.**
   `unsigned int func_02071644(void) { return 0xe12fff1e; }` under the pinned 2004/b56
   emits `e59f0000 e12fff1e e12fff1e`, and the object's mapping symbols put `$d` at
   offset 8. The final word has a return's exact bits and is a constant.
3. **`0xe8908000`, `ldm r0, {pc}`**, together with `ldmdb r0, {pc}` and
   `ldmib r0!, {pc}`.

Two new clauses, and a return classifier that no longer diverges from the helper it
cites:

* **(e) identity.** `_named_symbol` refuses when any symbol in EITHER revision names the
  retired address with anything but the placeholder config derives from the address
  itself (`func_02071694`, `func_ov006_020cb030`). `AutoloadCallback` is a name; a
  placeholder is not.
* **(f) code ownership.** `_compiled_code_reader` compiles the merged source at the
  revision under judgement with the pinned compiler and reads the ARM EABI mapping
  symbols of the object it produces. The retired address must lie inside the merged
  function's own compiled output in a `$a` region, and the word the object emits there
  must be the cartridge's word. `$d` is refused. This tool has no object of its own --
  the worker hands it `rombuild.py`'s JSON, which says whether a module reproduced, not
  where inside a function the instructions stop -- so it builds one.
* **the return set** is now classified by `evidence_rom.is_unconditional_return`,
  imported rather than re-derived, then narrowed to `bx lr` and a stack pop to pc.
  `ldm r0, {pc}` and its db/ib spellings are gone because the base register must be
  r13; `mov pc, lr` is gone because its return-ness is a fact about lr, not about the
  word; `ldr pc, [sp], #4` stays refused on the block-transfer bits. (The comment
  claiming capstone decodes that one as LDR was wrong. It renders it `pop {pc}`.)

New refusing tests: `test_a_named_callback_at_the_tail_is_refused`,
`test_a_literal_pool_at_the_tail_is_refused`,
`test_an_object_that_emits_a_different_word_is_refused`,
`test_a_block_load_through_a_register_other_than_sp_is_refused`,
`test_without_code_ownership_nothing_matched_may_leave`, and the same three through
`build_report`: `test_a_named_callback_at_the_tail_fails_the_report`,
`test_a_literal_pool_at_the_tail_fails_the_report`,
`test_a_block_load_through_r0_fails_the_report`,
`test_without_code_ownership_the_report_fails_closed`.

Two classes run the real compiler rather than a stub, and skip where it is absent:
`CompiledCodeOwnership` builds the literal-pool object and asserts offset 8 is data
while offset 4, the same bits, is an instruction; `LiteralPoolThroughBuildReport` drives
the literal-pool input end to end through `build_report` with no stub anywhere,
refusing the pool and still landing a body that really ends in that instruction. The
report fixtures elsewhere pass a stub, because the runner that runs this suite has no
toolchain and a stub is how the WIRING gets tested there; `code_evidence` is a seam, not
a policy knob, and no value of it grants the exception.

`tools/requirements.txt` gains pyyaml: `evidence_rom` imports it at module level, so the
suite that exercises the shared classifier needs it.

The warning and the report row now state what the guard establishes and stop there --
that a function this merge compiles owns those four bytes and emits the cartridge's own
return at them, that config has no independent name for them, and that no relocation
destination in a validated index points at them. Reachability is named as not claimed.

## Runs

`python -m unittest tools.test_validate_merge`: **139 tests, OK** (114 before). The
tool-tests.yml list, run whole: **717 tests, OK, 2 skips** on a Windows tree with the
toolchain (692 be

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ multer (1.4.5-lts.1 → 2.3.0) · [Repo](https://github.com/expressjs/multer) · [Changelog](https://github.com/expressjs/multer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 multer vulnerable to Denial of Service via crafted multipart field names

Impact

A vulnerability in multer allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to crash the Node.js process with a single multipart/form-data request. Two specially crafted text field names cause an uncaught RangeError: Invalid array length inside multer's field parsing, which is not routed to the application error handler and terminates the process. All applications using multer to parse multipart requests are affected.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.3.0.

Workarounds

None.

🚨 multer vulnerable to Denial of Service via file descriptor leak on aborted uploads

Impact

A vulnerability in multer 2.2.0 allows an attacker to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by aborting or truncating multipart uploads. When using diskStorage, the destination write stream is not closed if the upload is aborted before it finishes, so each failed request leaks an open file descriptor and retains its disk blocks until the process exits. Repeated failed uploads can exhaust the available file descriptors. All applications using multer's disk storage are affected.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.3.0.

Workarounds

None.

🚨 multer vulnerable to file size limit bypass via async fileFilter race condition

Impact

When multer is configured with an asynchronous fileFilter, the limits.fileSize limit can be bypassed. The 'limit' event is registered inside the async fileFilter callback, so if a file exceeds limits.fileSize before that callback runs, the event is missed and the oversized upload is accepted instead of being rejected with a LIMIT_FILE_SIZE error. Applications that rely on limits.fileSize to reject oversized uploads are affected on all upload methods (.single(), .array(), .fields(), .any()). Uploads using a synchronous fileFilter are not affected.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.3.0.

Workarounds

Use a synchronous fileFilter, or validate the uploaded file size after the upload completes.

🚨 multer vulnerable to Denial of Service via oversized array index in field names

Impact

multer is vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) via a crafted array index in multipart field names. The append-field dependency parses bracket notation in field names, and a large numeric index such as items[4294967294] forces allocation of a maximum-length sparse array. A following field with a non-numeric key on the same base then converts that array to an object by iterating its full length, which consumes CPU synchronously and leaves the process unable to handle other requests. A single HTTP request with a crafted multipart body is sufficient to exploit this, and it affects multer 1.x and 2.x.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.3.0 and configure limits.fieldArrayIndexLimit to the minimum array index their application requires.

Workarounds

None.

🚨 Multer vulnerable to Denial of Service via incomplete cleanup of aborted uploads

Impact

A vulnerability in Multer allows an attacker to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by aborting or sending malformed multipart uploads, causing orphaned partial files to accumulate on disk when using diskStorage.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.2.0, 3.0.0-alpha.2 or higher

Workarounds

None

🚨 Multer vulnerable to Denial of Service via deeply nested field names

Impact

Multer is vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) via deeply nested field names in multipart form data. The append-field dependency parses bracket notation in field names (e.g., a[b][c]) with no limit on nesting depth, allowing an attacker to force allocation of deeply nested object structures that consume CPU and memory. A single HTTP request with a crafted multipart body is sufficient to exploit this.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.2.0 and configure limits.fieldNestingDepth to the minimum depth their application requires.

Workarounds

Set limits.fields to a reasonable value to reduce the number of fields an attacker can send per request. This does not fully mitigate the issue but limits the impact.

🚨 Multer Vulnerable to Denial of Service via Uncontrolled Recursion

Impact

A vulnerability in Multer versions < 2.1.1 allows an attacker to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending malformed requests, potentially causing stack overflow.

Patches

Users should upgrade to 2.1.1

Workarounds

None

- `App.jsx`: `/explore/career-match` gates on `user?.country === 'GH'`, mirroring the existing `/admin` → `user?.is_admin` pattern. `ExploreLanding` drops the Career Match card entirely for non-GH users.

`tests/conftest.py` imported `core.database` before `main` (whose import triggers `load_dotenv()`), so `core.database`'s engine got permanently bound to a hardcoded `localhost` fallback instead of the real dev `DATABASE_URL` for the rest of the test process. Fixed by swapping the import order. Doesn't affect production (Render injects env vars before Python starts).

- [x] Playwright: NG user sees neither (card absent on Explore landing, direct URL nav redirects, WASSCE plan absent, University Entrance plan still shown)

author: amir20
body:
Groundwork for #361 — this does **not** fix that issue, but it removes the two things that make it undiagnosable and permanent.

### The problem

`stream_container_stats` swallowed every stream error with `Err(_) => break` and ended the task. Nothing re-armed monitoring afterwards: `active_containers` is only pruned by stop/die/destroy events, so `handle_container_start` saw the stale finished handle and took the "already monitored" branch. A container that never stopped sat at zero for CPU, memory, PIDs, network and disk for the rest of the session — and not even restarting it helped, since the entry still looked live.

### Changes

- Log the stats stream error (container + host), then re-open the stream with a capped 1s → 5s backoff.
- Before each retry, inspect the container and stop if it is no longer running, so a stopped or removed container does not spin against a 404. Lifecycle stays owned by the Docker events.
- Split into `stream_container_stats` (retry loop) and `stream_stats_once` (one pass). Smoothed EMA values and the cached cgroup path carry across a reconnect; the previous-sample counters reset, since a rate measured across the outage gap is not one worth reporting.
- `DockerHost::is_monitored` checks `!handle.is_finished()` instead of `contains_key`.
- `start_container_monitoring` aborts any handle it replaces — re-listing after a reconnect went through there for every running container and orphaned the old task each time.

### Tests

New `src/docker/stats_retry_tests.rs` drives a real Bollard client against a stand-in daemon on a unix socket that serves one sample and then hangs up mid-body:

- the stream gets re-opened and samples keep arriving (verified this fails without the fix — it times out after the single sample)
- the retry loop stops once the UI's channel closes

Plus a unit test for `is_monitored`.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all clean. Also smoke-tested against a live daemon: stats flow normally, no spurious retries.

### On #361 itself

I could not reproduce it. Tried engines 24, 26, 27, 28 and 29, rootful and rootless, with containers on a user-defined bridge (`external: true`), an `internal` network, macvlan, ipvlan and `none`, both compose shapes from the report, and containers created both before and while dtop was running. All streamed stats fine, and the raw `/containers/<id>/stats` payload is identical between an external-network-only container and a bridge one. After this lands, a report like that one should at least come with a log line naming the error.

Tab switches reset subsections and redraw hidden lists, adding friction to workout and food logging.

## Changes
- Remember subsection, scroll and food-entry mode during the page session. Explicit workout-start/edit actions still open the logger.
- Render visible views only, skip unchanged views and invalidate on persisted changes.
- Keep totals visible while adding food; add Done adding and group manual save/clear under Day options.
- Clearer primary actions, mobile input sizing/button targets, workout action placement, destination focus and reduced-motion support.
- v1.5.0 shell cache; no data migration.

## Validation
All 22 Node test files, syntax checks, and all 40 desktop/mobile Chromium tests passed. Navigation, scroll/form retention, live totals, invalidation, focus and reduced motion passed alongside existing regressions.

CI: https://github.com/klow1931/fitness-tracker/actions/runs/34286752497

Baseline render-count measurement for Nutrition → Workouts → Nutrition: 4 day loads, 2 hidden history and 2 hidden library renders. The browser test confirmed 1 day load and no hidden history/library renders in both viewports; timing remains environment-dependent.

## Limits
Navigation memory lasts until refresh. Physical iOS keyboard/camera and cached-upgrade behavior are not certified by Chromium tests. Not merged or deployed.

author: qianghan
body:
AU line-number coverage **4/34 → 23/34** — 9% to 68%, level with CA (69%) and US (70%). But the coverage number is the symptom; the shape was the bug.

## What was wrong

The AU business schedule had rows for **advertising, insurance, legal and professional, office supplies, travel, telephone and internet**. Those are the US Schedule C / CA T2125 categories, copied across when the pack was written.

**The ATO's P8 has none of them.** An Australian return groups by:

> opening stock · purchases and other costs · closing stock · cost of sales · foreign resident withholding · contractor, sub-contractor and commission · superannuation · bad debts · lease · rent · interest within Australia · interest overseas · depreciation · motor vehicle · repairs and maintenance · **all other expenses** · home office · total expenses

So the worksheet handed an Australian accountant six categories that don't appear on the form they're filling in. Adding item numbers could never have fixed that — which is exactly what reading the actual form revealed, and why I stopped at 4 last time rather than inventing letters.

## The mapping already existed

Every account in the AU chart of accounts already carries a `taxCategory` — `ITR - Motor vehicle expenses`, `ITR - Rent expenses`, `ITR - All other expenses`. The P8 row names, mapped correctly, and **never once used by the form**. This wires it up.

`expense_categories:` (plural) is new. The ATO folds nine of our accounts into one line, and the single-code query couldn't express that without exposing all nine as separate fields — the shape being removed. **6999, the uncategorised-expense suspense account, is deliberately in that roll-up** so an expense nobody categorised is still claimed rather than dropped from the return.

## On the label letters

Eleven come from complete sentences in the published instructions:

> add up your primary production and non-primary production motor vehicle expenses and write the total at **P8 – label N**

Not from proximity, which on my first pass produced two contradictory answers.

**Four rows carry "P8" with no letter.** The 2026 page states label `K` for *both* opening stock and rent expenses, in two separate complete sentences, which cannot both be right; "All other expenses" and "Total expenses" state none anywhere. Rather than pick, those rows name the item and let the label carry the rest — a wrong letter on a tax worksheet looks authoritative in a way a blank does not. Same reasoning that removed the fabricated MeF export in #513.

## Compatibility

`gross_business_income`, `total_expenses` and `net_business_income` keep their field IDs — `au/tax-review-pack.ts` names them as the critical fields it checks before a filing may be submitted. Verified, and now asserted so a future rename can't silently break the submit gate.

## Guards

The P8 row list is asserted **in both directions**: every published row has a field, and no Schedule C leftover survives. Mutation-checked — swapping rent back to advertising fails both, naming each:

```
P8 rows with no field: Rent
rows that do not exist on P8: Advertising
```

A third assertion checks every expense row reaches the total, so a row can't be quietly computed out of the return. Mutation-checked: dropping `cost_of_sales` from the SUM fails with `expense rows missing from the total: cost_of_sales`.

## Verification

Tax plugin 22 files / 203 tests pass. Jurisdictions 347 pass. web-next 2507 pass (6 known `DATABASE_URL` failures). Typecheck 344, at baseline.

Source: ato.gov.au — Business and professional items schedule 2026 instructions (NAT 2543-06.2026), Expenses P8; and Individual supplementary tax return 2026 instructions, question 15. Read 2026-09-08.

author: esafwan
body:
## Summary

Remediates the 28-finding source audit at `tracks/sa-code-coherence-audit/deep-report.md`: live bench verification, fixes across 9 packages, an adversarial review round, live re-validation, a full gap-closure pass, and — while chasing a full operator-journey test — a real, previously-undiscovered app bug that blocked **all** order creation on any branch, on any site, plus 5 related fixes it took to prove that fully live.

Full detail: all `tracks/sa-code-coherence-audit/*.md` files in `ury_workspaces`, especially `p7-operator-journey.md` for the newest work.

## The headline fix: order creation was broken everywhere

`URY Production Unit` has a `company` custom field (added 2026-07-17) that was never actually wired (`fetch_from: null`, never populated). `URY Item Production Configuration`'s own validation reads `production_unit.company` to enforce company-scoping — since it was always blank, **every** production config with a `production_unit` set has always failed that check, on any branch, on any site with this field installed. This is why every menu item showed "Temporarily unavailable" everywhere. Not one of the 28 audited findings; found while trying to run a full live order end-to-end against this PR's own fix branch.

Fixing it and proving it live surfaced a chain of 5 more real bugs (the "arbitrary company" pattern repeated in 13 places across the demo-seed package, a stock-seeding gap for real historical items, a Sales Plan coverage cap, a `docstatus` filter that could never match, and a missing cashier permission on an internal doctype) — all fixed, all shipped in this PR. Full live proof: logged in as a real cashier account, searched a real item, added to cart, placed a real order, printed, and paid — `POS Invoice` ended `Paid`/`docstatus=1`/fully reconciled, with a real KOT generated. See `p7-operator-journey.md` for the complete trail and reasoning (including one fix that was explicitly considered and rejected — `ignore_permissions=True` — because it would have reintroduced exactly the vulnerability class this audit's P1 package fixed elsewhere).

## Explicit product requirement addressed (U05)

> The daily scheduler runs demo seeding unconditionally — that was never what we needed. It should ideally be a method/command we can optionally run to seed data. Never seeded via scheduler unconditionally.

`ury.ury.dev_seed.demo_runner.seed_all` is removed entirely from `hooks.py`'s `scheduler_events`. Live-confirmed: zero registrations across every scheduler frequency, and the new `bench <site> seed-demo-data` command exercised end-to-end on a disposable site, performing real seeding.

## Status: 25/28 original findings have live-execution evidence, 0 known regressions

- **25/28** findings have live/real-execution evidence (not just a static read).
- **2/28** remain source-verified only for concrete, honest reasons: U06 was blocked by the production-unit bug above (now fixed — could be re-attempted); U21 would require deleting a live company on the shared dataset to exercise directly.
- **0 known regressions** — full existing test suite (45 modules) passes cleanly; running it for the first time against a live bench caught and fixed 5 test-only mock-setup issues before they could surface as CI failures.
- Two full review rounds (round 1 fixes the 28 findings, round 2 fixes what an Opus adversarial review found wrong with round 1, including a real authorization bypass in an untouched sibling file), both live re-validated, plus this final gap-closure pass.

## PR/merge status

- `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`, `mergeable: MERGEABLE` against `v3-stg` — no conflicts.
- No CI configured on this repo; the full test-suite sweep is this PR's regression check, and it is clean.
- Left in **draft** — no reviewer has looked at it yet, and the stock-ledger/closing/reporting stages beyond payment were not exercised in this pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `bench migrate` / `bench build --app ury` clean, every round
- [x] All Python files touched pass `py_compile`
- [x] Full existing test suite (45 modules) passes with zero failures
- [x] Live re-exploit of every P1/P2 security and correctness fix, rounds 1 and 2
- [x] Live fixture-based exploitation of U10/U11/U12/U19/U25 and U13 (real browser session)
- [x] Live end-to-end verification of U05 (scheduler absence + on-demand command)
- [x] **Live end-to-end order → KOT → payment through the real POS UI, as a real cashier account** — the strongest verification in this whole cycle
- [ ] Stock-ledger posting, closing, and reporting stages beyond payment
- [ ] U06 needs one more live attempt now that the blocking bug is fixed

author: mcdonc
body:
Fixes #3368.

## Summary

Two changes to the daily fuzz run, matching the issue's two open problems:

1. **`scripts/fuzz-api.py` — raise the `wait_for_server` boot budget from 30 s
   to 120 s.** A cold `ubuntu-latest` runner spends ~8 s on the uvicorn boot,
   ~3 s on migrations + seeding, then 12–30 s in `prewarm_podman()` (its own
   docstring allows ~20–30 s for the first `podman create`). Good days landed
   at ~23 s and squeaked under the old deadline; Sep 7/8 crossed it and the
   run aborted with 0 requests sent. The 120 s budget covers the slow path
   while staying small against the 10-minute session.

2. **`.github/workflows/fuzz-daily.yml` — build the network sidecar image
   alongside the workspace image** (`build-tasks: klangk:build-workspace-image
   klangk:build-network-sidecar`). `netfilter_enabled` defaults to true and
   the fuzz env doesn't override it, so workspace start/restart that attaches
   the sidecar tried to pull `klangk-network-sidecar` from docker.io and
   surfaced a raw 500 (observed Sep 6 on `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/restart`).
   The build task tags the image with exactly the name the backend's
   `network_sidecar_image` default expects, so the attach path now exercises
   the real container flow instead of failing. Same task combination the
   sandbox E2E workflow already uses.

The third item in the issue — ~50 false-green daily runs (Jul 18 – Sep 5,
login-body drift + aborts not counted as failures) — was already fixed by
`7422a6cfd` (login posts `identifier`; aborts set `tracker.runner_error` →
exit 1). This PR verifies those fixes are in place; no new change needed.

## Testing

- `scripts/tests` suite: 146 passed (CI invocation).
- `pre-commit run xenon --all-files`: passed (the fuzzer script is in the
  graded set).
- The real proof is the next scheduled run; the change is otherwise
  unexercisable locally without a cold stock runner.

author: limbit95
body:
### Motivation

- The existing lifecycle-safe restore still allowed a race where an in-flight `claim_push_subscription` RPC could finish after logout/account-switch and leave a stale DB ownership row tied to the old user. 
- The goal is a minimal fix that keeps the current `lifecycleEpoch`/`isCurrent` pattern and the DB/RLS/RPC security model unchanged while ensuring stale claims are compensated. 

### Description

- Track restore claim Promises per-user with a new `inFlightRestoreClaims` map and `trackRestoreClaim` helper, and expose a bounded waiter `waitForPushRestoreClaims(userId, timeoutMs)` to coordinate during sign-out. 
- When claiming in `restorePushNotifications` the code now captures the claim Promise (`const claimPromise = saveSubscription(subscription)`), tracks it, `await`s it, and if the lifecycle is stale after it resolves performs compensating cleanup using the claim-originating session access token via a REST call to the existing `remove_own_push_subscription` RPC (no RPC signature/schema changes). 
- `signOut` now increments `lifecycleEpoch` as before but also `await`s `waitForPushRestoreClaims(userId)` with a bounded timeout (3s) and logs a warning on timeout so logout is not indefinitely blocked. 
- Browser-subscription handling preserves `createdByRestore` semantics so newly-created subscriptions from a stale restore are unsubscribed, and preexisting subscriptions are not unsubscribed incorrectly; `restoredUserIds` and `restorePromises` behavior is preserved. 
- Tests and build artifacts updated: behavioral tests added to `tests/web-push.test.js` to cover the claim-in-flight scenarios (logout, account switch, relogin), and hashed assets / `index.html` updated to match the rebuilt bundle; modified files include `js/web-push.js`, `js/auth.js`, `tests/web-push.test.js`, `index.html` and regenerated `assets/build/*`. 

### Testing

- Ran `npm run test:web-push` which passed all web-push behavioral tests (18/18). 
- Ran `npm run test:admin-permissions` which passed (8/8). 
- Ran `npm run build:assets` and the repository static checks `node scripts/check-site.mjs`, `node --experimental-vm-modules scripts/check-community-modules.mjs`, `node scripts/check-community-api-boundaries.mjs`, and `node scripts/check-community-selects.mjs`, all of which completed successfully. 
- Attempted `npm run test:e2e` but the environment is missing the Playwright Chromium binary so the E2E run could not complete (Playwright install required); this is an environment limitation rather than a code failure. 

Notes: commits were made on the PR head branch `codex/push` and local tests/builds were performed, but pushing to the remote failed from this execution environment due to network restrictions (HTTP 403 on git push). No database migrations, RPC signatures, RLS rules, or service-role keys were changed.

author: samintisar
body:
## What

Design spec and implementation plan for hardening the CI/CD pipeline and adding post-deploy safety + observability. Docs only — no code or workflow changes in this PR.

- [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-cicd-deployment-observability-design.md`](https://github.com/samintisar/SolomindLM/blob/docs/cicd-deployment-observability-spec/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-cicd-deployment-observability-design.md) — approved design
- [`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-cicd-deployment-observability.md`](https://github.com/samintisar/SolomindLM/blob/docs/cicd-deployment-observability-spec/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-cicd-deployment-observability.md) — 30-task plan

## Scope

Five PR-sized phases, merge order `1 → 2 → 3 → 3.5 → 4`:

1. **CI correctness** — `Typecheck (Web)` job (currently web type errors reach `main` undetected), `actionlint`, loud E2E guard, fix `branch-protection.ps1` ghost check names, doc sync.
2. **CI performance** — composite setup action, bun + Playwright dependency caching, de-serialize `test-unit` from `lint`.
3. **Deployment safety** — Convex preview-deployment spike, E2E against the Vercel preview URL (`deployment_status`), post-deploy smoke check (root + `/api/health`), env-drift detection (weekly), rollback runbook.
4. **3.5 Observability** — `@sentry/react` for web, Convex error capture (Sentinel), Convex Log Stream → Axiom, external uptime monitor, deploy-notification webhook, observability runbook.
5. **Hardening** — Renovate (grouped weekly), CodeQL, baseline `bun audit`, `CODEOWNERS`, web coverage floor.

## Out of scope (per discussion)

Rolling releases / canary, staging environment, mobile app, `vercel.json` → `vercel.ts`, changing the "Vercel runs `convex deploy`" model.

## Notes

- Dashboard-only steps (GitHub settings, Vercel, Convex, Sentry, Axiom, uptime, Renovate app) are marked **[OPERATOR]** in the plan.
- Tasks 13/14 (per-PR Convex preview backends) are conditional on the Phase 3 spike outcome.

body:
## Summary

ADR-017 of the estate: every repository's `docs/` opens on the same fixed
spine (`01-architecture`, `02-developing`, `03-testing`, `04-operating` when
applicable, then the repository's own chapters). This repository had four
flat chapters (`01-workflows`, `02-composite-actions`, `03-wiring-a-repo`,
`04-secrets`) answering to no shape a reader could predict.

## Chapter moves

- `01-architecture.md` **absorbs** `01-workflows.md` and
  `02-composite-actions.md` — the five reusable workflows and the four
  composite actions they are built from are one catalogue, since the
  catalogue IS the shape.
- `02-developing.md` **new** — which file a change opens, what has to stay
  in step by hand (no compiler here to catch a drifted routing table or a
  duplicated `.artifacts` cache), and that no `actionlint` runs against
  this repository's own YAML today.
- `03-testing.md` **new**, and honest — nothing in `.github/` triggers on
  this repository's own push or pull request; the only rehearsal a change
  gets before every `@jterrazz` repository feels it is a consumer pinned
  to the branch.
- `04-operating.md` **new** — short, because this repository ships nothing
  of its own: merging here has no release and no deploy. See "Deviation"
  below for why it exists at all.
- `03-wiring-a-repo.md` → `05-wiring-a-repo.md`, `04-secrets.md` →
  `06-secrets.md`, via `git mv`; every inbound link (`README.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`, the `jterrazz-workflows` skill, the chapters themselves)
  follows.

`docs/decisions/` opens with the `_template.md` mold. No existing chapter
was a journal entry, so no ADR is cut from one — none added.

## Deviation from the plan

The row for this repository said "no `04-operating`", but the `docs-layout`
gate (`@jterrazz/typescript@9.2.0`, `src/docs.js:205-213`) reserves position
04 for the literal filename `04-operating.md` the instant a fifth chapter
claims number 05 — `docs-spine-name` refuses any other name at that
position, whatever the repository ships. Reaching `05`/`06` as the plan
asked for is only possible with a real (if short and honest) `04-operating.md`
in between, so that is what this PR carries instead of omitting it.

## Gate

Merging does not deploy: this repository ships no image, no
`.infrastructure/`, and its root carries no publishable package — nothing
here has a release of its own to redeploy on a docs-only commit.

This repository carries no `package.json` and no `Makefile`
(ADR-017 already names it as one of the five repositories with no local
gate to join), so the mechanical proof is a one-time run rather than a
wired CI step:

```
$ npx --yes @jterrazz/typescript@9.2.0 docs-layout .
EXIT: 0
```

## Test plan

author: maccoss
body:
The TIMS front-end study cost **55 hours** and now costs about **four**. Two changes — one arithmetic, one machinery — measured on a probe that is the shipped model with every phase duration scaled to a thousandth. The step size is set by the field and the mesh rather than by the window, so step *count* scales with duration and the solve is a one-off, which makes the probe a rate measurement rather than a shortened experiment.

| | 0.1% probe | implied full 18.3 ms run |
|---|---|---|
| as found | 199 s | 55 h |
| cycle mean in closed form | 26 s | 7.2 h |
| coefficient sweep across cores | **15 s** | **4.1 h** |

Cross-checked at 1%: 1,842 s measured against 1,990 predicted by scaling, and 1,420 ramp assemblies against 142 — exactly ten times. The answer moved **1.2e-15** across the whole of it, all from the closed form; the threading is bit-identical.

## The cycle mean

`DirectPotentialAt` evaluated the composite potential at sixteen instants **per density node, every step** — about half a million field evaluations per step here, each a superposition of bicubic interpolations.

It needs no sampling. A solved field's potential is `sum_k w_k(t) phi_k(x)` — linear in the weights, which is what basis superposition means — so its window mean is `sum_k mean(w_k) phi_k(x)`: **one evaluation per channel, no time sampling**, with `RfWaveform.Mean` already giving each weight's cycle mean in closed form. **7.7x.**

- **Guarded** on every drive completing a whole number of cycles in the window. That holds when every generator shares a frequency and fails when one is slower — and where it fails, the sampled average is itself only an approximation of the slower generator's mean. Falls back to the old loop, so the answer is unchanged either way.
- **It corrects a recorded claim.** The direct term needing "its sixteen samples whatever the ramp moves" is true of the composite and false of the parts.
- **An allocation came out of my own first version**: a `new double[]` per call on a path reached seven times per node per step, against CMP-1's "the inner loop allocates nothing". Bit-identical.

## Threading, and the half that was rejected

The coefficient sweep goes **5x**. The red–black Gauss–Seidel sweep goes **1.09x** — 12 s against 11 on the held probe, three runs each with no spread — so it was **not kept**.

`✶` The difference is legible rather than mysterious: bicubic superpositions are compute-bound and cache-resident, while a Gauss–Seidel cell is a few flops against several array touches plus an integer division and modulo per face. CLAUDE.md's warning that "a threaded smoother will disappoint" was right about the smoother and **wrong about the loop beside it**. The bandwidth ceiling is a property of a loop, not of a subsystem.

- Bit-identical however the rows are divided, because nothing is summed across nodes.
- The row body was moved out of its loop **verbatim**, and the parallel dispatch is its own method so the serial path allocates no closure it never uses — the 504-bytes-a-step finding avoided rather than repeated.

## Verified by forcing it

Setting the node threshold to **1** takes every diffusive test through the parallel path, so the Boltzmann equilibrium still has to hold to 8.9e-16, the ion ledger to 100.0000%, and the corpus drift tube to `L/(mu E)`. Chosen over a bespoke assertion because reaching both paths on one grid needs an `InternalsVisibleTo` this repository does not use anywhere.

**It found one defect, and not in the physics.** A test's `Counting` wrapper reported 8,337,733 field evaluations against a true 9,609,600, because `Fields++` is a read, an add and a write. **A test's own instrumentation is part of what must be thread-safe once the code it counts is.** `Interlocked` now.

It nearly hid: at the shipping threshold that test's grid is 561 nodes, below the cut, so it takes the serial path and passes. The defect existed only on a configuration nobody ships, and would have surfaced later looking like the well cache regressing.

## What is left

The **step count**: 56 ns a step where the diffusion limit alone allows 1.26e-4 s — a factor of 2,236, the drift limit binding — so the window is ~142,000 steps whatever the per-step cost. The implicit scheme gains against the *diffusion* limit and buys nothing there.

SPEC's new top item is the cost gate rather than the physics: `einzel estimate` says **8 s against 197,000**, four orders low, with the reason in its own prose basis line and not in the number a machine consumer reads. The estimate already measures its solve and flight rates with a runtime pilot; a probe of a few microseconds would return the real step.

Also: SPEC's cross-references now name the entry and carry **no number**. They have needed bumping twice today, because every top-insert renumbers the list.

## Verification

1,355 tests pass across twelve assemblies, in the shipping configuration and again with every diffusive test forced onto the parallel path.

author: plx
body:
## Summary

`DatabaseHealthProbe.check()` armed an outer `Promise.race` timeout while
`executeSelectOneInWorker()` armed a second, independent timer of the **same
duration**. Nothing enforced which fired first — it relied on the runtime's implicit
FIFO tie-break among equal-delay timers. If that assumption ever broke, `check()`
could settle via the outer timer while `pendingRequest` stayed set (cleared only by
the orphaned inner timer up to `timeoutMs` later), causing spurious "already running"
rejections on the next `check()`.

Collapse to a **single authoritative timeout**: `executeSelectOneInWorker()` no longer
arms any timer; `check()`'s timer is the sole owner and, on fire, calls the new
`abandonPendingWorkerRequest()` to synchronously null `pendingRequest`/`worker` and
fire-and-forget `terminate()` the abandoned worker. Cleanup is guaranteed by the one
timeout callback rather than by two timers racing, and there is no second timer to leak.
`daemon.ts` is unchanged — `check()`'s public `Promise<void>` contract is preserved.

Part of epic #6379.

## Linked Issue

Closes #6655

## Bug / Regression Context

- **Observed symptom:** two equal-duration timeouts race with no enforced ordering; if the non-FIFO order occurs, `pendingRequest` is left set and the next `check()` spuriously reports "already running", plus a leaked pending timer.
- **Repro:** a wedged probe worker + a Timer that fires the outer timeout before the inner one.

## Validation

- [x] `test/db/DatabaseHealthProbe.integration.test.ts` — added a `WedgedProbeWorker` and a `FakeTimer.fireNewestPendingTimeout()` seam to force the adversarial (non-FIFO) order; asserts `pendingRequest` cleared, zero leaked pending timers, and a follow-up `check()` succeeds. Red first: `getPendingTimeoutCount()` was 1 (leaked). 7 pass targeted; full `test/db` 1050 pass.
- [x] `bun run lint` — no new violations. `bun run typecheck` — no new errors.
- [x] `slack codex review` self-review: ran the targeted tests; verdict "timeout cleanup correctly resets the wedged worker state… no actionable regressions."

## Follow-ups

- None. `deviceTeardownOperationRepository` already behaves correctly and is unchanged.

## Description
Integrates an automated GitHub Pull Request code-review bot powered by OMNI/DeepWiki semantic analysis into the Contexto repository.

Key features:
- **Zero-Dependency Python Client (`scripts/deepwiki_query.py`)**: Communicates with OMNI API using stdlib `urllib.request` + `json`, with resilient polling, OPSEC reference scrubbing, and automatic carrier fallback routing.
- **Review Engine (`scripts/omni_pr_review.py`)**: Fetches PR diffs via GitHub REST API, discards non-code files (lockfiles, binaries, deleted files), enforces size bounds (`MAX_DIFF_SIZE`, `MAX_FILE_SIZE`, `MAX_FILES`), and categorizes findings into `CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`.
- **Deduplicated Commenting**: Scans for `<!-- omni-pr-review-bot -->` and updates existing PR comments via `PATCH` to eliminate comment spam on subsequent commits.
- **Strict Prompt Engineering (`prompts/pr_review.md`)**: Quarantines untrusted PR diffs (`<<<UNTRUSTED_PR_DIFF>>>`) against prompt injection, prioritizes correctness/security/performance/concurrency, and suppresses stylistic nits.
- **Least-Privilege GitHub Action (`.github/workflows/omni-pr-review.yml`)**: Uses minimal permissions (`contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`) and isolates untrusted fork code.
- **Comprehensive Unit Tests (`tests/test_omni_pr_review.py`)**: 23 unit tests covering diff filtering, bounding, injection defense, parsing, status logic, and carrier routing.

author: jgravelle
body:
## What was wrong

Two `git commit` calls today (72b8c6f4 and a30123ea on the #640 branch) went through with no fast-tier verdict: no `fast.md`, no warning line, nothing. Both were test-green on a manual rerun, which is luck, not a gate.

The mechanism, in `.claude/hooks/_common.run_budgeted`: `subprocess.run(timeout=)` kills the child at the deadline and then waits on the pipes. The child is `uv`; the grandchild is `python -m harness`, which still holds the pipes, so on Windows the hook waited for the whole harness (188 s on the first instance; that run's block was appended to `fast.md` after the hook was already dead). Past the 160 s backstop in `settings.json` the runner killed the hook. A killed hook is neither `ok()` nor `block()`, and the runner reads its silence as consent. FINDINGS W-42.

## The fix

One layer down, in the function every hook uses:

- `run_budgeted` runs the command under `Popen` and at the deadline kills the whole process tree (`taskkill /F /T` on Windows, the process group elsewhere), then returns `(None, "")` as before. The hook degrades under D7 instead of being killed.
- `pre_commit` writes `fast.md` BEFORE the run as a `NOT RUN` block carrying `HARNESS FAIL`. `harness --summary` appends its verdict beneath it (W-20) and `settle_summary` drops the block. A hook killed from outside now leaves a summary the checklist reads as unmet on rows 2 and 10, instead of leaving nothing.

- `pre_pr` reads `fast.md` directly, ahead of the checklist, and refuses when it is absent, still the pending block, or FAIL. A checklist generated before a killed pre_commit can still read 12/12, so the checklist alone was not the gate.

The kill path is bounded (`KILL_TIMEOUT` 5 s for the `taskkill`, `DRAIN_TIMEOUT` 3 s for the drain, a tree that outlives the kill written to stderr) and measured: the 3 s-budget arm takes 3.40 s under `--durations` (`evidence/durations.txt`), 8 s by construction. H1's backstop in `settings.json` moves from 160 s to 170 s over its 150 s budget, and a test binds it to `BUDGET_SECONDS + KILL_CEILING + 10` so it cannot drift under the budget again. Remedy (3) ships as absent / pending / FAIL, not the mtime-against-HEAD form: a PASS `fast.md` left by an earlier commit still passes H4, as it passes the checklist, and the FINDINGS row records that residual. DESIGN section 4's paragraph on the backstop says why `subprocess.run(timeout=)` was not enough.

## Reproduction

`tests/test_hook_budget_tree_kill.py`, four tests, and the `pre_pr` arms added to `test_workflow_hooks.py`. `red.txt`: 3 failed on main 068c086e, the timeout arm sitting through the grandchild's 30 s sleep on a 3 s budget. `green.txt`: 95 passed over the new file plus `test_workflow_hooks.py` and `test_workflows_registered.py`. The commit that carries the fix ran the rewritten hook live: the summary settled to a clean PASS block.

## Record

FINDINGS W-42 (FIXED, with the second instance); ARCHAEOLOGY row; DESIGN section 4. No CHANGELOG entry: workflows layer, as #632 (W-40). Label `no-changelog`.

## Checklist

| 6 | If a config key, env var or CLI subcommand was added: a row in `CONFIGURATION.md` or `CLI- | n.a. | config.py and cli/ untouched |
| 7 | If a new background, persistent or network behaviour was added: a README disclosure in "Ba | n.a. | no thread/socket/http/scheduled addition in the diff |

author: joshalbrecht
body:
`ParseAuthorizedEd25519Keys` called `ssh.ParseAuthorizedKey` and discarded the options it returned, then authorized every Ed25519 key it found. A line sshd would confine (`command="..."`, `restrict`, `from="..."`) or would not treat as a key at all (`cert-authority`) therefore got unrestricted root exec through the daemon, on both the VM (`/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`) and the in-container instance. No live impact today (slice provisioning writes plain keys), but a trap, and `cert-authority` is the sharp case now that the fleet trusts an SSH CA (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#850).

- Any line carrying options is skipped, never authorized. The whole set is deliberately **not** failed, so a restricted monitoring key next to the plain exec key cannot take the daemon down.
- The Ed25519 extraction moves into a shared helper; `ParsePublicKeyLine` (used for the request header and the host key) is unchanged in behavior.
- Tests cover each option form (`command=`, `restrict`, `from=`, `cert-authority`, comma-joined combinations, a quoted value with spaces) and a mixed file where only the plain key stays authorized.
- Spec and README note the rule. No wire-profile or vector change.

Follow-up from the mngr-internal gen-2 handoff (imbue-ai/mngr-internal#870); to be released as v0.2.2 and pinned in mngr-internal and default-workspace-template.

author: albinojimy
body:
## AOS-381 — revalidador e trust store selam no WORM único durável do nó

O revalidador de supply-chain e o trust store selavam num `audit.NewMemStore()` **volátil que nenhum leitor lia** — o sistema de tipos exigia audit mas não durabilidade, logo o código *parecia* auditado e não era (as decisões de revalidação e as mudanças do trust store evaporavam-se no restart). **Design WORM único** (decisão do dono). Política assinada e `AuditRecord`/`canonicalContent` intactos.

### As duas vias selam agora no WORM do nó
- **Via 1** (`referenceRevalidator`, por omissão): recebe o store por parâmetro e sela no `wormForChain` (o mesmo que vai para `SecuredConfig.WORM`).
- **Via 2** (opt-in `AOS_MODEL_TOOLS_REGISTER`): corria em `main.go` **antes** de o WORM existir → **movida para o `Bootstrap`** via `Config.SignedToolRegistry` (`parseSignedToolRegistryFromEnv` devolve os dados; o Bootstrap constrói o revalidador selado no `wormForChain`). Nenhuma via fabrica MemStore (AC1).
- `revalidation.New` ganha **`WithAudit`** (8ª opção, aditivo) + getter **`AuditStore()`** (AC5). `NewSecuredRuntime` recusa fail-closed (`ErrRevalidatorNotSealedToWORM`) um revalidador cujo destino ≠ `cfg.WORM`, comparado pelo **store base desembrulhado** (`wormBaseStore`) — porque com observabilidade o `cfg.WORM` é o decorador de tracing e a igualdade crua falharia.

### Achados da revisão adversarial (SHIP com SHOULDs) — fechados aqui
- `wormBaseStore` passa a ter **desembrulho limitado** (fail-safe contra ciclo/hang no arranque), com teste de terminação;
- a **invariante de segurança** do `Unwrap` («devolve o store onde o `Append` sela») está documentada como contrato;
- o erro deixou de afirmar «durável» — impõe **mesmidade** com o `cfg.WORM` (a durabilidade é ortogonal, garantida por `AOS_WORM_PATH` e declarada no banner);
- `WithAudit` ganhou teste dedicado (sobrepõe o posicional; `WithAudit(nil)` no-op).

### Banner, gate e registo
- `plataformaPostureBanner` declara selagem **DURÁVEL/VOLÁTIL** (molde de `modelAuditPostureBanner`).
- `scripts/ci/supplychain.sh` ganha um passo sobre o **nó composto** que prova que `registry.revalidation` **sobrevive ao processo** (reabre `FileStore` read-only) — falha se in-memory.
- `DEF-812`/`N-DEF-812` deixam de descrever a revalidação por chamada como «que CORRE» sem ressalva; `CHANGELOG` (AOS-051/054) qualificado + entrada AOS-381.
- Primeiro **teste-leitor** da cadeia no nó (`aos381_worm_unico_test.go`).

### Verificação
- `platform/registry`, `integration`, `cmd/aos` `go test -race` verdes; `build`, `layer-lint`, `deferrals`, `supplychain.sh` verdes; smoke `run-aos` **10/10**.
- **Não-vacuidade (AC4):** revertendo para `audit.NewMemStore()`, **388 casos** avermelham em `cmd/aos`.
- **AC2 por comando:** `aos audit-trail --path <worm> --run registry.revalidation` → `seq=1 allow`; `--run registry.truststore` idem.
- Nenhum critério deferido.

Ticks the first follow-up box of #70265: now that all nine backends ship `from_config` and have
been released, the legacy per-scheme `if/elif` chain in `airflow_local_settings.py` warns that it
is going away in Airflow 4.

## Why the warning is conditional

`_get_logging_config()` imports `airflow_local_settings` for its `DEFAULT_LOGGING_CONFIG` dict on
every stock deployment, so the chain runs even when ProvidersManager dispatch has already built the
real handler — it just builds a second handler that is discarded. Warning on execution alone would
therefore reach every operator, including those with nothing left to migrate.

So a branch warns only when provider dispatch cannot supersede it:

- the installed provider has no `from_config`, and so registers no scheme
  → *upgrade `<distribution>` to `<version>`*
- `[logging] remote_base_log_folder` carries no scheme to dispatch on
  → *set it to a `"<scheme>://"` URL*

The second case is not only Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, which are selected by `[elasticsearch] host`
rather than by a scheme (as discussed on #70265). A bare `wasb-logs` path also never dispatches,
because `urlsplit("wasb-logs").scheme` is empty. Both configurations work today and both would
break silently once the chain is removed, so both are told what to change. In each case the message
says to keep the existing backend options, since `from_config()` still reads them.

Provider versions are taken from the released changelogs and appear only in the message text. The
gate itself reads `from_config` off the already-imported class, so it costs nothing and cannot go
stale.

## Tests

24 cases across the nine backends: migrated (silent), provider too old (upgrade message),
un-dispatchable config (scheme message), plus `remote_logging = False`. The "stays silent" cases
are what pin the gate — they fail against an unconditional warning.

body:
## Summary

Harden the negative-test assertion without changing the production policy validator or weakening any gate. `expect_failure` now requires ordinary policy exit **1** and the expected invariant diagnostic; a crash, missing program, usage error, empty/wrong diagnostic, or successful validator can no longer count as negative-test success.

Seven self-tests exercise the assertion itself before the four existing repository mutations. The stub exists only inside that helper self-test's function-local scope; real repository tests continue calling the production validator. The existing all-occurrences `re.subn` fix on main is preserved. Append canonical `tmp/` and `temp/` ignore forms without removing earlier patterns.

## Scope and source history

Based on current main `88453e635aadeeee98646bb095412eab3d58776b`, not the stale base cached on PR #32. Inspection of #32's failed historical workflow found a repeated-phrase mutation problem, but fresh main already fixed that and merged the unique hardening content through #36. This PR does **not** recreate that fix or re-land #32. It fixes the still-present arbitrary-nonzero/incorrect-diagnostic false-pass behavior.

Changed paths: `tests/agent-policy-validator.sh`, `.gitignore`. No conflicts or history rewrites, no policy/protection/provider/billing/credential mutations.

## Validation

- `bash -n tests/agent-policy-validator.sh`: passed locally.
- Executed the exact assertion and self-test functions extracted from the edited script: **7 cases passed**.
- Running those self-tests against the old assertion failed on `wrong-diagnostic`, proving the previous false acceptance.
- Full repository validators were not run in the partial local source tree. **Exact-head hosted CI remains required; this PR starts draft.**

## Tracking

Closes #40. Related existing governance owner: DEN-629 (not reopening the broader completed rollout). A new issue in the exact Sonus Linear project was attempted but rejected at its free-issue limit. Specific plan and scope correction are tracked in https://linear.app/denman/project/githubcomsonus-auris-a557165528ef (pre-implementation comment `4a8dc704-6f3b-4014-b142-3f4b81c6ef8f`) and #40.

## Risk / roll-forward

A validator diagnostic change now intentionally requires updating its test expectation. This prevents unrelated errors from hiding a missing invariant. Preserve failing logs for diagnosis; do not disable the assertion to make CI green. No runtime application behavior changes.

author: tobibu
body:
Follow-up to the merged [#1](https://github.com/TobiBu/mimirax/pull/1). Thirteen commits that were pushed to `feat/m2m-module` after it merged, so they were never in an open PR and CI never ran on them — hence this one.

Report: [`reports/M2M_module.md`](https://github.com/TobiBu/edda-programme/blob/report/m2m-followup/reports/M2M_module.md) ([edda-programme#2](https://github.com/TobiBu/edda-programme/pull/2)).

## Two defects found by asking hard questions

**`minimize` fitted every leaf it was handed.** A fit given the `{"positions", "velocities", "weights"}` dict a rollout needs had **448 free parameters** for 64 particles instead of 64 — against ten observables — and moved the positions by 17 % and the velocities by 47 % while its docstring claimed to recover weights. Made-to-measure fits *weights*; the initial conditions are now opt-in via `also_fit`. **Every recovery and optimizer number in #1 was about a different, much larger problem, and all of them are re-measured here.**

**`minimize` did not accept "any optax rule".** `optax.lbfgs()` failed outright — a line-search rule's `update` needs `value`, `grad` and `value_fn`. Fixed, and it now reuses the rule's cached value/grad where it keeps one, because one recomputation per step is one extra rollout and backward pass.

## One mathematical correction to #1

**The objective is strictly convex in the weights, so the minimum is unique.** χ² is convex because the model is *linear* in them, `−μS` is convex, and the Hessian's smallest eigenvalue is ≥ `μ/max(w) > 0` by Weyl. Newton from four unrelated starts lands on the same point to **1.2e-15**.

So #1's claims that "the stationary set is 55-dimensional", that "the optimizer decides where in the flat valley the fit stops", and that a 0.173 weight gap "is the size of the valley" were **all wrong**. That spread was non-convergence in one anisotropic bowl (condition number 2.6e7), amplified by the over-parameterisation. Re-measured, everything that converges agrees:

| rule | distance to the minimum | weight error |
|---|---|---|
| classic force of change, ε = 3e-5 | **3.3e-08** | 0.2169 |
| `lbfgs()` × 500 | 6.1e-05 | 0.2169 |
| `adam`, every rate 0.01–0.5, ± schedules | 1.9e-02 … 2.8e-02 | 0.2195+ |

**LBFGS is the only rule that reaches the minimum on both constructions** — the classic update diverges on the self-consistent one, where SGD goes non-finite too.

## Gradient verification that isn't a finite difference

`force_of_change` calls `jax.grad` on the *same* objective `minimize` does, so it is **not** a gradient oracle. The real ones:

| oracle | measured |
|---|---|
| **Closed form, no autodiff anywhere** | **6.5e-16** on ‖g‖ = 7.68e+03 |
| **Forward vs reverse mode** (no step-size error, works on the production path) | **4.1e-16** / **4.4e-16** / **2.6e-16** |
| Remat invariance | `checkpoint=False` bit-identical; `checkpoint_substeps` to 8.8e-15 |

Two test dimensions turned out to be vacuous or unmeasured:

- **The `k_max = 1` tests never populated more than one rung.** A factor-3 spread in `|a|` is a factor 1.7 in `dt`, so every particle sat on rung 0 and the block schedule was never exercised — the same trap jaccpot names for an FMM with no far pairs. Now a log-spaced system with an asserted `{0: 7, 1: 6, 2: 3}` histogram.
- **The production `reassign_rungs=True` path was never measured.** It differs from the frozen-schedule gradient by however much the *schedules* differ: 7 % at one `dt`, 65 % at another, **nearly antiparallel** on a third. Neither is wrong; the production objective is only piecewise smooth, so an FD check on a frozen schedule does not license it.

## New capability

**`effective_parameters`** — `tr(H_data(H_data+H_prior)⁻¹)`, how many parameters the *data* determined. Returns **9.9999** on the tracer problem (64 weights, 10 observables) while χ² reaches 1.4e-08. So the objective cannot be made more informative by tuning μ or the optimizer; only by more observables.

**`FoldableObservable` + `FoldedRollout`** — a time average accumulated *inside* the integration, in checkpointed segments:

| `t` | stacked | folded, `balanced` | reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 6.8 MB | 1.2 MB | 5.8× |
| 1024 | **27.1 MB** | **1.5 MB** | **17.9×** |

A memory schedule, not an approximation: value and gradient agree with the stacked path to 1.1e-16 and 6.0e-16 over every divisor of a 24-step rollout and both averaging modes. Folding *alone* buys little — the segmenting is the win, and folding is what makes it possible.

**`DataResampling`** — Bovy, Kawata & Hunt's Algorithm 1 for weight uncertainties, verified against the theorem: the sample covariance converges to `(KᵀS⁻¹K)⁻¹` at the `1/√K` rate. Its two approximations are measured, and one becomes a rule: a prior makes it too narrow by roughly **`effective_parameters / d`**, so run that diagnostic first. Positivity bites only where it binds — where no draw wants a negative weight the transformed and untransformed samplers agree to *round-off*, because an argmin doesn't care which coordinates found it.

## One novelty claim narrowed

#1 said the orbit-response term is "the part no classic made-to-measure code computes". **Too strong** — Bovy et al. compute it for external-potential parameters by finite difference. What survives: they pay one integration per parameter and explicitly ignore self-gravity, so the `O(1)`-in-parameter-count cost is the claim, and it is what makes *self-consistent* M2M tractable. The term itself is measured at **68 %** of the gradient's norm and pinned by a test. Narrowed in the adapter docstring, README and concepts.

## Gate

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pytest` | **150 passed**, coverage **98.07 %** |
| `black` / `isort` / `flake8` / `pydoclint` / `pyright` | clean, 0 violations, 0 errors |
| Sphinx | exit 0, 1 pre-existing cosmetic warning |

GalIC (Yurin & Springel 2014) is recorded in `docs/concepts.md` as a parallel approach and deliberately **not** built — it adjusts velocities by stochastic hill-climbing, which `also_fit=("velocities",)` already expresses differentiably, but nothing here tests that.

Fourth cut. **Stacked on #306** (`refactor/std-003`); retarget to `main` once #306 merges.

The largest one so far. STD-010 was 3,020 words across ten sections and three kinds of content — obligations, lookup tables, and two irreversible acts with their own checklist. ADR-043 says those are three documents.

## The three files

| File | Shape | Body | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `STD-010-licensing.md` | standard, **`LIC-001..013`** | 522 | which licence, which direction, what may be depended on, how it is declared, provenance, generators, contributions |
| `STD-013-licence-allowlist-and-fields.md` | **register** (new) | — | the four-tier allowlist (§3), the per-format metadata field table (§5), the licence-text table (§10). Rows unchanged, plus the VRM CC0 overrides folded into the VRM row |
| `STD-014-publishing-gates.md` | standard, **`PUB-001..005`** (new) | 298 | the Arweave gate, the visibility gate, the four checks, birth-licence ≠ publication, legal-debt thresholds |

Every MUST of the old text has a plate. Mapped: §2 four questions → LIC-001/002; monorepo + dependency direction + floor rule + process boundary → LIC-003; separate repo for inherited copyleft → LIC-004; §3 allowlist + registry resolution → LIC-005; present-is-not-distributed → LIC-006; §5 files + language → LIC-007; one file one regime + pinned files → LIC-008; licence inside the file + VRM → LIC-009; §2.5 generators → LIC-010; §2.6 AI → LIC-011; §2.7 CC0 on media → LIC-012; §6 CLA/DCO → LIC-013; §4 → PUB-001..004; debt thresholds → PUB-005. `LIC-058..060` (core rules) are cited in the Check, not restated. §7 (the `CLAUDE.md` fragment) is gone: it said only "the block lives in CLAUDE.md, not here", which is true without a section.

Shape guard: STD-010 is **522 words against 500** (+4 %, SHOULD). Thirteen rules is the cost; the next cut removes one. STD-014 and STD-013 in shape.

Version 0.2.0 → 1.0.0 (draft stays draft; the section numbers are gone). Reading order updated: 010 → 014 → 013. No slug changed, no redirect.

author: octi35
body:
Cierra los objetivos **6** (recordatorios automáticos) y **7** (alertas ante pagos y cambios de estado) del pedido, más los entregables **8**, **15** y **16**.

## El punto de partida

El catálogo tenía **4 plantillas**, la tabla `notificaciones` existía desde la 0075 y **nadie podía verla**, y cuatro de las plantillas **no las disparaba nadie**. Una plantilla que existe y nunca se manda es peor que no tenerla: da la sensación de que el hotel avisa.

## Qué entra

**Catálogo: 4 → 21 eventos.** Seis son **internos** y no salen del sistema: aterrizan en la cartelera de `avisos` que el staff ya mira (migración **0086**). Mandarlos a una casilla del hotel obligaría a mantener destinatarios y se rompe el día que esa persona se va.

**Los cinco estados que pedía el prompt.** Faltaban `entregada` y `leida`, que son los únicos que puede informar el proveedor.
> ⚠️ **`enviada` NO es `entregada`.** El proveedor acepta el mensaje mucho antes de saber si el servidor del destinatario lo aceptó, y entre las dos está el rebote — el caso que el hotel de verdad necesita ver. Un huésped con la dirección mal cargada figuraba avisado.

**`/panel/notificaciones`** — el registro de envíos, con los cinco estados, búsqueda por destinatario, reintento de lo fallido y cancelación de lo pendiente. De solo lectura para todo lo demás: un registro que quien lo mira puede editar deja de ser un registro.

**Los 21 eventos se disparan solos**, enchufados en los flujos que ya existían: webhook de pagos y mostrador, cancelación, no-show, reprogramación, alta del portal, habitación inspeccionada, orden urgente, diferencia entre lo facturado y lo devengado por el canal.

**Cron nuevo `/api/cron/recordatorios`** (9:00 del hotel): llegada, saldo, salida, reserva por vencer y pedido de reseña.

**Webhook de entrega de correo** con firma Svix, la que usa Resend.

**WhatsApp por la Cloud API oficial**, no por un puente sobre WhatsApp Web: el número que Meta bloquearía es el del hotel, el publicado en su web y en Booking.

**`docs/despliegue.md`** — variables, puesta en producción y vuelta atrás.

## Lo que conviene mirar al revisar

1. **`avisos.rol`** (0086). Sin esa columna, la fila diría «recepcion» y la cartelera se la mostraría igual a housekeeping. Es **ruteo, no un secreto**: admin y gerencia siguen viendo todo, y los avisos escritos por una persona (`rol is null`) los sigue viendo todo el staff — la política está escrita para que las filas existentes no cambien de comportamiento.

2. **`lib/notificaciones/eventos.ts`.** `encolar` recibe un `Record<string, string|number>`, así que escribir `checkin` donde la plantilla dice `check_in` **no es un error**: el correo sale con `{{check_in}}` impreso adentro. `tests/eventos-de-aviso.test.ts` compara cada payload contra `PLANTILLAS` y falla nombrando el marcador que falta.

3. **`lib/notificaciones/cobros.ts` y `lib/reservas/cancelacion.ts`.** Los dos existen para no duplicar una regla de plata. Es la misma situación de `saldarSiCorresponde`: escrita dos veces, divergió, y el síntoma fue una reserva marcada «pagada» debiendo el frigobar.

4. **`esAvance`** en `lib/domain/entregas.ts`. Los eventos del webhook llegan **desordenados**: el de apertura puede entrar antes que el de entrega, y aplicarlos a ciegas haría retroceder de `leida` a `entregada`. Un rebote posterior sí pisa, porque eso es información nueva.

5. **El orden de los parámetros de WhatsApp.** Meta numera los huecos y valida la **cantidad**, no el significado: cruzarlos manda el código de reserva donde va la fecha y el mensaje sale igual. Hay un test que compara cada parámetro contra la plantilla del catálogo.

6. **`canalDelAviso` devuelve UN canal.** La clave de idempotencia no incluye el canal: duplicar chocaría contra el `unique` y una fila se descartaría en silencio. Y el canal se decide **al encolar**, no al despachar — si se recalculara, un aviso encolado como correo saldría por WhatsApp con un `destinatario` que es una dirección de mail.

## Lo que NO cierra esto

- **Las plantillas de WhatsApp las aprueba Meta**, con la cuenta del hotel. Fuera de la ventana de 24 horas no se puede mandar texto libre, así que los cuerpos del catálogo no sirven tal cual. Los pasos están en `docs/despliegue.md` §1.5.
- **El envío real de correo necesita `RESEND_API_KEY` y un dominio verificado.** El adapter está escrito desde antes; lo que faltaba era el webhook de entrega.
- **Nada de esto se probó contra un proveedor vivo.** Es la misma limitación que el resto del sistema: nunca corrió en producción.

## Verificación

`typecheck` 0 · `lint` 0 · `build` 0 · **1574 tests puros en verde**. Los tests contra base (canal interno, cinco estados, unicidad del id del proveedor) los corre el CI de este PR, que es el único lugar con Docker.

body:
## Objetivo

Entregar o inventário, a reconciliação e as provas da preservação dos oito worktrees de qualidade do EDUCA. Este ramo contém **88 arquivos de evidências/feedback**, não cópias do código das oito áreas: os commits do trabalho foram feitos nas pastas originais e enviados antes de qualquer PR.

## PRs de preservação para dev

| Área | Entradas preservadas | Arquivos no diff | PR |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| integration | 561 | 559 | https://github.com/shishiv/EDUCA/pull/211 |
| auth | 29 | 29 | https://github.com/shishiv/EDUCA/pull/212 |
| contracts | 25 | 25 | https://github.com/shishiv/EDUCA/pull/213 |
