| readmodels | 42 | 42 | https://github.com/shishiv/EDUCA/pull/216 |
| toolchain | 33 | 33 | https://github.com/shishiv/EDUCA/pull/217 |
| validation | 21 | 21 | Coberto pelo integration; ramo remoto `salvar/educa-quality-validation-20260908` |

Total: **801 entradas preservadas/reconciliadas**, correspondentes a **798 arquivos de diff entre os oito commits**, sem deduplicar sobreposições. Três entradas eram marcadores de caminhos já ausentes no disco e na base, sem bytes a commitar. Apenas 11 arquivos de índice `.pi/semantic-grep.sqlite*` foram excluídos e deixados intactos. Todos os `VENT.md` dos workers foram incluídos nos seus snapshots.

## Evidências deste ramo

Veja `artifacts/educa-quality-prs-dev/README.md`: status inicial/final das oito pastas, hashes SHA-256 e modos, HEADs, recibos de commits/pushes e confirmação de SHA remoto, comparação por arquivo, prova específica de cobertura de validation e logs dos checks. `VENT.md` registra a incompatibilidade do scaffold genérico com a autorização de preservação em múltiplos worktrees.

A verificação final confirmou zero alterações não preservadas. A API autenticada do GitHub confirmou URL, head/SHA, base `dev`, estado aberto/rascunho e corpo exato dos sete PRs de código. `dev` e `main` continuam nos mesmos SHAs; nenhum merge, fechamento, descarte ou remoção foi feito.

## Validação e pendências

- Integration: lint passou; testes passaram com `--maxWorkers=2 --no-file-parallelism`, 1316 testes aprovados e 20 ignorados.
- Integration: typecheck falhou em `app/tests/e2e/pilot/deployed-isolation.spec.ts:71:26` (`TS7006`, parâmetro `metric` implicitamente `any`). O snapshot foi preservado sem correções adicionais.
- Build, E2E, SQL e pilot não foram reexecutados. Não há afirmação de prontidão para merge/produção. Os workers não herdam os resultados de validação do integration.
- Os PRs de código são rascunhos; versões divergentes precisam de reconciliação manual, não de merge automático sobre o integration.
- Markdown/JSON autorais passam no `git diff --cached --check`. O check global aponta somente espaços finais/linhas vazias nos recibos brutos de push e logs, mantidos sem normalização para preservar a evidência.

Esta entrega direta cumpre a política de manter também a trilha de auditoria commitada e enviada no ramo `fm/educa-quality-prs-dev`.

author: n24q02m
body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced `new Date(string).getTime()` with `Date.parse(string)` when converting ISO 8601 strings to timestamps in `src/vendored/services/CalendarService.ts`. Also properly registered this modification as an intentional fork in the `NOTICE` file and `tests/sync-upstream.test.ts`.

🎯 **Why:** 
For performance-critical code or high-frequency inner loops (like sorting and resolving thousands of overlapping calendar busy-time intervals), instantiating a `Date` object merely to extract the underlying timestamp introduces unnecessary memory allocations and garbage collection pressure. `Date.parse()` skips object allocation and directly returns the integer timestamp.

📊 **Impact:** 
Eliminates intermediate Date object allocations when resolving overlapping busy blocks in calendar responses. Reduces overall GC pressure on long-running worker processes handling large calendar syncs.

🔬 **Measurement:** 
Run `bun run test tests/sync-upstream.test.ts` to ensure the upstream tracking contract is unbroken, and run the calendar test suite to ensure date parsing logic remains exactly the same. No regressions are expected since both methods use the same underlying V8 string parsing mechanism.

body:
## Summary
- fix #785 so page-content padding stays symmetric and scrollbar width is not mirrored into the opposite edge
- add a machine-readable cross-site UI behavior foundation contract for shared breakpoints, disabled states, touch targets, form fields, overflow tolerance, and responsive validation viewports
- formalize existing cross-site scroll/navigation, modal/Escape, empty/error-state, overflow, focus, and accessibility ownership instead of duplicating working runtimes
- add global reduced-motion handling at the semantic motion-token layer
- add a dedicated behavior-foundations validator to the normal Shared UI validation domain
- document all behavioral foundation contracts and their specialist exceptions

## Foundations covered
1. Responsive breakpoint foundation
2. Interaction-state foundation
3. Touch-target foundation
4. Form-field foundation
5. Scroll/navigation-state foundation
6. Modal interaction foundation
7. Empty / no-data / error-state foundation
8. Overflow-affordance foundation
9. Reduced-motion/accessibility foundation
10. Responsive validation matrix

## Page-padding contract
Page-content left/right padding is defined by the page gutter tokens only. The main scrollbar retains one stable inline-end gutter and is never mirrored onto the opposite side, so scrollbar width is not treated as page padding. The responsive matrix includes the same desktop viewport with and without a scrollbar to protect this contract.

## Ownership rule
Existing correct specialist behavior remains with its canonical owner. This PR promotes shared semantics into a documented and validated foundation rather than adding overrides, `!important`, duplicate global listeners, or page-specific compensation.

Closes #785

author: avsej
body:
Motivation
----------
CXXCBC-845 changed a bucket-scoped ping in the C++ core: it used to
report key/value alone, and now also pings the cluster-level HTTP
services (query, search, analytics, management, eventing, views) so
that bucket `wait_until_ready` considers them. `test_bucket_ping`
asserts the old contract, that the default bucket ping reports exactly
one service, so it fails as soon as those sessions are up. Every mock
job fails on it; a run that happens to ping before the cluster-level
sessions are established still sees key/value alone and passes, which
is why it reproduces only intermittently outside CI.

Modifications
-------------
The default bucket ping is asserted to report key/value and nothing
more is required of it, because which cluster-level services hold a
session at that moment is a matter of timing. The deterministic half of
the contract gets its own case: a bucket ping restricted to key/value
reports that service and no other, whether or not the HTTP sessions
have come up.

Results
-------
The diagnostics tests state the current core contract and no longer
turn on whether the cluster-level sessions have been established, so
they hold in both states. Checked against a mock run that pings before
those sessions exist and one that pings after.

author: valmonto-specbook[bot]
body:
## What was actually wrong

Four lyceo transfers failed with `no data for 120s after N bytes`, where N was the gzipped image size **byte for byte**:

| run | bytes at failure |
|---|---|
| 1 | 95,438,658 |
| 2 | 95,438,663 |
| 3 | 95,144,365 |
| 4 | **96,830,488** |

On the build server:

```
$ docker save lyceo_staging-api:6db32f6 | gzip -1 | wc -c
96830488
```

Every byte had crossed. The transfer completed and the watchdog killed it.

## Why

**Backpressure.** `srcStream.pipe(destStream)` honours it: when `docker load` cannot consume fast enough, Node **pauses the source**. No bytes are read, the counter stops advancing, and a healthy transfer becomes indistinguishable from a dead one.

An earlier attempt keyed a done-flag on the source's `'close'` event. That event never arrives while the source is paused, so the fix never fired — it shipped, and three more deploys failed behind it. `'end'` does not arrive either. Traced directly:

```
SRC_PAUSE
readableEnded=false
```

There is no event to hang this on. So the window simply has to exceed the destination's longest quiet stretch of work: **120s → 10 minutes**. `PIPE_MAX_MS` (45 min) remains the real ceiling for a link that is genuinely gone.

## Supporting changes

- **The transfer reports itself** — `transfer: 92.3 MB (3.1 MB/s)` every five seconds, into the deployment log. The byte counter always existed; nothing displayed it, so the blindest phase of a deploy was the one we had to diagnose from failure text after the fact.
- **A source `'close'` with no exit code is no longer a failure.** ssh2 may close a channel without one, and `undefined !== 0` would fail a transfer that worked.

## On the testing

The previous fix had a mutation-checked unit test on the stall predicate. The predicate was correct. It shipped broken anyway, because the trigger that sets its input never ran.

These tests drive `pipeOp`'s **real wiring** — fake ssh2 channels, real stream semantics, only the wall-clock timers faked (faking `nextTick`/`setImmediate` would stop the events under test from firing and the tests would pass for the wrong reason).

Mutation-checked: restoring `PIPE_STALL_MS = 120_000` fails the backpressure test; at 10 minutes all 17 ssh tests pass.

`DATABASE_URL=... pnpm verify` — exit 0.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ js-yaml (3.14.0 → 3.15.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml) · [Changelog](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 js-yaml: maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources

Summary

maxTotalMergeKeys does not count empty mappings. An attacker can repeatedly merge a large sequence of them and consume significant CPU without reaching the configured limit.

Example

arr: &arr [{}, {}, {}, ...] # N empty mappings
targets:
  - <<: *arr                # repeated K times

For every target, the loader iterates all N elements of arr. This results in O(N * K) work while totalMergeKeys remains unchanged.

PoC

import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'
import { load, YAML11_SCHEMA } from 'js-yaml'

const n = 20000

const src =
  'arr: &arr [' + '{},'.repeat(n).slice(0, -1) + ']\n' +
  'targets:\n' +
  '  - <<: *arr\n'.repeat(n)

const started = performance.now()

load(src, { schema: YAML11_SCHEMA })

console.log(`${(performance.now() - started).toFixed(1)} ms`)

Observed results:

N YAML size Time
800 ~13 KB ~20 ms
3200 ~50 KB ~180 ms
20000 ~500 KB ~13 s

Impact

An attacker can submit a relatively small YAML document that causes prolonged CPU consumption despite the default maxTotalMergeKeys limit.

Fix

Count each merge-source mapping as one budget unit, in addition to counting its keys.

Difference with v5

In v3 & v4, merge is enabled by default. So, the severity score is higher.

🚨 JS-YAML: Quadratic CPU consumption in !!omap resolution (3.x and 4.x) — CVE-2026-59870 fix not backported

Quadratic CPU consumption in !!omap resolution (js-yaml 3.x and 4.x)

Summary

resolveYamlOmap() enforces key uniqueness for !!omap sequences with a linear
scan (objectKeys.indexOf(...)) inside the per-element loop, making resolution
O(n²) in the number of entries. A modestly sized YAML document therefore
consumes disproportionate CPU inside yaml.load(), giving a denial of service
against any consumer that parses untrusted YAML.

!!omap is registered in the default schema
(lib/schema/default.js → require('../type/omap')), so a plain
yaml.load(untrustedInput) with no options is affected — no custom schema or
non-default configuration is required.

This is the same weakness as CVE-2026-59870 / GHSA-724g-mxrg-4qvm, which was
fixed in the 5.x line in 5.2.1. That fix was never backported: both currently
maintained legacy lines still carry the original implementation.

Affected versions

Line Latest tested Status
3.x 3.15.0 Affected — objectKeys.indexOf(pairKey) at lib/type/omap.js:29
4.x 4.3.0 Affected —

author: bpapillon
body:
Bumps `github.com/schematichq/schematic-datastream-ws` from v0.2.9 to v0.2.10.

v0.2.10 makes the datastream websocket client offer RFC 7692 permessage-deflate, which the Schematic API now negotiates, cutting the flags payload roughly 11x on the wire. It also stops the client mutating gorilla's package-level `websocket.DefaultDialer`.

The replicator is the largest beneficiary: it holds a long-lived datastream connection and receives full payloads continuously. No source changes — it consumes the client directly and has no dialer of its own.

author: mariusandra
body:
Bench findings from adopting a generic 2026.9.11 Buildroot card into a self-hosted backend (2026-09-08, `frame-2c2ea9` on a Pi Zero 2 W, through the Home Assistant add-on). The adoption itself worked — the row came up under the device's own name, its scene came with it, and the frame kept rendering. Four things after it did not.

### No logs reached the backend

The credential write-back reloads the runtime, but a reload updates the config in place while the logger thread keeps the `serverHost` it started with — empty on a standalone card. Nothing arrived until the frame was restarted by hand from its own admin panel.

Adoption now asks the runtime to restart as its last step (`POST /event/restart`, the control verb the device takes with the `serverApiKey` it was just given) and says so on the frame's log. A refused restart is reported there too, with what to do instead.

### "Unable to fetch image", and no scene snapshots

A fresh generic card is `private` with **no** web access key at all — nothing on the device mints one — so adoption kept the key `new_frame` minted and the device never saw it. Every backend `GET /image?k=` answered `401 Unauthorized`, and since a snapshot is only stored when an image fetch succeeds with a scene id, the scenes showed no covers either.

The write-back now hands a keyless card the backend's key, so both sides hold the same one.

### Restart / Reboot / Stop died with "No SSH private keys available for this frame."

Those tasks only knew two paths, SSH and the ESP32 action routes. Restart and reboot now go over the frame's admin API when the backend has no shell on it (`/event/restart`, `/event/reboot`; the reboot goes through the privileged door on a uid-990 card). Stop cannot work without a shell — the runtime cannot stop itself for good and systemd brings it back — so it logs why instead of failing on SSH keys.

### Every secret sat in "Pending changes" after a page load

The deploy baseline holds HMAC fingerprints rather than secrets, and the browser pairs them with the row's current fingerprints from its `GET`. But `FrameBase` never listed `secret_fingerprints` / `settings_fingerprints` (since #440), so the response model dropped both and every secret read as rotated — Frame access key, Frame admin auth, HTTPS proxy and Server API key pinned into Pending changes on a card with nothing to deploy.

### Also

The shell-less admin-login notice, and the ESP32 "set an admin password" one beside it, sat on a light amber box in dark mode. Both now use the amber dark variant the rest of the SPA uses.

## Bench doc

Setup portal round two, adopt #380 and the shell-less deploy drawer move to Done. What is left of them waits on the next release: the round-two re-check of all four fixes above, and "Update FrameOS" once a release newer than 2026.9.11 exists.

Verified on the bench and not changed here: the deploy drawer never offers a full deploy on such a card, "Check for updates" reports `debian-bookworm-arm64` correctly (a Buildroot card installs the *binary* artifact through its door; the rootfs is untouched), frame settings refuse a blank admin password with the switch disabled, and scenes push through the sync panel.

## Tests

`app/api/tests/test_frames.py` and `app/tasks/tests/test_restart_frame.py`: the post-adopt restart and its failure path, the keyless-card key push, the fingerprints on both `GET /api/frames/{id}` and the list, the shell-less restart/reboot/stop, a refused control event, and a Buildroot card that *does* carry SSH keys still taking the shell path.

Three changes to the docs site.

## ⌘K search area

The gradient behind the search input is gone, replaced with a flat, very dark green (`bg-emerald-950`). The magnifying glass, placeholder and `esc` button are lightened so they read against it, and the results list, footer bar and panel get dark variants.

## Footer

The emerald-to-sky gradient becomes a flat, fairly dark green (`bg-emerald-800`, `emerald-900` in dark mode) with light text.

## System / light / dark mode across the site

New to the site — there was no theme support before.

- `src/theme.tsx` holds the provider and the choice: `system`, `light` or `dark`, remembered in `localStorage` under `solandra.theme`.
- A small inline script in `_document` applies the stored choice to `<html>` before the first paint, so a reload never flashes the wrong theme. It also sets `color-scheme` so scrollbars and form controls match.
- While the choice is "system" the provider follows `prefers-color-scheme` live.
- Tailwind's `dark:` variant is pointed at the `dark` class (`@custom-variant` in `globals.css`) rather than the media query, so a pinned choice wins over the OS setting.
- `src/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx` is a three-way segmented control (screen / sun / moon), placed immediately to the left of the search button in the header and in the home page hero — the home page does not use `Header`, so it needs its own.
- Dark variants added across the site: header, docs contents and body, examples and export controls, tutorial cards, select controls, links and the command menu. Code blocks already render light on dark (`rehype-pretty-code` with a fixed dark theme) and are untouched.

## Checks

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm build` all pass. The e2e suite passes (4/4), including a new test covering picking a theme and it surviving a reload. `pnpm test` shows 561/561 unit tests passing; 3 test *files* fail to import in this sandbox because the `canvas` native binding was not built here — unrelated to this change.

author: joelteply
body:
A legacy core could save Persona working memory beneath its working directory while a new core loads the native user data directory. It could therefore start from an unrelated checkpoint. Existing load/read/schema errors could also become an empty-memory registration.

Add an explicit local `continuum checkpoint inspect/adopt` path that selects one complete legacy snapshot by declared Persona UUID and exact hashes, preserves selected/prior bytes, and records intent plus retry-verifiable receipt before and after replacement. No sequence/mtime merge or current-machine migration script. Adoption requires stopped legacy writers, checks one readable process snapshot, and rechecks offline state under the same per-Persona OS lock used by loading and saving.

Resident registration is now fallible: only a missing checkpoint permits fresh memory; lock/read/schema failures preserve an existing resident and surface a typed supervisor slot error. Ephemeral evaluation remains independent of resident files. Ordinary checkpoint saves flush bytes before replacement and synchronize parent directories on Unix.

The CLI protects both Persona stores from inspection-plan writes, rejects ambiguous process evidence, and refreshes executable paths without broadening core termination to parent-directory name matches. Recovery documentation describes the operator contract and limitations.

Validation:

- At b4e006019, three independent source reviews, rustfmt, git diff --check, and a clean merge-tree against canary 8c088d283 passed. [CI run 34286768088](https://github.com/CambrianTech/continuum/actions/runs/34286768088) passed 7,847 library tests, two compile-fail doctests, Windows library/test-harness checks, and binding checks. The native Windows library plus real CLI harness passed 20 tests at that head.
- Combined native Clippy on companion #3927 at 64703cedc exited 0 but emitted 1,356 warnings against a 1,351-warning baseline. The introduced warnings prevented a clean validation receipt.
- Current head 9d3fe8096 fixes the checkpoint-adoption nonminimal_bool and CLI items_after_test_module findings. Its [CI run 34296170337](https://github.com/CambrianTech/continuum/actions/runs/34296170337) passed 7,847 library tests (0 failed), both compile-fail doctests, Windows library/test-harness checks, and binding checks. Companion #3927 also checks its ignored test registration Result. These three mechanical corrections were source reviewed; no post-fix native Clippy run is claimed or required for readiness. Fresh CI has now passed at this head and companion #3927 head 7dd3bfffb.

Regressions exercise actual files, owner lock contention, changed source/destination, interrupted receipt completion, failed resident replacement, actual supervisor sibling isolation, CLI preconditions, and process classification. The reviewed corrected head has passed its executable CI checks.

Limits: the legacy payload has no embedded identity/lifetime; its UUID is explicitly declared, and every receipt says legacy_final_flush_acknowledged=false. Old binaries cannot retroactively honor the file lock or produce a final-flush acknowledgement. Both inputs must decode; corrupt native destinations remain untouched and are not repaired by this command. Windows receipts do not promise directory-journal persistence across power loss. No runtime adoption or restart performed.

author: biomatix
body:
Two BLOCKER defects in `gl.sample()`, both silent:

1. **Any population with exactly one member was dropped from the sample and its slots filled with unrelated individuals** drawn from elsewhere in the object. `sample(v, n)` treats a length-1 `v` as the range `1:v`, so a single-member population's index became a range to draw from. The returned individual count was always correct, which is why nothing signalled the substitution. On `testset.gl` this hit every call, the default call included, because the two singleton populations set the default `nsample` to 1. Over 20 consecutive runs those populations appeared zero times, so any bootstrap over a dataset with a rare population produced replicates that never contained it and were quietly enriched for others.

2. **The returned object lost all its metadata.** The result was assembled with `do.call(rbind, ...)`, whose SNPbin fallback discards the whole `@other` list, so `loc.metrics`, `ind.metrics`, `latlon`, `loc.metrics.flags` and `history` all came back `NULL`. `gl.filter.callrate()` on a `gl.sample()` result failed with "incorrect number of dimensions". `gl.compliance.check()` was the documented workaround and could not recover more than an `id` column of `ind.metrics`, so coordinates and sex assignments were gone for good.

## What changed

- Draw from each population's own index vector with `idx[sample.int(length(idx), nsample, replace)]`, and rename the lambda parameter so it no longer shadows the genlight `x` (F1, F13).
- Replace the split/rbind assembly with a positive-index subset, which restores `@other` on the SNPbin path, aligns the SNPbin and FBM paths, and puts returned rows in draw order (F2, F3, F10).
- Set every entry of `@other$loc.metrics.flags` to FALSE, because resampling individuals invalidates every locus metric computed across individuals (F4).
- Append `match.call()` to `@other$history` on the return path (F5).
- Write the new `indNames` through to `@other$ind.metrics$id` (F6).
- Validate `nsample` as a positive whole number, and when `replace = FALSE` check it against the smallest population and name that population in the error (F7).
- Add the FS9 completion message and a `verbose >= 2` line reporting the draw (F8).
- Resolve the default `nsample` deliberately instead of through a lazy promise, and document that `nsample` is per-population under `onepop = FALSE` and a whole-object total under `onepop = TRUE` (F9).
- Rewrite the roxygen block to DOC1 order with a single `@details` and a single `@family`, DOC2 verbose text, `[default ...]` on every parameter, DOC7 `@author` structure, and a `@return` that matches the code. Drop the `gl.compliance.check()` workaround from `@examples` (F11, F14).
- Drop the stale `build = "Jody"` argument and the commented-out metadata-removal block (F12, F13).

## Evidence

Characterization suite `tests/testthat/test-gl.sample.R`: an 80-assertion baseline captured at `ddaed27`, rewritten to 186 assertions, all passing. Every changed assertion carries a `# [approved Fn]` marker, so a diff outside those lines is a regression.

**F1**, on `testset.gl` (singleton populations `EmmacNormLeic` and `EmmacNormSalt`):

```
# before
set.seed(42); out <- gl.sample(testset.gl, nsample = 3, replace = TRUE)
#> 90 individuals, 28 of 30 populations, both singletons absent,
#> five unrelated populations over-represented at 4 or 5
# after
#> 90 individuals, 30 of 30 populations, every population at exactly 3
```

Across seeds 1-20 every population appears at its requested count and each singleton population returns its own member three times, never a stranger. The default call returns 30 individuals, one per population.

**F2**, on `platypus.gl`, `set.seed(1), nsample = 4, replace = TRUE`:

```
# before
gl.filter.callrate(out, threshold = 0.5, plot.display = FALSE, verbose = 0)
#> Error: incorrect number of dimensions
# after
#> dartR object, 12 individuals x 953 loci (from 1000)
```

`ind.metrics` returns 12 rows by 17 columns, the input's full width, and every non-`id` column equals the input row for the drawn individual. Repeated with `nsample = 20, onepop = TRUE` (3 duplicated draws): metadata rows repeat with the duplicated individuals, and the zero-padded ordinal prefix keeps `indNames` unique, so no duplicate-name desync is introduced.

**F3**: the same call and seed under `options(dartR_fbm = FALSE)` and `options(dartR_fbm = TRUE)` now agree on `names(@other)`, `nInd`, `nLoc`, the dimensions of `ind.metrics`, `loc.metrics` and `latlon`, every flag, history length, `indNames`, `pop`, `ploidy` and `ind.metrics$id`, with equal genotypes.

**F4**: on FBM-backed `testset.gl` the input carries `CallRate == TRUE`. After sampling, the stored `CallRate` disagrees with the truth for 248 of 255 loci (maximum absolute difference 0.9855) and the flag now reads FALSE, so `gl.filter.callrate` recalculates and keeps 227 of 255 loci instead of filtering on the original object's numbers.

**F5**: history goes from 4 entries to 5 on the SNPbin path and 1 to 2 on the FBM path, exactly one entry per call.

**F7**: `nsample = 2.7` and `0.5` stop with "nsample must be a whole number, it is a count of individuals and not a proportion"; `0` and `-1` with "nsample must be 1 or more"; `nsample = 25, replace = FALSE` with "nsample (25) exceeds the size of the smallest population, SEVERN_BELOW with 17 individuals".

**Genotype fidelity**: `as.matrix(out)` is identical to `as.matrix(x)[samps, ]` for every case tested, on both paths, with and without duplicates. The adegenet SNPbin duplicate-index hazard is still not triggered, and the negative control that proves it is pinned: `testset.gl[c(5,5,5,7,7,9), ]` gives 219 NA expected and 219 observed with zero cell mismatches, and end to end `gl.sample(testset.gl, nsample = 5, replace = TRUE)` at `set.seed(1234)` gives 5249 NA against 5249 expected from its source rows.

**Verbosity**: `verbose = 0` emits zero lines. `verbose = 1` emits Starting and Completed only; `verbose = 2, 3, 5` add the draw report.

**Skipped**: `R CMD check` and the full package suite were not run. The change is confined to `R/gl.sample.r`, `man/gl.sample.Rd`, `NEWS.md` and `tests/testthat/test-gl.sample.R`.

## API impact

Results change for any object containing a population with exactly one member: such populations now appear in the output instead of being replaced by unrelated individuals, so seeded output changes for those datasets. On `testset.gl` this includes the default call.

The returned object now carries `loc.metrics`, `ind.metrics`, `latlon`, `loc.metrics.flags` and `history`, which callers previously had to rebuild with `gl.compliance.check()`. All metric flags are FALSE, so downstream report and filter functions recalculate rather than trusting stored values, and their numerical output changes accordingly. Row order now follows draw order whether or not `nsample * nPop` exceeds `nInd(x)`.

`nsample = 2.7` errors instead of silently truncating to 2. The signature default moves from `min(table(pop(x)))` to `NULL`, resolved in the body; the sample sizes both settings produce are unchanged.

Recorded in `NEWS.md`. Caller grep across all eight `dartR.*` clones plus `dartR.data`: no call site to `gl.sample()` outside its own `@examples`; the only references are `@seealso` cross-links in `man/*.Rd`, which the signature change does not touch.

## Review

Report: [`function-review/reports/dartR.base/gl.sample.md`](https://github.com/green-striped-gecko/dartR.base/blob/dev/function-review/reports/dartR.base/gl.sample.md)

14 findings; all 14 approved by Arthur Georges on 2026-09-09; none rejected, none deferred.

One item for a separate review, discovered while applying this change and left in the function that owns it: the dartR `[` method cannot return more individuals than the object holds, because it assigns ploidy through the accessor after `@ind.names` has been replaced (`R/utils.dartR.class.def.r`, both the SNPbin and FBM branches). `platypus.gl[c(1:8

author: edersonangelo
body:
### What changes

The actions menu now fits on the page, and the reason is asked for in a dialog
built like the one the panel already has.

### Why

It shipped broken. The menu was anchored to the right of a trigger sitting at
the left edge, so a wide panel opened off the side of the screen: text cut off,
overlapping the table, unusable. It was never rendered before being called done
— the markup was checked with `grep`, which cannot see a layout.

What was wrong, and what each fix is:

- **The trigger belongs in the toolbar.** It sat on a line of its own below the
  filters. It is now the last control in that row, right-aligned.
- **A menu hangs from the side its trigger sits on.** Right-aligned trigger,
  right-anchored panel. Anchored the other way it runs off the page, which is
  the mirror of the original defect and something I reproduced on the way here.
- **The item is a label, not a sentence.** `Deliver anyway…`, and opening the
  dialog closes the menu instead of leaving two layers open.
- **The dialog is the one this panel already uses.** There was a `<dialog>` in
  the layout — the event detail — with its own head, body, border and backdrop.
  A generic `dialog { … }` rule fought it and lost, which is why the box
  stretched to fit its own paragraph on one line. The new one is scoped to its
  id and follows the same anatomy.

### How it was verified

`make ci`, and by rendering the page and looking at it: the menu open, and the
dialog opened with `showModal()` rather than the `open` attribute, which renders
non-modal and would have shown something the browser never displays. Both at
1920 wide, where the earlier version broke.

author: nsta1
body:
Refs #2208

## What this is

The file arm re-selects and re-embeds the same closed pool of files on every
pass, indefinitely. This gives it the cross-pass backoff the symbol arm already
has, and closes the hole that backoff would otherwise open in the wave's
acceptance tests.

## The diagnosis, established by measurement

#2208 offered two readings of "a zero-change pass still embeds ~43 files":

- **(a)** the same files are re-embedded every pass;
- **(b)** ~43 genuinely-missing vectors are lost and repaired each pass, at equilibrium.

Measured against the live `repocontextcontainer-repocontext-1` container, from
the per-pass gap-set-shape lines: the **rolling union stayed flat at 53 across
passes 5-17 while `entered` summed to 38**, so 38 files entered the selection
without the union growing at all - zero novel files. That is **(a)**, and it is
a computation on real data rather than a reading of the code. The union counter
is exact over this range (`MaxUnionTracked = 200_000`, saturation suffix
absent), and exact set digests repeat at non-adjacent passes.

Two candidate causes were **refuted**, both of which I had reason to want to be
true:

- **#2277** (access-gate-pruned key indistinguishable from an absent marker) is
  not the mechanism. A pure predicate on an invariant key string cannot produce
  files *entering* **and** *leaving* the selection, which the logs show; and the
  container carries no auth/tenant/membership configuration to exercise the gate
  at all. Its latent disposition is unchanged.
- **#2276/#2281** (build output can never converge) is not the mechanism. Of 50
  pool paths recovered from failed-batch log lines, `git check-ignore` reports
  **49 tracked-not-ignored, 1 ignored, 0 missing**, and the denominator agrees:
  the container walked **8,163** files against **8,100** non-ignored today, a
  0.8% gap. (Both are pre-#2281 figures and must not be compared forward.)

The actual signal is the one the arm was already measuring and throwing away:
**341 of 364 files (93.7%)** that a pass embedded *and recorded* were selected
again by the next pass. That is the symbol arm's re-embed-loop signature from
#2071/#2078 - a membership write that returns success but is not observable on
the next pass, because the tree is past its WAL replay budget (warm leaf replays
on `repo-context-vector-membership` grew from 1 to **59,429 in 6h52m** on an
idle box). The symbol arm gained a backoff for this. The file arm never did.

## The change

`LogGapDiagnosticsAsync` already computed the majority-repeat verdict, logged
it, and returned `void`. It now returns it, and a majority-repeat is folded into
the same backoff a saturated pass feeds. Both of the symbol arm's non-obvious
design properties carry across, because without them a backoff is a cover-up:

1. **A skipped pass does not clear the budget** - it never touched the plane hard
   enough to find out whether anything recovered. Mirrors the symbol arm's
   `if (!skippedGapScan && ...TryRemove(...))`.
2. **A skipped pass does not overwrite the last-landed record**, or the evidence
   of the loop is erased by the backoff that detected it. On the file arm this
   holds **structurally rather than by an explicit guard**: `_previousLanded` is
   written only inside `FileGapHistory.Observe`, which is reached only when
   `gapSelectedFiles.Count > 0`, and a skipped pass always leaves that empty. A
   reviewer looking for the symbol arm's `if (!skipGapScan)` guard will not find
   one; this is why.
3. Entering backoff logs a **warning**, clearing logs an info, so a skip is never
   silent in the field.

No new metric instrument, so the `lattice.dashboards` drift guard is not
implicated.

## The part that matters most: this change could have made the existing tests vacuous

Once the arm can skip, **`GapsSelected == 0` stops discriminating**. It is
satisfied both by "scanned and genuinely found nothing" and by "never scanned
because backoff was engaged" - so a future regression could be fully masked with
`A_second_quiet_pass_over_a_multi_batch_corpus_embeds_nothing` and
`A_third_quiet_pass_stays_converged` still green. Those tests are green today
**while the deployment does not converge**, so this is not hypothetical.

Three layers close it:

- `RepoFileVectorIngestOutcome.Converged` now also excludes a skipped pass, for
  the reason it already excluded a deferred one: *a pass can reach zero selected
  gaps by giving up before it looked*. Same rule, second instance.
- Both acceptance tests now additionally assert `GapScanSkipped` is false **and**
  that the outstanding skip budget is zero, with failure messages saying why
  `GapsSelected == 0` is no longer sufficient on its own.
- The new fixture **exhibits** the ambiguous state rather than arguing about it:
  a pass reports `GapsSelected == 0` over a corpus in which *nothing* is covered,
  and a third pass is the denominator - it runs the scan over identical input and
  selects all 128 files, proving the zero was the skip.

Every new guard asserts on its denominator, so it cannot go vacuous, and the
failure messages tell a future reader to fix the setup rather than lower the
floor.

## Which log line an operator reads

To distinguish "quiet because converged" from "quiet because backed off":

```
Repo {RepoId}: back-fill gap set shape not measured this pass: {Reason} ... gapScanSkipped={Skipped}
```

The reason clause is now three-way and mutually exclusive - probe failed / the
back-fill was **SKIPPED under the file-arm backoff** ("This is NOT convergence")
/ the probe succeeded and selected no gap files ("This IS convergence"). Entering
backoff additionally logs the warning *"the membership writes are not becoming
observable ... standing the gap back-fill down"*, and clearing logs an info.

## Verification

- Package suite: **2176 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** (non-chaos, non-emulator).
- Hygiene gates: **30 passed** (run after committing, so the new file is tracked
  and actually enumerated).
- **Mutation-tested**, each mutation applied and rebuilt in isolation:
  - drop `!GapScanSkipped` from `Converged` -> caught by exactly the property
    test and the core backoff test;
  - remove the `!skippedGapScan` budget guard -> caught by exactly
    `A_skipped_pass_does_not_clear_the_budget_it_was_granted_by`;
  - force `ClaimFileGapScanSkip` to return false -> caught by exactly the three
    backoff tests.

## What this does not claim

This makes the arm **stop making the problem worse** and stop reporting a skip as
convergence. It does not fix the underlying membership-tree replay-budget
saturation, which is the core-API issue the durability signal points at. Scoped
to the file arm of this ingestor.

body:
The Feynman Technique as a skill: explain a concept in plain language, find where the explanation went hand-wavy, fill those gaps, then rewrite it. Four steps with a structured output — a gap table, a jargon self-check, a refined explanation, and a 30-second version.

**Body cloned verbatim** from [neurofoo/agent-skills · feynman/SKILL.md](https://github.com/neurofoo/agent-skills/blob/main/feynman/SKILL.md) (MIT). Upstream `LICENSE.txt` copied to `skills/feynman/LICENSE`.

## Two deviations, both about packaging rather than content

**1. `$ARGUMENTS` removed from the end.**

That placeholder belongs to the Claude Code / claude-plugins templating. Lino's `buildSkillTurn` substitutes nothing — it appends the request *after* the skill block:

```js
...skills.flatMap((skill) => [renderSkillBody(skill), '']),
asked || SKILL_FALLBACK_REQUEST,
```

So it would have reached the model as seven literal characters. ⚠️ Worth knowing for anything else vendored from that ecosystem — Anthropic's own `eli5` has the same line.

**2. Frontmatter replaced with this repo's convention.**

`name` equal to the folder id, plus the required `trigger` / `author` / `version`, and `source` / `submitted_by` for provenance — the same shape `frontend-slides` uses. Upstream's `user-invocable: true` is dropped; nothing here reads it.

## Why this and not an ELI5 skill

Considered [anthropics/claude-plugins-community · eli5](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-community/blob/main/eli5/skills/eli5/SKILL.md) and [guicortei/feynman-technique](https://github.com/guicortei/feynman-technique) first. The Anthropic one is a single line and asks for an HTML artifact, which Lino has no target for. guicortei's is a bigger prescriptive template. This one is plain Markdown, self-contained, and its structure is the point rather than a rendering target.

⚠️ **Note it is a deep-dive, not a quick gloss.** Pressing *Explain* on a highlighted sentence should not run this — the four-step output with two tables is right for `/feynman <concept>` and wrong for a one-line question. The card bubble's Explain button is unchanged.

author: marwan116
body:
## Description

A retryable read error partway through a file silently drops data. No exception, exit code 0.

### Repro

A datasource that yields one block per 1 KiB of an 8 KiB file, with one transient error injected after the third read:

```python
class FlakyStream:
    fired = False

    def __init__(self, f):
        self._f, self._reads = f, 0

    def read(self, n=-1):
        self._reads += 1
        if not FlakyStream.fired and self._reads > 3:
            FlakyStream.fired = True
            raise OSError(DEFAULT_RETRIED_IO_ERRORS[0])   # transient network error
        return self._f.read(n)


class ChunkedDatasource(FileBasedDatasource):
    def _open_input_source(self, filesystem, path, **kw):
        return FlakyStream(super()._open_input_source(filesystem, path, **kw))

    def _read_stream(self, f, path):
        while (data := f.read(1024)):
            builder = DelegatingBlockBuilder()
            builder.add({"data": data})
            yield builder.build()
```

### Expected vs current

|                  | expected | current    | this PR |
| ---------------- | -------- | ---------- | ------- |
| blocks delivered | 8        | **5**      | 8       |
| bytes delivered  | 8192     | **5120**   | 8192    |
| data correct     | yes      | **no**     | yes     |
| error raised     | no       | no         | no      |

Current behavior loses 3072 bytes, 37.5% of the file, and the read reports success.

### Cause

`read_files` opens the file once, then passes a closure over that handle to `iterate_with_retry`:

```python
with RetryingContextManager(self._open_input_source(fs, read_path, ...)) as f:
    for block in iterate_with_retry(lambda: self._read_stream(f, read_path), ...):
```

`iterate_with_retry` recreates the iterable on a retryable error and skips the items the failed attempt already yielded, so the factory must replay the same sequence from the start. This one does not: it reuses the advanced handle, so attempt 2 resumes from wherever attempt 1 stopped, and the skip then discards real data instead of duplicates.

In the repro: attempt 1 yields 3 blocks and fails, attempt 2 resumes at byte 3072 and yields the remaining 5, and the first 3 of those are dropped as "already yielded". 3 + 2 = 5.

### Which formats are affected

Silent loss, cut at a record boundary with one injected error at ~50%:

| API                                 | current behavior                              |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `read_text`                         | silent, 1944 / 4000 rows                      |
| `read_binary_files`                 | silent, payload 32768 / 65536 bytes           |
| `read_csv` with `column_names`      | silent, 1501 / 4000 rows                      |
| `read_json` (Arrow)                 | silent, 1961 / 4000 rows                      |
| `read_csv` with inferred header     | raises `ValueError: ...check the CSV file has correct format` |
| `read_numpy`                        | raises `ValueError: contains pickled (object) data` |
| `read_json` (pandas JSONL)          | unaffected                                    |

All are correct after the fix. Whether CSV fails loudly is luck: Arrow takes the first surviving line as a header, which usually fails to parse. Supply `column_names` and the loss goes quiet.

Pandas JSONL escapes because #63233 added `f.seek(0)` to `_estimate_chunksize` in May 2026, which fixed an `AssertionError` there and incidentally restored replay-from-start for that one path. The general problem was not addressed.

Parquet is unaffected: it is not a `FileBasedDatasource`, and its read factory closes over a stateless fragment.

### Fix

Open the file inside the retry factory, with the `with` scoped inside a generator so each attempt's handle is closed as soon as that attempt ends, on both the success and the exception path:

```python
def open_and_read_stream() -> Iterator[Block]:
    with RetryingContextManager(
        self._open_input_source(fs, read_path, **open_stream_args),
        context=self._data_context,
    ) as f:
        yield from self._read_stream(f, read_path)

for block in iterate_with_retry(open_and_read_stream, ...):
```

Measured max 1 handle open at a time across a retry, with all handles closed on the clean, retried, and abandoned-midway paths.

Alternatives considered:

- **Rewind when the handle is seekable.** `_open_input_source` returns `open_input_stream`, whose `seekable()` is `False` even on a local filesystem. This would fix only ORC and uncompressed JSON and leave everything else failing silently.
- **`ExitStack` around the loop.** Correct, but a failed attempt's handle stays open for the remainder of that file's read, up to 10 at once.

Also documents the replay-from-start requirement on `iterate_with_retry`, and corrects two comments in `json_datasource.py` that asserted retries reuse the same handle.

### Behavior change worth noting

The open now sits inside `iterate_with_retry`, and the open path already retries at two levels (`RetryingPyFileSystem.open_input_file` and `RetryingContextManager.__enter__`, 10 attempts each). These multiply, so a persistently retryable open can now take roughly 10x as many attempts before giving up, with exponential backoff capped at 32s per attempt. Bounded, and only in a case that was already failing.

Retries are also more expensive by design: attempt 2 re-parses the blocks it will discard. Resuming was cheaper, and wrong.

## Related issues

None open. Searched open PRs and issues for `iterate_with_retry`, `file_based_datasource retry`, `_read_stream retry`, and `RetryingContextManager`. #63233 is merged and narrower, covering only the pandas JSONL chunksize path.

## Additional information

**Known follow-up, deliberately not in this PR.** `webdataset_datasource.py:439` wraps `_tar_file_iterator` in its own `iterate_with_retry` whose factory closes over the stream it was handed. That inner retry catches the error before the outer one can reopen, so a transient error there becomes `tarfile.ReadError: invalid header`, identically before and after this change. No regression, but it needs a separate fix. Removing a retry layer seemed like a maintainer's call.

**Tests.**

```
pytest python/ray/data/tests/datasource/test_file_based_datasource.py
  -> 32 passed, 3 skipped
```

New regression test `test_flaky_read_stream_retry_does_not_drop_data`: delivers 5 of 8 blocks on master, 8 of 8 with this change.

Wider run across the Data file-format suites (`test_text`, `test_csv`, `test_json`, `test_binary`, `test_image`, `test_avro`, `test_webdataset`, `test_numpy`, `test_parquet`), per file: 226 passed, 21 skipped, 30 failed. Set-differenced against the same run with this change reverted: zero new failures, one fixed. All 30 failures are missing optional imports in this environment (tensorflow x22, torch x4, decord x4) and fail identically on master.

`pre-commit run` is clean on the changed files.

**AI assistance was used** for this change: to build the repro, implement the fix, and write the tests and this description.

author: bruce1508
body:
Closes the last carried-forward item: the `use_alter` foreign-key drift that
`537d54fe5104` recorded but deliberately left unfixed.

## The defect

`db/models.py` declares two foreign keys with `use_alter=True` to break the circular
reference between `model_runs` and `taxonomy_versions`. The baseline revision
`70c5a19c093f` wrote each one inline in its own `op.create_table` call.

SQLAlchemy's `CreateTable` compiler **omits** any constraint marked `use_alter=True` —
it expects a follow-up `ADD CONSTRAINT` that only `create_all` schedules. `op.create_table`
never emits one. Both constraints were discarded at `CREATE TABLE` time and have never
existed in any database built from this chain.

The ORM promised referential integrity that the database was not enforcing.

## What changed

- `db/models.py` — both `ForeignKey`s gain an explicit `name`. Without a name,
  autogenerate emits `create_foreign_key(None, ...)`, whose paired
  `drop_constraint(None, ...)` can never drop anything, which is why the generated fix
  was unusable and had to be stripped by hand on every run.
- `migrations/versions/e2b7c4a91f36_use_alter_foreign_keys.py` — creates both
  constraints under the names PostgreSQL would have generated had the inline definitions
  survived, matching the sibling FK the baseline did create.

No `ON DELETE` behaviour is specified, matching the ORM exactly. Trading this drift for
a different one would leave the chain no more trustworthy than it is today.

## Verification

Checked against the database, not the migration text:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pg_constraint`, before | 1 FK across both tables (`taxonomy_versions_parent_version_id_fkey`) |
| `pg_constraint`, after | 3 FKs, both new ones `confdeltype = a` (NO ACTION) |
| Orphan rows pre-flight | 0 in both directions — nothing to reject the constraint |
| upgrade → downgrade → upgrade | 2 → 0 → 2. The downgrade that was previously impossible now works |
| `alembic revision --autogenerate` | **produces an empty migration** |
| `make check` | `All checks passed.` |

The autogenerate result is the one that matters: the pair is no longer re-proposed, so
the next person to run `make revision` has nothing to strip.

## Note for reviewers

The docstring on `537d54fe5104` still instructs the reader to strip the generated pair.
That instruction is now moot rather than wrong — it described the state at that revision,
and autogenerate no longer emits anything to strip. I left the historical record intact
rather than amending a merged migration.

author: betmoar
body:
Closes #32.

## The defect

A loop reaches a state where **no autonomous work remains** — every remaining path crosses a human decision. Pre-fix the agent's only move is a one-line "still parked" reply on each Stop. The hook charges every one as a full iteration and answers with the entire payload re-injected verbatim: 16 → 34 iterations of a 40 cap over a day of idle stops, ~18 identical multi-KB re-injects, and `/repete-cancel` as the only exit.

## The fix

A third sentinel, `<repete-parked>`, and the `paused-parked` status it yields. The Stop is allowed through, **the iteration is not charged**, and the one-line reason rides the hook's message. `/repete-continue` gained a `paused-parked` branch that reconstructs the pending decisions and insists the resolutions be written where the next iteration will read them. The statusline renders `·park`.

Design points, each with a test:

- **Not suppressed in autonomous mode**, unlike `<repete-checkpoint>`. That flag exists to run past *sub-goals*; "I cannot proceed without you" is the one state autonomy cannot clear — and the reported loop was autonomous, so suppressing it there reproduces the bug verbatim.
- **Precedence checkpoint > parked > done** — the I2 rule with one more rung. Both gated paths beat a teardown; between them the checkpoint wins because it carries a payload to promote. A turn claiming done *and* blocked-on-you is contradictory and resolves toward the human.
- No `transition.md` written (nothing to promote; clobbering one would destroy an approved payload), `stale_count` untouched (not a work turn), suppressed while `summarizing` (the budget two-step owns that Stop).
- `set_fm_or_warn` guards the write (#21): a park that cannot be persisted is never announced.

The golden re-inject sha moved deliberately — the parked rule joins the **frozen protocol core** rather than `RULES_EXTRA`, because it applies in both modes (7 → 8 lines).

## Not shipped from #32

- **Automatic no-op detection.** "The agent made no tool calls and changed no state" is not a fact the Stop hook can read — it sees the transcript, not effects. A false positive freezes the iteration counter, making `max_iterations` unreachable: a fail-closed trap, the one direction this engine must not fail. The sentinel puts the judgment where the evidence is.
- **General delta-only re-injection.** With the park yielding instead of re-injecting, the repeated-payload symptom is gone for this case; shrinking the payload generally is a separate change with its own golden-fixture blast radius.

## Verification

Red-first: the 18 new hook assertions and 1 statusline assertion all failed on the pre-fix hook, with the other 324/27 still passing.

End-to-end on a reproduction of the reported loop (gauntlet + autonomous, phase 2, iteration 16, cap 40):

```
A (plain reply) decision : block          <- pre-fix-only option
A iteration: 17                            <- charged
A re-inject bytes: 3183                    <- full payload
B (parked) decision : none — Stop allowed through
B status: paused-parked
B iteration: 17                            <- not charged
B active: true
B transition.md: not written
C (next Stop) output: <empty — no re-inject>
statusline: rp[17/40] ·park
```

Suites: **342 hook (was 319) + 28 statusline + 43 promote + 13 release-gate, ALL SUITES GREEN**; shellcheck clean; `release-gate.mjs v0.2.6` OK.

author: satur8d
body:
## What

A deterministic, zero-LLM verb, `totem resolve-threads <pr>`, resolves the bot review threads a round disposition has answered, as the last operator-gated step of the review-reply skill's `done` flow. It exists because the merge-ready gate's predicate 2 (mmnto-ai/totem#2800) denies on any unresolved, non-outdated bot thread, and a strict run over the five most recently merged totem PRs denied all five, three of them on minor findings a disposition had declined in prose but nobody had resolved in the thread. Ruled on 2026-09-08: resolve the threads, do not weaken the gate, mechanise the step. Serves mmnto-ai/totem#2841; the preflight spec and its R1–R4 rulings ride in as the two spec commits.

## How

- **Reads** the PR's review threads through one paginated GraphQL document (thread id, resolution, outdated flag, path, each comment's database id, author and instant; a second document by node id for a thread's comments past its first page) and the PR-level comments through the REST issue-comments endpoint, both behind one injected exec seam so the suite runs offline. An unfollowable page or a blown page budget is a hard error with no partial plan — the same no-silent-shrink rule the spine's thread reader carries.
- **Selects** threads rooted by a review-bot identity (`BOT_REVIEWER_IDENTITIES` from core, the exact GraphQL login test) that are unresolved and not outdated, and derives each one's evidence: any non-bot comment after the root in the thread, OR any non-bot PR-level comment created later than the root (R2 — the only lawful answer to a Gemini thread is at the PR level, and the round disposition is that comment). "Non-bot" on the REST side excludes GitHub Apps and `[bot]` logins as well as the four review bots, so the release cut sensor's comments never count as a human disposition.
- **Plans** one row per bot-rooted thread — `resolve`, `skip:already-resolved`, `skip:outdated`, `skip:not-selected`, `skip:no-evidence` — printed with the REST root id beside each; `--json` carries the same rows. A thread with no evidence is listed as needing a reply first and is never resolved under any flag.
- **Mutates** only under `--apply`: `resolveReviewThread` once per `resolve` row, continuing on a per-thread failure and exiting 2 at the end naming the count; a selected no-evidence row makes the exit 2 after the other rows were applied. Dry-run is the default and performs zero mutations. The verb never posts a comment, reply or review (an exec spy asserts every argv the verb can emit).
- **Selection** (R4): every evidenced bot thread by default; `--ids <REST root ids>` narrows; an unmatched or malformed id aborts with exit 2 before any mutation.
- **Skill step** (R3): the review-reply `done` flow, after the disposition comment posts, runs the verb dry, shows the plan, and applies only on the operator's explicit go; the three distributed surfaces stay byte-locked to the constant with string locks on the new step.

## Verification

Built stacked on the mmnto-ai/totem#2800 branch, then brought forward onto main at `6b984c33` (after mmnto-ai/totem#2843, mmnto-ai/totem#2844 and mmnto-ai/totem#2848 merged) with `git rebase --onto`: fifteen commits replayed, no conflicts, `git range-diff` reports every one `=` (patch-identical). On the rebased tree: full workspace build + test 12/12 tasks green (`pnpm build` then `pnpm test`), `pnpm format:check` clean, ESLint 0 errors, `totem lint` PASS. The verb's own suite: `resolve-threads.test.ts` (the fixture capture of a real round plus the synthetic arms — dry-run performs zero mutations, `--apply` resolves only evidenced threads, the allowlist exec spy names every argv the verb can emit, the failure and success `--json` documents locked), `resolve-threads-cli-wiring.test.ts` (the mmnto-ai/totem#2097 seam), and `init.test.ts` (the three review-reply surfaces byte-locked to the constant).

## Review leg (doctrine/model-tiering § Review legs)

Three legs, every deposit committed under `.totem/artifacts/legs/` (read 56fcab96, b8c65ec1 and — after the rebase onto main — 70351e0e, which the gate reads as the nearest ancestor of HEAD). The third, scoped to the rebase's interactions, named termination: the registry the verb consumes (`bot-identity.ts`) is blob-identical at the stack base, the head and main, so the verb was written against the final module; the three review-reply surfaces are byte-locked on this branch; the CLI seam holds; the wiki entry is placed and accurate; this `@mmnto/cli` minor folds into the 2.3.0 cut if merged before mmnto-ai/totem#2850, else rides 2.4.0. Two minor follow-ups it named are deferred to the pilot-install PR that re-renders this skill: the bot-identity parity sensor scans two consumers by name and this verb is a third (its `[bot]` suffix rule would need to move to core to join the scan), and the skill's step 4 should say in one clause that a clean resolve run is not an allow verdict — the gate's other predicates, a HIGH inline on the head commit or an unreadable read, still decide. Leg 1 (eleven findings, none blocking, two material): the never-writes spy was a denylist a `gh pr review` mutant escaped, rebuilt as an allowlist over the verb's five exact exec shapes and run in the dry-run test too; an App's in-thread reply counted as human evidence because the read never fetched the author's typename, so both documents now select it and a Bot typename, a `[bot]` suffix or core's exact list all mean bot. Nine minors folded: the mutation response is parsed and `isResolved` required, the narrative states R2's rule rather than "the disposition comment", a disclosed limit on the loose CodeRabbit pattern, the capture carries all seven PR-level comments, not-found fixtures shaped like the observed exit-1 body, the failure JSON document locked, the ordering locks assert presence first, the deleted-account rule recorded as a judgement on the design. Leg 2 (four minors, termination named): the row set is the four review-bot roots while the human-reply test is the three-arm one, stated in the wiki and the changeset; the fixture bot list derives from core's identities; the success JSON document's key set and every summary field asserted; one narration corrected in a test comment. Declined: none.

## Not in this PR

- Any change to merge-ready's predicates (predicate 2 keeps no severity floor).
- Auto-resolving on a fix push without a disposition.
- Selection by inbox number (R4: not stable across re-runs).
- The pilot install of merge-ready on totem, which follows this PR and the 2.3.0 cut.

## Related

Closes mmnto-ai/totem#2841
<!-- totem-close: #2841 -->

See mmnto-ai/totem#2800 (the gate and the calibration measurement), mmnto-ai/totem#2626 (ghcq has no listener), mmnto-ai/totem#2097 (the global `--json` collision the wiring test now locks against).

author: gustavoamigo
body:
## Problem

`ALTER TABLE ... ALGORITHM=COPY` — which is how `CREATE INDEX`, `DROP INDEX`, and every non-inplace `ALTER` run in this plugin — copies each row into a hidden `#sql-xxx` table via `write_row`. Every row was buffered into `MariaDBTxn`'s `ops_` + `lookup_` and committed as a single `apply_batch`. For a 1M-row table that is ~2M `WriteOp`s held several times over (~1 GB RAM) followed by one multi-hundred-MB `pwritev` + a single `fdatasync` — an OOM risk at 10M rows and a large latency spike.

## Approach

The `#sql-xxx` destination keyspace is invisible to every other transaction until the final catalog rename (under an exclusive metadata lock), so it is safe to commit it in fixed-size batches.

- **`MariaDBTxn` bulk-copy mode** — a dedicated snapshot-less `bulk_plan_` plus a byte counter and a small `bulk_seen_` set. It never touches `ops_` / `lookup_` / `snap_`: the copy's source-table scan runs on the *same per-THD txn* and holds a live `MergeIterator` over `snap_`+`lookup_` that must not be disturbed.
- **`write_row`** detects the copy destination (`is_alter_copy_target()` — a `#sql-` table path plus an `ALTER` / `CREATE INDEX` / `DROP INDEX` statement) and routes puts to the bulk buffer, flushing every `bytecaskdb_bulk_copy_flush_bytes` with `apply_batch({.sync=false})`.
- **`end_bulk_insert`** does the final `sync=true` flush as a durability barrier before the rename.
- **Duplicate probes** (`bulk_pk_exists`, `bulk_unique_prefix_exists`) check the current unflushed batch plus the DB directly — the stale pre-ALTER snapshot would miss rows written by earlier batches.

Peak plugin memory during a copy-ALTER is now **~2× the flush threshold, independent of row count**. No separate "activation" step is added: the existing `rename_table` + `delete_table` swap activates the table, and a crash mid-copy leaves an invisible orphan `#sql-` keyspace that MariaDB's `ddl_log` reclaims via `delete_table` → O(1) `del_range`.

## New system variable

`bytecaskdb_bulk_copy_flush_bytes` (GLOBAL, default 64 MiB, min 4 KiB, max 4 GiB) — max buffered bytes before a batch flush during a copy-ALTER.

## Tests

| Suite | Added |
| --- | --- |
| `mariadb_txn_tests` `[txn][bulk]` | mid-copy durability, within-batch + cross-flush duplicate detection, rollback/abort, tail flush on commit |
| `mariadb_proof_tests` `prove_bulk_index_build` | batches land mid-copy; a flush I/O failure aborts the ALTER; an aborted copy's flushed rows are `del_range`-reclaimable |
| functional `ddl.yaml` | 800-row batched `CREATE INDEX` + `CHECK TABLE`; cross-flush-boundary `ADD UNIQUE INDEX` rejected with `ER_DUP_ENTRY` (1062) |

`mariadb_txn_tests` 69 assertions / 7 cases · `mariadb_proof_tests` 1003 assertions / 202 cases · functional yaml 186 passed (1 pre-existing unrelated failure, `type_blob_explain`, fails identically on `main`).

No engine code path changed (`apply_batch` semantics untouched), so no benchmark run.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

True inplace `ADD INDEX` / `DROP INDEX` that skips the full-table row copy entirely — build only the new index keyspace in batches and flip it on with one small catalog write in `commit_inplace_alter_table`.

author: hyperb1iss
body:
The coding controller could use its entire tool allowance without seeing how many calls remained, then request another tool instead of returning a final answer. Each model request now includes the declared and remaining budgets. At zero tools, the provider is asked for a text-only response.

The execution guard still rejects an extra call if the provider ignores that request. Final responses remain subject to input, output, and cost limits. The existing controller-byte binding changes the experiment policy digest, so subsequent runs require a fresh frozen policy. Earlier calibration results remain unchanged.

## 🧪 Validation

The full agent-task suite passed 329 tests with one existing Linux-only case skipped on macOS. Independent review passed 13 cases, including batched calls at the final slot, a refused invocation consuming that slot, and input-token enforcement during finalization. Parent spot checks and integration checks passed after rebasing onto the merged collection harness. Lint passed.

A separately frozen remote calibration used the same two development tasks and budgets with the new controller policy. Both controllers completed normally: reservation reconciliation passed all six oracle cases in 13 tools, while build planning used 20 tools and a final text-only response but failed its duplicate-edge case. Total reported cost was $0.012652. The original incomplete results remain unchanged; this qualifies controller behavior and does not establish memory gain.

author: tomassonjw
body:
## Ce que ça corrige

Le CFS chauffait la buse à 220 °C à chaque chargement de PLA, quelle que soit la température demandée par le G-code. Attribué jusqu'ici au repli `Tn_extrude_temp` de `box.cfg`, puis à l'en-tête du fichier tranché. Les deux sont faux.

Le chargeur d'origine lit la fiche matière de l'emplacement qu'il va tirer dans `creality/userdata/box/material_database.json`. La fiche `00001 Generic PLA` porte `nozzle_temperature: 220`.

**Le départage** ne vient pas de la température mais de la vitesse journalisée dans le même bloc : le CFS annonce `max_volumetric_speed: 14`, qui est le `filament_max_volumetric_speed` de cette fiche, alors que le fichier tranché porte `23,24`. Et `tn_extrude_temp = 200` était bien chargé les 3, 5 et 8 septembre, avec `get next material temp: 220` les trois fois.

Conséquence utile : la température suit la matière de la bobine chargée, pas la liste des filaments du travail. Un fichier à seize filaments dont un ABS ne fera jamais charger du PLA à 260 °C.

## Ce que fait cette PR

- `scripts/corriger-temperatures-chargement-cfs-v1.py` : rend compte des matières présentes et de leur température de chargement, et corrige les fiches nommées avec sauvegarde et relecture. Appliqué sur la machine le 9 septembre : `00001` de `220` à `200`.
- `_KCTRL_LOAD_GUARD` : fenêtre ouverte par `START_PRINT` autour de son bloc CFS, qui **abaisse** toute cible au dessus de `EXTRUDER_TEMP + 15` au lieu de la refuser. Pas armée pendant le reste de l'impression, pour qu'un second filament puisse monter plus haut.
- `tests/test_cfs_load_temperature_ceiling_v1.py` : 12 tests, dont le rendu réel des macros `M104`/`M109` — une cible à 220 pendant le chargement ressort en `M104.1 S205.0` sans erreur, et la fenêtre de palpage continue de refuser.
- Documents 30 et 54 corrigés sur ce point par le document 67.

## Ce qui n'est pas prouvé

Le garde-fou n'est **pas encore chargé** : une impression de 13 h tournait et charger la configuration demande un redémarrage de Klipper. Aucun journal de départ réel ne prouve le résultat. Le module compilé contient `run_script_from_command` — donc les redéfinitions de `M104`/`M109` attrapent ce qui passe par le répartiteur — mais aussi `get_heater` et `set_temp` ; si le chargeur pose sa cible directement par l'API du chauffage, seule la correction de la base agira.

À lire au prochain départ : `get next material temp: 200`, `flush_temp: 200`, et une cible de buse qui ne dépasse jamais 205 entre le début du bloc CFS et la ligne d'amorce.

author: kouitic
body:
## 概要

Refs #273 #268

急変検知の比較相手を**通知種別で絞って**引いていたため、通知種別が切り替わった直後は
比較相手が見つからず、**急変検知が丸ごと skip** されていた問題を直します
（横断監査 Phase A の finding **N-05**）。

```
DISCLOSURE = PUBLIC_SANITIZED
方式  **O-2**（管理者の第一候補）+ 管理者判断 **A-1 / B-1**（#273 issuecomment-5592477960）
承認  IMPLEMENTATION_GATE = USER 承認済み（#213 issuecomment-5591555494 の実装順）
      管理者レビュー = PASS（head 74d6daa / JIRO-20260909-007）
計画  #273 issuecomment-5592464231 / 宣言 #273 issuecomment-5592518685
```

### 事象

```
急変検知（data_quality_service.detect_anomalies）の比較相手 previous を、
**再送防止と同じ scope**（= 通知種別で絞った直近ログ）から引いていた。

  _previous_recommendation -> _log_lookup_for_recommendation_scope
    holding_id あり  latest_by_holding_and_type(holding_id, ★ notification_type)
    holding_id なし  latest_by_stock_and_type(stock_code, ★ notification_type)

-> 通知種別が切り替わった直後は**新種別のログが無く** previous is None となり、
   ★ 適正価格・株価が大きく動いていても**検知されないまま通知される**（検知の欠落）。
```

```
★ 急変検知は**推奨種別を 1 つも参照していない**（実測）。
  「適正価格が前回分析から N% 動いた」は、前回が HOLD でも SELL でも同じ意味である。
  種別で絞っていたのは**再送防止の都合**であり、
  急変検知がその scope を借りているのが構造上の誤りだった。
```

## ★ なぜ「単純な横断化」（O-1）を採らないか

```
`_previous_recommendation()` 自体を種別横断にすると、
**再送防止（_notification_status_for_send）の scope まで一緒に変わる**。

-> 「種別が変わったのに前回送ったばかりとして抑止される」
   = ★ **通知の欠落**という**別方向の欠陥**を作る。

★ #271（参照先の消失 -> 過剰送信）と本 Issue（種別切替 -> 検知の欠落）は
  倒れる向きが逆であり、同じ関数で両方を直そうとすると相反する。

-> O-2 は「**急変検知だけ別の探索を使う**」ため、
   再送防止に一切影響せず、#271 とも独立に実装・検証できる。
```

## 変更内容

### 1) repository — 種別を問わない lookup を 2 つ追加（B-1）

```
infrastructure/local_repository/notification_log_repository.py

  list_by_stock(stock_code)   -> NotificationLookup
  list_by_holding(holding_id) -> NotificationLookup

★ **scope は従来どおり保つ**（holding-scope は holding_id、stock-scope は stock_code）。
  scope まで広げると、#33 が直した「別 owner の通知が判定へ influence する」
  scope 非対称が復活する。
★ 既存の `find_with_outcome()`（#279 で追加）を使い、**述語から種別の条件を外しただけ**。
  走査コストは既存の種別つき lookup と**同じ**（どちらも述語走査であり、
  新しい索引を必要としない）。
★ #279 の `undecidable` は**既存経路に従う**（後述）。
```

### 2) service — データ品質へ渡す previous だけを差し替え（A-1 / O-2）

```
services/line_notification_service.py

  _log_lookup_for_recommendation_scope_any_type()   scope は同じ、種別だけ問わない
  _previous_recommendation_any_type()               急変検知用の比較相手

  :2233 evaluate_notification_status
  :2339 check_data_quality_eligibility
    -> `_check_data_quality()` へ渡す previous **だけ**を種別横断へ差し替え
```

```
★ **変更していない**もの（実測して確認）
  `_previous_recommendation()`（種別つき）   再送防止用。**そのまま**
  `_notification_status_for_send()`          #271 の成果。**1 行も触れていない**
  `services/data_quality_service.py`         ★ A-1 のため **signature も本体も不変**
  `recommendation_repository.py`（**S-03**） B-1 を採ったため**不触**
  S-17 永続化ストア層 / enum                 不触（**enum は 1 つも追加していない**）
```

### ★ A-1 / B-1 を採った理由（管理者判断）

```
A-1（5 つの比較すべてを種別横断にする / signature 変更なし）

  `detect_anomalies()` で previous を使う比較は **5 つ**ある（実測）。
    1 fair_value_changed_sharply          ★ Phase A が名指しした急変検知
    2 price_change_resembles_split_ratio  ★ 同上
    3 profit_take_price_changed_sharply
    4 dividend_yield_changed_sharply
    5 record_date_regressed_to_unknown

  previous は **1 つの引数**として渡るため、「1・2 だけ別の previous」にするには
  signature 変更が要る。★ 3・4・5 も「前回の分析と比べる」意味では 1・2 と同じで、
  **種別で絞る必然性は同じく見当たらない**（Phase A が 1・2 について述べた理由が
  そのまま当てはまる）。同じ関数に 2 種類の previous を同居させるより、
  **まるごと揃えるほうが構造的に一貫する**と判断された。

B-1（NotificationLog 系から引く / S-03 に触れない）

  ★ 候補 B-2（RecommendationRepository を直接引く）には**落とし穴**がある。
    holdings / buy とも `recommendation_repo.save()` が品質チェックより**先**に走るため、
    `latest_by_stock()` をそのまま呼ぶと **current 自身**が返り、変化率は必ず 0 になる。
    = **直したのに何も検知しない**（fake で書くと気づけない）。
  B-1 は通知履歴を経由するため、まだ通知していない current 自身は候補に入らず、
  この落とし穴を**構造的に回避**する。さらに S-03 へ触れないため lock も D5 に収まる。
  ★ 見込みに頼らず `previous.recommendation_id != current.recommendation_id` を
    テストで固定している（T-5）。
```

### 判定不能（#279）の扱い

```
`undecidable` でも None を返す。**既存の `_previous_recommendation()` と同じ扱い**である。
送信可否は `_notification_status_for_send()` 側が `undecidable` を見て抑止するため、
ここで送信へ倒れることはない（#279 の設計をそのまま踏襲し、新しい規則を作らない）。
```

---

## TIME_SEMANTICS_IMPACT

TIME_SEMANTICS_IMPACT = NO

```
★ 実測による根拠（NO は免罪符ではないため、判断の材料を示します）

  T1  domain/market_session.py / business_calendar.py / jst.py /
      price_freshness.py                         -> **diff なし**
  T2  provider の日付・時刻の決定ロジック          -> **diff なし**
      （provider を 1 つも触らず、as_of_date / fetched_at / bar date / 取得窓の
        いずれにも diff が無い）
  T3  時刻由来値を受け取って業務分岐する consumer  -> **該当しない**
      本 PR が変えたのは「**どの前回と比べるか**」であり、時刻ではない。
      比較そのもの（変化率の計算式・閾値・単位）に 1 行も手を入れていない。
      時刻由来値で分岐する箇所を **1 つも増やしていない**。
  T4  test / mock / fixture の **clock または期待日**
      -> 新規テストは固定値の datetime を**データとして**使うだけで、

body:
`make sast`'s audit-npm leg is red on **main**. Not from any change — the advisory database moved and flagged dependencies that were already resolved.

| Project | Advisory | Severity | Package |
|---|---|---|---|
| docs-site | GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh | high | js-yaml |
| docs-site | GHSA-4vpr-x523-8j87 | moderate | svgo |
| docs-site | GHSA-w27v-7q3p-w38r | high | svgo |
| web | GHSA-4vpr-x523-8j87 | moderate | svgo |
| web | GHSA-w27v-7q3p-w38r | high | svgo |

Both svgo advisories are `removeScripts` failing to sanitize executable content — HTML in `foreignObject`, and links reaching through namespace and control-character bypasses. The js-yaml one is unbounded CPU on empty merge sources.

Lockfile-only, via `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` in each project. No manifest ranges change.

## `npm audit` disagreed with the repo's own tool

`npm audit` reported **"found 0 vulnerabilities"** in both projects, before and after the fix, while `tools/audit-npm.py` reported five. Acting on npm's verdict alone would have left all five in place. This repository queries the advisory endpoint directly for exactly that reason, and its self-test confirms the endpoint is live on every run (`advisory endpoint confirmed live (lodash@4.17.11 reported as expected)`).

## The resolved set moved more than the flagged packages

Diffed against `origin/main`'s lockfiles, not against the manifests:

| Project | Package | Change |
|---|---|---|
| docs-site | js-yaml | 4.3.1 → 4.3.2 |
| docs-site | svgo | 4.0.2 → 4.1.0 |
| docs-site | css-select | 5.2.2 → **6.0.0** (transitive major) |
| docs-site | css-what | 6.2.2 → **7.0.0** (transitive major) |
| web | svgo | 4.0.2 → 4.1.0 |
| web | sax | 1.6.0 → 1.6.1 |
| web | css-select | 5.2.2 → **6.0.0** (transitive major) |
| web | css-what | 6.2.2 → **7.0.0** (transitive major) |
| web | entities | 4.5.0, hoisted out of `dom-serializer` to the top level |

The two majors are svgo 4.1.0's own requirement rather than a gratuitous upgrade, and both sit on the build path — so this is verified by building, not by the audit alone. The `entities` entry is a hoist, not a version change: same 4.5.0, relocated as the tree resolved.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `make site-build` | exit 0, 238 pages |
| web vitest | 132 passed, 18 files |
| docs-site `test:plugins` | 13 passed |
| `tools/check-rendered-site-links.py` | 73,059 links across 288 pages, clean |
| `tools/check-docs-contrast.py` | all pairs pass |
| `tools/lint-npm-allow-scripts.py` | both lockfiles match `allowScripts` |
| `tools/audit-npm.py` | both projects clean |

The web suite's three `fixture-axe` cases fail without prior build output and pass once `make site-build` has run; that is the suite's documented precondition, not an effect of this bump.

author: djaaym
body:
Une affiche de vingt noms fait quinze écrans de haut sur un téléphone, et
pousse le lieu, la carte, la billetterie et les blocs de maillage hors de
portée : sur la fiche montrée, la liste occupe l'écran entier sans qu'on
atteigne jamais ce qui suit. Le bloc devient donc un `<details>` fermé par
défaut, dont le `<summary>` porte le titre existant, le nombre d'artistes et
un chevron. Au-delà de 720 px la place existe, le CSS le force ouvert et le
résumé redevient un simple titre.

Deux choix à ne pas défaire :

- `<details>` et pas un état React. Les liens du line-up restent dans le HTML
  rendu au serveur dans les deux états, donc le maillage interne qu'un crawler
  suit ne bouge pas, et la fiche événement, qui porte le SEO du site, ne paie
  pas un octet de JavaScript de plus. Même raisonnement que `SearchableLinks`,
  dont le champ masque des lignes sans rien aller chercher.
- Le forçage ouvert en desktop est écrit deux fois, exprès. Les navigateurs
  cachent le contenu d'un `<details>` fermé de deux façons selon leur âge :
  les moteurs récents posent `content-visibility: hidden` sur
  `::details-content`, qu'un `display` sur l'enfant ne peut pas atteindre, les
  plus anciens masquent les enfants eux-mêmes. Une seule des deux règles
  s'applique par navigateur, jamais aucune.

Le compteur reprend les clés `dyn.artist` / `dyn.artists`, déjà présentes en
FR et en EN : aucune clé d'i18n nouvelle.

author: madhavilosetty-intel
body:
## What

`PATCH /api/v1/devices` and `PATCH /api/v1/admin/profiles` decoded the request body with `json.Unmarshal`, which runs no validators. Both handlers used `ShouldBindBodyWithJSON` until #1169 replaced it while adding the partial-update field map, so every `binding` tag on `dto.Device` and `dto.Profile` has been unenforced on PATCH since August.

Reproduced against a running instance:

```
POST /api/v1/admin/profiles  {"profileName":"p","amtPassword":"P@ssw0rd",
                              "activation":"ccmactivate", ...}          201
PATCH /api/v1/admin/profiles {"profileName":"p","activation":"acmactivate",
                              "generateRandomMEBxPassword":false}       200  <-- stored
GET  /api/v1/admin/profiles/p            activation: acmactivate, no MEBX password
```

ACM activation requires a MEBX password, so that profile cannot activate a device. The same path accepted `"activation":"activate"`, outside the `oneof` list.

## How

- Bind through `binding.JSON.BindBody`, which decodes **and** validates.
- Run the password invariants against the **merged** profile instead of only on insert. Omitting a password in a PATCH still keeps the stored one — `applyPATCHMerge` fills it in — but a merge that would leave the profile with no password is rejected.

Two supporting changes:

- The v1 handler tests called `gin.DisableBindValidation()` from a package `init()`, which nils `binding.Validator` for the entire test binary. **No handler test has ever exercised validation**, which is how the regression shipped unnoticed. The tests now register the same validators `NewRouter` installs.
- Registering custom tags from a route constructor races a request being validated on another goroutine — the validator engine's tag map is not safe for concurrent use. The race detector reports this on `main` today. Registration is now guarded by `sync.Once` and pre-run from the test `init()`, before any parallel test serves a request.

`addCertificate - missing required field` asserted 500 because validation was off; it now asserts the 400 its name implies.

## Compatibility

This **tightens** `/api/v1`: a PATCH body violating a binding tag returns 400 where it recently returned 200, and `profileName` / `activation` are required on a profile PATCH again. That restores the pre-#1169 contract rather than adding a new restriction, and `sample-web-ui` already sends the full object on update (`profiles.service.ts:48`).

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -s -l` — clean
- `go test -count=1 ./...` — pass
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` — pass, no data races (run on Linux; `-race` needs cgo)
- New: `TestProfilesUpdatePatchRejectsInvalidBody` (3 cases), `TestDevicesUpdatePatchRejectsInvalidBody`, `TestUpdateRejectsMergedProfileWithoutPasswords` (2 cases)

Found while re-enabling the RPS Postman collection, which has not run in CI since #217 — 13 of its assertions fail on this bug. The CI change that turns the collection back on follows in a separate PR and depends on this one.

No route, request shape, or OpenAPI declaration changes, so `internal/controller/openapi/` and the Postman collections are untouched here.
