author: robertjbass
body:
## The bug

0.68.9 stopped the MariaDB to MySQL dump conversion from rewriting row data by skipping any line matching `ROW_STATEMENT = /^\s*(?:INSERT|REPLACE)\b/i`. That guard is applied per line, and it covers a single-line insert and nothing else.

`mariadb-dump` 11.x writes an extended insert as one statement spread over many lines, with the keyword alone on the first line and one row per line after it:

```sql
/*!40000 ALTER TABLE `t_text` DISABLE KEYS */;
INSERT INTO `t_text` VALUES
(1,'moved the table to utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci last week'),
(2,'sql_mode was STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER before'),
(3,'crémant and rosé, naïve café');
/*!40000 ALTER TABLE `t_text` ENABLE KEYS */;
```

Only the first line starts with `INSERT`. The row lines start with `(`, so the collation rewrite ran on them. Verified on staging against the just-released 0.68.9: the target row read `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci last week`. The `sql_mode` row survived only because that rule is anchored to a `SET sql_mode` context a row line has no reason to match.

Before and after, same fixture:

```
--- 0.68.9 (per-line guard) ---
INSERT INTO `t_text` VALUES
(1,'moved the table to utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci last week'),      <-- user data rewritten
(2,'sql_mode was STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER before'),

--- 0.68.10 (statement-aware) ---
INSERT INTO `t_text` VALUES
(1,'moved the table to utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci last week'),
(2,'sql_mode was STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER before'),
```

## The fix

`normalizeMariaDbDumpForMysql(line)` stays pure and single-line, so the rules themselves are still unit tested line by line. A small stateful wrapper, `createMariaDbDumpNormalizer()` returning `{ next(line) }` with the same `NormalizedDumpLine` result and counts, carries the row guard across lines: when a line matches `ROW_STATEMENT` and its trimmed content does not end with `;`, the guard opens and every following line passes through untouched until one ends the statement. `normalizeMariaDbDumpFile` uses the wrapper; nothing else changes at the call site.

Termination is read as "the trimmed line ends with `;`". That is safe for a dump and only for a dump, and the assumption is documented on the wrapper: `mariadb-dump` escapes `\n` and `\r` inside string literals, so a value never ends a physical line, and the generator always closes the statement at the end of its own line. Trimming first is also what makes CRLF input work.

Deliberately unchanged: `LOAD DATA` and a bare `VALUES` statement are not treated as row statements, and `/*!...*/` versioned comment lines keep taking the ordinary rules, which is what strips `NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER` out of the `/*!50003 SET sql_mode = ... */` line around every trigger.

## Tests

Unit (`tests/unit/mysql-dump-normalize.test.ts`), over the exact multi-line fixture above:

- every line of the extended insert is byte-identical after normalization and rewrites nothing
- the `CREATE TABLE` before it is still rewritten, and a `CREATE TABLE` after the `;` is rewritten again (4 DDL collations mapped, 0 row ones)
- a CRLF variant holds the guard and releases it on `);\r`
- a single-line `INSERT` does not open the guard, so the next line is DDL again
- a multi-line `REPLACE` is protected the same way
- the whole fixture through `normalizeMariaDbDumpFile`, which is the only caller a real dump goes through

Integration (`tests/integration/mysql-mariadb-interop.test.ts`): the MariaDB source table now stores the literal text `utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci` and `NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER` in two rows placed at the end of the insert on purpose, so they are never the first row of their statement, and a new assertion reads both back verbatim off the MySQL target. This is the fixture that should have caught the regression; the previous ones had no such row.

Verified the test actually catches it: with the streamer temporarily reverted to the per-line call, `leaves row data that names a collation or a sql_mode verbatim` fails against real binaries with `got: sql_mode was STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER before`, the collation row having been rewritten out from under the query.

## Run locally

- `pnpm format` clean, `pnpm lint` clean (eslint + tsc)
- `pnpm test:unit`: 1843 pass, 0 fail (591 suites)
- `pnpm test:engine mysql-mariadb-interop`: 7 pass, 0 fail (real MariaDB 11.8 source, real MySQL 9 target)
- `pnpm test:engine mysql`: 22 pass, 0 fail

Version bumped 0.68.9 to 0.68.10 with `pnpm build:version`, CHANGELOG entry under `[0.68.10]`.
